ex-pers.opening: adj. pars , having no part in , not sharing in , not privy to. Prop. (rare but class.).—Constr. with gen. : ne expers partis esset de nostris bonis, Ter. Heaut. 4, 1, 39 : communis juris et consilii (opp. particeps…

expertĭo.opening: experior , a trial , proof; in plur. , Vitr. 8, 5 .

expertus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from experior.

expĕtens.opening: , -entis, P. a. expeto , desirous , eager : expetenti et lubidinoso in voluptatibus, Cic. Rep. 2, 41, 68 .

expĕtesso.opening: ( ), , v. intens. a. [id.], to desire , long for (a Plautinian word): quae te amat tuamque expetessit pulcram pulcritudinem, Plaut. Mil. 4, 1, 13 : cf. id. ib. 4, 6, 14 : artem, id. Trin. 2, 1, 6 ; id. Rud. 1, 5, 1 :…

expĕtĭbĭlis.opening: adj. id. , desirable : expetendum est, inquiunt, quod bonum est: expetibile, quod nobis contingit, cum bonum consecuti sumus, Sen. Ep. 117, 4 : potentia, Boëth. Consol. 2, 6.

expĕtītor.opening: expeto , one who desires or longs for (late Lat.): vestri, Symm. Ep. 8, 45 .

ex-pĕto.grammar: īvi or ĭi, ītum, 3 v. a. and n.
ex-pĕto.opening: v. a. and n. Act. To long for , seek after , aspire to , desire , covet , wish a thing (freq. and class.; syn.: appeto, affecto, cupio, concupisco, aveo, gestio, volo, opto, desidero, requiro). With acc. : assunt, me…

expĭātĭo.opening: expio , satisfaction , atonement , expiation (rare but class.): at vero scelerum in homines atque impietatum nulla expiatio est, * Cic. Leg. 1, 14, 40 : foederis rupti, Liv. 9, 1, 4 ; Vulg. Exod. 29, 36 al.

expĭātor.opening: id. , an atoner , expiator (post-class.): impuritatis, Tert. Pudic. 15 fin.

expĭātōrĭus.opening: adj. expiator , atoning , expiatory (late Lat.): poenae, Aug. Civ. D. 21, 13 .

expĭātrix.opening: expiator , an atoning or expiating priestess : piatrix dicebatur sacerdos, quae expiare erat solita, quam quidam ... sagam, alii expiatricem vocant, Fest. s. v. piatrix, p. 213 Müll.

expĭātus.opening: expio , atonement , expiation (post-class.), Tert. adv. Val. 13 .

expīlātĭo.opening: expilo , a pillaging , plundering (rare but class.): expilatio direptioque sociorum, Cic. Off. 2, 21, 75 ; cf.: expilationes direptionesque sociorum et civium, id. ib. 3, 8, 36 .

expīlātor.opening: id. , a pillager , plunderer : quem domus hospitem, non expilatorem recepisse videatur, * Cic. Q. Fr. 1, 1, 2, 9 : expilatores, qui sunt atrociores fures, hoc est λωποδύται , in opus publicum dari solent, etc., Dig. 47,…

ex-pīlo.opening: v. a. , to pillage , rob , plunder (class.; syn.: privo, orbo, compilo, spolio, diripio, populor, vasto, praedor). Lit. : si socios spolias, aerarium expilas, Cic. Par. 6, 1, 43 ; cf. Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 27 : ad expilandos…

ex-pingo.opening: v. a. , to paint , depict; to paint , paint over. Lit. : quoniam et pericula expingimus, ne quis miretur et rogos pingi, Plin. 35, 7, 31, § 49 : genas, to paint, rouge, Mart. 7, 83, 2 : cutem, id. 8, 52, 8 : se…

ex-pinso.opening: v. a. , to bruise to pieces , grind : far, Cato, R. R. 2, 4 .

ex-pĭo.opening: v. a. , to make satisfaction , amends , atonement for a crime or a criminal; to purify any thing defiled with crime; to atone for , to expiate , purge by sacrifice (freq. and class.; syn.: pio, lustro, placo, paco).…

ex-piscor.opening: v. dep. a. (lit., to fish out; hence, trop.), to search out , find out (perh. only vulg.; syn.: rimor, perscrutor, scrutor, indago, investigo, quaero): proinde expiscare, quasi non nosses, Ter. Phorm. 2, 3, 35 : nescis…

explānābĭlis.opening: adj. explano , clear , intelligible : vox, Sen. de Ira, 1, 3, 5.

explānātĭo.opening: explano . An explanation , interpretation (class.): somniis, vaticinationibus, oraculis quod erant multa obscura, explanationes adhibitae sunt interpretum, Cic. Div. 1, 51, 116 ; cf. aequitatis, id. Rep. 5, 2 : unius…

explānātor.opening: id. , an explainer , interpreter : sunt enim explanatores, ut grammatici poëtarum, Cic. Div. 1, 51, 116 : explanator aut interpres ejus legis, Lact. (Cic. ap. Lact.?) 6, 8.

explānātōrĭus.opening: adj. explano , explanatory (late Lat.): liber, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 1, 5 .

explānātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from explano.

ex-plāno.opening: v. a. * Lit. , to flatten or spread out : suberi cortex in denos pedes undique explanatus, Plin. 16, 8, 13, § 34 .— Trop. , of speech, to make plain or clear , to explain (class.: syn.: explico, expono, interpretor):…

ex-planto.opening: v. a. , to pull up , root out a plant (post-Aug.): pampinos, Col. 4, 14, 1 ; cf. id. 4, 29, 11 ; 11, 2, 38 al.

explēmentum.opening: expleo , that which fills up. Lit. , of food, a filling , stuffing : inanimentis explementum quaerito, Plaut. Stich. 1, 3, 19 : cacumina arborum explementum esse ventris, Sen. Ep. 110, 12 .—* Trop. , of speech, a…

ex-plĕo.opening: (archaic form explenunt, for explent, acc. to Fest. p. 80 ; cf.: solinunt, nequinunt, danunt, for solent, nequeunt, dant; v. do, redeo and soleo init.; inf. praes. explerier, Lucr. 6, 21 .— Contracted form expleris,…

explētĭo.opening: expleo, I. B. 2. a. , a satisfying : in ea expletione naturae summi boni finem consistere, Cic. Fin. 5, 14, 40 .

explētīvus.opening: adj. expleo , serving to fill out , expletive; in the later grammarians, conjunctiones, such as quidem , equidem , autem , quoque , Don. p. 1763 P.; Charis. p. 199 ib. al.

explētŏr.opening: id. , he who fills , completes , finishes , Hier. in Pelag. 1, 32 init.

explētus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from expleo.

explĭcābĭlis.opening: adj. explico , that may be explained , explicable (very rare): mensura, Plin. 4, 13, 28, § 98 .— Adv. : , in an explicable manner , acc. to Diom. p. 401 P.; Mar. Plot. de Metr. p. 2623.

explĭcanter.opening: adv. id. , intelligibly , plainly , Pomp. Gram. Comm. Art. Don. p. 343, 2 Lindem.

explĭcātē.opening: adv. , v. explico, P. a. fin.

explĭcātĭo.opening: explico , an unfolding , uncoiling (for the most part only in Cic.). * Lit. : est quasi rudentis explicatio, Cic. Div. 1, 56, 127 .— Trop. of speech, an unfolding , expounding , an explication , exposition , explanation…

explĭcātor.opening: id. , an expounder , explainer (Ciceron.): rerum explicator prudens, severus, gravis, Cic. Or. 9, 31 ; id. Inv. 2, 2, 6 .

explĭcātrix.opening: id. , she that expounds or explains : orationis perpetuae ad persuadendum accommodatae, Cic. Ac. 1, 8, 32 .

explĭcātus.opening: explico , an unfolding , stretching apart. * Lit. : alterno crurum explicatu, Plin. 8, 42, 67, § 166 .— * Trop. , of speech, an explication , exposition : (natura deorum) quam difficiles explicatus haberet, Cic. N. D.…

explĭcĭtus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from explico.

ex-plĭco.opening: (the latter first in Verg. G. 2, 280 ; afterwards freq.; Hor. C. 3, 29, 16 ; 4, 9, 44 ; id. S. 2, 2, 125 ; Liv. 7, 23, 6 et saep.; cf. Gell. 1, 7, 20 ), ātum or ĭtum (Cic. uses mostly atum, Caes. atum and itum; cf.…

ex-plōdo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , Gr. πτερνοκοπεῖν , to drive out or off by clapping; orig. a scenic word said of a player, to hiss or hoot off , explode him. Prop.: histrio exsibilatur et exploditur, Cic. Par. 3, 26 ; cf.: Aesopum…

explōrātē.opening: adv. , with certainty , etc., v. exploro, P. a. fin.

explōrātĭo.opening: exploro , an examination , exploration (post-Aug.): surculi, Col. 3, 9, 5 : exploratione occulta fallere aliquem, Tac. H. 3, 54 .— In partic., in milit. lang., a spying , Dig. 49, 16, 3 .

explōrātor.opening: id. , a searcher out , examiner , explorer; a prying person , a spy (not in Cic.) In gen.: rerum, Lucil. ap. Non. 366, 31 : suppositicius, Plaut. Ps. 4, 7, 71 .— Adj. , searching : ignes, Claud. III. Cons. Hon. praef.…

explōrātōrĭus.opening: adj. explorator, II. , of or belonging to searching out , exploratory (post-Aug.): coronae, a reward for scouts or those who sought out and pursued the enemy, Suet. Calig. 45 : scaphae, spy-boats, Veg. Mil. 5, 7 .

explōrātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from exploro.

ex-plōro.opening: v. a. , to search out , seek to discover , to examine , investigate , explore (class.; in Cic. esp. freq. in the part. perf. and P. a.; syn.: speculor, scitor, sciscitor, percontor, quaero, interrogo). In gen. With acc.…

explōsĭo.opening: explodo , a driving off by clapping , an exploding : ludorum explosiones et funerum, Cael. ap. Cic. Fam. 8, 11, 4 .

expŏlĭo.grammar: īvi or ĭi, ītum, 4 v. a.
expŏlĭo.opening: v. a. , to smooth off , make smooth , polish. Lit. : hac (i. e. herinacei) cute expoliuntur vestes, Plin. 8, 37, 56, § 135 : libellus arida pumice expolitus, Cat. 1, 2 : aedes expolitae, Plaut. Most. 1, 2, 18 :…

expŏlītĭo.opening: expolio , a smoothing off , rubbing up , polishing , finishing. Lit. : parietum, pavimentorum, a plastering, Vitr. 6 fin. ; 7 praef. fin. : urbana, i. e. of a house in the city, Cic. Q. Fr. 3, 1, 2, § 6 : miniacea,…

expŏlītor.opening: id. , a polisher , August. in Psa. 85, 12 .

expŏlītus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from expolio.

ex-pōno.opening: (ante-class. perf. exposivit, Plaut. Cas. 4, 4, 27 ; sync. expostus, Verg. A. 10, 694 ; Stat. Th. 7, 197 ), v. a. , to put or set out , to set forth , expose (class.; most freq. in the trop. signif.; cf.: expedio,…

ex-porrĭgo.opening: (contr. imper. exporge, Ter. Ad. 5, 3, 53 ), v. a. , to stretch out , spread out , extend (ante-class. and post-Aug.). Lit. : equites in longitudinem, Auct. B. Afr. 78, 4: munitiones, id. 42 fin. : crura exporrigentia…

exportātĭo.opening: exporto . * A carrying out , exportation : rerum, quibus abundaremus, Cic. Off. 2, 3, 13 .—* Banishment , deportation , Sen. Tranq. 11, 7 .

ex-porto.opening: v. a. , to bear or carry out , to bring out , convey away , export (class.): per mare e Phoenice Europam (Juppiter), Varr. R. R. 2, 5, 5 : aurum quotannis ex Italia Hierosolymam, Cic. Fl. 28, 67 : aurum argentumque…

ex-posco.opening: v. a. , to ask earnestly , to beg , request , to entreat , implore (rare but class.). In gen.: quam (misericordiam) ipse non implorat, ego autem repugnante hoc et imploro et exposco, * Cic. Mil. 34, 92 : signum proelii,…

expŏsĭtē.opening: adv. , plainly , clearly; v. expono, P. a. fin.

expŏsĭtĭcĭus.opening: or , , adj. expono, I. B. 1. , exposed , foundling : puella, Plaut. Cas. prol. 79 .

expŏsĭtĭo.opening: expono . An exposing of an infant (post-class.), Justin. 1, 4, 9; 1, 5, 4.— Of speech. A setting forth , exposition , an exhibiting , showing; a narration : cursum contentiones magis requirunt; expositiones rerum…

expŏsĭtĭuncŭla.opening: dim. expositio, II. , a brief exposition (late Lat.), Hier. adv. Jovin. 1, 37 .

expŏsĭtor.opening: expono , an expounder , interpreter : somniorum, Firm. Math. 13, 5: juris, Cassiod. Var. 9, 21 .

expŏsĭtus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from expono.

expostŭlātĭo.opening: expostulo , an expostulation , complaint (rare but class.): cum esset expostulatio facta, Cic. Clu. 59, 161 : singulorum, Tac. A. 1, 13 .—In plur. : fuerunt nonnulli aculei in C. Caesarem, contumeliae in Gellium,…

expostŭlātus.opening: id. , a complaint (late Lat. for expostulatio), Symm. Ep. 9, 13 .

ex-postŭlo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
ex-postŭlo.opening: v. a. and n. To demand vehemently or urgently , to demand , require (mostly post-Aug. for class. exposco; not in Cic., since in Rosc. Com. 17, 50, the true read. is: et postulare; cf. also: peto, exigo, flagito,…

expressē.opening: adv. , with pressure; trop., expressly , etc.; v. exprimo, P. a. fin.

expressim.opening: adv. expressus, from exprimo , expressly , clearly , distinctly (postclass.), Dig. 46, 3, 98 ; 49, 1, 19 .

expressĭo.opening: exprimo (postAug.), a pressing or squeezing out. In gen.: mellis, Pall. Jun. 7, 3 : spiritus, Vitr. 9, 9 .— In partic. In mechanics, a forcing apparatus to raise water, Vitr. 1, 1 ; 8, 7 ; cf. 2. expressus.— In…

expressor.opening: exprimo , one who presses out or brings forth (post-class.); trop.: veritatis (with integrator), Tert. Apol. 46 .

expressus.opening: exprimo , a forcing apparatus for raising water, Vitr. 8, 7 ; cf. expressio, II. A.

exprētus.opening: perh. for exspretus, from ex-sperno; acc. to Salmas. for exprettus = expressus , spurned or pressed out , Plaut. Bacch. 3, 3, 42 dub., v. Ritschl.

ex-prĭmo.opening: v. a. premo , to press or squeeze out , to force out (class.). Lit. : oleum ex malobathro, Plin. 12, 26, 59, § 129 : sucum expresso semini, id. 20, 1, 2, § 3 : sucum flore, id. 21, 19, 74, § 127 : sucum radici, id. 27,…

exprō^brābĭlis.opening: adj. exprobro , worthy of reproach , Vulg. Prov. 18, 1 ; 25, 16 al.

exprō^brātĭo.opening: id. , a reproaching , upbraiding , reproach (syn. opprobrium; not in Cic.; cf.: probrum, opprobrium, crimen; vituperatio, reprehensio, maledictum): cuiquam veteris fortunae, Liv. 23, 35, 7 : istaec commemoratio quasi…

exprō^brātor.opening: id. , one who reproaches , a reproacher , upbraider (postAug.), Sen. Contr. 3, 21 fin. ; id. Ben. 1, 1, 4 .

exprō^brātrix.opening: exprobrator , she that reproaches or upbraids : memoria, Sen. Ben. 7, 22, 2 .

ex-prō^bro.opening: v. a. probrum , to make a matter of reproach , to cast in the teeth , to accuse of any thing; also to charge , upbraid , reproach a person with something (syn. obicere); constr. aliquid in aliqua re or alicui (class.):…

exprōmissor.opening: expromitto , one who promises to pay either for himself or for another (in jurid. Lat.), Dig. 18, 1, 53 ; 42, 1, 4 et saep.

ex-prōmitto.opening: v. a. , in mercant. lang., to promise or agree to pay for one's self or for another (not in Cic.): nummos, Varr. R. R. 2, 2, 5 : pecuniam alicui, Dig. 23, 3, 36 ; 16, 1, 22 .

ex-prōmo.opening: (msi), mptum (mtum), , v. a. , to take out or forth , to draw out , fetch out , bring forth (syn. proferre). Lit. (rare): heminas octo in urceum, Plaut. Mil. 3, 2, 18 : mox inde sensim ad mandendum manibus expromit,…

exprŏpĕrātus.opening: Part. [† ex + propero], hastened , hurried : AQVILA FATIS, i. e. quickly overtaken, early cut off, Inscr. Grut. 669, 10 .

ex-pugnābĭlis.opening: adj. expugno , that may be taken , carried , or reduced by assault; expugnable (very rare): urbs terra marique expugnabilis est, Liv. 33, 17, 8 : ne magnis quidem exercitibus, Tac. H. 3, 78 : situ non expugnabile robur,…

expugnans.opening: Part. and P. a. , from expugno.

expugnātĭo.opening: expugno , the taking of a place by assault , carrying by storm , storming : urbis, Caes. B. G. 7, 36, 1 : oppidi, Suet. Claud. 21 : Mytilenarum, id. Caes. 2 ; cf.: ut ipsorum adventus in urbes sociorum non multum ab…

expugnātor.opening: expugno , the taker , stormer , conqueror of a place. Prop. (rare but class.): urbis, Cic. Inv. 1, 50, 93 : urbium, Vulg. Prov. 16, 32 : rex Demetrius Expugnator cognominatus (transl. of Πολιορκητής ), Plin. 7, 38, 39,…

expugnātōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , conquering , overpowering (post-class.): dominatio, Tert. Anim. 57 .

expugnax.opening: adj. id. , victorious , controlling , effectual : sive expugnacior herba est, Ov. M. 14, 21 .

ex-pugno.opening: (archaic inf. fut. expugnassere, Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 55 ), v. a. , to take by assault , to storm , capture , reduce , subdue (freq. and class.; syn.: obsideo, oppugno, capio). Lit. , of places: id (oppidum Noviodunum) ex…

expulsim.opening: adv. expulsus, from expello , by driving out or away from one's self : pilā expulsim ludere, Varr. ap. Non. 104, 29 .

expulsĭo.opening: expello , a driving out , expulsion : expulsiones vicinorum, Cic. Par. 6, 2, 46 : Laenatis, id. Rep. 1, 3 .

expulso.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to drive out , to expel (post-Aug. and very rare): si me (i. e. pilam) nobilibus scis expulsare sinistris, Sum tua, to drive from one's self, drive back, Mart. 14, 46, 1 ; cf.: expulsim: Seleucia per…

expulsor.opening: id. , a driver out , expeller (very rare but class.): iste bonorum possessor, expulsor, ereptor, * Cic. Quint. 8, 30 : tyranni, Nep. Dion. 10, 2 .

expultrix.opening: expello , she that drives out or expels : philosophia, expultrix vitiorum, Cic. Tusc. 5, 2, 5 .

ex-pūmĭco.opening: v. a. , to rub off with pumice-stone; trop., to cleanse , Tert. adv. Val. 16 .

expunctĭo.opening: expungo, II. B. 2. , an execution , performance (post-class.): operae meae, Tert. Idol. 16 .

expunctor.opening: expungo , a blotter-out , obliterator (post-class.), Tert. Or. 1 .

expunctrix.opening: id. , she who blots out : meritorum, Jul. ap. August. cont. Sec. Resp. Jul. 1, 37.

ex-pungo.opening: v. a. * Lit. , to prick out : nates jam diu sunt saepe expunctae, Plaut. Pers. 5, 2, 67 .— Hence, Transf. To strike out , cross out , blot out , erase from a list by points (set above or below). Lit. , to expunge a…

expurgātĭo.opening: expurgo, II. , a justification , vindication , excuse (a Plautin. word): habui expurgationem, Plaut. Am. 3, 3, 10 ; id. Merc. 5, 3, 4 (Ritschl, expurigationem).

ex-purgo.opening: v. a. , to purge , cleanse , purify (class.). Lit. : dolabella quicquid emortuum est (trunci aut vitis), Col. 4, 24, 5 : capisterio quicquid exteretur, id. 2, 9, 1 : lepras, psoras, lichenas, lentigines, Plin. 23, 7,…

ex-pūtesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to rot , putrefy : intestina tibi, Plaut. Curc. 2, 1, 26 .

ex-pŭto.opening: v. a. To lop off , to prune , to crop : veteranam vitem, Col. 3, 15, 3 ; 5, 6, 31 : palos, id. 11, 2, 12 .— Trop. To consider well , to examine : utramque rem simul, Plaut. Trin. 2, 1, 8 : id exputando evolvere, Auct.…

ex-quīro.opening: (in Plautus also exquaero, Bacch. 4, 4, 70 al.), , v. a. , to search out diligently , to seek for; to make inquiry , to inquire , to ask (syn.: requiro, inquiro, investigo, perscrutor; freq. and class.): cum ex te…

exquīsītim.opening: adv. exquisitus, from exquiro , i. q. exquisite, carefully , accurately , precisely , Varr. ap. Non. 513, 29 .

exquīsītĭo.opening: exquiro , research , inquiry , investigation (in jurid. Lat.), Cod. Just. 5, 9, 9 fin. ; 7, 17, 1 .— A seeking for , devising : idolorum, Vulg. Sap. 14, 12 .

exquīsītor.opening: id. , an investigator , Vulg. Baruch, 3, 23 ; cf. Cassiod. Var. 7, 5 .

exquīsītus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from exquiro.

exrādīcĭtus.opening: ( ), adv. , from the very roots , climax after radicitus, Plaut. Most. 5, 1, 63 : subvertendam censeo radicitus, immo vero Plautino irati verbo exradicitus, Front. p. 239 , ed. II. Mai.

exrŏgāre.grammar: est ex lege vetere aliquid eximere per novam legem
exrŏgāre.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 82, 2 Müll. (usually abrogo).

ex-sā^crĭfĭco.opening: ( ), , v. n. , to sacrifice : exsacrificabat hostiis balantibus, Poëta (Enn.) ap. Cic. Div. 1, 21, 42 ( Enn. Fragm. p. 98 Vahl.)

ex-saevĭo.opening: ( ), , v. n. , to rage itself out , to cease raging : stetit ibi, dum reliquum tempestatis exsaeviret, Liv. 30, 39, 2 .

exsanguesco.opening: v. inch. [exsanguis], to become pale , grow faint or feeble : (mens) ad omnia exsanguescens dubia, Jul. ap. August. cont. Sec. Resp. Jul. 6, 14.

exsanguĭnātus.opening: ( ), , adj. exsanguis , deprived of blood , bloodless : exsan. et exsucta animalia, Vitr. 8 praef.

ex-sanguis.opening: ( ), , adj. , deprived of blood , without blood , bloodless (class.). Lit. : unde animantum copia tanta Exos et exsanguis, Lucr. 3, 721 : jacens et concisus plurimis vulneribus, extremo spiritu exsanguis et confectus,…

ex-sănĭo.opening: ( ), , v. a. sanies , to free from matter or corruption , to cause to suppurate , to cleanse , dress a wound, etc. (post-Aug.). Lit. : vulnus (sal aridus), Cels. 5, 27 .— Transf. : pressam bacam, to press out the juice,…

ex-sarcio.opening: (also , , or ), no perf. , , v. a. — Lit. , to patch up , mend; hence, transf., to amend , repair , restore (very rare): exercirent sarcirent, Paul. ex Fest. p. 81 Müll. N. cr. : aliis te id rebus exsarturum esse…

ex-sătio.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to satisfy , to satiate , glut , sate (not ante-Aug.; cf. exsaturo). Lit. : exsatiati cibo vinoque, Liv. 40, 28, 2 .— Trop. : enses multo cruore, Sil. 7, 535 : tela, Stat. Th. 9, 14 : clade exsatiata…

exsătŭrābĭlis.opening: adj. exsaturo , that may be satiated : pectus, Verg. A. 5, 781 .

ex-sătŭro.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to satisfy completely , to satiate , sate (syn. explere; rare but class.): belua exsaturanda visceribus meis, Ov. M. 5, 19 : quae exsaturata lubido hausit, Poët. ap. Cic. Tusc. 5, 35, 101 : cum ejus…

ex-scalpo.opening: v. a. , to cut out , shape. — Trop. , to frame , prepare , of a passage in verse: hunc locum nostra poetica scabies coepit exscalpare, Auson. Idyl. 11 praef.

exscensĭo.opening: ( ), , escendo, II.; cf. ex, IV. B. 2. , a debarkation , landing; usu. with facere (repeatedly in Liv.; elsewh. rare; not in Cic. or Caes.): quinqueremibus septem profectus ad Erythras exscensionem fecit, Liv. 28, 8, 8…

ex-scindo.opening: ( ), , v. a. (lit., to tear out; hence, in gen.), to extirpate , destroy (syn.: delere, evertere, vastare). Lit. (class.): templum sanctitatis, etc. ... inflammari, exscindi, funestari, Cic. Mil. 33, 90 ; cf. id. Planc.…

exscrĕābĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. exscreo , that may be hawked up or coughed out : vitia pulmonum, Plin. 20, 14, 55, § 157 .

falla.opening: fallo , = fallacia, an artifice , trick , Nov. ap. Non. 109, 20 .

fallācĭa.opening: ( abl. also fallacie, App. M. 5, p. 171 ), fallax , deceit , trick , artifice , stratagem , craft , intrigue (class.; in Cic. only plur.; syn.: fraus, dolus, astus, astutia, calliditas). Prop. Plur. : nonne ab imis…

fallācĭlŏquus.opening: adj. fallaxloquor , speaking deceitfully or falsely : fallaciloquae malitiae, Att. ap. Cic. Fin. 4, 25, 68 .

fallācĭōsus.opening: adj. fallacia , deceitful , deceptive , fallacious (post-class.): argumenta (with vafra), Gell. 7, 3, 34 : ambages, id. 14, 1, 34 : promissio, App. M. 8, p. 205, 9 .

fallācĭtas.opening: fallax , deceit , artifice , = fallacia, Cassiod. Amic. 46, 2 .

fallax.opening: ( gen. plur. fallacium, Cic. Lael. 25, 91 al. ; but fallacum, Cat. 30, 4 ), adj. fallo , deceitful , deceptive , fallacious (class.; esp. freq. in Cic.; syn.: captiosus, fraudulentus, subdolus, dolosus, vafer, astutus,…

fallo.opening: (archaic inf. praes. pass. fallier, Pers. 3, 50 ; perf. pass. fefellitus sum, Petr. Fragm. 61 , MSS.), v. a. Sanscr. sphal, sphul, to waver; Gr. σφάλλω, ἀ-σφαλής , to deceive , trick , dupe , cheat , disappoint (freq.…

falsārĭus.opening: falsus, from fallo , a forger of written documents, wills, etc. (post-Aug.), Suet. Ner. 17 ; id. Tit. 3 ; Dig. 4, 9, 1 al.

falsātĭo.opening: falsatus , a falsifying (eccl. Lat.), Hier. in Ruf. 2, 5 .

falsātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from 1. falso.

false.opening: adv. , v. fallo, P. a. fin. 2.

falsĭdĭcentia.opening: falsidicus , habitual falsehood (opp. veridicentia), Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. M. 2, 1 .

falsĭdĭcus.opening: adj. falsus-dico , speaking falsely , lying (ante- and postclass.): fallaciae, Plaut. Capt. 3, 5, 13 ; id. Trin. 3, 3, 40 ; Att. ap. Prisc. p. 709 ; Aus. Epigr. 118, 17 .

falsĭfĭcus.opening: adj. falsus + facio , that acts falsely : glossema, Plaut. Mil. 2, 2, 36 .

falsĭjūrĭus.opening: adj. falsus + jus , that swears falsely : glossema, Plaut. Mil. 2, 2, 36 .

falsĭlŏquĭum.opening: falsiloquus , false speaking , falsehood , lying (late Lat.), Aug. Retract. praef. fin.

falsĭlŏquus.opening: ( ), , adj. falsus + loquor , that speaks falsehoods : quarum rerum te falsilocum mihi esse nolo. Plaut. Capt. 2, 2, 14 ; Prud. Apoth. 107 ; also Plaut. Mil. 2, 2, 36 , glossema.— Subst. : , , , a false accuser , Vulg.…

falsĭmōnĭa.opening: falsus, from fallo , a trick , imposition : quos cum censeas Esse amicos, reperiuntur falsi falsimoniis, Plaut. Bacch. 3, 6, 12 .

falsĭ-părens.opening: adj. falsus , that has a pretended father : Amphitryoniades, i. e. Hercules, as only the reputed son of Amphitryo, Cat. 68, 112 .

falsĭtas.opening: id. , falsehood , falsity (post-class.), Lact. 5, 3, 23 (opp. verum); Amm. 15, 5, 12 ; Arn. 1, 33 ; Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 4, 65 ; Isid. 1, 20, 3 .— Plur. , Arn. 1, 56 ; 7, 49 .

falso.opening: adv. , v. fallo, P. a. fin. 1.

falsus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from fallo.

falx.opening: perh. akin to flecto , a sickle , reaping-hook , a pruning-hook , scythe. Prop., Cato, R. R. 10, 3 ; 11, 4 ; Varr. R. R. 1, 22, 5 ; Cic. Tusc. 5, 23, 65 ; id. Mil. 33, 91 ; Verg. G. 1, 348 : Ov. F. 4, 914 ; Hor. C. 1,…

fāma.opening: for, fa-ri , = φήμη , the talk of the multitude , like rumor, either as relating or as judging (v. rumor; cf. also: nomen, gloria, laudatio; clamor, plausus; honos, dignitas, honestas, laus, etc.). That which people say…

fāmātus.opening: adj. fama, II. B. 2. , in bad odor , notorious , disreputable : quibus criminibus haec causa famata est, Cic. Scaur. 13 dub. (al., ex conject., diffamata): tonsor Licinus, Schol. Cruq. ad Hor. A. P. 301 .

fămēlĭco.opening: v. a. famelicus , to make hungry , cause to famish : non famelicas sed reficis, Pseud. August. ad Fratr. Erem. Serm. 10 .

fămēlĭcus.opening: adj. fames , suffering from hunger , famished , starved (mostly ante- and post-class.; not in Cic.): lassus et famelicus, Plaut. Cas. 1, 42 : famelica hominum natio, id. Rud. 2, 2, 6 : ales, with rapacissima, Plin. 10,…

fāmella.opening: dim. a fama, Paul. ex Fest. p. 87, 17 Müll.

fămes.opening: (ante- and post-class. nom. sing. : famis, Varr. R. R. 2, 5, 15 ; Prud. Psych. 479 ; gen. : fami, Cato and Lucil. ap. Gell. 9, 14, 10 ; abl. , scanned fămē, Lucr. 3, 732 ; Verg. A. 6, 421 ; Ov. M. 5, 165 ; 8, 846 ; 11,…

fămescens.opening: Part. [fames], suffering hunger , hungering : ora famescentum ferarum, Alcim. Avit. ad Sor. 738 .

famex.opening: a bruise , contusion , Col. 6, 12, 2 Schneid. N cr.; Veg. Vet. 4, 19 ; cf. famex, θλάσμα , Gloss. Philox.

fāmĭgĕrābĭlis.opening: adj. fama-gero , famous , celebrated (ante- and post-class.), Varr. L. L. 6, § 55 Müll.: spectaculum, App. M. 1, p. 105, 16 : provincia, id. ib. 2 , p. 124, 5.

fāmĭgĕrātĭo.opening: famigeratus .— Prop., tale-bearing. —Hence, concr., a report , rumor : haec famigeratio Te honestet, Plaut. Trin. 3, 2, 66 .

fāmĭgĕrātor.opening: id. , a talebearer , Plaut. Trin. 1, 2, 178 and 182.

fāmĭgĕrātus.opening: Part. [famigero], famed , celebrated (post-Aug. and very rare): Crete multis famigerata fabulis, Mel. 2, 7, 12 : famigeratum antiquitus fanum, App. Flor p. 350, 32 .—Cf. the foll. art.

fāmĭgĕro.opening: διαφημίξω , Gloss. Philox. [fama-gero; cf. also the preced. art.].

fămĭlĭa.opening: (with pater, mater, filius, and filia, the class. gen. sing. is usually in the archaic form familias; familiae also occurs, v. infra ; gen. : familiai, Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 203 ; with the plur. of these words both the sing.…

fămĭlĭāresco.opening: v. inch. n. [familiaris], to grow familiar or intimate , Sid. Ep. 7, 2 .

fămĭlĭārĭcus.opening: adj. id. . Of or belonging to the house-servants or domestics : cellae, rooms for the servants, Vitr. 6, 10 : familiarica vestimenta sunt, quae ad familiam vestiendam parata sunt, sicuti saga, tunicae, paenulae, etc.,…

fămĭlĭāris.opening: ( abl. sing. regularly familiari; familiare, Varr. and P. Rutil. ap. Charis. p. 105 P.), adj. familia . Of or belonging to servants (rare; only as subst. ): , , , a servant : majores nostri servos (quod etiam in mimis…

fămĭlĭārĭtas.opening: familiaris, II. B. I. , familiarity , intimacy , familiar intercourse , friendship , intimate acquaintance. Prop. (freq. and class.; in sing. and plur. ; syn.: amicitia, necessitudo, notitia): familiaritas tanta nullo…

fămĭlĭŏla.opening: dim. familia , a little family (late Lat.), Hier. Ep. 108, 2 .

fāmōsĭtas.opening: famosus , ill fame , infamy , ignominy (post-class. and rare), Tert. Spect. 23 .

fāmōsus.opening: adj. fama , much talked of (well or ill), i. e. famed , celebrated. In a good sense, famous , renowned (not ante-Aug.): famosae mortis amorem amor, Hor. A. P. 469 : mors Junii Blaesi, Tac. H. 3, 38 : vir secundis…

fămŭlābundus.opening: adj. famulor , that serves zealously , serviceable , Tert. adv. Marc. 3, 7 .

fămŭlanter.opening: adv. , servilely , slavishly , etc., v. famulor fin.

fămŭlāris.opening: adj. famulus , of or belonging to servants or slaves (rare but class.): vestis, * Cic. Tusc. 1, 48, 116 : turba, Stat. Ach. 2, 67 : jugum, Sen. Troad. 747 : jura, i. e. of subjugation, Ov. M. 15, 597 : hederae, the…

fămŭlātĭo.opening: famulor , a body of domestics , household (post-class.), App. M. 2, p. 115, 10 ; 6 , p. 176, 20.

fămŭlātōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , servile , slavish (post-class.): mendicitas, Tert. ad Nat. 2, 14 ; id. de Anim. 33 ; Ambros. de Fid. 5, 5, 58 .—Hence, adv. : , slavishly , Cassiod. Amic. 5, 5 .

fămŭlātrix.opening: id. , that serves; subst. , a female servant , handmaid (postclass.): penna, Sid. Carm. 2, 128 : coquina medicinae famulatrix est, Don. ad Ter. And. 1, 1, 3 .

fămŭlātus.opening: famulor , servitude , slavery (rare but class.): in famulatu esse, Cic. Lael. 19, 70 : quam miser virtutis famulatus servientis voluptati! id. Off. 3, 33, 117 : gravis, Sen. Hippol. 991 : in famulatum subeunte natura,…

fămŭlĭtas.opening: famulus , a serving , servitude (ante-class.), Att. ap. Non. 109, 28 ; Pac. ib. 29 .

fămŭlĭtĭum.opening: id. (ante- and post-class.). Abstr., servitude , slavery : famulitium (al. famuletium) dicebatur, quod nunc servitium, Paul. ex Fest. p. 87, 3 Müll.— Concr., the servants or slaves of a household : unus e famulitio,…

fămŭlo.opening: v. a. id. , to use as a servant , to make serviceable (post-class.): elementa ipsa (Christus), Tert. Apol. 21 .

fămŭlor.opening: v. dep. n. [id.], to be a servant , to serve , attend , wait upon. Prop. (rare but class.): cum autem hi famulantur (with alterius esse and opp. sui esse), Cic. Fragm. ap. Non. 109, 6 (Rep. 3, 25 ed. Mai. et Mos.):…

fămŭlus.opening: adj. 1. famulus , serving , serviceable , servile ( poet. ; perh. not ante-Aug.): aquae, Ov. F. 1, 286 : turbae, Sil. 13, 360 : dextrae, Luc. 4, 207 : manus, Sil. 10, 647 : artus, Val. Fl. 1, 749 : vertex, Ov. Pont. 2,…

fānātĭcē.opening: adv. , enthusiastically , franticly , v. fanaticus fin.

fānātĭcus.opening: adj. 1. fanum . Pertaining to a temple : PECVNIA, Inscr. Veron. ap. Bull. Dell' Inst. 1836, p. 141 ; cf. Borghesi, ib.— Inspired by a divinity, enthusiastic. Lit. : ut fanaticus, oestro Percussus, Bellona, tuo, Juv. 4,…

fānĭtālis.opening: adj. 1. fanum , pertaining to a temple , Inscr. Guarin. Comment. XII. p. 28.

Fannĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens : 1. C. Fannius Strabo, son-in-law of Laelius , introduced as a speaker by Cicero in de Rep. and Lael.; 2. His son of the same name , who was consul A. U.C. 632, Cic. Brut. 26, 99 sq. ; id. de…

fāno.opening: v. a. fanum , to dedicate , consecrate : quod sacrificio quodam fanatur, id est ut fani lege sit, Varr. L. L. 6, § 54 .

fānŭlum.opening: dim. id. , a small temple , acc. to Paul. ex Fest. p. 103, 7 Müll.

fānum.opening: fari; cf. Varr. L. L. 6, § 54 Müll.; Paul. ex Fest. p. 88, 1, and 93, 17 Müll.; Cic. Div. 1, 41, 90 , a place dedicated to some deity by forms of consecration , a sanctuary , temple (syn.: templum, aedes, delubrum,…

Fanum.opening: a city in Umbria , on the Adriatic Sea , with a celebrated temple of Fortuna , now Fano , Caes. B. C. 1, 11 fin. ; called also Fanum Fortunae, Plin. 3, 14, 19, § 113 ; Tac. H. 3, 50 ; Inscr. Orell. 83 and 84; and…

far.opening: akin with frico, q. v. , a sort of grain , spelt , Gr. ζέα , Triticum spelta, Linn. Prop., the earliest food of the Romans , both roasted and ground into meal , Cato, R. R. 2, 4 ; Varr. R. R. 1, 63 ; 1, 2, 6 ; Col. 2,…

farcīmen.opening: farcio , a sausage (ante- and post-class.): a fartura farcimina in extis appellata, Varr. L. L. 5, § 111 Müll.; cf. Isid. Orig. 20, 2 ; Gell. 16, 7, 11 ; Arn. 7, 229 .

farcīmĭnōsus.opening: adj. farciminum , of or belonging to a disease called farciminum: morbus, Veg. Vet. 1, 14 ; cf. id. 1, 7 .

farcīmĭnum.opening: farcio , a disease in horses and other animals , perh. costiveness , Veg. Vet. 1, 7 .

farcĭno.opening: v. a. id. , to stuff; trop. (late Lat.): fandis tacenda farcinat, i. e. mixes, Mart. Cap. 9, § 998 .

farcĭo.opening: (post-class. form farsum, Petr. 69 ; Apic. 4, 2 ; 8, 8 ; and farcītum, Cassiod. Inst. Div. Litt. 22 ), , v. a. Gr. φρακ-, φράσσω, to shut in; cf. Lat. frequens; Germ. Berg, Burg , to stuff , cram , fill full (class.).…

farēdo.opening: a kind of abscess , Plin. Val. 3, 22 .

farfărus.opening: the plant colt's-foot , called also farfugium and chamaeleuce: tussilago, Linn.; Plin. 24, 15, 85, § 135 .— Also in the form , Plaut. Poen. 2, 1, 32 ; Paul. ex Fest. p. 88, 13 Müll. N. cr.

fărīna.opening: far , ground corn , meal , flour. Prop., Plin. 18, 9, 20, § 88 ; Varr. R. R. 2, 5, 17 ; Plin. 20, 13, 51, § 139 ; 22, 25, 67, § 137 .—Prov.: facis farinam, i. e. waste, scatter, Mart. 8, 16, 5 ; Vulg. Matt. 13, 33 .—…

fărīnārĭus.opening: adj. farina , of or belonging to meal , meal- : cribrum, Cato, R. R. 76, 3 ; Plin. 18, 11, 29, § 115 .

fărīnōsus.opening: adj. id. , of meal , mealy : congeries, Veg. Vet. 2, 30 .

fărīnŭla.opening: dim. id. , a little meal (late Lat.), Vulg. Reg. 1, 17, 13 .

fărīnŭlentus.opening: adj. id. , mealy : cinis, App. M. 9, p. 222, 33 .

fărĭo.opening: a salmon-trout , Aus. Mos. 130 ; cf. Isid. Orig. 12, 6 .

fārĭor.opening: v. dep. a. [for], to speak : NI TESTIMONIVM FARIATVR, Fragm. XII. Tab ap. Gell. 15, 13 fin.

farnĕus.opening: adj. farnus , of the ashtree : fungi, Apic. 7, 13 (al. faginei).

farnus.opening: perh. for franus, contr. from fraxinus , an ash , ash-tree , Vitr. 7, 1 dub. (al. fraxinus); cf. Pall. 1, 9, 3 .

farrācĕus.opening: or , , adj. far , of spelt : seges, Varr. R. R. 1, 31, 5 : pollen, Plin. 24, 7, 22, § 39 .

farrāgo.opening: id. , mixed fodder for cattle , mash. Prop.: farrago appellatur id, quod ex pluribus satis pabuli causa datur jumentis, Paul. ex Fest. p. 91, 14 Müll.; Varr. R. R. 1, 31, 5 ; Plin. 18, 16, 41, § 142 ; Verg. G. 3, 205 ;…

farrārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to spelt , and in gen. to corn or grain. Adj. : fistula, a sort of hand-mill for corn, Cato, R. R. 10, 3 ; cf. Plin. 18, 10, 23, § 97 .— In plur. subst. : , , , a granary , hay-loft , Vitr. 6,…

farrātus.opening: adj. id. . Filled with corn : olla, Pers. 4, 31 .— Made of corn : omnia, preparations of meal, Juv. 11, 109 .

farrĕārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to grain : pilum, Cato, R. R. 10, 5 .

farrĕātĭo.opening: id. , the use of speltbread in marrying (for the more usu. confarreatio, q. v.), Serv. Verg. A. 4, 374 .

farrĕātus.opening: , adj. [id.], made with the use of spelt-bread : nuptiae (i. e. confarreatio), Serv. Verg. A. 4, 104 .

farrĕus.opening: adj. id. , made of spelt , or in gen. of corn or grain : far. vel triticeus panis, Col. 7, 12, 10 : spicum, an ear of corn , Paul. ex Fest. p. 280, 9 Müll.— Subst. : , , (sc. libum), a speltcake , Plin. 18, 3, 3, § 10 .

farrĭcŭlum.opening: dim. farreum , a small spelt-cake , Pall. Oct. 21 init.

farsĭlis.opening: adj. farcio , crammed , fattened : porcellus, Apic. 8, 7 ; cf. fartilis.

farsūra.opening: id. , a fattening , Varr. R. R. 3, 9, 1 (al. assura); Tert. adv. Val. 27 ; cf. fartura.

fartĭcŭla.opening: dim. fartum , a little stuffing , Titin. ap. Non. 331, 27 .

fartĭlis.opening: adj. farcio , stuffed , crammed. Lit. : anseres, Plin. 10, 22, 27, § 52 : asinus, App. M. 3, p. 187, 6 .— Trop. , in neutr. plur. absol. : fartilia, stuffing, mixture, Tert. adv. Val. 27 .

fartim.opening: adv. id. , by stuffing or cramming; hence, closely , densely (post-class.): tectum omne fartim stipaverant, App. M. 3, p. 130, 12 : isicium fartim concisum, i. e. cut up fine as if for stuffing, id. ib. 2 , p. 117, 30.

fartor.opening: id. . A stuffer , fattener of fowls , poulterer : pinguem quoque facere gallinam quamquam fartoris non rustici sit officium, Col. 8, 7, 1 ; Inscr. Grut. 580, 15 ; Inscr. Rein. cl. 9, no. 12: cuppedinarii omnes, cetarii,…

fartūra.opening: (also ), , farcio . A cramming , fattening of fowls, Varr. R. R. 3, 8, 3 ; Col. 8, 9, 1 ; 8, 7 fin. — The filling up , rubble , of a wall, Vitr. 2, 8 med.

fartus.opening: ( ), , farcio , stuffing , for the usual fartum (v. farcio fin. ), Arn. 7, 231 .

fas.opening: root fa-, cf. for; Gr. φημί, φά-ναι Orig. belonging to the relig. lang., the dictates of religion , divine law; opp. to jus, or human law (rare; cf. also: aequitas, justitia): jus ac fas omne delere, Cic. Att. 1, 16, 6…

fascĭa.opening: ( ), , kindred with fascis , a band , bandage , swathe , girth , fillet. Prop. (to bind up diseased parts of the body; to wrap round the feet to prevent the boots from rubbing them; to bind under the breasts of women; a…

fascĭātim.opening: ( ), adv. fascis , in bundles , acc. to Quint. 1, 4, 20 , one of a class of adverbs which some grammarians improperly regard as a distinct part of speech.

fascĭcŭlārĭa.opening: fasciculus , things carried in bundles (as wood, hay, etc.), Veg. Mil. 2, 19 fin.

fascĭcŭlus.opening: dim. fascis , a small bundle , packet (class.): epistolarum, Cic. Q. Fr. 2, 12, 4 ; so of packets of letters, id. Att. 2, 13, 1 ; 5, 11, 7 ; 12, 53 : librorum, Hor. Ep. 1, 13, 12 : fasciculum ad nares admovebis? a bunch…

fascĭger.opening: adj. fascis-gero , bearing the fasces : honor, i. e. the consulship, Paul. Nol. 321 .

fascīna.opening: fascis , a bundle of sticks , fagot , Cato, R. R. 37, 5 .

fascĭnātĭo.opening: fascino , an enchanting , bewitching , witchcraft , Plin. 28, 4, 7, § 35 ; 28, 8, 27, § 101 ; Vulg. Sap. 4, 12 .

fascĭnātor.opening: id. , an enchanter , Primas. in Ep. ad Galat. c. 3: fascinator, βάσκανος , Gloss. Vet.

fascĭnātōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to enchantment or witchcraft : lingua, Serv. Verg. E. 7, 28 .

fascĭno.opening: v. a. cf. Gr. βάσκανος, βασκαίνω, v. fascinum , to enchant , bewitch , charm , fascinate by the eyes or the tongue: nescio quis teneros oculus mihi fascinat agnos, Verg. E. 3, 103 : malā linguā, Cat. 7, 12 : contra…

fascĭnōsus.opening: adj. fascinum , with a large fascinum: poëta fascinosior, Auct. Priap. 79 fin.

fascĭnum.opening: ( , , ) [quasi bascanum, βάσκανον , Cloat. Ver. ap. Gell. 16, 12, 4 ; but cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 88, 16 ]. A bewitching , witchcraft , Plin. 26, 10, 62, § 96 ; Symm. Ep. 1, 7 .— Transf. I. q. membrum virile (because an…

fascĭo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. fascia , to envelop with bands , to swathe (post-Aug. and very rare): fasciato trunco, Mart. 12, 57, 12 ; Capitol. Anton. 13 .— Pass. , Vulg. Ezech. 30, 21 .

fascĭŏla.opening: ( ), , dim. id. , a small bandage for the legs , Varr. L. L. 5, § 130 ; Hor. S. 2, 3, 255 ; Vop. Aur. 4 ; Cic. Har. Resp. 21, 44 .

fascis.opening: cf. φάκελος, fascia, but v fido , a bundle of wood, twigs, straw, reeds, etc. A fagot , fascine; a packet , parcel. In gen. (rare): fasces stramentorum ac virgultorum, Hirt. B. G. 8, 15, 6 : lignorum, Tac. A. 13, 35 :…

fastīdĭbĭlis.opening: adj. fastidio ; act. , nauseous , loathsome , disagreeable (postclass. and very rare): judicia, Tert. Anim. 33 fin.

fastīdĭenter.opening: adv. , disdainfully , scornfully; v. fastidio fin.

fastīdĭlĭter.opening: adv. fastidio , with disgust : Varr. ap. Non. 112, 11 .

fastīdĭo.grammar: īvi, or ĭi, ītum, 4 v. n. and a.
fastīdĭo.opening: v. n. and a. [fastidium], to feel disgust , loathing , or nausea , to shrink or flinch from any thing unpleasant to the taste, smell, hearing, etc.; to loathe , dislike , despise (not freq. till after the Aug. per.;…

fastīdĭōsus.opening: adj. fastidium , full of disgust or aversion. Pass. , that feels disgust , squeamish , disdainful , scornful , fastidious (class.). Lit. : vaccae fastidiosae fiunt, Varr. R. R. 2, 5, 15 : aurium sensus fastidiosissimus,…

fastīdĭtas.opening: , i. q. fastidium, a loathing , aversion , Cassiod. Var. 7, 1 fin.

fastīdĭum.opening: cf. 2. fastus , a loathing , aversion for any thing, esp. for any sort of enjoyment (very freq. and class.; cf. taedium, nausea, etc.). Lit. , nausea , squeamishness , loathing , distaste for food: cibi satietas et…

fastīgātĭo.opening: fastigo , a sharpening to a point , pointing (post-Aug. and very rare): ut fastigatio laevi descendat cuneo, Plin. 17, 14, 24, § 106 : recta, App. Flor. 2, 364 .

fastīgĭum.opening: cf. Sanscr. bhrshtīs, corner, rim; Gr. ἄ-φλαστον, aplustria, the ornamented stern of a ship; O. H. Germ. brort, the prow , the top of a gable , a gable end , pediment (syn.: cacumen, culmen, vertex, apex). Prop.:…

fastīgo.opening: v. a. v. fastigium , to make pointed , to sharpen to a point , to raise or bring to a point (in the verb. finit. only post-Aug., not in Cic.). Lit. : frumenta verno tempore fastigantur in stipulam, grow up into a straw…

fastōsus.opening: adj. 2. fastus , full of pride , proud , haughty (post-Aug. and rare): moecha, Mart. 10, 13, 7 : quid est, fastose? Petr. 131 .— Transf. , of things: domus, Auct. Pan. ad Pis. 107: garum, Mart. 13, 102, 2 .

firmātor.opening: firmo , a confirmer , establisher (post-Aug. and very rare): missus Drusus paci firmator (so acc. to Cod. Med., not pacis), Tac. A. 2, 46 : disciplinae militaris, Plin. Ep. 10, 38, 1 .

Firmĭcus.opening: , Julius F. Maternus, a Roman mathematician in the time of Constantine the Great , author of a work entitled Matheseos libri octo; cf. Bernhardy, Rom. Lit. pp. 645, 648.

firmĭtas.opening: firmus , firmness , durability , strength (class.; syn.: constantia, firmitudo, perseverantia). Lit. : ea, quae ille (Epicurus) propter firmitatem στερέμνια appellat, Cic. N. D. 1, 19, 49 : age specta, postes cujusmodi!…

firmĭtūdo.opening: firmus , firmness , durability , strength (less freq. than firmitas, but class.). Lit. : tanta in eis (navibus) erat firmitudo, Caes. B. G. 3, 13, 8 ; cf.: tanta erat operis (i. e. pontis) firmitudo, id. ib. 4, 17, 7 :…

Firmĭus.opening: a Roman proper name , e. g. Firmius Catus, Tac. A. 2, 27 ; 4, 31 .— Hence, , , adj. , of Firmius , an unknown silver-worker of that name: Firmiana vasa, Plin. 33, 11, 49, § 139 (Jan. Furniana).

firmo.opening: v. a. firmus , to make firm or fast , to strengthen , fortify , support (freq. and class.). Lit. : lacertos, Lucr. 6, 397 : corpora juvenum firmari labore voluerunt, Cic. Tusc. 2, 15, 36 : corpora cibo, Liv. 27, 13 fin.…

Firmum.opening: a fortified sea-port of Picenum , now Fermo , Mel. 2, 4, 6 ; Vell. 1, 14, 8 ; Pompei. ap. Cic. Att. 8, 12 , B. 1.— Deriv.: , , adj. , of or belonging to Firmum , Firmian : cohors, Liv. 44, 40 : L. Tarutius Firmanus, of…

firmus.opening: adj. Sanscr. dhar-, dharā-mi, hold, support; Gr. θρᾶ-, θρή-σασθαι, to sit down, θρῆνυς, θρόνος; cf.: frētus, frēnum , firm (in opp. to frail, destructible), steadfast , stable , strong , powerful (freq. and class.; esp.…

fiscālis.opening: adj. fiscus, II. B. , of or relating to the public or the imperial treasury , fiscal (post-class.): res fiscales quasi propriae et privatae principis sunt, Dig. 43, 8, 2, § 4 : jus, ib. 2, 14, 42 : debitores, ib. 49,…

fiscārĭus.opening: id. , a debtor to the treasury (post-class.): annuae fiscariorum praestationes, Firm. Math. 3, 13 med.

fiscella.opening: (also , , , Col. 12, 38, 6 , v. fiscellus), dim. fiscina , a small basket for fruit , cheese-forms , etc., woven of slender twigs , rushes , etc. (syn.: fscina, qualus, canistrum, calathus, sporta, corbis), Tib. 2, 3,…

fiscellus.opening: dim. fiscina . I. q. fiscella, q. v.— FISCELLUS casei mollis appetitor, ut catillones catillorum liguritores, Paul. ex Fest. p. 90, 2 (acc. to Müll. we should perh. read FISCELLO; see his note ad loc.).

Fiscellus.opening: a chain of mountains in the Sabine territory , in which the river Nar takes its rise , now called Monte Fiscello or Monti della Sibilla , Plin. 3, 12, 17, § 109 ; Varr. R. R. 2, 1, 5 ; Sil. 8, 519 .

fiscĭna.opening: fiscus , a small basket for fruit , wine , etc., made of slender twigs , rushes , broom , etc. (for syn. v. fiscella), Plaut. Merc. 5, 4, 29 : ficorum, Cic. Fl. 17, 41 ; Naev. ap. Serv. Verg. G. 1, 266 ; Verg. l. l.;…

fiscus.opening: a basket or frail woven of slender twigs , rushes , etc. (like fiscina, fiscella, q. v.); used, For olives in the oilpress, Col. 12, 52, 22 ; 54, 2 .—Far more freq., For keeping money in, a money-basket , or, as we say,…

fissĭcŭlo.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. fissum, from findo , in the lang. of the haruspices, to divide the entrails (post - class.): extis fissiculandis, App. de Deo Socr. p. 45 ; Mart. Cap. 2, § 151 ; and: fissiculatis extorum prosiciis,…

fissĭlis.opening: adj. findo . That may be cleft or split , fissile (rare; not in Cic. or Caes.): robur, Verg. A. 6, 181 ; lignum, id. G. 1, 144 ; Plin. 16, 39, 73, § 187 : arundo, id. 16, 36, 64, § 157 : vena lapidis, id. 36, 17, 27, §…

fissĭo.opening: id. , a cleaving , dividing : glebarum, Cic. N. D. 2, 63, 159 .

fissĭ-pes.opening: adj. fissus, from findo , cloven-footed. Lit. : juvencae, Aus. Ep. 5, 3 .— Transf. , in gen., split : calamus, a pen for writing, Aus. Ep. 7, 49 .

fissūra.opening: findo ; a cleft , chink , fissure (post-Aug.): quorum in digitos pedum fissura divisa est, Plin. 10, 63, 83, § 176 : vitis, Col. 4, 29, 4 .—In plur. , Plin. 33, 6, 33, § 101 : efficax asini sevum labrorum fissuris,…

fistella.opening: dim. fistula , a little pipe , Pelagon. Art. Vet. 24.

fistūca.opening: an instrument for ramming down , a rammer , beetle , Caes. B. G. 4, 17, 4 ; Cato, R. R. 28, 2 ; Plin. 36, 25, 61, § 185 .

fistūcātĭo.opening: fistuco , a ramming down , ramming fast , Vitr. 7, 1 ; 10, 3 .

fistūco.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. fistuca , to ram down or in , to ram fast : fundamenta, Cato, R. R. 18, 7 : solum, Plin. 36, 25, 63, § 188 ; Vitr. 7, 4 fin. : rudus pedali crassitudine, Plin. 36, 25, 62, § 186 .—In the part. perf.…

fistŭla.opening: findo, fis-sum . In gen., a pipe , tube , e. g. a water-pipe (usually of lead; syn.: tubus, canalis, sypho), Cic. Rab. Perd. 11, 31 ; Front. Aquaed. 25 sq. ; Plin. 2, 103, 106, § 224 ; 31, 6, 31, § 58 ; Ov. M. 4, 122 ;…

fistŭlāris.opening: adj. fistula (post-class.). (Acc. to fistula, II. A. 2. a.) Like a shepherd's pipe : versus, which gradually increase by a syllable, Diom. p. 498 P.— (Acc. to fistula, II. B.) Of or for a fistula : medicamentum, Veg.…

fistŭlārĭus.opening: id. , a player on the shepherd's pipe , a piper (in Cic. fistulator), Inscr. Fabr. p. 625 , no. 218.

fistŭlātim.opening: adv. id. , in the shape of pipes (post-class.): excussus fimus, App. M. 4, p. 144, 4 .

fistŭlātor.opening: id. , a player on the shepherd's pipe , a piper : fistulatorem domi relinquetis, Cic. de Or. 3, 61, 227 (see the passage in connection); Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 1, 22 .

fistŭlātōrĭus.opening: adj. fistulator , of or belonging to a player on the pipes : artes, Arn. 2, 73 .

fistŭlātus.opening: adj. fistula (postAug.). Furnished with pipes : tabulae, Suet. Ner. 31 Oud. N. cr. — Pipe-shaped : venae, Arn. 2, 84 : aera, Sid. Ep. 9, 13 Carm. 4.

fistŭlesco.opening: v. inch. n. [id.], to become full of holes (late Lat.): ligna fistulescunt, Fulg. Myth. 2, 19 .

fistŭlōsus.opening: adj. id. . Pipeshaped , full of holes , porous (post-Aug.): terra bibula et pumicis vice fistulosa, Plin. 18, 11, 29, § 110 ; so, terra, id. 17, 5, 3, § 34 : telum culicis sorbendo fistulosum, hollow, id. 11, 2, 1, § 3…

fitilla.opening: or , , , a gruel used at sacrifices , Sen. Ben. 1, 6, 3 Fickert N. cr.; Plin. 18, 8, 19, § 84 ; Arn. 2, 58 ; 7, 230 .

fivere.opening: (apud Catonem) pro figere, Paul. ex Fest. p. 92, 8 Müll.

fixē.opening: adv. , v. figo, P. a. fin.

fixūra.opening: figo , a fastening , driving in of nails (post-class.), Tert. adv. Gnost. 1 med.; the print of nails , Vulg. Johann. 20, 25 .

fixus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from figo.

flābellĭfĕra.opening: flabellum-fero , a fan-bearer , a female slave, Plaut. Trin. 2, 1, 22 .

flābello.opening: v. a. flabellum , to fan (post-Aug.): cum calor in affectationem flabellatur, Tert. Pall. 4 .

flābellŭlum.opening: dim. id. , a little fan , Ter. Eun. 3, 5, 50 (Bentl., Fleck., Umpfenb.; dub.; al. flabellum).

flābellum.opening: dim. flabrum , a smali fan or fly-flap. Lit. : cape hoc flabellum, et ventulum huic sic facito, Ter. Eun. 3, 5, 47 ; 50 ; Mart. 3, 82, 10 ; for this a peacock's tail was used, Prop. 2, 24 (3, 18), 11; Hier. Ep. 27, 13…

flābĭlis.opening: adj. flo , airy. * Lit. : nihil est in animis mixtum atque concretum ... nihil ne aut humidum quidem aut flabile aut igneum, Cic. Tusc. 1, 27, 66 .— Trop. , spiritual (eccl. Lat.): aedes, Prud. στεφ . 10, 347 al.

flābra.opening: id. , blasts , esp. of wind; or, concr., breezes , winds ( poet. ): flabraque ventorum violento turbine vexant, Lucr. 5, 217 : Etesia Aquilonum, id. 5, 742 ; 6, 730 : Boreae, Prop. 2, 27, 12 (3, 23, 12 M.): lenia…

flābrālis.opening: adj. flabra , breezy , airy (post-class.): frigus, Prud. Apoth. 841 .

flaccĕo.opening: v. n. flaccus , to be flabby or flaccid. Lit. (post-class.): aures pendulae atque flaccentes, Lact. Opif. D. 8, 8 . — Trop. , to be faint , languid , weak; to flag , droop : flaccet, languet, deficit, Non. 110, 10…

flaccesco.opening: (ante-class. also ), , v. inch. n. , to wilt , wither , dry up (cf. tabesco). Lit. : faeniculum cum legeris, sub tecto exponito, dum flaccescat, Col. 12, 7, 4 : flaccescente fronde, Vitr. 2, 9, 2 : stercus cum flaccuit,…

flaccĭdus.opening: adj. flaccus , flabby , flaccid , pendulous (cf. marcidus). Lit. : aures, Col. 7, 6, 2 ; Plin. 8, 51, 77, § 205 : folium, id. 15, 30, 39, § 127 : vela (with pendula), App. Flor. p. 365 .— Trop. , languid , feeble :…

flaccus.opening: adj. etym. dub. , flabby , hanging down. Lit. : auriculae, Varr. R. R. 2, 9, 4 .— Transf. , of persons, flap-eared : ecquos deos paetulos esse arbitramur? ecquos silos, flaccos, frontones, capitones, quae sunt in nobis?…

Flaccus.opening: a Roman surname; cf.: aures homini tantum immobiles: ab iis Flaccorum cognomina, Plin. 11, 37, 50, § 136 ; esp. freq. in the gens Valeria, Cornelia, and Horatia; e. g. si quid in Flacco viri est, i. e. in Q. Horatio,…

flăgellātīcĭus.opening: = μαστιγίας , Gloss. Philox., one who deserves the whip , verbero.

flăgellātĭo.opening: flagello , a whipping , scourging , flagellation (eccl. Lat.), Tert. ad Martyr. 4 fin.

flăgello.opening: v. a. flagellum , to whip , scourge , lash ( poet. and in postAug. prose). Lit. : quaestorem suum in conjuratione nominatum flagellavit, Suet. Calig. 26 : aliquem manu sua, id. ib. 55 ; id. Claud. 38 : canes extremis…

flăgellum.opening: dim. flagrum , a whip , scourge; more severe than scutica. (Cf. also: flagrum, verber, lorum.) Lit. : nec scuticā dignum horribili sectere flagello, Hor. S. 1, 3, 119 ; cf.: ille flagellis Ad mortem caesus, id. ib. 1,…

flāgĭtātĭo.opening: flagito , an earnest request or demand , importunity (rare but class.): nolui deesse ne tacitae quidem flagitationi tuae, * Cic. Top. 1, 5 : uxorum flagitatione revocantur, Just. 2, 4 .—In plur. : crebrae populi…

flāgĭtātor.opening: id. , an importunate asker , demander , dun (rare but class.): eicite ex animo curam atque alienum aes: Ne quis formidet flagitatorem suum, Plaut. Cas. prol. 24 ; cf. id. Most. 3, 2, 81 ; so of a dunning creditor ,…

flāgĭtātrix.opening: flagitator , she that importunately demands or duns (late Lat.): epistola vehemens flagitatrix, Aug. Ep. 140 .

flāgĭtĭōsus.opening: adj. flagitium , shameful , disgraceful , infamous , flagitious , profligate , dissolute (both of persons and things): flagitiosi sunt, qui venereas voluptates inflammato animo concupiscunt, Cic. Tusc. 4, 32, 68 : homo…

flāgĭtĭum.opening: flagito; cf. Doed. Syn. 2, p. 143; Corss. Ausspr. 1, 398 sq.; orig., burning desire, heat of passion . Lit. , an eager or furious demand , importunity , urgency (post-Aug. and rare; cf. flagitatio): Lentulus credebatur…

flāgĭto.opening: (archaic inf. pres. pass. flagitarier, Plaut. Men. prol. 48 ), v. freq. a. [from the root bherag-; Sanscr. bhraj-, to roast; Zend. berja, earnest longing; cf. Gr. φρύγω ; Lat. frīgĕre, frictum, Fick, Vergl. Wört. p. 141…

flā^grans.opening: Part. and P. a. , from flagro.

flā^granter.opening: adv. , v. flagro, P. a. fin.

flā^grantĭa.opening: flagro , a burning , a glowing heat , ardor (mostly post-class.). Lit. : montis (Aetnae), Gell. 17, 10, 8 : solis, App. M. 4, p. 157 ; 6 , p. 178: aestatis, Arn. 2, p. 69 : aestiva, the heat of summer, Mart. Cap. 8, p.…

flagrātōres.grammar: dicebantur genus hominum, quod mercede flagris caedebantur
flagrātōres.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 89, 5 Müll.; cf.: † flagratores qui flagris conducti caedunt, Placid. p. 463 .

flā^grĭfer.opening: adj. flagrum + fero , bearing a whip : Automedon, Aus. Ep. 14, 10 .

flagrĭōnes.opening: , quod flagris subjecti sunt: ut verberones a verberibus. Afranius in Vopisco: Tu flagrionibus, etc., Non. 28, 29 (Com. Rel. v. 391 ed. Rib.).

flā^grī^trĭba.opening: flagrum + tero , a whip-spoiler , i. e. one who wears out the whip with being flogged , a comic appellative of a slave, Plaut. Ps. 1, 2, 5 .

flā^gro.opening: v. n. root in Sanscr. brag-, to glow; Gr. φλέγω, φλεγέθω, φλόξ; Lat. fulgeo, fulgur, fulmen, flamma, flamen, fulvus; Angl.-Sax. blāc, pale; Germ. bleich; connected with flagito, flagitium, etc., by Corss. Ausspr. 1, 398…

flā^grum.opening: cf.: fligo, af-fligo, etc. and flagellum , a whip , scourge , lash (syn.: verber, scutica, flagellum). Lit. , Plaut. Am. 4, 2, 10 ; id. Cas. 1, 35 ; id. Merc. 2, 3, 81 ; Liv. 28, 11, 6 ; Suet. Oth. 2 ; Juv. 5, 173 ;…

flāmen.opening: flo , = πνεῦμα , a blowing , blast , esp. of wind ( poet. , most freq. in the plur. ; cf.: ventus, flatus, flabra, spiritus, aura). Lit. : cur Berecynthiae Cessant flamina tibiae? Hor. C. 3, 19, 19 ; Nemes. Ecl. 1, 16 :…

Flāmen.opening: a surname in the gens Claudia, Liv. 27, 21, 5 .

flāmentum.opening: flo , a blowing of the wind: tempestatum, Fulg. Myth. 1 praef.

flāmĭna.opening: 1. flamen , the wife of a flamen , usu. flaminica, Inscr. Grut. 459, 9 .

flāmĭnālis.opening: id. , one who has been a flamen , Inscr. Orell. 3932 .—In apposition: FLAMINALES VIRI, Inscr. Orell. 155 .

flāmĭnātus.opening: id. , the office of flamen , Inscr. Orell. 3281 ; 3978 .

flāmĭnĭca.opening: 1. flamen , the wife of a flamen , who assisted at the sacrifices: Ov. F. 2, 27 ; Tert. Exhort. ad Cast. 13 ; Inscr. Orell. 2225 sq. : flaminicae Diales, Massur. Sabin. ap. Gell. 10, 15, 26 : Dialis, Tac. A. 4, 16 ;…

Flāmĭnīnus.opening: a Roman surname in the gens Quintia. So in partic.: T. Quintius Flamininus, the conqueror of King Philip of Macedonia, Cic. Verr. 1, 21, 55 ; id. Mur. 14, 31 ; id. Pis. 25, 61 .

flāmĭnĭus.opening: adj. 1. flamen , of or belonging to a flamen. Adj. : flaminia aedes domus flaminis Dialis, Paul. ex Fest. p. 89, 10 Müll.; so, ex domo flaminia, id. s. v. ignem, p. 106, 4 Müll.; cf. in the foll.: flaminius camillus…

Flāmĭnĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens. So C. Flaminius Nepos, who , when censor , A.U.C. 534, built a circus and constructed a road , and , when consul , was overcome and slain by Hannibal at the lake of Trasimenus , Liv. 22, 4 sq.…

flamma.opening: (archaic gen. sing. flammaï, Lucr. 1, 725 ; 900 ; 5, 1099 ), for flagma, v. flagro; cf. Gr. φλέγμα, from φλέγω , a blazing fire , a blaze , flame (cf. ignis). Lit. : fana flammā deflagrata, Enn. ap. Cic. Tusc. 3, 19, 44…

flammābundus.opening: adj. 1. flamma , flaming (post-class.): subsellia, Mart. Cap. 1, § 90 .

flammātrix.opening: flammo , she that inflames (post-class.), Mart. Cap. 5, § 428 .

flammĕārĭus.opening: flammeum, from flammeus , a maker of bridal-veils : Plaut. Aul. 3, 5, 36 ; cf.: flammearii, infectores flammei coloris, Paul. ex Fest. p. 89, 11 Müll.

flammĕŏlum.opening: dim. id. , a small bridal veil , Juv. 10, 334 ; Prud. Psych. 449 .

flammesco.opening: v. inch. n. [1. flamma], to become inflamed : flammescere caelum, Lucr. 6, 669 .

flammĕus.opening: adj. id. , flaming , fiery. Lit. : sunt stellae naturā flammeae, Cic. N. D. 2, 46, 118 ; Att. ap. Cic. Div. 1, 22, 44 : halitus, Col. 5, 5, 15 ; Mart. 10, 62, 6 .— Transf. , of color, flaming , flamecolored , fiery red…

flammĭcŏmans.opening: adj. flamma + como , having fiery hair , flaming : taedae, Juvenc. 25, 4, 202 .

flammĭcŏmus.opening: adj. flamma + coma , having fiery hair , flaming : ignes, Prud. Psych. 775 ; Avien. Descr. Orb. 1089 .

flammĭcrĕmus.opening: adj. flamma + cremo , consumed with fire : ruinae, Fortun. 1, 15, 47 .

flammĭdus.opening: adj. flamma , flaming , burning , fiery (Appuleian): glacialibus flammida confundit, App. de Mundo, p. 66, 37: roseo rubore flammida, id. Met. 11, p. 158, 22 .

flammĭfer.opening: adj. flamma + fero , flame-bearing , i. e. flaming , burning , fiery ( poet. ): fer mi auxilium; pestem abige a me, flammiferam hanc vim, quae me excruciat, etc., Enn. ap. Cic. Ac. 2, 28, 89 (Trag. 50 ed. Vahl.): crinis…

flammĭgĕna.opening: flamma + gigno , fire-born : fur, i. e. Cacus, son of Vulcan, Sid. Carm. 13, 9 .

flammĭger.opening: adj. flamma + gero , flame-bearing , flaming , fiery ( poet. ): ales, i. e. the eagle, Stat. Th. 8, 676 : sol, Val. Fl. 5, 582 ; cf. Titan, Luc. 1, 415 : zona, Claud. Idyll. 4, 9 .

flammĭgĕro.opening: v. n. id. , to flame , blaze , Ambros. ap. Luc. 7, § 132 ; id. Off. Min. 3, 18, 103 al.

flammĭgo.opening: v. n. flamma + ago , to emit flames (post-class.): noctu flammigare (Aetnam), Gell. 17, 10, 11 ; cf. Macr. S. 5, 17 .

flammĭpŏtens.opening: adj. flamma + potens , powerful by fire : Vulcanus, Arn. 3, p. 112 .

flammĭvŏlus.opening: adj. flamma + volo , flying with flames : sol, Arator. Act. Apost. 2, 531.

flammĭvŏmus.opening: adj. flamma + vomo , vomiting flames , Mart. Cap. 1, § 70 ; Juvenc. 23 praef.

flammo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
flammo.opening: v. n. and a. [1. flamma]. Neutr. , to flame , blaze , burn ( poet. and perh. only in the part. pres. ): super raros feni flammantis acervos Traicit immundos ebria turba pedes (in the purifications at the Palilia), Prop.…

flammōsus.opening: adj. id. , fiery , burning (late Lat.): carbones, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 17, 174 : febris, id. ib. 2, 32, 165 .

flammŭla.opening: dim. id. , a little flame. Lit. : Timagoras negat sibi umquam, cum oculum torsisset, duas ex lucerna flammulas esse visas, Cic. Ac. 2, 25, 80 ; Col. 9, 14, 9 .— Transf. , in late Lat., a little banner used by cavalry,…

flātĭlis.opening: adj. flo , produced by blowing , blown (post-class.): sonitus, Amm. 30, 1 : laminae, i. e. founded, cast, Arn. 6, 201 : virus, blown in, Prud. Ham. 533 ; Prisc. 560 P.

flāto.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to blow. Lit. : cantores tibia calamoque flatantes, Arn. 2, p. 69 .— Trop. , August. Conf. 7, 6 med.

flātor.opening: id. , a blower of a windinstrument: flator tibicen, Paul. ex Fest. p. 89 Müll.; cf.: flat, flator φυσᾷ, αὐλητής , Gloss. Lab.: flatores, tibicines a flando, Placid. p. 463 ; a caster of metals : triumviri monetales,…

flātūra.opening: flo , a blowing (post-Aug. and very rare): ventos jamdiu non esse, et caeli conquievisse flaturas, Arn. 1, 7 : aeris, a melting, coining, Vitr. 2, 7 med. : auri, Plin. 7, 56, 57, § 197 : ARGENTARIAE, Inscr. Orell. 4217 .

flātūrālis.opening: adj. flatura , blowing : artus, i. e. containing air, Tert. Anim. 10 .

flātūrārĭus.opening: id. , a metal-caster , money-coiner , minter , Cod. Theod. 9, 21, 6 ; Inscr. Orell. 4192 sq. : FABER, ib. 4280 .

flātus.opening: flo , a blowing , breathing , snorting (mostly poet. ; syn.: flamen, flabra, ventus, aura). Lit. : nondum spissa nimis complere sedilia flatu (sc. tibiae), Hor. A. P. 205 ; Phaedr. 5, 7, 14 : flatuque secundo, Carbasa…

flāvĕo.opening: v. n. flavus , to be golden yellow or gold-colored , to be light yellow ( poet. ): sed cum maturis flavebit messis aristis, Col. poët. 10, 311; Paul. Nol. Carm. 20, 124 .—In part. pres. : flaventes cerae, Ov. M. 8, 671…

flāvesco.opening: v. inch. n. [flaveo], to become golden yellow or gold-colored , to turn a light yellow ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): molli paulatim flavescet campus arista, Verg. E. 4, 28 : flavescere haphe, Mart. 7, 66, 5 ; so of…

flāvĭcŏmans.opening: adj. flavus + comans , yellow-haired , flaxen-haired : pueri, Prud. Apoth. 495 .

flāvĭcŏmus.opening: adj. flavus + coma , yellow-haired , flaxen-haired : corymbion, Petr. 110 (al. flavus).

flāvĭdus.opening: adj. flavus , of a golden yellow , yellowish : fel, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 20, 194 : rapacia, Plin. 18, 13, 34, § 127 .

Flāvīna.opening: a small city of Etruria , Sil. 8, 492 ; called also , , , Serv. Verg. A. 7, 698 .—Hence, , , adj. , Flavinian : arva, Verg. A. 7, 696 Serv.

flavissae.opening: , a false reading in Non. 112, 29 , for favissae, v. h. v.).

Flāvĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens: gens Flavia, Suet. Vesp. 1 ; Mart. 9, 2, 8 .— So in partic. Cn. Flavius, the scribe of the pontifiex maximus , Appius Caecus, who published the Fasti, Liv. 9, 46, 1 sqq.; Plin. 33, 1, 6, § 17 ;…

flāvus.opening: adj. for flag-vus from FLAG, flagro, burning, light-colored , golden yellow , reddish yellow , flaxen-colored , ξανθός (mostly poet. ): color, Col. 4, 3, 4 : mellis dulci flavoque liquore, Lucr. 1, 938 ; 4, 13 : mella,…

flēbĭlis.opening: adj. fleo . Pass. , to be wept over , to be lamented , lamentable (class.): ponite ante oculos miseram illam et flebilem speciem, Cic. Phil. 11, 3, 7 : o flebiles vigilias! id. Planc. 42, 101 : Hector, Ov. Am. 2, 1, 32…

flecto.grammar: xi, xum, 3 v. a. and n.

foedĕro.opening: v. a. 2. foedus , to establish by treaty or league (in verb. finit. , late Lat.): cum foederaretur concordia, Amm. 31, 4 : pacem, id. 25, 7 : amicitias, Hier. Ep. 5, 1 ; but class. in the part. : , , leagued together ,…

foedĭfrăgus.opening: adj. 2. foedus + frango , league-breaking , perfidious (very rare): Poeni, Cic. Off. 1, 12, 38 ; cf. Mos. Cic. Rep. Fragm. 2, p. 513 sq. ; so, hostes, Laev. ap. Gell. 19, 7, 6 : Chaos, Mart. Cap. 9, § 912 .

foedĭtas.opening: 1. foedus , foulness , filthiness , horridness , hideousness , ugliness , deformity (class.). Physically: multae beluae insectantes odoris intolerabili foeditate depellunt, stench, Cic. N. D. 2, 50, 127 : foeditas, qua…

foedo.opening: v. a. id. , to make foul , filthy , hideous; to defile , pollute , disfigure , mar , deform (mostly poet. and in postAug. prose). Physically: Harpyiae contactu omnia foedant immundo, Verg. A. 3, 227 : foedare in pulvere…

foedus.opening: (for foedus, Ennius wrote fidus, acc. to Varr. L. L. 5, § 86 Müll. Archaic form of the gen. plur. foedesum, acc. to Varr. L. L. 7, § 27 ; v. the letter R ), from the root FID; Sanscr. bandh, ligare; v. fido , a league ,…

Fōlĭa.opening: the name of a witch of Ariminum , Hor. Epod. 5, 42 .

fŏlĭācĕus.opening: adj. folium , leafy , like leaves : semen, Plin. 19, 3, 15, § 42 ; 19, 7, 36, § 119 .

fŏlĭātĭlis.opening: adj. foliatus , leafy (late Lat.): umbra, Venant. Vit. S. Mart. 4, 535 .

fŏlĭātūra.opening: id. , leaf-work , foliage (post-Aug. and very rare): cupresseae foliaturae, Vitr. 2, 9, 13 .

fŏlĭātus.opening: adj. folium , leaved , leafy. Adj. : caulis, Plin. 21, 16, 59, § 99 ; 21, 15, 54, § 91 ; Pall. Mart. 10 fin. : arbores, App. M. 4, p. 143 .— Subst. : , , (sc. unguentum), an ointment or oil made of the leaves of…

fŏlĭōsus.opening: adj. id. , leafy , full of leaves : aizoum foliosum usque ad cacumen, Plin. 25, 13, 102, § 161 : arbor foliosior, id. 12, 11, 23, § 40 .

fŏlĭum.opening: Gr. φύλλον, for φυλιον; cf. alius, ἄλλος; root prob. φλα-, φλασμός; Lat. flos, Flora , a leaf (cf. frons). Lit. , of plants: quid in arboribus? in quibus non truncus, non rami, non folia sunt denique, nisi, etc., Cic.…

follĕātus.opening: adj. follis , expanding and contracting like a pair of bellows , loose , baggy : lingulati calcei sunt, quos nos folleatos vocamus, Isid. Orig. 19, 34 ; cf. follicans, in follico.

follĕo.opening: v. n. id. , to bag or puff out like bellows (late Lat.): si pes laxa pelle non folleat, Hier. Ep. 22, 28 .

follĭco.opening: , no perf. , , v. n. id. , to expand and contract one's self like a pair of bellows (post-Aug. and rare): animalia follicent, Veg. Vet. 5, 75, 1 .—Usu. in the part. praes. : muli senes ... follicantes nares languidas,…

follĭcŭlāre.grammar: appellatur pars remi, quae folliculo est tecta, a quo vita follicularis
follĭcŭlāre.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 85 Müll. (the Gr. ἄσκωμα ).

follĭcŭlōsus.opening: adj. folliculus , full of husks : papaver, App. Herb. 53 .

follĭcŭlus.opening: dim. follis , a small bag or sack. Lit. In gen.: folliculis frumentum vehere, Liv. 9, 13, 9 : quidam judicatus est parentem occidisse: ei statim ... os obvolutum est folliculo et praeligatum, Cic. Inv. 2, 50, 149 .—Of a…

follĭgĕna.opening: adj. follis-gigno , produced by a bellows , droning , dull : bombi, Poët. in Anth. Lat. II. p. 64 Wernsd. N. cr.

follis.opening: cf. flo . Lit. A pair of bellows : formae, quas vos effici sine follibus et sine incudibus non putatis, Cic. N. D. 1, 20, 54 ; cf.: folle fabrili flando accenderunt, Liv. 38, 7, 12 ; Verg. G. 4, 171 ; id. A. 8, 449 :…

follītim.opening: adv. follis, I. C. , by the purseful : nihil moror vetera et vulgata verba, Peratim ductare: at ego follitim ductitabo, will cheat of his money by the purseful, Plaut. Ep. 3, 2, 15 .

fōmentātĭo.opening: fomento , a fomentation (post-class.): fomentationis gratia, Dig. 32, 1, 70 .

fōmento.opening: v. a. fomentum , to foment (post-class.): caput, Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 9 ; Veg. Vet. 2, 8 .

fōmentum.opening: contr. from fovimentum from foveo , a warm application , warm lotion or poultice , fomentation. Lit. : calida, Cels. 2, 17 med. : aquae calidae, id. 8, 10, 7 : calida, sicca, id. 3, 11 init. ; 4, 14 ; cf. Suet. Aug. 81…

fōmes.opening: foveo , kindling-wood , touch-wood , tinder. Lit. : silici scintillam excudit Achates . . . rapuitque in fomite flammam, Verg. A. 1, 176 ; Luc. 8, 776 ; Plin. 16, 40, 77, § 208 .— Trop. (postclass.): fomes et…

fons.opening: root in Gr. χέϝω, χεύσω, to pour, χύμα, χοή, etc.; Lat. fundo, futtilis. Fons, i. e. stem font, for fovont = χεϝοντ-; cf. Varr. L. L. 5, § 123 Müll.; and Paul. ex Fest. p. 84 , a spring , fountain , well-source (syn.:…

fontānĕus.opening: adj. fons , of or from a spring , from the fountain-head : scaturigo, Sol. 37 fin. : defluvia, id. 4, 4 .

fontānus.opening: adj. id. , of or from a spring or fountain , spring -. Adj. : aqua, Cels. 2, 18 ; Col. 12, 9, 2 : ora, Ov. F. 1, 269 .— Subst. , in late Lat.: , , , a spring , fountain , Innocent. de Cas. p. 245 Goes.

Fontēĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens. So M. Fonteius, a praetor in Gaul , in defence of whom Cicero delivered the oration still preserved in part , Cic. Att. 1, 6, 1 . His sister Fonteia, a vestal , Cic. Font. 17, 37 .— , , adj. ,…

fontĭcŏla.opening: adj. fons-colo , dwelling by fountains : ite igitur Camoenae, Fonticolae puellae, Aug. de Mus. 3, 7 .

fontĭcŭlus.opening: dim. fons , a little spring or fountain (very rare), Hor. S. 1, 1, 56 : exsiliente dulci fonticulo, Plin. 31, 10, 46, § 107 .

fontĭgĕna.opening: adj. fons-gigno , born by fountains , a poet. epithet of the Muses: virginum chorus, Mart. Cap. 9, § 908 ; and subst. : o sacra doctarum prudentia fontigenarum, id. 6, § 574 .

fontĭnālis.opening: (also ), , adj. fons , of or from a spring or fountain , spring -. Lit. : aqua, Vitr. 8, 3 .—Deriv. Transf. Adj. : Fontinalis (Fontan-) porta, in Rome , towards the Campus Martius, between the Capitoline and Quirinal…

for.opening: v. defect. (the forms in use are fatur, fantur, fabor, fabitur; part. perf. fatus; perf. fatus sum or eram; imper. fare, poet. ; inf. fari; and parag. farier, Verg. A. 11, 242 ; gerund. fandi, fando; sup. fatu; part.…

fŏrābĭlis.opening: adj. foro , that may be pierced , penetrable : forabilia ac sectilia quae modice umida, Plin. 16, 43, 83, § 227 . — Vulnerable : contemptor ferri nulloque forabilis ictu, Ov. M. 12, 170 .

fŏrāgo.opening: id. , a dividing-thread in a web: forago filum, quo textrices diurnum opus distinguunt: a forando dictum, Paul. ex Fest. p. 90 Müll.; cf.: forago trames diversi coloris, Gloss. Isid.: residens inter pensa et foragines…

fŏrāmen.opening: id. , an opening or aperture produced by boring, a hole (rare but class.): neque porta neque ullum foramen erat, qua posset eruptio fieri, outlet , Sisenn. ap. Non. 113, 27 : foramina parietum et fenestrarum, Col. 9,…

fŏrāmĭnātus.opening: adj. foramen , bored or pierced through , having holes (late Lat.): paries, Sid. Ep. 2, 2 .

fŏrāmĭnōsus.opening: adj. id. , full of holes (post-class.): caro, Tert. Pat. 14 .

fŏras.opening: adv. acc. form like alias, alteras, utrasque; while foris is an abl. form; both from an obsol. nom. fora; Sanscr. dvār; Gr. θύρα; O. H. Germ. tor; Engl. door , out through the doors , out of doors , forth , out…

fŏrastĭcus.opening: adj. foras , out of doors , public : philosophorum disciplinae, Aldh. Septen. Col. 167 M.

fŏrātus.opening: foro , a boring (postclass., and only in the abl. sing. ): a quo foratu frontem nominatam Varro existimavit, Lact. Opif. 8 : aurem foratu effeminatus, Tert. Pall. 4 .

forbeam.opening: , quam Graeci φορβήν vocant, Paul. ex Fest. p. 84 Müll.

forceps.opening: ( gen. plur. forcipium, Lucil. ap. Charis. p. 74 ), and ( , Cels. 7, 12 ; 8, 4 ; , Ov. M. 12, 277 ) [root in Sanscr. ghar-mas, glow, warmth; Gr. θερ-, θέρμη, θέρος ; Lat. for-mus, for-nus, fornax and cap-io], a pair of…

Forcŭlus.opening: contr. from Foriculus, from 1. foris , a deity who presides over the doors , Tert. Idol. 15 ; Coron. Mil. 13; Aug. Civ. D. 4, 8 fin.

fordĭcīdĭa.opening: (archaic form † , Paul. ex Fest. p. 102 Müll., v. the foll. art.), , forda + caedo , the sacrifice of a cow that is with calf , which was performed on the 16th of April, in honor of Tellus, Varr. L. L. 6, § 15 ; Paul.…

fordus.opening: (archaic form , v. in the foll. ), adj. fero , with young , pregnant : fordicidia a fordis bubus: bos forda quae fert in ventre, etc., Varr. L. L. 6, § 15 Müll.; cf.: fordicidiis boves fordae id est gravidae…

fŏre.opening: inf. , irregular, from the obsolete fuo, and equivalent to futurum esse; and , , subj. imperf. , equivalent to essem, esses, etc., v. sum init.

fŏrensis.opening: adj. forum , of or belonging to the market or forum , public , forensic : oratio judicialis et forensis, i. e. delivered in the forum, Cic. Or. 51, 170 ; cf.: Thucydides hoc forense, concertatorium, judiciale non…

Fŏrentum.opening: (in some MSS. of Horace ), , , a small town in Apulia , now Forenza , Liv. 9, 20, 9 ; Hor. C. 3, 4, 16 .—Hence, , , its inhabitants , Plin. 3, 11, 16, § 105 .

forfex.opening: forus-facio , a pair of shears or scissors : forfices sunt quibus incidimus: forcipes quibus aliquid firmum tenemus, Serv. ad Verg. A. 8, 453 : vitiosa grana (in uva), forficibus amputant, Col. 12, 44, 4 ; Cels. 7, 21,…

forfĭcŭla.opening: dim. forfex , a pair of small shears , scissors : quod incisum forficulis, cribrant, Plin. 25, 5, 23, § 58 .

fŏrĭa.opening: the flux , a disease of swine, Varr. R. R. 2, 4, 5 ; cf.: foria stercora liquidiora, Non. 114, 11 . (Hence, foriolus and conforio.

fŏrĭca.opening: forum , a public privy : conducunt foricas, Juv. 3, 38 ; cf. Schol. Vet. ad Juv. 3, 38 .

fŏrĭcārĭus.opening: forica , one who rents a forica, Dig. 22, 1, 17, § 5 .

fŏrĭcŭla.opening: dim. foris , a windowshutter , Varr. R. R. 1, 59, 1 .

fŏrĭcŭlārĭum.opening: (sc. vectigal) [forica], custom-house duty , transit duty , Inscr. Orell. 3347 .

fŏrinsĕcus.opening: adv. foris + secus, analogous with extrin-secus . from without , on the outside , = ἔξωθεν (post-Aug.). Lit. : ab cohorte forinsecus praedictis fenestellis, Col. 8, 3, 6 : quarundam naturae lignum omne corticis loco…

fŏrĭo.opening: v. n. foris : forire est pro dehonerare ventrem, forire est enim fossas eicere, Schol. Vet. ad Juv. 3, 38 .

fŏrĭŏlus.opening: foria , one who has a flux or diarrhœa , Laber. ap. Non. 114, 13 .

fŏris.opening: adv. abl. form (denoting both the place where and the place whence), and answering to the acc. form foras, v. foras init. . Out at the doors , out of doors , abroad , without (opp. intus, domi, etc.): sinito ambulare,…

forma.opening: Sanscr. dhar-, dhar-āmi, bear; dhar-i-man, figure; Gr. θρα- in θρῆνυς, θρόνος; cf. Lat. frētus, frēnum, fortis, etc. , form , in the most comprehensive sense of the word, contour , figure , shape , appearance (syn.:…

formābĭlis.opening: adj. formo , that may be formed or fashioned (eccl. Lat.): os, Prud. Apoth. 1034 : primordia, Aug. Trin. 11, 2 fin.

formābĭlĭtas.opening: formabilis , capacity for being fashioned , plasticity : secundum materiae quandam, ut ita dicam, formabilitatem, August. Gen. ad Lit. 5, 4 .

formācĕus.opening: adj. forma , made in a form or mould : parietes, quos appellant formaceos, quoniam in forma circumdatis duabus utrimque tabulis inferciuntur verius quam instruuntur, Plin. 35, 14, 48, § 169 .

formālis.opening: adj. forma (post-Aug.). (Acc. to forma, I. B. 2.) Of or for a form or mould : temperatura aeris, proper for making moulds, Plin. 34, 9, 20, § 98 .— (Acc. to I. B. 4.) Having a set form , of the nature of a rescript ,…

formāmentum.opening: formo , a shaping , forming; concr., a shape , form (anteand post-class.): omnia principiorum, Lucr. 2, 819 : divina, Arn. 3, 109 .

formaster.opening: forma , one who beautifies or adorns himself , a coxcomb , dandy : aut luculentaster aut formaster frigidus, Tit. ap. Fest. s. v. OBSTRVDANT, p. 193 Müll.

formātĭo.opening: formo , a shaping , forming; a form , design , plan (post-Aug.). Lit. : formationem puto probandam, locum improbandum, Vitr. 2 praef. : oblonga fori, id. 5, 1 : formationes columnarum, id. 4, 1 .— Trop. : morum, Sen.…

formātor.opening: id. , a former , fashioner (post-Aug.). Lit. : universi, Sen. Cons. ad Helv. 8 ; Vulg. Isa. 44, 8 ; 24 . — Plur. : imperii, Amm. 18, 6 .— Trop. : praeceptor rector est alienorum ingeniorum ac formator, Quint. 10, 2, 20…

formātrix.opening: formator , she who forms (post-class.): regina (Dido) tantae civitatis formatrix, foundress, Tert. Monog. 17 al.

formātūra.opening: formo , a forming , fashioning , shaping (ante- and post-class.): labrorum, Lucr. 4, 550 : res formatura varia, of various shapes, Arn. 2, 50 .

formella.opening: dim. forma , a little form or mould for baking in (late Lat.): in formella piscem formare, Apic. 9, 13 ; or for moulding cheese: casei, Vulg. 1 Reg. 17, 18 .

Formĭae.opening: for sformiae, σϝορμιαι, from old form Ὁρμίαι, place of anchorage; cf. ὅρμος , a very ancient city of Latium , on the borders of Campania , the fabled seat of the Laestrygones , now Mola di Gaeta , Mel. 2, 4, 9 ; Plin.…

formīca.opening: root mur-, to swarm, Gr. μύρμος, μύρμηξ; cf. Georg Curtius Gr. Etym. p. 339 sq. , an ant , emmet , pismire : te faciam ut formicae frustillatim differant, Plaut. Curc. 4, 4, 20 ; Plin. 11, 30, 36, § 108 ; Cic. N. D. 3,…

formīcābĭlis.opening: adj. formica , resembling the creeping of ants (late Lat.): pulsus, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 27, 145 .—Also called , Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 14, 198 ; cf. formicatio and formico, II.

formīcātĭo.opening: formico , an irritation of the skin resembling the crawling of ants , produced by pustules; Gr. μυρμηκία : corporum, Plin. 28, 7, 20, § 71 ; Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 1, 2 : eorum articulorum, qui tanguntur, id. ib. 5, 2, 30 .

formīcīnus.opening: adj. formica , of or like ants : gradus, i. e. creeping, crawling, Plaut. Men. 5, 3, 12 .

formīco.opening: v. n. id. . * To creep or crawl like ants : venarum inaequali aut formicante percussu, Plin. 7, 51, 52, § 171 .— * To feel like the creeping of ants , μυρμηκιζω : donec formicet cutis, Plin. 30, 13, 41, § 120 .

formīcōsus.opening: adj. formica , full of ants : arbor, Plin. 10, 74, 95, § 206 .

formīcŭla.opening: dim. id. , a little ant , Fronto Ep. ad Ver. 8 ed. Mai.; App. M. 6, p. 177 ; Arn. 4, 145 ; 7, 240 .

formīdābĭlĭs.opening: adj. 1. formido , causing fear , terrible , formidable ( poet. and in post-class. prose; cf. formidolosus): lumen, Ov. M. 2, 857 : nec formidabilis ulli, id. ib. 2, 174 : Orcus, id. ib. 14, 116 : aspectus, Gell. 14, 4,…

formīdāmen.opening: id. , a fright , a spectre (post-class.): bustorum formidamina, sepulcrorum terriculamenta, App. Mag. p. 315, 26 .

formīdo.opening: Sanscr. root dhar-, whence firmus; prop. the fear that makes rigid, Corss. Ausspr. 1, 148 , fearfulness , fear , terror , dread (class.). Lit. : parasitus, qui me conplevit flagiti et formidinis, Plaut. Men. 5, 5, 3 :…

formīdŭlōsĭtas.opening: formidulosus , cruelty , extreme severity : poenae, Cypr. Laud. Mart. p. 134 ed. Wurzb.

formīdŭlōsus.opening: ( , v. Corss. Ausspr. 2, 145), , adj. 2. formido , full of fear , fearful. Act. , producing fear , dreadful , terrible , terrific (class.): nimis formidulosum facinus praedicas, Plaut. Am. 5, 1, 65 : loca tetra,…

formĭdus.opening: adj. † formus , warm : aedificium aestate frigidum, hieme formidum, Cato ap. Paul. ex Fest. s. v. forma, p. 83 Müll.

formĭtas.opening: formo , a shaping , fashioning , forming , Isid. Orig. 6, 17, 4 .

formo.opening: v. a. forma , to shape , fashion , form (class.; esp. freq. in the trop. sense). Lit. : omnis fere materia nondum formata rudis appellatur, Paul. ex Fest. p. 265 : materia, quam fingit et format effectio, Cic. Ac. 1, 2,…

formōsĭtas.opening: formosus , beauty (very rare): uxor eximia formositate praedita, App. M. 9, p. 224, 24 : decorum positum est in tribus rebus, formositate, ordine, ornatu ad actionem apto, * Cic. Off. 1, 35, 126 .

formōsŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [id.], pretty (ante- and post-class.): uxor, Varr. ap. Non. 27, 5 : formosulus tuus, Hier. Ep. 117, 10 : formosuli nostri, id. ap. Jovin. 2, 14.

formōsus.opening: (FORMONSVS, Inscr. Grut. 669, 10 ; comp. : FORMONSIOR, Inscr. Fabr. p. 374 , no. 169: formonsam, Verg. E. 1, 5 Rib.), , adj. forma, I. B. 1. , finely formed , beautiful , handsome (freq. and class; syn.: pulcher,…

formucales.grammar: forcipes dictae, quod forma capiant, id est ferventia
formucales.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 91 Müll. N. cr. (acc. to Scalig. to be read † formucapes).

formŭla.opening: dim. forma, I. B. , acc. to the different signiff. of forma. * (Acc. to I. B. 1.) A fine form , beauty : formula atque aetatula, Plaut. Pers. 2, 2, 47 .— (Acc. to forma, I. B. 2.) A small pattern , mould , last , acc.…

formŭlārĭus.opening: formula, II. C. , a lawyer skilled only in composing writs or forms of process in courts of law : alii se ad album ac rubricas transtulerunt et formularii vel, ut Cicero ait, leguleii quidam esse maluerunt, etc., Quint.…

formus.opening: adj. ferv-veo; Sanscr. ghar-mas, glow, warmth; Gr. θερμός, θέρος; Lat. ferveo, fornus, fornax; O. H. Germ. waram; Engl. warm, Georg Curtius Gr. Etym. p. 485 , warm (ante-class.): forma significat modo faciem cujusque…

fornācālis.opening: adj. fornax , of or belonging to ovens. Adj. : dea, i. e. the goddess Fornax (v. fornax, II.), Ov. F. 6, 314 .— Subst. : , , , the festival of the goddess Fornax, instituted , according to the fable , by Numa; the oven…

fornācārĭus.opening: ( ), , adj. id. , of or belonging to a furnace : servus, i. e. a furnace-heater, Dig. 9, 2, 27, § 9 .

fornācātor.opening: (FVRNACATOR in an inscr. found at Pompeii, v. Rosin. Dissert. Isag. p. 66, tab. 10, no. 2), , id. , the heater of a bath-furnace , a bath-heater , Dig. 33, 7, 14 .

fornācŭla.opening: dim. id. , a little furnace or oven. Lit. , Juv. 10, 82 ; Vitr. 7, 10, 1 ; Front. Ep. ad M. Caes. 1, 2 ed. Mai. —* Trop. , a kindler , exciter : hic totius calumniae fornacula, App. Mag. p. 321, 32 .

fornax.opening: cf.: fornus and furnus, Gr. πῦρ , a furnace , oven , kiln (cf. also: caminus, clibanus, focus): in ardentibus fornacibus, Cic. N. D. 1, 37, 103 : calcaria, Cato, R. R. 38 ; Plin. 17, 9, 6, § 53 : aeraria, id. 11, 36,…

fornĭcārĭus.opening: , and , , fornix, II. , a fornicator; a prostitute , Tert. Anim. 35 ; id. Pudic. 9 ; 16 ; cf. Isid. Orig. 10, 110 ; Hier. Ep. 53, 8 ; Vulg. Isa. 57, 3 al. : fornicaria πόρνη ἀπὸ καμάρας , Vet. Gloss.

fornĭcātim.opening: adv. fornicatus , in the form of an arch , archwise , Plin. 16, 42, 81, § 223 .

fornĭcātĭo.opening: fornicor , whoredom , fornication (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Pudic. 1 ; 2 ; 16 ; 22; Vulg. Num. 14, 33 al.
