fornĭcātor.opening: id. , a fornicator (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Pudic. 1 ; 16 ; 22 ; Vulg. 1 . Cor. 5, 11 al.

fornĭcātrix.opening: fornicator , a fornicatress , prostitute (late Lat.), Isid. Orig. 10, 110 .

fornĭcātus.opening: adj. fornix, I. , vaulted , arched. Lit. : paries vel solidus vel fornicatus, Cic. Top. 4, 22 : ambitus, Plin. 12, 5, 11, § 22 .— As an adj. prop. : Via Fornicata, or Arch Street , a street in Rome leading to the Campus…

fornĭcor.opening: v. dep. n. [id. II.], to commit whoredom or fornication (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Pudic. 22 ; Vulg. Gen. 38, 24 et saep.

fornix.opening: an arch or vault (cf.: camera, testudo, tholus, lacunar). Lit. : Democritus invenisse dicitur fornicem, ut lapidum curvatura paulatim inclinatorum medio saxo alligaretur, Sen. Ep. 90 med. : si quis in pariete communi…

fŏro.opening: v. a. root bhar-, Zend. bar-, cut, bore; Gr. φαρ-, φάρος, plough; cf. φάραγξ, φάρυγξ; Germ. bohren; Angl.-Sax. borian; Engl. bore , to bore , pierce (mostly post-Aug. and very rare). Lit. : forata arbos, Col. 5, 10, 20…

Forojuliensis.opening: , v. Forum Julii, under forum fin.

forpex.opening: corrupted from forfex , fire-tongs , Cato, R. R. 10, 3 ; 11, 5 ; Suet. Aug. 75 ; Sid. Epith. 15, 184 .

fors.opening: fero, to bring, whence fortuna, v. Georg Curtius Gr. Etym. p. 300 sq. , chance , hap , luck , hazard. Subst. As an appellative noun (used only in the nom. and abl. ; syn.: fortuna, casus, sors): quo saxum impulerit…

fors-an.opening: adv. ellipt. for fors sit an; v. fors, II. A. and forsitan, and cf. fortan and fortassean , perhaps , perchance , peradventure ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): me miseram, forsan hic mihi parvam habeat fidem, Ter. Eun.…

forsit.opening: adv. contr. from fors sit; cf. fors, II. A. , perhaps , Hor. S. 1, 6, 49 (quoted Prisc. p. 1015 P.).

forsĭtan.opening: adv. contr. from fors sit an; v. fors, A.; cf. also: forsan, fortan, and fortassean , perhaps , peradventure. Usually in principal clauses. With subj. (class. and freq.; only so in Cicero): si altera illaec magis…

fortan.opening: , false read. for jam, Cic. Rep. 3, 35, 47 .

fortassē.opening: (also , , and not in Caes.; Plaut. As. 2, 4, 86 ; id. Bacch. 4, 4, 20 ; Cic. Clu. 52, 144 Klotz, B. and K.; 71, 201 B. and K.; Hor. S. 1, 4, 131 ; 2, 7, 40 ; Plin. 2, 20, 18, § 82 ; 27, 12, 77, § 102 ; Traj. ap. Plin.…

fortasse-an.opening: (sometimes written separately fortasse an), adv. cf.: forsan, forsitan, fortan , perhaps , perchance (ante- and post-class.): fortassean sit, quos hic non mertet metus, Att. ap. Non. 138, 33 ; Sisenn. ib. 82, 6 : de…

fortax.opening: , = φόρταξ (bearer), the basis on which a furnace rests, Cato, R. R. 38, 1 .

fortesco.opening: v. inch. n. [fortis], to become brave : item notavimus, quod fortescere posuit (Laevius) pro fortem fieri, Gell. 19, 7, 8 .

fortĭcŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [id.], somewhat bold , brave , or resolute (very rare): quamvis idem (Epicurus) forticulum se in torminibus praebeat, * Cic. Tusc. 2, 19, 45 ; App. M. 8, p. 212, 32 : carmina, Aus. Idyll. 3 fin.

fortĭfĭcātĭo.opening: fortifico , a strengthening , fortifying (post-class.): corpori adhibere, Cael. Aur. Tard. 4, 3, 44 .

fortĭfĭco.opening: v. a. fortis - facio , to make strong , to strengthen , fortify (postclass.): corpora, Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 2, 38 ; 3, 7, 91 : dentes (with constringere), id. ib. 2, 4, 78 .

fortis.opening: (archaic form FORCTIS, Fragm. XII. Tab. ap. Fest. s. v. sanates, p. 348 Müll.; cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 84 ; and perh. also in the form FORCTUS; v. id. s. v. horctum, p. 102; cf. Müll. ad Fest. p. 320 , b), , adj. Sanscr.…

fortĭtūdo.opening: fortis , strength. Physically (very rare). In gen.: haec feminalia de bysso retorta ob fortitudinem solent contexi, firmness , durability , Hier. Ep. 64, 10 : galeae, Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Al. 2, 25 ; cf. vini, Macr. S.…

fortĭuscŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [fortis.; cf. forticulus], somewhat strong or powerful , Sutrius ap. Fulg. Myth. 3, 8 .

fortŭī^tus.opening: (i long, Hor. C. 2, 15, 17 ; Phaedr. 2, 4, 4 ; Aus. Sept. Sap. de Solon. 3 ; short, Petr. Poët. Sat. 135; Juv. 13, 225 ; Manil. 1, 182 ), , adj. forte; analog. with gratuitus , that takes place by chance or accident ,…

fortūna.opening: (archaic gen. sing. fortunas, like familias, escas, vias, etc., Naev. ap. Prisc. p. 679 P.), lengthened from fors; cf. Nep-tunus, v. Corss. Ausspr. 1, 434 , chance , hap , luck , fate , fortune (good or ill; syn.:…

fortūnārĭus.opening: adj. fortuna , resulting from fortune , brought about by chance; n. as subst. : in haec et hujuscemodi fortunaria dispositis equis, Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. 1, 44 .

fortūnātē.opening: adv. , v. fortuno, P. a. fin.

fortūnātim.opening: adv. fortunatus , luckily , fortunately : fortunatim, feliciter ac bene vortat, Enn. ap. Non. 112, 2 (Ann. v. 112 ed. Vahl.).

fortūnātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from fortuno.

fortūno.opening: (archaic form of the perf. subj. fortunassint, Afran. ap. Non. 109, 18 ), v. a. fortuna, II. A. 1. , to make prosperous or fortunate , to make happy , to prosper , bless : prosperare, omnibus bonis augere, Non. l. l.…

fŏrŭli.opening: dim. forus . A book-case : libros Sibyllinos condidit duobus forulis auratis sub Palatini Apollinis basi, Suet. Aug. 31 ; Juv. 3, 219 .— Fori significant et Circensia spectacula, ex quibus etiam minores forulos dicimus,…

Fŏrŭli.opening: an ancient city of the Sabines , now Cività Tommasa , Liv. 26, 11, 11 ; Verg. A. 7, 714 ; Sil. 8, 417 .—Hence, FORVLANVS, of or belonging to Foruli , Forulan , Inscr. Orell. 3794 .

fŏrum.opening: , (archaic form , , , to accord with locus, Lucil. ap. Charis. p. 55 P., and ap. Non. 206, 15 ; Pompon. ib.), etym. dub.; perh. root Sanscr. dhar-, support; dhar-as, mountain, etc.; Lat. forma, fortis, frenum, etc.;…

Fosi.opening: a Germanic tribe , a branch of the Cheruscans , near the modern Celle , Tac. G. 36 .

fossa.opening: fodio, i. e. fossa terra , a ditch , trench , fosse (syn.: fovea, scrobs, fossio). Lit. In gen.: salso suffudit gurgite fossas, Lucr. 5, 482 : fodere fossam, Liv. 3, 26, 9 : ut unus aditus maximo aggere objecto fossa…

fossīcĭus.opening: or , , adj. fossus, from fodio , dug out , dug up from the ground: creta, Varr. R. R. 1, 7, 8 : sal, id. ib. : harena, Plin. 36, 23, 54, § 175 ; Pall. 1, 10 . Cf. the foll. art.

fossĭlis.opening: adj. id. , dug out , dug up , fossil : sal, Varr. 2, 11, 6 : harena, Plin. 36, 26, 66, § 192 : ebur, id. 36, 18, 29, § 134 : flumen, Amm. 24, 6 .

fossĭo.opening: fodio , a digging (rare but class.): recenti fossione terram fumare calentem, Cic. N. D. 2, 9, 25 ; Col. 11, 2, 41 ; Plin. 17, 26, 39, § 247 .—In plur. : quid fossiones agri repastinationesque proferam? Cic. de Sen. 15,…

fosso.opening: v. freq. a. fodio , to dig , pierce (ante-and post-class.): corpora telis, Enn. ap. Varr. L. L. 7, § 100 (Ann. v. 569 ed. Vahl.).—Hence, , , , a ditch , fosse , Pall. Sept. 13 ; Capitol. Gord. 28 ; Veg. Mil. 4, 16 .— ,…

fossor.opening: id. , a digger , delver , ditcher. Lit. In gen. ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): et labefacta movens robustus jugera fossor, Verg. G. 2, 264 : squalidus in magna compede fossor, Juv. 11, 80 ; Hor. C. 3, 18, 15 ; Mart.…

fossōrĭus.opening: fodio , adapted to digging , fit for delving : pars (securis), Isid. 19, 19, 11 .—As subst. : , , , digging (as an occupation), Firm. Math. 2, 10 init.

fossŭla.opening: dim. fossa , a little ditch , Cato, R. R. 161, 4 ; Col. 11, 3, 54 ; 12, 46, 3 .

fossūra.opening: fodio , a digging (postAug., whereas fossio is quite class.). Lit. : plana fossura, Col. 4, 14, 2 ; Pall. 10, 14, 2 .—In plur. : complanata juga fossuris montium, Suet. Calig. 37 : puteorum, Vitr. 5, 9, 8 ; Col. 4, 28,…

fōtus.opening: foveo , a warming , fomenting (post-Aug., rare except in abl. ). Lit. , Amm. 21, 2, 3 : solis, Lact. 1, 12, 7 : decoctum eorum coeliacos juvat et potione et fotu, Plin. 23, 1, 10, § 14 ; 23, 9, 82, § 164 : fotus ex aqua…

fŏvĕa.opening: kindred with favissae , a small pit , esp. for taking wild beasts, a pit fall (syn.: scrobs, specus: fossa, etc.). Lit. In gen.: (humor) ut in foveam fluat, Lucr. 2, 475 : (cadavera) Donec humo tegere ac foveis…

fŏvēla.opening: foveo , a comforting , refreshment (post-class.): incorporalitas est immunis a poena et a fovela, Tert. Anim. 7 .

fŏvĕo.opening: v. a. Corss. assumes a root bhag-, to be hot; Gr. φώγειν, to roast; O. H. Germ. bachan; Germ. backen; Engl. bake; hence, fovere for fog-vēre; favilla for fag-villa; and to this refers: favere, faustus, etc., Ausspr. 1,…

Fovii.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 87 Müll. N. cr.

fracebunt.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 90 Müll. N. cr.; cf.: FRACEBUNT sordebunt, displicebunt, dictum a fracibus, qui sunt stillicidia sterquilinii, Placid. p. 463 .

frăces.opening: (sing. form FRAX; v. the foll. ), kindr. with FRAG, frango; cf. fragosus; lit., broken bits, fragments; hence , grounds or dregs of oil : FRAX τρυγία γάρου ; fraces ἐλαίου τρυγία· ὑπόστασις ἐλαίου ; fracere ἐξίστασθαι ;…

frăcesco.opening: v. inch. n. [FRACEO; v. fraces and FRACEBUNT], to become soft or mellow , to rot , spoil : olea lecta si nimium diu fuit in acervis, caldore fracescit, et oleum foetidum fit, Varr. R. R. 55, 5 sq. ; so, oleum, becomes…

frăcĭdus.opening: adj. FRACEO; whence fracesco and fraces , soft , mellow : ut fracida sit (olea), cato, R. R. 64, 1.

fractārĭa.opening: (sc. machina) [frango], a machine for crushing flint-stones : caedunt (silices) fractariis CL libras ferri habentibus, Plin. 33, 4, 21, § 71 ; v. Sillig. ad h. l.

fractĭo.opening: id. , a breaking , breaking in pieces (eccl. Lat.): panis, Hier. Ep. 108, 8 ; Aug. Cons. Evang. 4, 25 ; Vulg. Luc. 24, 35 .

fractor.opening: id. , a breaker , breaker in pieces (post-class.): ferularum, Sid. Ep. 3, 13 .

fractūra.opening: frango , a breach , fracture , cleft : ad luxum aut ad fracturam alliga, Cato, R. R. 160 : quo propior fractura capiti (ossis) vel superiori vel inferiori est, eo pejor est, Cels. 8, 10 .—In plur. , Plin. 29, 6, 39, §…

fractus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from frango.

frāga.opening: root Sanscr. dhraj-, breathe; prop., the fragrant berry; hence, Fr. fraise , strawberries : Fragaria vesca, Linn.; Verg. E. 3, 92 ; Ov. M. 1, 104 ; Plin. 15, 24, 28, § 98 ; Sen. Hippol. 516 .—* In sing. : , , , a…

frăgesco.opening: v. inch. n. [FRAG, frango], to become broken; trop., to be conquered , subdued , Att. ap. Non. 111, 1 sq. (Trag. Rel. v. 26, 338 Rib.).

frăgĭlis.opening: adj. id. , easily broken , brittle , fragile (class.; esp. freq. in the transf. signif.; cf.: caducus, fluxus). Lit. : cadi, Ov. M. 12, 243 : coryli (with tiliae molles), id. ib. 10, 93 : rami, Verg. E. 8, 40 : myrtus,…

frăgĭlĭtas.opening: fragilis , brittleness , fragility. Lit. : tus probatur candore, amplitudine, fragilitate, Plin. 12, 14, 32, § 65 : tenuiora ferramenta oleo restingui mos est, ne aqua in fragilitatem durentur, id. 34, 14, 41, § 146 .—…

frăgĭum.opening: FRAG, frango , a fracture of a part of the body (for fractura): crurum, App. M. 9, p. 225, 35 .

fragmen.opening: FRAG, frango . * A fracture : percussit subito deceptum fragmine pectus, Val. Fl. 3, 477 .— Mostly in plur. : fragmina, um, pieces broken off , fragments , ruins , wreck ( poet. and in postAug. prose for the class.…

fragmentum.opening: FRAG, frango , a piece broken off , a piece , remnant , fragment (class.; mostly in plur. ; cf.: frustum, segmentum). Plur. : inermem atque imparatum tribunum alii gladiis adoriuntur, alii fragmentis septorum et…

frăgor.opening: id. , a breaking , breaking to pieces. Lit. (very rare): pausam stare fragori, to fragility, Lucr. 1, 747 : so, id. 5, 109 ; 317 .— Transf. , a crashing (as when something is broken to pieces), a crash , noise , din…

frăgōsus.opening: adj. fragor . (Acc. to fragor, I.) Apt to be broken , fragile ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : fragosa putri corpore, Lucr. 2, 860 .— Transf. , rough , uneven : silvis horrentia saxa fragosis, Ov. M. 4, 778 :…

frāgrans.opening: Part. and P. a. , v. fragro.

frāgranter.opening: adv. , v. fragro, P. a. fin.

frāgrantĭa.opening: fragro , scent , odor , fragrance (post-class.; cf.: odor, nidor, suffimen): unguentorum, Val. Max. 9, 1, 1 ext. : vestimentorum, Vulg. Gen. 27, 27 . — Trop. : bonorum morum, Ambros. in Luc. 6, § 15 .

frāgro.opening: (collat. form fraglo, Dracont. Carm. 10, 287 ), , v. n. Sanscr. dhraj-, breathe, etc.; hence frāga; cf. flare, to blow , to emit a smell , to smell (of both good and bad odors), to emit fragrance , to reek ( poet. and…

frămĕa.opening: an old Germ. word . A spear , javelin , used by the ancient Germans: hastas vel ipsorum vocabulo frameas gerunt angusto et brevi ferro, sed ita acri et ad usum habili, ut eodem telo, proüt ratio poscit, vel comminus vel…

Franci.opening: the Franks , a Germanic confederacy on the Rhine , Claud. I. Laud. Stil. 189 ; 227 ; II. Laud. Stil. 243; Vop. Procul. 13 al. —In sing. collect.: ante pedes humili Franco tristique Suevo Perfruor, Claud. in Eutrop. 1,…

frango.opening: v. a. root in Gr. FPAT, ῥήγνυμι, ῥῆγμα, ῥωγαλέος; Goth. Brikkan; Irish brissim; Germ. brechen; Engl. break; but cf. Fick, Vergl. Wörterb. p. 182, and v. the letter F , to break , break in pieces , dash to pieces ,…

frāter.opening: Sanscr. bhrātā; Gr. φράτηρ, φράτωρ, clansman; Goth. brothar; Engl. brother , a brother. Lit. : frater mi, salve, Plaut. Curc. 5, 2, 58 ; cf.: mi frater, mi frater, mi frater, tune id veritus es? etc., Cic. Q. Fr. 1, 3,…

frātercŭlo.opening: v. n. fraterculus , a word comically formed by Plautus, after the analogy of sororiare, and also used of the breasts, to swell up alike (v. sororio), Plaut. Fragm. ap. Fest. p. 297 Müll.; cf. also FRATRARE.

frātercŭlus.opening: dim. frater , a little brother. Lit. : unde fit, ut malim fraterculus esse Gigantis, i. e. of unknown parents. qs. sprung from the earth , Juv. 4, 98 . — Transf. (acc. to frater, II. A.), a familiar appellation given to…

frāternĭtas.opening: fraternus , brotherhood , fraternity (post-Aug. and very rare): fraternitatis vinculum, Lact. 5, 6, 12 : Aedui soli Gallorum fraternitatis nomen cum populo Romano usurpant, Tac. A. 11, 25 ; Vulg. Rom. 12, 10 ; Quint.…

frāternus.opening: adj. frater , brotherly , fraternal. Lit. : sese et amore fraterno et existimatione vulgi commoveri, Caes. B. G. 1, 20, 3 : tametsi in ipso fraterno parricidio nullum scelus praetermissum videtur, tamen, etc. ... ab…

frātrāre.grammar: puerorum mammae dicuntur, cum primum tumescunt
frātrāre.opening: (al. † ) , quod velut fratres pares oriuntur: quod etiam in frumento spica facere dicuntur, Paul. ex Fest. p. 91 Müll.; cf.: † fratrarent, turgerent, pubescerent, Placid. p. 463 (cf. fraterculo).

frātria.opening: ( sister-inlaw ), Paul. ex Fest. p. 90 Müll.; cf.: fratriae appellantur fratrum inter se uxores, Non. 557, 9 ; and: fratria, εἰνάτηρ , Gloss. Philox; also called † fratrissa, acc. to Isid. Orig. 9, 7, 17 .

fratria.grammar: est Graecum vocabulum partis hominum, ut Neapoli etiam nunc
fratria.opening: Varr. L. L. 5, § 85 Müll. (= φρατρία , a division of the people , answering to the Lat. curia, the third part of a φυλή ).

frātrĭcīda.opening: frater-caedo , one who murders a brother , a fratricide , Nep. Timol. 1 ; Cic. pro Domo, 10, 26.

frātrĭcīdĭum.opening: fratricida , the murder of a brother. fratricide (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Monog. 4 ; Hier. adv. Jovin. 1, 14 ; Salv. de Gub. Dei, 1, p. 25.

frātrŭēlis.opening: frater, analog. with patruelis , a father's brother's son , a cousin (late Lat.), Hier. Ep. 22, 26 ; cf.: fratrueles filii materterae sunt, Isid. Orig. 9, 6, 15 .

fraudābĭlis.opening: adj. fraudo , deceiving , fraudulent , Cassiod. Var. 1, 37 .

fraudātĭo.opening: id. , a cheating , deceiving , defrauding , deceit , fraud (rare but class.): ex hac parte pudor pugnat, illinc petulantia: hinc fides, illinc fraudatio, Cic. Cat. 2, 11, 25 : VT INTER BONOS BENE AGIER OPORTET ET SINE…

fraudātor.opening: id. , a cheat , deceiver , defrauder (rare but class.): creditorum Trebellius et homo diruptus dirutusque, Cic. Phil. 13, 12, 26 : fraudatorum et infitiatorum impudentia, id. Fl. 20, 48 : beneficiorum, Sen. Ben. 4, 26 .

fraudātōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or relating to cheating or fraud : interdictum, Dig. 46, 3, 96 ; 36, 1, 67 .

fraudātrix.opening: fraudator , she who cheats or defrauds (eccl. Lat.; opp. servatrix), Tert. Res. Carn. 12 .

fraudĭfer.opening: adj. fraus + fero , fraudulent , deceitful : flatus, Cypr. Carm. de Genes. 114 .

fraudĭger.opening: adj. fraus + gero , cheating , fraudulent (post-class.): loquelae, Tert. Genes. 3 .

fraudo.opening: (arch. ), (archaic perf. subj. : fraudassis, Plaut. Rud. 5, 2, 58 ; in the dep. form: fraussus sit, id. As. 2, 2, 20 ; cf.: frausus erit, fraudem commiserit, Paul. ex Fest. p. 91 Müll.), v. a. fraus , to cheat , beguile…

fraudŭlentĭa.opening: deceitfulness , a disposition to defraud : mentientium, Hilar. ap. Matt. 4, 23: simulatae mentis, id. ib. 22, 7 ; id. Trin. 1, 25 ; Ambros. Ep. 2 , §§ 13, 16; Vulg. Job, 13, 9 (but in Plaut. Ps. 2, 1, 7 , the correct…

fraudŭlentus.opening: adj. fraus , cheating , deceitful , fraudulent (class.): ecquem recalvom ac silonem senem (vidistis), fraudulentum, Plaut. Rud. 2, 1, 12 : Carthaginienses fraudulenti et mendaces, Cic. Agr. 2, 35, 95 : homo, Auct. Her.…

fraudŭlōsus.opening: adj. id. , deceitful , fraudulent (post-class. and very rare): contrectatio, Dig. 47, 2, 1 .

fraus.opening: ( gen. plur. fraudium, Cic. Off. 3, 18, 75 ; id. Pis. 19, 44 ; Dig. 9, 2, 23, § 4 al. : fraudum, Tac. A. 6, 21 ; Gell. 14, 2, 6 ; Claud. Laud. Stil. 2, 214 ; archaic form dat. sing. frudi, Lucr. 6, 187 Lachm.; cf. acc.…

Fraus.opening: a deity , Cic. N. D. 3, 17, 44 . In the service of Mercury , as the god of thieves , Mart. Cap. 1, § 51 .

fraxĭnĕus.opening: adj. 1. fraxinus , of ash-wood , ashen : sudes, Verg. G. 2, 359 : trabes, id. A. 6, 181 : frons, Col. 6, 3, 6 : hasta, Ov. M. 5, 9 ; 12, 369 .

fraxĭnus.opening: adj. 1. fraxinus , of ash-wood , ashen (usually fraxineus): virga, Ov. H. 11, 76 .

Frĕgellae.opening: a very old city of the Volsci , in Latium , on the Liris , made a Roman colony B. C. 328, now Ceperano , Liv. 8, 22; 9, 12; Auct. Her. 4, 15, 22 ; 4, 27, 37 ; Sil. 8, 477 ; 12, 529 al. —Hence, A quarter of Rome…

Frĕgēnae.opening: , = φρεγηνία, ἡ , a small town of Etruria , near Alsium, now Maccarese , Plin. 3, 5, 8, § 51 ; Liv. 36, 3, 5 ; Vell. 1, 14 fin.

frĕmĕbundus.opening: adj. fremo , making a low roaring , growling , snorting , muttering , murmuring ( poet. ): tanta moles (Argo), Att. ap. Cic. N. D. 2, 35, 89 : illapsu (elephantorum), Sil. 3, 463 : tum vero praeceps (Achilles) curru…

frĕmĭtus.opening: id. , a dull , roaring sound , a rushing , resounding , murmuring , humming , snorting , loud noise (class.; syn.: crepitus, fremor, strepitus, stridor): omne sonabat Arbustum fremitu silvaï frondosaï, Enn. ap. Macr. S.…

frĕmo.grammar: ŭi, ĭtum, 3 v. n. and a.
frĕmo.opening: v. n. and a. [cf. βρέμω, βρόμος, βροντή ]. Neutr. , to make a low roaring , to roar , resound , to growl , murmur , rage , snort , howl (class.; syn.: frendo, strideo, strepo, crepo): (ventus ibi) Speluncas inter magnas…

frĕmor.opening: fremo , a low roaring , rushing , murmuring ( poet. and in postclass. prose for fremitus): arma sonant, fremor oritur, Poët. ap. Varr. L. L. 6, § 67 Müll.: variusque per ora cucurrit Ausonidūm fremor, Verg. A. 11, 297 ;…

frēnātĭo.opening: freno , a bridling , subduing : libidinis, August. Cont. Jul. 5, 7, 25 .

frēnātor.opening: id. , a curber , tamer , controller (post-Aug.). Lit. : (sol) ignipedum frenator equorum, Stat. Th. 1, 27 .— Poet. transf.: ingentis frenator Sarmata conti, i. e. a hurler, Val. Fl. 6, 162 .— Trop. : infinitae…

frendesco.opening: v. inch. [frendo], to begin to gnash with the teeth: crudelitate doloris, Fulg. Serm. 11 .

frendo.grammar: frendui, frēsum and fressum 3 v. n. and a.
frendo.opening: and , (v. infra), 2 and , v. n. and a. [cf. Gr. χρεμ-ίζω , to neigh, χρόμη ; Germ. greinen, grinsen, Fick, Vergl. Wörterb. p. 72]. Neutr. , to gnash the teeth (for syn. cf. fremo): ego illum male formidabam, ita…

frendor.opening: frendo , a gnashing (post-class.): dentium in Gehenna, Tert. Res. Carn. 35 fin. ; Veg. Vet. 3, 31 .

frēnĭger.opening: ( ), , adj. frenum-gero , bridle-bearing , bridled : ala, i. e. the cavalry, Stat. S. 5, 1, 98 .

frēno.opening: ( ), (archaic inf. pres. pass. frenarier, Prud. Psych. 191 ), v. a. frenum , to furnish with a bridle , to bridle (mostly in poets). Lit. : frenati equi, Hirt. B. G. 8, 15, 4 : equos, Verg. A. 5, 554 ; Hor. Ep. 1, 15,…

Frentāni.opening: a mixed Italian tribe of Samnites and Illyrians who settled in Samnium , on the Adriatic Sea , in the south-eastern part of what is now the Abruzzo Citra , Caes. B. C. 1, 23 fin. ; Cic. Clu. 69, 197 ; Liv. 9, 16 ; 45…

frēnum.opening: or , , , and more freq. (cf. Neue, Formenl. 1, 567; and v. infra ), plur. heterocl. , , , and mostly poet. , , root dhar-; Sanscr. dhar-ā-mi, hold, support; Gr. θρα-, in θρῆνυς, θρόνος; Lat. frētus , a bridle , curb ,…

frĕquens.opening: adj. root φρακ-, φράσσω, to enclose, make close; Lat. farcio, fartilis, etc.; cf. Germ. Berg, Burg , that takes place repeatedly , often , or frequently , often , frequent (class.; syn.: celeber, creber). Lit. Of…

frĕquentāmentum.opening: frequento , a repetition in speaking (post-class.), Gell. 1, 11, 12 ; 5, 1, 1 .

frĕquentātĭo.opening: frequento , frequency , frequent use , a crowding together. In gen. (very rare): matrimoniorum, Gell. 1, 6, 6 .— In partic., in rhet. lang. (esp. in Cic.): densa et continens verborum, Auct. Her. 4, 19, 27 :…

frĕquentātīvus.opening: adj. frequento , in the later gramm., that denotes the repetition of an act , frequentative : verba, Gell. 9, 6, 1 ; Diom. 336 P.: verborum qualitas, id. 335 P.— Adv. : , frequentatively , Fest. s. v. verberitare, p.…

frĕquentātor.opening: id. (postclass.), a frequent visitor , a frequenter (late Lat.): prandiorum et cenarum cum publicanis, Tert. Monog. 8 fin. (but in App. Trism. 94, 23 , the better read. is gubernator; v. Hildebr. ad h. l.).

frĕquentātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from frequento.

frĕquentĭa.opening: frequens, II. , an assembling in great numbers , a numerous attendance , concourse; and more freq. concr., a numerous assembly , multitude , crowd , throng (class.; a favorite expression of Cicero). With gen. : testis…

frĕquento.opening: v. a. frequens . (Acc. to frequens, I.) To visit or resort to frequently , to frequent; to do or make use of frequently , to repeat (class.): sermones eorum, qui frequentant domum meam, Cic. Fam. 5, 21, 1 : juventus,…

Fresilĭa.opening: a city of the Marsi , Liv. 10, 3, 5 .

frĕtāle.opening: a frying-pan : infunditur in fretali piper, etc., Apic. 7, 5, § 275 .

frĕtālis.opening: adj. fretum , of or belonging to a strait (post-class.): a Rhaetiarum exordio adusque fretalem Oceanum, the English Channel, Amm. 28, 2 .

frĕtum.opening: , and , , root φρυ, to be in uneasy motion, boil, flash; cf. Sanscr. bhur; Lat. ferveo , a strait , sound , channel. Lit. In gen. Form fretum: fretum dictum a similitudine ferventis aquae, quod in fretum saepe concurrat…

frētus.opening: 1. fretus , reliance , confidence (post-class.): animi tui fretu, Symm. Ep. 2, 82 .

frĭābĭlis.opening: adj. frio , easily broken , or crumbled to pieces , friable : tofus, Plin. 17, 4, 3, § 29 : sandaracha, id. 34, 18, 55, § 177 .

frĭcae.opening: a kind of stones in Sicily , Auct. Aetn. 526 .

frĭcāmentum.opening: frico , a rubbing (post-class.): blando articulorum uti, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 6, 27 ; id. Tard. 3, 2 .

frĭcātĭo.opening: id. , a rubbing , rubbing down , friction (post-Aug.): omnibus vertebris utilis est, Cels. 4, 3 : assidua, Col. 6, 12, 1 : vehemens, Plin. 28, 4, 14, § 53 : diligens tectoriorum, Vitr. 7, 6 .

frĭcātor.opening: id. , one who rubs (post-class.), Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 7, 92 .

frĭcātūra.opening: id. , a rubbing , rubbing down of walls (post-Aug.): exacta, Vitr. 7, 1, 4 .

frĭcātus.opening: id. , a rubbing , rubbing down (post-Aug.): emendat dentium vitia crebro fricatu, Plin. 23, 7, 63, § 124 ; 13, 15, 30, § 99 .

frĭcĭum.opening: id. , a powder for rubbing the teeth , tooth-powder , Plin. Val. 1, 36 ; cf. dentifricium.

frĭco.grammar: cŭi, ctum, and fricātum, 1 v. a.
frĭco.opening: (rarely) , v. a. Sanscr. ghar-, gharsh-, rub; Gr. χρίω, χρῖμα; Lat. frio; cf. Gr. χρίμπτω, χραίνω, to touch, color , to rub , rub down (not in Cic. or Caes.; cf.: perfrico, palpo, titillo): mulos qui fricabat, Poët. ap.…

frictĭo.opening: frico , a rubbing , rubbing down , friction of parts of the body: vehemens, lenis, Cels. 2, 14 : frictionem adhibere, id. ib. : frictione uti, id. ib. : frictionem lenem admovere, id. 3, 18 .

frictrix.opening: id. , she that rubs (cf. frico fin. ; post-class.), Tert. Pall. 4 fin. ; id. Res. Carn. 16 ; cf. tribas.

frictūra.opening: id. , a rubbing , in mal. part., App. M. Fragm. p. 717 Oud.

frictus.opening: frico , a rubbing : palmularis, Mart. Cap. 8, § 805 .—In mal. part., Juv. 6, 322 .

frīgēdo.opening: frigeo , cold , Varr. ap. Non. 139, 11 , and 206, 21.

frīgĕ-facto.opening: v. a. frigeo + facio , to make cold , to cool : os nunc frigefactas, Plaut. Poen. 3, 5, 15 ; id. Rud. 5, 2, 39 .

frīgĕo.opening: v. n. frigus , to be cold , chilly , to freeze (opp. calere, to be hot, to glow; whereas algere, subject., to feel cold, to freeze, is opp. aestuare, to feel hot; v. caleo and algeo; class.; esp. freq. in the trop.…

frīgĕro.opening: v. a. id. , to make cool , to cool , to refresh with coolness (very rare): frigerans Aganippe, Cat. 61, 30 : frigerandi cholerici, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 21, 208 .

frīgesco.opening: (frigui, Hier. Ep. 52 , no. 2), 3, v. inch. n. [frigeo], to become or grow cold , to be chilled (mostly ante-class. and post-Aug.; perh. not used by Cic.). Lit. : eodem addito oleum, postea fervefacito: infundito in…

frīgĭdārĭus.opening: adj. frigidus , of or for cooling : ahenum, i. e. to hold cold water, Vitr. 5, 10 : cella balinei, the coolingroom, Plin. Ep. 2, 17, 11 ; 5, 6, 25 sq.: maltha, Pall. 1, 41 : fistula, id. 1, 40 : cisterna, Petr. 73 .—…

frīgĭdātĭo.opening: frigido , a chilling , chilliness , translation of Gr. ψυχρότης , August. Categor. Decem. 12 .

frīgĭdĕ-facto.opening: , false read. in Plaut. Rud. 5, 2, 39 , inst. of frigefacto, q. v.

frīgĭdĭuscŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [frigidus], somewhat frigid : alia quoque ibidem congerit frigidiuscula, rather flat, stupid, Gell. 3, 10, 16 .

frīgĭdo.opening: v. a. id. , to make cold , to cool (post-class.): corpus, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 17 : plumbum tactu, id. ib. : membranam, id. ib. 1, 17, 168 .

frīgĭdŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [id.], somewhat cold ( poet. ): puella, Verg. Cir. 250 : ocelli, id. ib. 347 .—* Somewhat feeble or faint : singultus, Cat. 64, 131 .

frīgĭdus.opening: adj. frigeo , cold , cool , chill , chilling (opp. calidus; syn.: gelidus, algidus, glacialis; corresp. in most of its senses to the Gr. ψυχρός ). Lit. : calida et frigida, et amara et dulcia, Cic. Rep. 3, 8 fin. : fons…

frīgo.opening: (acc. to Diom. p. 369 P.), ctum (frixum, Sid. Ep. 8, 14 ), , v. a. cf. φρύγω , to roast , parch , fry (syn.: torreo, coquo): sesquilibram salis frigito, Cato, R. R. 106, 1 : frictae nuces, Plaut. Poen. 1, 2, 113 :…

frĭgo.opening: v. a. , acc. to Novius, i. q. erigo, to erect , Att. ap. Non. 308, 7 sq. and 7, 10 (Fragm. Trag. v. 441, 463 Rib.); Varr. ib.

frīgor.opening: frigeo , cold (late Lat.): molestissimus, Theod. Prisc. 2, 29 .—Also, (contr. from frigidor, from frigidus], Theod. Prisc. 2, 16 ; id. de Diaet.

frīgŏrĭfĭcus.opening: adj. frigus+facio , cooling (post-class.): acetum omnium maxime frigorificum est, Gell. 17, 8, 14 .

frīgŏro.opening: v. a. frigus , to cool down (post-class.): cholericos, Cael. Aur. Tard. 4, 4 ; id. Acut. 3, 21, 208 .

frĭgŭlo.opening: v. n. , a word denoting the natural note of the jackdaw: graculus at frigulat, Auct. Carm. Philom. 28.

frīgus.opening: Gr. ῥῖγος, cold, ῥιγέω; the connection with Lat. rĭgeo, rĭgor, is doubtful, Georg Curtius Gr. Etym. 353; Corss. Ausspr. 1, 451 , cold , coldness , coolness (for syn. cf.: algor, gelu, rigor, glacies, pruina). Lit. In…

frīguscŭlum.opening: dim. frigus , slight cold (post-class.). Lit. , Tert. de Anim. 25 .— Trop. , coolness , variance , disagreement between man and wife: quid si divortium non intercesserit, sed frigusculum? profecto valebit donatio, si…

frĭgūtĭo.opening: ( , , , , ), , v. n. and a. [a lengthened form of 2. frigo], to twitter , chirp. Lit. , of birds: merulae in remotis tesquis frigutiunt, App. Flor. p. 358, 22 : fringulit et graculus, Poët. ap. Anthol. Lat, 5, 43, 124.—…

fringilla.opening: (also and ), , , a small bird , perh. the robin redbreast , Motacilla rubecula, Linn.; acc. to others, the chaffinch , Fringilla coelebs, Linn.; Varr. L. L. 7, § 104 ; Mart. 9, 55, 7 ; Paul. ex Fest. p. 90 Müll.

Frinĭātes.opening: a Ligurian people on the northern slope of the Apennines , Liv. 39, 2, 1 ; 9 .

frĭo.opening: v. a. , to rub , break or crumble into small pieces : terra, quae facile frietur, Varr. R. R. 1, 9, 7 : glaebis terrarum saepe friatis, Lucr. 1, 888 : ut inter se tritum tarde frietur, Plin. 12, 19, 42, § 92 ; 34, 12,…

Frīsĭi.opening: φρίσιοι or φρείσιοι , Ptol. and Dio Cass., in the Middle Ages Frisones and Fresones, the Frisians , a people of northern Germany , between the Rhine and the Ems , in the modern West Friesland , Plin. 4, 15, 27, § 101 ;…

frit.opening: ( ) vocatur illud summa in spica jam matura, quod est minus quam granum, Varr. R. R. 1, 48, 3 .

frĭtillus.opening: a box from which the dice were thrown , a dice-box , Mart. 14, 1, 3 ; 4, 14, 8 ; Juv. 14, 5 ; Sen. Apocol. fin.

frĭtinnĭo.opening: v. n. , to twitter or chirp as a small bird. Lit. : et pullos peperit fritinnientes, Varr. ap. Non. 7, 15 ; of the cicada: et cuculi cuculant et rauca cicada fritinnit, Auct. Carm. Phil. 35.— Transf. , of the noise made…

Frīvŏlārĭa.opening: the title of a comedy of Plautus , of which only a few fragments have been preserved.

frīvŏlus.opening: adj. etym. dub.; perh. from frico , silly , empty , trifling , frivolous; pitiful , sorry , worthless (mostly post-Aug.; perh. not in Cic.; cf. futtilis). Adj. : frivolus hic quidem jam et illiberalis est sermo, Auct.…

frixo.opening: v. freq. [1. frigo], to roast thoroughly , Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 11, 77 .

frixōrĭum.opening: id. , a frying-pan , Plin. Val. 2, 7 ; cf. frixorium, τήγανον , Vet. Gloss. Cf. the foll. art.

frixūra.opening: id. , a frying-pan , Ven. Carm. 6, 10, 13. Cf. the preced. art.

frondārĭus.opening: adj. 1. frons , of or for leaves , leaf- : fiscinae, Plin. 18, 31, 74, § 314 .

frondātĭo.opening: 1. frons , a stripping off of leaves , a pruning , Col. 5, 6, 16 .

frondātor.opening: id. , one who strips off leaves , a leaf-stripper , a dresser , pruner of trees, etc., Verg. E. 1, 57 ; Ov. M. 14, 649 ; Plin. 18, 31, 74, § 314 .

frondĕo.opening: v. n. id. , to have or put forth leaves , to be in leaf , to become green : cum jam per terras frondent atque omnia florent, Lucr. 5, 214 : nunc frondent silvae, Verg. E. 3, 57 ; Ov. Am. 2, 6, 49 : vitis multa materia…

frondesco.opening: (acc. to Prisc. p. 768 P.), 3, v. inch. n. [frondeo], to become leafy , to put forth leaves , to shoot out. Lit. (class.): caelum nitescere, arbores frondescere, Vites pampinis pubescere, etc., Enn. ap. Cic. Tusc. 1,…

frondĕus.opening: adj. 1. frons , of leaves , covered with leaves , leafy : nemora, Verg. A. 1, 191 : Romulus frondea (corona) coronavit Hostilium, Plin. 16, 4, 5, § 11 : tecta, leafy coverts , poet. for trees in full leaf , Verg. G. 4,…

frondĭcŏmus.opening: adj. 1. fronscoma , leafy : locis habitare, Prud. Cath. 3, 102 .

frondĭfer.opening: (anciently also ), , adj. 1. frons-fero , leaf-bearing , leafy ( poet. ): frundiferi loci, Naev. ap. Non. 323, 1 (Trag. Rel. v. 25 Rib.): nemus, Lucr. 2, 359 ; Sen Oedip. 276: silvae, Lucr. 1, 256 : domus avium, id. 1,…

frondĭflŭus.opening: adj. 1. frons-fluo , leaf-falling , i. e. when the leaves fall off : brumae frigore, Boëth. Cons. 1, 5, 14.

frondōsus.opening: (anciently also ), , adj. 1. frons , full of leaves , leafy : omne sonabat Arbustum fremitu silvaï frondosaï, Enn. ap. Macr. S. 6, 2 ( id. Ann. v. 197 Vahl.); so, montes, Varr. R. R. 2, 5, 11 : vertex (collis), Verg. A.…

frons.opening: ( masc. , Cato ap. Gell. 15, 9, 5 ; and ap. Fest. s. v. recto, p. 286, b, Müll.; Plaut. Mil. 2, 2, 46 Ritschl, N. cr.; id. ap. Non. 205, 4 ; Caecil. ap. Gell. 15, 9, 3 ; Vitr. 10, 17 ) [cf. Sanscr. brhū; Gr. ὀφρύς ;…

frontālĭa.opening: 2. frons , an ornament for the forehead , frontlet , of horses, Liv. 37, 40, 4 ; Plin. 37, 12, 74, § 194 ; Amm. 23, 4 .

frontāti.opening: (sc. lapides) [2. frons, I. B. 1.], in architect., stones that go from one side of a wall to the other , and are faced both ways , binding-stones , copingstones , Vitr. 2, 8, 7 .

Frontīnus.opening: a Roman surname. So esp., Sex. Julius Frontinus, superintendent of the Roman aqueducts under Nerva , in the latter half of the first century of the Christian era; author of the works De Aquis Urbis Romae, Strategetica,…

fronto.opening: amplif. [2. frons], one who has a broad forehead : ecquos naevum habere? ecquos silos, flaccos, frontones, capitones? Cic. N. D. 1, 29, 80 .—Hence,

Fronto.opening: a proper name. So esp.: M. Cornelius Fronto, a famous Roman orator from Cirta , in Numidia , who lived about A. D. 90-168. Small portions of his writings have been discovered in palimpsests by Angelo Mai. — Deriv. , ,…

frontōsus.opening: adj. 2. frons , manybrowed , having several foreheads. Lit. , said of Janus: frontosior, Aug. Civ. D. 1, 4 fin. — Trop. , that has a bold forehead , shameless (late Lat.), Aug. Serm. in Psa. 1, 68 .

fructēta.opening: , a later form for frutecta, bushes , thickets : arbusta, fructeta scholastici vocabant, Serv. Verg. E. 1, 40 .

fructĭfer.opening: adj. fructus + fero , fruit-bearing , fruitful (post-Aug. for the class. frugifer): arbores, Col. 11, 2, 46 ; Plin. 12, 25, 54, § 112 : sarmentum, Pall. Febr. 29, 3 ; Vulg. Act. 14, 16 .

fructĭfĭcātĭo.opening: fructifico , a bearing of fruit (post - class.), Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 39 fin.

fructĭfĭco.opening: v. n. fructus+facio , to bear fruit (post-class.): laurus fructificat, Calp. Ecl. 4, 91 ; Tert. Res. Carn. 52 ; Vulg. Marc. 4, 20 al.

fructŭārĭus.opening: adj. fructus . of or belonging to fruit , fruit-bearing , fruitful : palmes, Col. 5, 6, 29 ; Plin. 17, 22, 35, § 181 : rami olcae, Col. 5, 9, 15 : oculi vitis, id. 3, 18, 4 : pars villae, that serves for laying up the…

fructŭōsus.opening: adj. fructus, 2. , abounding in fruit , fruitful , productive; profitable , advantageous (very freq. and class.; syn.: fertilis, frugifer). Lit. : ager quamvis fertilis sine cultura fructuosus esse non potest, Cic.…

fructus.opening: (archaic gen. sing. fructuis, Varr. ap. Non. 492, 14 ; id. R. R. 1, 2, 19 ; cf. Gell. 4, 16 : fructi, Cato, R. R. 4 ; Ter. Ad. 5, 4, 16 ; Turp. ap. Non. 491, 7 ), fruor , an enjoying , enjoyment. In abstracto. Lit.…

frūgālis.opening: adj. frux . * Of or belonging to fruits : maturitas, App. de Mundo, p. 71, 29.— (Acc. to frugi, v. frux, II. B.) Economical , thrifty , temperate , frugal , provident , careful; and in gen., worthy , virtuous; only in…

frūgālĭtas.opening: frugalis, II. , economy , temperance , thriftiness , frugality; and in gen., worth , virtue (the Gr. σωφροσύνη ; class.). Prop.: omnes in illo sunt rege virtutes, sed praecipue singularis et admiranda frugalitas ... ego…

frūgesco.opening: v. inch. n. [frux], to bear fruit , be fruitful (post-class.), Prud. adv. Symm. 2, 913 ; so with florescere, Tert. Res. Carn. 22 .

frūgĭfer.opening: (archaic gen. sing. fem. frugiferaï, Enn. ap. Charis. p. 7 P.; cf. Mart. 11, 90, 5 , and v. infra ), adj. frux + fero , fruit-bearing , fruitful , fertile (class.). Lit. : ut agri non omnes frugiferi sunt, qui coluntur,…

frūgĭfĕrens.opening: adj. id. , fruitbearing , fruitful (for the class. frugifer): terrae, Lucr. 1, 3 .

frūgĭlĕgus.opening: adj. frux+lego , fruit-gathering , a poet. epithet of the ant: formicae, Ov. M. 7, 624 .

frūgĭpărus.opening: adj. id. , fruitbearing , fruitful ( poet. ; ante- and postclass.): fetus, Lucr. 6, 1 : vultus (temporum), Avien. Arat. 1054 .

frūgĭperdus.opening: adj. frux + perdo , fruit-losing , a transl. of the Homeric ὠλεσίκαρπος , salix, Plin. 16, 26, 46, § 110 (cf. Hom. Odyss. 10, 510).

fruĭtĭo.opening: fruor , enjoyment , Hier. in Philem. 1, 20 al.

frūmen.opening: fruor (post-class.). * A gruel or porridge made of corn , and used in sacrifices , Arn. 7, 230 .— = λάρυγξ , the larynx , throat , Don. Ter. Phorm. 2, 2, 18 ; id. Ad. 5, 8, 27 ; Serv. Verg. G. 1, 74 , and A. 1, 178;…

frūmentācĕus.opening: adj. frumentum , of corn or grain , corn - (late Lat.): farina, Veg. Vet. 2, 57 : panes, Hier. Ep. 37, 4 .

frūmentālis.opening: adj. id. , = frumentarius, Cassiod. in Psa. 34, 21 .

frūmentārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to corn , corn-; milit., of or belonging to provisions , provision- : ager, Varr. R. R. 1, 11, 2 ; cf. campus, id. ib. 1, 7, 9 : res, corn, provisions, Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 5, § 11 ; Caes. B. G.…

frūmentātĭo.opening: frumentor . A providing of corn , milit., a foraging , Caes. B. G. 6, 39, 1 ; Suet. Galb. 20 .—In plur. : pabulationes frumentationesque, Caes. B. G. 7, 16, 3 ; 7, 64, 2 .— A distribution of corn , Suet. Aug. 40 ; 42 ;…

frūmentātor.opening: id. , a provider of corn , purchaser of grain : in Volscis frumentum ne emi quidem potuit; periculum ipsis frumentatoribus fuit, Liv. 2, 34, 4 .— Milit. t. t. , a forager , Liv. 31, 36, 8 ; ib. § 9 al.

frūmentor.opening: v. dep. n. and a. [frumentum]. Neutr. , milit. t. t., to fetch corn , to forage , purvey : erat eodem tempore et materiari et frumentari et tantas munitiones fieri necesse, Caes. B. G. 7, 73, 1 : cum in propinquo agro…

frūmentum.opening: contr. from frugimentum, from FRVG, v. fruor; fruit, κατʼ ἐξοχήν, i. e. , corn , grain (class.; in sing. usually of corn harvested): Julianus scribit: frumentum id esse, quod arista in se teneat, recte Gallum definisse:…

frūniscor.opening: v. dep. n. [a lengthened form of fruor], to enjoy (anteand post-class.); constr. with acc.; rarely with abl. : (Q. Claudius Quadrigiarius) Domus, inquit, suas quemque ire jubet et sua omnia frunisci ... ut fatiscor a…

frŭor.opening: ( perf. fruitus est, Dig. 7, 4, 29 : fruiti sumus, Sen. Ep. 93, 7 : fructus sum, Vell. 2, 104, 3 ; Lucr. 3, 940 ; v. Neue, Formenl. 2, 562; part. fut. fruiturus, v. in the foll. ; imp. FRVIMINO, Inscr. Orell. 3121 ; as…

Frŭsĭno.opening: a city of the Hernici , in Latium , situated on the Via Latina , now Frosinone , Liv. 27, 37 ; Juv. 3, 224 .— Deriv.: , , adj. , of or belonging to Frusino : ager, Liv. 26, 9 : fundus, in the neighborhood of Frusino,…

frustātim.opening: adv. frustum , piecemeal , in pieces (very rare): objectare leonibus prandium, Pompon. ap. Non. 113, 7 : coquitur in olla, aut frustatim in patinis, Plin. 20, 9, 39, § 99 ; Prud. Psych. 720 .

frustillātim.opening: adv. frustillum , in small pieces , in little bits (ante-class.): nisi mihi virgo redditur, Jam ego te faciam ut hic formicae frustillatim differant, Plaut. Curc. 4, 4, 20 ; Poët. ap. Non. 112, 8 .

frustillum.opening: dim. frustum , a small piece , little bit (ante-class.): parvula, Arn. 7, 231 : ignea, id. 2, 84 .

frusto.opening: v. a. , to break to pieces : cum Punicae praedae omnibus promontoriis insulisque frustarentur et fluitarent, etc., i. e. the booty taken from the Carthaginians went to wreck and was driven in pieces on the promontories,…

frustrā.opening: ( , Prud. στεφ . 1, 13), adv. orig. acc. plur. neutr., afterwards abl. sing. fem. of frusterus, for frud-; v. fraus; hence . In deception, in error (so mostly anteclass. and in historians; not in Cic. and Caes.): ambo,…

frustrābĭlis.opening: adj. frustror , that will be disappointed , vain , deceitful (post-class.): exspectatio, Arn. 2, 58 : res, id. 6, 206 .

frustrāmen.opening: id. , deception : nos in fraudem induimus frustraminis ipsi, Lucr. 4, 817 .

frustrātĭo.opening: id. , a deceiving , deception , disappointment , frustration (rare; not used by Cicero): in horunc familiam Hodie frustrationem iniciam maximam, Plaut. Am. 3, 1, 15 ; so, frustrationes dare (with ludificare), id. Most.…

frustrātor.opening: id. , a deceiver; delayer (post-class.): judicum, Symm. Ep. 10, 44 ; Dig. 43, 16, 19 .

frustrātōrĭus.opening: adj. frustrator , deceptive , deceitful (post-class.): somnia, Tert. Anim. 47 : aures, Arn. 7, 219 : appellatio, Dig. 22, 1, 41 .

frustrātus.opening: frustror , a deceiving , deception : aliam invenito, quam habeas frustratui, Plaut. Men. 4, 3, 21 .

frustror.opening: v. dep.; also: , , v. a. frustra , to deceive , disappoint , trick , frustrate (syn.: decipio, deludo, fraudo, fallo, etc.). Lit. (class.). In the dep. form: nescio quis praestigiator hanc frustratur mulierem, Plaut.…

frustŭlentus.opening: adj. frustum , full of small pieces : aqua, i. e. filled with crumbs, Plaut. Curc. 2, 3, 34 .

frustŭlum.opening: dim. id. , a small piece , little bit (post-class.): frustulum panis, App. M. 1, p. 110, 34 .

frustum.opening: a piece , bit (syn.: fragmentum, segmentum). Lit. , of food (class.): frusto panis conduci potest, vel uti taceat, vel uti loquatur, Cato ap. Gell. 1, 15, 10 : necesse est, offa objecta cadere frustum ex pulli ore cum…

frŭtectōsus.opening: (also ), , adj. frutectum , full of bushes or shrubs , shrubby , bushy , bosky : nemorosi frutectosique tractus, Col. 2, 2, 11 : smilax spinosis frutectosa ramis, Plin. 16, 35, 63, § 153 ; 16, 37, 71, § 179 .

frŭtectum.opening: or , , contr. from fruticetum , a place full of shrubs or bushes. Lit. : ager frutectis aut arboribus obsessus, Col. 3, 11, 3 : rosa silvestris in frutecto, Plin. 25, 2, 6, § 17 : tenebrosa, Prud. adv. Symm. 2, 872 :…

frŭtex.opening: ( fem. : Nilotica, Mart. Cap. 3, § 225 ) [prob. kindr. with βρύω , to sprout forth], a shrub , bush (cf. arbor). Lit. : ex surculo vel arbor procedit, ut olea, ficus, pirus; vel frutex, ut violae, rosae, arundines; vel…

frŭtĭcātĭo.opening: fruticor , a springing forth of shoots , a sprouting out (very rare): inutilis, Plin. 17, 1, 1, § 7 .

frŭtĭcesco.opening: v. inch. n. [frutex], to put forth shoots , to sprout , become bushy (very rare): quia (hae arbores) celeriter fruticescunt, Plin. 17, 27, 45, § 257 .

frŭtĭcētum.opening: id. , a place full of shrubs or bushes , a thicket , covert , Hor. C. 3, 12, 12 (10); Suet. Ner. 48 ; cf. frutectum and fructeta.

frŭtĭco.opening: (ū long in frūtĭcăt arbor, Tert. Judic. Dom. 135 ), , v. n. , and , , v. dep. n. [id.], to put forth shoots , to sprout out , to become bushy. Lit. : excisa est arbor, non evulsa: itaque, quam fruticetur, vides, Cic.…

frŭtĭcōsus.opening: adj. id. , full of shrubs or bushes , shrubby , bushy : vimina, Ov. M. 6, 344 : (aizoum) a radice, Plin. 25, 13, 102, § 161 : arbor (terebinthus), id. 13, 6, 12, § 54 : rutae rami fruticosiores, id. 20, 13, 51, § 131 :…

Frūtis.opening: (Etrusc. form ; v. in the foll. ), an Etruscan modification of the Gr. Ἀφροδίτη , an Etruscan name of Venus : Veneri matri, quae Frutis dicitur, Sol. 2, 14 .—Hence: , , : templum Veneris Fruti, Paul. ex Fest. p. 90 Müll.

frux.opening: , and more freq. in plur. , (also in nom. sing. : frugi rectus est natura frux, at secundum consuetudinem dicimus, ut haec avis, haec ovis, sic haec frugis, Varr. L. L. 9, § 76 dub.), from the root FRUG; v. fruor ,…

fūcātē.opening: adv. , v. fuco, P. a. fin.

fūcātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from fuco.

fūcĭlis.opening: falsa: dicta autem quasi fucata, Paul. ex Fest. p. 92 Müll. N. cr.

fūcĭnus.opening: adj. 1. fucus , colored with orchil : si adhibeas fucinis sulphura, Quint. 12, 10, 76 Spald. N. cr.

Fūcĭnus.opening: a lake of Latium , in the territory of the Marsi , now Lago Fucino or Lago di Celano , Verg. A. 7, 759 ; Mart. de Spect. 28, 11 ; more freq. called Lacus Fucinus, Liv. 4, 57, 7 ; Plin. 3, 12, 17, § 108 ; 36, 15, 24, §…

fūco.opening: v. a. 1. fucus , to color , paint , dye. In gen.: Alba nec Assyrio fucatur lana veneno, Verg. G. 2, 465 ; so, vellera Milesia saturo hyali colore, id. ib. 4, 334 : tabulas colore, Tac. A. 2, 14 : pinnas vario veneno,…

fūcōsus.opening: adj. id. , painted , colored , beautified , counterfeit , spurious (Ciceron.): visae merces, fallaces quidem et fucosae, chartis et linteis et vitro delatae, Cic. Rab. Post. 14, 40 : vicinitas non assueta mendaciis, non…

fue.opening: or (or , acc. to Charis. p. 213 P.), interj. , denoting aversion, foh! fie! fu! Plaut. Most. 1, 1, 37 ; id. Ps. 5, 2, 5 .

Fūfĭdĭus.opening: name of a Roman gens. So, Fufidius, Cic. Pis. 35, 86 ; another of the same name, id. Q. Fr. 3, 1, 2 : L. Fufidius, an orator, id. Brut. 30, 113 ; cf. Ruhnk. Vell. 2, 16, 2 : Q. Fufidius, a knight, of Arpinum, Cic. Fam.…

Fūfĭus.opening: name of a Roman gens. So esp., Q. Fufius Calenus, a tribune of the people , A. U. C. 692, Cic. Fam. 5, 6, 1 ; id. Att. 1, 14, 6 ; id. Prov. Cons. 19, 46 ; id. Sest. 15, 33 ; id. Pis. 4, 9 ; from whom the Fufia lex…

fŭga.opening: (archaic gen. sing. fugaï, Lucr. 1, 1047 ; 4, 713 ), Sanscr. bhug'-, bend; Gr. φεύγω, φυγή, flight, φύζα, terror; Germ. biegen, bend. On fugere and flectere, AngloSax. būgan and fleon; Germ. biegen and fliehen, v.…

fŭgālĭa.opening: fuga , a festival celebrated on the 24 th of February , to commemorate the expulsion of the kings , the flight of the kings , Aug. Civ. D. 2, 6 ; cf. regifugium.

fŭgātor.opening: fugo , he who puts to flight (post-class.): mortis, Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 10 .

fŭgātrix.opening: fugator , she that puts to flight (post-class.): dilectio fugatrix timoris, Tert. adv. Gnost. 12 .

fŭgax.opening: adj. fugio , apt to flee , flying swiftly , swift , fleet (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; cf. fugitivus). Lit. : fugaces Lyncas et cervos cohibentis arcu, Hor. C. 4, 6, 33 ; so, caprea, Verg. A. 10, 724 : ferae,…

fŭgēla.opening: id. , flight (ante-and postclass. for fuga): maxima, Cato ap. Prisc. p. 601 P.: magna, App. Mag. p. 336, 8 .

fŭgĭens.opening: Part. and P. a. , from fugio.

fŭgĭo.opening: ( gen. plur. part. sync. fugientum, Hor. C. 3, 18, 1 ; part. fut. fugiturus, Ov. H. 2, 47 al. ), , v. n. and a. [root FUG; Gr. ΦΥΓ, φεύγω ; Sanscr. bhuj; syn.: flecto, curvo; v. fuga], to flee or fly , to take flight ,…

fŭgĭtans.opening: Part. and P. a. , from fugito.

fŭgĭtīvārĭus.opening: fugitivus . One employed to catch and bring back fugitive slaves , a slave-catcher , Flor. 3, 19, 7 ; Dig. 19, 5, 18 .— Transf. : (cochleae) aquā finiendae, ne fugitivarius sit parandus, that they may not crawl away ,…

fŭgĭtīvus.opening: adj. fugio , fleeing away , fugitive; usually subst. : , , , a fugitive , runaway , deserter. Adj. : dicitur mihi tuus servus anagnostes fugitivus cum Vardaeis esse, runaway slave , Vat. ap. Cic. Fam. 5, 9, 2 ; so,…

fŭgĭto.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. freq. a. and n.
fŭgĭto.opening: v. freq. a. and n. fugio , to flee eagerly or in haste (mostly ante-class.). Neutr. : ita miserrimus fui fugitando, ne quis me cognosceret, Ter. Eun. 5, 2, 8 : Graeci fugitantes, Amm. 15, 9, 5 .— Act. , to flee , avoid…

fŭgĭtor.opening: fugio , one who flees or runs away , Plaut. Trin. 3, 2, 97 .

fŭgo.opening: v. a. id. , to cause to flee , to put to flight , drive or chase away , to rout , discomfit (rare but class.): qui homines inermes armis, viris, terrore repulerit, fugarit, averterit, Cic. Caecin. 12, 33 ; cf.: fugatus,…

fulcīmen.opening: fulcio , a prop , support , pillar ( poet. and very rare): terra nullo fulcimine nixa, Ov. F. 6, 269 . Cf. the foll. art.

fulcīmentum.opening: id. , a prop , stay , support (post-class.), App. M. 1, p. 109 med. ; Macr. S. 7, 9 ; Dig. 33, 7, 12, § 19 .

Fulcīnius.opening: name of a Roman gens: C. Fulcinius, Cic. Phil. 9, 2 : M. Fulcinius, id. Caecin. 4, 11 .

fulcĭo.opening: (late form perf. FVLCIVIT, Inscr. ap. Mur. 466, 3.— Part. perf. : fulcītus, Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 1, 46 ), v. a. etym. dub.; cf.: falx, flccto; Corss. refers it to root dhar-; v. firmus, Ausspr. 1, 476 , to prop up , to…

fulcĭpĕdĭa.opening: fulcio-pes , propfoot , of a drunken woman, who needs support, Petr. 75, 6 .

fulcrum.opening: fulcio , the post or foot of a couch (a bed or an eating-couch), a bedpost : eburnum, Prop. 2, 13, 21 (3, 5, 5 M.); Ov. P. 3, 3, 14 ; Gell. 10, 15, 14 : tricliniorum pedibus fulcrisque, Plin. 34, 2, 4, § 9 : aurea…

Fulfŭlae.opening: a city of the Samnites , Liv. 24, 20, 5 .

fulgens.opening: Part. and P. a. , from fulgeo.

fulgenter.opening: adv. , v. fulgeo, P. a. fin.

Fulgentĭus.opening: , Fabius Planciades Fulgentius, a Roman mythographer and grammarian in the beginning of the sixth century of the Christian era.

fulgeo.opening: (ante-class. and poet. form acc. to the third conj.: fulgit, Lucil. and Pompon. ap. Non. 506, 8 and 9; Lucr. 5, 768 Lachm. N. cr.; 6, 160; 174; 214; fulgĕre, Pac., Att., Lucil. ap. Non. 506, 17 sq. ; Lucr. 5, 1095 ; 6,…

fulgesco.opening: v. inch. n. [fulgeo], to flash , to glitter : solis radiatione fulgescere, Firm. Astr. 1, 4 fin.

fulgē^trum.opening: ( fem. plur. acc. fulgetras, Plin. 28, 2, 5, § 25 .—Post-class. plur. fulgitrua, Hyg. F. 183 , unless we should read fulgetra), fulgeo , heat-lightning , lightning : Heraclitus existimat fulgurationem esse velut apud…

fulgĭdŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [fulgidus], shining a little , somewhat bright , Ter. Maur. p. 2388 P.

fulgĭdus.opening: adj. fulgeo , flashing , glittering , shining (ante- and post-class.): lumina, Lucr. 3, 363 : acies ornatu fulgida Martis, Claud. in Ruf. 2, 351 ; Anthol. Lat. 5, 41, 15 .— Comp. : fulgidier radio, Ven. Carm. 8, 5 fin.

Fulgĭnĭa.opening: a city of Umbria , between Perusia and Spoletium , now Foligno , Sil. 8, 462 ; Inscr. Orell. 2409 .— Deriv. , , adj. , of or belonging to Fulginia , Fulginian : municipium, Cic. Fragm. ap. Prisc. p. 768 P.: in…

fulgor.opening: fulgeo , lightning , a flash of lightning (mostly poet. for fulgur): fulgorem quoque cernimus ante Quam tonitrum accipimus, Lucr. 6, 170 Lachm. N. cr.; so ib. 217 ; Verg. A. 8, 524 ; Ov. M. 7, 619 .—In plur. : prospera…

Fulgŏra.opening: fulgur , a goddess who presided over lightning , Sen. ap. Aug. Civ. D. 6, 10 .

fulgur.opening: (also in the nom. FVLGVS, acc. to Fest. s. v. fulgere, p. 92 fin. Müll. N. cr. ), , fulgeo , flashing lightning , lightning. Prop. (=splendor fulminis, opp. fulmen, a thunderbolt): fulgur, ignis qui coruscat fulmine,…

fulgŭrālis.opening: adj. fulgur , of or relating to lightning : Etruscorum et haruspicini et fulgurales et rituales libri, treating of lightning as an omen, Cic. Div. 1, 33, 72 ; Amm. 23, 5, 13 .

fulgŭrātĭo.opening: fulguro , sheetlightning , lightning : fulguratio est late ignis explicitus: fulmen est coactus ignis et impetu jactus, Sen. Q. N. 2, 16 ; 2, 12 ; 21 ; 56.—In plur. : nubes mediocriter collisae fulgurationes faciunt:…

fulgŭrātor.opening: fulgur . A priest who interprets and propitiates lightning , a lightning-interpreter : fulguratores, ut extispices et haruspices, ita hi fulgurum inspectores. Cato de moribus Claudii Neronis: haruspicem, fulguratorem si…

fulgŭrātūra.opening: fulguro , the interpretation of lightnings (late Lat.): Etrusci libri de fulguratura, Serv. Verg. A. 1, 42 .

fulgŭrĕus.opening: adj. fulgur , full of lightning , charged with lightning (late Lat.): nubes, Mart. Cap. 5, § 427 .

fulgŭrĭo.grammar: īvi, ītum, 4 v. n. and a.
fulgŭrĭo.opening: v. n. and a. [fulgur] (ante-class.). Neutr. , to hurl lightnings , to lighten : suo sonitu claro fulgurivit Juppiter, Naev. ap. Non. 110, 17 (Trag. Rel. v. 13 Rib.).— Act. , to strike with lightning; only in the part.…

fulgŭro.opening: v. impers. [id.], to lighten (less freq. than fulgeo; in many MSS. the reading oscillates between the two words; cf. Spald. and Zumpt ad Quint. 2, 16, 19 , and Mos. and Orell. ad Cic. N. D. 2, 25, 65 ). Lit. : noctu…

fŭlĭca.opening: (also , , Cic. poët. Div. 1, 8, 14), , a coot , a water-fowl, Plin. 11, 37, 44, § 122 al. ; Verg. G. 1, 363 ; Ov. M. 8, 625 .

fūlīgĭnātus.opening: adj. fuligo , painted with a black powder , powdered black (late Lat.): orbes oculorum, Hier. Ep. 10 .

fūlīgĭnĕus.opening: adj. fuligo , like soot , sooty : color, Arn. 7, 254 : nubes, Petr. 108, 2 .

fūlīgĭnōsus.opening: adj. id. , full of soot , sooty (post-class.): Lares, Prud. στεφ . 10, 261.

fūlīgo.opening: cf. fumus; v. Fick, Vergl. Wörterb. p. 104 , soot. Lit. : os oblitum fuligine, Plaut. Poen. 5, 4, 36 : quasi fuligine abstersa, Cic. Phil. 2, 36, 91 ; Col. 11, 3, 60 ; Verg. E. 7, 50 : lucubrationum bibenda, Quint. 11,…

fullo.opening: A fuller , cloth-fuller , Plaut. Aul. 3, 5, 34 ; Plin. 28, 6, 18, § 66 ; Mart. 6, 93, 1 ; Dig. 12, 7, 2 ; Gai. Inst. 3, 143 ; 162 al. —In mal. part.: comprimere fullonem, Nov. ap. Prisc. p. 879 P. (Com. Rel. v. 95…

fullōnĭcus.opening: adj. fullo , of or belonging to fullers. Adj. : pila, Cato, R. R. 10, 5 ; 14, 2 .— Subst. : , , (Sc. ars.) The fuller's craft , fulling : si non didicisti fullonicam, Plaut. As. 5, 2, 57 (dub. fulloniam, Fleck.):…

fullōnĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to fullers. Adj. : ars, the art of fulling, Plin. 7, 56, 57, § 196 : creta, fuller's earth, id. 17, 8, 4, § 46 : aenae, id. 24, 13, 68, § 111 : saltus, a jumping in fulling, Sen. Ep. 15…

fulmen.opening: contr. from fulgimen, v. fulgeo , lightning that strikes or sets on fire , a thunderbolt (opp. fulgur, lightning). Lit. : placet Stoicis, eos anhelitus terrae cum se in nubem induerint ejusque tenuissimam quamque partem…

fulmenta.opening: contr. from fulcimenta, from fulcio (ante-class.), a prop , support of a building, Cato, R. R. 14, 1 .— In partic., the heel of a shoe, Lucil. ap. Non. 206, 26 ; Plaut. Trin. 3, 2, 94 .

fulmentum.opening: , i. contr. from fulcimentum, from fulcio , a prop , support. In gen., Vitr. 5, 1 fin. : porticus fulmentis Aquitanicis superba, i. e. columns, Sid. Ep. 2, 10 in Carm. — In partic., a bedpost : Cels. 2, 15 .—Prov.:…

fulmĭnātĭo.opening: fulmino , a darting of lightning , a lightning : fulguratio ostendit ignem, fulminatio emittit, Sen. Q. N. 2, 12 init.

fulmĭnātor.opening: id. , lightninghurler , a post-class. designation of Jupiter, Arn. 6, 207 .

fulmĭnātrix.opening: , false read. for fulminata, v. fulminatus.

fulmĭnātus.opening: adj. fulmino , provided with thunder-bolts , bearing thunder : legio XII. fulminata, probably because their shields bore the device of Jupiter brandishing the thunder-bolt, Inscr. Orell. 517 ; 3174 ; Inscr. Murat. 869,…

fulmĭnĕus.opening: adj. fulmen , of or belonging to lightning ( poet. ). Lit. : ignis, Lucr. 2, 382 ; Ov. M. 11, 524 ; id. P. 2, 2, 118 : ictus, Hor. C. 3, 16, 11 ; Ov. M. 14, 618 : fragor, Val. Fl. 2, 501 .— Trop. * Sparkling , splendid…

fulmĭno.opening: v. n. and a. [id.]. Neutr. , to lighten , to hurl lightnings; hence, impers. : fulminat, it lightens ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose, for the class. fulgeo): at Boreae de parte trucis cum fulminat, Verg. G. 1, 370 :…

fultor.opening: fulcio , a supporter , support , prop (late lat.); trop.: ecclesiae, Venant. Carm. 2, 15, 19.

fultūra.opening: id. , a prop , stay , support (perh. not ante-Aug.). Lit. : fundamenta pro fultura et substructione fungentur, Col. 1, 5, 9 .—In plur. : Vitr. 10, 22 fin. — Transf. , a strengthening , refreshing (cf. fulcio, I. B.):…

fulvaster.opening: adj. fulvus , yellowish (post-class.): radix, App. Herb. 109 .

Fulvĭus.opening: name of a Roman gens, Cic. Planc. 8, 20 . So esp., M. Fulvius Flaccus, a friend of C. Gracchus , who lost his life with him , Cic. Brut. 28, 108 ; id. Cat. 1, 2, 4 ; 1, 12, 29 ; id. Phil. 8, 4, 14 ; Liv. Epit. 59 .— M.…

fulvus.opening: adj. v. fulgeo , deep yellow , reddish yellow , gold-colored , tawny (mostly poet. ): corpora leonum, Lucr. 5, 902 ; cf. Hor. C. 4, 4, 14 : tegmen lupae, Verg. A. 1, 275 : canis Lacon, Hor. Epod. 6, 5 : cassis equinis…

fūmārĭŏlum.opening: dim. fumarium , a smoke-hole (post-class.): fumariola Vesuvii, Tert. Poen. 12 .

fūmārĭum.opening: fumus , a smokechamber for ripening wine , Col. 1, 6, 19 sq. ; Mart. 10, 36, 1 ; Vulg. Osee, 13, 3 .

fūmātor.opening: fumo , one who ripens wine , Inscr. Orell. 5044 .— Transf. , a deceiver , Acron. ad Hor. Ep. 1, 2, 28 .

fūmesco.opening: v. inch. n. [fumus], to smoke , emit smoke , Isid. 17, 8, 2 .

fūmĕus.opening: adj. id. , full of smoke , smoky , smoking : lumina taedis, Verg. A. 6, 593 : flatus, Macr. S. 7, 10 : Acheron, Val. Fl. 4, 595 : vina Massiliae, ripened by smoke, Mart. 13, 123 (cf. fumarium).

fūmĭcus.opening: adj. id. , smoky (late Lat.): culinae, Sid. Ep. 1, 11 .

fūmĭdus.opening: adj. fumus , full of smoke , smoky , smoking. Lit. : fax, Lucr. 3, 304 ; cf.: piceum fert fumida lumen Taeda, Verg. A. 9, 75 : templa caeli (ignibus Aetnae), Lucr. 6, 644 : altaria, Ov. M. 12, 259 : caligo, Plin. 2, 42,…

fūmĭfer.opening: adj. fumus-fero , producing smoke , smoking , steaming ( poet. ): ignes, Verg. A. 9, 522 : nox (in antro Caci), id. ib. 8, 255 : Aponus, Luc. 7, 193 .

fūmĭfĭco.opening: v. n. fumus-facio , to make or cause smoke , to burn incense : Ephesiae Dianae, Arabio odore, Plaut. Mil. 2, 5, 2 .

fūmĭfĭcus.opening: adj. id. , making or causing smoke , smoking , steaming (poet): faces, Prud. στεφ . 3, 118: mugitus (taurorum), Ov. M. 7, 114 (shortly before: Vulcanum naribus efflant): Epeum fumificum, qui legioni nostrae habet Coctum…

fūmĭgābundus.opening: adj. fumigo , causing smoke , smoking (late Lat.): terra, Vulg. Sapient. 10, 7 .

fūmĭgĭum.opening: id. , a fumigating , fumigation (late Lat.), Theod. Prisc. 3, 5 .

fūmĭgo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
fūmĭgo.opening: v. a. and n. fumus-ago . Act. , to smoke , to fumigate : alvos, Varr. R. R. 3, 16, 17 ; Col. 9, 14, 7 : gallinaria, id. 8, 5, 20 : (pulli) pulegii surculis fumigentur, id. 8, 5, 16 : fumigati parietes, App. Mag. p. 312,…

fūmo.opening: v. n. fumus , to smoke , steam , reek , fume. Lit. (class.): acri sulphure montes Oppleti calidis ubi fumant fontibus aucti, Lucr. 6, 748 : late circum loca sulphure fumant, Verg. A. 2, 698 : recenti fossione terram…

fūmōsus.opening: adj. id. , full of smoke , smoking , smoky , smoked (class.). Lit. : ligna, Cato, R. R. 130 : flamma, id. ib. 38, 4 : fax, Petr. 97 : December (because many fires are then made), Mart. 5, 30, 5 : paries, well smoked,…

fūmus.opening: Sanscr. dhū, dhumas, smoke; Zend. dun-man, vapor; Gr. θύω, to rage, sacrifice, θυμός, θῦμα, θύος, etc.; Goth. dauns, odor; Engl. dust; cf.: fūnus, fuligo , smoke , steam , fume : in lignis si flamma latet fumusque…

fūnālis.opening: adj. funis , consisting of or attached to a rope or cord : equus, an extra horse yoked to a chariot , but attached to it at the side of the others by a rope or trace , a trace-horse , Suet. Tib. 6 ; Stat. Th. 6, 462 ;…

fūnambŭlus.opening: funis-ambulo , a rope-dancer , Ter. Hec. prol. 4 ; prol. alt. 26; Suet. Galb. 6 .— Transf. : tu funambule pudicitiae et castitatis, Tert. de Pudic. 10 . —Called also , Aug. in Psa. 39, 9 .

fūnārĭus.opening: adj. funis , of or belonging to a rope (post-class.): equus, i. q. funalis equus, an extra horse, trace-horse, Isid. Orig. 18, 35, 2 .— Subst. : , , , a surname of Gratianus, father of the emperor Valentinianus (so…

functĭo.opening: fungor , a performing , executing , discharging; a performance , execution. In gen. (Ciceron., but very rare): labor est functio quaedam vel animi vel corporis gravioris operis et muneris, Cic. Tusc. 2, 15, 35 : ut iis…

funda.opening: Sanscr. spandē, itch; Gr. σφαδάζω, to move convulsively; σφοδρός, σφεδανός, impassioned; σφενδόνη; cf. 3. fūsus , a sling. Lit. : funda dicta eo, quod ex ea fundantur lapides, id est emittantur, Isid. Orig. 18, 10, 1 :…

fundālis.opening: adj. funda , of or belonging to a sling (post-class.): stridor, Prud. Psych. 293 .

fundāmen.opening: 2. fundo , a foundation ( poet. for the class. fundamentum; mostly in plur. ): ponere fundamina, Verg. G. 4, 161 : Siculae terrae, Ov. M. 5, 361 : rerum, id. ib. 15, 433 ; id. F. 4, 835 .—In sing. : fundamine magno res…

fundāmentum.opening: id. , a foundation , ground-work , basis (class.; mostly in plur. ; cf. basis). Lit. Sing. (rare): quin cum fundamento (aedes) Perierint, Plaut. Most. 1, 2, 69 : substruere fundamentum, id. ib. 1, 2, 40 .— Plur. :…

fundātĭo.opening: 2. fundo , a founding , foundation (very rare): fundationes aedium, Vitr. 5, 3 : substructionis fodere, id. 3, 3 ; Hil. Trin. 11, 37.

fundātor.opening: id. , a founder (very rare for conditor, creator): Praenestinae urbis, Verg. A. 7, 678 : terrae, Lact. 2 . 1, 5: imperii Romani, Inscr. Grut. 56, 5 sq. — Trop. : securitatis publicae (Licinius), Inscr. Orell. 1071 :…

fundātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from 2. fundo.

Fundi.opening: a sea-coast town of Latium , on the Appian Way , between Formiae and Tarracina , now Fondi , Mel. 2, 4, 9 ; Cic. Att. 14, 6, 1 ; Liv. 41, 27 ; Hor. S. 1, 5, 34 ; Suet. Tib. 5 ; id. Galb. 4 ; 8 .— Derivv. , , adj. , of…

fundĭbălum.opening: ( ), , , or , , vox hibr. from funda and βάλλω , a hurling or slinging machine (late Lat.), Vulg. 1 Macc. 6, 51 ; Ambros. Ep. 37, 40 ; cf. Isid. Orig. 18, 10, 2 : Fundibali λιθοβόλοι , Gloss. Lat. Gr.

fundĭbŭlārius.opening: a slinger (for the class. funditor), Vulg. 4 Reg. 3, 25 ; Judith, 6, 8: σφενδονι^ται , Gloss. Lat. Gr.

fundĭbŭlum.opening: χώνη , a funnel , Gloss. Philox. [1. fundo].

fundĭto.opening: v. freq. a. 1. fundo (anteand post-class.). To hurl or sling at : globos volantes jussi funditarier, Plaut. Poen. 2, 36 : spicula, Amm. 24, 4, 16 .— Trop. : tantilla tanta verba funditat, pours forth, Plaut. Poen. 1, 2,…

fundĭtor.opening: funda , one who fights with a sling , a slinger , σφενδονίτης , a sort of light-armed soldier (cf.: jaculator, sagittarius), Caes. B. G. 2, 7, 1 ; 2, 10, 1 ; 2, 19, 4 ; 2, 24, 4 et saep.; Sall. J. 46, 7 ; 49, 6 al.

fundĭtus.opening: adv. fundus , from the very bottom , from the foundation (syn.: a fundamento, ab radicibus, radicitus, penitus; freq. and class.). Lit. : monumentum P. Scipionis funditus delevit ac sustulit, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 36, § 79 ;…

fundo.opening: v. a. fundus , to lay the bottom , keel , foundation of a thing, to found (syn.: condo, exstruo, etc.). Lit. (perh. only poet. ): haec carina satis probe fundata et bene statuta est, i. e. is laid, Plaut. Mil. 3, 3, 44…

fundŭla.opening: a street without an outlet , a cul de sac : a fundo, quod exitum non habent ac pervium non est, Varr. L. L. 5, § 145 .

fundŭlus.opening: dim. fundus . * A kind of sausage : FUNDULUM a fundo, quod non ut reliquae partes, sed ex una parte sola apertum, Varr. L. L. 5, § 111 .—* In mechanics, a kind of sucker or piston : ambulatiles, Vitr. 10, 13 .

fundus.opening: Sanscr. budh-nas, ground; Gr. πυθμήν, πύνδαξ; O. H. Germ. Bodam; Germ. Boden; v. fodio , the bottom of any thing (class.). Lit. In gen.: armarii fundum exsecuit, the bottom of the chest, Cic. Clu. 64, 179 : ollae, Plin.…

gĕōrgĭcus.opening: adj. , = γεωργικός , of or belonging to husbandry , agricultural , georgic : carmen, i. e. the Georgics, the title of an agricultural poem by Virgil, Col. 7, 5, 10 ; 10 praef. 3.— Subst. , , : Vergilius hunc Ennii…

Gĕraestĭcus portus.opening: a harbor near the town of Teos , in Ionia , Liv. 37, 27, 9 .

gĕrănĭon.opening: or , , , = γεράνιον , the plant stork's-bill , Plin. 26, 11, 68, § 108 sqq.

gĕrănītis.opening: , = γερανῖτις , a precious stone , otherwise unknown , Plin. 37, 11, 72, § 187 .

gerdĭus.opening: , = γέρδιος , a weaver (ante- and post-class.), Lucil. ap. Non. 118, 10 ; Firm. 8, 25 med.

gĕrens.opening: P. and P. a. of gero; v. gero fin.

germānĭtas.opening: 1. germanus , the relation between brothers and sisters , brotherhood , sisterhood. Lit. : moveant te horum lacrimae, moveat pietas, moveat germanitas, Cic. Lig. 11, 33 : subituram vobis aliquando germanitatis memoriam…

germānĭtus.opening: adv. 1. germanus , in a brotherly manner , faithfully , truly (anteand post-class.): germanitus fideliter, dictum a germanitate, Non. 118, 14 ; Pompon. ap. Non. l. l.; Aug. Ep. 120, 34 .

germānus.opening: adj. v. germen , of brothers and sisters who have the same parents, or at least the same father, full , own (very freq. and class.). Lit. Adj. : spes mihi est vos inventuros fratres germanos duos Geminos, una matre…

germen.opening: Sanscr. root grabh-, grah-, to conceive; garbh-as, child; whence, βρέφος (for γρέφος), germanus, perh. gremium , a sprig , offshoot , sprout , bud ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : huc aliena ex arbore germen…

germĭnasco.opening: v. inch. n. [germen], to sprout , shoot , Ambros. de Caïn et Abel, 2, 8, § 26.

germĭnātĭo.opening: germino , a sprouting forth , budding , germination. Lit. : palmitis, Col. 4, 24, 18 : tria tempora germinationis, Plin. 17, 18, 30, § 134 ; cf. id. 16, 25, 41, § 98 .—In plur. , Plin. 17, 2, 2, § 16 . — Transf. ,…

germĭnātus.opening: id. , a sprouting forth , putting forth , germination (less freq. than germinatio): oleam, si capra depaverit primo germinatu, sterilescere, Plin. 15, 8, 8, § 34 : serotino quaedam germinatu florent maturantque…

germĭno.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
germĭno.opening: v. n. and a. [germen] (post-Aug.). Neutr. , to sprout forth , put forth , bud , germinate : asparagus altissime germinat, Plin. 19, 8, 42, § 146 ; 13, 24, 46, § 129 ; 16, 25, 41, § 97 sqq. et saep. — Act. , to put forth…

gĕro.opening: 1. gero , a carrier; connected per hyphen with foras: ite, ite hac, simul eri damnigeruli, foras gerones, Bonorum hamaxagogae, that carry off, ravishers, Plaut. Truc. 2, 7, 1 .

Gĕrōnĭum.opening: or , , , a small city or fortress in Appulia , now called Gerione or Girone , Liv. 22, 18, 7 ; ib. 23, 9 ; ib. 24 sq.

gĕrontēa.opening: , = γεροντεία , the plant groundsel , called also senecio and erigeron, Senecio vulgaris, Linn.; App. Herb. 75 .

gĕrontŏcŏmīum.opening: , = γεροντοκομεῖον , a public hospital or alms-house for poor old people , Cod. Just. 1, 2, 19 ; 22 ; 23 .

Gĕrontŏdĭdascŭlus.opening: (= γεροντοδιδάσκαλος , an old man's teacher), the title of one of the satires of Varro , Varr. Frag. p. 279 Bip.

gerrae.opening: , = γέρρα , orig. wattled twigs; hence, transf., trifles , stuff , nonsense : gerrae crates vimineae. Athenienses cum Syracusas obsiderent et crebro gerras poscerent, irridentes Siculi gerras clamitabant. Unde factum…

gerro.opening: , (archaic orthogr.: † cerrones leves et inepti, Paul. ex Fest. v. p. 40 Müll.), , gerrae , a trifler , idle fellow : gerro, iners, fraus, heluo, Ganeo, damnosus! Ter. Heaut. 5, 4, 10 .

gĕrŭla.opening: gero , she that bears or carries , Tert. Anim. 19 fin. ; id. adv. Jud. 9 med. ; App. M. 6, p. 181 : navis gerula sacrorum, Sol. 1 fin.—A working bee , Plin. 11, 10, 10, § 24 .

gĕrŭlĭfĭgŭlus.opening: gerulus + figulus , comic, an accessory , abettor : flagiti, Plaut. Bacch. 3, 1, 14 ; cf. 1. gerulus, I. B.

gĕrŭlum.opening: gero , a bearer : cornua potuum gerula, Sol. 20, 5 .

gĕrŭlus.opening: id. . A bearer , carrier : nae ille alium gerulum (argenti) quaerat sibi, Plaut. Bacch. 4, 9, 79 ; Hor. Ep. 2, 2, 72 ; Col. poët. 10, 310; Suet. Calig. 40 ; Sid. Ep. 8, 13 ; Inscr. Orell. 575 ; 874 ; 976 ; Schol. Juv.…

gĕrundĭum.opening: id. , in gram., a gerund , Diom. p. 350 P.; Prisc. p. 808 ib. al.; also called , Serv. p. 1788 P.

gestābĭlis.opening: adj. gesto , portable (late Lat.), Cassiod. Varr. 1, 45 ; Ambros. de Noë et Arca, 15, 52 fin.

gestāmen.opening: id. . That which is borne or worn , a burden , load; ornaments , accoutrements , arms , etc. ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): clipeus, magni gestamen Abantis, Verg. A. 3, 286 ; so of a shield, Sil. 5, 349 : hoc Priami…

gestātĭo.opening: id. . Act. , a bearing , carrying : infantium gestationes, Lact. 3, 22 fin. — Pass. (not ante-Aug.), a being carried or conveyed about (in a litter, carriage, boat, etc.), a riding , driving or sailing for pleasure.…

gibbĕrōsus.opening: adj. 2. gibber , badly hump-backed or hunch-backed. Lit. , Auct. ap. Suet. Gram. 9 : vel protervi vel gibberosi vel curvi vel pruriginosi, etc., Dig. 21, 1, 3 (al. gibbosi).— Trop. : sermones, crooked, twisted, Fronto,…

gibbōsus.opening: , v. the preceding art. I. fin.

gingĭlismus.opening: , = γιγγλισμός , pealing laughter , Petr. 73, 4 (where others read in the same signification).

gingriātor.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 95 Müll. N. cr.

glăbrĭtas.opening: id. , smoothness of the skin , baldness : calvitiis et glabritatibus rasi, Arn. 3, 108 .

glaebŭlentus.opening: ( ), , adj. id. , cloddy , consisting of earth : animalia, App. de Deo Socr. p. 46 .

grăcĭlĭpes.opening: adj. gracilis-pes , slender-footed : ciconia, Publ. Syr. ap. Petr. 55 .
