halonem.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. s. v. ELUCUM, p. 75 Müll.

hălŏphanta.opening: m , = ἁλοφάντης (a word comically formed after the analogy of sycophanta, συκοφάντης ), a salt-informer , i. q. a rascal , scoundrel , Plaut. Curc. 4, 1, 2 ; cf. Non. 126, 7 , and see halapanta.

hălōs.opening: , = ἅλως (a round threshing-floor), a circle round the sun or moon , a halo , pure Lat. corona: circa solem visum coloris varii circulum, qualis esse in arcu solet. Hunc Graeci halo vocant: nos dicere coronam aptissime…

hălōsis.opening: , = ἅλωσις , a taking by storm , capture , Petr. 89, 1 (in Suet. Ner. 38 , written as Greek).

halter.opening: , = ἁλτήρ , in gymnastics, leaden weights held in the hands in leaping exercises, to add to the impetus of the body, the dumb-bells of modern gymnastics, Mart. 14, 49, 1 ; 7, 67, 6 (pure Lat. manipuli, Cael. Aur. Tard.…

Halus.opening: a small place in Assyria , near Artemita, only mentioned by Tac. A. 6, 41 .

Hălys.opening: , = Ἅλυς . A river in Asia Minor , flowing between Paphlagonia and Cappadocia , now Kisil-Irmak : secundum Halyn, Mel. 1, 19, 9 ; Plin. 6, 2, 2, § 6 ; 6, 3, 3, § 8 : circa Halyn, Liv. 38, 16, 13 : Croesus Halym…

hăma.opening: ( ), , , = ἄμη , a waterbucket , esp. for extinguishing fires, a firebucket , Plin Ep. 10, 42, 2; Juv. 14, 305 ; Dig. 1, 15, 3 ; 33, 7, 12 , §§ 18, 21 (in Plaut. Mil. 3, 2, 42 , false reading for aula, Lorenz ad loc.).

Hămādrўas.opening: , = Ἁμαδρυάς , a wood-nymph , hamadryad; in sing. , Stat. S. 1, 3, 63 ; in plur. , Verg. E. 10, 62 ; Prop. 2, 32 (3, 30), 37; Ov. M. 1, 690 ; 14, 624 ; id. F. 2, 155 ; dat. Grœc. : Hamadryasin, Prop. 1, 20, 32 (like ib.…

Hamae.opening: a place in Campania , near Cumœ , mentioned only by Liv. 23, 35, 3 .

hămarthrītis.opening: ἅμα-ἀρθρῖτις , the general gout , Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 2, 28 .

Hămartĭgĕnīa.opening: , = Ἁμαρτιγένεια , The Origin of Sin , the title of a poem by Prudentius.

hāmātĭlis.opening: adj. hamatus , with hooks , i. e. performed by or furnished with hooks (ante- and post-class.): piscatus, Plaut. Rud. 2, 1, 10 : spiculum scorpii, Tert. adv. Gnost. 1 .

hāmātus.opening: adj. hamus , furnished with a hook , hooked. Lit. : ungues, Ov. M. 12, 563 : harundo, id. ib. 5, 384 : sentes, id. ib. 2, 799 .— Transf. , shaped like a hook , hooked , crooked : hamatis uncinatisque corporibus concreta…

hămaxa.opening: , = ἅμαξα , a wagon , Capitol. Max. duob. 6 (in Gell. 2, 21, 9 , in the signification of septentriones, written as Greek).

hămaxăgōga.opening: , = ἁμαξαγωγός , one who carries off any thing in a wagon , in comic transf.: bonorum, Plaut. Truc. 2, 7, 2 .

hămaxītis.opening: a plant , i. q. agrostis, App. Herb. 77 .

hămaxo.opening: v. a. ἅμαξα, a wagon , to yoke to a wagon , Plaut. Truc. 2, 2, 22 .

Hămaxŏbĭi.opening: or , , , = Ἁμαξόβιοι (living, going about in wagons), a Scythian people , Mel. 2, 1, 2 ; Plin. 4, 12, 25 (cf. Hor. C. 3, 24, 9 ; Just. 2, 2 ).—In sing. : Hamaxobio instabilior, Tert. adv. Marc. 1, 1 .

Hămilcar.opening: ( ), , A general , son of Gisgo , slain in besieging Syracuse , Cic. Div. 1, 24, 50 ; Val. Max. 1, 7 , ext. 8.— Hamilcar Barca, the father of Hannibal , Cic. Off. 3, 26, 99 ; Nep. Ham. ; Liv. 21, 2 sq. ; Val. Max. 6, 6,…

Hămillus.opening: the name of a teacher , Juv. 10, 224 .

hāmĭōta.opening: hamus , an angler (ante-class.): conchitae atque hamiotae, Plaut. Rud. 2, 2, 5 : hamiotae aucupesque, Varr. ap. Non. 25, 10 .

hammītis.opening: , = ἁμμῖτις , a precious stone , otherwise unknown, Plin. 37, 10, 60, § 167 .

hammŏchrȳsos.opening: ( ), , , = ἀμμόχρυσος (gold sand), a precious stone unknown to us , perh. golden mica , Plin. 37, 11, 73, § 188 ; Isid. 16, 15, 5 .

hammŏdўtes.opening: ( ), , , = ἁμμοδύτης (sand-crawler), an African serpent , Sol. 27, 33 ; Isid. 12, 4, 39 ; Luc. 9, 716 al.

Hammōn.opening: ( ), , , = Ἄμμων , an Egyptian and Libyan deity , worshipped ( in the present oasis Siwah ) in the form of a ram , and identified by the Greeks and Romans with Ζεύς and Jupiter; hence, Juppiter Hammon. Connected with…

hāmotrăhōnes.grammar: alii piscatores, alii, qui unco cadavera trahunt

hāmŭla.opening: dim. hama , a small water-bucket : habilem lymphis hamulam, Col. poët. 10, 387.

hāmŭlus.opening: dim. hamus , a small hook : piscarius, a small angle, Plaut. Stich. 2, 1, 17 .—As a surgical instrument, Cels. 7, 7, 4 and 7.

hāmus.opening: kindr. with ἁπ-, ἅπτω , a hook. Lit. In gen.: taleae pedem longae, ferreis hamis infixis, totae in terram infodiebantur, Caes. B. G. 7, 73 fin. : hamis ferreis pectitur stupa, heckles, Plin. 19, 1, 3, § 17 : loricam…

Hannĭbal.opening: ( ), (ālis, Enn. Sat. 14 Vahl.), = Ἀννίβας [Phoen.], a Punic surname. The most celebrated of the name is Hannibal , son of Hamilcar , the leader of the Carthaginians in the second Punic war , Nep. Han. 1 al. ; Liv. 21,…

Hanno.opening: ( ), , , = Ἄννων , a Punic name. The most celebrated of the name is Hanno , general of the Carthaginians , who , about the year 500 B.C., navigated the western coast of Africa , Plin. 5, 1, 1, § 8 ; Cic. Tusc. 5, 32, 90…

hăpălopsis.opening: a spice , Plaut. Ps. 3, 2, 47 Ritschl N. cr.

hăpălūrĭa.opening: hapalus , a vessel for soft eggs , Aus. Ep. 20 dub.

hăpălus.opening: adj. , = ἁπαλός , soft; only with ova, Apic. 7, 17 ; Scrib. Comp. 104 ; Marc. Emp. 20 .

hăphē.opening: ( ), , , = ἁφή (a touching, handling; hence), the yellow sand with which wrestlers, after being anointed, were sprinkled. Lit. : flavescit haphe, Mart. 7, 67, 5 .— Transf. , the dust of a road , Sen. Ep. 57, 1 .

hapsus.opening: , = ἅψος (a binding together; hence), a lock of wool used in bandaging : lanae, Cels. 4, 6, 9 ; 7, 26, 5 .

hăra.opening: a pen or coop for animals: anserum, a goose-pen, Varr. R. R. 3, 10, 3 sq. ; Col. 8, 14, 5 ; Plaut. As. 2, 4, 24 al. ; a hog-stye , Varr. R. R. 2, 4, 14 ; Col. 7, 9, 9 ; Ov. H. 1, 104 ; cf.: confer nunc, Epicure noster,…

hărēna.opening: (better than , Bramb. s. v. R ib. Prol. Verg. p. 422 , and v. infra ), , Sabin. fas-ena; from Sanscr. root bhas-, to shine, gleam, Corss. Ausspr. 1, 102 . Prop., sand (syn.: sabulum, glarea, suburra): harenae tria…

hărēnācĕus.opening: ( ), , adj. , sandy , = harenosus (only in Plin.): terra, Plin. 17, 7, 4, § 43 al.

hărēnārĭus.opening: ( ), , adj. harena . Prop., of or pertaining to sand : lapis, sandstone (= lapis bibulus of Verg.), Serv. Verg. G. 2, 348 .— Transf. , of or pertaining to the amphitheatre : fera, destined for the arena, Arn. 29, 1 .—…

hărēnātĭo.opening: ( ), , id . Prop., a sanding , plastering with sand. — Transf. , a plastering , cementing , Vitr. 7, 3, 9 .

hărēnātus.opening: ( ), , adj. id. , sanded , covered or mixed with sand (very rare): calx, Cato, R. R. 18, 7 ; Inscr. Grut. 207 .—As subst. : , (sc. opus), , sand-mortar , Vitr. 7, 4 ; Plin. 36, 23, 55, § 176 sq.

hărēnĭfŏdīna.opening: ( ), , harena - fodio , a sand-pit (late Lat. for harenaria; s. v. harenarius, III. B.), Dig. 7, 1, 13, § 5 ; 24, 3, 7 ; Varr. L. L. 5, § 7 Müll.

hărēnĭvăgus.opening: ( ), , adj. harena - vagus , wandering over sands : Cato, Luc. 9, 941 .

hărēnōsus.opening: ( ), , adj. harena , full of sand , sandy : Ladon, Ov. M. 1, 702 : terra, id. ib. 14, 82 ; Plin. 17, 7, 4, § 44 : litus Libyae, Verg. A. 4, 257 : urina, Plin. 23, 3, 36, § 73 : lapis harenosior, id. 33, 6, 33, § 101 :…

hărēnŭla.opening: ( ), , dim. id. , fine sand , a grain of sand , Plin. 30, 3, 8, § 24 .

hărĭŏlātĭo.opening: ( ), , hariolor , a soothsaying , prophesying , Enn. ap. Cic. Div. 1, 31, 66 (Fragm. Trag. 42 Rib.).

hărĭŏlor.opening: ( ), , v. dep. n. [hariolus], to foretell , prophesy , divine. Lit. : Προθεσπίζω igitur, non hariolans, ut illa (Cassandra) cui nemo credidit, sed conjectura prospiciens, Cic. Att. 8, 11, 3 : quaestus causa hariolari,…

hărĭŏlus.opening: ( ), , , and , , Sanscr. hira, entrails; Gr. χορδή, χολάδες; cf. haruspex , a soothsayer , prophet , prophetess (= augur, auspex, haruspex, extispex). Masc. : hariolos, haruspices Mitte omnes: quae futura et quae facta,…

Harmŏdĭus.opening: , = Ἁρμόδιος , a famous Athenian , murderer of Hipparchus , Cic. Tusc. 1, 49, 116 ; Plin. 7, 23, 23, § 87 ; Gell. 9, 2 .

harmŏgē.opening: , = ἁρμογή , a proper combination or mingling of colors , Plin. 35, 5, 11, § 29 .— Transf. , harmony of sound, Varr. Sat. Men. 63, 18 .

harmŏnĭa.opening: (archaic gen. sing. harmoniaï, Lucr. 3, 131 ), , = ἁρμονία , an agreement of sounds , consonance , concord , harmony; pure Lat. concentus. Lit. : velut in cantu et fidibus, quae harmonia dicitur, Cic. Tusc. 1, 10, 20 ;…

Harmŏnĭa.opening: daughter of Mars and Venus , the wife of Cadmus , and mother of Semele , Ino , Agave , and Polydorus , Hyg. Fab. 6 ; 148 ; 159 .— Acc. : Harmonien, Ov. A. A. 3, 86 .

harmŏnĭcē.opening: , = ἁρμονική , the science of sounds , harmonics , Vitr. 5, 3, 8 .— Called , , , Vitr. 5, 4, 1 .

harmŏnĭcus.opening: adj. , = ἁρμονικός , of or belonging to agreement or harmony , harmonious , harmonic (very rare): res, Varr. L. L. 10, § 64 Müll.: harmonica ratio, quae cogit rerum naturam sibi ipsam congruere, Plin. 2, 109, 113, § 248…

harpa.opening: , = ἅρπη (a sickle, transf.), a harp (late Lat.), Ven. Carm. 7, 8, 63.

harpactĭcon.opening: , false read. in Plin. 35, 15, 50, § 176 ; v. 1. harpax.

harpăga.opening: , = ἁρπάγη , a hook , for the usual harpago, Sisenn. ap. Non. 556, 20 .

harpăgĭnētŭlus.opening: dim. harpago , a small hook , Vitr. 7, 5, 3 dub.

harpăgo.opening: ἁρπάγη , a hook for drawing things to one's self, for tearing down any thing, etc., a grappling-hook , grapple , drag (pure Lat. manica, manus ferrea). Lit. , Caes. B. G. 7, 81, 1 ; id. B. C. 1, 57, 2 ; Liv. 30, 10 ;…

Harpăgus.opening: a Median nobleman , to whom Astyages committed his grandson Cyrus to be destroyed , but by whom he was preserved alive , Just. 1, 4 sq. ; Sen. de Ira, 3, 15, 1.

Harpălus.opening: one of Cicero's slaves , Cic. Fam. 16, 24, 1 .

Harpălўcē.opening: , = Ἁρπαλύκη , the daughter of the Thracian king Harpalycus , brought up as a warrior , Verg. A. 1, 317 Serv.; Hyg. Fab. 193 ; 252 ; 254 .

harpastum.opening: , = ἁρπαστόν , a hand-ball : sive harpasta manu pulverulenta rapis, Mart. 4, 19, 6 ; 7, 67, 4 .

harpax.opening: adj. , = ἅρπαξ , drawing to itself , rapacious. — Lit. , of amber and brimstone: in Syria feminas verticillos inde (i. e. ex electro) facere et vocari harpaga, quia folia paleasque et vestium fimbrias rapiat, Plin. 37,…

Harpax.opening: ἅρπαξ , the name of a slave , Plaut. Ps. 2, 2, 58 sq. ; 4, 2, 53 sq. —Also in voc. : Harpage, Plaut. Ps. 2, 2, 70 .

harpē.opening: , = ἅρπη . A sickleshaped sword , a falchion , cimeter , Ov. M. 5, 69 ; 176 ; Luc. 9, 663 ; Val. Fl. 4, 388 .— A species of falcon , tassel gentle : Falco gentilis, Linn.; Plin. 10, 74, 95, § 204 .

Harpŏcrătēs.opening: , = Ἁρποκράτης , The Egyptian god of silence , represented with his finger on his mouth; acc. to others, a Greek philosopher , who enjoined silence respecting the nature of the gods , Varr. L. L. 5, § 57 Müll. N. cr.…

Harpȳiae.opening: (trisyl.; scanned as a quadrisyl. Hārpўĭās, Rutil. Itin. 1, 608 ), , , = Ἅρπυιαι (qs. the spoilers). Mythical rapacious monsters , half bird and half woman , the Harpies , Verg. A. 3, 212 sq. ; 6, 289 ; Hor. S. 2, 2, 40…

Harūdes.opening: a Germanic tribe in the army of Ariovistus , perh. the same as the Charudes in the Chersonesus Cimbrica ( in the Northern Jütland ), Caes. B. G. 1, 31, 10 ; 1, 37, 2 ; 1, 51, 2 Monum. Ancyr.

hărundĭfer.opening: ( ), , adj. harundo - fero , reed-bearing , crowned with reeds : caput, Ov. F. 5, 637 .

hărundĭnācĕus.opening: ( ), , adj. harundo , like a reed , Plin. 18, 7, 10, § 58 .

hărundĭnārĭus.opening: ( ), , id. II. B. , a dealer in limed twigs , Inscr. Orell. 4199 .

hărundĭnātĭo.opening: ( ), , id. II. L. , the poling of vines, the propping with reeds , Varr. 1, 8, 3 (ex conj. Schneid. The vulg. reading is: Canusini in harundulatione in ficis).

hărundĭnētum.opening: ( ), , harundo, II. , a thicket or jungle of reeds , Cato, R. R. 6, 3 ; Varr. R. R. 1, 24, 4 ; Col. 4, 32, 3 ; Plin. 10, 8, 10, § 28 ; Vulg. Josue, 16, 8 ; 17, 9 .

hărundĭnĕus.opening: ( ), , adj. id. . Of reeds , reedy : silva, Verg. A. 10, 710 : paniculae, Plin. 8, 32, 50, § 117 : cuneoli, Col. 4, 29, 10 : ripae, Stat. Th. 6, 174 .— Poet. : carmen, a shepherd's song, Ov. Tr. 4, 1, 12 . — Like a reed…

hărundĭnōsus.opening: ( ), , adj. id. , abounding in reeds : Cnidus, Cat. 36, 13 .

hărundo.opening: (better than , Bramb. s. v.; Wagn. Orthog. Verg. p. 441 ; R ib. Prol. Verg. p. 422 , though the latter is freq. in MSS. and edd.; v. infra ), , etym. dub.; perh. from root ar-, to set in motion; Sanscr. aras, swift;…

hăruspex.opening: ( ), , Sanscr. hirā, entrails; Gr. χολάδες, χορδή; cf. hariolus, Georg Curtius Gr. Etym. p. 202 sq. , a soothsayer , diviner among the Etruscans , who foretold future events from the inspection of the entrails of…

hăruspĭca.opening: ( ), , haruspex , a female haruspex or soothsayer , Plaut. Mil. 3, 1, 99 .— = haruspicium, Plin. 7, 56, 57, § 203 .

hăruspĭcālis.opening: adj. id. , of a soothsayer : ars, Serv. Verg. A. 4, 56 .

hăruspĭcīnus.opening: ( ), , adj. id. , of or relating to the inspection of victims. Adj. : quod Etruscorum declarant et haruspicini et fulgurales et tonitruales libri, Cic. Div. 1, 33, 72 .— Subst. : , , (sc. ars), the art of divining ,…

hăruspĭcĭum.opening: ( ), , id. , inspection of victims , divination , Cat. 90, 2 .

Hasdrŭbal.opening: ( ), , , a Punic name. The most celebrated are, Son of Mago , the founder of the power of Carthage , Just. 19, 1 .— Son of Hanno , who fought in Sicilia during the first Punic war , Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 54, § 125 .— The…

hasta.opening: ( ), , Sanscr. hastas, hand; cf. Gr. root χαδ- in χανδάνω, pre-hendo , a spear (syn.: hastile, dolo, gaesum, sarisa, sparus, lancea, pilum, spiculum, telum, etc.). Lit. Most freq. as a military weapon, a lance , pike ,…

hastārĭum.opening: hasta, I. B. , an auction-catalogue , Tert. Ap. 13 ; id. ad Nat. 1, 10 .

hastārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to the spear : censio, Paul. ex Fest. 54, 12 .— Of or belonging to auctions , auction- : PRAETOR, Inscr. Grut. 379, 7 .

hastātus.opening: adj. hasta, I. A. , armed with a spear. In gen. (very rare): Bellona, Stat. Th. 2, 718 : prima utcumque acies hastata: ceteris praeusta aut brevia tela, Tac. A. 2, 14 : currum decem milia hastatorum sequebantur, Curt.…

hastīle.opening: (also ), , hasta , the shaft of a spear or javelin. Lit. : ferrum, quod ex hastili in corpore remanserat, Nep. Epam. 9 : hastili nixus, Cic. Rab. Perd. 7, 21 : missile telum hastili abiegno, Liv. 21, 8, 10 .— Transf.…

hastŭla.opening: dim. id. . A little spear , Fronto de Or. 1 med. — Transf. A little branch , Sen. Q. N. 2, 31, 2 .— Hastula regia, a plant , called also asphodelus, asphodel , Plin. 21, 17, 68, § 109 ; App. Herb. 32 .

Hatĕrĭānus.opening: adj. , of or belonging to Haterius (a jurist), Cic. Fam. 9, 18, 3 .

haud.opening: or (in the form , , several times in Plautus acc. to the Cod. Ambros., and in Inscr. Orell. 4848 : HEIC. EST. SEPVLCRVM. HAV. PVLCRVM. PVLCRAI. FEMINAE; also Tac. A. 2, 36; 6, 43 (49), Nipperdey, Ritter; hence, also…

hauddum.opening: and , v. haud, II. A. and B.

haurĭo.opening: (archaic imperf. hauribant, Lucr. 5, 1324 ; perf. subj. haurierint, Varr. ap. Prisc. p. 905 P.; part. perf. haurītus, App. M. 3, p. 139 ; 6 , p. 178; supin. hauritu, id. ib. 2 , p. 121; part. fut. hauritura, Juv. in…

haurītōrĭŭm.opening: , ii. , = ἀντλητήριον ( a bucket ), Gloss. Philox.

haustor.opening: ( ), , haurio , a drawer (post-Aug. and very rare): aquarum, water-drawer , Firm. Math. 8, 29.— Poet. : ultimus aquae, drinker, Luc. 9, 591 .—Esp., he who fills casks with wine , Inscr. Orell. 5089 .

haustrum.opening: (also ), , id. , a machine for drawing water , Lucr. 5, 516 ; cf. Non. 13, 5 .

haustus.opening: haurio , a drawing. Lit. : aqua, quae non sit haustus profundi, Col. 1, 5, 1 : puteus in tenues plantas facili diffunditur haustu, Juv. 3, 227 ; Mel. 2, 4, 4 : aquae ductus, haustus, iter, actus, etc.... a jure civili…

Hĕautontīmōrūmĕnos.opening: , = Ἑαυτὸν τιμωρούμενος , The Self-tormentor , the title of a comedy of Terence, Ter. Heaut. prol. 5 (= Ipse se puniens, Cic. Tusc. 3, 27, 65 ).

hebdŏmăda.opening: hebdomas , the number seven : annorum, librorum, Gell. 3, 10, 17 .—Esp., = hebdomas, seven days , Gell. 3, 10, 14 ; Isid. de Nat. R. 3 ; Vulg. Gen. 29, 27 sq. ; id. Exod. 34, 22 al.

hebdŏmădālis.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to a week , weekly : festa, Sid. Ep. 9, 3 med.

hebdŏmas.opening: , = ἑβδομάς , the number seven , seven days : libri, qui inscribuntur Hebdomades, Gell. 3, 10, 1 : septima fere hebdomade, id est, nono et quadragesimo die, Varr. ib. § 7: hebdomadibus lunae, on every seventh day of the…

hebdŏmătĭcus.opening: ( ), , adj. , = ἑβδοματικός , relating to the number seven : septeni et noveni anni, qui hebdomatici a Graecis atque enneatici appellantur, i. e. critical , decisive of one's fate , Firm. Math. 4, 14 med.

Hēbē.opening: = Ἥβη (youth), the goddess of youth (pure Lat. Juventas), the daughter of Juno , cup-bearer to the gods , and , after the deification of Hercules , his wife , Ov. M. 9, 400 ; Prop. 1, 13, 23 ; Cat. 68, 116 ; Serv. Verg.…

hĕbĕnĭnus.opening: , or , , adj. , ἐβένινος , of ebony : tigna, Hier. Ezech. 27, 16 : dentes, id. ib.

hĕbĕnus.opening: (less correctly , R ib. Prol. Verg. p. 421 ), i. , Gr. ἕβενος, ἔβενος , the ebon-tree , ebony : Diospyros ebenum, Linn.; Plin. 16, 40, 76, § 204 ; 6, 30, 35, § 197 ; Verg. G. 2, 117 ; Ov. M. 11, 610 ; Pers. 5, 135 ; cf.…

hĕbĕo.opening: v. n. , to be blunt or dull (perh. not ante-Aug.). Lit. : ferrum nunc hebet? Liv. 23, 45, 9 .— Trop. , to be dull , sluggish , inactive , not lively : gelidus tardante senecta Sanguis hebet, Verg. A. 5, 396 : corpus…

hĕbes.opening: ( acc. sing. hebem, Enn. and Caecil. ap. Charis. p. 107 P.; abl. hebeti; but hebete, Cels. 7, 3 ), adj. hebeo , blunt , dull , in opp. to pointed or sharp (class.; esp. freq. in the trop. sense). Lit. : cujus (lunae) et…

hĕbesco.opening: v. inch. n. [hebeo], to grow blunt , dull , dim , or faint (rare but class.). Lit. : acumina (gladiorum) densis ictibus hebescebant, Amm. 16, 12, 54 : hebescunt sensus, membra torpent, Plin. 7, 50, 51, § 168 :…

hĕbĕtātĭo.opening: hebeto , dulness , dimness : oculorum, Plin. 28, 6, 16, § 58 : nascitur ex assiduitate laborum animorum hebetatio quaedam ac languor, Sen. Tranq. An. 15, 12 .

hĕbĕtātrix.opening: adj. id. , that makes dull or dim : umbra, i. e. darkening (shortly before: umbra terrae lunam hebetari), Plin. 2, 13, 10, § 57 .

hĕbĕtesco.opening: v. inch. n. [hebes], to grow dull , dim , or faint (post-Aug. and very rare): aciem in cultris tonsorum, Plin. 28, 7, 23, § 79 : acies oculi hebetescit ac paene caligat, Cels. 6, 6, 37 : dolor hebetescit, Scrib. Comp.…

hĕbĕto.opening: v. a. id. , to make blunt or dull , to blunt , dull , dim , deaden , weaken (perh. not ante-Aug.; not in Cic.). Lit. : hastas, Liv. 8, 10, 3 : vulneribus suis ferrum hostium, id. 30, 35, 8 : tela, Sil. 16, 105 : aciem…

hĕbĕtūdo.opening: id. , bluntness , dulness (post-class.; cf. hebetatio): sensuum, Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 14 : superba istorum, Aug. Civ. D. 7, 21 .

Hĕbraei.opening: , = Ἑβραῖοι , the Hebrews : Hebraei, qui nunc Judaei: igitur et litterae Hebraeae, Tert. Apol. 18 ; cf.: postea vero cum in deserto consedissent, amiserunt vetus nomen Hebraei, et Judaei sunt appellati, Lact. 4, 10 ; 2,…

hettēmătĭcus.opening: adj. , = ἡττηματικός , poor of its kind , Firm. Math. 3, 9.

heu!.opening: interj. (constr. absol. or with acc. , rarely with nom. or voc.; cf. Huschke ad Tib. 2, 6, 28 ; Forbig. and Wagn. ad Verg. A. 2, 274 . The passages cited for heu mihi, etc., Hand, Turs. III. 68 sq., are mostly corrected…

heurĕta.opening: , = εὑρετής , an inventor , inventive person , Plaut. Ps. 2, 4, 9 .

heus!.opening: interj. Used in calling attention, ho! ho there! hark! holloa! heus, reclude: heus, Tranio, etiamne aperis? ... heus vos, pueri, quid istic agitis? Plaut. Most. 4, 2, 28 sq. ; cf.: Syre, Syre inquam, heus, heus Syre,…

hexăchordos.opening: adj. , = ἑξάχορδος , having six musical strings or stops : machina, a water - organ with six stops, Vitr. 10, 13 .

hexaclīnon.opening: , = ἑξάκλινον , a couch to hold six persons , Mart. 9, 60, 9 .

Hexăēmĕron.opening: , = Ἑξαήμερον ( of or in six days ), the six days of the creation , Ambros. Ep. 6, 42 ; also the title of a work on the creation of the world , by Ambrosius; cf. Ambros. Ep. 6, 42 .

hexăgōnum.opening: , = ἑξάγωνον , a six-sided figure , hexagon , Col. 5, 2, 10 (in Varr. R. R. 3, 16, 5 written as Greek); also called , Ambros. Hexaēm. 5, 21, 69.

hexămĕter.opening: ( , Ter. Maur. p. 2430 P.), , , = ἑξάμετρος (of six measures), with or without versus, a verse consisting of six feet , a hexameter : versus, Lucil. ap. Porphyr. Hor. S. 1, 5, 87 ; so, metrum, Isid. 1, 38, 6 : Antipater…

hexăphŏros.opening: adj. , = ἑξαφόρος , one of six who carry a load together : phalangarii, Vitr. 10, 8 med. — Borne by six together; subst. : , , , = ἑξάφορον , a litter borne by six men , Mart. 2, 81, 1 : non debes ferri mortuus…

hexaptōta.opening: (sc. nomina), = ἑξάπτωτα , in gram., nouns that have six cases , Prisc. p. 673 P.; Isid. 1, 6, 43 .

Hexăpўlon.opening: , = Ἑξάπυλον , a gate in Syracuse with six entrances , Liv. 24, 21 ; 32 ; 39 .

hexas.opening: , = ἑξάς , the number six , Mart. Cap. 2, § 108 al.

hexastĭchus.opening: adj. , = ἑξάστιχος , of six lines or rows : hordeum, perh. our long-eared barley , Hordeum caeleste, Linn.; Col. 2, 9, 4 : myrtus, Plin. 15, 29, 37, § 122 .

hexastўlos.opening: adj. , = ἑξάστυλος , having six columns , Vitr. 3, 2, 7 .

hexēcontălĭthos.opening: , = ἑξηκοντάλιθος (sixty-colored stone), a precious stone , otherwise unknown, Plin. 37, 10, 60, § 167 ; Solin. 31.

hexēris.opening: , = ἑξήρης ( ναῦς ), a vessel with six banks of oars , Liv. 37, 23, 5 ; 29, 9, 8 .— Abl. hexere, Val. Max. 1, 8 , ext. 11.

hĭantĭa.opening: hio , an opening : oris, Tert. Anim. 10 .

hĭasco.opening: v. inch. n. [id.], to open , break open (ante- and post-class.): ubi primum nuces pineae incipiunt hiascere, Cato, R. R. 17, 2 ; Gargil. de Re Hort. 2, 1.

hĭātus.opening: id. , an opening , aperture , cleft (class. in sing. and plur. ; cf. rima, rictus). Lit. : animalia cibum partim oris hiatu et dentibus ipsis capessunt, partim unguium tenacitate arripiunt, Cic. N. D. 2, 47, 122 : oris,…

Hĭbēres.opening: (less correctly, ), , , = Ἴβηρες . Iberians , the Greek name for Spaniards , Cat. 9, 6 .—In sing. collect.: me peritus Discet Hiber Rhodanique potor, Hor. C. 2, 20, 20 : durus Iber, Luc. 6, 258 .—Hence, ( ), , adj. , of…

hībernācŭlum.opening: hiberno , a winter residence , winter apartment. In gen., Vitr. 1, 2, 4 ; 7, 4, 4 ; Plin. Ep. 2, 17, 7 .— In partic., in milit. lang., , , , tents for winterquarters , an encampment for winter , winter tents (opp.…

hībernālis.opening: adj. hibernus , wintry , winter- : glacies, Vulg. Sap. 16, 29 .

Hĭbernĭa.opening: (= Ἰουερνία Ptol.), the island now called Ireland , Caes. B. G. 5, 13, 2 ; Plin. 4, 16, 30, § 103 ; Tac. Agr. 24 .— Also called , , Mel. 3, 6, 6 : , , Juv. 2, 160 ; and (acc. to the Gr. form Ἰέρνη Strab.) , , App. de…

hīberno.opening: v. n. hibernus , to pass the winter , to winter. In gen.: furcillas reducit hibernatum in tecta, Varr. R. R. 1, 8, 6 : (thynni) ubicumque deprehensi usque ad aequinoctium, ibi hibernant, Plin. 9, 15, 20, § 51 :…

hībernus.opening: adj. root Sanscr. himas, Gr. χιών, snow, v. hiems; for hiemernus (hīm-), cf. χειμερινός , of or belonging to winter , wintry , winter -. Adj. : hiberno tempore, Lucr. 5, 699 : tempus, id. 5, 940 ; cf.: in aprico maxime…

hĭbiscum.opening: (also , Scrib. 80 ; 82 ; and , , , Serv. Verg. E. 2, 30 ), , , = ὶβίσκος , the marsh-mallow , Althaea officinalis, Linn.; Plin. 20, 4, 14, § 29 ; 19, 5, 27, § 89 ; Verg. E. 10, 71 : haedorumque gregem viridi compellere…

hibrĭda.opening: or ( ), , most prob. kindred with ὑβρίζω, ὕβρις, qs. unbridled, lawless, unnatural; hence , of animals produced from two different species, a mongrel , hybrid. Lit. : in nullo genere aeque facilis mixtura cum fero (quam…

hīc.opening: ( gen. hujus, monosyl., Plaut. Am. prol. 51 ; 96 ; 1, 1, 115 ; dat. huïc, Sidon. Carm. 7, 145; Avien. Descr. Orb. 22 ; dat. sing. fem. hae rei, Cato, R. R. 14, 3 ; acc. HONC for hunc, C. I. L. 1, 32; nom. plur. hic,…

Hĭcĕtāon.opening: , = Ἱκετάων , son of Laomedon king of Troy , App. de Deo Socr. p. 152, 9 .—Hence, , a um, of Hicetāon : Thymoetes, i. e. his son, Verg. A. 10, 123 .

Hĭcĕtas.opening: , = Ἱκέτας . A tyrant of Leontini , Nep. Tim. 2, 3 .— A philosopher of Syracuse , Cic. Ac. 2, 39, 123 dub. (al. Nicetas).

hĭĕmālis.opening: adj. hiems , of or belonging to winter , wintry , winter-. Adj. (class.): arbores ut hiemali tempore tempestive caedi putentur, Cic. Div. 2, 14, 33 : dies, Col. 11, 1, 21 : circulus, i. e. the tropic of Capricorn, Hyg.…

hĭĕmātĭo.opening: hiemo , a passing the winter , wintering : reliquum (mellis) hiemationi relinquatur, Varr. R. R. 3, 16, 34 .

hĭĕmo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
hĭĕmo.opening: v. n. and a. [hiems]. Neutr. Of persons, to pass the winter , to winter; of soldiers, to keep in winter-quarters : ubi piratae quotannis hiemare soleant, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 47, § 104 : naviget ac mediis hiemet mercator in…

Hĭempsal.opening: Son of Micipsa and king of Numidia , Sall. J. 5, 7 ; 11, 3 ; Flor. 3, 8, 4 ; Suet. Caes. 71 .— Another king of Numidia , perh. son of the former , Sall. J. 17 .— A king of Mauritania , Cic. Vatin. 5, 12 al.

hĭems.opening: or , , Gr. χιών, χεῖμα; Sanscr. himas, snow , the winter , winter time , rainy season (cf.: bruma, solstitium). Lit. : aestatem autumnus sequitur, post acer hiemps fit, Enn. ap. Prisc. p. 647 P. (Ann. v. 406 Vahl.):…

hĭĕra.opening: (sc. antidotus), = ἱερά (sacred; Lat. sacra), a sort of antidote against poison, Scrib. Comp. 99 ; 156 .— Perh. = corona, a garland : hieran fecimus, Sen. Ep. 83, 4 .

Hĭĕra.opening: The name of several islands , Mel. 2, 7, 18 ; Plin. 2, 106, 110, § 238 ; 4, 12, 23, § 70 al. — , a place in Caria , Liv. 38, 12, 10 ; cf. 38, 15, 7; 37, 19, 7.

hĭĕrābŏtănē.opening: (also separately ), , , = ἱερὰ βοτάνη (sacred plant), a plant , also called verbenaca, vervain , Verbena officinalis, Linn.; Plin. 25, 9, 59, § 105 ; Scrib. Comp. 163 .

hĭĕrācītis.opening: , = ἱερακῖτις (hawk-stone), a precious stone , otherwise unknown, Plin. 37, 10, 60, § 167 ; 37, 11, 72, § 187 .

hĭĕrācĭum.opening: , = ἱεράκιον , a sort of eye-salve , Plin. 34, 11, 27, § 114 .

Hĭĕrāpŏlis.opening: , = Ἱεράπολις . A city of Great Phrygia , now Pambouk Kaleh , Vitr. 8, 3, 10 ; Plin. 2, 93, 95, § 208 ; Vulg. Col. 4, 13 .—Hence, , , , the inhabitants of Hierapolis , Plin. 5, 29, 29, § 105 .— , , , the same, Macr. S.…

hĭĕrātĭcus.opening: adj. , = ἱερατικός , belonging to sacred uses , hieratic : charta hieratica appellatur antiquitus religiosis tantum voluminibus dicata, quae ablutione Augusti nomen accepit, sicut secunda Liviae, a conjuge ejus. Ita…

Hĭĕrĭcūs.opening: , = Ἱερικοῦς , the city of Jericho , in Palestine , Plin. 5, 14, 15, § 70 ; 13, 4, 9, § 44 .—Also called , = Ἱεριχώ , Prud. Psych. 536 ; acc. Jerichon, Prud. Ham. 480 Dressel.

Hĭĕro.opening: , = Ἱέρων . Ruler of Syracuse , a friend of the poet Simonides , Cic. N. D. 1, 22, 60 ; 3, 34, 83 .— A son of Hierocles , and ruler of Syracuse in the latter half of the third century B.C. , a friend of the Romans ,…

Hĭĕrŏcaesărīa.opening: or , , , = Ἱεροκαισάρεια , a city of Lydia , Tac. A. 2, 47 . —Hence, , , , its inhabitants , Tac. A. 3, 62 .

Hĭĕrō^cles.opening: , = Ἱεροκλῆς , a celebrated orator of Alabanda , an older contemporary of Cicero , Cic. Brut. 95, 325 ; id. de Or. 2, 23, 95 ; id. Or. 69, 231 .

hĭĕrŏdūlus.opening: , = ἱερόδουλος , a temple servant , Firm. Math. 8, 21.

hĭĕroglўphĭcus.opening: adj. , = ἱερογλυφικός , hieroglyphic : litterae, Macr. S. 1, 21, 12 : notae, Amm. 17, 4, 8 .

hĭĕrŏgrăphĭcus.opening: adj. , = ἱερογραφικός , i. q. hieroglyphicus, hierographic : litterae, Amm. 22, 15, 30 dub. (al. hieroglyphicas).

hĭĕrŏmnēmon.opening: , = ἱερομνήμων , a precious stone , also called erotylos, Plin. 37, 10, 58, § 160 .

hĭĕrŏnīca.opening: , = ἱερονίκης , a conqueror in the sacred games : Neapolin albis equis introiit, disjecta parte muri, ut mos hieronicarum est, Suet. Ner. 25 ; Inscr. Orell. 2160 ; 2628 sq. al.

Hĭĕrōnўmus.opening: , = Ἱερώνυμος . a ruler of Syracuse , the grandson and successor of the younger Hiero , Liv. 24, 4 sq. — A Greek peripatetic philosopher of Rhodes , Cic. Fin. 2, 3, 8 ; 5, 5, 14 ; id. Tusc. 2, 6, 15 ; 5, 30, 84 ; 5, 31,…

hĭĕrŏphanta.opening: or , , , = ἱεροφάντης , a teacher of religious rites and ceremonies , a high-priest , hierophant , Arn. 5, 174 ; Hier. adv. Jovin. 1, 49 fin. : agrorum, in the country , Cod. Th. 16, 4, 10; Inscr. Orell. 2305 ; 2351 sq.…

hĭĕrŏphўlax.opening: , = ἱεροφύλαξ , the keeper of a temple (pure Lat. aedituus), Dig. 33, 1, 20, § 1 .

Hĭĕrŏsŏlўma.opening: (secondary forms; v. infra ), = Ἱεροσόλυμα , the city of Jerusalem , in Palestine , Plin. 5, 14, 15, § 70 ; Cic. Fl. 28, 67 sq. ; Tac. H. 2, 4 ; 5, 1 ; 8 ; 9; Suet. Ner. 40 ; id. Tit. 5 ; Flor. 3, 5, 30 .— Also, fem.…

hĭĕto.opening: v. freq. n. and a. [for hiato, from hio; cf. Diom. p. 336 P.], to open the mouth wide , to gape , yawn (ante-class.): ego dum hieto, Plaut. Men. 3, 1, 4 ; cf. id. Fragm. ap. Diom. p. 336 P.: praei hercle tu, qui mihi…

Hilaīra.opening: , = Ἱλάειρα , daughter of Leucippus and bride of Ida , Prop. 1, 2, 16 .

hĭlăresco.opening: v. inch. n. [hilaris], to grow cheerful or merry : cum amicorum domus fumat, hilaresco, Varr. ap. Non. 121, 12 .

hĭlăris.opening: , and , , adj. , = ἱλαρός [cf. Sanscr. hlād, rejoice; Gr. χλαρός ; Engl. glad], cheerful , of good cheer , lively , gay , blithe , merry , jocund , jovial.—Adj. (class.; syn. laetus). Form hilaris: oderunt hilarem…

hĭlărĭtas.opening: hilaris , cheerfulness , gayety , good-humor , joyousness , merriment , hilarity (class.): hilaritatem illam, qua hanc tristitiam temporum condiebamus, in perpetuum amisi, Cic. Att. 12, 40, 3 ; cf.: tristitia deductis,…

hĭlărĭtūdo.opening: hilaris , cheerfulness , merriment (ante-class. for the class. hilaritas): numquam ego te tristiorem Vidi esse: quid cedo tam abhorret hilaritudo? Plaut. Cist. 1, 1, 56 : onera te hilaritudine, id. Mil. 3, 1, 83 : ut in…

hĭlăro.opening: v. a. hilaris , to make cheerful , to cheer , gladden , exhilarate (rare but class.): omnes jucundum motum, quo sensus hilaretur, Graece ἡδονήν , Latine voluptatem vocant, Cic. Fin. 2, 3, 8 : Periclis suavitate maxime…

hĭlărŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [hilaris], cheerful , contented : Atticae, quoniam, quod optimum in pueris est, hilarula est, meis verbis suavium des, Cic. Att. 16, 11 fin.

Hĭlărus.opening: name of a Roman freedman , Cic. Att. 1, 12, 2 et saep.

hillae.opening: dim. hira , the smaller and anterior intestines of animals (other than men and sheep). Lit. : ab hoc ventriculo lactes in homine et ove, per quas labitur cibus, in ceteris hillae, a quibus capaciora intestina ad alvum,…

Hīlōtae.opening: , = Εἵλωτες , the original inhabitants of the city Helos ( Ἕλος ), in Laconia , afterwards the bondsmen of the Spartans , the Helots , Nep. Paus. 3, 6 .— Called also , , Liv. 34, 27, 9 .

hīlum.opening: the primitive of nihilum, i. e. ne-hilum and nihil; etym. unknown; acc to Festus: hilum putant esse, quod grano fabae adhaeret, ex quo nihil et nihilum, Paul. ex Fest. p. 101 Müll.; cf.: hilum breve quoddam, Non. 121,…

hĭmantŏpūs.opening: , = ἱμαντόπους, ποδος , Lat. loripes, thongfoot, a kind of long-legged water-fowl , Plin. 10, 47, 64, § 130 .— Plur. : , , , a people of Æthiopia , Plin. 5, 8, 8, § 46 ; Mel. 3, 10, 3 ; Sol. 31, 6 ; Jul. Val. Res. Gest.…

Hĭmella.opening: a small river in the Sabine territory , now Aia , Verg. A. 7, 714 .

Hīmĕra.opening: , = Ἱμέρα . M. and , a river of Sicily , which divides into two branches , of which the northern one is now called Fiume Grande , and the southern Fiume Salso , Mel. 2, 7, 17 ; Plin. 3, 8, 14, § 90 ; Liv. 24, 6 ; Sil.…

hinc.opening: adv. for hince, locative form from hic , from this place. hence. In space: Imus huc: illuc hinc: cum illuc ventum est, ire illinc lubet, Enn. ap. Gell. 19, 10, 12 (Trag. v. 258 Vahl.): abiit hinc in exercitum, Plaut.…

hinnībĭlis.opening: adj. hinnio , that neighs , neighing (post-class.): quod hinnibile est, equus est, App. Dogm. Plat. 3, p. 30 : exscreatus, Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 10, 119 .

hinnĭbundus.opening: adj. id. , constantly neighing : equi, Quadrig. ap. Non. 122, 14 (Lachm. ad Lucr. 2, p. 236 ex conj.; MSS. hinnibunde).

hinnĭo.opening: ( perf. hinnisset, Val. Max. 7, 3 , ext. 2), v. n. , to neigh , whinny : ut si finias equum, genus est animal, species mortale, differentia irrationale (nam et homo mortale erat), proprium hinniens, Quint. 7, 3, 3 ;…

hinnītat.opening: χρεμετιζει , Gloss. Philox. [ freq. v. hinnio].

hinnītus.opening: hinnio , a neighing : subito exaudivit hinnitum, Cic. Div. 1, 33, 73 ; Lucr. 5, 1073 ; Verg. G. 3, 94 ; Hor. C. 2, 16, 34 .—In plur. , Ov. M. 2, 154 ; 669 ; Suet. Ner. 46 .

hinnŭlĕus.opening: hinnus , a young stag or roebuck , Prop. 3, 13, 35 ; Hor. C. 1, 23, 1 ; Plin. 28, 9, 42, § 150 .—As adj. : cervus, Scrib. 13 .— A young mule , Varr. L. L. 9, § 28 Müll.

hinnŭlus.opening: dim. id. , a young mule : tu tuum sodalem Hinnulo videas strigosiorem, Maecen. ap. Suet. Vit. Hor. (al. hinno me v. str-); cf. Plin. 8, 44, 69, § 172 Sill. N. cr.; and: hinnulus ὁ ἐξ ἵππου καὶ ὄνου , Gloss. Philox.;…

hinnus.opening: , = ἵννος , a mule (from a stallion and a she-ass; opp. mulus, from a he-ass and a mare): ex equa et asino fit mulus: contra ex equo et asina hinnus ... Hinnus est ex equo et asina, minor quam mulus corpore, etc., Varr.…

hĭo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
hĭo.opening: v. n. and a. [weakened from ΧΑΩ, χαίνω, χάσκω ; cf. Germ. gähnen]. Neutr. , to open , stand or be open , to gape. Lit. In gen. (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose): hiavit humus multa, Sall. Fragm. ap. Non. 318, 29 ;…

hippacāre.opening: est celeriter animam ducere ab equi halitu, qui est supra modum acutus, Paul. ex Fest. p. 101 Müll.; cf.: † hippicare = oscitare, badare, Gloss. Isid.

hippăcē.opening: , = ἱππάκη . Cheese made of mare's milk , Plin. 28, 9, 34, § 131 ; 28, 14, 58, § 204 .— A plant , now unknown, Plin. 25, 8, 44, § 83 .

hippāgĭnes.opening: , quas Graeci ἱππαγωγούς dicunt, Paul. ex Fest. p. 101 Müll.; so Gell. 10, 25, 5 ; cf. hippagogi and hippegus.

hippăgōgi.opening: (Gr. acc. -gūs, v. infra ), , = ἱππαγωγοί , vessels for transporting horses , cavalry-transports : quinque et triginta naves, quas hippagogus vocant, ab Elea profectae, cum equitibus Gallis equisque, Liv. 44, 28, 7 ;…

Hippălus.opening: another name of the wind Favonius, in the Indian Ocean , Plin. 6, 23, 26, § 104 .

Hipparchus.opening: , = Ἵππαρχος . A son of Pisistratus tyrant of Athens , and brother of Hippias , killed by Harmodius and Aristogiton , Gell. 17, 21, 7 .— A celebrated astronomer of Nicœa , Cic. Att. 2, 6, 1 ; Plin. 2, 26, 24, § 95 ; 2,…

Hippărīnus.opening: , = Ἱππαρῖνος , the name of the father of Dion , Nep. Dion. 1, 1 .

Hippăris.opening: a small river of Sicily , flowing by the city of Camarina , whence it is now called Fiume di Camarana , Sil. 12, 230 .

Hippăsus.opening: Son of Eurytus , Ov. M. 8, 313 .— A centaur , Ov. M. 12, 352 .

hippēgus.opening: , = ἱππηγός (sc. navis), a transport for cavalry , Plin. 7, 56, 57, § 209 ; cf. hippagogi.

hippeus.opening: ( ), ĕï, , = ἱππεύς (horseman), a kind of comet : hippeus equinas jubas (habet), Plin. 2, 25, 22, § 90 .

Hippias.opening: , = Ἱππίας . A son of Pisistratus tyrant of Athens , and brother of Hipparchus , after whose assassination he fled to the Persians; he fell in the battle of Marathon , Cic. Att. 9, 10, 3 ; Gell. 9, 2, 10 .— A famous…

Hippius.opening: a Roman proper name , Cic. Fam. 13, 76 . † , , etc., Paul. ex Fest. p. 101 Müll. [= Ἵππειος or Ἵππιος ].

Hippo.opening: , = Ἱππών , the name of several cities. A city of Numidia , also with the surname of regius, Gr. Ἱππὼν βασιλικός , afterwards a bishop's see , now Bonah , Mel. 1, 7, 1 ; Liv. 29, 3, 7 ; Sil. 3, 259 .— Hippo Diarrhytus,…

hippŏcămēlus.opening: , = ἱπποκάμηλος , a fabulous animal , half horse and half camel , Aus. Epigr. 70 .

hippŏcampus.opening: or , , , = ἱππόκαμπος , a sea-horse : Syngnathus hippocampus, Linn.; Plin. 32, 11, 53, § 149 ; 32, 7, 23, § 67 ; 32, 9, 30, § 93 ; 36, 5, 4, § 26; Naev. and Lucil. ap. Non. 120, 17 and 19.

hippŏcentaurus.opening: , = ἱπποκέϝταυπος , a fabulous creature , half horse and half man , hippocentaur , Cic. N. D. 2, 2, 5 ; id. Tusc. 1, 37, 90 ; Plin. 7, 3, 3, § 35 : si quis rem quae in rerum natura non est aut esse non potest, velut…

Hippŏcŏon.opening: Of Amyclœ , father of Enœsimus , who took part in the Calydonian hunt , Ov. M. 8, 314 and 363; Hyg. Fab. 173 .— A companion of Æneas , an archer , Verg. A. 5, 492 ; Hyg. Fab. 273 .

hippocoum.grammar: vinum ex insula Coo dictum ab agro generoso, cui nomen est Hippo

Hippocrătes.opening: , = Ἱπποκράτης , the celebrated Greek physician of Cos , founder of the art of medicine , Cels. praef.; Cic. de Or. 3, 33, 132 ; Quint. 3, 6, 64 .— Deriv.: , , adj. , of or belonging to Hippocrates , Hippocratic :…

Hippocrēnē.opening: , = Ἱπποκρήνη , a fountain near Mount Helicon , sacred to the Muses , and which is fabled to have been produced by a stroke of Pegasus's hoof , Ov. F. 5, 7 ; Sol. 7 med. (in Hor. Ep. 1, 3, 10 : fons Pindaricus, and in…

hippŏdămantĭum vīnum.opening: a sort of wine , otherwise unknown, Plin. 14, 7, 9, § 75 .

Hippŏdămas.opening: , = Ἱπποδάμας , the father of Perimele , Ov. M. 8, 592 .

Hippŏdămē.opening: , and or , , , = Ἱπποδάμη or Ἱπποδάμεια . Daughter of Œnomaüs , king of Elis; she became the wife of Pelops , who won her in a race with her father , Enn. ap. Cic. Tusc. 3, 12, 26 (Trag. v. 398 Vahl.); Prop. 1, 2, 20 ;…

Hippŏdămus.opening: , = Ἱππόδαμος , the horse-tamer , a poet. epithet of Castor, Mart. 7, 57, 2 .

hippodrŏmos.opening: , = ἱππόδρομος , a race-course for horses , hippodrome , Plaut. Bacch. 3, 3, 27 ; Plin. Ep. 5, 6, 19 ; Mart. 12, 50, 5 ; Sid. Ap. 2, 2 .

Hippŏlўtē.opening: , and , , , = Ἱππολύτη . An Amazon , daughter of Mars , taken captive in the war of the Amazons by Theseus , to whom she bore Hippolytus , Hyg. Fab. 30 ; Just. 2, 4, 23 ; Plaut. Men. 1, 3, 17 .— The wife of Acastus ,…

Hippŏlўtus.opening: , = Ἱππόλυτος , son of Theseus and Hippolyte; his step-mother Phœdra fell in love with him , but , on her advances being repelled , she accused him to her husband of attempts upon her chastity; the king in his rage…

hippŏmănes.opening: , = ἱππομανές (horse-heat, horse-rage). A slimy humor that flows from a mare when in heat , and which was used to excite desire , Verg. G. 3, 280 sq. ; Tib. 2, 4, 8 ; Prop. 4, 5, 18 (cf. Verg. A. 4, 516 ).— A plant that…

hĭppŏmărăthum.opening: or , , , = ἱππομάραθον , horse-fennel , wild fennel , Plin. 20, 23, 96, § 258 .

Hippŏmĕnēis.opening: , = Ἱππομενηΐς , Limone , a daughter of Hippomenes of Athens , who , as a punishment for unchastity , was thrown by her father to a horse to be devoured , Ov. Ib. 337 ; cf. id. ib. 461 (al. Hippomeneia).

Hippŏmĕnes.opening: , = Ἱππομένης , son of Megareus , who conquered Atalanta , the daughter of Schœneus , in a race , and thus obtained her as his wife , Ov. M. 10, 575 sq. ; 632 ; Hyg. Fab. 185 ; Serv. Verg. A. 3, 113 .

Hippōnax.opening: , = Ἱππώναξ , a Greek poet of Ephesus , who wrote in iambics , celebrated for the bitterness of his satires , Cic. N. D. 3, 38, 91 ; Plin. 36, 5, 4, § 12 . — Deriv.: , , adj. , of Hipponax , in the style of Hipponax ,…

Hippŏnīcus.opening: , = Ἱππόνικος , an Athenian , father-in-law of Alcibiades , Nep. Alcib. 2 .

hippŏphăes.opening: , = ἱπποφαές , a plant (perh. the Euphorbia spinosa, Linn.), Plin. 21, 15, 54, § 91 ; 22, 12, 14, § 29 .

hippŏphaeston.opening: , = ἱππόφαιστον , a prickly plant (perh. Centaurea calcitrapa, Linn.), Plin. 27, 10, 66, § 92 .

Hippŏpŏdes.opening: , = Ἱππόποδες , a fabulous race of men , with horses' feet , Plin. 4, 13, 27, § 95 ; Mel. 3, 6, 8 .

hippŏpŏtămus.opening: , = ἱπποπόταμος , a river - horse , hippopotamus , Plin. 8, 25, 39, § 95 ; Mel. 1, 9, 3 ; Amm. 22, 15 .

hippŏsĕlīnum.opening: , = ἱπποσέλινον , a sort of wild parsley; lit., horse-parsley , Plin. 19, 8, 37, § 124 ; Pall. Apr. 3 ( Col. 11, 3, 36 , written as Greek, and translated by olus atrum).

Hippŏtădes.opening: , = Ἱπποτάδης , the descendant of Hippotes , i. e. Æŏlus (as the son of Segesta, a daughter of the Trojan Hippotes), Ov. M. 4, 663 ; 11, 431 ; 14, 224 : Hippotadae regnum, i. e. the Æolic (Liparic) Isles , id. ib. 14,…

Hippŏthŏus.opening: son of Cercyon , who took part in the Calydonian hunt , Ov. M. 8, 306 .

hippŏtoxŏtae.opening: , = ἱπποτοξόται , mounted archers , Caes. B. C. 3, 4, 5 ; Auct. B. Afr. 19, 6 (pure Lat., equites sagittarii, Tac. A. 2, 16 ; Curt. 5, 4 ).

hippūris.opening: , = ἵππουρις , horsetail , a water-plant; pure Lat., equisetum, Plin. 26, 13, 83, § 132 ; App. Herb. 39 .

hippūrus.opening: , = ἵππουρος , a fish (perh. golden carp , gold fish , Coryphaena hippurus, Linn.), Ov. Hal. 95 ; Plin. 9, 16, 24, § 57 ; 32, 11, 53, § 149 .

hippus.opening: , = ἵππος , a sea-fish , otherwise unknown, Plin. 32, 11, 53, § 149 .

hir.opening: or , from χείρ, like heres from χῆρος, and hiems from χεῖμα, χειμών , a hand : quibu' vinum Defusum e pleno siet, ir siphove, cui nil Dempsit, i. e. the palm of the hand , used in tasting wine , Lucil. ap. Cic. Fin. 2,…

hīra.opening: the empty gut; called also intestinum jejunum, Gr. νῆστις , Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 6 fin. ; Plaut. Curc. 2, 1, 23 ; Arn. 7, 24 .

hircīnus.opening: ( ), , adj. hircus , of a goat , goat's : barba, Plaut. Ps. 4, 2, 12 : sanguis, Plin. 20 prooem. § 2; 37, 4, 15, § 59: pelles, id. 12, 17, 40, § 81 : folles, Hor. S. 1, 4, 19 : sidus, i. e. the constellation Capricorn,…

Hircĭpes.opening: hircus - pes , goat-footed , an appellation of Pan, Mart. Cap. 9, § 906 .

hirco.opening: v. n. , to howl , of the sound of the lynx, Auct. Carm. de Philom. 51.

hircōsus.opening: adj. hircus , that smells like a goat , goatish : senex, Plaut. Merc. 3, 3, 14 : gens centurionum, Pers. 3, 77 : subulcus, Mart. 10, 98, 10 ; cf.: licet scripti sint inter hircosos, possint tamen inter unguentatos…

hircŭlus.opening: dim. id. . A little goat , Auct. Priap. 86, 16 (Ps.-Catull. 19, 16). — A plant , otherwise unknown, Plin. 12, 12, 26, § 46 .

hircŭōsus.opening: adj. id. , goatish : Pan, App. M. 5, p. 169 fin.

hircus.opening: (also and ; cf. Quint. 1, 5, 20 ; and the Sabine form, FIRCUS, Varr. L. L. 5, § 97 Müll.; cf. haedus init. ), i, m., a he-goat , buck (cf. haedus, caper). Lit. , Verg. E. 3, 8 ; 91 ; id. G. 3, 312 ; Hor. Epod. 16, 34 ;…

hirnĕa.opening: (also ), , , a jug for holding liquids, Cato, R. R. 81 ; Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 273 ; 276 .

hirnŭla.opening: dim. hirnea , a small jug or pitcher for liquids; in an unaspirated form: irnela vasis genus in sacris, Paul. ex Fest. p. 105 Müll. N. cr. (but urnulas is the true reading in Cic. Par. 1, 2, 11 ).

Hirpi.opening: a very ancient Sabine family near Rome , in the territory of the Falisci , Plin. 7, 2, 2, § 19 ; Sol. 2, § 26 .

Hirpīni.opening: ( ), , , a people of Lower Italy , between Campania , Lucania , and Apulia , Plin. 3, 11, 16, § 99 ; Liv. 22, 61, 11 ; 23, 37 ; 27, 15 : in Hirpinis, in the territory of the Hirpini, Cic. Div. 1, 36, 79 ; Plin. 2, 93,…

hirpus.opening: or , in the Sabine lang., the wolf , Paul. ex Fest. p. 106, 1 Müll.; Serv. ad Verg. A. 11, 785 .

hirquitallĭo.opening: v. n. hircus , of new - born children, to acquire a strong voice : in secunda hebdomade vel incipiente tertia vocem crassiorem et inaequabilem fieri: quod Aristoteles appellat τραγίζειν , antiqui nostri † hirquitallire:…

hirrĭo.opening: ( ), , v. n. , of dogs, to snarl : hirrire = garrire, quod genus vocis est canis rabiosae, Paul. ex Fest. p. 101 Müll. N. cr.; cf.: hirrit ὅταν κύων ἀπειλῇ ὑλακτῶν , Gloss. Philox.: veluti est canibus innatum, ut, etsi…

hirrītus.opening: ( ), , hirrio , a snarling of dogs, Sid. Ep. 9, 16 in carm.

hirsūtĭa.opening: hirsutus , roughness , shagginess : nullae setarum, Sol. 25, § 10 .

hirsūtus.opening: adj. primary form HIRSUS, a variation of hirtus , rough , shaggy , bristly , prickly , hirsute = δασύς . Lit. (class.; syn. hirtus, pilosus, villosus): quarum (animantium) aliae villis vestitae, aliae spinis hirsutae,…

hirtipili.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 101 Müll. N. cr.

Hirtĭus.opening: name of a Roman gens.; in partic., A. Hirtius, consul A. U. C. 711, and author of the eighth book of Cœsar's Commentaries on the Gallic war: he fell before Mutina , Cic. Att. 7, 4, 2 ; Q. Cic. ap. Cic. Fam. 16, 27, 1 .—…

hirtŭōsus.opening: , false read. in App. M. 5, p. 169 , inst. of hircuosus.

hirtus.opening: adj. , rough , hairy , shaggy , = δασύς (mostly post-Aug.; cf. hirsutus, hispidus, pilosus, villosus, setosus). Lit. : oves, Varr. R. R. 2, 2, 19 : hirto corde quosdam homines nasci proditur, Plin. 11, 37, 70, § 185 :…

hĭrūdo.opening: (also called sanguisūga), a leech , blood-sucker , Plin. 32, 10, 42, § 122 : ego me convortam in hirudinem atque exsugebo sanguinem, Plaut. Ep. 2, 2, 4 .—Fig., of any thing that exhausts, etc.: aerarii, Cic. Att. 1, 16,…

hĭrundĭnĕus.opening: adj. hirundo , of or belonging to swallows (post-class.): adventus, of the swallows, Sid. Ep. 2, 14 ; cf. the foll. art.

hĭrundĭnīnus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to swallows , swallows' (class.): sanguis, fel, Plin. 30, 14, 46, § 133 : nidus, Plaut. Rud. 3, 1, 6 ; Mart. 11, 18, 20 .

hĭrundo.opening: (weakened from χελιδών ), a swallow. Lit. , Plin. 10, 33, 49, § 92 ; 10, 24, 34, § 70 ; Plaut. Rud. 3, 1, 12 ; Verg. G. 1, 377 ; id. A. 12, 474 ; Ov. F. 2, 853 ; Hor. Ep. 1, 7, 13 .—As a term of endearment: dic me…

hisco.opening: v. inch. n. and a. [hio; whence also hiasco]. Neutr. , to open , gape , yawn. In gen.: tellus, ait, hisce, Ov. M. 1, 546 ; cf.: magnae nunc hiscite terrae, Poët. ap. Quint. 9, 2, 26 : rima hiscit, Plin. 17, 14, 24, §…

Hispălis.opening: a city of Hispania Baetica, now Sevilla , Plin. 2, 97, 100, § 219 ; Caes. B. C. 2, 18 ; 20 ; Asin. Pollio ap. Cic. Fam. 10, 32, 3 .—In the neut. form: , , Mel. 2, 6, 4 ; Plin. 3, 1, 3, § 11 ; Sil. 3, 392 .— Deriv.: or ,…

Hispānē.opening: adv. , after the manner of Spain , v. Hispani, II. A. fin.

Hispāni.opening: the Spaniards , Liv. 21, 27 ; Tac. A. 1, 78 ; Suet. Caes. 76 al. — Derivv. , , adj. , of or belonging to the Spaniards , Spanish : mare, Plin. 3, 5, 10, § 74 : aurum, Mart. 7, 88, 7 : Tarraco, id. 10, 104, 4 : populi,…

Hispellum.opening: a city of Umbria , at the foot of the Apennines , now Spello , Plin. 3, 14, 19, § 113 ; Sil. 8, 458 ; Inscr. Orell. 3885 . — , , , the inhabitants of Hispellum , Plin. Ep. 8, 8, 6 .

hispĭdo.opening: v. a. hispidus , to make bristly , prickly : spinosis fastigiis hispidatur, Sol. 26 dub. (al. hispida turgescit).

hispĭdus.opening: adj. , rough , shaggy , hairy , bristly , prickly. Lit. ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose; syn. v. hirtus): facies, Hor. C. 4, 10, 5 ; cf. frons, Verg. A. 10, 210 : membra, Juv. 2, 11 : corpus Nereïdum squamis, Plin. 9, 5,…

Hispo.opening: a Roman surname , Cic. Fam. 13, 65 ; 14, 1 ; Juv. 2, 50 .

Hispulla.opening: the name of a woman , Juv. 6, 74 ; 12, 11 ; Plin. Ep. 4, 19 tit.

Hister.opening: (less correctly ), , = Ἴστρος , the lower part of the Danube (the upper part, Danubius). Prop. In gen.: Ponticum simul et Hadriaticum mare et Histrum amnem et Alpes conspici posse, Liv. 40, 21 : turbidus et torquens…

histon.opening: , = ἱστών , the place where a loom stands , a weaving-room : habere institutos histonas, Varr. R. R. 1, 2, 21 .

histŏrĭa.opening: , = ἱστορία , a narrative of past events , history (syn.: annales, fasti). Lit. : historia testis temporum, lux veritatis, vita memoriae, magistra vitae, nuntia vetustatis, qua voce alia nisi oratoris immortalitati…

histŏrĭālis.opening: adj. historia , of or belonging to history , historical (late Lat.): venerabilis patriarchae Joseph historialis diligentia, i. e. related in sacred history, Sid. Ep. 6, 12 .

histŏrĭcē.opening: , = ἱστορική , explanation , interpretation of an author: finitae quidem sunt partes duae, quas haec professio pollicetur, id est ratio loquendi et enarratio auctorum: quarum illam methodicen, hanc historicen vocant,…

histŏrĭcus.opening: adj. , = ἱστορικός , of or belonging to history , historical. Adj. : earum rerum historiam non tam historico quam oratorio genere perscripsit, Cic. Brut. 83, 286 ; cf. Plin. Ep. 7, 9, 8 : sermo, Cic. Or. 36, 124 :…

histŏrĭŏgrăphus.opening: , = ἱστοριογράφος , a writer of history , historiographer (post-class.), Capitol. Gord. 11, 21 ; Ambros. Ep. 42, 2 ; Cassiod. Eccl. Hist. 1, 1 ; Hier. Galat. 2, 14 .

Histri.opening: (less correctly ), , , the people of Istria , Istrians , a barbarous Illyrian tribe subdued by the Romans B. C. 177: principes Histrorum, Liv. 41, 11 ; Plin. 3, 19, 23, § 129 : Histrorum gentem originem a Colchis…

histrĭcŭlus.opening: λογοποιός , Gloss. Philox. [ dim. from histrio; cf. the foll. art.].

histrĭcus.opening: adj. hister, histrio , of or belonging to stage-players : imperator histricus, the manager, Plaut. Poen. prol. 4 ; cf. imperium, the management, id. ib. 44 .

histrio.opening: Etrusc. prim. form HISTER, Liv. 7, 2, 6; Val. Max. 2, 4, 4; whence histricus and histriculus , a stage-player , actor , either tragic or comic (syn.: actor, mimus, tragoedus, comoedus). Lit. : quod verbum in cavea dixit…

histrĭōnālis.opening: adj. histrio , of or belonging to a stage-player , like an actor (a word of Tac.): studium, Tac. A. 1, 16 : modi, id. Or. 26 : favor, id. ib. 29 .

histrĭōnĭa.opening: (sc. ars) [id.], the art of stage-playing , dramatic art : facere histrioniam, to assume the character of an actor, Plaut. Am. prol. 90 ; Macr. S. 2, 10, 12 : exercere, Petr. Fr. 10 .

histrĭōnĭcus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to a player , histrionic (post-class.): operae, Dig. 32, 1, 73 : gestus, Amm. 14, 6, 18 .— Subst. : , , , the player's art , Lampr. Heliog. 12, 1 .

hĭulco.opening: , no perf. , , v. a. hiulcus , to cause to gape or split open , to break into chinks : cum gravis exustos aestus hiulcat agros, Cat. 68, 62 : per hiulcatos agros, Fortun. Carm. 6, 12, 6 .

hĭulcus.opening: adj. hio , gaping , split , cleft , opened , open. Lit. (only poet. ): ubi hiulca siti findit Canis aestifer arva, Verg. G. 2, 353 : Aegyptus, Stat. Th. 4, 708 : venae fluminis, id. ib. 9, 450 : juga montis Tauri, Sol.…

ho!.opening: interj. , an expression of astonishment, oh! ho! tune is eras? Ter. Phorm. 5, 7, 52 dub. (al. oh!).

hŏdĭē.opening: adv. contr. from hoc die, on this day , to-day. Lit. : quem quidem negat Eros hodie: cras mane putat, Cic. Att. 13, 30, 2 ; so opp. cras, Ov. R. Am. 94 ; Hor. Ep. 1, 16, 33 : hodie mane, this morning, Cic. Att. 13, 9, 1…

hŏdĭernus.opening: adj. hodie , of this day , to-day's. Lit. : quod ex hodierno ejus edicto perspicere potestis, Cic. Phil. 4, 3, 7 : disputatio hesterni et hodierni diei, id. de Or. 3, 21, 81 : hodierno die, mane, today, id. Cat. 3, 9,…

hŏdoedŏcos.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 103 Müll. [= όδοιδόκος ].

holcē.opening: , = ὁλκή , a drachma : holceque a drachma non re sed nomine differt, Fann. de Pond. 19.

holcus.opening: , = όλκός , a sort of grain , mouse - barley , Hordeum murinum, Linn.; Plin. 27, 10, 63, § 90 .

hŏlĕrācĕus.opening: ( ), , adj. holus , resembling herbs , vegetable : frutex, Plin. 26, 8, 53, § 85 .

hŏlĕrārĭum.opening: ( ), , id. , a vegetable-garden , kitchen-garden : olerarium, λαχανάριον , Gloss.

hŏlĕrātor.opening: ( ), , holero , one who cultivates vegetables , a market-gardener : holerator, λαχανοπώλης , Gloss. Philox.

hŏlĕro.opening: ( ), , v. a. holus , to plant with vegetables : hortulos, Matt. ap. Prisc. p. 722 P.: holeratus, holeribus consitus, Not. Tir. p. 168 .

hŏlŏcaustum.opening: , = ὁλόκαυστον , a whole burnt - offering , holocaust , Prud. Apoth. 537 ; id. Psych. 784 ; Vulg. Exod. 40, 6 ; id. Lev. 4, 7 al. ; cf. the foll. art.

hŏlŏcautōma.opening: , = ὁλοκαύτωμα , a whole burnt-offering , holocaust , Tert. adv. Jud. 5 ; id. adv. Marc. 5, 5 fin. ; Vulg. Jer. 6, 20 ; id. Ev. Marc. 12, 33 al. (in some edd. falsely holocaustoma).

hŏlŏchrȳsus.opening: , = ὁλόχρυσος , a plant , otherwise unknown, Plin. 21, 8, 24, § 48 ; 21, 20, 85, § 148 ; App. Herb. 128 .

hŏlŏcўron.opening: , = ὁλόκυρον , a plant , called also chamaepitys, ground-pine , App. Herb. 26 .

hŏlŏgrăphus.opening: adj. , = ὁλόγραφος , entirely autograph (late Lat.): epistula, entirely written by one's own hand, autograph, Hier. adv. Ruf. 3, 5 : membrana, Sid. Ep. 9, 11 med. : testamentum, Isid. Orig. 5, 24 .

hŏlŏporphўrus.opening: adj. , = ὁλοπόρφυρος , entirely purple : stola, Varr. ap. Non. 537, 30 : vestis, Isid. Orig. 19, 22, 14 .

hŏloschoenos.opening: , = ὁλόσχοινος , a sort of rush , Plin. 21, 18, 69, § 113 .

hŏlŏsērĭcus.opening: adj. , = ὁλοσηρικός , all of silk : vestis, Lampr. Heliog. 20 ; Vop. Aur. 45 ; id. Tac. 10 ; Cod. Th. 15, 9, 1. —Collat. form, , , Aug. in Psa. 85, 3 .

hŏlŏsĭdērus.opening: adj. , = ὁλοσίδηρος , all iron : spatula, Theod. Prisc. 1, 28 .

hŏlosphȳrātus.opening: adj. , = ὁλοσφύρᾶτος (Doric for ὁλοσφύρητος , all hammered), beaten , solid : aes, Plin. 33, 4, 24, § 82 .

hŏlostĕon.opening: , = ὁλόστεον , a whitish plantain , Plantago albicans, Linn.; Plin. 27, 10, 65, § 91 .

hŏlŏthūrĭa.opening: , = ὁλοθούρια, τά , a sort of water-polype , Holothuria priapus, Linn.; Plin. 9, 47, 71, § 154 .

hŏlŏvērus.opening: adj. vox hybr. from ὅλος-verus , quite real; entirely of purple : vestimenta, Cod. Th. 10, 21, 3.

hŏlus.opening: (better than ; archaic ; cf.: helus et helusa antiqui dicebant, quod nunc holus et holera, Paul. ex Fest. p. 100 Müll. A form, holu, anciently helu, can be inferred from helvola, helvella, and olvatum; v. Müll. Paul. ex…

hŏluscŭlum.opening: dim. holus , a small herb or vegetable , a little cabbage (class.), Cic. Att. 6, 1, 13 ; Hor. S. 2, 6, 64 ; Juv. 11, 79 ; Gell. 19, 7, 1 .

Hŏmērŏcento.opening: Homeruscento , a poem made up of verses from Homer , Tert. de Praescr. 39 ; Hier. Ep. 103, 7 .

Hŏmērŏmastix.opening: , = Ὁμηρομάστιξ (Homer's scourge), the censurer of Homer. Lit. , an epithet given to the critic Zoilus, Vitr. 7 praef. — Transf. , in gen., a censorious person : ut obiter caveam istos Homeromastigas, etc., Plin. H. N.…

Hŏmērŏnĭdes.opening: v. the foll. art. II. E.

Hŏmērus.opening: , = Ὅμηρος , the Greek poet Homer , Cic. Tusc. 1, 1, 3 ; 1, 32, 79 ; id. Rep. 2, 10 ; id. Brut. 10, 40 ; id. Arch. 8, 19 ; id. de Or. 3, 34, 137 ; Vell. 1, 5, 2 ; Quint. 10, 1, 47 sq. ; Hor. A. P. 359 al. — Derivv. , ,…

hŏmĭcīda.opening: homo-caedo , a man-slayer , homicide , a murderer , murderess (syn.: interfector, sicarius, percussor). Lit. : statuendum tibi esse, utrum illi, qui istam rem gesserunt, homicidaene sint, an vindices libertatis ...…

hŏmĭcīdālis.opening: adj. homicida , homicidal , murderous (late Lat.), Pseudo-Hilar. in Job, 1, p. 101.

hŏmĭcīdārĭus.opening: or , , adj. homicida and homicidium , of or relating to man-slaying , homicidal : sanguis, Auct. Pan. ad Const. 4.

hŏmĭcīdĭum.opening: homicida , manslaughter , homicide , murder (post-class.): si quis homicidii accusetur, Quint. 3, 10, 1 ; 4, 2, 52 ; 11, 3, 59 ; Petr. 137 ; Plin. 18, 3, 3, § 12 ; Tac. G. 21 .

hŏmo.opening: (archaic form hemonem hominem dicebant, Paul. ex Fest. p. 100 Müll.; cf. humanus init. , and nēmo, from nĕ-hĕmo: homōnem, Enn. ap. Prisc. p. 683 P. = Ann. v. 141 Vahl.: hŏmōnes, Naev. 1, 1 ), root in humus, Gr. χαμαί;…

hŏmŏcīdālis.opening: adj. homo-caedo , murderous : animus suus, Anon. (Hilar.) in Job, 1, p. 101.

hŏmoeŏmĕrīa.opening: , = ὁμοιομέρεια ; in the philosophy of Anaxagoras, the homogeneousness of the elements or first principles , Lucr. 1, 830 ; Serv. Verg. A. 4, 625 .

hŏmoeŏprŏphĕron.opening: , = ὁμοιοπρόφερον , alliteration , as in the verse of Ennius (ap. Prisc. p. 947 P. = Ann. v. 113 Vahl.): o Tite tute Tati tibi tanta tyranne tulisti, Mart. Cap. 5, § 514 .

hŏmoeoptōton.opening: , = ὁμοιόπτωτον , similar case-endings , Mart. Cap. 5, § 532 ; Charis. 251 P.; cf. Quint. 9, 3, 78 sqq.

hŏmoeŏtĕleuton.opening: , = ὁμοιοτέλευτον , like ending , rhyme , Mart. Cap. 5, § 532 ; Charis. 251 P.

Hŏmŏlē.opening: , = Ὁμόλη , a high mountain in Thessaly , near Tempe , Verg. A. 7, 675 .—At the foot of it was the city , Plin. 4, 9, 16, § 32 ; Liv. 42, 38, 10 .— Deriv. , , (sc. portae), = Ὁμολωίδες πύλαι , the Homoloian gate in…

hŏmŏlŏgus.opening: , = ὁμόλογος , a later colonist , Cod. Theod. 11, 24, 6, § 3 .

hŏmōnўmĭa.opening: , = ὁμωνυμία , homonymy , Fronto, Diff. Verb. p. 353 .

hŏmōnўmus.opening: adj. , = ὁμώνυμος , of the same name , homonymous : sicut in his, quae homonyma vocantur: ut, Taurus animal sit, an mons, an signum in caelo, an nomen hominis, an radix arboris, nisi distinctum non intelligitur, Quint.…

hŏmŏtŏnus.opening: adj. , = ὁμότονος , stretched alike or in unison : nervi, funes, etc., Vitr. 1, 1 med.

hŏmŏūsius.opening: adj. , = ὁμοούσιος , of like substance , consubstantial (Lat. consubstantialis): Trinitas, Hier. Ep. 77, 2 .

hŏmullŭlus.opening: dim. homullus , a manikin , Prisc. p. 614 P.

hŏmullus.opening: dim. homo , a little man , manikin : brevis hic est fructus homullis, Lucr. 3, 914 : quid cessat hic homullus, ex argilla et luto fictus Epicurus, etc., Cic. Pis. 25, 59 .

hŏmuncĭo.opening: dim. id. , a little man , manikin : ego homuncio hoc non facerem? Ter. Eun. 3, 5, 42 : homuncio hic, qui multa putat praeter virtutem homini cara esse (opp. deus), Cic. Ac. 2, 43, 134 : (Augustus Horatium) inter alios…

impī^grĭtas.opening: ( ), , impiger , activity , indefatigableness : viri fortissimi fortitudinis, impigritatis, patientiae, Cic. Rep. 3, 28, 40 (ap. Non. 125, 22 ).

impī^grĭtĭa.opening: ( ), , id. , activity , indefatigableness , persistency , Ambros. de Noë, 2, 3; id. de Jacob. 2, 2, 8 : impigritas pro impigritia, Non. 125, 20 .

impingo.opening: ( ), (archaic inf. pres. pass. impingier, Plaut. Capt. 3, 5, 76 ), v. a. in-pango , to push , strike , or drive at or into any thing; to thrust , strike , or dash against (not freq. till after the Aug. per.; cf.:…

impinguo.opening: ( ), no perf. , , v. a. and n. in-pinguis . Act. , to make fat (post-class.): impinguo πιαίνω, Gloss. Philox.: cui cor impinguatum, Tert. Jejun. 6 .—* Neutr. , to become fat : porcellum tamdiu coques, donec lenis fiat…

impĭo.opening: ( ), , v. a. impius , to render impious or sinful , to stain or defile with sin , to pollute (ante- and postclass.): si erga parentem aut deos me impiavi, Plaut. Rud. 1, 3, 8 : impias, ere, te! oratorem verberas, id.…

impĭus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-pius , without reverence or respect for God, one's parents, or one's country; irreverent , ungodly , undutiful , unpatriotic; abandoned , wicked , impious (rare but class.; cf.: nefarius, sacrilegus).…

implācābĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inplacabilis , unappeasable , implacable (rare but class.); constr. with alicui , in aliquem , and absol. : seque mihi implacabilem inexpiabilemque praeberet, Cic. Pis. 33, 81 : implacabilis esse alicui,…

implācātus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-placatus , unappeased , unsatisfied , unallayed ( poet. ): Charybdis, Verg. A. 3, 420 : gula, Ov. M. 8, 847 .

implăcĭdus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-placidus , ungentle , rough , savage , fierce ( poet. ): Genauni, implacidum genus, Hor. C. 4, 14, 10 : Mars divum implacidissimus, Stat. Th. 9, 4 : implacido letalis Sirius igni, Stat. S. 2, 1, 216 :…

implăgo.opening: ( ), , v. a. in-plaga , to bring into a net , to entangle , ensnare. — Trop. : in retia sua praecipites implagabuntur, Sid. Ep. 9, 9 fin.

implāno.opening: ( ), , v. a. 2. in-plano = impedio, hence trop. = decipio , to deceive , delude (late Lat.), Vulg. Sirach, 15, 12 al.

implānus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inplanus , uneven (post-class.): inter implana urbis, Aur. Vict. Caes. 27, 2 .

implēbĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. impleo , filling up (post-class.): vomitus, Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 8, 139 .

implectĭcus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-plecto , that turns about with difficulty , immovable : bos, Veg. Vet. 3, 29 dub.

implecto.opening: ( ), , v. a. in-plecto , to plait , wind , or twist into , to wind or twist among , to interweave , interlace , entwine ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose; usually in the part. perf. ). Lit. : multae hirudines dentibus…

implēmentum.opening: ( ), , impleo , a filling up , as a diseased condition: capitis, i. e. a determination of blood to the head, Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 5, 148 .

implĕo.opening: ( ), (sync. forms: implerunt, Verg. E. 6, 48 ; id. G. 4, 461 ; Pers. 1, 99 ; Ov. M. 11, 666 al. : impleris, Hor. Epod. 17, 59 : implerit, Ov. M. 6, 111 : implerint, Cic. Agr. 2, 18, 47 : implerat, Ov. M. 9, 280 al. :…

implētĭo.opening: ( ), , impleo , the ful filment (eccl. Lat.), Salv. Gub. 2, 2, p. 52 Rittersh.; Hier. in Isa. 11, 40, 3 sqq.

implexĭo.opening: ( ), , implecto , an entwining , entangling (post-class.): serpentis gemini, Mart. Cap. 2, § 176 .

implexus.opening: implecto , an entwining , infolding , embrace (post-Aug. and only in the abl. sing. ): polypus cavernam cancellato bracchiorum implexu claudit, Plin. 9, 51, 74, § 164 : ut terra et aqua mutuo implexu jungerentur, id. 2,…

implĭcāmentum.opening: ( ), , inplico , an involvement , entanglement (late Lat.).— Trop. : miseriarum implicamentis se expedire, Aug. de Serm. Dom. 1, 3 med.

implĭcātĭo.opening: ( ), , id. , an entwining , interweaving , entanglement (Ciceron.): nervorum implicatio toto corpore pertinens, Cic. N. D. 2, 55, 139 : oportebit per locorum communium implicationem demonstrare, etc., an interweaving,…

implĭcātūra.opening: ( ), , implico , an entangling (late Lat.): vernaculae, Sid. Ep. 9, 9 fin.

implĭcātus.opening: ( ), , Part. and P. a. , from implico.

implĭciscor.opening: ( ), , v. dep. inch. n. [implico], to become confused , disordered : ubi primum tibi sensisti, mulier, impliciscier? Plaut. Am. 2, 2, 97 . — In the act. form: ne quid tibi ex frigore impliciscat, Poët. ap. Fronto, Ep.…

implĭcĭtē.opening: ( ), adv. , v. implico, P. a. fin.

implĭcĭto.opening: ( ), , v. freq. a. implico , to entwine , interweave : delphinus exsilit, mergitur, variosque orbes implicitat expeditque, Plin. Ep. 9, 33, 5 (dub.; al. implicat).

implĭco.opening: ( ), (twice in Cic., and freq. since the Aug. per.) ŭi, ĭtum (v. Neue, Formenl. 2, 550 sq.), , v. a. in-plico, to fold into; hence , to infold , involve , entangle , entwine , inwrap , envelop , encircle , embrace ,…

implōrābĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. imploro , that may be prayed to for help : lumen nautis, Val. Fl. 1, 572 .

implōrātĭo.opening: ( ), , id. , a beseeching for help , imploring (rare but good prose): omnium deorum et hominum et civium et sociorum imploratio, Cic. de Or. 2, 47, 196 : acerba, Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 63, § 163 : ad invidiosam implorationem…

implōro.opening: ( ), (archaic form: endoplorato implorato, quod est cum questione inclamare: implorare namque est cum fletu rogare, quod est proprie vapulantis, Paul. ex Fest. p. 77 Müll.), v. a. in-ploro , to invoke with tears , call…

implumbo.opening: ( ), , v. a. inplumbo , to solder in with lead : ferreos cnodaces in capitibus scaporum, Vitr. 10, 6 .

implūmis.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-pluma , without feathers , unfledged , callow. Lit. ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): assidens implumibus pullis avis, Hor. Epod. 1, 19 : fetus columbarum, Plin. 11, 37, 64, § 170 : coni (galearum),…

implŭo.grammar: ŭi, ūtum, 3 v. n. and a.
implŭo.opening: ( ), , v. n. and a. [in-pluo]. Neutr. , to rain into or upon , to rain (very rare): deorsum, quo impluebat, impluvium dictum, Varr. L. L. 5, § 161 Müll.: fanum Veneris, in cujus quandam aream non impluit, Plin. 2, 96,…

implŭvĭātus.opening: ( ), , adj. impluvium , shaped like an impluvium, i. e. four-sided , having a square border : vestis, a kind of garment worn by women, Plaut. Ep. 2, 2, 40 .

implŭvĭum.opening: ( ), , impluo . Lit. , a skylight , the opening in the roof of the atrium in a Roman house through which the smoke issued , so called because it admitted the rain (cf. compluvium): per inpluvium intro spectant, Plaut.…

impŏlītĭa.opening: ( ), , impolitus , want of neatness , carelessness , negligence : si quis eques Romanus equum habere gracilentum aut parum nitidum visus erat, impolitiae notabatur: id verbum significat, quasi si tu dicas incuriae,…

impŏlītus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-politus , unpolished , rough (class.). Lit. : structurae lapidum impolitorum, Quint. 8,63 . — Trop. , unpolished , inelegant , unrefined (class.): orationes Catonis valde laudo, significant enim…

impollūtus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inpollutus , unstained, unpolluted (post-Aug.): fides, Sil. 13, 679 : virginitas, Tac. A. 14, 35 : intemeratus, impollutus, id. ib. 16, 26 .

impōmenta.grammar: quasi imponimenta, quae post cenam mensis imponebant

impōno.opening: (arch. forms of the perf. imposivit, Plaut. Rud. 2, 3, 27 : imposisse, id. Most. 2, 2, 4 ; sync. form of the part. perf. impostus, a, um, Lucr. 5, 543 ; Verg. A. 9, 716 ; Val. Fl. 4, 186 ; Prop. 5, 2, 29 ; Stat. Th. 1,…

Imporcĭtor.opening: ( ), , imporco , a deity that presides over the drawing of furrows : Fabius Pictor hos deos enumerat, quos invocat flamen sacrum Cereale faciens Telluri et Cereri ... Imporcitorem, Serv. Verg. G. 1, 21 ; cf.: Imporcitor…

imporco.opening: ( ), no perf. , , v. a. in-porca , to put into furrows; imporco αὐλακιζω, Gloss. Philox.: semen imporcatum occabimus, Col. 2, 10, 6 .

importābĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inportabilis , that cannot be borne , insupportable; lit. and trop. (late Lat.), Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 27 med. : moenium arietes, Cassiod. Var. 7, 6 : malum, id. ib. 9, 2 al. — Adv. : , in an insupportable…

importātīcĭus.opening: ( ) or , , adj. importo , brought in from abroad , imported : frumentum, Auct. B. Afr. 20, 4.

importo.opening: ( ), , v. a. inporto , to bring , carry , or convey into , to bring in from abroad , to import (class.). Lit. : qui (D. Laelius) commeatus Bullide atque Amantia importari in oppidum prohibebat, Caes. B. C. 3, 40, 5 :…

importūnĭtas.opening: ( ), , importunus . In gen., unsuitableness , unfitness (perh. only ante- and post - class., and very rare): importunitatem spectate aniculae, Ter. And. 1, 4, 4 : loci, dangerousness, Gell. 3, 7, 5 .— In partic., of…

importūnus.opening: ( ), , adj. from porto, qs. not conducive, not proper; opp. opportunus; hence , unfit , unsuitable , inconvenient (cf.: molestus, intempestivus, praeposterus). In gen. (rare): num importunum tempus in tanto otio? Cic.…

importŭōsus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-portuosus , without a harbor : mare, Sall. J. 17, 5 : laeva inportuosa Italiae litora, Liv. 10, 2, 4 ; Tac. A. 4, 67 : litus, Plin. Ep. 6, 31, 17 : insula importuosissima omnium, Plin. 4, 12, 23, § 73 .

impŏs.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-potis; cf. the opp., compos , not master of , not possessed of , without power over (ante- and postclass.): homo, animi impos, Plaut. Trin. 1, 2, 94 : sui est impos animi, id. Cas. 3, 5, 7 ; id. Bacch.…

impŏsĭtīcĭus.opening: ( ), or , , adj. impono , laid on , applied (anteand post-class.). Lit. : canthari, only laid on, not fastened, Dig. 30, 1, 41, § 11 .— Trop. : nomina, i. e. the primitive names applied to things, Varr. L. L. 8, § 5…

impŏsĭtĭo.opening: ( ), , id. , gramm. t. t., the application of a name to a thing, Varr. L. L. 8, § 5 Müll.; 10, § 51; § 61 (in Plin. 27, 13, 115, § 141 , the true reading is in potione).

impŏsĭtītĭus.opening: adj. impono , imposed , prescribed (late Lat.): jus civile, imposititium, Fragm. Dosith. 2. ap. Huschke, Jurisp. Antejust. p. 404.

impŏsĭtīvus.opening: ( ), , adj. impono , i. q. impositicius, applied : nomina, i. e. primitive names, Plin. 28, 4, 6, § 33 .

impŏsĭtor.opening: ( ), , id. , one who applies a name to a thing, Varr. L. L. 7, § 2 Müll.

impossĭbĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inpossibilis , impossible (post-Aug.): impossibile aut potius infinitum est, Quint. 5, 10, 18 : impossibilia aggrediantur, id. 5, 13, 34 : nihil impossibile arbitror, App. M. 1, p. 111 : ut Herculi quasi…

impossĭbĭlĭtas.opening: ( ), , impossibilis , impossibility (post-class.), App. M. 6, p. 179 ; Tert. Bapt. 2 fin. al.

impostor.opening: ( ), , impono, II. B. 3. , a deceiver , impostor (post-class.; cf.: planus, sycophanta), impostores aut mendaces aut litigiosi, Dig. 21, 1, 4, § 3 ; Hier. Ep. 38 fin. ; 54, 5 ; Paul. Nol. Carm. 21, 338 .

impostūra.opening: ( ), , id. , deceit , imposture (late Lat.), Dig. 47, 20, 3 ; Treb. Gall. 12; Coll. Mos. et Rom. Leg. 2, 1.

impōtābĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-potabilis , not drinkable , Hier. Ep. 78 ; Mans. 5.

impŏtens.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-potens , powerless , impotent , weak , feeble (class.). In gen. Absol. : neque homini infanti aut impotenti injuste facta conducunt, Cic. Fin. 1, 16, 52 : ad opem impotentium, id. Mur. 28, 59 ; cf.…

impŏtentĭa.opening: ( ), , impotens . * Inability , want of wealth , poverty : magis propter suam impotentiam se semper credunt neglegi, Ter. Ad. 4, 3, 16 .— Want of moderation or self-restraint , ungovernableness , passionate behavior ,…

impraegno.opening: ( ), , v. a. in-praegno , to impregnate , make pregnant (late Lat.; perh. only in part. perf. ): illa ab eo impregnata vidit in somnis per fauces introisse solem, etc., Myth. Vat. ap. Mai. Auct. Class. t. 3, p. 117.

impraemĕdĭtātus.opening: adj. 2. in-praemeditor , unprepared : visio, Mart. Cap. 2, § 99 .

impraepărātus.opening: adj. 2. inpraeparatus , unprepared , without preparation , Hier. Eph. 6, 11 .

impraepĕdītus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-praepeditus , unhindered (late Lat.): cursu tendentes, Amm. 21, 5, 6 . — Adv. , without hinderance; in two forms. , Amm. 27, 10, 2 . — , Amm. 26, 6, 11 .

impraepūtĭātus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-praeputiatus , having the prepuce , uncircumcised (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Monog. 11 , acc. to Cor. 1, 7, 18.

impraescĭentĭa.opening: ( ), , 2. in-praescientia , a not knowing beforehand , want of prescience (post-class.): futuri, Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 7 .

impraesentĭārum.opening: ( ), adv. contr. from in praesentia rerum , at present , for the present , under present circumstances , now (in the vulg. lang.; post-class. and not infrequent; syn.: pro temporibus, in praesentia, hodie): si quem…

impraestābĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in - praestabilis , useless (late Lat.), Firm. Math. 8, 29 med. ; Salv. Gub. Dei , 4, 11.

impraevārĭcābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. inpraevarico , not to be transgressed , Ambros. de Fuga Saec. 3, 16 .

impransus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inpransus , that has not breakfasted , fasting : quia illo die impransus fui, Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 98 : verum hic impransi mecum disquirite, Hor. S. 2, 2, 7 ; Plaut. Am. 3, 2, 71 ; id. Rud. 1, 2, 56 ; Hor. S.…

imprĕcātĭo.opening: ( ), , imprecor , an invoking of evil , imprecation (postAug.): exsecraris illum et caput sanctum tibi dira imprecatione defigis, curse, Sen. Ben. 6, 35, 1 ; id. Ep. 94, 52 : imprecationes nefariae, Amm. 29, 1, 25 :…

imprĕcor.opening: ( ), , v. dep. a. [in-precor]. To invoke on a person, to call down upon , to imprecate (perh. not anteAug.). Of good wishes (rare): solito sermone salutem ei fuerat imprecatus, had wished health to her (on sneezing),…

impressĭo.opening: ( ), , imprimo , a pressing into , an impressing , impression (class.). Lit. In gen.: materiam signari impressione formarum, App. Dogm. Plat. 1, p. 4 : signaculi, Schol. Juv. 1, 68 : nummorum, stamping, coining, Aug.…

impressus.opening: ( ), , imprimo , a pressing upon , impression : sub pectoris impressu, Prud. Psych. 273 .

imprĕtĭābĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inpretium , priceless , invaluable , inestim tble : sanitatis munus, Cassiod. Var. 9, 6 fin. : notitia litterarum, id. ib. 11, 1 al.

imprĭmo.opening: ( ), , v. a. in-premo , to press into or upon , to stick , stamp , or dig into , to impress , imprint (class.). Lit. : si in ejusmodi cera centum sigilla hoc anulo impressero, Cic. Ac. 2, 26, 86 : locus ubi vestigium…

imprincĭpālĭter.opening: ( ), adv. , by preference , especially (late Lat.), Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 9, 55 .

imprŏbābĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inprobabilis , not deserving of approbation , objectionable , exceptionable (not ante-Aug.; for in Cic. Ac. 2, 11, 33 , the correct read. is probabilem; cf. Cic. Off. 2, 2 ): rationes, Cels. praef. med. :…

imprŏbātĭo.opening: ( ), , improbo , disapprobation , blame (very rare): haec et ad improbationem et approbationem testium pertinebunt, Auct. Her. 2, 6, 9 ; Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 74, § 172 : accusatoris erit, improbatione hominis uti, id. Inv.…

imprŏbātor.opening: ( ), , id. , a disapprover , condemner (post-class.): malorum, bonorum probator, App. de Deo Socr. p. 51 : malorum, Tert. Patient. 5 .

imprŏbĭtas.opening: ( ), , improbus , badness , wickedness , depravity , dishonesty , improbity (freq. and class.): cum te alicujus improbitas perversitasque commoverit, Cic. Q. Fr. 1, 13, 38 : amicorum neglectio improbitatem coarguit, id.…

imprŏbĭto.opening: ( ), , v. freq. a. improbo , to disapprove strongly , condemn : illud inhumaniter scriptum, Gell. 20, 1, 11 .

imprŏbo.opening: ( ), , v. a. 2. in-probo , to disapprove , blame , condemn , reject (class.; syn.: culpo, vitupero, criminor, etc.): multi, qui domi aetatem agerent, propterea sunt improbati, Enn. ap. Cic. Fam. 7, 6 (Trag. v. 296…

imprŏbus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inprobus , not according to the standard. Lit. Below the standard, i. e. of bad quality , bad , poor , inferior (rare; mostly post-Aug.): merces, Plaut. Rud. 2, 3, 43 : opera araneorum et textura inproba,…

imprōcērus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in - procerus , not tall , undersized (postAug.): corpora, Gell. 4, 19, 1 : pecora, Tac. G. 5, 2 .

imprōcrĕābĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-procreabilis , that cannot be procreated : materia, App. Dogm. Plat. 1, p. 3 .

imprōdictus.opening: adj. 2. in-prodictus , not postponed : ne improdicta die quis accusetur, Cic. Dom. 17, 45 .

imprŏfessus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-professus . M i d., that has not professed or declared himself (post-Aug.): deferebantur, qui vel improfessi Judaicam intra Urbem viverent vitam, Suet. Dom. 12 : servus, Dig. 34, 4, 16 .—* Pass. , that…

imprōlus.grammar: qui nondum esset ascriptus in civitate
imprōlus.opening: vel , , Paul. ex Fest. p. 108 Müll.

imprōmiscŭs.opening: ( ), , adj. 2 in-promiscus , unmixed , unmingled (postclass.): suavitas, Gell. 12, 4, 3 : verbum neque numeris neque generibus praeserviens, sed liberum undique et impromiscum, id. 1, 7, 6 .

impromptus.opening: ( ), , um. adj. 2. in-promptus , not ready , not quick (rare): infacundior et lingua impromptus, Liv. 7, 4, 5 : imprompto jam Arminio ob continua pericla, Tac. A. 2, 21 : sermone impromptus Latio, Aus. Idyll. 2, 9 .

imprŏpĕ.opening: ( ), adv. in-prope , near (post-class.): imprope est caelo, Tert. Exhort. ad Cast. 10 .

imprŏpĕranter.opening: ( ), adv. 2. inproperanter , gradually , by degrees (postclass.), Aus. Epit. 35, 3 .

imprŏpĕrātus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-properatus , not hastened , not hasty , lingering : vestigia, Verg. A. 9, 798 .

imprŏpĕrĭum.opening: ( ), , 2. impropero , a reproach , taunt (eccl. Lat.), Lact. 4, 18, 32 ; Vulg. Rom. 15, 3 al. ; cf. improperium ὀνείδισις, Gloss. Philox.

imprŏpĕro.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.

imprŏpĕrus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-properus , not hasting , slow : sorores, Sil. 3, 96 .

imprō^prĭĕtas.opening: ( ), , improprius , impropriety , improper use (postAug.): verbi, Gell. 1, 22, 21 .

imprō^prĭus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-proprius , not befitting a thing, unsuitable , improper (post-Aug.): nec improprium nec inusitatum nomen, Quint. 8, 4, 16 ; cf. cognomen, Plin. 37, 8, 37, § 116 : verba, Quint. 8, 3, 57 : tropus maxime…

imprōpugnātus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-propugnatus , not defended , undefended : civitas, Amm. 29, 6 ; 26, 5 ; 12 ; Gell. 1, 6, 4 .

improspectus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-prospectus , not seen from afar , unseen : Aetna, Auct. Carm. Aetn. 339.— Adv. : , improvidently : Jephte improspecte voverat, Hier. adv. Jovin. 1, 23 : satis, Tert. Anim. 24 .

improsper.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-prosper , unfortunate , unprosperous (post-Aug.): fortuna, Tac. A. 3, 24 : moles insidiarum, id. ib. 14, 65 : multa claritudine generis sed improspera, id. ib. 4, 44 .— Adv. : , unfortunately : cessit,…

imprōvĭdentĭa.opening: ( ), , improvidus , want of foresight , improvidence (post-class.): improvidentia sententias vertere, Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 23 .

imprōvĭdus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-providus , not foreseeing , not anticipating , improvident (class.; syn.: incautus, imprudens, inconsultus). Absol. : duces, Cic. Att. 7, 20, 2 : senes, id. Lael. 26, 100 : improvidos incautosque…

imprōvīsus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-provisus , not foreseen , unforeseen , unexpected (class.): sapienti nihil improvisum accidere potest, nihil inopinatum, nihil omnino novum, Cic. Tusc. 4, 15, 37 ; Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 28, § 69 ; id. de…

imprūdens.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inprudens , not foreseeing , not anticipating or expecting , without knowing , unaware , ignorant , inconsiderate , inadvertent , imprudent (class.; syn.: inconsideratus, incautus, improvidus). Absol. :…

imprūdentĭa.opening: ( ), , imprudens , want of foresight or of knowledge , inconsiderateness , imprudence , ignorance , inadvertence : tantusque ab imprudentia eventus utraque castra tenuit pavor, Liv. 4, 39, 6 : quo modo prudentia esset,…

in-circumcīsus.opening: adj. , uncircumcised (eccl. Lat.), Tert. adv. Jud. 2 ; Prud. Psych. 389 .

in-circumscriptus.opening: adj. , unlimited , infinite (eccl. Lat.): dominus, Prud. Apoth. 863 .

incīsim.opening: adv. incisus, from 2. incīdo , in short clauses (very rare): haec quidem duo binis pedibus incisim; deinde membratim, etc. (shortly before: incise membratimve), Cic. Or. 63, 213 : incisim et membratim tractata oratio,…

incīsĭo.opening: 2. incīdo . A cutting into , cut , incision : ne incisio vulnus exasperet, Ambros. in Psa. 37, § 42 . — Transf. Rhet. t. t, an incision , i. e. a division , member , clause of a sentence, Gr. κόμμα : de eorum…

incīsūra.opening: 2. incīdo , a cutting into , incision , incisure (post-Aug.). In gen., Col. 12, 54, 1 ; Plin. 11, 39, 94, § 231 . — Plur. , Vulg. Lev. 21, 5 .— In partic. A natural incision , indentation; as in the palm of the hand,…

incīsus.opening: 2. incīdo , an incision : proximo anno ab incisu, Plin. 16, 12, 23, § 60 .

incĭtābŭlum.opening: incito , an incentive , stimulus : ingenii virtutisque, Gell. 15, 2, 3 .

incĭtāmentum.opening: id. , an incitement , inducement , incentive. In abstr. with gen. or ad : et periculorum et laborum, * Cic. Arch. 10, 23 : educandi, Plin. Pan. 27, 1 : turbarum, Amm. 21, 12 al. : ad honeste moriendum, Curt. 9, 5, 4 ;…

incĭtātē.opening: adv. , v. incito, P. a. fin.

incĭtātĭo.opening: incito , an inciting , incitement in an act. and pass. sense (Ciceron.). Act. , an inciting , rousing , instigating : languentis populi, Cic. de Or. 2, 9, 35 : acris et vehemens, id. ib. 2, 43, 183 .— Pass. , violent…

incĭtātor.opening: id. , an inciter , instigator (post-class.): Fauni vaticinantium incitatores, Front. Eloqu. med. ; Prud. στεφ. 10, 67: male sanus, Amm. 28, 1 .

incĭtātrix.opening: incitator , she that incites or instigates (eccl. Lat.): ad vitia, Arn. 2, 64 : libidinum (opulentia), Lact. Ira D. 23 : licentiae, Nazar. Pan. ad Const. 34 .

incĭtātus.opening: incito , rapid motion; v. l. for incitu, Plin. 2, 45, 45, § 116 .
