incĭtēga.grammar: machinula, in qua constituebatur in convivio vini amphora, de qua subinde deferrentur vina
incĭtēga.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 107 Müll. [mutilated from ἐγγυθήκη or ἀγγοθήκη; v. Müll. N. cr. ].

in-cĭto.opening: v. a. , to set in rapid motion , to hasten , urge forwards; and with se, to put one ' s self in rapid motion , to hasten , rush (freq. and class.). Lit. In gen.: vehementius equos incitare, Caes. B. C. 2, 41, 4 : saxa…

in-cĭtus.opening: adj. , set in rapid motion , rapid , swift , violent ( poet. ): venti vis, Lucr. 1, 271 : inciti atque alacres Delphini, Cic. poët. N. D. 2, 35, 89: hasta, Verg. A. 12, 492 : silex, Sil. 1, 491 : longis Porticibus…

incĭtus.opening: in-cieo , quick motion : adsiduo mundi incitu, Plin. 2, 45, 45, § 116 .

in-cīvīlis.opening: adj. , unmannerly , impolite , uncivil; hence, also, unreasonable , unjust (post-class.): homo ferus et incivilis ingenii, Eutr. 9, 27 : saevi atque inciviles animi, Aur. Vict. Caes. 22 : verba, tam improba ac tam…

incīvīlĭtas.opening: incivilis , uncourteousness , incivility (post - class. and very rare): per incivilitatem militis, Amm. 18, 2, 7 ; 29, 5 .

inclāmātĭo.opening: inclamo , a calling out , exclaiming against one (postclass.): imprecationis et comminationis, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 41 .

inclāmĭto.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to call out or exclaim against one; hence, to abuse , scold : inclamitor quasi servus, Plaut. Ep. 5, 2, 46 .

in-clāmo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
in-clāmo.opening: v. a. and n. To cry out to , to call upon , in a good or bad sense. In a good sense (class.), to call upon for assistance, to invoke. With acc. : comitem suum inclamavit, Cic. Inv. 2, 4, 14 : Fulvium Taurea nomine…

inclango.opening: v. n. (late Lat.), Jul. ap. Aug. cont. Sec. VI. 28.

in-clāresco.opening: v. inch. n. Lit. , to become clear or light (late Lat.): ubi primum dies inclaruit, Amm. 25, 1, 1 . — Trop. , to become famous or celebrated (postAug.): docendi genere maxime inclaruit, Suet. Gramm. 17 ; cf. ib. 18 :…

in-clārus.opening: adj. , obscure (late Lat. and very rare): fides, Symm. Ep. 3, 4 .

in-clēmens.opening: adj. , unmerciful , rigorous , harsh , rough , severe (as an adj. perh. not ante-Aug. and very rare; not in Cicero): increpabant inclementem dictatorem, Liv. 8, 32, 13 : signifer, Sil. 8, 440 : verbo inclementiori…

inclēmentĭa.opening: inclemens , unmercifulness , rigor , harshness , roughness , severity ( poet. and in post-class. prose): divum inclementia, divum, Has evertit opes, Verg. A. 2, 602 : durae mortis, id. G. 3, 68 : gravis fati, Stat. S.…

inclīnābĭlis.opening: adj. inclino , that readily leans to any thing, prone. — Trop. : in pravum inclinabiles animi, Sen. Ep. 94, 40 .— Not to be moved or bent (lat. Lat.): atque immobilis permansit, (Hilar.) Anon. in Job, 1, p. 104.

inclīnāmentum.opening: id. , in gram., the formative termination of a word: inclinamentum hujuscemodi verborum, ut vinosus, mulierosus, numosus, signat copiam quandam immodicam rei, Nigid. ap. Gell. 4, 9, 2 .

inclīnātĭo.opening: id. , a leaning , bending , inclining to one side (class., esp. in the trop. signif.). Lit. In gen.: (corporis) ingressus, cursus, accubitio, inclinatio, sessio, etc., Cic. N. D. 1, 34, 94 : corporis, Quint. 1, 11, 16 :…

inclīnātīvus.opening: adj. id. , in gram., the Greek ἐγκλιτικός, enclitic : conjunctiones, Prisc. p. 1225 P.: pronomina, id. 1062 P.

inclīnātus.opening: inclino , in gram., the formation or derivation of a word: simili inclinatu, Gell. 3, 12, 3 .

in-clīno.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
in-clīno.opening: v. a. and n. clino, clinatus . Act. , to cause to lean , bend , incline , turn a thing in any direction; to bend down , bow a thing. Lit. In gen. (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose): vela contrahit malosque inclinat,…

in-clūdo.opening: v. a. claudo , to shut up , shut in , confine , enclose , imprison , keep in (class.).—Constr. with in and abl. , in and acc. , rarely with the simple abl. , dat. , or absol. Lit. With in and abl. : habemus…

inclūsĭo.opening: includo , a shutting up , confinement. * Lit. : Bibulum, cujus inclusione contentus non eras, interficere volueras, Cic. Vatin. 10, 24 . — * Trop. , rhet. t. t., the Gr. ἐπαναδίπλωσις, Rufin. p. 234 .

inclūsor.opening: id. , one who encloses , enchases (late Lat.): auri atque gemmarum, setter, Hier. in Jer. 5, 24 .

inclŭtus.opening: and (not inclytus; the first syll. accented acc. to Cic. Or. 48, 159 ), , adj. in-clueo; cf. the Gr. κλυτός, from κλύω, much heard of, talked of, praised; hence , celebrated , renowned , famous , illustrious , glorious…

in-cŏactus.opening: adj. , not compelled , voluntary (post-Aug. and rare): omne honestum injussum incoactumque est, Sen. Ep. 66 med. (false read. for incohata, Val. Max. 4, 7 ).

incoctĭlis.opening: adj. incoquo . * Cooked in any thing: incoctile ἐνεψημένον, Gloss. Philox.—* Transf. , subst. : , , (sc. vasa), vessels overlaid or washed with metal , tinned vessels , Plin. 34, 17, 48, § 162 .

incoctĭo.opening: id. , a boiling in any thing, an incoction (late Lat.), Cael. Aur. Tard. 4, 3, 62 .

incoctus.opening: adj. 2. in-coquo , uncooked , raw (ante-class. and rare): incoctum non expromet, bene coctum dabit, Plaut. Mil. 2, 2, 53 : collyrae facite ut madeant et colyphia: incocta ne mihi detis, id. Pers. 1, 3, 13 : caro, Fab.…

incoercitus.opening: adj. 2. in-coërceo , unrestrained : incoercitos affectus, Jul. ap. Aug. C. Saec. Jul. 4, 41.

in-cōgĭtābĭlis.opening: adj. Act. , thoughtless , inconsiderate (ante- and post - class.): nunc demum scio, me fuisse excordem, caecum, incogitabilem, Plaut. Mil. 2, 6, 63 ; Lact. 1, 8 .— Pass. , inconceivable , incomprehensible (post-class.):…

incōgĭtans.opening: adj. 2. in-cogito , thoughtless , inconsiderate (ante- and postclass.): ni fuissem incogitans, Ter. Phorm. 1, 3, 3 : adeon' te esse incogitantem atque impudentem, ut? etc., id. ib. 3, 2, 14 ; Aus. Sap. Periandr. 15 .

incōgĭtātus.opening: adj. 2. in-cogito . Pass. , unconsidered , unstudied (postAug.): opus, Sen. Ben. 6, 23 med. : alacritas, id. Ep. 57 : incogitata dicere, App. Flor. p. 364 (de Deo. Soc. p. 102 Hild.).— Act. , thoughtless , inconsiderate…

in-cōgĭto.opening: v. a. , to think of , contrive , design ( = intendere, moliri; perh. formed after the Gr. ἐννοεῖν ): fraudem socio, Hor. Ep. 2, 1, 122 .

in-cognĭtus.opening: adj. Not examined , untried : vestra solum legitis, vestra amatis, ceteros causā incognitā condemnatis, Cic. N. D. 2, 29, 73 : res, id. Caec. 10, 29 .— Not known , unknown (class.; esp. freq. in Cic.): ne incognita pro…

in-cognoscĭbĭlis.opening: adj. , incomprehensible , not to be known or discerned : Deus, Hilar. in Psa. 143, 8.

in-cognosco.opening: v. inch. n. , to learn , find out a thing: ut incognosceret, quisnam esset, App. Flor. p. 362, 22 (dub. al. ut inde cognosceret).

incŏhāmenta.opening: ( ), , incoho , first principles , rudiments , elements (post-class.), Mart. Cap. 6, § 576 : incohamentorum primordia, id. 5, § 437 al.

incŏhātĭo.opening: ( ), , id. , a beginning (late Lat.), Aug. Ep. 120 al.

incŏhātīvus.opening: ( ), , adj. id. , beginning , denoting a beginning , inchoative; in gram.: verba, Charis. p. 223 P.; Diom. p. 333 P.; Prisc. p. 824 P. et saep.

incŏhātor.opening: ( ), , id. , a beginner (post-class.): mortis (Cain), Prud. Ham. 27 praef.

incŏhĭbeo.opening: , false read. in Lncr. 3, 444, inst. of is cohibessit; v. Lachm. ad h. l.

incŏhĭbĭlis.opening: adj. in-cohibeo , that cannot be held or kept together (post-class.): illo genere oneris tam impedito ac tam incohibili, Gell. 5, 3, 4 .— That cannot be restrained : cursus, Amm. 24, 1, 5 : ardor, id. 14, 2 .

incoho.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
incoho.opening: (better than , Plaut. Trin. 1, 2, 95 ; cf. Corss. Ausspr. 1, 109; Cic. Rep. 1, 35 Mai.; 3, 2; Front. p. 154 Rom.; Marin. Fratr. Arv. p. 363; Bramb. p. 291 sq.), , v. a. and n. for in-coco; from in and Sanscr. root kuk-,…

incoinquĭnābĭlĭter.opening: adv. in-coinquinabilis (eccl. Lat.), Aug. de Nat. Boni, 44.

in-cŏinquĭnātus.opening: adj. , unde filed , unpolluted (late Lat.): corpus, Vulg. Sap. 8, 20 : mulier, id. ib. 3, 13 ; Ambros. Apol. David, 11, 56.

incŏla.opening: ( Phaedr. 1, 6, 6 ; Prud. Ham. 642 ) [in-colo], an inhabitant of a place, a resident. Lit. : optati cives, populares, incolae, accolae, advenae omnes, Plaut. Aul. 3, 1, 1 : incola est, qui in aliquam regionem domicilium…

incŏlātus.opening: 2. incolo , a resid?*!ing , a dwelling in a place (post-class.), Dig. 50, 1, 34 ; Cod. Th. 12, 1, 5; 12 al.; Inscr. Orell. 3725 .— Transf. : per incolatum Spiritus Sancti, Tert. Res. Carn. 26 .

in-cŏlo.opening: (post-class. collat. form , āre: paradisum incolare et custodire, Tert. Res. Carn. 26 fin. ; whence incolatus), v. a. and n. Lit. (for the simple colere), to cultivate (late Lat.): in his terris, quas incolunt…

incŏlōrātē.opening: adv. 2. in-coloratus: without coloring or palliation, i. e. , without alleging a cause , Dig. 4, 4, 18 .

in-cŏlŭmis.opening: ( abl. sing. regularly incolumi; incolume, Pomp. and Cic. ap. Charis. p. 108 P.), adj. , unimpaired , uninjured , in good condition , still alive , safe , sound , entire , whole (class. and freq.; syn.: salvus,…

incŏlŭmĭtas.opening: incolumis , good condition , soundness , safety (class.): incolumitas est salutis tuta atque integra conservatio, Cic. Inv. 2, 56, 169 : in incolumitate, id. Post Red. ad Quir. 1, 3 : concordi populo et omnia referenti…

in-cōmis.opening: adj. , unpleasant : vita, Macr. S. 1, 7 med. — Adv. : , ungracefully , without pleasantry : haud incomiter, Flor. 4, 8, 4 .

in-cŏmĭtātus.opening: adj. , unaccompanied , unattended (rare and mostly poet. ; not in Cic., for in de Or. 1, 55, 234, the correct read. is incompta): virginibus in Illyrico incomitatis vagari licet, Varr. R. R. 2, 10, 9 : funera, Lucr. 6,…

incŏmĭtem.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 107 Müll.; cf. incomitatus.

in-cŏmĭtĭo.opening: v. a. , prob. to insult or reproach in public : incomitiare significat tale convicium facere, pro quo necesse sit in comitium, hoc est in conventum venire. Plautus (Curc. 3, 40): quaeso ne me incomities, Paul. ex Fest.…

incomĭum.opening: one of the ingredients of an ointment , otherwise unknown, Veg. Vet. 6, 28, 18 .

incomma.opening: or , , ἔγκομμα, an incision, mark; hence , the standard height of soldiers, Veg. Mil. 1, 5 ; Hier. in. Jovin. 2, 34; cf.: incomma mensura militum, Gloss. Isid.

in-commĕābĭlis.opening: adj. , not traversable , impassable : via, Amm. 16, 11, 8 (al. difficiles).

in-commendātus.opening: adj. , unrecommended; poet. , given up , abandoned : tellus, sc. ventis, Ov. M. 11, 435 .

incommĭnātus.opening: , false read. in App. Mag. 10, p. 241 , for in comminata.

incommĭnūtus.opening: adj. 2. incomminuo , not broken , entire : ut fundamentum immobilis, tamquam adamas incomminutus, (Hilar.) Anon. in Job, 2, p. 137.

in-commiscĭbĭlis.opening: adj. , that cannot be mixed (post-class.): animus, Tert. Anim. 12 .

in-commōbĭlĭtas.opening: immovableness , insensibility; a transl. of the Gr. ἀοργησία, App. Dogm. Plat. 2, 14, 28 .

incommŏdestĭcus.opening: adj. , a comically formed word for incommodus, Plaut. Capt. 1, 1, 19 .

incommŏdĭtas.opening: incommodus , inconvenience , incommodiousness , unsuitableness; disadvantage , damage , loss , injury (mostly ante- and post-class.; syn.: incommodum, molestia, difficultas): incommoditas denique huc omnis redit (opp.…

incommŏdo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
incommŏdo.opening: v. n. and a. [id.]. Neutr. , to occasion inconvenience or trouble to any one, to be inconvenient , troublesome , annoying (rare): alicui, Ter. And. 1, 1, 135 : alicui nihil, Cic. Quint. 16, 51 ; id. Q. Fr. 1, 2, 3, § 10…

in-commŏdus.opening: adj. , inconvenient , unsuitable , unfit , unseasonable , troublesome , disagreeable. Adj. Of things (class. and freq.): iter, Ter. Hec. 3, 4, 1 : res, id. ib. 4, 2, 27 : valetudo, Cic. Brut. 34, 130 : colloquium pro re…

incommōtē.opening: adv. 2. in-commotus , immovably , unchangeably , firmly : permanere, Cod. Just. 1, 1, 7 .

in-commūnĭcābĭlis.opening: adj. , incommunicable (late Lat.): nomen, Vulg. Sap. 14, 21 .

incommūnĭcātus.opening: adj. incommunico , shared with : alteri, Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. 1, 13 .

in-commūnis.opening: adj. , not common (post-class.): incommunes ceteris, Tert. Pall. 3 fin. ; Gell. 12, 9, 1 .

in-commūtābĭlis.opening: adj. , unchangeable , immutable (rare but class.): omnia verbi principia incommutabilia viderentur (opp. commutabilia), Varr. L. L. 9, § 99 Müll.: status rei publicae, * Cic. Rep. 2, 33, 57 : bonum, Aug. Retract. 1, 9…

incommūtābĭlĭtas.opening: incommutabilis , unchangeableness , immutability (late Lat.); with aeternitas, Aug. Conf. 12, 12 .

incommūtātus.opening: adj. 2. incommuto , unchangeable (late Lat.), August. de Manich. 11 .

in-compărābĭlis.opening: adj. , that cannot be equalled , incomparable (post-Aug.): sublimitas, Plin. 7, 25, 26, § 94 : magister, Quint. 1, 2, 11 ; freq. in epitaphs: MARITO, CONIVGI, etc., Inscr. Grut. 486, 7 ; 432, 8 .— Comp. : divinitatis…

incompărātus.opening: adj. 2. in-, 1. comparo , unequalled , incomparable , for incomparabilis, as an epithet of one deceased: CONIVGI INCOMPARATISSIMO, Inscr. ap. Fabr. p. 421, no. 386.

in-compassĭbĭlis.opening: adj. , that cannot suffer with another , share another ' s sufferings (eccl. Lat.): Pater, Tert. ap. Prax. 29.

incompellābĭlis.opening: 2. in-, 2. compello , that cannot be named , not to be addressed by name (eccl. Lat.), Rufin. Invect. ap. Hier. 2, 29 fin.

in-compertus.opening: adj. , of which one has no information , unknown (not anteAug.): inter cetera vetustate incomperta hoc quoque in incerto positum, Liv. 4, 23, 3 : ne quid incompertum deferret, id. 10, 40, 10 ; 9, 26, 15 : origo atque…

in-compĕtens.opening: adj. , insufficient (late Lat.), Theod. Prisc. 2, 17 .— Adv. : , insufficiently , Cod. Just. 1, 3, 19 ; Cassiod. Var. 5, 14 .

in-complētus.opening: adj. , uncompleted , incomplete (late Lat.): consilia, Firm. Math. 5, 2.

incompos.opening: adj. 2. in-compos , not having control over (late Lat.): incompotem mentis hominem, [App.] Polem. Physiog. p. 125.

in-compŏsĭtus.opening: adj. Not compounded , simple , Ambros. Hexaëm. 1, 7, 25; Boëth. Inst. Arith. 1, 17 : trinitas incompositae naturae corrumpi non potest, Ambros. Ep. 81, 8 .— Not well put together , not properly arranged , out of order ,…

incomprĕhensĭbĭlis.opening: adj. 2. incomprehendo , that cannot be seized or held , that cannot be grasped (post-Aug.). Lit. : parvitas arenae, Col. 10 praef. § 4: alces incomprehensibili fuga pollet, that cannot be overtaken, Sol. 20 .— Neutr. as…

in-comprĕhensus.opening: adj. , not comprehended , incomprehensible (post-class.): manet virtus, Prud. Ap. 821 . (In Cic. Ac. 2, 29, 95 , the correct reading is non comprehensa.)

in-comptus.opening: ( ), , adj. , unadorned , inelegant , artless , rude (rare but class.). Lit. : incomptis Curium capillis, Hor. C. 1, 12, 41 ; so Ov. M. 9, 789 ; cf. caput, Hor. Epod. 5, 16 ; and: nuda, nudis incompta capillis, Ov. M.…

inconcessĭbĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-concedo , inadmissible (post-class.): delicta, Tert. Pud. 9 fin.

in-concessus.opening: adj. , not allowed , impossible (not ante-Aug. and rare): hymenaei, unlawful, forbidden, Verg. A. 1, 651 ; cf. ignes, Ov. M. 10, 153 : spes, id. ib. 9, 638 : cum totum exprimere paene sit homini inconcessum, Quint. 10,…

in-concĭlĭo.opening: v. a. , to win over to one ' s side , to gain over artfully (anteand post-class.). In gen.: inconciliasti, comparasti, commendasti, vel ut antiqui, per dolum decepisti, Paul. ex Fest. p. 107 Müll.: inconciliastin' eum,…

inconcinnĭtas.opening: inconcinnus , inelegance , awkwardness , impropriety (postAug.): vitatis sententiarum ineptiis atque inconcinnitate, Suet. Aug. 86 ; App. Dogm. Plat. 2 , pp. 14, 21.

in-concinnus.opening: adj. , inelegant , awkward , absurd (rare but class.): qui in aliquo genere inconcinnus aut multus est, is ineptus dicitur, * Cic. de Or. 2, 4, 17 : personamque feret non inconcinnus utramque, Hor. Ep. 1, 17, 29 :…

in-concrētus.opening: adj. , bodiless , incorporeal (eccl. Lat.): substantia, Nazar. Pan. Const. 14 .

inconculcābĭlis.opening: adj. 2 in-conculco , not capable of being trodden under foot (eccl. Lat.), Fulg. Rusp. Incarn. Filii, 50.

in-concussus.opening: adj. , unshaken , undisturbed , firm , constant , unchanged (post-Aug.). Lit. : caelestia sidera, Luc. 2, 268 ; so, vestigia, id. 2, 248 .— Trop. : inconcussus ipse et immotus, Plin. Pan. 82, 2 ; cf.: inconcussus…

incondĭtē.opening: adv. , see the foll. art. fin.

incondĭtus.opening: adj. (Acc. to condo, I.) Not made , uncreated (post-class.): ne quid innatum et inconditum praeter solum deum crederemus, Tert. adv. Hermog. 18 .— (Acc. to condo, II.) Not stored up : fructus, Col. 1, 5, 6 ; 3, 2, 1 .—…

in-cōnexĭo.opening: ( ), , , rhet. t. t., = ἀσύνδετον, the omission of a copulative particle , asyndeton , Jul. Ruf. de Schem. Lex. 20 .

in-cōnexus.opening: ( ), , adj. , not joined together , disconnected (late Lat.): res, Aus. Edyll. ad Paul. 12 .— Transf. , gram. t. t., = ἀσυνάρτητος, of metrical construction, loose , disjointed , said of verses in which various forms of…

in-confectus.opening: adj. , not wrought out , undigested (late Lat.), Hier. Ep. 119 , no. 1; Cels. 4, 16 (dub.).

inconfūsĭbĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-confusus , that cannot be embarrassed or confused (late Lat.): operarius, Vulg. 2 Tim. 2, 15 .— Adv. : , without confusion : misceri, Claud. Mam. Stat. An. 1, 15 .

inconfūsus.opening: adj. id. , unconfused (post-Aug.). Lit. : ut inconfusus eat (mundus), Sen. Q. N. 2, 45 : recursus, Claud. VI. Cons. Hon. 622 .— Trop. , unembarrassed , not disconcerted : animus intrepidus inconfususque, Sen. Q. N. 3…

incongĕlābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-congelo , that cannot be frozen : mare omne, Gell. 17, 8, 16 .

incongressĭbĭlis.opening: adj. 2. incongredior , unapproachable , inaccessible : Deus, Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 27 .

in-congrŭens.opening: adj. , inconsistent , incongruous , unsuitable (post-Aug.): sententia, Plin. Ep. 4, 9, 19 : quod est incongruens et absurdum, ut, etc., Lact. 3, 8, 35 . —With dat. : Stoica disciplina pleraque est et sibi et nobis…

in-congrŭentĭa.opening: unsuitableness , incongruity (late Lat.): definitionis, Tert. Anim. 6 ; id. adv. Marc. 2, 25 .

in-congrŭus.opening: adj. , inconsistent , incongruous , unsuitable = incongruens, inconveniens (post-class.): quam incongruo ambitu amplectar, Val. Max. 4, 1, 12 : inter se propositiones, App. Dogm. Plat. 3 ; Veg. Mil. 2, 19 ; Symm. ep. 4,…

in-cōnīvens.opening: (also ), , adj. 2. in-conniveo , that does not close the eyes (late Lat.). Lit. : stare solitus Socrates dicitur, Gell. 2, 1, 2 .— Trop. , of the eye, that does not close , unclosing : justitiae oculus, Amm. 29, 2, 20 .

in-conjŭgus.opening: adj. : verba ( epithets , etc.), not applicable to ordinary names (e. g. fulminat and tonat can be said of Jupiter only), Prisc. p. 1065 P.

inconnīvus.opening: (better ), , adj. 2. in-coniveo , that does not close the eyes , sleepless (Appuleian; cf. inconivens): vigiliae, App. M. 6, p. 179, 5 . — Of the eyes, not closing : oculi, App. M. 2, p. 124, 19 .

in-conscĭus.opening: adj. , unaware , unconscious (late Lat.), Cassiod. Var. 10, 4 (but in Liv. 21, 12, 4 , the correct reading is insciis).

in-conscriptus.opening: adj. , not arranged (late Lat.): incondita, id est inconscripta, Serv. ad Verg. E. 2, 4 .

in-consentānĕus.opening: adj. , unsuitable , unfit (late Lat.), Mart. Cap. 3, § 228 al.

in-consĕquens.opening: adj. , not logically consequent , inconsequent (post-class.): locutio, Ascon. ad Cic. Verr. 2, 9 : per inconsequens, Gell. 14, 1, 10 .— Adv. : , inconsequentially , illogically , Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 4, 36 ; 3, 17, 172 .

inconsĕquentĭa.opening: inconsequens , want of logical connection , inconsequence (post-Aug.): rerum foedissima, Quint. 8, 6, 50 .

in-consīdĕrans.opening: adj. , inconsiderate (late Lat.): inconsiderantissime Marcion, Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 29 fin. — Adv. : , inconsiderately : tutor, qui inconsideranter pupillum abstinuit hereditate, Dig. 26, 10, 3, § 17 ; Hier. p. 108 , n.…

inconsīdĕrantĭa.opening: inconsiderans , want of reflection , inconsiderateness (= temeritas, incuria): alicujus inconsiderantiam sustinere (where some read considerantiam), Cic. Q. Fr. 3, 9, 2 : mirari inconsiderantiam (al. inconsiderationem),…

inconsīdĕrātĭo.opening: inconsiderateness (late Lat.): mentis, Salv. de Gub. Dei, 1 extr.; cf. inconsiderantia. — From , , adj. (class.). Act. , thoughtless , heedless , inconsiderate (cf. inconsultus): nos ita leves atque inconsiderati sumus,…

in-consĭlĭum.opening: ill-advisedness , thoughtlessness , = ἀβουλία, Gloss. Gr. Lat.

inconsĭtus.opening: adj. 2. in-consero , unsown , untilled ( = incultus): ager, Varr. L. L. 5, § 36 Müll.

inconsōlābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-consolor , inconsolable , trop. incurable : vulnus, Ov. M. 5, 426 : malum, Amm. 29, 2, 14 : maeror, Ambros. de Elia. et Jejun. 16, § 60.

in-consŏnans.opening: adj. , ill-sounding , unsuitable; with incongruum, Pompei. ap. Donat. de Barb. 6 . — Adv. : , unsuitably; with inconsequenter, Vet. Interpr. Iren. 5, 17.

in-conspectus.opening: adj. , indiscreet , imprudent (post-class.): inconspectum aliquid temere dicere, Gell. 17, 21, 1 .

in-conspĭcŭus.opening: adj. , not conspicuous , not remarkable ( = inglorius, ignobilis; post-Aug.): mors, Flor. 4, 2, 67 .— Invisible : stella, Mart. Cap. 8, § 838 ; id. 6, § 593 .

inconsprētus.opening: adj. 2. inconsperno , not despised or slighted : non improbatus, Paul. ex Fest. p. 107 Müll.

in-constans.opening: adj. , inconstant , changeable , fickle , capricious , inconsistent (class.). Of persons: mihi ridicule es visus esse inconstans, qui eundem et laederes, et laudares, Cic. Rosc. Com. 6, 19 : populus in omnibus…

inconstantĭa.opening: inconstans , inconstancy , changeableness , fickleness (class.). Of persons: quid est inconstantia, mobilitate, levitate, cum singulis hominibus, tum vero universo senatui turpius? Cic. Phil. 7, 3, 9 : levitate…

inconstrŭo.opening: v. a. in-construo , to build up with (late Lat.), Fulg. Serm. 11 .

in-consŭētus.opening: adj. Unusual (post-Aug.): sermo, Vitr. praef. 5: salsitudo, id. 1, 4 .— Unused , unaccustomed; with gen. : opimae mensae, Sil. 11, 282 .

in-consultus.opening: adj. Not consulted , unasked (so perh. not in Cic.): inconsulto senatu, Liv. 36, 36, 2 ; so, inconsulto se, Suet. Tib. 52 : me inconsulto, Amm. 17, 5, 12 ; 27, 2 fin. ; Ambros. Ep. 6, 43 ; Plin. Ep. 10, 107, 2 ; Symm.…

inconsultus.opening: 2. in-consulo , the not advising with another (anteclass.; only in the abl. sing. ): inconsultu meo, without consulting me, Plaut. Trin. 1, 2, 130 .

inconsummātĭo.opening: 2. in-consummo , incompleteness , imperfection : generationis, Tert. adv. Val. 10 .

in-consummātus.opening: adj. , unfinished , incomplete , imperfect (post-class.); with rudis, Amm. 31, 14 ; with subagrestis, id. 21, 10, 8 .— Trop. , of persons, uncultivated , not well educated , Ambros. de Fide, 2, 15, § 129.

inconsumptĭbĭlis.opening: adj. in-consumo , not to be consumed , indestructible : perennitas, Cassiod. in Psa. 127, 2 .

in-consumptus.opening: adj. , unconsumed , undiminished (Ovidian): pars turis, Ov. M. 7, 592 : jecur, id. P. 1, 2, 41 : juventa, id. M. 4, 17 .

inconsūtĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-consuo , not sewed together , without seam : tunica, Vulg. Joh. 19, 23 .

in-consūtus.opening: adj. , not sewed together , without seam (eccl. Lat.): tunica, Hier. Ep. 22, 19 .

incontāmĭnābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-contamino , that cannot be defiled (eccl. Lat.): Deus, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 14 ; Aug. Conf. 7, 3 .— Adv. : , without defilement , Aug. de Gen. ad Litt. c. ult.

in-contāmĭnātus.opening: adj. , uncontaminated , undefiled , pure (class., but not in Cic.): ne quid incontaminati sit, Liv. 4, 2, 5 : facies, Varr. R. R. 3, 9, 16 .— Sup. : a quibus longe absunt, ut incontaminatissimi perseverent, Aug. Civ.…

incontemplābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-contemplor , that cannot be looked upon or contemplated (eccl. Lat.): claritas, Tert. Res. Carn. 55 : facies, id. adv. Marc. 5, 11 .

incontemptĭbĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-contemno , not contemptible , not to be despised (eccl. Lat.): Deus, Tert. Apol. 45 .

in-contentus.opening: adj. , unstretched : fides, out of tune Cic. Fin. 4, 27, 75 .

incontĭgŭus.opening: adj. 2. in-contingo , that cannot be touched (eccl. Lat.): Deus omni est incontiguus tactu, Arn. 7, p. 267 .

in-contĭnens.opening: adj. Not containing , not retaining (class., but not in Cic.): uterus, Plin. 8, 43, 68, § 168 .— Incontinent , immoderate , intemperate : homo, Plaut. As. 5, 2, 9 : Tityos, Hor. C. 3, 4, 77 : manus, id. ib. 1, 17, 26 .…

incontĭnentĭa.opening: incontinens . Lit. , inability of containing or retaining (post-Aug.): urinae, Plin. 20, 15, 57, § 161 .— Trop. , inability of restraining one ' s desires , greediness , incontinence (class.): multa de incontinentia…

incontrādīcĭbĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-contradico , that cannot be contradicted , undeniable (late Lat.); comp. , Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 39 .

in-contrītus.opening: adj. , not contrite (eccl. Lat.), Hier. Orig. in Jer. Hom. 3, 1 .

incontrōversus.opening: , false read. in Cic. de Or. 1, 57, 241 , for in controversiis or sine controversiis; v. Orell. and Klotz ad h. l.

in-convĕnĭens.opening: adj. Lit. , not accordant , unsuitable , dissimilar (class., but not used by Cic. or Cæs.): facta, Cass. ad Cic. Fam. 12, 13, 1 : inconvenientia jungere, Sen. Vit. Beat. 12 : corpus, Phaedr. 3, 13, 6 .— Trop. ,…

inconvĕnĭentĭa.opening: inconveniens , inconsistency , incongruity : voluntatis et facti, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 16 : litterarum, Macr. de Diff. 23, § 3 .

in-conversĭbĭlis.opening: adj. , not convertible , not to be turned about (in order or rank); opp. conversibilis, Aug. de Music. 5, 21 .

inconvertĭbĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-converto , unchangeable (eccl. Lat.): deus, Tert. adv. Hermog. 12 ; id. de Anim. 21 .

inconvertĭbĭlĭtas.opening: inconvertibilis , unchangeableness (eccl. Lat.): Verbi, Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 1, 14 .

in-convincĭbĭlis.opening: adj. , not to be convinced (eccl. Lat.), Hier. Orig. in Jer Hom. 3, 1 .

inconvŏlūtus.opening: adj. in-convolvo , conglobate , heaped together : post inconvolutos multiplices casus, Amm. 29, 2, 21 .

inconvulsus.opening: adj. 2. in-convello , undestroyed (late Lat.): inconvulsa a se vectigalium pensione, i. e. while they are not relieved from the obligation of paying taxes , Fragm. Cod. Th. 5, 13, 14; ib. 12, 14, 1 .

in-cōpĭōsus.opening: adj. , not furnished with provisions (late Lat.): solitudo, Tert. de Jejun. 5 .

incō^prĭo.opening: v. a. κοπρίας, scurra , to defile , abuse , revile : civis omnes, Commod. Instruct. 19 .

in-cŏquo.opening: v. a. , to boil in or with any thing, to boil down , to boil , seethe (not in Cic. or Cæs.). Lit. , constr. aliquid rei alicui or re aliquā : radices Baccho, in wine, Verg. G. 4, 279 : cotonea melle, Plin. 15, 17, 18 .…

incōram.opening: adv. , for coram (Appuleian). In the presence of; with gen. omnium, in the presence of all , before all , App. M. 7, p. 197, 21 ; 9 , p. 221, 17: sui, id. ib. 10 , p. 241, 5: populi, id. ib. 10 , p. 249, 33 Hild. N. cr.…

in-cŏrōnātus.opening: adj. , uncrowned (post-Aug.): simulacra, App. M. 4, p. 155, 40 .

incorpŏrābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-corpus , incorporeal (late Lat.): habitu, Tert. adv. Marc. 3, 17 al.

incorpŏrālis.opening: adj. id. , bodiless , incorporeal (post-Aug.): quod est aut corporale est aut incorporale, Sen. Ep. 58, 11 : jus, Quint. 5, 10, 116 : nomina, that denote something incorporeal , e. g. virtus, Prisc. 2, p. 579 .—Hence,…

incorpŏrālĭtas.opening: incorporalis , incorporeity (post-class.), Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 15, 13 ; 1, 11, 12 ; Tert. de Anim. 7 .

incorpŏrātĭo.opening: incorporo , an embodying , incorporating , furnishing with a body (late Lat.). In gen., Claud. Mam. Stat. An. 2, 3 ; of Christ, Cassiod. Inst. Div. Litt. 32 .— Esp., incorporation with the public funds, paying into the…

incorpŏrātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from incorporo.

in-corpŏrātus.opening: adj. , not embodied : ut incorporatum pro non corporato, Claud. Mam. Stat. An. 2, 2 init.

incorpŏrĕus.opening: adj. 2. in-corpus , incorporeal (post-class.): corpusne sit vox an incorporeum: hoc enim vocabulum quidam finxerunt proinde quod Graece dicitur ἀσώματον, Gell. 5, 15, 1 ; Macr. S. 7, 15 .

in-corpŏro.opening: v. a. (postclass.). To fasten or mark in or upon a body. Lit. : variae animalium effigies incorporantur, Sol. 22, 20 . — Trop. , to incorporate : sibi, with itself (of the church), Aug. Doctr. Christi, 2, 6, 7 init. —…

in-correctus.opening: adj. , uncorrected , unimproved : opus, Ov. Tr. 3, 14, 23 .

in-corrĭgĭbĭlis.opening: adj. , not to be corrected or cured (post-Aug.; syn. insanabilis), Sen. de Ira, 3, 41 fin.

in-corruptēla.opening: ( ), , , imperishableness , incorruptibility (eccl. Lat.), Tert. de Carne Christi, 15; Aug. Ep. 146, 15 ; Vulg. 1 Cor. 15, 50 .

in-corruptĭbĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. , imperishable , incorruptible (eccl. Lat.), Lact. 1, 3 ; Tert. de Anim. 50 . — * Adv. : , imperishably , Aug. Conf. 3, 2 .

incorruptĭbĭlĭtas.opening: ( ), , incorruptibilis , imperishableness , incorruptibility (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Apol. 48 fin. ; id. adv. Marc. 2, 16 .

in-corruptĭo.opening: ( ), , , imperishableness , incorruptibility (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Res. Carn. 51 ; Aug. de Trin. 13, 7 .

incorruptīvus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-corrumpo , imperishable (eccl. Lat.), Hier. Ep. 152 .

incorruptōrĭus.opening: ( ), , adj. id. , imperishable : sensus in Deo, Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 16 .

in-corruptus.opening: ( ), , adj. , unspoiled , uninjured , uncorrupted (class.). Lit. : sucus et sanguis, Cic. Brut. 9, 36 : incorruptum a fraude advehentium frumentum, Sen. Brev. Vit. 19, 1 : aquae, Plin. 2, 103, 106, § 230 : templa,…

incoxo.opening: v. n. in-coxa , to bend down , to cower or squat down , Pomp. ap. Non. 39, 9 (Com. Fragm. v. 97 Rib.).

incrassātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from incrasso.

in-crasso.opening: v. a. , to make thick or stout (post-class.; used mostly in the part. ), Tert. adv. Psych. 6 .—Hence, , , P. a. , made stout , fattened , Tert. adv. Marc. 3, 6 ; id. Jejun. 6 .

incrĕābĭlis.opening: adj. in-creabilis , not of a created nature , self-existent (eccl. Lat.): non peperit creatura eum qui est increabilis. Mar. Marc. Serm. 1, 7.

in-crĕātus.opening: adj. , uncreated , not made , Hier. in Didym. de Spir. Sanc. 8 init. ; Claud. Mam. Stat. An. 2, 4 .

in-crebresco.opening: (also , bui), , v. n. , to become frequent or strong , to increase , gain ground , prevail , spread (= crebrior fieri, augeri, crescere; class.): mores deteriores, Plaut. Merc. 5, 1, 9 : ventus, Cic. Fam. 7, 20, 3 ;…

in-crēbro.opening: v. n. , to do any thing frequently : sin increbravit, but if he has frequently done it, has often visited his mistress, Plaut. Truc. 1, 1, 29 dub. (Speng.: sin crebras ducit; sc. noctes).

incrēdĭbĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-credo . Pass. That cannot be believed , incredible , extraordinary , unparalleled (class.): fides, Cic. Fam. 13, 54 : quaedam et prope singularis et divina vis ingenii, id. Or. 1, 38, 172 : voluptas, id. Cat.…

incrēdĭbĭlĭtas.opening: incredibilis (post-class.). Incredibility , Dig. 48, 5, 29 init. — Incredulity : humana, App. Trim. p. 93, 12 .

in-crēdĭtus.opening: adj. , disbelieved , discredited (post-class.): vaticinia Cassandrae, App. de Deo Socrat. p. 52, 11 .

incrēdŭlĭtas.opening: incredulus , disbelief , incredulity (post-class.). In gen., App. M. 1, p. 111, 18 .— Esp., religious disbelief , incredulity , Cod. Th. 16, 8, 19; Paul. Nol. Carm. 6, 95 : venit ira Dei super filios incredulitatis,…

in-crēdŭlus.opening: (perh. not anteAug.). Act. , unbelieving , incredulous , without faith : odi. Hor. A. P. 188 : patronus, Quint. 12, 8, 11 : quidam, id. 10, 3, 11 : Judaei, Vulg. Act. 14, 2 al. — Pass. , incredible : res, Gell. 9, 4, 3 .

incrēdundus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-credo , not to be believed , incredible (Appuleian): fabula, App. M. 2, p. 120, 15 : potentiae caerimoniarum, id. Flor. 2, p. 351 : illecebrae frugum, id. Mag. p. 304, 25 .

incrĕmātus.opening: , false read. in Flor. 4, 12, 24 , instead of in crucem actis.

incrēmento.opening: v. n. , to increase (late Lat.), Aug. c. Litt. Pet. 3, 54; Val. Prob. ap. Verg. 3, 23 .

incrēmentŭlum.opening: dim. incrementum , a little growth or increase : tantum locupletis uteri, App. M. 5, p. 164, 18 .

incrēmentum.opening: incresco , growth , increase , augmentation (class.). Lit. , of plants and animals: quid ego vitium satus, ortus, incrementa commemorem? Cic. Sen. 15, 52 : ponendae sunt plantae majoris incrementi, Pall. Feb. 24, 7 ;…

incrĕpātĭo.opening: increpo , a chiding , rebuking , i. q. objurgation (post-class.), Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 7 ; 5, 20 .

incrĕpātīvē.opening: adv. from the obsol. increpativus , chidingly , Sid. Ep. 6, 9 .

incrĕpātor.opening: increpo , Gloss. ἐπιτιμητής, a chider , abuser : per dilectionem accedit, Cassiod. in Psa. 140, 6 ; Acr. ad Hor. A. P. 174 .

incrĕpātōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , chiding , objurgatory (late Lat.), Sid. Ep. 9, 7 .

incrĕpĭto.opening: v. freq. [id.]. To call or cry out to one (class.). Encouragingly, to call upon , challenge (only in Verg.): tum Bitiae dedit increpitans, Verg. A. 1, 738 .— Reprovingly, to chide , blame , rebuke : increpitare atque…

incrĕpĭtus.opening: increpo , i. q. increpatio, a chiding , rebuking (post-class.), App. de Deo Socr. p. 52, 49 : et increpitu daemonia expellens, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 8 .

in-crĕpo.opening: (increpavi, Plaut. Most. 3, 2, 63 ; Vulg. Psa. 9, 6 ; Suet. Tib. 52 : increpatus, Just. 11, 4, 5 ; Prud. 7, 195 ; Liv. 24, 17, 7 Cod.), , v. n. and a. , to make a noise , sound , resound , to rush , rustle , patter ,…

incrĕpundia.opening: , Fab. Claud. Gord. Fulgent. Aet. M. 11 .

in-cresco.opening: v. n. , to grow in or upon any thing (perh. not ante-Aug.). Lit. : non taedia animalium capillis increscunt, do not grow in the hair, Plin. 28, 11, 46, § 163 . — In gen., to grow , increase : lacrimis quoque flumina…

incrēto.opening: v. a. in-creta , to chalk , whiten with chalk (post-Aug.): increta facies, Petr. 102 : locum, Veg. 5, 17, 4 .

in-crētus.opening: adj. 2. in-cretus, part. of cerno , unsifted (rare): ac sordidi furfures, App. M. 7, p. 194, 37 .

in-crīmĭnātĭo.opening: blamelessness , irreprehensibleness (late Lat.), Tert. Res. Carn. 23 .

incrispātĭo.opening: incrispo , a crisping or curling of the hair (eccl. Lat.), Aug. Ep. 112, 22 ; id. ad Paul. 22 ext. 1; id. Petri, 3, 3.

incrispo.opening: v. a. in-crispus , to crisp or curl (al. incrustare), Tert. Idol. 8 .

in-crŭcĭo.opening: v. a. , to torture greatly , Not. Tir. p. 109 .

in-crūdesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become very raw , Not. Tir. p. 81 .

in-crŭentātus.opening: adj. , made bloody , bloody : panis, Tert. ad Nat. 1, 7 .

in-crŭentus.opening: adj. , bloodless , that sheds no blood , without bloodshed (freq. in the histt., but not in Cic. or Cæs.): certatum haud incruento proelio foret, ni, etc., Liv. 2, 56, 15 : victoria, Sall. C. 61, 7 ; Liv. 4, 17, 8 ; 7,…

incrustātĭo.opening: incrusto , an incrusting of walls, e. g. with plaster, lime, marble, etc. (post-class.): parietis, Dig. 8, 2, 12 fin. ; id. 50, 16, 79 .

in-crusto.opening: v. a. , to cover with a coat or rind , to incrust (mostly anteand post-class.): ollam sapā et farre, Varr. R. R. 3, 14, 5 : tota maceria levi lapide aut tectoria intrinsecus incrustetur, id. ib. 15, 1 : sincerum vas, i.…

incŭbātĭo.opening: incubo , a lying upon eggs (in order to hatch them), a brooding , incubation. Lit. : incubationi datur initium post novam lunam, Plin. 10, 54, 75, § 152 : noxia ovis, id. 10, 56, 77, § 156 : derelicta, id. 10, 60, 80, §…

incŭbātor.opening: id. . One who lies in any place (post-class.): fani, one who sleeps in a temple , Tert. Anim. 49 .— An oppressive or unlawful possessor : inclementissimus aulae Siculae Dionysius, Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 10 : imperii…

incŭbĭto.opening: v. freq. [incubo], to lie in or upon any thing: cellae, in quibus incubitant, in which they brood, Col. 8, 14, 9 . In Plin. 8, 43, 68, § 169 , the best read. is in cubitu.—In mal. part.: jam incubitatus es, Plaut. Pers.…

incŭbĭtus.opening: (only in abl. sing. ), incubo , a lying upon (Plinian). In gen.: dextri lateris, a lying on the right side, Plin. 28, 4, 14, § 54 .— In partic., a brooding , incubation , Plin. 10, 54, 75, § 152 .

in-cŭbo.grammar: ŭi, ĭtum, āre 1 v. n. and a.
in-cŭbo.opening: (rarely āvi, ātum, in the sense of to brood), , v. n. and a. , to lie in a place or upon a thing (class.). Lit. : hic leno aegrotus incubat in Aesculapii fano, Plaut. Curc. 1, 1, 61 : namque incubare satius te fuerat…

incŭbo.opening: 1. incubo , one who lies upon any thing. A spirit that watches over buried treasures (post-class.): cum modo incuboni pileum rapuisset, thesaurum invenit, Petr. Fragm. Trag. 38, 8 .— The nightmare , incubus…

in-cŭbus.opening: id. , the nightmare , incubus , Aug. Civ. Dei , 15, 23; Isid. Orig. 8, 11 .

in-cūdo.opening: v. a. , to forge with the hammer , to fabricate ( poet. , used only in part. pass. ): incusa auro dona, Pers. 2, 52 : lapis, an indented or sharpened stone for a handmill , Verg. G. 1, 275 ; Col. 7, 1, 3 .

inculcātĭo.opening: inculco , an inculcating (late Lat.), Tert. Apol. 39 .

inculcātor.opening: id. . One who tramples upon : diaboli, Tert. adv. Gnost. 6 . — One who insists on or inculcates : rationis, Cassiod. Var. 12, 1 fin.

in-culco.opening: v. a. in-calco , to tread in , tread down (class., esp. in the trop. signif.). Lit. , to tread down , ram down : aliquid, Col. 2, 20, 1 : semen obrutum pavicula, id. 11, 3, 34 .— Trop. To stuff , press , or force in :…

in-culpābĭlis.opening: adj. , unblamable , blameless (post-class.): numen, Prud. Apoth. 1015 : mores, Avien. Arat. 28 : lapis, i. e. faultless, without a flaw, Sol. 30 . — Adv. : , without blame , Cassiod. Var. 5, 27 ; 11, 18 sq.

inculpātim.opening: adv. inculpatus , without blame : ad calcem pervenire, Cod. Th. 6, 30, 20.

in-culpātus.opening: adj. , blameless ( poet. and post-class.): vita fidesque, Ov. M. 9, 673 ; cf.: vita inculpatissima, Gell. 14, 2, 4 : virtus, id. 2, 6, 10 : inculpatum visum esse, id. 7, 22, 4 al. — Adv. : , without blame , Cod. Th. 9,…

in-cultus.opening: want of cultivation or refinement (not in Cic. or Cæs.): incultu, tenebris, odore foeda ejus (Tulliani) facies est, Sall. C. 55, 4 : ingenium incultu atque socordiā torpescere sinunt, id. J. 2, 4 : honores desertos per…

incumba.opening: incumbo , archit. t. t., the impost or chaptrel of a pillar that bears the weight of an arch, Vitr. 6, 11 .

incumbo.opening: v. n. 1. incubo , to lay one ' s self upon , to lean or recline upon a thing (cf. ingruo; class., partic. in the trop. sense). Lit. , constr. with in , ad , super , or dat.; also with the simple acc. : olivae, Verg. E.…

incŭmŭlātĭo.opening: in-cumulo , a filling up , puffing out : buccarum, Arn. 3, 14 .

in-cūnābŭla.opening: swaddlingclothes , swathing-bands. Lit. : fasciis opus est, pulvinis, cunis, incunabulis, Plaut. Truc. 5, 13 ; id. Am. 5, 1, 52 .— Transf. The cradle : Bacchi, Ov. M. 3, 317 .— A birthplace : in montes patrios, et ad…

incunctābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-cunctor , that admits of no delay : illud quoque incunctabile est, ut, etc., Dig. 22, 5, 21 .—Hence, adv. : , unhesitatingly , without delay , Alcim. Sent. ad Phil. 4 .

in-cunctans.opening: adj. , not delaying , unhesitating (eccl. Lat.): fides, Paul. Petr. Vit. S. Mart. 5, 233 .— Adv. : ( ), without delay , unhesitatingly (post-class.); with fortiter, Lact. 6, 12 : fateri, id. 1, 15, 26 : incunctanter et…

incunctātus.opening: and , , adj. 2. in-cunctatus , undelayed : domum penetrant, without delay, App. M. 5, p. 165, 13 .

in-cŭpĭdus.opening: adj. , very desirous : incupidiores liberūm, Afran. ap. Non. 496, 5 (Com. Fragm. v. 361 Rib.).

incūrābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-curo , incurable , without remedy (late Lat.), Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 2, 6 .

in-cūrātus.opening: adj. * Uncared for : quidquam (with imperfectum), Vop. Aur. 28 .—* Uncured : ulcera, Hor. Ep. 1, 16, 24 .

incūrĭa.opening: 2. in - cura , want of care , carelessness , negligence , neglect (class.): milites populi R. incuriā, fame, morbo, vastitate consumpti, Cic. Prov. Cons. 3 : magistratuum, Tac. A. 3, 31 : eorum comperta, id. ib. 4, 48 :…

in-cūrĭōsĭtas.opening: carelessness , negligence , inattention (late Lat.), Cassiod. Var. 7, 4 ; Salv. de Gub. Dei, 1.

in-cūrĭōsus.opening: adj. , careless , negligent (post-Aug.). Act. , careless , unconcerned , regardless , indifferent respecting any thing; constr. with gen. , abl. , in , or absol. With gen. : proximorum incuriosi, Plin. Ep. 8, 20, 1 :…

in-curro.opening: (incurri, Cic. Or. 67, 224 ; Liv. 1, 37, 3 ; 9, 21, 3 ; Curt. 4, 5, 19 ; Sen. Q. N. 5, 13, 1 saep.: incucurri, Liv. 27, 18, 19 ; Sen. Ep. 96, 1 al. ), , v. n. and a. [in-curro], to run into or towards , run upon , fall…

incursax.opening: adj. id. , that makes frequent inroads : Massagetae, Sid. Ep. 8, 12 .

incursim.opening: adv. incurro , rapidly , quickly , Caecil. ap. Non. 127, 20 (Com. Fragm. v. 46 Rib.).

incursĭo.opening: id. , a running against , onset , assault , attack (class.). In gen.: atomorum, Cic. N. D. 1, 41, 114 : atque impetus armatorum, id. Caecin. 15, 44 ; Quint. 6, 4, 14 Spald. N. cr. — In partic., a hostile inroad ,…

incursĭto.opening: v. freq. n. [incurso], to rush upon , assault , attack (a favorite word of Seneca). Lit. : in aliquem, Sen. Vit. Beat. 27 : incursitans, instans, fugans, id. de Ira, 2, 35: in multos, id. ib. 3, 6 .— Trop. , to dash…

incurso.opening: v. freq. n. and a. [incurro], to run to or against , to dash or strike against , to assault , attack (class.). Lit. With in : jam in vos incursabimus, Plaut. Bacch. 5, 2, 29 : in agmen Romanum, Liv. 36, 14, 12 .— With…

incursus.opening: incurro , a running against , an assault , attack (class.). Lit. : ceterorum tela atque incursus refugit, Cic. Caecin. 8, 22 : equitum incursus sustinere, Caes. B. C. 1, 71 ; Hirt. B. G. 8, 18, 4 : primo statim incursu,…

incurvābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-curvabilis , not flexible (late Lat.): pedes elephantorum, Cassiod. Var. 10, 30 .

incurvātĭo.opening: incurvo , a bending , curving (post-Aug.): materiae, Plin. 17, 23, 35, § 207 : caudae, Hyg. Astr. 3, 16 .

incurvesco.opening: or , , v. n. incurvus , to bend down : bacarum ubertate, Enn. ap. Cic. de Or. 3, 38, 154 ; and ap. Cic. Tusc. 1, 28, 69 (Trag. v. 194 Vahl.; Trag. Inc. Fab. v. 135 Rib.).

in-curvĭ-cervīcus.opening: adj. incurvus-cervix , having a crooked or wry neck : pecus, Pac. ap. Varr. L. L. 5, § 7 Müll.; and ap. Quint. 1, 5, 67 (Trag. Rel. v. 408 Rib.).

in-curvo.opening: v. a. , to bend , bow , crook , curve (in Cic. only once in part. pass.; elsewhere poet. and post-Aug.). Lit. : flexos arcus, Verg. A. 5, 500 .— Pass. : robur et olea incurvantur, Plin. 16, 42, 81, § 222 : lentos remos,…

in-curvus.opening: adj. , bent , bowed , crooked , curved (opp. recurvus, pandus; class.). Of persons: incurvus, tremulus, Ter. Eun. 2, 3, 44 : incurvi umeris, Plin. 11, 52, 114, § 274 .— Of things: lituus, id est incurvum, et leviter a…

incūs.opening: incudo , an anvil. Lit. (class.): sine follibus et incudibus, Cic. N. D. 1, 20, 54 : si faber incudem fregerit, Dig. 14, 2, 2 : impositos duris crepitare incudibus enses, Verg. G. 2, 540 : positis incudibus, i. e.…

incūsābĭlis.opening: adj. incuso , blameworthy (late Lat.); comp. , Tert. ad Nat. 1, 12 .

incūsātĭo.opening: id. , a blaming , accusing , accusation : vitiorum, et peccatorum incusatio, aut querela, Cic. de Or. 3, 27, 106 ; Don. ad Ter. Phorm. 2, 3, 12 .

incūsātīvus.opening: adj. id. , accusing; for accusativus; casus, and absol. : incusativus, the accusative, Diom. p. 296 P.

incūso.opening: v. a. in-causa , to accuse one of something, to complain of , find fault with , blame (cf.: arguo, accuso, vitupero; class., but not in Cic.).—Constr. aliquem alicujus rei , aliquem quod , aliquid , etc.—With acc. of…

incussĭo.opening: incutio , a falling in , inroad (late Lat.), Jornand. Get. 40 .

in-cussor.opening: id. , one who strikes , Paul. Petr. Vit. S. Mart. 5, 285 .

incussus.opening: incutio , a striking or dashing against , a shock (rare, and only in abl. sing. ): armorum, Tac. H. 4, 23 : arietis, Sen. Const. Sap. 6 : silicis, Prud. Cathem. 5, 7 .

in-custōdītus.opening: adj. Pass. Lit. , not watched , unguarded ( poet. and post-Aug.): ovile, Ov. Tr. 1, 6, 10 : incustodita et aperta limina, Mart. 1, 35, 1 .— Trop. Disregarded , neglected : dierum observatione, Tac. A. 15, 55 .—…

incŭtĭo.opening: v. a. inquatio , to strike upon or against (syn.: impingo, illido, infligo; class.; in Cic. only in the trop. signif.). Lit. : scipionem in caput alicujus, Liv. 5, 41, 9 : pedem terrae, to strike or dash against ,…

indāgātĭo.opening: id. , a searching into , investigation (class. but rare): initiorum, Cic. Tusc. 5, 24, 69 : atque inventio veri, id. Off. 1, 5, 15 : rarioris verbi, Gell. 18, 2, 6 .

indāgātor.opening: id. , one who traces out , a tracker of prey, Isid. Orig. 10 fin. : apum, one who hunts swarms of bees, Col. 9, 8, 12 : aquarum, a hunter of springs (= aquilex), id. 2, 2, 20 .— Transf. , an investigator , searcher :…

indāgātrix.opening: indagator , she who searches into , investigates , explores : virtutis, Cic. Tusc. 5, 2, 5 : avaritia latentium indagatrix lucrorum, Val. Max. 9, 4 init. : virorum, Non. 23, 1 .

indāgātus.opening: 1. indago (only in the abl. sing. ), an exploring , encircling , surrounding , App. M. 7, p. 191, 3 .

indāges.opening: id. , a searching into , investigation , exploration (post-class.), Claud. Mam. Stat. Anim. 2, 2 ; Prud. Symm. 2, 845 .

indāgo.opening: an encircling , enclosing (mostly post - Aug.). Lit. , of surrounding wild beasts with nets, in hunting: dum trepidant alae, saltusque indagine cingunt, Verg. A. 4, 121 : densos indagine colles Claudere, Tib. 4, 3, 7 :…

inde.opening: adv. i-im, locative from is, and de = die; hence , Of place, from that place , thence : inde e promptuaria cella, Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 4 : si quis me quaeret, inde me vocatote aliqui, id. Stich. 1, 2, 9 : eo die mansi…

in-dēbĭtus.opening: adj. , that is not owed , not due ( poet. and post-class.): non indebita posco, I ask nothing that is not due to me, Verg. A. 6, 66 : praemia, Ov. H. 16, 9 . — Subst. : , , , that which is not due , the performance or…

in-dĕcens.opening: adj. , unseemly , unbecoming , indecent , improper , unsightly , ugly (post-Aug. and poet. ). Of persons: numquid indecens sum? Petr. 128 ; Mart. 5, 14, 7 . — Of things: nasus, Mart. 2, 11, 4 : morbus, id. 11, 61, 13 :…

in-dĕcentĭa.opening: unseemliness , impropriety , Vitr. 7, 5, 6 ; Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 8, 107 .

in-dĕcĕo.opening: v. n. , to misbecome; constr. with acc. pers. (post-Aug. and rare): juvenes confusa quaedam non indecent, Plin. Ep. 3, 1, 2 .

in-dēclīnābĭlis.opening: adj. , inflexible , unchangeable , only in a trop. sense (postAug.). In gen., of things: virtus animum rectum et indeclinabilem praestat, Sen. Ep. 66 : justitia, id. ib. 74 : series re rum, Gell. 6, 2 .—Of persons:…

in-dēclīnātus.opening: adj. , unchanged , constant (Ovidian). Of persons: qui perstas indeclinatus amico, Ov. P. 4, 10, 83 .— Of things: amicitia, Ov. Tr. 4, 5, 24 .

indĕcor.opening: , or , , adj. 2. in-decorus , unbecoming , unseemly , indecorous , inglorious , disgraceful , shameful (very rare; for the most part poet. ): cujus sit vita indecoris, Att. ap. Non. 489, 1 : non indecorem tua te regina…

in-dĕcŏrābĭlĭter.opening: adv. 2. in-decoro , unbecomingly : alienos alunt, Att. ap. Charis. 182 P. (Trag. Fragm. v. 258 Rib.).

in-dĕcŏro.opening: v. a. , to disgrace , disfigure (rare): me sermone indecorans, Att. ap. Non. 125, 1 (Fragm. Trag. v. 459 Rib.): indecorant bene nata culpae, Hor. C. 4, 4, 36 (al. dedecorant).

in-dĕcōrōsus.opening: adj. 2. in-decorosus , disgraceful (eccl. Lat.), Hilar. in Job, 2, p. 150.

in-dĕcōrus.opening: adj. , unbecoming , unseemly , indecorous , disgraceful , shameful , unsightly (class.): quod animo magno fit, id dignum viro et decorum videtur: quod contra, id ut turpe, sic indecorum, Cic. Off. 1, 27, 94 : nihil…

indēfătīgābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-defatigo , that cannot be wearied , indefatigable (post-Aug.): vigilia, Sen. de Ira, 2, 12, 7.

in-dēfătīgātus.opening: adj. 2. in-defatigo , unwearied (post-Aug.), Sen. Cons. ad Marc. 18, 1 .

in-dēfectus.opening: adj. , undiminished , unfailing , unweakened , unexhausted (post-class.): (with aeterna) vivacitas, App. de Deo Socr. p. 44, 6 : (with jejunus) chamaeleon, Tert. Pall. 3 .

in-dēfensus.opening: adj. , unprotected , undefended (perh. not ante-Aug.): Capua deserta indefensaque, Liv. 25, 15, 2 : indefensi, inulti, id. 4, 28, 4 : inauditus et indefensus, Tac. A. 2, 77 : conjux, id. ib. 11, 34 .— Adv. : , without…

in-dēfessus.opening: adj. , unwearied , indefatigable ( poet. and post-Aug.): dextra, Verg. A. 11, 651 : agendo, Ov. M. 9, 199 : assiduus et indefessus, Tac. A. 16, 22 : Germani ob prospera indefensi, id. ib. 1, 64 .— Hence, and , advv. ,…

in-dēfĭcĭens.opening: adj. , unfailing (eccl. Lat.): decor, Tert. adv. Jud. 14 . — , adv. : , continually , incessantly (eccl. Lat.), Aug. Conf. 12, 11 .

indēfĭcĭentĭa.opening: an unfailing supply (eccl. Lat.), Facund. Def. 4, 2.

in-dēfīnītus.opening: adj. , indefinite (post-class.): sermo, Gell. 16, 4 . — , adv. : , indefinitely : largiri, Gell. 2, 24, 7 .

in-deflēbĭlis.opening: adj. , not to be lamented , Gloss. Philox.

in-deflētus.opening: adj. , unwept , unlamented : animae, Ov. M. 7, 611 .

in-deflexus.opening: adj. , unbent , unchanged (post-Aug.): maturitas, Plin. Pan. 4, 7 : cursus, App. de Deo Socr. p. 42, 16 : saevitia, Amm. 27, 9 .

in-dējectus.opening: adj. , not thrown down : domus, Ov. M. 1, 289 .

in-dēlēbĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-deleo , indelible , imperishable (Ovidian): nomen, Ov. M. 15, 876 : decus, id. P. 2, 8, 26 .

in-dēlectātus.opening: adj. , not delighted , displeased with something: aliquā re, Petr. 87, 4 .

in-dēlībātus.opening: adj. , untouched , uninjured (only in the trop. signif. and poet. ): virgo, Sil. 15, 271 : opes, Ov. Tr. 1, 5, 28 .

indēlībĕranter.opening: adv. , without reflection , Hilar. in Job, 2, p. 126.

indēlībĕrātus.opening: adj. 2. in-delibero , not reflected on , inconsiderate (late Lat.), Cassiod. Var. 7, 8 ; 12, 21 .

in-dēlictus.opening: adj. , not criminal , faultless , blameless , Att. ap. Fest. s. v. probrum, p. 229 Müll. (Fragm. Trag. v. 384 Rib.).

indemnātus.opening: adj. 2. in-damnatus , uncondemned , unsentenced (class.): indemnatus atque intestatus, Plaut. Curc. 5, 3, 17 : bona indemnatorum civium, Cic. Agr. 2, 21, 56 : si hoc indemnato indicta causa non liceat, Liv. 3, 56, 13 :…

indemnis.opening: adj. 2. in-damnum , unhurt , uninjured (post-Aug.): illaesus et indemnis evasit, Sen. Ep. 9 ; id. Const. Sap. 5 ; Amm. 26, 6 ; Dig. 50, 8, 9, § 4 sq. ; 17, 2, 23 .

indemnĭtas.opening: indemnis , security from damage or loss , indemnity (post-class.): alicujus indemnitati consulere, Dig. 3, 5, 31 ; 12, 4, 5 : provinciarum indemnitati prospicere, Amm. 21, 16 al.

indēmonstrābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-demonstro , not to be proved , undemonstrable : modi, App. Dogm. Plat. 3, p. 37, 9 .

indēmūtābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-demuto , unchangeable , immutable (late Lat.): Deus, Tert. adv. Herm. 12 .— Adv. : , immutably , Ennod. Ep. 5, 11 .

in-dēnuntĭātus.opening: adj. , not declared or announced (post-Aug.): arma, Sen. Suas. 5, 2 : sors, id. ib. 2, 2 .

indĕpisci.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 106 Müll.; cf. Non. 128, 23 .

in-deprāvātus.opening: adj. , uncorrupted , undepraved (post-Aug.): virtus, Sen. Ep. 76, 15 .

indeprĕcābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-deprecor , that cannot be averted by prayer : poena, Gell. 1, 13, 3 .

indeprĕhensĭbĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-deprehendo , undiscoverable (late Lat.): error, Pseudo Quint. Decl. 4, 15 : est, id. 8, 11 .— Written INDEPRĕHENSĭVĭLIS, Inscr. Orell. 1912 .

indeprensus.opening: adj. id. , unobserved , undiscovered ( poet. ): (with irremeabilis) error, Verg. A. 5, 591 : vestigia, Stat. Th. 6, 565 : retinacula, Prud. Hamart. 141 .

in-descriptus.opening: adj. , not divided (post-Aug.): vites, Col. 3, 21, 4 : agri, Sid. Carm. 2, 412 .

in-dēsertus.opening: adj. , not deserted , unforsaken : regna, Ov. Am. 2, 9, 52 .

in-dēsĕs.opening: adj. , not inactive , free from indolence : homo, Gell. 7, 22, 4 .

in-dēsignātus.opening: adj. , undesigned (late Lat.), Vict. Tunon. de Poenit. 8.

indēsĭnens.opening: adj. 2. in-desino , incessant (late Lat.), Ennod. Ep. 6, 10 . — Adv. : , incessantly (late Lat.): affero sacrificia, Cypr. Ep. 69 : et indeficienter inhaerere, Aug. Conf. 12, 11 .

in-despectus.opening: adj. , that one cannot look down into , unfathomable (postAug.): Tartara, Luc. 6, 748 .

in-destrictus.opening: adj. , untouched , uninjured , unhurt : abibo, Ov. M. 12, 92 (al. indistrictus).

indētermĭnābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-determino , that cannot be defined , indeterminable (late Lat.): quaestiones, Tert. adv. Haer. 7 .

indētermĭnātus.opening: adj. id. , undefined , unlimited (late Lat.): genealogiae, Tert. adv. Haer. 33 .

in-dētonsus.opening: adj. , unshorn , = intonsus, ακερσεκόμης, with unshorn hair or beard : Thyoneus, Ov. M. 4, 13 .

indetrībĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-detero , that cannot be rubbed or worn out : soliditas, Paul. Nol. Ep. 16 .

indetrītus.opening: adj. id. , not worn out (late Lat.): vestimenta, Tert. Res. Carn. 58 .

indēvītātus.opening: adj. 2. in-devito , unavoided , = certus, certainly striking : telum, Ov. M. 2, 605 .

indēvŏrātus.opening: , false read. for et devorato, Mart. 7, 20, 15 .

in-dēvōtĭo.opening: want of religion , or want of principle , irreverence , irreligion , impiety (post-class.), Cod. Just. 7, 2, 15 ; Dig. 39, 9, 1 fin. ; Ambros. de Elia, 17, 62.

in-dēvōtus.opening: adj. , irreligious , impious , unconscientious : donator, Cod. Just. 8, 55, 35 .— Adv. : , impiously , unconscientiously : eas (hereditates) percipere, Justin. Novell. 1, 3.

index.opening: 1. indico , he who ( that which ) points out , a pointer , indicator (class.). Lit. Of things. Of the forefinger , index-finger. With digitus: indice monstraret digito, Hor. S. 2, 8, 26 ; Isid. Orig. 11, 1, 70 .— Alone:…

Indĭa.opening: India , a country extending from the Indus to China , Cic. Tusc. 5, 27, 77 sq. ; Cat. 43, 6 ; Verg. G. 1, 57 al. : citerior, India this side of the Ganges : ulterior, India beyond the Ganges, Plin. 6, 17, 21, § 57 ;…

Indĭānus.opening: adj. India , Indian : ALA, Inscr. ap. Grut. 519, 7.

indĭcābĭlis.opening: adj. 1. indico , that indicates , indicative : signum, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 3, 13 .

indĭcātĭo.opening: id. , an indicating , setting , or rating the valuation of a thing, a valuation; hence, value , price , rate (mostly ante- and post-class.): tua merx est, tua indicatio est, Plaut. Pers. 4, 4, 37 : mellis, Plin. 22, 24,…

indĭcātīvus.opening: adj. id. (postclass.), gram. t. t., indicative , Diom. p. 329 ; Prisc. 819 P.

indĭcātor.opening: id. , one that points out (late Lat.): naturae (al. indagator), Sol. 40 .

indĭcātūra.opening: id. , an indicating or rating the value of a thing; hence, value , price , rate , = indicatio (Plinian): neque est hodie murrhini alterius praestantior indicatura, Plin. 37, 2, 7, § 18 : dolorum, physicians ' fees for…

indīcens.opening: adj. 2. in-dīco , that does not say , i. q. non dicens: non me indicente haec fiunt, not without my telling, Ter. Ad. 3, 4, 62 ; so, me indicente, Liv. 22, 39, 2 .

indĭcīna.opening: index , i. q. indicium, delatio, a notice , information , summons (post-class.): indicinae praemium, App. M. 7, p. 199, 10 ; id. ib. 6 , p. 176, 14; Sen. Contr. 4, 28, § 4 .

indĭcĭum.opening: id. , a notice , information , discovery , disclosure , charge (class.). Lit. : facite indicium, si quis vidit, Plaut. Cist. 4, 2, 9 : id anus mihi indicium fecit, Ter. Ad. 4, 4, 7 ; cf. Plaut. Most. 3, 2, 57 ; id. Mil.…

indĭcīvus.opening: adj. 1. indico , indicating , indicative , Not. Tir. p. 90 .—Hence, subst. : , , , the informer ' s reward , Jul. Vict. Art. Rhet. 4, 4.

in-dĭco.opening: v. a. (indicasso, is, for indicavero, is, Plaut. Poen. 4, 2, 66 ; id. Rud. 4, 3, 89 ), to point out , indicate (class.). In gen., to show , declare , disclose , make known , reveal , betray. Of persons: rem omnem…

in-dīco.opening: ( imp. indice, Plaut. Ps. 1, 5, 132 : indixti for indixisti, Front. de Cels. Ep. 3 ), v. a. in-dico , to declare publicly , to proclaim , publish , announce , to appoint (class.): totius Galliae concilium Bibracte…

indictīcĭus.opening: or , , adj. 2. indico , declared , proclaimed : onera, Cassiod. Var. 5, 14 .

indictĭo.opening: id. , a declaration (post-Aug.). In gen.: belli, Flor. 4, 10, 2 ; Paul. ex Fest. p. 254, 34 .— In partic. A declaration or imposition of a tax; an impost , tax , Plin. Pan. 29 ; Dig. 33, 2, 28 .— A space of fifteen…

indictĭōnālis.opening: adj. indictio , of or relating to an impost or tax (late Lat.): augmentum, Amm. 17, 3, 5 .

indictīvus.opening: adj. 2. indico , declared , proclaimed : funus, Paul. ex Fest. p. 106 Müll.; Varr. L. L. 5, § 160 ; 7, § 42 .

in-dictus.opening: adj. Not said , unsaid (class.): quod dictum, indictum'st: quod modo erat ratum, irritum est, Ter. Phorm. 5, 7, 58 : quae tum cecinerit, ea se nec, ut indicta sint, revocare posse, Liv. 5, 15, 10 : nec tu carminibus…

indĭcŭlum.opening: , and , , dim. index , a short list or catalogue (post-class.), Symm. Ep. 6, 49 ; 7, 81 .

Indĭcus.opening: adj. India , of India , Indian : elephanti, Ter. Eun. 3, 1, 23 : pecudes, Mart. 5, 37, 5 : cornu, i. e. ivory, id. 1, 73, 4 : aqua, Ov. P. 1, 5, 80 : margarita, Petr. 55 . — Subst. : , , , indigo , a blue pigment for…

indĭdem.opening: adv. inde-idem , from the same. Lit. , of place, from the same place : quos homines? indidemne Ameria, an hosce ex urbe sicarios? Cic. Rosc. Am. 27, 74 : Thebis, likewise from Thebes, Nep. Epam. 5, 2 : ex Aventino, Liv.…

in-dĭes.opening: from day to day; v. dies.

in-diffĕrens.opening: adj. , in which there is no difference , indifferent. Act. , of persons, making no difference , indifferent , careless (post-class.): circa victum, Suet. Caes. 53 .— Pass. Philos. t. t., neither good nor evil , not to…

in-diffĕrentĭa.opening: indifferens , want of distinction or difference , similarity , equivalence (post-class.): utriusque vocabuli, Gell. 13, 3, 6 ; Hier. in Didym. de Spir. Sanc. 1, 20 .

in-diffĭculter.opening: adv. , easily (late Lat.): haurire, Claud. Mam. Stat. Anim. 1, 21 .

indĭgĕna.opening: adj. indu-gigno , born in a country , native , indigenous (class., but not in Cic. or Cæs.): miles, Liv. 23, 5, 11 : Fauni Nymphaeque, Verg. A. 8, 314 : Latini, id. ib. 12, 823 : coloni, Col. 1, 7, 3 : bos, Ov. Am. 3,…

indĭgens.opening: , entis. P. a. , from indigeo.— Vid. Indigetes fin.

indĭgentĭa.opening: indigeo . Need , want , indigence (rare; mostly Ciceron.): a natura mihi videtur potius, quam ab indigentia orta amicitia, Cic. Lael. 8, 27 : quid est malitia nisi indigentia boni? Ambros. de Isaac. 7, § 60 . —…

indĭgĕnus.opening: adj. indigena , i. q. indigena, native , vernacular : sermo, App. M. 1, p. 102 .

indĭgĕo.opening: v. n. indu-egeo , to need , want , to stand in need or want of any thing (class.). Lit. , with abl. : bona existimatione, Cic. Rosc. Com. 15, 44 : pecunia, Nep. Ages. 7 : medicina, id. Att. 21 : iis rebus, quae ad…

indĭges.opening: adj. indigeo , needy , indigent : i. q. indigens: quem aetate exacta, indigem liberum lacerasti, Pac. ap. Cic. de Or. 2, 46, 193 (Fragm. Trag. v. 328 Rib.).

indīgestē.opening: adv. , v. indigestus, a, um, fin.

indīgestĭbĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-digero , indigestible , Theod. Prisc. de Diaet. 6 ; Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 9, 55 ; id. Tard. 4, 6, 90 .

in-dīgestĭo.opening: indigestion (late Lat.), Hier. Ep. 22, 17 ; Schol. Juv. 1, 146 al.

in-dīgestus.opening: adj. , unarranged , without order , confused ( poet. and post-Aug.). Lit. : (Chaos) rudis indigestaque moles, Ov. M. 1, 7 : simplicitas, Plin. 13, 15, 30, § 98 : turba, id. 17, 10, 12, § 65 : multitudo, Sen. Ben. 6, 31,…

Indĭgĕtĕs.opening: plur. [indu-gigno], heroes elevated to the rank of gods after their death , and regarded as the patron deities of their country : patrii Dii sunt, qui praesunt singulis civitatibus, ut Minerva Athenis, Juno Carthagini:…

indĭgĕto.opening: or , , v. freq. [2. indico], relig. t. t., to call upon , invoke a deity: virgines Vestales ita indigetant, Apollo Medice, Apollo Paean, Macr. S. 1, 17 ; cf.: indigitanto imprecanto, Paul. ex Fest. p. 114 Müll.: deam,…

indĭgĭtāmenta.opening: ( ), , plur. [in-digito], religious books containing the names of the gods and prescribing the mode of worshipping them , Censor. 3, 4 : Apollinis nomen Pompiliana indigitamenta nescire, Arn. 2, 95 ; Serv. ad Verg. G.…

indignābundus.opening: adj. indignor , full of indignation , enraged , indignant (not ante-Aug.): illa muliebriter indignabunda, Liv. 38, 57, 7 ; with clamitans, Suet. Aug. 40 : animo irritato, indignabundus, Gell. 19, 9, 8 .

indignātĭo.opening: indignor , displeasure , indignation , disdain. Lit. In gen.: sive indignatione et dolore vinculorum, Hirt. B. G. 8, 44, 2 (Kraner, indignitate; class.): liberrima, Hor. Epod. 4, 10 : erumpens animo ac pectore, Vell. 2,…

indignātĭuncŭla.opening: dim. indignatio , slight indignation : indignatiunculam capere ... per epistulam effundere, Plin. Ep. 6, 17, 1 .

indignātīvus.opening: adj. indignor , passionate , irascible : indignativum, quod appellant θυμικόν, Tert. Anim. 16 .

indignĭtas.opening: indignus , unworthiness , vileness (class.). In gen.: si quid affert praeterea hominis aut dignitas aut indignitas, Cic. de Or. 2, 32, 63 : nemo propter indignitatem repudiatus est, id. Div. in Caecil. 19, 63 : summa,…

in-dignor.opening: (archaic inf. indignarier for indignari, Lucr. 3, 870 ), v. dep. a. [in-dignus], to consider as unworthy or improper , to be angry or displeased at , to be indignant (syn. stomachor). In gen. (class.). With acc. : se…

in-dignus.opening: adj. , unworthy , undeserving (class.). Of persons. In gen., unworthy. Absol. : divitias quivis quamvis indignus, habere potest, Cic. Tusc. 5, 16, 46 : indignissimi candidati, Liv. 4, 57, 11 al. — With abl. : te omni…

indĭgus.opening: adj. indigeo , needing , in want ( poet. and post-Aug.). In gen. With gen. : nostrae opis, Verg. G. 2, 428 ; so, externae opis, Tac. H. 3, 48 : stipendiorum, Plin. 8, 40, 61, § 143 : rectoris, Tac. H. 3, 22 (but Lucr.…

indĭgŭus.opening: adj. id. , i. q. indigus, needing , in want (post-class.).—With gen. : opis, Paul. Nol. Carm. 27, 4 ; 16, 196 . —With abl. : refectione virium, App. M. 9, p. 222 med.

in-dīlĭgens.opening: adj. (class., but not in Cic.). Act. , careless , heedless , negligent : ne quis tractet illam indiligens, Plaut. Bacch. 2, 2, 23 : paterfamilias, Nep. Att. 4, 3 ; cf. Ter. Ad. 4, 5, 50 .— Comp. : si indiligentiores…

in-dīlĭgentĭa.opening: indiligens , carelessness , heedlessness , negligence (class.), Plaut. Pers. 4, 4, 9 : litterarum missarum, Cic. Q. Fr. 1, 2, 2, § 7 : Aeduorum, Caes. B. G. 7, 17 : neglecta indiligentiā praedia, Plin. 14, 4, 5, § 50 :…

in-dīlūcesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to begin to grow light : cum jam ferme dies insequens indilucesceret, Jul. Valer. Res Gest. Alex. M. 3, 42.

in-dīmensus.opening: adj. , immeasurable , innumerable (late Lat.): populi, Amm. 19, 2, 4 .

in-dīmissus.opening: adj. , not put away , not divorced (late Lat.): uxor, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 34 .

indĭpiscor.opening: v. dep. a. [indu = in-apiscor], to obtain , attain , reach. Lit. (mostly ante- and post-class.): largiter mercedis indipiscar, Plaut. Rud. 5, 2, 28 : divitias magnas indeptum, id. Ep. 3, 4, 15 : navem, Liv. 26, 39, 12 ;…

in-dīrectus.opening: , a false reading in Quint. 5, 13, 2 , instead of inde recta, v. Spalding ad h. l.

in-dīreptus.opening: adj. , unplundered : Capitolium, Tac. H. 3, 71 fin.

indisciplīnātē.opening: adv. , v. indisciplinatus, a, um, fin.

in-disciplīnātĭo.opening: 2. in-disciplina , want of discipline (late Lat.), Cassiod. Var. 7, 3 .

in-disciplīnātus.opening: adj. id. , without discipline , undisciplined (eccl. Lat.), Cypr. Ep. 62 ; Aug. Ep. 169 .— Adv. : , in an undisciplined manner , disorderly : loqueris, Commod. Instruct. 16 .

in-disciplīnōsus.opening: adj. id. , without discipline , undisciplined (eccl. Lat.), Vulg. Sir. 23, 7 .

in-discissus.opening: adj. , not cut to pieces , undivided (late Lat.): tunica Domini, Hier. Ep. 15, 1 .

in-disco.opening: v. a. , to learn thoroughly : magna res est posse indiscere, Schol. Juv. 6, 474 .

in-discrētē.opening: and , advv. , v. indiscretus, a, um, fin.

in-discrētĭo.opening: lack of discernment , indiscretion , Hier. in Didym. de Spir. S. 36 .

in-discrētus.opening: adj. , unseparated , undivided , closely connected (syn. indivisus; mostly post-Aug.). Lit. : agricultura, Varr. R. R. 3, 1, 7 : quibusdam indiscretum caput, ut cancris, Plin. 11, 37, 46, § 129 ; 16, 29, 43, § 84 : suum…

in-discrīmĭnābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-discrimen , that cannot be distinguished , undistinguishable (late Lat.), Claud. Mam. Stat. Anim. 2, 10 .

in-discrīmĭnātim.opening: adv. , without distinction , Varr. ap. Non. 127, 23 .

in-discussĭbĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-discutio , that is not to be discussed (late Lat.): auctoritas (al. discussibilis), Claud. Mam. Stat. Anim. 2, 12 ; 3, 11 .

in-discussus.opening: adj. id. , not discussed , not considered (late Lat.), Claud. Mam. Stat. Anim. 3, 11 ; Nov. 23, 1 .—Hence, , adv. , without examination , Aug. Serm. 35 , n. 2 Mai.

indĭsertē.opening: adv. , v. indisertus, a, um, fin.

in-dĭsertus.opening: adj. , not eloquent (class.): Academicus, Cic. N. D. 2, 1, 1 .— Of inanim. and abstr. things: prudentia, at a loss for words, Cic. de Or. 3, 35, 142 .— Adv. : , not eloquently (rare but class.): orationem non indiserte…

indisjunctim.opening: adv. 2. in-disjunctus, i. e. not separated in time , immediately (late Lat.), Claud. Mam. Stat. Anim. 1, 12 .

in-dispensātus.opening: adj. 2. in-dispenso , not properly distributed , immoderate (post-class.): nisus, Sil. 16, 342 (cf. Drak. ad Liv. 17, 50, 10 ).

indispertĭbĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-dispertio , indivisible (eccl. Lat.), Mar. Merc. Cyrill. Incarn. Unigen. 25.

in-dispŏsĭtē.opening: adv. , v. indispositus, a, um, fin.

in-dispŏsĭtus.opening: adj. , without order , confused (post-Aug. and very rare): apud Vitellium omnia indisposita, temulenta, etc., Tac. H. 2, 68 .— Of persons, unprepared , August. Ep. 59 .— * Adv. : , without order , confusedly : moveri,…

in-dispŭtābĭlis.opening: 2. in-disputo , indisputable (late Lat.): testimonium, Cassiod. Var. 12, 21 .

in-dissĭmĭlis.opening: adj. , not unlike , Varr. L. L. 9, § 40 Müll. dub. (Müll. conjectures in re simili); Hier. in Didym. de Spir. Sanc. 36 .

in-dissĭmŭlābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. indissimulo , that cannot be dissembled : veritas, Gell. 10, 22, 24 .

in-dissŏcĭābĭlis.opening: adj. , inseparable (eccl. Lat.): unitas, Lact. Opif. D. 10 ; Ambros. Ep. 14 .— Adv. : , inseparably , Claud. Mam. Stat. Anim. 1, 18 .

indissŏcĭālus.opening: inseparable (eccl. Lat.), (Hilar.) Anon. in Job, 1, p. 23.

in-dissŏlūbĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-dissolvo , that cannot be dissolved or loosed , indissoluble (in Cic. only in the transf. signif.). Lit. : nodus, Plin. 11, 24, 28, § 81 . — Transf. , of persons, indestructible , imperishable : quoniam orti…

in-distanter.opening: adv. 2. in-disto (late Lat.). Uninterruptedly : syllaba uno spiritu indistanter profertur, Prisc. p. 565 P. — Without distinction , without exception (post-class.), Amm. 27, 9, 41 ; 31, 6 .

in-distinctē.opening: adv. , v. indistinctus, a, um, fin.

in-distinctus.opening: adj. (post-Aug.). Not properly distinguished , confused : neque inordinata, neque indistincta, Quint. 8, 2, 23 ; Cat. 64, 283 : cf.: indistincta et confusa, Gell. 13, 30, 5 .— Esp., indistinct , obscure : vocabulum,…

indīvĭdŭĭtas.opening: individuus , indivisibility (eccl. Lat.): animae, Tert. Anim. 51 : matrimonii, id. Monog. 5 .

in-dīvĭdŭus.opening: adj. 2. in-divido . Lit. , not divided , indivisible (class.): arbores, with stems not branched, Plin. 16, 30, 53, § 122 : ille atomos, quas appellat, id est, corpora individua, Cic. Fin. 1, 6, 17 : nihil esse…

indīvīsē.opening: adv. , v. indivisus, a, um, fin.

indīvīsĭbĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-divido , indivisible (post-class.): materia, Diom. p. 415 P.: anima, Tert. Anim. 51 ; Isid. 3, 5, 3 .— Adv. : , indivisibly , Tert. Anim. 51 .

in-dīvīsus.opening: adj. , undivided (ante-class. and post-Aug.). Lit. : ungulae equorum, i. e. not cloven, Varr. R. R. 2, 7, 2 ; Just. 43, 1, 3 : rerum media indivisaque magis fratribus, Stat. Th. 8, 312 .— Transf. , common : negotium,…

in-dīvulsus.opening: adj. , not separated : comes, Macr. S. 1, 11 .

in-do.opening: v. a. in-, 2. do , to put , set , or place into or upon (mostly anteclass. and post-Aug.). Lit. With in and acc. : coronam in focum, Cato, R. R. 143, 2 : in urnam, id. ib. 143, 23 : ignem in aram, Plaut. Mil. 2, 5, 1 :…

in-dŏcĭbĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-doceo , unteachable (late Lat.), Vulg. Interpr. Iren. 4, 28 ; Ambros. in Psa. 47, § 21 fin. : indocibilis, δυσμαθής, Gloss. Philox.

in-dŏcĭbĭlĭtas.opening: , false reading in App. for indocilitas.

in-dŏcĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-doceo . Difficult to be taught , that cannot be taught , indocile. Lit. (class): quia nimis indociles quidam tardique sunt, Cic. N. D. 1, 5, 12 ; so, hebetes et indociles homines, Quint. 1, 1, 2 : hirundines,…

indŏcĭlĭtas.opening: indocilis , unteachableness , indocility (post-class.), App. Dogm. Plat. 2, p. 14 med.

in-doctus.opening: adj. , untaught , unlearned , uninstructed , ignorant , unskilful. Of persons (class.): homo, Auct. Her. 4, 46, 59 : (Juventius) nec indoctus, et magna cum juris civilis intellegentia, Cic. Brut. 48, 178 : est habitus…

in-dŏlātĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-dolo , that cannot be fashioned , formed , or cultivated : corporibus ac sensibus rigidi indolatilesque (al. indociles), Sid. Ep. 5, 5 .

in-dŏlātus.opening: adj. , not cut , unhewn (post-class.): lapis, Arn. 7, 253 : lignum, id. 6, 196 ; Hier. Ep. 98, 22 .

in-dŏlentĭa.opening: 2. in-doleo , freedom from pain (a word made by Cicero), Cic. Fin. 2, 4, 11 ; 2, 6 fin. ; id. Off. 3, 3, 12 ; Sen. Ep. 66 .— Insensibility , Cic. Tusc. 3, 6, 12 .

ind-ŏles.opening: indu = in-olesco; indoles, incrementum, industria, Paul. ex Fest. p. 106 Müll. , an inborn or native quality , natural quality , nature (class.; cf. ingenium). In gen.: quae indoles in savio est! Plaut. Rud. 2, 4, 10 :…

in-dŏlesco.opening: v. n. and a. [in-dolor], to feel pain , to smart , ache (mostly postAug.). Lit. : locus tactu indolescit, Cels. 8, 9 : oculi indolescunt, Plin. 31, 3, 27, § 45 .— With acc. , to feel pain at : tactum hominum, Just. 12,…

in-dŏlōrĭa.opening: 2. in-dolor , i. q. indolentia (late Lat.; cf. Madv. ad Cic. Fin. 2, 4, 11 ), absence of pain , Sid. Ep. 14 .

in-dŏlōris.opening: adj. 2. in-dolor , free from pain , Gloss. Philox: indoloria medicamenta, i. q. anodyna, Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 4, 79 .

indŏlōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , painless , Hier. in Eph. 4, 17 -19.—Hence, plur. as subst. : , = anodyna, anæsthetics , Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 4, 79 ; cf. indoloria, ἀνάλγητα, Gloss.

in-dŏmābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-domo , that cannot be broken in or tamed , untamable , Plaut. Cas. 4, 3, 12 : tauri, Mythogr. Lat. 2, 136: cervix, Cassiod. Var. 10, 29 .

in-dŏmĭnābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-dominus , that cannot be mastered , Gloss. Philox.

indŏmĭtābĭlis.opening: adj. indomitus , not to be subdued (eccl. Lat.), Victor Tunon. Poenit. 30.

in-dŏmĭtus.opening: adj. , untamed , unsubdued , ungoverned , unrestrained; untamable , ungovernable , fierce , wild (class.). Lit. : boves indomitos emere, unbroken, Varr. R. R. 2, 5, 11 : equus, Auct. Her. 4, 46, 59 ; Hor. S. 2, 2, 10 ;…

in-dōnātus.opening: adj. , without a present (late Lat.), Lampr. Heliog. 28, 6 .

in-dormĭo.opening: v. n. , to sleep or fall asleep at , on , or over a thing; constr. with dat. , with in , or with abl. (class. only in the trop. signif.). Lit. : congestis undique saccis Indormis, Hor. S. 1, 1, 71 : unctis cubilibus,…

indormis.opening: adj. 2. in-dormio , i. q. insomnis, sleepless , Gloss. Philox.

in-dōtātus.opening: adj. , unportioned , portionless (class. only in the trop. signif.). Lit. : virgo, Ter. Ad. 4, 7, 11 ; id. Phorm. 1, 2, 70 ; 5, 7, 45 : soror, Hor. Ep. 1, 17, 46 .— Transf. ( poet. ): corpora, that have not received the…

in-dŭbĭtābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-dubito , that cannot be doubted , indubitable (postAug. and post-class.), Quint. 4, 1, 55 ; 4, 5, 13 ; Dig. 28, 5, 9, § 8 ,—Hence, adv. : , indubitably , without doubt , doubtless , Arn. 5, 183 .

in-dŭbĭtandus.opening: adj. id. , not to be doubted , indubitable (late Lat.): veritas, Aug. Ep. 19, 2 .

in-dŭbĭtanter.opening: adv. id. , indubitably , without doubt (post-class.): probatur, Dig. 37, 11, 2 : invictus, Aug. de Vera Relig. 46 .

in-dŭbĭtātus.opening: adj. , undoubted , without doubt , certain , sure (post-Aug.): in iis ero, quae indubitata sunt, brevior, Quint. 9, 4, 2: litterarum inter se conjunctio, id. 1, 1, 31 : spes, Plin. 31, 3, 27, § 45 : indubitatum est, id.…

in-dŭbĭto.opening: v. n. , to doubt of ( poet. ); with dat. : viribus tuis, Verg. A. 8, 404 : tuis moribus, Stat. S. 3, 5, 110 .

in-dŭbĭus.opening: adj. , not doubtful , certain (post-Aug.): innocentia plurimorum, Tac. A. 14, 45 : exempla, Quint. 5, 13, 24 .— , adv. : , doubtlessly , Cassiod. Fragm. in Auct. Class. Tom. 3, 355 Mai.

in-dūco.opening: ( imp. induce for induc, Varr. R. R. 3, 2, 18 ; induxti for induxisti, Ter. And. 5, 3, 12 ; induxis for induxeris, Plaut. Capt. 1, 2, 46 ), v. a. in-duco , to lead , bring , or conduct into a place; to lead or bring in…

inductĭbĭlis.opening: adj. induco , that may be drawn or smeared over a thing (late Lat.), Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 37, 201 ; 203 .

inductīcĭus.opening: or , , adj. id. , introduced , Gloss. Philox.; Aug. de Duab. Anim. 12, 18 .

in-ductĭo.opening: id. , a leading or bringing into , introducing , admission (class.). Lit. : nos aquarum inductionibus terris fecunditatem damus, Cic. N. D. 2, 60, 152 : horum (juvenum in circum), introduction, exhibition, Liv. 44, 9, 5…

inductīvus.opening: adj. induco , relating to an assumption , Prisc. 1144 P.— Hence, , adv. , by yielding : indulgere (late Lat.), Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 5, 157 .

inductor.opening: id. , one who stirs up or rouses one, a chastiser , scourger : acerrimi, Plaut. As. 3, 2, 6 .

inductōrĭum.opening: id. , a covering : facere inductorium, Plin. Val. 1, 3 .

inductōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , misleading , August. contr. Acad. 1, 4.

inductrix.opening: id. , she that misleads or deceives , App. Flor. 23 fin. al.

inductūra.opening: id. , a covering , coating (late Lat.), Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 17, 148 .

inductus.opening: (only in abl. sing. ) [induco], an inducement , persuasion (rare but class.): hujus persuasu et inductu, Cic. Fragm. ap. Quint. 5, 10, 69 : inductu alieno facere aliquid, at another ' s persuasion , Auct. Her. 2, 17, 26…

indūcŭla.opening: induo , a kind of under-garment worn by females , Plaut. Ep. 2, 2, 39 .

in-dulceo.opening: v. n. in-dulcis , to become very sweet , Gloss. Philox.

in-dulcĭtas.opening: , false read. for dulcitas, Caecil. ap. Non. 96, 29 ; v. Com. Rel. p. 60 Rib.

in-dulco.opening: v. a. , to make sweet , to sweeten (late Lat.). Lit. : aquam amaram, Tert. adv. Jud. 13 ; Vulg. Sirach, 38, 5 .— Trop. , to speak sweetly , Vulg. Sirach, 12, 15 .

in-dulcōro.opening: v. a. , to make very sweet , Gloss. Philox.

indulgens.opening: Part. and P. a. , from indulgeo.

indulgentĭa.opening: indulgens , indulgence , gentleness , complaisance , tenderness , fondness (class.). Of persons: quid est dignius, in quo omnis nostra diligentia indulgentiaque consumatur? Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 44, § 112 : in hujus (matris)…

indulgĕo.grammar: si, tum, 2 v. n. and a.
indulgĕo.opening: v. n. and a. [etym. dub.; cf. dulcis], to be courteous or complaisant; to be kind , tender , indulgent to; to be pleased with or inclined to , to give one ' s self up to , yield to , indulge in a thing (as joy or…

indulgĭtas.opening: indulgeo , indulgence , for indulgentia (ante-class.): indulgitate victus, Sisenn. ap. Non. 126, 9 : indulgitate liberum, Cael. ap. Serv. ad Verg. G. 2, 345 .

indultor.opening: id. , a favorer (late Lat.): legis, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 9 .

indultum.opening: id. , indulgence , permission , grace , favor (post-class.): legis, Cod. Th. 4, 15, 1: principis, id. ib. 3, 10, 1 .

indultus.opening: indulgeo , leave , permission (late Lat.): indultu clementiae tuae scribere, Sid. Ep. 1, 11 .

indūmentum.opening: induo , a garment (post-class.). Lit. : indumenta induere, Gell. 16, 19, 12 : oris, a mask , Bass. ap. Gell. 5, 7.— Transf. , a covering , clothing : carnis indumenta, i. e. bodies, Prud. Cath. 9 . 99.— Trop. :…

indŭo.opening: v. a. cf. Gr. ἐνδύω , to put on an article of dress or ornament (class.). Lit. : Herculi tunicam, Cic. Tusc. 2, 8, 20 : sibi torquem, id. Fin. 2, 22, 73 : galeam, Caes. B. G. 2, 21 : zmaragdos et sardonychas, Plin. 37,…

indŭpĕdĭo.opening: and , , um; v. impedio, etc., and in init.

indŭpĕrans.opening: Part. ; v. imperans and in init.

indŭpĕro.opening: , etc.; v. impero, etc., and in init.

indūrātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from induro.

in-dūresco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become hard , to harden (cf. percallesco; postAug.). Lit. : si vetus condyloma jam induruit, Cels. 6, 18, 8 : grana, Col. 2, 20, 2 . — Trop. : miles induruerat pro Vitellio, had become unalterably firm…

in-dūro.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
in-dūro.opening: v. a. and n. , to make hard , to harden ( poet. and post-Aug.). Act. Lit. : nivem Indurat Boreas, Ov. Tr. 3, 9, 14 : sues indurantes attritu arborum costas, Plin. 8, 52, 78, § 212 .— Trop. , to harden , steel :…

Indus.opening: , = Ἰνδός, the name of two rivers. The Indus , that empties into the Indian Ocean , now Sind , Cic. N. D. 2, 52, 130 ; Mel. 3, 7 ; Plin. 6, 20, 23, § 71 ; Ov. Tr. 5, 3, 24 al. — A river in Caria , Plin. 5, 28, 29, § 103…

indūsĭārĭus.opening: indusium , a maker of women ' s under-garments , Plaut. Aul. 3, 5, 35 ; cf.: indusiarii vestiarii, Gloss. Isid.

indūsĭātus.opening: (in Varr. L. L. 5, § 131 , written intusiatus; cf. indusium), , adj. id. , that has on an under-garment (ante- and post-class.), Plaut. Ep. 2, 2, 47 : pueri, App. M. 2, p. 123 ; 10 , p. 253.

indūsĭo.opening: v. a. id. , to clothe (postclass.): aliqua re, Mart. Cap. 1, § 65 ; 2, § 114 .

indūsĭum.opening: (in Varr. L. L. 5, § 131 , written intusium), , induo , a woman ' s under - garment , Varr. l. l.: indusium est vestimentum, quod corpori intra plurimas vestes adhaeret, quasi intusium, Non. 539, 32 ; cf. indusium…

industrĭa.opening: industrius , diligence , activity , assiduity , industry : ingenium industriā alitur, Cic. Cael. 19, 45 : in agendo, id. de Imp. Pomp. 11, 29 : qui in scribendo tantum industriae ponam, spend so much pains on writing,…

Industrĭa.opening: a city in Liguria , on the right bank of the Padus , now Monteù di Po , near Chivasso , Plin. 3, 5, 7, § 49 ; 3, 16, 20, § 122 .—Hence, , , adj. , Tab. Aenea ap. Maff. Mus. Ver. p. 230.

industrĭōsus.opening: adj. industria , very active , diligent , or industrious (postAug.), Cassiod. Var. 8, 33 ; Sen. Prov. 2 dub.; Val. Max. 3, 4, 2 dub.—Hence, adv. : , very industriously , Cassiod. Var. 5, 1 ; Suet. Vit. Juv.— Comp. ,…
