industrĭus.opening: adj. perh. indo for in, and struo; lit. building within, i. e. active within; hence , active , diligent , assiduous , industrious (class.): homo gnavus et industrius, Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 21, § 53 : homines vigilantes,…

indūtĭae.opening: (less correctly ), , for indu-itiae, from indu for in and ire, a going into rest or retirement; cf. Aur. ap. Gell. 1, 25, 17; hence , a cessation of hostilities , a truce , armistice (class.). Lit. : indutiae sunt belli…

indūtĭlis.opening: adj. induo , that can be inserted or joined in : vomis, Cato, R. R. 135, 2 dub.

Indŭtĭomărus.opening: ( ), , , a chief of the Treviri , Caes. B. G. 5, 3 .

indūtor.opening: induo , a wearer (late Lat.): fabularum sartor aut indutor, Aug. c. Faust. 8.

indūtōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , that can be put on : pellis, Paul. Sent. 3, 6, § 79 .

indūtus.opening: induo , a putting on (very rare; only indutui and indutibus in use): prius dein quae indutui, tum amictui quae sunt tangam, Varr. L. L. 5, § 131 Müll.; Symm. Ep. 3, 10 ; Varr. L. L. 10, § 27 Müll.: vestis, quam indutui…

indŭvĭae.opening: id. , clothes , garments (ante- and post-class.): tuae, Plaut. Men. 1, 3, 9 : nudata induviis, Prud. Psych. 578 .

indŭvĭum.opening: Plin. 13, 4, 7, § 35 ; v. Sillig ad h. l.

inebrae.opening: , quae in auguriis aliquid fieri prohibent; et prorsus omnia inebra appellantur, quae tardant vel morantur agentem, Paul. ex Fest. p. 109 Müll.

inēmigrābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-emigro (eccl. Lat.): immobilis et inemigrabilis Deus, not capable of removing , (Hilar.) Anon. in Job, 2, p. 128.

in-ēmŏrĭor.opening: v. dep. , to die in or at any thing (for the more usual immorior); with dat. : spectaculo, Hor. Epod. 5, 34 .

in-euschēmē.opening: , false reading in Plaut. Trin. 3, 1, 24 (ei euscheme, Fleck., Ritschl, Wagner: sane euscheme, Brix).

in-fā^brē.opening: adv. , in an unworkmanlike manner , unskilfully , rudely (opp. affabre; not in Cic. or Cæs.): pestem novā figurā factam, commissam infabre, Pac. ap. Non. 40, 31 , and 248, 22 (Trag. Rel. p. 93 Rib.): vasa, non infabre…

in-făbrĭcātus.opening: adj. , unwrought , unfashioned ( poet. and in late Lat. prose): robora, * Verg. A. 4, 400 .— Trop. , unfinished , rude : verba, Ennod. Ep. 2, 6 : confabulatio, id. ib. 8, 59 .

infăcētĭae.opening: (or ), , plur. [infacetus], rude jests , coarse jokes or puns : pleni ruris et infacetiarum Annales Volusi, Cat. 36, 19 .

in-făcētus.opening: ( ), , adj. , coarse , blunt , rude , unmannerly , not witty , stupid (class.). Of persons: inficetus (homo), Plaut. Truc. 2, 4, 4 : Canius nec infacetus, et satis litteratus, Cic. Off. 3, 14, 58 : saeclum (with…

infactus.opening: , acc. to the reading of some, in Tert. Apol. 11 .

in-fācundus.opening: adj. , ineloquent (not in Cic. or Cæs.): vir acer, nec infacundus, Liv. 4, 49, 12 ; Suet. Claud. 40 ; Gell. 18, 3, 6 .— Comp. : infacundior, Liv. 7, 4, 4 .

in-faeco.opening: v. a. in-faex , to pollute : animam concretione carnis (late Lat.), Tert. Anim. 53 fin.

in-fallĭbĭlĭter.opening: adv. 2. in-fallo , infallibly (late Lat.), Aug. Praedest. Sanct. 15, 2 .

in-falsātus.opening: adj. , falsified (late Lat.): codices, Aug. contra Faust. 13, 4 fin.

infāmātĭo.opening: infamo , a calumny , defamation (post-class.), Non. p. 263, 8 .

infāmĭa.opening: (infamis], ill fame , ill report of a person or thing; bad repute , dishonor , disgrace , infamy (class.; cf.: ignominia, opprobrium): hominum immortalis est infamia, Plaut. Pers. 3, 1, 27 : in infamiam populo ponere,…

in-fāmis.opening: adj. 2. in-fama , of ill report , ill spoken of , disreputable , notorious , infamous (class.): homines ceteris vitiis atque omni dedecore infames, Cic. Clu. 47, 130 : Metellus, infamis auctor deserendae Italiae, Liv.…

in-fāmo.opening: v. a. infamis , to bring into ill repute , to brand with infamy , to disgrace , dishonor , defame (rare but class.). Lit. : ut tua moderatio et gravitas aliorum infamet injuriam, Cic. Fam. 9, 12 : Juppiter infamat seque…

in-fandus.opening: adj. , unspeakable , unutterable , unheard of , unnatural , shocking , abominable (class.): res crudelis, infanda, Cic. de Or. 2, 79, 322 : impurum atque infandum corpus, id. Sest. 55, 117 : epulae, i. e. of human…

in-fans.opening: ( , Momms. Inscr. R. N. 66; 5376; Inscr. Grut. 688, 2 ), fantis ( gen. plur. infantium, but infantum, Plin. Ep. 9, 20, 14 ), adj. in-for , that cannot speak , without speech , mute , speechless (class.): seu rubra…

infantārĭus.opening: adj. infans , that has to do with infants ( poet. and post-class.). — Only substt. , , , a woman fond of infants , Mart. 4, 88, 3 .— , , plur. , sacrificers of infants , an epithet applied to the Christians, who were…

infantĭa.opening: id. , inability to speak. Lit. : linguae, Lucr. 5, 1031 .— In partic., want of eloquence : infantia ejus, qui rem norit, sed eam explicare dicendo non queat, Cic. de Or. 3, 35, 142 : incredibilis accusatorum, id. Att.…

infantĭcīda.opening: and infans-caedo , a child-murderer , an infanticide (late Lat.), Tert. Apol. 4 ; id. ad Nat. 1, 15 .

infantĭcīdĭum.opening: infanticida , child-murder , infanticide (late Lat.), Tert. Apol. 2 .

infantĭlis.opening: adj. infans , of or belonging to infants or little children (post-class.): vestis, Dig. 34, 2, 25 : blandimenta, Just. 17, 3, 20 : uterus, little, young, App. M. 5, p. 164, 12 .— , adv. : , like a child , Hier. Orig. in…

infanto.opening: v. a. id. , to nourish or feed as an infant (late Lat.), Tert. adv. Marc. 1, 14 .

infantŭla.opening: dim. id. , a little girl (post-class.), App. M. 10, p. 252, 15 ; Sid. Ep. 7, 2 al.

infantŭlus.opening: dim. id. , a little infant (post-class.), App. M. 8, p. 207, 39 ; Nazar. Paneg. Const. 16, 6 ; Hier.in Isai. 3, 7, 16.

in-farcĭo.grammar: si, sum and tum, 4 v. a.
in-farcĭo.opening: ( ), , v. a. To stuff into any thing. Lit. : in eas partes largum salem infarcito, Col. 12, 53, 2 : crumenis turpe lucrum, Prud. Psych. 459 .— Pass. : parietes quos appellant formaceos, inferciuntur verius quam…

in-fascĭnābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-fascino , that cannot be bewitched , Gloss. Philox.

in-fascĭnātē.opening: adv. id. , without being bewitched , Gloss. Philox.

in-fastīdĭbĭlis.opening: adj. , not to be loathed , not repulsive : sedulitas, Cassiod. Inst. Div. Litt. 16 .

in-fastīdītus.opening: adj. , not loathed , not loathsome (late Lat.): cadaver, Sid. Carm. 16, 124 : suggestio, Cassiod. Var. 5, 41 .

in-fătīgābĭlis.opening: adj. , indefatigable (post-Aug.): cursus, Plin. 28, 19, 78, § 257 : quiddam est virtus, Sen. Vit. Beat. 7 : animus, id. Ep. 66 med. ; Lact. 7, 27 fin. ; Macr. S. 1, 21, 17 .— Adv. : , indefatigably : gaudere, Aug. Ep.…

in-fătīgātus.opening: adj. , unwearied (late Lat.): viatrix, Mart. Cap. 6, § 582 .

in-fătīgo.opening: v. a. , not to weary , Not. Tir. p. 118 .

infătŭātĭo.opening: infatuo , infatuation (late Lat.), Hilar. in Job, 3, p. 219.

infătŭo.opening: v. a. in-fatuor , to make a fool of , to infatuate (class.): aliquem, Cic. Phil. 3, 9, 22 ; id. Fl. 20, 47 ; Sen. Suas. 2 fin. : verbis, Auct. B. Afr. 16, 1: quemque adulatio infatuat, Sen. Ep. 59 med. : hominem, Amm.…

in-faustus.opening: adj. , unfortunate , unpropitious ( poet. and post-Aug.): infaustas exurite puppes, Verg. A. 5, 635 : nomen, id. ib. 7, 717 : auspicium, id. ib. 11, 347 : gradus, Ov. M. 3, 36 : dies, Tac. H. 2, 91 : castra, id. A. 1,…

in-făvōrābĭlis.opening: adj. , unfavorable (post-class.): sententia, Dig. 37, 6, 6 .— Adv. : , unfavorably : respondere, Dig. 50, 2, 2, § 6 .

infectĭo.opening: inficio , a dyeing (late Lat.): capillorum, Theod. Prisc. 1, 1 : purpurae, Ambros. Apol. David, 8, § 45.

infectīvus.opening: adj. id. , pertaining to dyeing. —Only subst. plur. : , , , dye-stuffs , dyes , Vitr. 7, 14, 2 .

infector.opening: id. , a dyer (class.): eum infector moratur, Cic. Fam. 2, 16, 7 : lanarum, Plin. 20, 7, 25, § 59 .— Adj. , dyeing : infector ille sucus, Plin. 11, 3, 2, § 8 .

infectōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , that serves for dyeing (late Lat.): alumen, Marc. Emp. 4 .— Subst. : , , , a dye-house , Gr. βαφεῖον, Gloss. Philox.

infectrix.opening: id. , one that infects (eccl. Lat.), Jul. ap. Aug. c. Sec. Resp. Jul. II. 105.

infectus.opening: inficio , a dyeing (post-Aug.).—In abl. : lanarum, Plin. 8, 48, 73, § 193 .

in-fēcundĭtas.opening: infecundus , unfruitfulness (post-Aug.): agrorum, Col. prooem. 1, 1: terrarum, Tac. A. 4, 6 : apum, Plin. 11, 16, 16, § 50 : bienni, Sall. H. Fragm. 3, 1 Dietsch.

in-fēcundus.opening: adj. , unfruitful (rare): ager frugum fertilis, arbore infecundus, Sall. J. 17, 5 ; Verg. G. 2, 48 ; Ov. Tr. 3, 14, 34 .— Comp. : infecundior materia, Col. 2, 4, 7 .— * Adv. : , unfruitfully , i. e. meagrely , sparingly…

in-fēlīcĭtas.opening: infelix , ill-luck , misfortune (rare but class.): quid hoc infelicitatis? Ter. Ad. 4, 5, 5 : haruspicum, Cic. Div. 2, 29 fin. : gravior, Liv. 40, 55 fin. al.— Plur. : miseriae et infelicitates, calamities, App. Dogm.…

infēlīcĭto.opening: (or , v. infra ), , v. a. infelix , to render unhappy , make wretched , plague (ante-class.): di me et te infelicitent, Plaut. Cas. 2, 3, 30 (Ritschl et MSS.; al. infelicent): Hercle illum infelicitent di, id. Merc. 2,…

in-fēlix.opening: adj. , unfruitful , not fertile : vulgus infelicem arborem eam appellat, quoniam nihil ferat, nec seratur unquam, Plin. 24, 9, 41, § 68 ; cf. id. 16, 26, 45, § 108 ; hence, of the gallows , Cic. Rab. Perd. 4, 13 ; cf.…

infenso.opening: v. a. and n. infensus , to treat in a hostile manner , to ravage , destroy (Tacitean). V. a. : bello Armeniam, Tac. A. 13, 37 : pabula, id. ib. 6, 34 .— V. n. , to act like an enemy , to be hostilely disposed : quasi…

infensus.opening: adj. 2. in-fendo , hostile , inimical , enraged (class.; cf. infestus): infenso atque inimico animo venire, Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 61, § 149 .— With dat. : Drances infensus Turno, Verg. A. 11, 122 : opes principibus infensae,…

in-fĕrax.opening: adj. , unfruitful (late Lat.): silvae, Hier. Homil. ex Orig. 2.

infĕrĭae.opening: plur. [inferi], sacrifices in honor of the dead (class.); nom. , Ov. M. 13, 613 ; abl. , id. Ib. 454 : alicui inferias afferre, Cic. N. D. 3, 16, 42 ; cf.: absenti ferat inferias, Verg. A. 9, 215 ; so, referre, Hor. C.…

infĕrĭālis.opening: adj. inferiae , of or belonging to a funeral : officia, App. M. 8, p. 204 . — Hence, , , plur. , = inferiae, sacrifices to the dead, Gloss. Philox.

infĕrĭus.opening: adj. infero , that is offered or sacrificed (ante- and post-class.): vinum, sacrificial wine, Cato, R. R. 132, 2 ; 134, 3 ; Arn. 4, 138 .

in-fermentātus.opening: adj. , unleavened (late Lat.): panes, Paul. Nol. Carm. 23, 47 .

infernālis.opening: adj. infernus , nether , lower , belonging to the lower regions , infernal (post-class.): nox, Alcim. Avit. 2, 290 : Juppiter, i. e. Pluto , Prud. adv. Symm. 1, 389 .

infernas.opening: adj. infernus , of or from the lower country , lowland (rare): abies, Plin. 16, 39, 76, § 197 ; Vitr. 2, 10 : navicularii, Inscr. Orell. 1084 : terra, Mart. Cap. 6, § 603 .

infernĕ.opening: adv. , v. infernus, a, um, fin.

infernus.opening: adj. infer , lower , that which lies beneath (mostly poet. and postAug.). In gen.: hic sese infernis de partibus erigit Hydra, from beneath , Cic. poët. N. D. 2, 44, 114: superi infernique Di, Liv. 24, 38, 8 : stagna,…

in-fĕro.opening: v. a. , to carry , bring , put , or throw into or to a place (class.); constr. with in and acc. , ad , or the dat. Lit. With in and acc. : in equum, to bring or set upon a horse , Caes. B. G. 6, 29 : coronam in curiam,…

infertor.opening: (infero), one who serves up dishes , a waiter , steward , παραθέτης, Gloss. Philox.; Schol. Juv. 5, 83 ; 9, 109 .

infĕrus.opening: (ante-class. collat. form of the nom. sing. infer: ubi super inferque vicinus permittet, Cato, R. R. 149 ), adj. cf. Sanscr. adh-aras, adh-amas, the lower, lowest; and Lat. infra , that is below , underneath , lower;…

in-fervĕfăcĭo.opening: v. a. ( pass. fīo, factus, fĭēri), to cause to boil in any thing; or simply to cause to boil , to boil : infervefacito paulisper, Cato, R. R. 156, 7 : liquatum acetum, Col. 12, 17, 2 : cum infervefiunt, Scrib. Comp. 271…

in-fervĕo.opening: v. n. , to boil in any thing; to boil , seethe : facito bis aut ter inferveat, Cato, R. R. 108 ; Cels. 5, 25, 4 : mel Atticum ter infervere facito, Col. 12, 38, 5 .

in-fervesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to boil down , to boil , to grow hot , be heated : fabae tertia pars ut infervescat, Cato, R. R. 90 : mulsum quod inferbuit, Cels. 2, 30 : hoc ubi inferbuit, Hor. S. 2, 4, 67 : ne infervescat aqua sole, be…

infestātĭo.opening: infesto , a disturbing , troubling (post-class.), Tert. Apol. 1 .

infestātor.opening: id. , a disturber , troubler (post-Aug. and very rare), Plin. 6, 28, 32, § 143 .

in-festīvus.opening: adj. , not agreeable , not pleasant , inelegant (post-class.): subagresti ingenio et infestivo, Gell. 1, 5, 3 .— Adv. : , inelegantly : cetera vertit non infestiviter, i. e. quite elegantly, Gell. 9, 9, 9 .

infesto.opening: v. a. infestus , to attack , trouble , molest , disturb , infest (mostly post-Aug.). Lit. : Scylla latus dextrum, laevum Charybdis infestant, Ov. M. 13, 730 : eas insulas infestari beluis, Plin. 6, 32, 37, § 205 :…

in-festus.opening: adj. 2. in-festus for fenstus, from fendo; whence defendo, infensus , made unsafe , disturbed , molested , infested; unquiet , unsafe (class.; cf. infensus). Lit. : via excursionibus barbarorum infesta, Cic. Prov. Cons.…

in-fībŭlo.opening: ( ), , v. a. in-fibula , to clasp , buckle , or button together , to close with a clasp or pin (rare): infibulati sacrificabant flamines propter usum aeris antiquissimum aereis fibulis, Paul. ex Fest. p. 113 Müll.;…

infĭcĭens.opening: adj. 2. in-facio , that does nothing , inactive (ante-class.): homo, Varr. L. L. 6, § 78 Müll.: apes (with inertes), id. R. R. 3, 16, 8 .

in-fĭcĭo.opening: v. a. in-facio , to put or dip into any thing; hence, Lit. , to stain , dye , color , tinge with : quia tibi suaso infecisti pallulam, Plaut. Truc. 2, 2, 16 : omnes se Britanni vitro inficiunt, Caes. B. G. 5, 14 : lana…

in-fĭdēlis.opening: adj. , that cannot be relied upon , unfaithful , faithless. In gen. (rare but class.): si hoc sibi sument, nullam esse fidem, quae infideli data sit, Cic. Off. 3, 29, 106 : Bellovaci, qui ante erant per se infideles,…

infĭdēlĭtas.opening: infidelis , unfaithfulness , faithlessness , infidelity : amicitiarum, Cic. Tusc. 5, 22 : infidelitatis suspicionem sustinere, * Caes. B. C. 2, 33 . — In plur. : quantae infidelitates in amicitiis, Cic. Mil. 26, 69 .

infīdigrăphus.opening: adj. vox hybr., infidus- γράφω , writing faithlessly (eccl. Lat.): infidelis Deo nec infidigraphus nec ingratus, (Hilar.) Anon. in Job, 1, 124.

in-fīdus.opening: adj. , not to be trusted , unsafe , faithless , treacherous , false (class.): quos fidos amicos habuisset, quos infidos, Cic. Lael. 15, 53 : nihil stabile quod infidum est, id. ib. 18, 65 : gentes, id. Prov. Cons. 13,…

in-fīgo.opening: v. a. , to fix , thrust , drive , or fasten in. Lit. : gladium hosti in pectus, Cic. Tusc. 4, 22, 50 : ferreis hamis infixis, Caes. B. G. 7, 73 fin. : hastam portae, Verg. A. 9, 746 : signum, Cic. Div. 2, 31 : (sagitta)…

infĭgūrābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-figura , shapeless , ill-shaped , deformed : fornix, Amm. 24, 4, 15 .

infĭmātis.opening: ( ), , adj. infimus , one of the lowest (in condition, rank, etc.), opp. summas: ego infumatis infumus, Plaut. Stich. 3, 2, 37 ; cf. Prisc. 943 P.: infimates ὑστερεύοντες, Gloss.

infĭmĭtas.opening: id. , lowness , humility (late Lat.): sortis, Amm. 29, 11 : obsequiorum, id. 17, 13, 12 ; Aug. 1 Music. 9, 15.

infĭmo.opening: v. a. id. , to make low , to lower (post-class.): deos, App. M. 1, p. 106, 2 : ingenia ad miserias infimata (opp. ad beatitudinem sublimata), id. de Deo Socr. p. 44, 8 .

in-findo.opening: v. a. , to cut into , to cleave ( poet. ): telluri sulcos, Verg. E. 4, 33 ; so poet. , sulcos, for to plough up , make by sailing , id. A. 5, 142 : silvam, Dig. 50, 66 : volat cava pinus infinditque salum, cuts through,…

infīnībĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-finio , endless (post-class.): materia, App. Dogm. Plat. 1, p. 4, 1 ; Mart. Cap. 2, § 203 .

infīnĭtas.opening: 2. in-finis , boundlessness , endlessness , infinity : locorum, boundlessness, endless extent, Cic. N. D. 1, 26, 73 : rerum atque naturae, id. Tusc. 5, 36 fin. : naturae, id. Ac. 2, 37 ; Plin. 2, 2, 1, § 3 : mundorum,…

infīnītĭo.opening: infinitus , boundlessness , infinity : infinitio ipsa, quam ἀπειρίαν vocant, Cic. Fin. 1, 6, 21 .

infīnītīvus.opening: adj. id. , unlimited , indefinite : modus, or absol. : , , ; in gram., the infinitive, Mart. Cap. 3, § 310 sqq.; Isid. Orig. 1, 8 ; Diom. p. 331 P. al.

in-fīnītus.opening: adj. , not enclosed within boundaries , boundless , unlimited. Lit. : quod finitum est habet extremum ... nihil igitur cum habeat extremum, infinitum sit necesse est, Cic. Div. 2, 50, 103 : aër, materia, id. Ac. 2, 37,…

infirmātĭo.opening: , ōnis. 1. infirmo , a weakening , invalidating. Rerum judicatarum, Cic. Agr. 2, 3, 8 ; 2, 4, 10 .— Transf. , a refuting , disproving : judicatio est, quae ex infirmatione et confirmatione rationis nascitur…

infirmĭtas.opening: infirmus , want of strength; weakness , feebleness. Lit. : puerorum, Cic. de Sen. 10, 33 : summa gracilitas et infirmitas corporis, id. Fam. 7, 1 : oculorum, Plin. Ep. 7, 21 : propter sexus infirmitatem, Ulp. Fragm. 11,…

infirmo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
infirmo.opening: v. a. and n. infirmus . Act. , to deprive of strength , to weaken , enfeeble. Lit. : legiones, Tac. A. 15, 10 : munimenta madore, Sall. Fragm. ap. Non. 138, 6 : hominem, Cels. 2, 12 .— Trop. To invalidate , disprove ,…

in-firmo.opening: v. a. , to establish in , fix , or confirm in (late Lat.), Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 4, 36 .

in-firmus.opening: (post-class. , , Amm. 20, 6 ), adj. , not strong , weak , feeble. Lit. : viribus infirmis, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 43, § 95 : valetudo, id. Brut. 48, 180 : classis inops et infirma, Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 33, § 86 : valetudo…

in-fit.opening: v. def. (infĭunt, Mart. Cap. 2, § 220 : infe ἄρξαι, Gloss.: infĭo, Varr. ap. Prisc. 8 fin. ), he ( she , it ), begins : infit me percontarier, Plaut. As. 2, 2, 76 : laudare formam virginis, id. Rud. prol. 51 . postulare…

infĭtens.opening: Part. , from infiteor, that does not confess , Gloss. Philox.; cf. the foll. art.

infĭtĭae.opening: ( ), , 2. infateor , denial; only in the acc. in connection with ire, and very rarely without a negative, except in ante-class. Lat.: infitias ire, to deny (not in Cic. or Cæs.); constr. with acc. and inf. , aliquid or…

infĭtĭālis.opening: ( ), , adj. infitiae , negative , consisting in denial : quaestio, Cic. Top. 24, 92 : status, Quint. 3, 6, 15 ; 32 .

infĭtĭātĭo.opening: ( ), , infitior , a denial. In gen.: causam infitiatione defendere, Cic. de Or. 2, 25, 105 : ipsam negationem infitiationemque, id. Part. 29, 102 . — In partic., a denying or disowning of a debt , Sen. de Ira, 2, 9, 1:…

infĭtĭātor.opening: ( ), , id. , a denier , esp. one who denies a debt or refuses to restore a deposit : ille infitiator, Cic. de Or. 1, 37, 168 ; with fraudulentus, Sen. Ben. 3, 27 : lentus, a bad debtor, Cic. Cat. 2, 10 .

infĭtĭātrix.opening: ( ), , id. , she that denies or disowns , Prud. Psych. 680 .

infĭtĭor.opening: ( ), , v. dep. a. [infitiae], not to confess , to contradict , deny , disown. In gen.: omnia infitiatur ea, quae dudum confessa est mihi, Plaut. Cist. 4, 1, 9 : cum id posset infitiari, repente confessus est, Cic. Cat.…

inflābellātus.opening: Part. [from the obs. inflabello], breathed into (late Lat.): corporibus ignis, Tert. adv. Val. 23 .

inflābĭlis.opening: adj. inflo , that may be inflated (late Lat.): viscus, Lact. Opif. D. 11, 4 .— Puffing up , causing wind : cibi, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 40, 233 .

in-flaccĕo.opening: v. n. , to become flaccid or weak; hence, trop., to become useless : inflaccebunt condiciones, Enn. ap. Non. 110, 14 dub. (Vahl. Enn. p. 142 reads: sin flaccebunt).

in-flāgro.opening: v. n. , to kindle (late Lat.): nullo inflagrante halitu, Sol. 5 fin.

inflāmen.opening: inflo , a state of inflation , puffing out : buccarum inflamina, Fulg. Myth. 3, 9 .

inflammātĭo.opening: inflammo , a kindling , setting on fire , conflagration. Lit. (post-class.): portarum, Nazar. in Pan. Constant. 21 : imperium quodam quasi diluvio et inflammatione corripuit, Flor. 4, 2, 3 . — Transf. , of the body, an…

inflammātrix.opening: id. , she that kindles or inflames (late Lat.), Amm. 14, 1, 2 ; Mamert. Pan. Julian. 3, 3 .

in-flammo.opening: v. a. , to set on fire , light up , kindle (syn. incendere). Lit. : taedas ignibus, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 48 ; id. Att. 8, 2, 4 : patriam inflammandam relinquere, id. ib. 8, 2, 3 : classem, Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 35 : tecta, Liv.…

inflātĭlis.opening: adj. inflo , of or for blowing : instrumenta, Cassiod. de Mus. 1, 1 .

inflātĭo.opening: id. , a blowing itself up , swelling up. Lit. , of boiling water, Vitr. 8, 3 .— Transf. , of the body; med. t. t., a swelling or puffing up , inflation , flatulence : habet inflationem magnam is cibus (faba), produces…

inflātus.opening: in-flo , a blowing into , a blast. Lit. : eae (tibiae) si inflatum non recipiunt, Cic. Brut. 51, 192 : primo inflatu tibicinis, id. Ac. 4, 7, 20 .— Trop. , a breathing into , inspiration : aliquo instinctu inflatuque…

in-flecto.opening: v. a. , to bend , bow , curve. Lit. : cum ferrum se inflexisset, Caes. B. G. 1, 25 : bacillum, Cic. Div. 1, 17 : capillum leniter, Suet. Aug. 79 . —Mid.: sinus ad urbem inflectitur, bends itself, curves round, Cic.…

in-flētus.opening: adj. , unwept , unlamented ( poet. ): animae viles, inhumata infletaque turba, Verg. A. 11, 372 ; Val. Fl. 6, 651 .

in-flexĭbĭlis.opening: adj. , that cannot be bent , inflexible. Lit. : dolor (cervicum), lockjaw = opisthotonos, Plin. 28, 12, 52, § 192 ; cf. Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 6, 65 .— Transf. : judicium, unchangeable, Sen. Ep. 95 : obstinatio, Plin. Ep.…

inflexĭo.opening: inflecto , a bending. Prop.: quasi helicis inflexio, Cic. Univ. 9, 27 : dextra inflexio Bospori, Amm. 22, 8, 14 : laterum inflexione forti ac virili, a vigorous and manly attitude, Cic. de Or. 3, 59, 229 .— Transf. , an…

in-flexŭōsus.opening: adj. 2. in-flecto , not flexible , without bending : serpens, Isid. Orig. 12, 4, 26 .

inflexus.opening: inflecto , a bending , curving , inflecting (post-Aug.). Lit. : vicorum, Juv. 3, 237 : adire inflexibus flexuosis, Arn. 2, 57 .— Trop. : vocem inflexu modulationis torquere, Sen. Brev. Vit. 12, 3 .

in-flexus.opening: adj. ; gram. t. t., not declined, not inflected, Mart. Cap. 3, § 305 .

inflictĭo.opening: infligo , a laying on , inflicting (late Lat.): multae, Cod. Th. 9, 17, 2.

inflictus.opening: infligo , a striking on or against : labiorum et dentium, Arn. 3, 111 .

in-flīgo.opening: v. a. , to strike a thing on or against (syn.: incutere, illidere). Lit. : alicui securim, Cic. Planc. 29, 70 : cratera viro, Ov. M. 5, 83 : caput suum parietibus, Lact. de Mort. Pers. 49 : puppis inflicta vadis, dashed…

in-flo.opening: v. a. , to blow into or upon any thing, to inflate. Lit. In gen.: age, jam infla buccas, Plaut. Stich. 5, 5, 26 : ex ore in os palumbi inflare aquam, Cato, R. R. 90 : tumidoque inflatur carbasus Austro, is swelled,…

in-flōresco.opening: v. inch. n. , to begin to blossom , put forth blossoms : pristina aetas, Claud. Laud. Stil. 3, 124 .

in-flŭo.opening: v. n. , to flow or run into. Lit. : Hypanis in Pontum influit, Cic. Tusc. 1, 39, 94 : in quem sanguis a jecore per venam illam cavam influit, id. N. D. 2, 55, 138 : lacus qui in flumen Rhodanum influit, Caes. B. G. 1, 8…

inflŭus.opening: adj. influo , flowing in , Paul. Nol. Carm. 15, 107 .

influxĭo.opening: id. , a flowing in (late Lat.): materialis influxio in corpus, Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 12, 10 ; Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 37, 192 .— Transf. , a cold , catarrh : ad nares, ad fauces, ad thoracem, Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 7 et saep.

influxus.opening: id. , a flowing in (late Lat.); trop.: stellarum, influence , Firm. Math. 1, 1.

in-fŏdĭo.opening: v. a. , to dig in or up , make by digging; to bury in the earth , inter : locus alte duos pedes infodiendus est, Col. 3, 13, 5 : sarmenta, Cato, R. R. 37, 3 : squalentes conchas, Verg. G. 2, 348 corpora terrae, id. A.…

in-foedĕrātus.opening: adj. , not leagued together , not allied (late Lat.): reges, Tert. Praeser. 12 .

in-formābĭlis.opening: adj. , insusceptible of form , that does not assume a form (late Lat.): Deus, Tert. adv. Prax. 27 .

in-formātĭo.opening: informo , a representation. Lit. , an outline , sketch , first draft : aedium sacrarum informationes, Vitr. 4, 6 fin. — Trop. , an idea , conception : anticipatio, quam appellat πρόληψιν Epicurus, id est anteceptam…

informātor.opening: id. , one who fashions , an instructor (late Lat.): populi, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 22 .

in-formīdābĭlis.opening: adj. , not to be feared , not formidable (late Lat.): judex, Coripp. Laud. Just. 2, 354 .

informis.opening: adj. 2. in-forma , that has no form or not a proper form , unformed , shapeless. Lit. : cum res muta aut informis fit loquens et formata, Auct. Her. 4, 53, 66 : alveus, Liv. 21, 26, 9 : caro, Plin. 7, 15, 13, § 63 .—…

informĭtas.opening: informis , unshapeliness , ugliness , deformity (late Lat.): materiae, Tert. adv. Hermog. 42 ; so Aug. Conf. 12, 12 .

in-formo.opening: v. a. , to give form to a thing, to shape , form , mould , fashion. Lit. (mostly poet. ): clipeum, Verg. A. 8, 447 : aream, Col. 11, 3, 13 : effigiem, Sil. 17, 525 : Martem cerā, Poët. ap. Plin. Ep. 9, 7 : taedas,…

in-fŏro.opening: v. n. in-foro , to bore into : mox ausi inforare medio trunco, Plin. 17, 14, 24, § 102 Jan. (Sillig, imperare); cf. also the foll. art.

infŏro.opening: v. a. in-forum , to accuse in a court of justice: Curc. Quaeso ne me incomities. Ly. Licetne inforare, si incomitiare haud licet? Curc. Non inforabis me quidem (with double meaning, in mal. part.; cf. 1. inforo), Plaut.…

in-fortūnātus.opening: adj. , unfortunate (class.): o infortunatum senem, Ter. Eun 2, 3, 7 : nihil me infortunatius, Cic. Att. 2, 24, 4 : infortunatissimus maritus, App. M. 4, p. 154, 37 .

infortūnĭtas.opening: , ātis. 2. in-fortuna , misfortune (with felicitas). Gell. 6, 1, 5 dub.

infortūnĭum.opening: id. , misfortune (mostly ante-class. and post-Aug.; not in Cic. or Cæs.): ferres infortunium, thou wouldst come badly off, Ter. Ad. 2, 1, 24 : ni pareat patri habiturum infortunium esse, * Liv. 1, 50, 9 : invenire,…

infossĭo.opening: infodio , a digging in (late Lat.), Pall. 3, 16 .

infrā.opening: infer, inferă, sc. parte , adv. and prep. Adv. , on the under side , below , underneath. Lit. : infra nihil est nisi mortale ... supra Lunam sunt aeterna omnia, Cic. Rep. 6, 17 : in occipitio et infra, qua summa…

infractĭo.opening: infringo , a breaking to pieces , Prisc. 1282 P.— Trop. , a weakening : infractio et demissio animi, despondency, Cic. Tusc. 3, 7, 14 .

infractus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from infringo.

in-fractus.opening: adj. , unbroken , unweakened (late Lat.): animi, Symm. Ep. 1, 3 : infractus hoc spectaculo, Hier. Vit. Pauli.

infrā-fŏrānus.opening: adj. forum , that is under the Forum : COLLEGIUM, Inscr. ap. Le-Vita AA. BB. 26, 3.

in-frăgĭlis.opening: adj. , that cannot be broken to pieces. Lit. : adamas, Plin. H. N. 20 prooem. § 2.— Trop. , strong , that cannot be weakened : vox, Ov. Tr. 1, 5, 53 : animi, Sen. Vit. B. 9 .

in-frĕmo.opening: v. n. , to make or utter a noise ( poet. ). Lit. , to growl , bellow : infremuitque ferox, of the wild boar, Verg. A. 10, 711 .— Transf. , of things, to roar , rage : bellum infremuit, Sil. 3, 230 .

in-frēnātĭo.opening: ( ), , in freno , a taming (late Lat.): libidinis, Tert. adv. Marc. 1, 29 .

in-frēnātus.opening: ( ), , adj. , without a bridle : equites frenati et infrenati, on unbridled horses, Liv. 21, 44, 1 . — Trop. : lingua, Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 12, 4 .

in-frendĕo.opening: , and , , v. n. , to gnash the teeth ( poet. and postclass.): dentibus infrendens gemitu, Verg. A. 3, 664 : ac simul infrendens, Stat. Th. 5, 663 : infrendite, inspumate, Tert. Apol. 12 . — To gnash the teeth at ,…

infrendis.opening: adj. 2. in-frendo , that cannot gnash (late Lat.): infantes sine dentibus infrendes dicuntur, Lact. ad Stat. Th. 5, 663 .

infrēnis.opening: , and , ( ), adj. 2. in - frenum , without a bridle , unbridled ( poet. and post-class.). Lit. : infrenis equus, Verg. A. 10, 750 : Numidae infreni, on unbridled horses, id. ib. 4, 41 .— Trop. , untamed , unchecked :…

in-frēno.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to put on a bridle. Lit. , to furnish with a bridle , to bridle : equos, Liv. 37, 20, 12 ; cf.: non stratos, non infrenatos equos habere, ib. § 4: currus, to harness the horses to a chariot, Verg. A. 12,…

in-frĕquens.opening: adj. , that does not often or frequently take place , unfrequent. Lit. , of persons, that is not often at a place , that seldom does a thing , seldom , rare : sum et Romae et in praedio infrequens, Cic. Q. Fr. 3, 9, 4 :…

in-frĕquentātus.opening: adj. , not much used (late Lat.): metrum, Sid. Ep. 9, 15 .

in-frĕquentĭa.opening: A small number , thinness , scanliness : summa senatus, Cic. Q. Fr. 3, 2, 2 : senatus, Liv. 2, 23, 12 : prodita (sc. legionum), the small number of his troops, Tac. A. 15, 10 .— Solitariness , loneliness : locorum, Tac.…

in-frĭco.grammar: cŭi, ctum, and cātum, 1 v. a.
in-frĭco.opening: v. a. , to rub in : aliquid alicui rei, Col. 12, 30, 2 : cinerem ex aceto, Plin. 30, 3, 8, § 26 : dentes, id. 28, 11, 49, § 178 : sal infricatus juvat, id. 31, 9, 45, § 100 : muscae infricatae, id. 30, 12, 34, § 108 .

infrĭcŏlo.opening: v. freq. a. infrico , to rub in repeatedly (late Lat.): oculum infricolato, Pelag. Veter. 31 fin.

infrictĭo.opening: infrico , a rubbing , friction : infrictionem ei membro adhibere, Cels. 8, 11 fin. dub. (al. frictionem).

in-frīgesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become cold (late Lat.), Veg. Vet. 3, 28 : cum infrixit, Cels. 5, 25, 4 .

infrīgĭdātĭo.opening: infrigido , a cooling (late Lat.): sudoris, Veg. Vet. 1, 29 : corporis, Isid. Orig. 4, 7, 25 .

in-frīgĭdo.opening: v. a. , to make cold or cool , to cool (late Lat.): caput, Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 1 med. : infrigidatus fuit, Vet. Schol. ad Juv. 7, 149 .

in-fringo.opening: v. a. infrango , to break off , to break , bruise , crack. Lit. : infractis omnibus hastis, Liv. 40, 40, 7 : ut si quis violas riguove papavera in horto Liliaque infringat, Ov. M. 10, 191 : genibusque tumens infringitur…

in-frĭo.opening: v. a. , to rub into , crumble into , strew upon : farinam in aquam, Cato, R. R. 156 : papaver, id. ib. 79 ; Cels. 7, 12 : seni papaverem, Varr. ap. Non. 220, 11 : ruta infriata, Plin. 20, 13, 51, § 140 .

in-frons.opening: adj. , without foliage , treeless , Ov. P. 4, 10, 31 .

in-frontātē.opening: adv. , impudently , Fulg. de Prisc. Serm. no. 22.

infructĭfĕrus.opening: adj. , bearing no fruit (eccl. Lat.), Ps.-Aug. ad Fr. Erem. 3 .

infructŭōsĭtas.opening: infructuosus , unfruitfulness , unproductiveness , uselessness (late Lat.): Judaica, Tert. Resurr. Carn. 33 .

in-fructŭōsus.opening: adj. , unfruitful (post-Aug.). Lit. : vites, Col. Arb. 8, 4 : cultura, id. 11, 2, 32 . — Trop. , fruitless , useless : preces, Plin. Ep. 8, 23 : epistula, Sen. Contr. 3, 19 fin. : militia, Tac. H. 1, 51 .— Adv. : ,…

infrūnītus.opening: adj. 2. in-fruniscor , unfit for enjoyment , tasteless , senseless , silly (post-Aug.): animus, Sen. Vit. Beat. 13, 23 : mulier, id. Ben. 3, 16 : copia, Macr. S. 5, 1 med. ; Vulg. Eccli. 31, 23 , and 23, 6.— , adv. : ,…

in-fūcātus.opening: adj. 2. in , not painted (late Lat.), Arn. 2, 75 .

infulgĕrat.opening: v. impers. , it lightens , Not. Tir. p. 118 .

infullōnĭcātus.opening: adj. 2. infullo , not fulled , ἄκναφος, Gloss. Philox.

in-fūmo.opening: v. a. , to smoke , dry in the smoke : asini cerebrum infumatum, smoked, smoke-dried, Plin. 28, 16, 63, § 225 ; 28, 11, 48, § 176 .

infundĭbŭlum.opening: ( , ), , infundo , a funnel (cf. infurnibulum). In gen., Col. 3, 18, 6 ; Cato, R. R. 10, 1 ; 11, 2 ; 13, 3 ; Pall. 7, 7 ; Vitr. 10, 10, 12 and 13 (infidibula). — In partic., the funnel in a mill, through which the grain…

in-fundo.opening: v. a. , to pour in , upon , or into (syn. invergere). Lit. : aliquid in aliquod vas, Cic. Tusc. 1, 25, 61 : vinum reticulo aut cribro, Sen. Ben. 7, 19 : aliquid in nares, Plin. 20, 17, 69, § 180 : sine riguis mare in…

infurnĭbŭlum.opening: in - furnus , a funnel for inhaling smoke : is nidor per infurnibulum imbibitur in tussi, Plin. 24, 15, 85, § 135 (Jahn and others read infundibulum; Gloss. Philox. infumibulum καπνοδόχη ).

in-fusco.opening: v. a. , to make dark or dusky , to darken , obscure. Lit. : humida fulmina non urunt sed infuscant, Plin. 2, 51, 52, § 137 : aquā infuscatā atramento, id. 9, 29, 45, § 84 ; Vict. Orig. Gentis R. 14: vellera, Verg. G. 3,…

in-fuscus.opening: adj. , dusky , dark brown , blackish : apes infusci coloris, Col. 9, 3, 1 ; 9, 10, 1 .

infūsor.opening: id. , one who pours in; trop.: fidei, Prud. Cath. 4, 11 .

infūsōrĭum.opening: infundo , a can , reservoir for a lamp , Vulg. Zach. 4, 2 .

infūsus.opening: infundo , a pouring in , an injection : sonitus auris emendat infusu, Plin. 24, 6, 15, § 24 (only in abl. ).

in-gĕmisco.opening: , 3. v. a. and n. , to groan or sigh over a thing. Act. With acc. and inf. : quid ingemiscis hostem Dolabellam judicatum, Cic. Phil. 13, 10, 23 : ingemuit citro non satis esse suo, Mart. 9, 59, 10 . — With acc. obj. :…

in-gĕmĭtus.opening: a groan : ingemitus, ἐπιστεναγμός, Gloss. Philox.

in-gemmesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become a jewel , Isid. 16, 14, 7 .

in-gĕmo.opening: v. a. and n. , to groan or sigh over a thing; to mourn over , lament , bewail. Act. : alicujus interitum, Verg. E. 5, 27 : caesos ingemunt nati patres, Sen. Herc. Oet. 1758 : jacentem, Stat. Th. 9, 2 .— With inf. :…

in-gĕnĕro.opening: v. a. To implant , engender , produce. Lit. : natura ingenerat amorem in eos qui, etc., Cic. Off. 1, 4, 12 : homini soli cupiditas ingeneratur, id. Fragm. ap. Non. 123, 5 : non ingenerantur hominibus mores, id. Agr. 2,…

ingĕnĭātus.opening: ( ), , adj. ingenium , naturally constituted , disposed or apt by nature : lepide ingeniatus, Plaut. Mil. 3, 1, 136 : primordia, Gell. 12, 1, 17 : ad astutiam, App. Flor. n. 18, p. 360, 20.

ingĕnĭŏlum.opening: dim. ingenium , a little genius , feeble intellect , Arn. 5, 157 ; Hier. adv. Ruf. 4 fin.

ingĕnĭōsus.opening: ( ), , adj. ingenium , intellectual , superior in intellect , endowed with a good capacity , gifted with genius , of good natural talents or abilities , clever , ingenious. Lit. : Aristoteles quidem ait, omnes…

ingĕnĭum.opening: in-geno, from gigno , innate or natural quality , nature. In gen. (so mostly poet. ; in Sall. and in postAug. prose; not in Cic. or Cæs.): pro ingenio ego me liberum esse ratus sum, pro imperio tuo tibi servire aequom…

ingens.opening: adj. 2. in-genus, gens, that goes beyond its kind or species, qs. uncouth, monstrous , of immoderate size , vast , huge , prodigious , enormous; great , remarkable : magnas vero agere gratias Thais mihi? Gn. Ingentes,…

ingĕnŭīlis.opening: adj. ingenuus , sincere , ingenuous : AVRELIVS, Inscr. ap. Grut. 538, 9.

ingĕnŭīnus.opening: adj. id. , that belongs to an ingenuus, Inscr. ap. Grut. 8, 7.

ingĕnŭus.opening: adj. ingeno, ingigno . Native , indigenous , not foreign. Lit. : fontes, Lucr. 1, 230 : tophus, produced in the country, Juv. 3, 20 .— Transf. , inborn , innate , natural : inest in hoc amussitata sua sibi ingenua…

in-gĕro.opening: v. a. ( imper. inger for ingere, Cat. 27, 2 ), to carry , pour , throw , or put into , in , or upon a place. Lit. In gen.: aquam ingere, Plaut. Ps. 1, 2, 24 : ligna foco, Tib. 2, 1, 22 : quicquid vini oleique erat,…

in-gestābĭlis.opening: adj. , that cannot be borne , insupportable : onus, Plin. 7, 6, 5, § 41 .

ingestĭo.opening: ingero , a pouring in , introduction : liquentis plumbi, Cod. Th. 9, 24, 1; Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 8, 152 .— An uttering : primae vocis, Mart. Cap. 5, § 459 .

in-gesto.opening: v. a. , to bear : votum, a dub. read. in App. M. 11, p. 264, 37 , where now intextas; v. Hildebr. ad h. l.

ingestus.opening: ingero , a presenting with , bestowment (late Lat.): immortalitatis, Tert. Res. Carn. 42 .

in-gigno.opening: v. a. , to instil by birth or nature , to implant , engender. Lit. : herbasque nocentes rupibus ingenuit tellus, Luc. 6, 439 : vites ingenita sterilitate, Col. 3, 7, 3 .— Trop. : natura cupiditatem nomini ingenuit, Cic.…

in-glŏmĕro.opening: v. a. , to heap together , accumulate : noctem, Stat. Th. 1, 351 .

in-glōrĭōsus.opening: adj. , = ἄδοξος, inglorious , without repute : gubernator, Plin. Ep. 9, 26, 4 ; Arn. in Psa. 130 .

inglōrĭus.opening: adj. 2. in-gloria , without glory or fame , not glorious , inglorious. Lit. (class.): beati qui honorati sunt videntur; miseri qui sunt inglorii, Cic. Leg. 1, 11, 32 : latam trahens inglorius alvum, Verg. G. 4, 94 :…

inglūtĭnātus.opening: adj. , not glued or fastened , = ἀκόλλητος, Gloss. Philox.

in-glūtio.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to swallow down , Isid. 4, 9, 9 .

inglŭvĭōsus.opening: adj. ingluvies , voracious , gluttonous , Paul. ex Fest. p. 112, 2 Müll.

in-grandesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to grow big , increase (post-Aug.): asinus, Col. 3, 6, 3 : sata, id. 2, 10, 15 : porrum, si jam ingranduit, id. 11, 3, 17 .

ingrātĭfĭcentĭa.opening: unthankfulness (eccl. Lat.), Fulg. Rusp. ad Monim. 3, 4 .

ingrātĭfĭcus.opening: adj. ingratusfacio , unthankful , ungrateful : Argivi, Att. ap. Cic. Sest. 57, 122 (Trag. Rel. v. 364 Rib.).

ingrātĭtūdo.opening: ingratus . Unthankfulness , ingratitude (late Lat. for animus ingratus), Firm. 5, 1 med. ; Cassiod. Var. 5, 8 .— Displeasure , Cassiod. Var. 1, 30 .

in-grātus.opening: adj. Unpleasant , disagreeable (class. in prose and poetry). Of things: bene quae in me fecerunt, ingrata habui, Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 30 : sin autem ingrata esse sentiam, Cic. Fam. 5, 5, 3 : fuit haec oratio non ingrata…

in-grăvātē.opening: adv. , not grudgingly , willingly (late Lat.), Amm. 17, 10 fin. ; 18, 2, 6 .

ingrăvātĭo.opening: ingravo , a load , burden (late Lat.), Cod. Th. 7, 13, 7.

in-grăvo.opening: v. a. ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). To weigh down : puppem, Stat. Th. 5, 402 .— Transf. To cause its weight to be felt , to oppress , molest : saevitia hiemis ingravat, Plin. 19, 8, 51, § 166 : annis ingravantibus,…

ingressĭo.opening: ingredior , a going into , entering (Ciceron.). Lit. : ab ingressione fori, entrance, Cic. Phil. 5, 4, 9 .— Transf. A gait , pace : interdum cursus est in oratione incitatior, interdum moderata ingressio, Cic. de Or.…

inguen.opening: (also late Lat. , , , Isid. 4, 6, 19 ), the front part of the body between the hips. Lit. The groin. — Sing. , Cels. 7, 20 : lentum destillat ab inguine virus, Verg. G. 3, 281 ; more freq. plur. : candida succincta…

inguĭnālis.opening: adj. inguen , of or belonging to the inguen: herba, Plin. 26, 9, 59, § 92 (al. ); App. Herb. 60 .

ingurgĭtātĭo.opening: ingurgito , immoderate eating and drinking , gormandizing , guzzling (late Lat.), Firm. 5, 8.

ingurgĭto.opening: v. a. in-gurges , to pour in like a flood or whirlpool. Lit. : merum ventri suo, App. M. 4, p. 145, 27 : vide ut avariter merum in se ingurgitat faucibus plenis, Plaut. Curc. 1, 2, 35 : umor ex nivibus non universus…

ingustābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-gusto , that cannot be tasted , not fit to be eaten or drunk : fons, Plin. 2, 106, 110, § 238 : bacae omnibus animantibus, id. 16, 26, 43, § 105 .

in-gustātus.opening: adj. id. , untasted , not tasted before : ilia rhombi, Hor. S. 2, 8, 30 .

in-gusto.opening: v. a. , to give to taste (late Lat.): Jovi sanguinem humanum, Tert. adv. Gnost. 7 .

in-hisco.opening: v. n. , i. q. inhio: inhisco ἐπιχαίνω, Gloss. Philox.

injectĭo.opening: inicio . A throwing in; lit., med. t. t., an injection , clyster , Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 4, 69 ; 5, 1, 10 ; id. Acut. 1, 17, 167 .— A laying on : manus, a laying on of the hand , an act by which one takes possession of a…

injecto.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to lay on , apply ( poet. ): dextram, Stat. Th. 9, 133 ; Sil. 3, 183 ; Luc. 3, 611 .

injectus.opening: inicio , a throwing or casting on or over. Lit. : opprimere senem injectu multae vestis, Tac. A. 6, 50 ; so Plin. 8, 16, 21, § 54 ; 8, 17, 21, § 60 : pulveris, id. 11, 17, 18, § 58 ; Stat. S. 4, 3, 22 .— Transf. , a…

injūcundĭtas.opening: injucundus , unpleasantness : ne quid habeat injucunditatis oratio, Cic. N. D. 2, 55, 138 .

in-jūcundus.opening: adj. Unpleasant (class.): minime nobis injucundus labor, Cic. Fin. 1, 1, 3 : rumor bonis, id. Q. Fr. 3, 8, 4 : odor, Plin. 25, 7, 36, § 74 : sonus vocis, Gell. 13, 20, 12 : schemata, Quint. 4, 5, 4 : non injucundus…

in-jūdĭcātus.opening: adj. 2. in-judico . Unsentenced , not formally tried by a judge : decem hominibus vitam eripis, indicta causa, injudicatis, incondemnatis, Cato ap. Gell. 13, 24, 12 .— Undecided : id injudicatum relinquo, Quint. 10, 1,…

in-jŭgātus.opening: adj. 2. in-jugo , not yoked , unyoked (late Lat.): taurus, Sid. Ep. 9, 16 in carm.

in-jŭgis.opening: adj. , not yoked , that has borne no yoke. Hostia, Macr. S. 3, 5 ; cf.: boves, qui sub jugo non fuerint, Paul. ex Fest. p. 113 Müll.; Fulg. p. 560, 33 .— Injuges versus, verses in which no connecting particle occurs (e.…

in-jūrātus.opening: adj. , unsworn , having taken no oath (class.; cf. injuro): injurato scio plus credet mihi quam jurato tibi, Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 281 ; cf.: cum id jurati dicunt quod ego injuratus insimulo, Cic. Caecin. 1, 3 ; so opp.…

injūrĭa.opening: injurius , any thing that is done contrary to justice and equity , injury , wrong , violence : injuria ex eo dicta est, quod non jure fiat! omne enim, quod non jure fit, injuria fieri dicitur: hoc generaliter.…

injūrĭor.opening: v. dep. injuria , to do an injury , to injure (post-Aug. and rare): omne fortuitum citra nos saevit atque injuriatur (a dub. reading), Sen. Const. 9, 1 .— Impers. : plus victoriatum est, quam injuriatum, Tert. adv.…

injūrĭōsus.opening: adj. injuria , acting unjustly , injurious , wrongful , criminal. Lit. : injuriosi in proximos, Cic. Off. 1, 14, 44 : injuriosa et facinorosa vita, id. Leg. 1, 14, 40 : appetitio alienorum (avaritia), Auct. Her. 4, 25,…

injūrĭus.opening: adj. 2. in-jus , that acts unlawfully , injurious , wrongful , unjust (mostly ante-class.): Scel. Quis igitur vocare? Phil. Δικαίᾳ nomen est. Scel. Injuria's, Plaut. Mil. 2, 5, 27 : injuria's qui, etc., id. Curc. 1, 1,…

in-jūro.opening: v. a. 2. in-juro , not to swear (very rare; cf. injuratus): qui injuraverit, Inscr. ap. Mar. Fratr. Arv. p. 70.

in-largĭo.opening: v. a. , to bestow , grant : pecuniam inlargibo tibi, Cato ap. Non. 470, 27 .

innābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-no , that cannot be swum in : unda, Ov. M. 1, 16 .

in-nōbĭlĭtātus.opening: adj. 2. in-nobilito , not ennobled , ignoble (late Lat.), Lampr. Elag. 4 .

in-nōmĭnātus.opening: adj. id. , unnamed , Sarisb. 2, 27; Don. Vit. Verg. 16 .

in-nūbĭlo.opening: v. a. , to cloud over , to overcast , make gloomy. Lit. , Sol. 53, 24 . — Trop. : serenitatem gaudii, Aug. Ep. 238 .

innūbis.opening: adj. 2. in-nubes , cloudless : dies, Sen. Herc. Oet. 238 .

in-nŭmĕrābĭlis.opening: adj. , countless , innumerable (class.): mundi, Cic. Ac. 2, 17, 55 ; 1, 10, 25 : atomi, id. N. D. 1, 20, 54 : homines, id. de Or. 2, 38, 142 : pecunia, id. Quint. 11, 37 : series annorum, Hor. C. 3, 30, 4 : numerus…

in-nŭmĕrus.opening: adj. , countless , innumerable , numberless. In gen. ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose; false reading instead of meri, Cic. de Or. 2, 22, 94 ; v. Orell. and Klotz): numerus, Lucr. 2, 1054 : scaena est deserta, dein Risus,…

in-nŭo.opening: v. n. , to give a nod , to nod to; to give a sign , to intimate , hint. With dat. : ubi ego innuero vobis, Plaut. Rud. 3, 4, 26 : abiens innuit mihi, Ter. Eun. 4, 5, 9 : stabat innuebat digito similis vocanti, Plin. Ep.…

in-nuptus.opening: adj. 2. in-nubo , unmarried. Lit. Adj. : pueri innuptaeque puellae, Verg. G. 4, 476 : Minerva, virginal, virgin-, id. A. 2, 31 : manus, the Amazons, Sil. 2, 75 .— Subst. : , , , an unmarried woman , a virgin , Cat. 62,…

in-nūtrībĭlis.opening: adj. , not nourishing : juscellum, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 9, 55 .

in-nūtrītus.opening: adj. 2. in-nutrio , not nourished , without nourishment , Cael. Aur. Acut. 17, 1, 17, § 177 .

in-quassātus.opening: adj. , unbroken : inquassatus, ἄθραυστος, Gloss. Philox.

inquĭlīnātus.opening: inquilinus , an inhabiting of a place which is not one ' s own , sojourning : inquilinatūs tempus, Tert. Anim. 38 fin. ; Sid. Ep. 5, 19 .

inquĭlīno.opening: v. a. id. , to be an inhabitant or sojourner : inquilino, ἐνοικέω, Gloss. Philox.
