insānībĭlis.opening: adj. insanio , insane , raging : furor, Lact. 4, 19 dub.

insānĭo.opening: ( imperf. : insanibat, Ter. Phorm. 4, 3, 37 ), , v. n. insanus , to be of unsound mind (syn.: furo, deliro, desipio). Lit. As a medic. t. t., to be mad , insane , of men, Cels. 3, 18, 66 ; 2, 7, 69 al. ; of animals,…

insānĭtas.opening: insanus , unsoundness , unhealthiness , disease : nomen insaniae significat mentis aegrotationem et morbum, id est insanitatem et aegrotum animum, Cic. Tusc. 3, 4, 8 : sapientia sanitas sit animi, insipientia autem…

in-sānus.opening: adj. , unsound in mind. Lit. , mad , insane (syn.: furiosus, fanaticus): quod idem contigit insanis, Cic. Ac. 2, 17, 52 : si fecisset Juno maritum insanum, Juv. 6, 620 . — Transf. , that acts like a madman , raging ,…

Insāni montes.opening: the insane mountains ( = τὰ μαινόμενα ὄρη ), i. e. absurdly high, Weissenb. (acc. to others, the raging or stormy mountains ), a range in the western part of Sardinia , Liv. 30, 39, 2 ; cf.: Sardiniam Gracchus arripuit.…

in-sarcĭo.opening: v. a. , to stuff in (late Lat.): nummos in calceos sibi, Porphyr. ad Hor. S. 1, 8, 39 .

in-sătĭābĭlis.opening: adj. That cannot be satisfied , insatiable : cupiditas, Cic. Tusc. 1, 19, 44 : gaudium, id. ib. 5, 25, 70 : crudelitas, id. Phil. 1, 3, 8 : humanus animus, Liv. 4, 13, 4 : acquirendi votum, Juv. 14, 125 . — With gen. :…

in-sătĭātus.opening: adj. , unsatisfied , insatiate : ardor eundi, Stat. Th. 6, 305 ; Prud. Psych. 478 .

in-sătĭĕtas.opening: insatiateness , greedy disposition : quorum animis avidis atque insatietatibus neque lex est, etc., Plaut. Aul. 3, 5, 13 .

in-sătŭrābĭlis.opening: adj. , insatiable : abdomen, Cic. Sest. 51, 110 ; with gen. : sanguinis humani, Oros. 3, 18 fin. — Adv. : , insatiably : annis praeteritis expleri, Cic. N. D. 2, 25, 64 .

in-sătŭrātus.opening: adj. , unsatisfied , insatiate : noverca insaturata odiis, Avien. Phaen. Arat. 183 .

in-saucĭātus.opening: adj. , not wounded, Ambros. Dign. Sacerd. 5 .

inscendo.grammar: scendi, scensum, 3 v. n. and a.
inscendo.opening: v. n. and a. [in-scando], to step into or upon , to climb up , mount , ascend. Lit. : cum inscenderet in rogum ardentem, Cic. Div. 1, 23, 47 : supra pilam inscendat, Cato, R. R. 127, 2 : quadrigas Jovis, Plaut. Am. 1,…

inscensĭo.opening: inscendo , a mounting , ascending : in navem inscensio, an embarking, Plaut. Rud. 2, 6, 19 .

inscensus.opening: inscendo , a mounting , i. e. covering : equarum, App. M. 7, p. 194, 17 .

in-scĭens.opening: adj. , unknowing. Without knowledge , unaware : si peccavi, insciens feci, Ter. Heaut. 4, 1, 19 : nihil me insciente esse factum, without my knowing it, Cic. Fam. 5, 2, 3 : saepe jam Plus insciens quis fecit quam…

in-scĭentĭa.opening: Want of knowledge , ignorance , inexperience (cf. inscitia init. ): in tantis tenebris erroris et inscientiae, Cic. Sull. 14, 40 : mea, id. de Or. 1, 46, 203 : alicujus, id. ib. 3, 35, 142 ; id. Ac. 2, 47, 146 .—With…

inscītĭa.opening: inscitus , ignorance , inexperience , unskilfulness , awkwardness , stupidity , stolidity in any thing (usu. with suggestion of blame; while inscientia is simply the absence of knowledge; but the distinction is…

inscītŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [inscitus], ignorant , awkward , unmannerly : ancillula, Afran. ap. Non. 12, 21 (Com. Fragm. v. 386 Rib.).

in-scītus.opening: adj. Ignorant , inexperienced , unskilful , silly , simple , stupid; freq. coupled with stultus (rare in Cic.; a favorite word of Plaut.), Plaut. Most. 1, 3, 51 : inscita atque stulta mulier, id. ib. 2, 3, 85 ; id. Mil.…

in-scĭus.opening: adj. , not knowing , ignorant of a thing (not used by Plaut. or Ter.; v. Ritschl, Proleg. p. 64 sq.; and cf. insciens); constr., absol. , with gen. , rarely with de , an acc. , an inf. , or a rel. clause (class.).…

in-scrībo.opening: v. a. , to write in or upon any thing, to inscribe (class.). Lit. : aliquid in basi tropaeorum, Cic. Pis. 38, 92 : in statua inscripsit, Parenti optime merito, id. Fam. 12, 3, 1 : nomen suum monumentis, id. Har. Resp.…

in-scriptĭlis.opening: adj. , that cannot be written , Diom. p. 413 P.

inscriptĭo.opening: inscribo , a writing upon , inscribing; an inscription , title (class.): nominis inscriptio, Cic. Dom. 20, 51 : quod de inscriptione quaeris, non dubito, quin καθῆκον officium sit; sed inscriptio plenior, de officiis,…

inscriptūra.opening: inscribo , an inscription (al. in scriptura), Tert. adv. Val. 30 .

in-scriptus.opening: adj. Unwritten : unde et illa divisio est, alia esse scripta, alia inscripta, Quint. 3, 6, 36 ; 7, 4, 36 .— Not marked or entered at the custom-house , contraband : inscriptum pecus, Varr. R. R. 2, 1, 16 .— Concerning…

in-scrūtābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-scrutor , inscrutable (eccl. Lat.): Dei judicia, Aug. Ep. 106, 4 ; Hilar. Trin. 8, 38.

in-scrūtor.opening: v. dep. , to search or examine into : si Homeri latentem prudentiam inscruteris altius (al. scruteris), Macr. S. 7, 1 .

in-sculpo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to cut or carve in or upon , to engrave. Lit. With dat. ( poet. and in postAug. prose): summam patrimonii saxo (shortly before, incidere), Hor. S. 2, 3, 90 : litteras tabellae, Quint. 1, 1, 27 : elogium…

insculptĭo.opening: insculpo , a cutting , carving (late Lat.), Jul. Val. 2, 28 .

in-sĕcābĭlis.opening: adj. , that cannot be cut up or divided , inseparable , indivisible (post-Aug.), Sen. Ep. 118 : corpora, i. e. atoms, Quint. 2, 17, 38 ; 3, 3, 13 .

in-sĕco.opening: v. a. , to cut into , cut up (class.): aliquid dentibus, Auct. Her. 4, 49, 62 : olivam acuta harundine, Col. 12, 47 : corpora mortuorum ad scrutandos morbos, to dissect, Plin. 19, 5, 26, § 86 : insecandi sunt favi, Col.…

insĕco.opening: or , , old form for , to pursue the narration , to proceed , relate , declare; so imper. : insece, Musa, Enn. ap. Gell. 18, 9, 3 (Ann. v. 332 Vahl.): virum mihi, Camena, insece versutum, Liv. Andr. ap. Gell. 18, 9, 5 ;…

insectanter.opening: adv. insector , harshly , bitterly (with graviter): vituperari, Gell. 19, 3, 1 .

in-sectātĭo.opening: id. , a pursuing , pursuit (class., but not in Cic. or Cæs.). Lit. : hostis, Liv. 21, 47, 2 .— Trop. , a pursuing with words , a censuring , railing at , deriding , insulting : tanta est hominum insolentia et nostri…

in-sectātor.opening: id. , a persecutor (very rare; not in Cic. or Cæs.). Lit. : plebis, Liv. 3, 33, 7 .— Trop. , a censurer : vitiorum, Quint. 10, 1, 129 .

insectĭo.opening: 2. inseco , a narration , i. q. narratio, acc. to a remark of Gell. 18, 9, 4 ; 11 .

insecto.opening: v. a. , a rare form for insector, to pursue (ante- and postclass.): nos insectabit lapidibus, Plaut. Capt. 3, 4, 61 .— Hence, pass. : insectatus, pursued , Auct. B. Afr. 71, 4.

insector.opening: v. dep. a. freq. [insequor], to pursue (class.). Lit. : impios agitant insectanturque furiae, Cic. Leg. 1, 14, 40 ; cf. id. Div. 2, 70, 144 : aliquem hastis, Plaut. Capt. 3, 4, 17 : aliquem verberibus, to pursue with…

in-sectūra.opening: [1. inseco), an incision , Sen. Q. N. 1, 7 .

in-sectus.opening: adj. 2. in-seco , for non sectus, Paul. ex Fest. p. 111 Müll.

in-sĕcundus.opening: adj. , not following , unyielding , uncomplying : secundus, insecundus, Not. Tir. 95 .

insĕcūtĭo.opening: insequor , a pursuing : incerta, App. M. 8, p. 208, 23 .

insĕcūtor.opening: id. , a pursuer , persecutor (post-class.), Tert. Mag. 5 : frustratis insecutoribus, App. M. 7 init.

in-sēdābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-sedo , that cannot be stayed or stilled , incessant : insedabilis, ἀκατάπαυστος, Gloss. Philox.— * Adv. : , unquenchably , incessantly : sitis arida, Lucr. 6, 1175 .

insēdūcĭbĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-seduco , not to be drawn away (eccl. Lat.), Anon. (Hilar.) in Job, 2, p. 188.

in-sēdŭlus.opening: adj. , not zealous : insedulus, ασπούδαστος, Gloss. Philox.

in-segnis.opening: adj. , inactive , indolent : insegnis, ἀδρανής, Gloss. Philox.

in-sĕmĕl.opening: adv. , at once , Flor. prooem. § 3; id. 2, 20, 1 ; Dig. 18, 1, 35, § 7 .

in-sēmĭno.opening: v. a. , to sow or plant in , to implant (post-Aug.): tabem et morbos visceribus, Gell. 19, 5, 3 : terra ex caelestium imbrium conceptionibus inseminata, impregnated, fertilized, Vitr. 8 praef. init. : ex conventu Jovis…

insēmĭtātĭo.opening: (2. in-semita], pathlessness , impassableness : insemitatio, ἀνοδία, Gloss. Philox.

insĕnescĭbĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-senesco , not growing old , undecaying : insenescibilis, ἀγήραος, ἀγήρατος, Gloss. Philox.

in-sĕnesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to grow old in or at a thing; constr. with dat. ( poet. and post-Aug. prose): insenuit Libris et curis, Hor. Ep. 2, 2, 82 : malis, Ov. P. 1, 4, 48 : singulis actionum partibus, Quint. 10, 3, 11 : iisdem…

in-sensātus.opening: adj. , irrational (eccl. Lat.), Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 43 al. — Adv. : , foolishly , Vulg. Sap. Sir. 12, 23 .

in-sensĭbĭlis.opening: adj. , that cannot be felt , insensible , imperceptible (post-class.). Pass. : morbus, Ser. Samm. 3, 2 . — As subst. : , , , things of no account , Lact. 2, 2, 17 ; 2, 5, 1 .— Things imperceptible , Apul. Asclep. 19, p.…

insensĭbĭlĭtas.opening: insensibilis , insensibility , Claud. Mam. Stat. An. 1, 3 ; Ambros. de Bono Mort. 7, 26 .

in-sensĭlis.opening: adj. , insensible , imperceptible , = insensibilis: principia, Lucr. 2, 866 ; 888 .

insensŭālĭtas.opening: insensualis , insensibility (eccl. Lat.), Aug. contr. Faust. 15, 4.

in-sēpărābĭlis.opening: adj. , that cannot be separated , inseparable (post-Aug.): quaedam inter se, Sen. Ep. 118, 85 : societas, Gell. 1, 9, 12 .— Comp. : trinitas inseparabilior, Aug. Trin. 15, 23 .— Adv. : , inseparably (post-class.), Macr.…

insēpărābĭlĭtas.opening: inseparabilis , inseparableness , inseparability (eccl. Lat.), Aug. Trin. 15, 23 : virtutum, id. Ep. 29, 2 .

in-sēpărātus.opening: adj. , not separate (eccl. Lat.), Tert. adv. Prax. 9 .

in-sĕpultus.opening: adj. 2. in-sepultus , unburied (class.): acervi civium, Cic. Cat. 4, 6, 11 : membra, Hor. Epod. 5, 99 : insepultos projecit, Liv. 29, 9, 10 . — Transf. , without burial : mors, Sen. Tranq. 14 : sepultura, a burial…

insĕquens.opening: Part. and P. a. , from insequor.

insĕquenter.opening: adv. , v. insequor, P. a. fin.

in-sĕquenter.opening: adv. 2. in-sequor , not in the proper order of succession , without connection , unconnectedly : particula posita, Gell. 10, 29, 4 .

in-sĕquor.opening: (quūtus), 3, v. dep. n. and a. , to follow , to follow after or upon a person or thing (class.). Lit. In gen.: proximus huic, longo sed proximus intervallo Insequitur Salius, Verg. A. 5, 321 : fugientem lumine pinum,…

in-sĕrābĭlĭter.opening: adv. 2. in-sera , so as not to be unlocked : obstruere, Auct. Itin. Alex. M. 100 Mai.

in-sĕrēnus.opening: adj. , not clear or serene , overcast : Hyas, Stat. S. 1, 6, 21 .

in-sĕro.opening: v. a. in-, 2. sero , to put , bring , or introduce into , to insert (class.); constr. with in and acc. , or with dat. Lit. In gen.: collum in laqueum, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 17, § 37 ; id. de Or. 2, 39, 162 : oculos in…

in-serpo.opening: v. n. , to crcep on or over any thing; only trop.; constr. with dat. ( poet. and post-class.): jam somnus avaris Inserpit curis, Stat. Th. 1, 340 : ei lanugo malis inserpebat, covered over his cheeks, App. M. 7, p. 189…

inserta.opening: 2. insero , an ornament (very rare): frugalitas inserta est rumoris boni, Macr. S. 2, 7 .

insertātĭo.opening: inserto , an inserting , Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 1, 43 .

insertīcĭus.opening: adj. 2. insero , that can be inserted : inserticius, ἐγκεντρήσιμος, ἐντάξιμος, Gloss. Philox.

insertĭo.opening: 2. insero , a putting in , ingrafting , grafting (post-class.), Isid. Orig. 17, 6, 2 : oleastri, Aug. Ep. 120, 20 : surculorum, Macr. S. 1, 7, 25 .

insertīvus.opening: adj. id. , inserted , ingrafted; only trop. (very rare): stirps, i. e. an illegitimate posterity, Calp. Decl. 24 : liberi, Phaedr. 3, 3, 10 .

inserto.opening: v. a. freq. [id.], to put into , insert; with dat. ( poet. and post - Aug.): clipeoque sinistram Insertabam aptans, Verg. A. 2, 672 : dextras catenis, Stat. Th. 12, 460 : insertans commissuris secures, Petr. 97 .

in-servĭo.opening: (archaic forms, inservibas, Plaut. Most. 1, 3, 59 : inservibat, Sil. 7, 341 ), v. n. and (rarely) a. , to be serviceable , to be devoted or attached to , to be submissive to , to serve (syn.: deservio, ministro); with…

in-servo.opening: v. a. To attend to , observe (a favorite word of Statius): gemit, inservante noverca, Liber, Stat. Th. 10, 886 : volucres, id. ib. 8, 194 : fata, id. ib. 6, 935 .— To keep : sagittae volitantes vires integras…

insessĭo.opening: insideo , a sitting down (late Lat.): hostium insessio, id est hostilis circundatio, Cassiod. in Psa. 21, 12 .

insessor.opening: id. , a besetter , occupant (very rare); of a ship, Jul. Val. Res Gest. Alex. 1, 1 : viarum, a waylayer, Symm. Ep. 2, 48 ; cf.: insessores, latrones, Paul. ex Fest. p. 111 Müll.: quod circa vias insidientur sedentes.

in-sessus.opening: adj. 2. in-sedeo , unsettled , without a permanent dwelling : gentes, Sic. Fl. de Cond. Agr. p. 3.

insībĭlātor.opening: insibilo , one that breathes in by hissing (late Lat.): venenorum insibilator serpens, Aug. in Joh. 8, 6 .

in-sībĭlo.opening: v. n. and a. , to hiss , whistle , or rustle in ( poet. ): Eurus, Ov. M. 15, 603 : ignis membris, Sil. 12, 616 : Erinys atros insibilat ore tumores, hisses in, breathes in, with a hissing noise, id. 2, 626 .

in-siccābĭlis.opening: adj. , that cannot be dried , Sid. Ep. 9, 16 .

in-siccātus.opening: adj. , undried , not dried up (only in Statius): vulnera cruore, Stat. Th. 3, 364 : cruor, id. ib. 8, 246 .

insĭcĭa.opening: , and ( ), , inseco , stuffing , force-meat , a dish of minced meat (very rare). Form insicia, Varr. L. L. 5, § 110 Müll.— Form insicium, Macr. S. 7, 8 ; Arn. 2, 92 .

insĭcĭārĭus.opening: insicia , a forcemeat-maker , Hier. in Ruf. 1, 4 .

insĭcĭātus.opening: or , , adj. id. , stuffed with force-meat : pullus, Apic. 8, 7 .

insĭcĭŏlum.opening: or , , dim. insicium , a little force-meat (post-class.): porcina, Apic. 2, 2 ; 5, 3 .

insĭdĕo.grammar: sēdi, sessum, 2 v. n. and a.
insĭdĕo.opening: v. n. and a. [in-sedeo], to sit in or upon any thing; mostly with dat. (class.). Neutr. Lit. : equo, Liv. 7, 6, 5 : curru insidens, Sen. Med. 29 : solo, Suet. Aug. 82 .— To settle : ubi Lydia quondam jugis insedit…

insĭdĭae.opening: plur. (in sing. insidia prima, Sall. Fragm. ap. Charis. p. 75 P.) [insideo], an ambush , ambuscade (class.). Lit Of persons: qui sustinuerant primos impetus insidiarum, Hirt. B. G. 8, 19 : equites procedere longius…

insĭdĭanter.opening: adv. insidior , craftily , artfully , insidiously : insidianter speculati (al. insidiantes), Just. 6, 6 .

insĭdĭātor.opening: id. , a soldier lying in ambush , Hirt. B. G. 8, 18 .— Transf. , one who lies in wait , a lurker , waylayer (rare but class.): viae, Cic. Cat. 2, 12, 27 : in foro collocatur, id. Mil. 7, 19 : imperii, Nep. Reg. 2 .

insĭdĭātrix.opening: adj. insidiator , that lies in wait : manus, Amm. 24, 4 .

insĭdĭor.opening: v. dep. ( act. form insidiaverint for insidiati erunt, Dig. 48, 19, 28, § 11 ) [insidiae], to lie in ambush , lie in wait for; constr. with dat. Lit. : quam diu mihi, Catilina, insidiatus es, Cic. Cat. 1, 5, 11 : apris,…

insĭdĭōsus.opening: adj. insidiae , cunning , artful , deceitful , dangerous , insidious (class.). Of persons: quis insidiosior unquam fuit? Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 78, § 192 . — Of inanim. and abstr. things: Capraria insidiosa naufragiis, Plin.…

in-sīdo.opening: ( perf. insidi, Amm. 28, 6, 4 ), , v. n. and a. , to sit down in or on , to settle on; constr. with dat. ( poet. and post-Aug.). Lit. In gen.: apes floribus insidunt, Verg. A. 6, 708 : inscia Dido, Insidat quantus…

insigne.opening: insignis , a mark , sign , signal; a distinctive mark , a badge of office (class.). Lit. : quod erat insigne, eum facere, etc., Cic. de Or. 3, 33, 133 : Minerva singulare est insigne ejus gymnasii, id. Att. 1, 4, 3 :…

insignĭārĭus.opening: insigne , a keeper of insignia : insigniarius, ὁπλοπάροχος, Gloss. Philox.

in-signĭfĭcātīvus.opening: (sc. modus) [2. in-significo], the insignificative , a name given by some grammarians to the infinitive , Diom. p. 331 P.

insignĭo.opening: ( imperf. insignibat, Verg. A. 7, 790 ; Stat. Th. 7, 56 ), v. a. insignis , to put a mark upon , to mark; to distinguish (mostly post-Aug.): pueri insigniti, marked with some bodily defect , Plaut. Fragm. ap. Fest. p.…

insignis.opening: adj. in-signum , distinguished by a mark; remarkable , noted , eminent , distinguished , prominent , extraordinary (class.): insignes appellantur boves, qui in femine et in pede album habent, quasi insigniti, Paul. ex…

insignītē.opening: adv. , v. insignio, P. a. fin.

insignītor.opening: insignio , an engraver (late Lat.), Aug. Civ. Dei , 21, 4.

insignītus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from insignio.

in-signo.opening: v. a. , to engrave : insigno, ἐγχαράσσω, Gloss. Philox.

insĭlĭa.opening: plur. [insilio], the treadle of a weaver's loom, Lucr. 5, 1353 .

insĭlĭo.opening: (insilivi, Liv. 8, 9, 9 : insilii, Claud. ap. Ruf. 1, 349 ; imperf. insilibat, Gell. 9, 11, 7 ), , v. n. in-salio , to leap into or upon , to spring at; constr. with in and acc. , with the simple acc. , with dat. , or…

in-sĭmul.opening: adv. , at the same time (postAug.; first in Statius), Stat. S. 1, 6, 36 (in Flor. 2, 20, 1 , read insemel).

insĭmŭlātĭo.opening: ( ), , insimulo , a charge against one, an accusation (class.): in falsam atque iniquam probrorum insimulationem vocabatur, Cic. Font. 13, 29 : criminis, Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 9, § 23 : falsae, App. M. 10, p. 253, 19 .

insĭmŭlātor.opening: ( ), , id. , an accuser (post-class.), App. Mag. p. 293, 37 ; Pacat. Pan. Theod. 43 .

insĭmŭlātus.opening: adj. 2. in-simulo , undisguised , unfeigned (eccl. Lat.), Vulg. Sap. 18, 16 .

in-sĭmŭlo.opening: v. a. , to make a plausible charge (true or false) against a person before a tribunal; to make suspected , charge , accuse , blame , esp. falsely; to invent a charge or bear false witness against (syn.: accuso, incuso,…

in-sincērus.opening: adj. , not genuine , not pure , adulterated , spoiled; not honest or candid , insincere ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : cruor, Verg. G. 4, 285 : acies, imperfect, Prud. Ham. 4 .— Trop. : philosophus, Gell. 5, 3,…

insĭnŭātĭo.opening: insinuo , an entrance through a narrow or crooked way. Lit. : Ponti, Avien. Perieg. 397 .— Trop. An insinuating or ingratiating one ' s self into the favor of others : exordium in duas partes dividitur, in principium et…

insĭnŭātor.opening: id. , an introducer (eccl. Lat.): deorum, Tert. ad Nat. 2, 1 .

insĭnŭātrix.opening: insinuator , she that introduces or makes known (eccl. Lat.): rei novae, Aug. Ep. 110, 1 .

in-sĭnŭo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
in-sĭnŭo.opening: v. a. and n. Act. Lit. , to put , place , or thrust into the bosom (post-class.): sicine vacuus et otiosus insinuatis manibus ambulabis, with folded arms, App. M. 9, p. 219, 23 : manum in sinum, Tert. Res. Carn. 28 .—…

in-sĭpĭdus.opening: adj. 2. in-sapidus , tasteless , insipid (late Lat.): sapor, Firm. Math. 2, 12; Paul. Nol. Ep. 39, 4 .

in-sĭpĭens.opening: ( , Schol. Bob. ad Cic. Sest. 53 ; p. 304, 16 Bait.), , adj. 2. in-sapiens , unwise , senseless , foolish (class.): sed ego insipiens nova nunc facio, Plaut. Cas. 5, 2, 4 : insipiens fortunatus, Cic. Lael. 15, 54 :…

insĭpĭentĭa.opening: insipiens , want of wisdom , senselessness , folly (class.): ita fit, ut sapientia sanitas sit animi, insipientia autem quasi insanitas quaedam, quae est insania eademque dementia, Cic. Tusc. 3, 5, 10 ; 3, 28, 68 ;…

insĭpo.opening: ( pres. pass. insipitur, Varr. L. L. 5, § 105 Müll.), , v. a. , to throw in (ante-class.), Cato, R. R. 85 : ligna, Pompon. ap. Non. 10 , n. 3 (Com. Fragm. v. 50, 86 Rib.).

in-sisto.opening: v. n. , to set foot upon , to stand , tread , or press upon; constr. mostly with dat. , also with in and abl. or acc. , or the simple acc. (class.). Lit. In gen. With dat. : nec desunt villae quae secutae fluminis…

insĭtīcĭus.opening: adj. insitio , that is inserted , ingrafted (ante-class. and postAug.); hence, trop.: somnus, that is inserted between the occupations of the day, a noon-day nap, siesta, Varr. R. R. 1, 2, 5 : muli, produced from two…

insĭtĭo.opening: 1. insero . An ingrafting , grafting : nec consitiones modo delectant, sed etiam insitiones, Cic. de Sen. 15, 54 ; Col. 3, 9, 6 .— That which is ingrafted : insitionem nutrire, Pall. 5, 2 ; Col. Arb. 8, 3 .— The time of…

insĭtĭum.opening: id. , a putting in , insertion : insitium, ἔνθεσις, Gloss. Philox.

insĭtīvus.opening: adj. id. , ingrafted , grafted ( poet. and post - Aug.). Lit. : pira, Hor. Epod. 2, 19 .— Trop. , substituted , spurious : liberi, Phaedr. 3, 3, 10 : heres, adopted, Sen. Contr. 2, 8 : alimentum lactis, of another…

insĭtor.opening: id. , an ingrafter , grafter , Prop. 4 (5), 2, 17 ; Plin. 18, 33, 76, § 329 .

Insĭtor.opening: the god that presides over grafting , Serv. ad Verg. G. 1, 21 .

insĭtus.opening: (only in the abl. sing. ), 1. insero , an ingrafting , Plin. 15, 14, 15, § 52 .

Insochi.opening: a people of Armenia , Tac. A. 13, 37 (dub.; al. Moschi).

in-sŏcĭābĭlis.opening: adj. , that cannot be joined together , unsociable , incompatible (mostly post-Aug.): gens, Liv. 37, 1 : diversae, insociabilesque naturae arborum, Plin. 17, 19, 30, § 137 : anum insociabilem nurui efficiebat, Tac. A.…

in-sŏcĭālis.opening: adj. , for insociabilis, unsociable (late Lat.): inconcinna, insocialis, Porphyr. ad Hor. Ep. 1, 18, 6 .

in-sōlābĭlĭter.opening: adv. 2. in-solor , inconsolably : dolere, Hor. Ep. 1, 14, 8 .

insōlātĭo.opening: insolo , a setting or placing in the sun : cerae, Plin. 21, 14, 49, § 84 .

insōlātus.opening: Part. and P. a. of insolo.

in-sŏlens.opening: adj. 2. in-soleo . In gen., i. q. insuetus, contrary to custom , unaccustomed to a thing; unusual , not in use (class.); constr. absol. , or with gen. : quid tu Athenas insolens? Ter. And. 5, 4, 4 : mutatos deos flebit…

in-sŏlentĭa.opening: insolens . A being unaccustomed to a thing, unusualness , novelty; with gen. (class.). In gen.: fori, judiciorumque, Cic. Rosc. Am. 31, 88 : itineris, Sall. J. 94, 2 : loci, Cic. Deiot. 2, 5 : voluptatum, id. Cael. 31,…

in-sŏleo.opening: v. n. , to be wont , i. q. soleo, Caecil. ap. Gell. 3, 16, 4 dub. (perh. solet).

insŏlesco.opening: v. inch. n. [insolens], to become unusual or strange. Lit. , of the voice, to begin to change , to become manly : coepit Caelo vox insolescere, Tert. ad Nat. 2, 12 ; of the womb: uterus insolescens, i. e. swelling up,…

in-sŏlĭdus.opening: adj. , not solid , soft , tender : herba, Ov. M. 15, 203 .

insŏlĭtē.opening: adv. , v. insolitus, a, um, fin.

in-sŏlĭtus.opening: adj. , unaccustomed , unusual (class.). Act. , unaccustomed to a thing; constr. absol. , with ad or with gen. Absol. : cur pudentissimas feminas in tantum virorum conventum insolitas, invitasque prodire cogis? Cic.…

in-sollĭcĭtus.opening: adj. , unconcerned , careless : insollicitus dies, ἀμνήμονος ἡμέρα (dub.; perh. ἀμέριμνος ), Gloss. Philox.

in-sōlo.opening: v. a. in-sol , to place in the sun , i. e. expose to the sun , in order to warm, dry, etc. (a favorite word with Columella): uvas, Col. 12, 39, 2 : insolati dies, sunny, sunshiny days, id. 11, 3, 51 : humus insolatur,…

in-sŏlūbĭlis.opening: adj. , that cannot be loosed , indissoluble (post-Aug.). Lit. : vinculum, Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 6, § 24 : colligatio, id. ib. § 28.— Trop. That cannot be paid : beneticium, creditum insolubile est, Sen. Ben. 4, 12, 1 .—…

in-sŏlūtus.opening: adj. , not solved : quaestio, Aug. Civ. Dei , 15, 23, 1.

insomnĭa.opening: ( plur. , , Plin. 20, 9, 33, § 82 ; Prop. 2, 25, 47 ; Val. Fl. 1, 329 ; 7, 6 ; 2, 140 ) [insomnis], sleeplessness , want of sleep (class.): consequitur comes insomnia, Caecil. ap. Non. 209, 15 : aut mox noctu te adiget…

insomnĭĕtas.opening: id. , for insomnia, sleeplessness (late Lat.), Theod. Prisc. 2, 1 ; Plin. Val. 1, 35 .

insomnĭōsus.opening: adj. insomnia , sleepless , troubled with want of sleep , Cato, R. R. 157, 8 .

in-somnis.opening: adj. 2. in-somnus , sleepless ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Of living beings, Hor. C. 3, 7, 8 : juventus, Pers. 3, 54 : insomnes magis, quam pervigiles, Tac. A. 1, 65 : draco, Ov. M. 9, 190 .— Of things: oculi, Stat.…

in-sŏno.opening: v. n. , to make a noise in or on , to sound , sound loudly , resound (mostly poet. ): Boreae cum spiritus alto Insonat Aegaeo, roars on the Ægean Sea, Verg. A. 12, 366 : insonuere cavernae, id. ib. 2, 53 : caeli delapsa…

in-sons.opening: adj. Guiltless , innocent; constr. with gen. or absol. (class., but not in Cic. or Cæs.): insontem probri accusare, Plaut. Am. 3, 1, 9 : aliquem falso atque insontem arguere, id. Bacch. 3, 3, 10 : publici consilii, Liv.…

in-sŏnus.opening: adj. , without sound , noiseless , silent (post-class.). Lit. : passus, Amm. 27, 12 ; cf. gressus, id. 29, 5 : vestigium, App. M. 3, p. 138, 22 .— Transf. : litterae, i. e. mutae, App. de Mundo, p. 66, 29.

in-sōpībĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-sopio , that cannot be lulled to sleep (post-class.): flamma, i. e. inextinguishable, Mart. Cap. 1, § 7 : ignis, id. 9, § 910 .

in-sōpītus.opening: adj. , not lulled to sleep , sleepless , wakeful ( poet. ): draco, Ov. M. 7, 36 ; Luc. 9, 357 : ignis, inextinguishable, Claud. Rapt. Pros. 3, 401 .

in-sordesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become dirty or foul (post-class.), Sid. Ep. 5, 13 .— Esp., to become gloomy , to darken , Sid. Ep. 2, 2 ; Rutil. Itin. 1, 617 .

in-sortītus.opening: adj. , not allotted : spicula insortita (al. specula in sortitu), Plaut. Cas. 2, 4, 27 .

in-spătĭor.opening: v. dep. n. , to walk about in a place: inspatiantem (al. exspatiantem), Prud. Apoth. 130 .

in-spĕcĭātus.opening: adj. , unshapen : substantia informis et inspeciata (late Lat.), Tert. adv. Val. 10 fin.

in-spĕcĭōsus.opening: adj. , unshapely , ugly : puer, Petr. Fragm. Trag. 74, 8 Burm.

inspectābĭlis.opening: adj. inspecto , worth looking at , glorious : victoria, Gell. 4, 18, 2 .

inspectātĭo.opening: inspecto , a looking into , considering (post-Aug.).— Lit. : Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 17 ; 4, 35 (in Sen. Q. N. 1, 7, 3 , read inseptiones).

inspectātor.opening: id. , for inspector, an overseer (late Lat.), Symm. Ep. 6, 9 .

inspectĭo.opening: inspicio , a looking into , inspection (post-Aug.). Lit. In gen.: ager prima inspectione neque vitia, neque virtutes abditas ostendit, Col. 1, 4, 1 : speculi non tam possessio culpatur quam inspectio, App. Mag. 13, p.…

inspectīvus.opening: adj. inspectio , considering , reflecting , contemplative (postclass.): pars rationis philosophiae (opp. actualis), Isid. Orig. 2, 24 .

inspecto.opening: v. freq. a. inspicio , to look at , observe , view (class. only in part. pres. ): aliquid, Plaut. Poen. 3, 3, 69 : nescio quis inspectavit per impluvium, id. Mil. 2, 2, 18 : me inspectante, before my eyes, Cic. Fam. 1,…

inspector.opening: id. . A viewer , observer (post-Aug.), Sen. Ben. 1, 9, 3 .— An inspector , examiner (late Lat.), Dig. 13, 6, 10 ; Cod. Th. 11, 1, 31; Mos. et Rom. Leg. Coll. 15, 1, 2 al.

inspectrix.opening: inspector , she that inspects or examines (late Lat.), Ambros. Ep. 5 .

inspectus.opening: inspicio . A looking at , inspection , an examination (postAug.): jecoris, Amm. 22, 1, 25 .— Contemplation : animus liber ad inspectum, oculis inspectu minacibus, App. M. 10, p. 254, 26 : universi, Sen. Ep. 92, 6 .

in-spērābĭlis.opening: adj. , that cannot be hoped for (post-class.): pax, Gell. 4, 18, 3 : nuntius, Amm. 15, 5, 17 .

in-spērans.opening: adj. (usually in the oblique cases), not hoping , not expecting , contrary to one ' s hopes or expectations (class.): insperanti mihi, sed valde optanti cecidit, ut, Cic. de Or. 1, 21, 96 : quibus tu salutem…

inspērātē.opening: and , advv. , v. insperatus, a, um, fin.

in-spērātus.opening: adj. , unhoped for , unexpected (class.).—Of inanim. and abstr. things: insperata accidunt magis saepe, quam quae speres, Plaut. Most. 1, 3, 40 : insperatum et repentinum praesidium, Cic. Phil. 10, 11, 24 :…

inspergo.opening: (also , Plin. 18, 11, 29, § 115 ; and insparsus, id. 26, 14, 87, § 140 ), , v. a. in-spargo , to sprinkle or scatter into or upon; to sprinkle (class.). Lit. : molam ac vinum, Cic. Div. 2, 16, 37 .—With dat. : farinam…

inspersĭo.opening: inspergo , a sprinkling or scattering upon , inspersion (late Lat.): cineris, Pall. 4, 9, 13 .

inspersus.opening: inspergo , a sprinkling upon , inspersion (post-class.; only in abl. sing. ), App. M. 7, p. 197, 35 ; id. ib. 9 , p. 231, 5.

inspĭcĭo.opening: v. a. inspecio , to look into; to look at , inspect; to consider , contemplate , examine (class.). Lit. In gen.: intro inspice, Plaut. Bacch. 4, 4, 72 : inspicere tanquam in speculum, in vitas omnium, Ter. Ad. 3, 3, 61…

inspĭcĭum.opening: inspicio , a looking into , inspection (late Lat.): extorum, Tert. Carm. adv. Marc. 1, 12 .

in-spīco.opening: v. a. , to cleave , split (i. q. incīdere): faces (i. e. ligna in usum facium ita incidere, ut multis incisuris dividantur), Verg. G. 1, 292 (cf.: novas incidere faces, id. E. 8, 29 ).

inspīrāmentum.opening: inspiro , for inspiratio, an inspiration , Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 13, 150 .

inspīrātĭo.opening: id. , inspiration (late Lat.): litteraria, Sol. 7, 23 : divina, Tert. de Patient. 1 .

inspīrātor.opening: id. , an inspirer : furoris, Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 5, 144 ; and , id. , Jul. ap. Aug. contr. Sec. Resp. Jul. 198.

in-spīro.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
in-spīro.opening: v. a. and n. , to blow into or upon a thing; to breathe into , inspire ( poet. and post-Aug.). Lit. , to blow into; with the simple acc. : foramen, Plin. 10, 29, 43, § 84 .— To blow upon; with abl. : fistulā sensim…

in-splendesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to shine into , illuminate : insplendesco, ἐνλάμπω, Gloss. Philox.

in-spŏlĭātus.opening: adj. , not plundered ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): occi sus est non praedae gratiā, quia inspoliatus est, Quint. 7, 1, 33 ; Sen. Contr. 5, 30 : arma, Verg. A. 11, 594 .

in-spūmo.opening: v. n. , to foam , rage (late Lat.): O impiae voces! infrendite, inspumate, etc., Tert. Apol. 12 .

in-spŭo.opening: v. n. and a. , to spit into or upon (post-Aug.). Neutr. : alicui in frontem mediam, Sen. Ira, 3, 38 : in faciem alicujus, id. Cons. ad Helv. 13 .— Act. : aliquid oculis jumentorum, Plin. 31, 9, 45, § 105 ; cf. id. 22,…

in-spurco.opening: v. a. , to defile : utrum illum pecunia purum effecit, an ipse pecuniam inspurcavit, Sen. Ep. 87, 16 .

in-spūto.opening: v. a. freq. [inspuo], to spit upon : ain' eum mihi esse morbum, ut qui med opus sit insputarier? ... quibus insputari saluti fuit, Plaut. Capt. 3, 4, 21 ; 43 .

in-stăbĭlĭo.opening: v. a. , to fortify , Hyg. de Munit. Castr. § 54.

in-stăbĭlis.opening: adj. , that does not stand fast , unsteady , unstable , tottering , not firm (mostly poet. ; syn. varius, mutabilis, vagus; not in Cic.). Lit. : sic erat instabilis tellus, Ov. M. 1, 16 : locus ad gradum instabilis,…

instăbĭlĭtas.opening: instabilis , unsteadiness , instability (post-Aug.; syn. inconstantia): mentis, Plin. 24, 17, 102, § 162 .

in-stagno.opening: v. n. , to overflow , Not. Tir. p. 183 .

instantĭa.opening: insto . Lit. , a being near or close upon , hence presence : futura quorum consequenti tempore vera erit instantia, ea vera dicimus, Cic. Fat. 12, 27 B. and K.: infestus dicitur ab instantia atque imminentia fraudis,…

instar.opening: perh. in and root sta-; cf. Gr. ἵστημι, στήλη, etc. . A sketch , image , resemblance , likeness , kind , manner : parvum instar eorum, quae, etc., Liv. 28, 17, 2 .— Ad instar, or simply instar. According to the likeness…

instaurātīcĭus.opening: ( ), , adj. instauro , renewed , repeated (postclass.): dies, the day when the games are repeated, Macr. S. 1, 11, 5 .

instaurātĭo.opening: id. , a renewing , renewal , repetition : ludorum, Auct. Har. Resp. 11; Liv. 2, 36 : templorum, restoration, Eum. Pan. ad Const. 20 : pugnae, Gell. 15, 18, 2 : causae, Paul Sent. 5, 5, a. 10.

instaurātīvus.opening: adj. instauro , renewed , repeated : ludi, Cic. Div. 1, 26, 55 .

instaurātor.opening: id. , a renewer , restorer (post-class.): moenium, Inscr. ap. Reines. 2, 31; Amm. 27, 3, 5 .

in-stauro.opening: v. a. staurus, obs., = Gr. σταυρός, a paling, stake; cf. Sanscr. sthavaras, firm; root stare, ἵστημι , to renew , repeat , celebrate anew; to repair , restore; to erect , make (syn.: renovo, integro; class.): Latinas,…

in-sterno.opening: v. a. To cover , cover over : instrata cubilia fronde, Lucr. 5, 987 ; so, instratos ostro, Verg. A. 7, 277 ; cf.: si palo adacto caverna paleā insternatur, Plin. 19, 5, 26, § 84 : pontes altos, Verg. A. 12, 675 .—…

instīgātĭo.opening: instigo , an urging , stimulating , instigating , an incitement , instigation : auditorum, Auct. Her. 2, 30, 47 : novercalibus instigationibus corrupti, Dig. 5, 2, 4 : praedonum, Lact. 5, 19, 2 .

instīgātor.opening: id. , a stimulator , instigator (post-Aug.): sibi quisque dux et instigator, Tac. H. 1, 38 : superfluus, Aus. Ep. 17 fin. : accusationis, Dig. 3, 2, 20 .

instīgātrix.opening: instigator , she that instigates (post-Aug.): acerrima adversum Galbianos, Tac. H. 1, 51 .

instīgātus.opening: instigo , an instigation , setting on : si instigatu alterius fera damnum dederit, Dig. 9, 1, 1, § 6 .

instīgo.opening: v. a. from in and stigo (unused), cf. Gr. στίζω; Sanscr. tig, tij, to be sharp; cf. stimulus for stig-mulus, stilus for stig-lus , to urge , stimulate , stir up , set on , incite , instigate (class.): si hic non insanit…

instillātĭo.opening: instillo , a dropping in , instillation : lactis, Plin. 29, 6, 39, § 133 ; Pall. Nov. 10 .

instillo.opening: v. a. , to pour in by drops , to drop in , to instil (class.). Lit. : haec quoque, nisi tamquam lumini, oleum instilles, extinguuntur senectute, Cic. de Sen. 11 : (oleum) caulibus. Hor. S. 2, 2, 62 : auribus sucum…

instĭmŭlātor.opening: instimulo , a stimulator , instigator : seditionis (al. stimulator), Cic. Dom. 5, 11 .

in-stĭmŭlo.opening: v. a. , to prick or urge on , to stimulate ( poet. ): aliquem, Ov. F. 6, 508 : verbis, id. M. 14, 495 ; Stat. Th. 1, 715 : voce, Sil. 2, 543 : falso instimulari, Dig. 5, 2, 3 .

instinctor.opening: instinguo , an instigator (post-Aug.): sceleris, Tac. H. 1, 22 : belli, id. ib. 4, 68 ; Amm. 21, 12 ; 30, 1 .

instinctus.opening: instinguo , instigation , impulse (class.; mostly in abl. sing. ): oracula, quae instinctu divino afflatuque funduntur, inspiration, Cic. Div. 1, 18, 34 ; id. ib. 1, 6 fin. ; 1. 31, 66: sine caelesti aliquo mentis…

in-stinguo.opening: v. a. , to instigate , incite , impel (class. only in the part. pass. ): Christus intus instinxerat, Tert. Anim. 26 ( Gell. 17, 20, 7 , read instrinxit).— Part. pass. : , , instigated , incited : furore et audaciā, Cic.…

in-stīpo.opening: v. a. , to stuff into (anteand post-class.): vinum in culleum, Cato, R. R. 113 ; Marc. Emp. 10 .

in-stĭpŭlor.opening: v. dep. , to bargain , stipulate for (Plautinian): dolo malo, Plaut. Rud. 5, 3, 25 (but id. Ps. 4, 6, 7 , est stipulatus, Ritschl).

instĭta.opening: insisto . The border or flounce (laid in several plaits) of a Roman lady ' s tunic ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): quarum subsutā talos tegit instita veste, Hor. S. 1, 2, 29 : longa, Ov. Am. 1, 32 : nulla, i. e. no…

instĭtĭo.opening: id. , a standing still : errantium stellarum, Cic. Tusc. 1, 25, 62 .

instĭtĭum.opening: id. , = institio, a standing still , Kalend. ap. Grut. 138.

instĭto.opening: , a false read. for instare, Caes. B. G. 1, 25 .

instĭtor.opening: insisto , a person who sells goods for another , a factor , broker , agent; a huckster , hawker , peddler (cf.: circulator, negotiator): amata nautis multum et institoribus, Hor. Epod. 17, 20 : mercis, Liv. 22, 25 :…

instĭtōrĭus.opening: adj. institor , of or relating to institores (post-Aug.). Adj. : operae, Suet. Ner. 21 : artes, Hier. ap. Helv. 21: actio, Dig. 14, 3 ; Gai. Inst. 4, 71 ; 74 .— Subst. : , , , a female broker or huckster , Dig. 14, 3, 5…

instĭtŭo.opening: (institivi, Plaut. Most. 1, 2, 2 ), , v. a. in-statuo . To put or place into , to plant , fix , set (cf.: instruo, informo; class.): vestigia nuda sinistri Instituere pedis, Verg. A. 7, 690 .— Trop. : argumenta in…

instĭtūtĭo.opening: instituo , disposition , arrangement (class.): rerum, Cic. N. D. 2, 13, 35 .— Custom , manner : institutionem suam conservare, Cic. Att. 1, 17, 10 . — Instruction , education : doctoris, Cic. de Or. 3, 9, 35 : puerilis,…

instĭtūtor.opening: id. , a founder , creator , erector , contractor (post-class.): veteres urbium, Amm. 14, 8, 6 : sordidissimorum artificiorum, Sen. Ben. 6, 17, 1 : materiae, Lact. 2, 8 med. — A teacher , instructor : morum, Treb. Pol.…

instĭtūtum.opening: id. , a purpose , intention , design; an arrangement , plan; mode of life , habits , practices , manners; a regulation , ordinance , institution; instruction; agreement , stipulation (class.): ejus omne institutum…

in-sto.opening: (e. g. instaturum, Liv. 10, 36, 3 : instaturos, Front. Strat. 2, 6, 10 al. ), , v. n. , to stand in or upon a thing (class.). Lit. In gen., constr. with dat. , in and abl. , or acc. With dat. : jugis, Verg. A. 11, 529…

instrāgŭlum.opening: insterno , a covering , coverlet (ante-class.), Cato, R. R. 10, 11 .

instrātum.opening: insterno , a covering (ante- and post-class.), Cato, R. R. 10, 3 ; Dig. 50, 16, 45 .

in-strātus.opening: adj. 2. insterno , not covered or spread over : cubile, an unspread couch, Verg. G. 3, 230 (so interpp. plur. ad loc.; but it is better to construe instrato as part. of insterno, with frondibus hirsutis; cf.: instrata…

instrēnŭē.opening: adv. , v. instrenuus, a, um, fin.

in-strēnŭus.opening: adj. , not brisk , inactive , sluggish , spiritless ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): homo, Plaut. Most. 1, 2, 23 : animus, Ter. Heaut. 1, 1, 68 : dux, Suet. Vesp. 4 . — Adv. : , without spirit : non instrenue moriens,…

instrĕpĭto.opening: v. n. freq. [instrepo], to make a noise anywhere (late Lat.): floribus instrepitans (apis). humming over the flowers , Ven. Carm. 3, 9, 26.

in-strĕpo.opening: v. n. , to make a noise anywhere; to sound , resound , rattle , clatter , creak (mostly poet. and post-class.): sub pondere faginus axis Instrepat, * Verg. G. 3, 172 : dentibus, to gnash, Claud. Cons. Mall. Theod. 222…

in-strīdo.opening: v. n. , to hiss in a place ( poet. ): fax instridens pelago, Sil. 14, 435 .

in-stringo.opening: v. a. To bind , girdle , fasten , chain (rare; not anteAug.): aliquem vinculis, Quint. Decl. 5, 16 : adhuc feralibus amiculis instrictus, App. M. 10, p. 244, 14 .— Absol. , Isid. 19, 10, 1 .— Of a weapon, to draw ,…

in-structĭlis.opening: adj. , not compound (late Lat.): anima, Tert. Anim. 14 .

in-structĭo.opening: a constructing , erecting , building. Lit. : novi balinei, Trajan. ad Plin. Ep. 10, 35 : tubulorum in cloacas, i. e. a sinking into, insertion, Vitr. 5, 9 .— Transf. , an arranging , planting , setting in array :…

instructor.opening: instruo , a preparer : convivii, Cic. post Red. in Sen. 6, 15 .

instructūra.opening: id. . Lit. , a building in , enclosure , barrier , Gromat. Vet. p. 347, 8.— Plur. , Gromat. Vet. p. 255, 25; p. 349, 14.— Transf. Array , order of battle : Macedonum, Front. Strat. 2, 3, 17 .— Arrangement , construction…

instructus.opening: instruo , arrangement , preparation (syn. apparatus): oratio eodem est instructu ornatuque comitata, Cic. de Or. 3, 6, 23 .

instrūmentum.opening: id. , an implement of any kind, a utensil , tool , instrument (class.). Lit. : militare, Caes. B. G. 6, 30 : culinarum argentea, Just. 38, 10, 4 : crudelia jussae instrumenta necis, Ov. M. 3, 698 .— Esp., sing. collect.…

in-strŭo.opening: ( perf. sync. instruxti, Plaut. Mil. 4, 1, 34 ), , v. a. , to build in or into; to build, , erect , construct (class.). Lit. In gen.: contabulationem in parietes, Caes. B. C. 2, 9 : tubulos in earum (cloacarum)…

in-stŭdĭōsus.opening: adj. , not studious , regardless of a thing; with gen. (postclass.): medicinae, App. Mag. p. 299, 28 .

in-stŭpĕo.opening: v. n. , to be torpid , numb; only in part. pres. : membro instupente, Plin. 28, 4, 7, § 38 .

insuāsăbĭlĭtas.opening: 2. in-suadeo , the incapacity to be persuaded , Hier. Eph. 5, 6 .

insuāsum.opening: a kind of dark color : quia tibi insuaso infecisti pallulam, Plaut. Truc. 2, 2, 16 ; cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 111 Müll.

in-sŭāvis.opening: adj. , unpleasant , disagreeable (class.): herba cibo non insuavis, Plin. 24, 16, 97, § 154 : vita, Cic. Att. 10, 4 : voces, Gell. 18, 11 .— Comp. : quid insuavius quam clamor? Auct. Her. 3, 12 .— Sup. : insuavissima…

insŭāvĭtas.opening: insuavis , unpleasantness , disagreeableness (post-class.): per insuavitatem medentur, Tert. ad Martyr. 3 ; Poen. 10: dictionis, Gell. 1, 21, 4 ; Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 19, 115 .

in-subdĭtīvus.opening: adj. , not counterfeit , not supposititious (late Lat.): matris semen, Tert. adv. Val. 27 fin.

Insŭber.opening: adj. (Insubris for Insuber, Spart. Julian. 1 ; gen. plur. Insubrium, Plin. 10, 29, 41, § 77 : Insubrum, id. 3, 17, 21, § 125 ), of or belonging to Insubria , a country in the neighborhood of Milan , Insubrian : eques,…

intĕr-āresco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become dry , to dry up. Lit. , Vitr. 7, 8, 2 : animalia sine humoris potestate interarescent, will die off, id. 8 praef. § 3.— Trop. , to dry up , decay; with exstingui et cadere, Cic. Tusc. 5, 14, 40 .

inter-bĭbo.opening: v. n. , to drink in , drink up , Plaut. Aul. 3, 6, 22 : mare, Naev. ap. Isid. Orig. 5, 26 (Fragm. Trag. v. 55 Rib.).

inter-bīto.opening: v. n. beto , i. q. intereo, to perish , come to naught : ne interbitat quaestio, Plaut. Most. 5, 1, 47 .

inter-blandĭens.opening: Part. [blandior], flattering : obsequiis meis, Aug. Conf. 9, 12 .

inter-caelestis.opening: adj. , between heaven and earth , Claud. Mam. Stat. An. 2, 12 .

intercălāris.opening: adj. intercalo , of or for insertion , that is to be or is inserted , intercalary : dies, an intercalary day, Plin. 2, 8, 6, § 35 ; Censor. de Die Nat. 20 ; Macr. S. 1, 13 ; Sol. 1 : mensis, an intercalary month, Macr.…

intercălārĭus.opening: adj. intercalaris , of or for insertion , intercalary : mensis, an intercalary month, Liv. 1, 19, 6 ; 37, 59, 2 ; Suet. Caes. 40 ; the same absol. : intercalarius, Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 52, § 130 : annus, leap-year, Plin. 2,…

intercălātĭo.opening: intercalo , an insertion , intercalation of a day or month, Plin. 2, 47, 47, § 122 ; Macr. S. 1, 13 .

intercălātor.opening: id. , an intercalator; as adj. , that intercalates : dies intercalatores, intercalary days, Macr. S. 1, 14 (al. intercalantes).

inter-călo.opening: v. a. , lit., to proclaim that something has been intercalated , to insert , intercalate a day or month (syn.: interpono, intericio); usu. in pass. : si intercalatum erit Calendis Maiis, Cato, R. R. 159 : ut duodecim…

intercăpēdĭnans.opening: intercapedo , interrupting , intermitting , Fulg. Myth. 1, p. 9 .

intercăpēdĭnātus.opening: id. , separated , interrupted , Mart. Cap. 9, § 921 : exacerbationes (opp. continuae), Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 1 .

inter-căpēdo.opening: capio , an interruption , intermission , interval , pause , respite : intercapedo, tempus interceptum, cum scilicet mora est ad capiendum, Paul. ex Fest. p. 111 Müll.: intercapedinem scribendi facere, Cic. Fam. 16, 21 :…

inter-căpĭo.opening: v. a. , to take away , Prisc. p. 624 P.

inter-cardĭnātus.opening: adj. , joined together by mortise and tenon , mortised : trabes (acc. to others, interordinatae), Vitr. 10, 20, 2 .

Intercatĭa.opening: a city of Hispania Tarraconensis, Liv. Epit. 48 med. ; Val. Max. 3, 2, 6 .—Hence, , , adj. , of or from Intercatia , Plin. 37, 1, 4, § 9 . — Plur. absol. : , , , the inhabitants of Intercatia , Plin. 3, 3, 4, § 26 .

inter-cēdo.opening: v. n. , to go or come between , to intervene , to be between (syn. intervenio). Lit. In gen.: si quis intercedat tertius, Plaut. Most. 5, 1, 56 : intercedente lunā, Plin. 2, 11, 8, § 49 : palus intercedebat, Caes. B. G.…

interceptĭo.opening: intercipio , a taking away (very rare): poculi, Cic. Clu. 60, 167 ; Hilar. in Psa. 51, 18; id. in Gal. 68 .

interceptor.opening: id. , an intercepter , usurper , embezzler : praedae, Liv. 4, 50, 1 : litis alienae, id. 3, 72, 4 : donativi, Tac. H. 3, 10 : divini beneficii, one who renders void, Val. Max. 9, 11, 4 .

interceptus.opening: intercipio , a taking away , Fulg. Myth. 3, 10 .

intercessĭo.opening: intercedo , a coming between , intervention. Lit. : testium, Gell. 14, 2, 7 .— Transf. An interposition , a becoming surety for one: mea intercessio parata et est et fuit, Cic. Att. 1, 4 : intercessiones pecuniarum in…

intercessor.opening: id. , one who intervenes. A mediator in money matters, a surety : utinam semper esses tribunus: intercessorem non quaereres, Cic. Fam. 7, 27, 1 ; id. Rosc. Am. 38, 110 : rem aliquam agere intercessore ac deprecatore…

intercessus.opening: id. , an intervention; only in abl. sing. Lit. : aliquem intercessu suo servare, Val. Max. 5, 4, 2 : alicujus, Salv. Gub. D. 1, p. 27 .— Trop. : intercessu auctoritatis suae prohibere ne, etc., Imp. Diocl. et Const.…

inter-cīdo.opening: v. a. caedo , to cut asunder , cut up , cut to pieces , divide , pierce , cut through. Lit. : harundinetum, to thin out by cutting, Col. 4, 32, 4 : venas, Plin. 11, 37, 65, § 174 : radices, id. 18, 19, 49, 2, § 177 :…

inter-cĭdo.opening: v. n. cado , to fall between. Lit. : ita in arto stipatae erant naves ut vix ullum telum in mari vanum intercideret, Liv. 26, 39 ; 21, 8 ; 3, 10, 6 .— Transf. To occur meanwhile , to happen : si quae interciderunt,…

Intercīdōna.opening: 1. intercīdo , one of the three deities (Intercidona, Pilumnus, and Deverra) who protected the house of a lying-in woman against Silvanus , Varr. ap. Aug. Civ. Dei , 6, 9; cf. Voss. Verg. E. 10, 24 .

inter-cĭlĭum.opening: the space between the eyebrows : intercilium, μεσόφρυον, Gloss. Philox.; Isid. Orig. 11, 1 .

inter-cĭno.opening: v. a. cano , to sing between : neu quid medios intercinat actus, Hor. A. P. 194 .

inter-cĭpĭo.opening: v. a. capio , lit., to take away between, i. e. to seize on the passage before arrival at the destined place , to intercept. Lit. : tun redimes me, si me hostes interceperint? Plaut. As. 1, 1, 93 : venenum, to take the…

intercīsīmen.opening: 1. intercīdo , a cutting through , intersection : intercisimen, διακοπή, Gloss. Gr. Lat.

intercīsĭ.opening: o, , id. , a cutting through , Varr. ap. Aug. Civ. Dei , 6, 9.

inter-clāmo.opening: v. n. , to cry out between or among : multis interclamantibus, Amm. 31, 13, 1 .

inter-clūdo.opening: v. a. claudo , to shut out , shut off. Lit. To cut off , hinder , stop , block up , shut off. Of one's way, passage, entrance, retreat, etc.; constr. (syn. intersaepio). With acc. of thing and dat. of person : hisce…

interclūsĭo.opening: intercludo , a stopping or shutting up. Animae, a want of breath , Cic. de Or. 3, 46, 179 .— A parenthesis , Quint. 9, 3, 23 .

inter-cŏlumnĭum.opening: columna , the space between two columns , intercolumniation : ambulationis, Cic. Q. Fr. 3, 1, 2, § 5 : signa omnibus intercolumniis disposita, Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 19 ; Vitr. 3, 1 ; 4, 3 ; Vulg. 1 Reg. 7, 31 .

inter-concĭlĭo.opening: v. a. , to gain the favor of , conciliate a person, Quint. 12, 10, 59 dub. (al. conciliandi).

inter-crĕātus.opening: adj. , inwardly created or produced : humor, Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 1 .

inter-culco.opening: v. a. calco , to tread between : ita distantes ut interculcari possint vinacea (al. intercalcari), Col. 12, 43, 10 .

inter-cultus.opening: adj. , cultivated , tilled between : fines, Sic. Fl. Cond. Agr. p. 7.

inter-curro.grammar: curri, rsum, 3 v. n. and a.
inter-curro.opening: v. n. and a. (tmesis in Lucr. 5, 1374 : inter plaga currere). Neutr. , to run between. Lit. In gen.: latitudine intercurrentis freti, Plin. 3, 11, 16, § 100 .— In partic., to hasten in the meantime anywhere: indicto…

inter-curso.opening: v. n. freq. [intercurro] (tmesis: inter enim cursant, Lucr. 3, 262 ), to run between. Lit. : intercursantibus barbaris, Liv. 21, 35, 1 .— Transf. , to be or lie between; to grow , move , or be in motion between : acinos…

intercursus.opening: intercurro , only abl. sing. , a running between , intervention , interposition (rare, except in Liv.): periculum intercursu tum primum pubescentis filii propulsatum, Liv. 21, 46, 7 : impeditus intercursu suorum, id.…

inter-cus.opening: adj. cutis , under the skin , intercutaneous. Esp., as med. t. t.: aqua intercus, the dropsy, Plaut. Men. 5, 4, 3 : medicamentum alicui dare ad aquam intercutem, Cic. Off. 3, 24, 42 : morbus aquae intercutis, Suet. Ner.…

intercussus.opening: inter-quatio , a striking between : luminis, a flashing between, Sen. Q. N. 3, 27 .

intercŭtītus.opening: adj. intercus , greatly abused , dishonored , Paul. ex Fest. p. 113 Müll.; v. fullo.

interdĭānus.opening: adj. interdiu , throughout the day , daily (late Lat.): cibus, Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 7, 95 (dub.).

interdĭārĭus.opening: id. , a thief who steals by day : interdiarius, ἡμεροκλέπτης, Gloss. Philox.

inter-dīco.opening: (interdixem for interdixissem, Cat. ap. Gell. 19, 9 fin. ), , v. a. , to speak between , i. e. to interpose by speaking. Lit. To say among other things , to remark meanwhile , interpose : in praesentiarum hoc…

interdictĭo.opening: interdico , a prohibiting , interdicting : tecti et aquae et ignis interdictione, banishment , Auct. Or. pro Dom. 30: finium, Liv. 41, 24 : habes igitur et theatri interdictionem de interdictione impudicitiae, Tert.…

interdictor.opening: id. , a forbidder , interdicter : delicti, Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 9 .

interdictōrĭus.opening: adj. interdictor , prohibitory , interdictory , Salv. contr. Avar. 3 med. p. 130 Rittersh.

interdictum.opening: interdico . In gen., a prohibition : nequeone ego ted interdictis facere mansuetem meis? Plaut. As. 3, 1, 1 : deorum, Cic. Pis. 21, 48 .— In partic., as a legal t. t., a provisional decree of the prætor, esp. in…

interdictus.opening: , = interdictum, Jul. ap. Aug. contr. Sec. Resp. Jul. 6, 20.

Interdidĭum.opening: a place in Alexandria , Jul. Val. Res Gest. Alex. M. 1, 30 Mai.

inter-dĭgĭtālĭa.opening: plur. [digitus], excrescences (warts, etc.) between the fingers , Plin. Val. 2, 52 .

interdĭgĭtĭa.opening: plur. [id.], excrescences (warts, etc.) between the fingers and toes , Marc. Emp. 34 : intedita (leg. interdigitia) μεσοδάκτυλα, Gloss. Philox.

interdĭu.opening: (ante-class. form interdius, Cato, R. R. 83 ; Varr. R. R. 2, 10 Schneid.; Plaut. Aul. 1, 1, 33 ; Most. 2, 2, 14; Merc. 5, 2, 21), adv. dies , during the day , in the daytime , by day (not in Cic.): canes interdiu…

inter-do.opening: , dăre. To give an interval , to give at intervals : nec mora nec requies interdatur ulla fluendi, Lucr. 4, 227 . — To distribute : cibus interdatus (through the body), Lucr. 4, 868 (by Lachm. written as two words,…

interdŭātim.opening: adv. , an old form for interdum, sometimes , now and then , acc. to Paul. ex Fest. p. 111 Müll. (but the true reading is interdum, Plaut. Truc. 4, 4, 29 ).

Inter-dūca.opening: inter-duco , an epithet of Juno , Mart. Cap. 2, § 149 Grotius (Kopp, Iterduca); cf. domiduca.

inter-dum.opening: adv. , sometimes , occasionally , now and then , = nonnumquam: interdum fio Juppiter, quando lubet, Plaut. Am. 3, 1, 4 : interdum cursus est in oratione incitatior, interdum moderata ingressio, Cic. Or. 59 :…

intĕr-ĕā.opening: adv. Meanwhile , in the meantime , in the interim (class.): saepe interea mihi senex narrabat, Ter. Phorm. 2, 3, 18 : interea dies advenit, Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 15, § 37 : cum interea, Ter. Hec. 3, 4, 7 ; Cic. Verr. 1, 6,…

intĕremptĭbĭlis.opening: adj. interimo , that can be destroyed or killed (eccl. Lat.): Christus, Tert. adv. Marc. 3, 6 .

intĕremptĭo.opening: ( ), , id. , destruction , slaughter , Tert. adv. Prax. 27 ; Porc. Lat. Decl. in Cat. 10 (but a false reading for internecione, Cic. de Imp. Pomp. 11, 30 ).

intĕremptor.opening: ( ), , id. , one who destroys or kills , a slayer , murderer (post-Aug.): fratris, Vell. 2, 129, 1 : eri, Sen. Ep. 70, 12 : puellae, Val. Max. 6, 1, 2 .

intĕremptrix.opening: ( ), , interemptor , she that destroys or kills , a murderess (eccl. Lat.). Lit. : fratris, Lact. 1, 10, 4 .— Trop. : pudoris, Tert. Spect. 17 .

intĕr-ĕo.opening: ( perf. -īvi, App. M. 7, 7 ; sync. -issent, Cic. Div. 2, 8, 20 al. ), , v. n. —Prop., to go among several things, so as no longer to be perceived (class.). Lit. : ut interit magnitudine maris stilla muriae, becomes lost…

intĕr-ĕquĭto.opening: v. n. and a. , to ride between (a favorite word with Livy). Absol. , Liv. 34, 15, 4 ; 35, 5, 10 ; Curt. 4, 13, 22 .— With acc. : ordines, Liv. 6, 7, 3 : agmina, Curt. 4, 13, 1 .

intĕr-erro.opening: v. n. , to wander between or among , to come , go , or be between (postclass.): Deus locis omnibus intererrat, Minuc. Fel. Octav. 10: splendor, Prud. Cath. 6, 43 .

interfātĭo.opening: interfor , a speaking between , an interrupting in speaking (syn. interpellatio): contra verba atque interfationem, Cic. Sest. 37, 79 : expositiones brevi interfatione distinguere, Quint. 4, 2, 50 Spald. N. cr.

interfectĭbĭlis.opening: adj. interficio , deadly : ruta viperarum, App. Herb. 89 .

interfectĭo.opening: id. , a killing , murdering (rare): Trebonii, Brut. ap. Cic. Ep. ad Brut. 2, 3 init. : Clodii, Ascon. ap. Argum. Milon. p. 34, 16.

interfectīvus.opening: adj. id. , deadly (post-class.): morbus, Cael. Aur. praef. § 12.

interfector.opening: id. , a slayer , murderer. Lit. : alicujus, Cic. Mil. 27, 72 ; id. Phil. 1, 14, 35 ; Nep. Att. 8, 3 ; Tac. A. 1, 9 ; 12, 48 ; 14, 44 ; Liv. 24, 7, 7 ; 44, 40, 9 . — Trop. , a destroyer : veritatis, Tert. Carn. Christ. 5…

interfectōrĭus.opening: adj. interfector , deadly , murderous (late Lat.), Aug. de Lib. Arb. 3, 25 ; Isid. Orig. 17, 7, 7 .— Subst. : , , , a means of destruction , Ambros. de Elia et Jejun. 10, 37 fin. —Hence, adv. : , destructively ,…

interfectrix.opening: interfector , a murderess (post-Aug.): nepotis, Tac. A. 3, 17 ; Hyg. Fab. 122 .— Trop. : abstinentia, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 8, 95 .

interfĕmĭnĭum.opening: inter-femen , i. q. cunnus (post-class.), App. Mag. p. 296, 15 and 22.

inter-fĕmus.opening: the space between the thighs : interfemus, μεσομήριον, Gloss. Philox.

interfĭcĭo.opening: (archaic pass. : interfiat, Lucr. 3, 872 : interfieri, Plaut. Trin. 2, 4, 131 ), , v. a. inter-facio , to put between. In gen. (rare): terrae natura medicatas aquas interficit, Plin. 2, 100, 104, § 222 (al. inficiat).—…

inter-flŭo.opening: v. n. and a. (in tmesi, Lucr. 4, 227 ), to flow between (rare but class.): quantum interfluit fretum, Liv. 41, 23, 16 : angusto freto interfluente, Plin. 3, 5, 11, § 76 .— With acc. : fretum, quod Naupactum et Ratras…

inter-flŭus.opening: adj. interfluo , flowing between (rare and post-Aug.): interfluo Euphrate, Plin. 6, 26, 30, § 121 : amnis, Sol. 66 : umor, Pall. Sept. 10 fin.

inter-fŏdĭo.opening: v. a. , to dig out , dig between , pierce : pupillas, Lucr. 4, 716 : radices, Pall. Oct. 12, 2 .

inter-for.opening: v. dep. n. and a. (interfari, interfatur, interfatus are the forms in common use), to speak between , to interrupt in speaking (syn. interpello): priusquam ille postulatum perageret, interfatur Appius, Liv. 3, 47 :…

inter-frīgesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to grow old , die away , or be dropped in the meanwhile (post-class.): res, Fragm. Jur. Civ. Antejustin. p. 45.

inter-fringo.opening: v. a. frango , to break to pieces (ante-class. and post-Aug.): si quid ventus interfregerit, Cato, R. R. 44 ; Plin. 17, 18, 30, § 127 .

inter-fŭgĭo.opening: v. n. , to flee between or into; in tmesi: inter enim fugit, Lucr. 6, 332 .

inter-fulgĕo.opening: v. n. , to shine or glitter between : aurum cumulo aliarum rerum interfulgens, Liv. 28, 23, 4 .

inter-fundo.opening: v. a. 2. fundo , to pour between; pass. , to flow between (mostly poet. ): pelagus interfunditur oras, Avien. Perieg. 250 .— Hence, , , Part. : interfusum mare, Plin. 3, 8, 14, § 86 : Dido maculis trementis interfusa…

inter-fŭro.opening: v. n. , to rage between or through ( poet. ): orbem, Stat. Ach. 1, 395 .

interfūsĭo.opening: interfundo , a flowing between (eccl. Lat.): maris, Lact. 7, 3, 25 .

intergarrītus.opening: Part. , from the obsolete intergarrio [inter-garrio], prated or chattered between (post-class.): dein pauculis verbis intergarritis (al. intergannitis), App. Mag. p. 284, 38 .

inter-gĕrĭes.opening: 1. gero , a partition , party-wall : intergeries, paries, τοῖχος ὁ δύο κτήσεις διορίζων, i. e. murus duas possessiones separans, Gloss. Philox.

intergĕrīvus.opening: adj. intergeries , that is placed between; subst. : , , (sc. paries), a partition , party-wall , Plin. 13, 12, 26, § 82 ; 35, 14, 49, § 173 .—Of the walls of wax in a beehive , Plin. 11, 10, 10, § 23 .

inter-gĕro.opening: v. a. , to place between , interpose , insert walls: intergerivi parietes dicuntur, qui inter confines struuntur, et quasi intergeruntur, Paul. ex Fest. p. 110, 21 Müll.

intergressus.opening: (only in abl. sing. ), from the obs. intergredior , a coming between , intervention (post-class.): disputationis, Min. Fel. Octav. 15 .

intĕr-hĭo.opening: v. n. , to be open between (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Apol. 48 .

intĕr-ĭbĭ.opening: (interibei, Sen. con. de Bac. C. 1 R. 196), adv. , in the meantime , for interea, interim (ante- and post-class.), Plaut. As. 5, 2, 41 ; id. Capt. 5, 1, 31 ; 33 ; id. Mil. 2, 1, 26 ; id. Poen. 3, 3, 3 ; id. Rud. 4, 6,…

intĕrĭbĭlis.opening: adj. intereo , perishable , mortal (eccl. Lat.): nihil, Tert. adv. Herm. 34 : animae, Arn. 2, 65 .

intĕrim.opening: adv. inter and old acc. of is . I.q. interea, meanwhile , in the meantime : ibo intro: tu hic ante aedes interim speculare, Plaut. Mil. 4, 3, 28 : interim dum ante ostium sto, Ter. Eun. 5, 2, 3 : hoc interim spatio…

intĕr-ĭmo.opening: (better than , Bramb. s. v., but v. Munro, Lucr. Introd. p. 33 ), ēmi, emptum, or , v. a. emo , to take out of the midst , to take away , do away with , abolish; to destroy , slay , kill (syn.: interficio, perimo;…

intĕrĭor.opening: gen. ōris [ comp. from inter, whence also sup. intimus], inner , interior; nearer (class.). In gen.: in interiore aedium parte, Cic. Sest. 10 : spatium, Ov. M. 7, 670 : secessit in partem interiorem, Liv. 40, 8 : in…

intĕrĭtĭo.opening: intereo , for interitus, destruction , ruin (rare but class.): aratorum, Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 54, § 125 ; Arn. 2, p. 87 ; Vitr. 8, 1 .

intĕrĭtus.opening: intereo , destruction , ruin , annihilation (class.): interitus est quasi discessus et secretio, ac diremptio earum rerum, quae junctione aliqua tenebantur, Cic. Tusc. 1, 29 : omnium rerum interitus atque obitus, id.…

intĕrĭus.opening: . Adj. comp. , from interior. — Adv. , v. interior fin.

inter-jăcĕo.opening: v. n. and a. , to lie between; constr. with dat. , acc. , or inter (not in Cic. or Cæs.): interjacebat campus, Liv. 37, 41 .—With dat. : campus interjacens Tiberi ac moenibus Romanis, Liv. 21, 30 : via interjacente,…

inter-jăcĭo.opening: and , (in tmesi: inter enim jecta est, Lucr. 3, 859 ), , v. a. jacio , to throw or cast between; to set , place , or put between; to join or add to , to intermix (class., most freq. in the part. pass. ): legionarias…

interjectĭo.opening: interjacio , a throwing or placing between , insertion. In gen.: verborum, Auct. Her. 1, 6, 9 .— In partic. In gram., an interjection , Quint. 1, 4, 19 .— In rhet., a parenthesis, an interruption of the principal idea…

interjectīvus.opening: adj. interjacio , placed between (post-class.): rigor, Simplic. de Re Agrar. p. 78.—Hence, , adv. , in the manner of an interjection , Prisc. 15 fin.

interjectūra.opening: id. , an insertion , Front. de Colon. p. 135 .

interjectus.opening: interjacio , a throwing or placing between , interposition; a coming between , intervention (class.). Lit. : lapides temerario interjectu ponere, App. de Deo, Soc. Prol. p. 365, 15: luna interpositu interjectuque terrae…

inter-jungo.grammar: nxi, nctum, 3 v. a. and n.
inter-jungo.opening: v. a. and n. To join together , join , unite : dextrae interjunctae, Liv. 22, 30, 6 (cf. interaptus): interjunctus (equus) equis, harnessed among, Stat. Th. 6, 308 . — To unyoke. Lit. : lassos equos, Mart. 3, 67, 7 : et…

inter-lābor.opening: v. dep. n. and a. , to fall , slip , slide , glide , or flow between ( poet. ): per has stellis interlabentibus umbras, Stat. Th. 2, 649 : (in tmesi), inter enim labentur aquae, Verg. G. 2, 349 ; Sil. 6, 18 .—With acc.…

inter-lătĕo.opening: v. n. , to lurk or lie hid between (very rare), Sen. Q. N. 6, 16, 4 dub.

inter-lătrans.opening: Part. [interlatro], barking between (eccl. Lat.), trop.: peccata inter nos et Deum, Paul. Nol. Ep. 4 med.

inter-lectĭo.opening: 2. lego , a reading between , a reading together (eccl. Lat.): scripturarum, Tert. ad Uxor. 2, 6 .

inter-lĕgo.opening: v. a. , to cull or pluck off here and there ( poet. and postclass.): (in tmesi) uncis Carpendae manibus frondes, interque legendae, Verg. G. 2, 366 : poma, Pall. Febr. 25, 16 ; id. Jun. 5, 1 .

inter-līdo.opening: v. a. laedo . To thrust out of the midst , to strike out (post-class.): litteris interlisis, Macr. S. 2, 14 .— To strike against : dentem, Paul. Nol. Carm. 10, 261 .

inter-lĭgo.opening: v. a. 1. ligo , to bind together : alterno maculas ostro, Stat. Th. 7, 571 : (alga) insanas interligat undas, restrains, hinders, Rutil. 1, 539 .

inter-lĭno.opening: v. a. , to smear between , smear , spread between , lay at intervals. Lit. : caementa luto, Liv. 21, 11, 8 ; cf.: murus bitumine interlitus, Curt. 5, 1, 9 : caseum oleo, Plin. 28, 9, 34, § 132 .— Transf. , to falsify by…

inter-lŏco.opening: v. a. , to place between , Mela, 2, 1.

interlŏcūtĭo.opening: interloquor , a speaking between , interlocution. In gen.: brevi interlocutione patroni refutandus est, Quint. 5, 7, 26 ; so Gell. 14, 2, 17 , — In partic., an interlocutory sen , tence : severā interlocutione…

inter-lŏquor.opening: v. dep. , to speak between , interrupt in speaking. In gen.: siccine mihi interloquere? Ter. Heaut. 4, 3, 13 .— Absol. , Gell. 14, 2, 19 : ipse raro et breviter interlocutus, Plin. Ep. 7, 6, 6 .— In law, to pronounce an…

interlūcātĭo.opening: interluco , a lopping off of useless branches , a thinning , pruning (Plinian), Plin. 17, 27, 45, § 257 .

inter-lūcĕo.opening: v. n. , to shine or glitter forth at intervals (class.). Lit. : duos soles visos, et noctu interluxisse, Liv. 29, 14, 3 : quia terrena quaedam animalia plerumque interlucent (in amber), Tac. G. 45, 4 ; Sol. 20, 3 .—…

inter-lūcesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to shine through : interlucesco, διαφαίνομαι, Gloss. Philox.

inter-lūco.opening: v. a. lux , to let the light through a tree by clearing it of its useless branches; to lop or thin a tree (Plinian): interlucata densitate ramorum, Plin. 17, 23, 35, § 214 : arbores, id. 17, 12, 19, § 94 .

inter-lūdo.opening: v. a. , to play between or together (post-class.), Aus. Idyll. 10, 76 : interludamus epistolis, Ambros. Ep. 47, 4 .

inter-lūnis.opening: adj. luna , at new moon , interlunar (post-class.): nox, Amm. 19, 6, 7 .

interlūnĭum.opening: interlunis , the new moon , time of new moon , interlunary interval , Plin. 18, 32, 75, § 324 ; 7, 5, 4, § 38 . —In plur. , Hor. C. 1, 25, 11 .

inter-lŭo.opening: v. a. To wash while doing any thing : manus ( between the acts of a sacrifice ), Cato, R. R. 132 .— Of rivers, to wash under , to flow between : pontus ... arva et urbes Litore diductas angusto interluit aestu, Verg. A.…

interlŭvĭes.opening: interluo , water that flows between two places, a strait (post-class.): angusta, Sol. 22, 14 : angusta fluminis, Amm. 24, 2, 4 .

inter-mănĕo.opening: v. n. , to remain between ( poet. ): mediis agris, Luc. 6, 47 .

inter-mĕdĭus.opening: adj. , that is between , intermediate (ante - class. and late Lat), Varr. R. R. 3, 5, 11 ; Paul. Nol. Carm. 26, 637 .

inter-menstrŭus.opening: adj. , between two months : lunā intermenstruā, i. e. at the time of new moon, Plin. 18, 32, 75, § 322 .— Subst. : , i. (sc. tempus), the new moon , time of new moon , Varr. R. R. 1, 37, 1 ; Cic. Rep. 1, 16, 25 :…

inter-mĕo.opening: v. a. , to go between , flow or pass through the midst of; with acc. (Plin. and late Lat.): Pergamum intermeat Selinus, Plin. 5, 30, 33, § 126 : paludem, Amm. 15, 11, 16 : saepe, to visit often, id. 26, 6, 5 .

inter-mestris.opening: adj. mensis , between two months : a mensibus intermestris dictus, Varr. L. L. 6, 2, § 10 Müll.: luna, the new moon, Cat. R. R. 37 ; Plin. 16, 39, 75, § 194 .

inter-mētĭum.opening: meta , the space between the goals : intermetium, τὸ μεταξὺ τῶν καμπτήρων, Gloss. Philox.

inter-mĭco.opening: v. n. and a. , to glitter among , to gleam forth ( poet. ): squamis intermicat aurum, Claud. Rapt. Pros. 1, 183 . —With acc. : tenebras nimbosque intermicat ignis, Val. Fl. 4, 662 .— Absol. : ignis, Stat. Th. 12, 252 .

intermĭnābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-terminalis , endless , interminable (post-class.): aetas, Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 3 : jurgium, Sid. Ep. 2, 7 .

intermĭnātĭo.opening: interminor , a threatening , menacing (post-class.): judicii, Cod. Th. 10, 20, 18; 16, 5, 18 al.

in-termĭnātus.opening: adj. , unbounded , endless (class.): immensa et interminata magnitudo regionum, Cic. N. D. 1, 20, 54 : saeculorum cursus, Jul. Val. Res Gest. Alex. 1, 31, 22 .— Transf. : cupiditas imperii, Vell. 2, 33, 2 : petendi…

intermĭnis.opening: adj. 2. in-terminus , boundless , endless (post-class.): mundus, Jul. Val. Res Gest. Alex. M. 1, 30 .

inter-mĭno.opening: , a false read. for in terrast, Plaut. Mil. 2, 3, 42 ; v. Ritschl ad h. l.

inter-mĭnor.opening: v. dep. , to threaten , menace; to forbid with threats ( poet. ): mihi tibique interminatus est, nos futuros, etc., Plaut. As. 2, 2, 95 ; id. Ps. 3, 1, 10 : alicui vitam, id. Cas. 3, 5, 28 : istuceine tibi, Ter. Eun. 5,…

in-termĭnus.opening: adj. , boundless , endless (post-class.): oceanus, Avien. Perieg. 74 : felicitas, Aus. Ep. 16, 38 : lapsus stellarum, App. Mund. p. 57, 18 .

inter-miscĕo.grammar: scui, xtum, or stum, 2 v. a.
inter-miscĕo.opening: v. a. , to mix among , intermix. —With dat. (not in Cic. or Cæs.): tibi undam, Verg. E. 10, 5 ; so, aliquid alicui, Col. 11, 3, 57 : turbam indignorum dignis, Liv. 4, 56 .—With abl. : intermixti hostibus cognoscunt,…

intermissĭo.opening: intermitto , a breaking off , intermission , interruption; a neglecting , ceasing , discontinuance (class.): forensis operae, Cic. Div. 2, 68, 142 : sine ulla intermissione, without any intermission, id. N. D. 1, 41,…

intermissus.opening: intermitto , for intermissio, an intermission , interruption : garrulus sine intermissu cantus, incessant, Plin. 10, 29, 43, § 81 .

inter-mitto.grammar: mīsi, missum, 3 v. a. and n.
inter-mitto.opening: v. a. and n. Act. To leave off , intermit , omit , neglect; constr. with acc. , aliquid ab , ad , or inf. With acc. : studia, Cic. Or. 10 : iter, Caes. B. C. 3, 3 : proelium, id. B. G. 3, 5 : opus, id. ib. 3, 29 :…

inter-mŏrĭor.opening: v. dep. To die in secret , perish unobserved , to die off , fall to decay (not in Cic. or Cæs.), Cato, R. R. 161, 3 : radices intermoriuntur, Plin. 21, 18, 69, § 114 : ignis, Curt. 6, 6, 31 : civitas, Liv. 34, 49 .—…

inter-mŏvĕo.opening: v. a. , to move or pass between (post-class.): alios sulcos stilo, Symm. Ep. 8, 69 .

inter-mundĭa.opening: plur. [mundus], spaces between the worlds , in which, acc. to Epicurus, the gods reside, Cic. Fin. 2, 23, 75 ; cf. id. Div. 2, 17, 40 : id. N. D. 1, 8, 18 .

inter-mūnus.opening: a gift for a time , i. e. a loan , Ennod. Dict. 21 .

inter-mūrālis.opening: adj. , between two walls : amnis, Liv. 44, 46, 1 .

intermūtātus.opening: inter-muto , interchanged (eccl. Lat.): intermutatis manibus, Tert. Baptism. 8 .

internas.opening: inter, cf. supernas , inward , inner , Fronto ad Amic. 1, 17.

inter-nascor.opening: v. dep. , to grow between or among : internascentes herbae, Plin. 18, 16, 43, § 146 : virgulta internata, Liv. 28, 2 : internatum corpus, Plin. 17, 27, 42, § 251 .

inter-nătĭdus.opening: adj. internates , situated between the nates , Fronto ad Amic. 1, 16.

internĕcĭālis.opening: , a false read. for perniciales, Liv. 27, 23 .

internĕcīda.opening: internecio , one who by false testimony deprives another of his life , acc. to Isid. Orig. 10 .

internĕcĭes.opening: id. , for internecio, slaughter , death , destruction : internecies, mors, jactura, Gloss. Isid.

internĕcīnus.opening: or , , adj. internecio , deadly , murderous , destructive (class.): bellum, Cic. Phil. 14, 3, 7 ; Liv. 9, 25 fin. ; 22, 58, 3 : odia, Just. 6, 6 : internecini actio, for poisoning , Cod. Th. 9, 1, 14: internecini…

internĕcĭo.opening: ( ), , interneco , a massacre , general slaughter , carnage , utter destruction , extermination (class.): neque resisti sine internecione posse arbitramur, Cic. Att. 2, 20 : civium, id. Cat. 3, 10 : bella, quae ad…

internĕcĭum.opening: id. , for internecio, slaughter , death , destruction , Isid. 5, 26, 17 ; Not. Tir. p. 123 .

inter-nĕco.opening: v. a. , to kill , destroy (ante- and post-class.; cf.: interficio, trucido, etc.). Lit. : internecatis hostibus, Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 34, 6 . — Transf. : sementes, Amm. 23, 6, 50 : culmum, Prud. prooem. Apoth. 61.

inter-necto.opening: v. a. , to bind together , bind up ( poet. ): ut fibula crinem Auro internectat, Verg. A. 7, 816 : plagas, to bind up, Stat. Th. 8, 168 .

inter-nīdĭfĭco.opening: v. n. , to build a nest among , Plin. 10, 33, 49, § 95 .

internĭgrans.opening: Part. [inter-nigro], being black here and there ( poet. ): maculae, Stat. Th. 6, 336 .

inter-nĭtĕo.opening: v. n. , to shine among , shine forth (post-Aug.): etiam si qua sidera internitebant, Curt. 5, 4, 25 : quicquid lucis internitebat, id. 4, 3, 16 : internitentes gemmae, id. 3, 3, 16 ; cf. Plin. 37, 5, 17, § 65 ; Curt. 4,…

internoctātĭo.opening: inter-nox , night-watching : pernoctatio, excubiae, = παννυχίδες, Gloss. Philox.

inter-nōdĭum.opening: nodus , the space between two knots or joints , an internode or joint. Of plants: harundinum, Plin. 7, 2, 2, § 21 .— Of the leg: mollia nervosus facit internodia poples, Ov. M. 6, 256 . — Transf. , the leg itself: longa…

inter-nosco.opening: v. a. , to distinguish between , to tell apart , to discern , distinguish (class.): fortuna dignum atque indignum nequit internoscere, Pac. ap. Auct. Her. 2, 23, 36 (Trag. Rel. v. 371 Rib.): gemini duo, ita forma…

internucŭlus.opening: one who gives himself up to prostitution , Petr. 7 .

internundĭnĭum.opening: and , , inter-nundinae , the space of time between two nundinae, Mar. Victorin. p. 2469 P.: quoties rusticus internundino barbam radiebat, Varr. ap. Non. 214, 28 ; Macr. S. 1, 16, 34 .

inter-nuntĭo.opening: ( ), , v. n. , to send messengers from both sides : paulisper internuntiando cunctatio fit, Liv. 42, 39, 4 .

inter-nuntĭus.opening: ( ), , that serves as a messenger or mediator between two parties or persons; only subst. , a mediator , messenger , go-between. , , (class.): egone ut ad te ab libertina esse auderem internuntius? Plaut. Mil. 4, 1, 16…

internus.opening: adj. in; cf. interior, intestinus, intus , inward , internal (postAug.). Adj. Lit. : ignis, Sen. Q. N. 6, 27, 2 : arae, Ov. H. 7, 113 : maria, inland, Plin. 2, 68, 68, § 173 .— Trop. , domestic , civil , internal :…

in-tĕro.opening: ( second pers. perf. intrīsti; see below), , v. a. , to rub into , to rub , bruise , or crumble in ( poet. and postAug.). Lit. : infundito in catinum: eo interito, Cato, R. R. 156, 6 : aliquid potioni, Plin. 28, 19, 80,…

intĕr-ordĭnātus.opening: adj. , fitted together : trabes, fitted into each other, Vitr. 10, 14, 2 .

intĕr-ordĭnĭum.opening: ordo , the space between two rows , Col. 3, 13, 3 ; 4, 14, 2 ; 5, 5, 3 .

inter-pătĕo.opening: v. n. , to be open between or among , to lie between , intervene (post-class.): tectum, Macr. S. 1, 18 : pulmo, id. ib. 7, 15 : Syria, Amm. 14, 8, 8 : senos pedes inter singulas acies, Veg. Mil. 3, 15 ; Lact. Opif. D.…

interpĕdĭo.opening: v. a. , i. q. impedio, to hinder , impede (post-class.): gustatum linguae, Macr. S. 7, 12, 38 .

interpellātĭo.opening: interpello , a speaking between , an interruption in speaking; an interruption , hinderance. In gen.: quid tibi interpellatio aut in consilium huc accessiost? What business have you to interrupt? Plaut. Trin. 3, 2, 83 :…

interpellātor.opening: id. , one who interrupts another in speaking , an interrupter , disturber (class.), Auct. Her. 2, 11, 16 : ubi se oblectare sine interpellatoribus posset, Cic. Off. 3, 14, 58 : matrimoniorum, a seducer, Paul. Sent. 5,…

interpellātrix.opening: interpellator , she that disturbs (late Lat.), Hier. Ep. 60, 11 .

interpellātus.opening: (only in abl. sing. ) [interpello], i. q. interpellatio, a disturbance (post-class.), Auct. Itin. Alex. M. 31.

inter-pello.opening: v. a. , to interrupt by speaking , to disturb , molest , etc. (syn. obloquor; class.). To interrupt by speaking , to disturb a person speaking: si interpellas, ego tacebo, Plaut. Men. 5, 9, 62 : nihil te interpellabo,…

inter-pensīvus.opening: adj. pendeo , hanging or suspended between. — Hence, subst. : , , plur. , (sc. tigilla), cross-beams , Vitr. 6, 3, 1 .

inter-plĭco.opening: v. a. , to fold or plait between , to interweave , to surround : ducem, Stat. Th. 2, 282 : cristas, id. ib. 4, 218 .

interpŏlāmentum.opening: interpolo , an intermixture , admixture (post-class.), Claud. Mam. de Stat. Anim. praef.

interpŏlātĭo.opening: id. , an alteration made here and there (post-Aug.): tenuatam (chartam) curiosa interpolatione, principalem fecit e plebeia, by a curious dressing made the best paper from common, Plin. 13, 12, 23, § 75 ; Tert. adv.…

interpŏlātor.opening: id. , one who gives another appearance to things , a polisher , furbisher; a corrupter , spoiler (eccl. Lat.): multum est inter institutorem et interpolatorem, Tert. Spect. 2 : veritatis, id. Apol. 46 : Satanas totius…

interpŏlātrix.opening: interpolator , she that alters the appearance of a thing , a falsifier , corrupter (eccl. Lat.): veri, Nazar. Pan. Constant. 15 : veritatis, Tert. adv. Haer. 7 .

interpŏlis.opening: , and , , adj. inter-polio , that has received a new appearance , altered by furbishing , polished up , vamped up , repaired; esp., falsified , painted , not genuine (ante-class. and post-Aug.). Lit. , Plin. 19, 2, 8, §…

interpŏlo.opening: v. a. interpolio; cf. Non. p. 34, 2 sq. , to give a new form , shape , or appearance to any thing; to polish , furbish , or dress up; to spoil , corrupt , falsify; to vary , change (class.; cf. interlino, vitio,…

inter-pondĭum.opening: ( ), , pondus , equipoise , equilibrium : interpondium, παράλληλον, Gloss. Philox.

inter-pōno.opening: v. a. , to put , place , lay , or set between or among , to interpose , insert between. Lit. Of place, constr. with acc. and dat. , or inter with acc. : equitatus praesidia levis armaturae, Hirt. B. G. 8, 17 ; 13 ; 19 :…

interpŏsĭtĭo.opening: interpono , a putting between , insertion. In gen.: tetrastyli, propter columnarum interpositiones, spatiosiores constituantur, Vitr. 5, 3, 8 .— Esp. An inserting or introduction of persons in discourse: personarum,…

interpŏsĭtus.opening: (only in abl. sing. ), a putting between , interposition (rare but class.): luna interpositu interjectuque terrae repente deficit, Cic. N. D. 2, 40, 103 : solis radios luna interpositu suo auferens terrae, Plin. 2, 10,…

inter-prĕs.opening: inter, and Sanscr. root prath-, to spread abroad; cf. πλατύς, latus . An agent between two parties , a broker , factor , negotiator (class.): quod te praesente isti egi, teque interprete, through your agency, Plaut.…

interprĕtābĭlis.opening: adj. interpretor , that can be explained or translated (late Lat.): nomen, Tert. adv. Val. 14 .

interprĕtāmentum.opening: id. , an explanation , exposition , translation , interpretation (post-class.): obscurius, Gell. 6, 2, 2 : Graeci (verbi), id. 13, 9, 4 : alicujus rei Latinum, id. 5, 18, 7 : somniorum, Petr. 10 .

interprĕtātĭo.opening: , ōnis. id. . An explanation , exposition , interpretation (class.): juris, Cic. Off. 1, 10 : facilis, Liv. 2, 8 : fulgurum, Plin. 2, 53, 54, § 141 : ostentorum et somniorum, id. 7, 56, 57, § 203 ; Suet. Caes. 14 :…

interprĕtātĭuncŭla.opening: dim. interpretatio , a brief explanation (late Lat.), Hier. Ep. 112, 19 .

interprĕtātor.opening: interpretor , an explainer , interpreter (eccl. Lat.), Tert. adv. Prax. 19 : utriusque testamenti, id. Monog. 6 .

interprĕtātōrĭus.opening: adj. interpretator , pertaining to an interpreter (late Lat.), Tert. ad Nat. 2, 4 .

inter-prĕtĭum.opening: the difference between the buying and selling price , profit (post-class.), Amm. 28, 1, 18 ; cf.: interpretium παράλληλον, Gloss. Philox.

interprĕtor.opening: (in tmesi: inter quaecumque pretantur, Lucr. 4, 832 ), , v. dep. interpres , to explain , expound , interpret , give expression to , translate; to understand , conclude , infer , appreciate , recognize , comprehend. In…

inter-prĭmo.opening: v. a. premo , to press or squeeze to pieces , to crush (ante- and post-class.). Lit. : qui sacerdoti scelestus faucis interpresserit, Plaut. Rud. 3, 2, 41 .— Trop. , to suppress , conceal , Min. Fel. Oct. 10 .

Interpromĭnĭus.opening: a place in the territory of the Marrucini , on the Adriatic Sea , the modern S. Valentino , Inscr. ap. Romanelli, Topogr. Napol. 3, 117.

interpunctĭo.opening: interpungo , a placing of points between words , interpunctuation : interpunctiones verborum, Cic. Mur. 11, 25 .

interpunctum.opening: id. , i. q. interpunctio, a separating of words by points , interpunctuation : interpuncta verborum, Cic. de Or. 3, 46, 181 .

inter-pungo.opening: v. a. , to place points between words , to point , punctuate : cum scribimus, interpungere consuevimus, Sen. Ep. 40 .—Hence, , , P. a. , well divided : narratio distincta personis et interpuncta sermonibus, Cic. de Or.…

inter-purgo.opening: v. a. , to cleanse here and there : ficus, Plin. 18, 26, 65, § 243 .

inter-pŭto.opening: v. a. , to prune here and there : ficos, Cato, R. R. 50 : oleam, Varr. R. R. 1, 30 : rosas, Col. Arb. 30 .

inter-quĕror.opening: v. dep. : interquaesti sunt, false reading for leniter questi sunt, Liv. 33, 35, 10 .

inter-quĭesco.opening: v. n. , to rest between whiles , rest a while , pause , Lit. , of persons: bibe, interquiesce, Cato, R. R. 159 : cum haec dixissem et paululum interquievissem, Cic. Brut. 23, 91 . — Trop. , of things: dolor, Sen. Ep. 78…

inter-rādo.opening: v. a. (al. most exclusively in Pliny and Columella). Lit. , to scrape here and there : interrasa cortice, Paul. Nol. Carm. 27, 254 . — Esp., to emboss or work in low relief : latera vasorum, Plin. 33, 11, 49, § 140 .—…

interrāsĭlis.opening: adj. interrado , scraped here and there , worked in low relief , embossed (post-Aug.): aurum, Plin. 12, 19, 42, § 94 : decus, Ven. Carm. 1, 13, 15: corona, Vulg. Exod. 25, 25 al.

interrāsor.opening: id. , a filigreeworker : interrasor, διακρινητής, Gloss. Philox.

inter-regnum.opening: the time between the death of one king and the election of another , an interregnum : populus flagitare regem non destitit; cum . . . illi principes novam interregni ineundi rationem excogitaverunt, Cic. Rep. 2, 12, 23…

inter-rex.opening: one who held the regal office between the death of one king and the election of another; a regent , interrex , Liv. 1, 17 ; 1, 32 .— During the times of the republic, one who held the supreme power from the death or…
