in-terrĭtus.opening: adj. , undaunted , undismayed , unterrified ( poet. and in postAug. prose; cf. impavidus): bracchia interritus extulit ad auras, Verg. A. 5, 427 : spectatque interrita pugnas, id. ib. 11, 837 : vultu, Quint. 1, 3, 4 :…

inter-rīvātĭo.opening: rivo , a drawing off of water between two places (postclass.), Mart. Cap. 6, § 661 .

inter-rīvātus.opening: adj. id. , of water, drawn off between two places (postclass.), Mart. Cap. 6, § 584 ; 627 .

interrŏgāmentum.opening: interrogo , i. q. interrogatio, a question , interrogation : interrogamentum, πεῦσις, Gloss. Philox.

interrŏgātĭo.opening: id. , a questioning , inquiry , examination , interrogation (class.). In gen.: sententia per interrogationem, Quint. 8, 5, 5 : instare interrogatione, id. 6, 3, 38 : testium, Tac. A. 6, 47 : insidiosa, Plin. Ep. 1, 5, 7…

interrŏgātĭuncŭla.opening: dim. interrogatio , a short argument or syllogism : minutae, Cic. prooem. Par.: nectere, Sen. Ep. 82 .

interrŏgātīvus.opening: adj. interrogo , of or belonging to a question , interrogative : adverbia, Prisc. p. 1059 P.— Adv. : , interrogatively , Ps.-Ascon. ap. Verr. 2, 1, 56; Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 41 ; Schol. Vet. Juv. 9, 48 .

interrŏgātor.opening: id. , an interrogator (post-class.), Dig. 11, 1, 11, § 7 : mortuorum, a wizard , Mos. et Rom. Leg. Coll. 15, 1, 2.

interrŏgātōrĭus.opening: adj. interrogator , consisting of questions , interrogatory (post-class.): actiones, Dig. 11, 1, 1 : sonus, Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 25 .

inter-rŏgo.opening: v. a. , to ask , question , inquire , interrogate (syn.: percontor, sciscitor; class.). In gen.: hoc quod te interrogo, responde, Plaut. Merc. 1, 2, 70 : pusionem quendam interrogat Socrates quaedam, Cic. Tusc. 1, 34,…

inter-rumpo.opening: (in tmesi: inter quasi rumpere, Lucr. 5, 287 : inter quasi rupta, id. 5, 299 ), v. a. , to break apart or asunder , break to pieces , break up (class., esp. in part. pass. ). Lit. : contingere idem terrae necesse est,…

interruptĭo.opening: interrumpo , an interrupting , interruption , interval (postAug.). In gen.: muri, Hier. in Isa. 9, 3, § 12 sqq.: Oceani, Mart. Cap. 6, § 622 ; Macr. Somn. Scip. 2, 5, 32 . — Transf. Rhet. t. t., = ἀποσιώπησις, a sudden…

interruptor.opening: id. , an interrupter , spoiler : interruptor, διαφθορεύς, Gloss. Philox.

inter-saepĭo.opening: v. a. To fence about , hedge in , stop up , enclose , secure : foramina intersaepta, Cic. Tusc. 1, 20, 47 : quaedam operibus, Liv. 34, 40 : muro intersaepta urbs, id. 31, 46 : legionem densis arbustis, Tac. A. 3, 21 .—…

intersaeptum.opening: intersaepio , the midriff , diaphragm : intersaeptum, διάφραγμα, Gloss. Philox. — In gen., a boundary : regnorum, Aus. Grat. Act. § 82.

inter-scalmĭum.opening: scalmus , the space between two oars , Vitr. 1, 2, 4 .

inter-scalptus.opening: adj. , engraved in the middle , ornamented with carved work in the middle (late Lat.): columnae, Jul. Val. Res Gest. Alex. M. 3, 58 .

inter-scăpĭlĭum.opening: scapula , the space between the shoulders (post-class.), App. Flor. 14, p. 350, 11 ; Hyg. Astr. 3, 3 ; Isid. Orig. 11, 1, 93 .— Plur. , Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 4, 77 .

inter-scindo.opening: v. a. , to tear asunder , break down; to separate , interrupt (class.). Lit. : pontem, Caes. B. G. 2, 9 ; Cic. Leg. 2, 4 : aggerem, Caes. B. G. 7, 24 : venas, i. e. to open, Tac. A. 15, 35 . — Transf. , to break or cut…

inter-scrībo.opening: v. a. , to write between (post-Aug.). Lit. : alia interscribere alia rescribere, Plin. Ep. 7, 9, 5 .— Transf. , of the phœnix: in cauda (phoenicis) caeruleus interscribitur nitor, i. e. is intermingled, Sol. 33 .— Of…

intersĕcīvus.opening: adj. interseco , separated , cut off , Front. de Colon. 112 .

inter-sĕco.opening: v. a. , to cut asunder , separate , divide , intersect (postclass.): Tiberis media intersecans moenia, Amm. 29, 6, 17 : mediam paludem, id. 15, 4, 4 : aquarum ductibus intersectis, id. 21, 12, 17 : terras, id. 23, 6, 13…

intersectĭo.opening: interseco , an intersection; in archit., the part cut out between two teeth in indented work : intersectio, quae Graece μετοχή dicitur, Vitr. 3, 3 .

intersēmĭnātus.opening: Part. [intersemino], sown between or at intervals : remedia, App. Mag. p. 299, 30 .

inter-sĕro.opening: v. a. 2. sero , to put or place between , to interpose , add : causam interserens, Nep. Milt. 4, 1 : oscula mediis verbis, Ov. M. 10, 559 .

inter-sĭlĕo.opening: v. n. , to be silent in the meanwhile (late Lat.), Aug. Ord. 1, 19 .

inter-sisto.opening: v. n. , to stand still in the middle; trop., to stop in the midst , to make a pause in speaking (perhaps only in Quint.); of a speaker: indecentissime, Quint. 8, 3, 45 : ut intersistat fatigatus, id. 12, 11, 2 ; 10, 7,…

inter-sŏno.opening: v. n. , to sound among : remigiis, Stat. Th. 5, 344 .

inter-spătĭum.opening: the interval : diei, Tert. de Orat. 20 init.

inter-spersus.opening: spargo , strewn , sprinkled upon or between , interspersed (post-class.): interspersus rara canitie, App. M. 5, p. 165, 36 : sunt multa naturae munere interspersa, id. Mag. p. 299, 30 .

interspīrātĭo.opening: interspiro , a fetching of breath between (class.), Cic. de Or. 3, 44, 173 ; Plin. 23, 1, 18, § 29 .—In plur. : aequalibus interspirationibus uti, Cic. de Or. 3, 51 fin.

inter-spīro.opening: v. n. , to fetch breath between; hence, to admit air : qua interspirat (operculum), Cato, R. R. 112, 1 .

inter-sterno.opening: v. a. , to strew or lay between or among (perh. only in part. pass. ): bitumine interstrato, Just. 1, 2, 7 : assulis interstratis, Plin. 29, 2, 9, § 34 .

interstĕs.opening: adj. intersto , that stands or is between or among (eccl. Lat.), Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 33 .

interstinctĭo.opening: interstinguo , a distribution of gems, set here and there (post-class.), Arn. 6, 191 (al. interstitio).

inter-stinguo.opening: ( ), , v. a. In gen., to separate , mark off , divide; to variegate or checker with any thing (only in perf. pass. ): spatia interstincta columnis, Stat. S. 3, 5, 90 : facies medicaminibus interstincta, Tac. A. 4, 57 :…

interstĭtĭo.opening: intersisto . A pause , respite , interval , Gell. praef. init. ; id. 20, 1, 43 .— A difference , distinction : interstitio fieri quae poterit singulorum, cum, qui Juppiter fuerat, idem possit existimari Mars esse? Arn.…

interstĭtĭum.opening: id. , a space between , interstice , interval (post-Aug.). Of place, Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 6 ; Mart. Cap. 8, § 837 ; Amm. 20, 3, 10 .— Of time, an interval : quantum interstitii dies habet, Mart. Cap. 6, § 601 .— Plur. ,…

inter-sto.opening: v. n. and a. , to stand or be between or in the midst of (post-class.): tempus interstat, Amm. 22, 11, 3 ; 16, 9, 4 . —With acc. , Avien. Perieg. 849 .

inter-strĕpo.opening: v. n. , to make a noise among , to sound in the midst of ( poet. ): Nereus undis, Claud. in. Rufin. 2, 303 (but in Verg. E. 9, 36 , the correct read. is inter strepere).

inter-stringo.opening: v. a. , to squeeze tight ( poet. ): alicui gulam, to throttle, strangle, Plaut. Aul. 4, 4, 32 .

inter-strŭo.opening: v. a. , to join together; to add ( poet. and eccl. Lat.): qua spina interstruit artus, Sil. 10, 147 : nullam distinctionem, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 39 med.

inter-sum.opening: (interfŭtūrus, Cic. Div. in Caecil. 11, 35 ; in tmesi: interque esse desiderat pugnis, Arn. 7, 255 ), v. n. , to be between , lie between (class.; syn. interjaceo). In gen. Of space: quas (segetes) inter et castra unus…

inter-tālĕo.opening: v. a. talea , to cut out between , to cut by lopping off both ends , Non. p. 414, 27 .

inter-texo.opening: v. a. Lit. , to intertwine , interweave , intersperse : flores hederis intertexti, Ov. M. 6, 128 : vestis intertexta notis, Quint. 8, 5, 28 : chlamys auro intertexta, Verg. A. 8, 167 .— Transf. , to interweave , combine…

inter-tignĭum.opening: tignum , the interval or space between two beams , Vitr. 4, 2, 4 .

inter-tortus.opening: adj. , wound between , intertwisted : intertorto pectore, Petr. 124 dub.

inter-trăho.opening: v. a. , to take away , withdraw from : illi animam omnem intertraxero, Plaut. Am. 2, 2, 41 .

intertrīgĭnōsus.opening: adj. intertrigo , chafed , galled , Not. Tir. 180 .

inter-trīgo.opening: tero , a chafing , fretting , or galling of the skin in riding, walking, etc., Varr. L. L. 5, § 176 Müll.: intertrigines, Plin. 20, 14, 53, § 151 .

inter-trīmentum.opening: inter-tero; cf. Varr. L. L. 5, § 176 Müll. , loss by attrition , i. e. waste of gold or silver in melting or working it. Lit. : in auro, Liv. 34, 7, 4 : argenti, id. 32, 2 .— Trop. , loss , damage (syn.: detrimentum,…

inter-trītūra.opening: loss by attrition , wear and tear , i. q. intertrimentum: culleorum, Dig. 13, 7, 43, § 1 .

inter-trūdo.opening: v. a. , to thrust between (late Lat.), Aug. Ord. 1, 7 .

interturbātĭo.opening: interturbo , disquietude , confusion : patre animi quoque ejus haud mirabilem interturbationem causante, Liv. 23, 8, 7 .

inter-turbo.opening: v. a. , to produce disquietude or confusion , to cause a disturbance (ante- and post-class.): ne interturba, Plaut. Bacch. 4, 4, 81 ; Amm. 18, 2, 5 ; 26, 4 ; 31, 12 (but not Ter. And. 4, 1, 39 ; v. Bentl. ad h. l.): qui…

interturrĭum.opening: inter-turris , a wall between two towers , Inscr. ap. Don. 220, 3.

interŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [inter], inward , inner (post-class.): nexus, Mart. Cap. 9, § 888 : tunica, under-garment, shirt, App. Flor. 9 . — Also, subst. : , , , App. M. 8, p. 205, 16 : interulae dilores duae, Vop. Bonos. 15, 8 .

intĕr-undātus.opening: adj. , done in waves , waved , watered , Sol. 17, 5 .

intĕr-ūsūrĭum.opening: usura , interest accruing in the meantime (post-class.), Dig. 15, 1, 9, § 8 ; 35, 2, § 66 .

inter-văcans.opening: Part. [vaco], being empty between : intervacantibus spatiis, Col. 4, 32, 2 .

intervallātĭo.opening: intervallo , an interval (late Lat.): frequenti intervallatione, Cael. Aur. Signif. Diaet. Pass. 42 ; cf. id. ib. 45 .

inter-vallo.opening: v. a. vallum , to take or assume at intervals (post-class.): intervallando potestates assiduas, Amm. 27, 11 . — Hence, , , P. a. , separated , having intervals : febris, intermittent fever, Gell. 1, 12 : intervallato…

inter-vallum.opening: , prop., the open space within the mound or breastwork of a camp , the space between two palisades. Lit. : opus, pedum sexaginta, quod est inter vallum et legiones ... a quibusdam intervallum cognominatum, Hyg. de…

inter-vĕnĭo.opening: v. n. , rarely a. , to come between , come upon , to come in during , to intervene , interrupt (class.; syn. intercedo). Lit. , constr. with dat. , rarely with acc. Of persons: sponsae pater intervenit, Ter. And. 4, 3,…

inter-vēnĭum.opening: vena , the space between the veins , in the earth, in stones, etc., Vitr. 2, 6 ; 8, 1 .

interventĭo.opening: intervenio , an interposition , a giving security (post-class.), Dig. 4, 4, 7, § 3 .

interventor.opening: id. . One who comes in , a visitor : vacuus ab interventoribus dies, Cic. Fat. 1, 2 .— A surety , bondsman : si filius fidejussor, vel quasi interventor acceptus sit, Dig. 15, 1, 3 .— An intercessor , mediator , Lampr.…

interventus.opening: id. , a coming up , appearance , coming between , intervention. Lit. Of persons: interventus alicujus, Cic. Part. 8, 30 : Caleni et Calvenae, id. Att. 16, 11, 1 : Pomptini, id. Cat. 3, 3, 6 : hominum, Liv. 26, 19 :…

interversĭo.opening: interverto . An overthrowing , frustrating , thwarting (post-class.): praedicationis (Christi), Tert. adv. Marc. 1, 20 .— A purloining , pilfering , embezzling : de interversione convictus, Cod. 10, 70, 12.

interversor.opening: id. , a purloiner , pilferer , embezzler (post-class.), Cod. 10, 1, 8.

interversūra.opening: id. , a bending , turning (post-class.), Hyg. de Limit. 178 al.

inter-verto.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to turn aside , turn or draw in another direction , divert. Lit. : in extremis partibus triglyphi semicanaliculi intervertantur, Vitr. 4, 3, 5 : ductum aquae, Dig. 43, 20, 8 .— Trop. , to alter , change…

inter-vī^brans.opening: Part. [vibro], glittering among (post-class.): aethra intervibrans, Mart. Cap. 6, § 586 .

inter-vĭgĭlo.opening: v. n. , to watch between whiles , to awake now and then during sleep (post-Aug.), Lampr. Alex. Sev. 61 .

inter-vĭrĕo.opening: v. n. 1. vireo , to be green here and there , to be green between or among ( poet. ), Claud. Rapt. Pros. 2, 100 .— Of a snake: laetisque minax interviret herbis, Stat. Th. 4, 98 .

inter-vīso.opening: v. a. To look after , inspect secretly (class.): nunc interviso jamne a portu advenerit, Plaut. Stich. 3, 2, 3 : domum, id. ib. 1, 2, 90 ; id. Aul. 2, 2, 25 : intervisam, quid faciant coci, id. ib. 2, 9, 1 ; id. Rud. 2,…

inter-vōcālĭter.opening: adv. , loudly (postclass.): clamare, App. M. 9, p. 231, 13 .

intervŏlĭto.opening: v. n. freq. [intervolo], to fly about between or among : quem imbrem ingens numerus avium intervolitando rapuisse fertur, Liv. 3, 10, 6 .

inter-vŏlo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
inter-vŏlo.opening: v. n. and a. , to fly between or among (post-Aug.). Lit. , of birds, Col. 8, 10, 1 .— In gen.: ille recens oculis intervolat Idmon, flits before, Val. Fl. 5, 27 : medias intervolat urbes, id. 2, 614 : hasta auras, Stat.…

inter-vŏmo.opening: v. n. , to pour forth among ( poet. ): aequor undas, Lucr. 6, 894 .— Transf. : tenebras hinc blasphemiae intervomunt, Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 20 .

in-testābĭlis.opening: adj. , that is incapable , by reason of misconduct , of being a witness or of making a will. Lit. : si quis ob carmen famosum damnetur, senatusconsulto expressum est, ut intestabilis sit, ergo nec testamentum facere…

intestābĭlis.opening: adj. in-, 2. testis , = 2. intestatus; in double sense with 1. intestabilis, II. A., Plaut. Curc. 1, 1, 30 ; id. Mil. 5, 1, 24 (cf. Lorenz ad loc.).

in-testātus.opening: 2. testis , emasculated : si intestatus non abeo hinc, Plaut. Mil. 5, 1, 23 .

intestīnārĭus.opening: adj. intestinus , that does inlaid work or fine joiner ' s work (post-class.): FABER, Inscr. Orell. 4182 . — , , , a joiner , Cod. Th. 13, 4, 2.

intestīnus.opening: adj. intus , inward , internal , intestine (class.). Adj. : neque ut quidquam interesset inter intestinum et oblatum, Cic. Ac. 2, 15, 48 : occultum, intestinum ac domesticum malum, Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 15 ; id. Fam. 7, 25,…

in-testis.opening: adj. 2. in-, 2. testis , without testicles , emasculated , Arn. 5, 160 (cf. Salmas ad Tert. Pall. 3 ).

in-texo.opening: v. a. , to weave into , to inweave , interweave; to plait , join together , interlace , surround , cover. Lit. : purpureasque notas filis intexuit albis, Ov. M. 6, 577 : diversos colores picturae, Plin. 8, 48, 74, § 196…

intextĭo.opening: intexo , a weaving together , Ambros. in Luc. 10, 23, § 118 .

intextus.opening: intexo , an interweaving , joining together , Plin. 2, 8, 6, § 30 (but in Quint. 8, 4, 8 , contextu is the true reading).

in-thrŏnizo.opening: v. a. thronus , to enthrone , Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 12, 10 .

intĭbācĕus.opening: adj. intibus , of or belonging to endive , endive- : folia, Plin. 27, 12, 82, § 106 .

Intibili.opening: a city in Hispania Tarraconensis, on the farther side of the Ebro , at its mouth , now Torre del Sol , Liv. 23, 49, 12 ; the same, , Front. Strat. 2, 3 init.

intĭbus.opening: ( or ), , or , or ( ), , ἔντυβον , endive , succory (Cichorium, Linn.), Ov. M. 8, 666 ; Plin. 19, 8, 29, § 139 : intiba, Verg. G. 1, 120 ; 4, 120 : edere acres intibos, Pomp. ap. Non. 209, 4 (Com. Fragm. v. 128 Rib.):…

intĭmātĭo.opening: intimo , an announcement , declaration , intimation , Mart. Cap. 9, § 897 .

intĭmātor.opening: id. , one who announces or publishes (post-class.), Capitol. Pert. 10, 9 .

in-tĭmĭdē.opening: adv. , fearlessly; in comp. : intimidius, Amm. 26, 6, 17 .

intĭmo.opening: v. a. intimus , to put or bring into (post-class.). Lit. : partem gurgiti, Sol. 5 : Nilus mari intimatur, flows into, id. 32 ; Amm. 22, 8, 40 : argentum tabulis, Tert. Hab. Mul. 5 .— Transf. To drive or press into :…

intĭmōrātē.opening: adv. 2. in-timor , fearlessly , Vet. Interpr. Iren. 1, 1.

intĭmus.opening: adj. sup. [in-ter; cf. interior], inmost , innermost , most secret , most profound , most intimate (class.). Lit. : traxit ex intimo ventre suspirium, from the deepest part, Plaut. Truc. 2, 7, 41 : in eo sacrario…

intinctĭo.opening: intingo , a dipping in , a baptizing (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Poenit. 2, 6 ; 12 ; Hier. Ep. 125 .

intinctus.opening: intingo , a dipping in; concr., a sauce or pickle in which meat, etc., is dipped, Plin. 20, 7, 26, § 65 ; 20, 9, 33, § 81 ; in plur. , id. 15, 29, 35, § 118 .

in-tingo.opening: or , , v. a. tinguo , to dip in. In gen.: brassicam in acetum, Cato, R. R. 156 : buccas rubricā cerā omne corpus intinxti tibi, Plaut. Truc. 2, 2, 39 : faces in fossa sanguinis atra, Ov. M. 7, 260 : aliquid in aqua,…

intĭtŭbābĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-titubo , firm , unwavering (eccl. Lat.), Cassiod. in Psa. 134, 2 .

in-tĭtŭlo.opening: v. a. , to entitle , give a name to , Rufin. Invect. in Hier. 1, 8 .

in-tŏlĕrābĭlis.opening: adj. Act. , that cannot bear a thing, impatient (ante-class.): didicisset id ferre, et non esset intolerabilis, Afran. ap. Non. 125, 25 (Com. Fragm. v. 255 Rib.). — Pass. , that cannot be borne , insupportable ,…

intŏlĕrābĭlĭtas.opening: intolerabilis , insupportableness : intolerabilitas, ἀνυποιστότης, Gloss. Philox.

in-tŏlĕrandus.opening: adj. , insupportable , intolerable (class): tyrannus, Cic. Vatin. 9, 23 : anxitudo, Pac. ap. Non. 72, 33 (Trag. Fragm. v. 164 Rib.): res, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 35, § 78 : frigora, Liv. 22, 1 : licentia rerum, Cic. Agr. 1, 5,…

in-tŏlĕrans.opening: adj. Act. , that cannot bear or endure a thing (syn. impatiens), impatient , intolerant (not anteAug.); constr. with gen. : secundarum rerum nemo intolerantior fuit, Liv. 9, 18 : corpora intolerantissima laboris atque…

intŏlĕrantĭa.opening: intolerans . Act. , impatience : intolerantia, cum injurias, quae sunt ferendae, non toleramus, neque ferimus, Gell. 17, 19, 5 .— Pass. Unendurableness : sitis, Oros. 5, 15 .— Esp., of conduct, insufferableness ,…

in-tŏlĕrātus.opening: adj. , not nourished or refreshed by food : aeger, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 19, 124 .

in-tŏlĕro.opening: v. a. , not to bear , not to suffer , to take ill : tolerat, intolerat, Not. Tir. p. 140 .

in-tollo.opening: v. a. , to raise (post-class.): clamores absonos, App. M. 8, p. 213, 27 .

in-tondĕo.opening: v. a. , to clip off : fibrarum summas partes, Col. 11, 3, 31 .

in-tŏno.opening: (āvi), , v. n. , to thunder (class.). Lit. : partibus intonuit caeli Pater ipse sinistris, Cic. poët. Div. 1, 47, 106: cum deus intonuit, Ov. Tr. 5, 14, 27 : intonuere poli, Verg. A. 1, 90 : pater omnipotens ter…

intonsus.opening: adj. 2. in-tondeo , unshorn. Lit. : scindens dolore identidem intonsam comam, Acc. ap. Cic. Tusc. 3, 26 : capilli, Hor. Epod. 15, 9 : crinis, Tib. 1, 4,38 : Cynthius, Hor. C. 1, 21, 2 : deus, Ov. Tr. 3, 1, 60 ; Prop. 3,…

in-torpĕo.opening: v. n. , to be very stiff or numb : torpet, intorpet, Not. Tir. p. 94 .

in-torquĕo.opening: v. a. , to twist , turn round , turn to; to wrench , sprain (class.). Lit. : mentum in dicendo, to distort, Cic. de Or. 2, 66 : oculos, Verg. G. 4, 451 : caulem, Plin. 19, 6, 34, § 114 : talum, to sprain , Auct. B.…

intortĭo.opening: intorqueo , a curling , crisping (post-class.): capillorum, Arn. 3, 108 .

intortus.opening: P. a. , from intorqueo, q. v. fin.

intrā.opening: adv. and prep. contr. from intĕrā; sc. parte , on the inside , within (class. only as a prep. ). Adv. (post-Aug.). In gen.: quadraginta per oram, intra centum erunt, Quint. 1, 10, 43 : pars, quae intra, longior esse…

intrābĭlis.opening: adj. intro , that can be entered : ōs amnis, Liv. 22, 19, 12 .

intrā-clūsus.opening: (also separately ), , adj. claudo , shut in , enclosed (post-class.), Aggen. Urb. de Limit. 49 .

in-tractābĭlis.opening: adj. , not to be handled or meddled with , unmanageable , intractable; rough , rude , wild , fierce (since the Aug. per.): genus intractabile bello, Verg. A. 1, 339 ; cf. in comp. : homo naturā intractabilior et…

in-tractātus.opening: adj. 2. in-tracto , not handled or managed , untamed , wild; untried , unattempted (class.): equus, unbroken, Cic. Lael. 19, 68 : decor, wild, natural, simple, Grat. Cyn. 134 : lanae, not carded, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 5,…

intractĭo.opening: intraho , a dragging , drawling : linguae (al. contractio), Plin. 7, 12, 10, § 55 .

in-trăho.opening: v. a. To draw or drag along , to trail (post-Aug.): gressus, App. M. 5, p. 167, 23 .— To draw on : vesperam, App. M. 11, p. 268, 28 .— To throw abuse upon , assail : intrahere est contumeliam intorquere, Paul. ex Fest.…

intrā-mĕātus.opening: ( ), , , a going between or within : meatus, intrameatus, intromeatus, Not. Tir. p. 85 .

intrā-mūrānus.opening: adj. murus , that is within the walls (post-class.): magistratus, i. e. within the city of Rome , Ps.Ascon. ap. Verr. 2, 2, 6, § 17: spatia, Amm. 31, 7, 5 .

intrānĕus.opening: adj. intra , inner (opp. extraneus), Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 1, 12 .

in-transgressĭbĭlis.opening: adj. , that cannot be crossed , surpassed , transferred , Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 1, 14 .

intransĭbĭlis.opening: adj. 2. in-transeo , impassable (post-class.): Nilus, Hier. in Isa. 4, 11, 15 .

intransĭtīvus.opening: adj. 2. intranseo , gram. t. t., intransitive , i. e. that does not pass over to another person, Prisc. p. 982 P.— Adv. : , intransitively , Prisc. p. 1134 P.

in-transmĕābĭlis.opening: adj. , impassable (late Lat.): chaos, Claud. Mam. Stat. Anim. 3, 8 ; 9, 1 : oceanus, Jorn. Reb. Get. 1 al.

intrĕmisco.opening: v. n. inch. [intremo], to begin to tremble or quake (post-Aug.): insidiarum metu, Plin. 8, 4, 5, § 9 : terrae, id. 2, 79, 81, § 192 : manu intremiscente, Cels. 7 praef. med.

in-trĕmo.opening: v. n. and a. Neutr. , to tremble , shake , quake : totum corpus intremit, Cels. 3, 3 : omnem Murmure Trinacriam, Verg. A. 3, 581 : intremuit malus, id. ib. 5, 505 ; so, tellus, Ov. M. 1, 284 : quercus, id. ib. 7, 629 :…

intrĕmŭlus.opening: adj. intremo , shaking , tremulous (post-class.): manus, Aus. Epit. 34, 4 .

in-trĕmŭlus.opening: adj. 2. in , not tremulous , Cassiod. Var. 12, 39 .

intrĕpĭdans.opening: adj. 2. in-trepido , not shaking , firm , strong , powerful (post-class.), Inscr. ap. Paulovich. Marm. Macarens. p. 61.— Adv. : , without trembling , intrepidly : ascendere, Non. 530, 5 .

in-trĕpĭdo.opening: v. a. , to perform tremblingly , i. e. hastily , rapidly (postclass.): multos orbes, Symm. ap. Jornand. de Reb. Get. 15 .

in-trĕpĭdus.opening: adj. 2. in , unshaken , undaunted , intrepid ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Of living beings: intrepidus minantibus, Tac. H. 1, 35 : paucae bestiarum in hostem actae, Liv. 30, 33, 14 : dux, id. 44, 6, 6 : tranquillus,…

intrĭbŭlātus.opening: adj. 1. in-tribulo , pressed , pressed out (ante-class.), Cato, R. R. 127 .

in-trĭbŭo.opening: v. a. , to contribute , to pay tribute or taxes (post-Aug.): modo ne quid intribuant, Trajan. ad Plin. Ep. 10, 35 .

intrĭbūtĭo.opening: intribuo , a contribution (post-class.): ab intributionibus excusari, Dig. 49, 18, 4 : patrimonii intributionibus fungi, ib. 50, 1, 22 fin. al.

in-trīco.opening: v. a. 1. in-tricor , to entangle , perplex , embarrass (mostly ante- and post-class.). Of persons: Chrysippus intricatur hoc modo, Cic. Fragm. ap. Gell. 6, 2 : lenonem intricatum dabo, will entangle, embarrass him,…

intrīmentum.opening: intero , that which is rubbed in , a seasoning made of ingredients rubbed in , App. M. 10, p. 244, 31 .

intrinsĕcus.opening: adj. , inward (late Lat.): lumina cordis intrinseca, Cassiod. in Psa. 118, 82 .

in-trītus.opening: adj. 2. in , not rubbed or worn away , whole , entire , sound. Lit. : oliva, Col. 12, 49, 2 .— Transf. , not worn out , not exhausted : cohortes intritae ab labore, Caes. B. G. 3, 26, 2 .

intrō.opening: adv. contr. from interō sc. loco . Inwardly , internally; on the inside : omnia sana faciet, intro quae dolitabunt, Cato, R. R. 157, 7 : stare, Pall. 1, 40, 2 ; Cato, R. R. 157, 6 ; cf. Quint. 1, 5, 50 .— To the inside…

intro.grammar: āvi, ātum 1 v. a. and n.
intro.opening: (intrassis for intraveris, Plaut. Men. 2, 3, 63 ), , v. a. and n. 1. intro , to go or walk into , to enter (syn.: ingredior, introeo). Lit. In gen.; constr. with acc. , with in and acc.; poet. with dat. With acc. : tu…

intrō-cēdo.opening: v. n. , to go or come in , to enter : post opimas dapes quidam introcessit, App. M. 5, p. 160, 13 ; 10 , p. 254, 3.

intrō-clūdo.opening: v. a. , for intracludo, to shut up in : introcludo, ἐγκατακλείω, Gloss. Philox.

intrō-curro.opening: v. n. , to run in : per fretum, Nov. ap. Non. 205, 27 (Trag. Fragm. v. 59 Rib.).

intrō-dūco.opening: v. a. , to lead or bring into a place, to conduct into or within (syn.: induco, immitto). Lit. With acc. : gregem venalium, Plaut. Aul. 3, 3, 4 : noctu milites, Sall. J. 12, 4 : Volturcium cum legatis, id. C. 46, 6 :…

intrōductīo.opening: introduco , a leading in , introduction : adulescentulorum nobilium, Cic. Att. 1, 16, 5 : saeculi, a beginning, Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 6 .

intrōductor.opening: id. , an introducer , Ruf. ap. Hier. 2, 7 .

intrōductōrĭus.opening: adj. introductor , introductory : libri, Cassiod. Inst. Div. Litt. 24 .

intro-ĕo.opening: (ante-class. ; introiet for introibit, Hier. in Lucifer. 5 ), īvi, or , v. n. , to go in or into , to enter (syn.: intro, ingredior); constr. with in or ad and acc. , with acc. , with in and abl. , with inf. Lit. With…

intrō-fĕro.opening: v. anom. a. , to carry or bring in : lecticā in urbem introferri solitus est, Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 13, § 34 : lecticā est introlatus, Liv. 43, 7, 5 ; Suet. Tib. 30 .

intrō-grĕdĭor.opening: v. dep. gradior , to step or go in , to enter ( poet. ): introgressi, Verg. A. 1, 520 ; 11, 248 .

intrŏĭtōrĭus.opening: adj. 2. intrŏī tus , of or belonging to entry : introitorius, εἰσόδιος, Gloss. Philox.

intrŏĭtus.opening: introeo , a going in or into , an entering , entrance (class.). Lit. : nocturnus introitus Zmyrnam quasi in hostium urbem, Cic. Phil. 11, 2, 5 : militum, Caes. B. C. 1, 21 : in urbem, id. Dom. 28 : sol in Geminos…

intrō-jŭgus.opening: adj. , that is under the yoke : tres equi, Inscr. ap. Grut. 337.

intrō-mitto.opening: v. a. ( inf. pass. intromittier, Plaut. Truc. 4, 2, 53 ), to send in , to let in or into (syn. induco, immitto; class.). Lit. , with in and acc. : lepores in leporarium, Varr. R. R. 3, 12, 4 ; cf.: legiones (sc. in…

intrō-pōno.opening: v. a. , to put in , Not. Tir. p. 38 .

intrō-porto.opening: v. a. , to bring in Not. Tir. p. 11 .

intrō-rēpo.opening: v. n. , to creep in : introrepens mustela, App. M. 2, p. 125, 32 ; id. ib. 9 , p. 125, 19.

introrsum.opening: and (access. form INTROSVS, Inscr. Orell. 4034 ; v. also introversus), adv. contr. from intro versum . Form introrsum. Towards the inside , inwards , into : hostem introrsum in media castra accipiunt, Liv. 10, 33 . —…

intrō-rumpo.opening: v. n. , to break or burst into , to break in , enter by force : in aedis, Plaut. Mil. 2, 5, 50 : quod ea non posse introrumpere videbantur, Caes. B. G. 5, 51, 4 : cerva in cubiculum Sertorii, Gell. 15, 22, 9 .

intrōspecto.opening: v. a. freq. [introspicio], to look into (ante-class.): quid introspectant? Plaut. Most. 4, 2, 27 .

intrōspector.opening: id. , one who looks into , an inspector , August.

intrō-spĭcĭo.opening: v. a. specio , to look into , look at (syn. inspicio). Lit. To look into any thing: domum, Cic. Har. Resp. 15, 1, 33 : casas omnium, id. Div. 2, 51, 105 .— To look at : aliorum felicitatem aegris oculis, Tac. H. 2, 20 .…

intrō-trūdo.opening: v. a. , to thrust in (anteclass.): turundam introtrudito (al. intro trudito), Cato, R. R. 157, 14 .

intrō-vĕnĭo.opening: v. n. , to come in , trop., Jul. Obseq. de Prodig. 127 .

intrō-versus.opening: (also separately ), adv. for introrsus, towards the inside , inwards (ante-class.): introversus, et ad te Spectant, Lucil. ap. Non. 402, 7 : spectantia genua, Varr. R. R. 2, 7, 5 : se proicere, Petr. 63 .

intrōvŏcātus.opening: introvoco , a calling in (post-class.): primo introvocatu, Amm. 29, 1, 25 .

intrō-vŏco.opening: v. a. , to call in : aliquem, Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 26, § 66 (more correctly intro vocari, as in Liv. 10, 13, 11 ; 10, 24, 18 ).

in-trūdo.opening: v. a. , to thrust in , force in : se ipse inferebat et intrudebat, Cic. Caecin. 5, 13 B. and K. (dub.; Klotz, intro dabat; cf. Krebs, Antibarb. p. 620).

in-tŭĕor.opening: v. dep. (in tmesi: inque tueri, Lucr. 4, 713 ; archaic form indo tuetur, Enn. ap. Non. 378, 18 = Ann. 73 Vahl.; and intuor, Plaut. Most. 3, 2, 150 ; Ter. Heaut. 2, 4, 23 ; Turp. ap. Non. 470, 30 ; Sen. Hippol. 898 , and…

intŭĭtus.opening: intueor , a look , view , Salv. Gub. Dei , 2, 1: quaqua intuitus erat oculi, Varr. L. L. 7, § 7 Müll. (ex conject.).— Transf. (only in abl. sing. ), respect , consideration , Treb. Poll. Claud. 1, § 1 ; Dig. 23, 2, 67 ;…

in-tŭmesco.opening: v. n. inch. , to swell up; to rise ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : fluctus flatu intumescens, Plin. 2, 81, 83, § 196 ; id. 37, 5, 18, § 69 : vidi virgineas intumuisse genas, Ov. F. 6, 700 .— Of dropsical…

in-tundo.opening: v. a. , to bruise , pound (post-class.), Scrib. Comp. 71 .

in-turbātus.opening: adj. , undisturbed , calm (post-Aug.): sedit inturbatus, interritus, Plin. Pan. 64, 2 .

in-turbĭdus.opening: adj. Pass. , undisturbed , quiet (Tacitean): inturbidus externis rebus annus, Tac. A. 3, 52 : juventa, id. ib. 14, 22 .— Act. , not turbulent : vir sanctus, inturbidus, Tac. H. 3, 39 .

in-turgesco.opening: v. n. inch. , to swell up (post-class.), Veg. Vet. 1, 56, 19 .

intus.opening: adv. 1. in and the abl. termination -tus; Sanscr. -tas; cf. ἐντός . On the inside , within : ibi intro atque intus subducam ratiunculam, Plaut. Capt. 1, 2, 89 : vide sitne istaec nostra intus, id. Mil. 2, 6, 55 : intus…

in-tūtus.opening: adj. , unguarded , defenceless; unsafe , dangerous : rem publicam intutam patiemini, Sall. Hist. Fragm. 1, 48, 17 Dietsch: castra Gallorum intuta neglectaque, Liv. 5, 45, 2 : amicitia, Tac. A. 2, 42 : proinde intuta…

in-vādo.grammar: vāsi, vāsum 3 v. n. and a.
in-vādo.opening: (invasse, Lucil. Sat. 2, 4 ), , v. n. and a. , to go , come , or get into , to enter upon. Lit. : ignis quocumque invasit, cuncta disturbat ac dissipat, Cic. N. D. 2, 15, 41 : consul exercitusque Romanus sine certamine…

in-vălentĭa.opening: weakness , inability , indisposition (post-class.); with imbecilitas, Gell. 20, 1, 27 ; App. Dogm. Plat. 1, p. 11, 36 .

in-vălĕo.opening: to be strong against , to prevail (late Lat.; vique valebunt is the true reading, Lucr. 2, 301 ; v. Lachm. ad h. l.; and the perf. invaluit belongs to invalesco; v. the foll. art.): egredi conatus, invalente morbi…

in-vălesco.opening: v. n. inch. [valeo], to become strong; only trop. To grow strong or powerful : tantum opibus invaluit, Cic. Mur. 15 ; Tac. H. 2, 98 .— To increase , prevail , predominate : libido atque luxuria invaluerat, Suet. Vesp.…

invălētūdĭnārĭus.opening: , false read. for in valetudinario, Sen. Q. N. praef. 5.

in-vălētūdo.opening: 2. in , infirmity , indisposition , sickness (very rare; not in Cic.; cf. Krebs, Antibarb. p. 621), Plin. Val. 1, 18 .

in-vălĭdus.opening: adj. , not strong , infirm , impotent , weak , feeble (not in Cic. or Cæs.). Lit. : Camillus, jam ad munera corporis senectā invalidus, Liv. 6, 8 : milites, id. 23, 16 : paucos graves aetate aut invalidos inveniunt, id.…

invānum.opening: , false read. for in vanum, Tert. adv. Herm. 37 .

invāsĭo.opening: invado , an attack , invasion (post-class. for incursio, aggressio), Symm. Ep. 10, 41 (48).

invāsor.opening: id. , an invader , intruder , usurper (post-class.), Aur. Vict. Epit. 35 ; Cod. 7, 4, 5; Ambros. in Psa. 118 , Serm. 6, § 20.

invāsus.opening: invado , only in abl. sing. , an attack (post-class.), Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 4, 82 .

invectīcĭus.opening: or , , adj. inveho , imported , not indigenous , not native (post-Aug.). Lit. : columbae, Plin. 10, 29, 41, § 79 : frumentum, Ambros. Off. 3, 7 . — Trop. : gaudium, i. e. not hearty, not sincere, Sen. Ep. 23, 4 .

invectĭo.opening: id. . A bringing in , importing of goods, importation (opp. exportatio), Cic. Off. 2, 3, 13 : eodem flumine invectio, the entrance, id. Fin. 5, 24, 70 .— An attacking or assailing with words , an inveighing against ,…

invectīvālĭter.opening: adv. invectio , with invectives : carpere vitia, Sid. Ep. 1, 11 .

invectīvus.opening: adj. id. , scolding , abusive , reproachful , full of invectives (postclass.): oratio acer, et invectiva, Amm. 21, 10, 7 : volumen, id. 22, 14, 2 .— Subst. : , , , invectives , abuse : quaedam in principem, Amm. 28, 1,…

invector.opening: inveho , one who brings in , an importer (post-class.): lanati pecoris, Symm. Ep. 10, 27 .

invectrix.opening: invector , she that brings in or introduces (post-class.): mali, Ambros. Ep. 63, 3 .

invectus.opening: inveho , a bringing in (post-Aug.), only in abl. sing. : terrae invectu, Plin. 4, 1, 2, § 5 ; with gen. subj. : terrae nascuntur fluminum invectu, id. 2, 85, 87, § 201 .— Esp., an importation , Varr. R. R. 1, 16, 2 .

in-vĕho.opening: v. a. , to carry , bear , or bring to or into a place, in one's hands, on a horse, by water, etc. Lit. Act. With in and acc. : tantum in aerarium pecuniae invexit, ut, Cic. Off. 2, 22, 76 : Euphrates in Mesopotamiam…

in-vēlātus.opening: adj. , unveiled , uncovered (post-class.), Mart. Cap. 1, § 5 ; Ambros. in Psa. 43, § 22 .

in-vēnālis.opening: ἄπρᾶτος, not for sale , Gloss. Philox.

in-vĕnĭābĭlis.opening: adj. , not pardonable , Ambros. in Psa. 35, § 12 .

in-vĕnĭo.opening: v. a. ( fut. invenibit for inveniet, Pompon. ap. Non. p. 479, 28 ), lit., to come or light upon a thing; to find , meet with (cf.: reperio, offendo). Lit. : neque domi, neque in urbe invenio quemquam, qui illum viderit,…

inventārĭum.opening: invenio , a list , inventory (post-class.), Dig. 26, 7, 57 ; 27, 3, 1 ; 42, 5, 15 al.

inventĭo.opening: id. , an inventing , invention (class.). In gen.: illa vis quae investigat occulta, quae inventio atque excogitatio dicitur, Cic. Tusc. 1, 25, 61 ; 1, 26, 65 ; Plin. Pan. 72 .— Rhet., the faculty of invention : inventio…

inventĭuncŭla.opening: dim. inventio , a trifling invention (post-Aug.): minimis inventiunculis gaudere, Quint. 8, 5, 22 .

inventor.opening: invenio , one that finds out , a contriver , author , discoverer , inventor (class.): o mearum voluptatum omnium Inventor, inceptor, perfector, Ter. Eun. 5, 9, 5 : Aristaeus, qui olivae dicitur inventor, Cic. N. D. 3,…

inventrix.opening: inventor , she that finds out or invents , an inventress (class.): omnium doctrinarum inventrices Athenae, Cic. de Or. 1, 4, 13 : belli, id. N. D. 3, 21, 53 : carminis hujus, Ov. F. 6, 709 .

inventum.opening: invenio , a device , contrivance , invention (class.): ut te omnes di cum istoc invento atque incepto perduint, Ter. Heaut. 4, 6, 7 : inventa Zenonis, Cic. Mur. 29, 61 : inventum medicina meum est, Ov. M. 1, 521 :…

inventus.opening: , only in abl. sing. [invenio], an invention (for inventio), Plin. 17, 21, 35, § 162 .

in-vĕnustus.opening: adj. Not elegant or graceful , ungraceful , not beautiful , unattractive : scortillum, Cat. 10, 4 : non invenustus actor, Cic. Brut. 67, 237 : res, Cat. 12, 5 : arbustum, Col. 5, 6, 37 . — (Without Venus, i. e.)…

invĕrēcundĭa.opening: inverecundus , shamelessness , immodesty (post-class.), Arn. 4, 150 ; Tert. Apol. 7 ; Schol. Juv. 6, 456 .

in-vĕrēcundus.opening: (inverĕcundus, Ven. de Vit. S. Mart. 1, 393 ), adj. , without shame , shameless , immodest. Of persons: impudens, impurus, inverecundissimus, Plaut. Rud. 3, 2, 43 : deus, i. e. Bacchus, Hor. Epod. 11, 13 . — Of things:…

in-vergo.opening: v. a. , to incline or turn to , to pour upon ( poet. ; syn. infundo): liquores in me, Plaut. Curc. 1, 2, 12 : carchesia lactis, mellis, Ov. M. 7, 246 and 247: fronti vina, Verg. A. 6, 244 : pelago vina, Val. Fl. 2, 611 .

in-vērĭsĭmĭlis.opening: 2. in , adj. , improbable , not plausible : ratio, Prisc. 715 P.

inversĭo.opening: inverto , an inversion. Verborum, i. e. an ironical inversion of meaning , Cic. de Or. 2, 65 . 261.— An allegory , transl. of Gr. ἀλληγορία, Quint. 8, 6, 44 .— A transposition , i. q. ἀναστροφή (as quoque ego for ego…

in-versor.opening: v. dep. , to be among , to be occupied about (ante-class.): quīs inversamur, Lucil. ap. Lact. 6, 5, 2 (perh. quīs in versamur).

inversūra.opening: inverto , a turn , curve : aditus sine inversuris, Vitr. 5, 3, 5 .

inversus.opening: Part. and P. a. , v. inverto fin.

invertĭbĭlĭtas.opening: 2. in-verto , unchangeableness (eccl. Lat.): incommutabilitas, atque, ut ita dicam, invertibilitas, Aug. de Mor. Eccl. 13, 28 .

in-verto.opening: v. a. , to turn upside down , turn about , to upset , invert (class.). Lit. : pingue solum Fortes invertant tauri, to turn up, plough up, Verg. G. 1, 64 : campum, id. ib. 3, 161 : Boreas invertit ornos, upturns,…

in-vespĕrascit.opening: v. impers. , it becomes evening , evening is approaching : jam invesperascebat, Liv. 39, 50, 1 .

investīgābĭlis.opening: adj. investigo , that may be searched into , investigable (eccl. Lat.), Tert. ap. Herm. 43; Lact. 3, 26, 13 (dub. al. vestigabiles).

in-vestīgābĭlis.opening: adj. , not to be traced , unsearchable : gressus, Vulg. Prov. 5, 6 : divitiae Christi, id. Eph. 3, 8 : viae, id. Rom. 11, 33 .

investīgātĭo.opening: investigo , a searching or inquiring into , investigation (class.): rerum occultissimarum, Cic. Fin. 5, 4, 10 : veri (with inquisitio), id. Off. 1, 4, 13 : sapientiae ejus, Vulg. Isa. 40, 28 .

investīgātor.opening: id. , he that searches or inquires into , an investigator (class.): acer et diligens rerum, Cic. Univ. 1, 1 : antiquitatis, id. Brut. 15, 60 : conjurationis, id. Sull. 30, 85 . — A contriver : malorum, Vulg. Prov. 11,…

investīgātrix.opening: investigator , she that investigates (post-class.): comprehensio, Mart. Cap. 5, § 442 .

in-vestīgo.opening: v. a. (investigandum for investigandorum, Pac. ap. Non. 495, 26 ), to track or trace out , as a dog; to search after (class.). Lit. : canum tam incredibilis ad investigandum sagacitas narium, Cic. N. D. 2, 63, 158 :…

in-vestĭo.opening: v. a. , to clothe , cover (very rare). Lit. : scrupeo investita saxo, Enn. ap. Non. 162, 22 (Trag. Fragm. v. 139).— In gen., to surround : focum, Sen. Ep. 114, 6 .

in-vestis.opening: adj. 2. in , unclothed (postclass.). In gen.: homo nudus et investis, Tert. Pall. 3 .— In partic. Without a beard , beardless : puer, App. M. 5, p. 171 ; id. Mag. p. 336 : pueri et puellae, Macr. S. 3, 8 ; Fest. s. v.…

in-vĕtĕrasco.opening: v. n. inch. (in the form inveteresco, Inscr. ap. Att. dell' Acad. Rom. Archeol. 2, p. 46, n. 17), to grow old , to become fixed or established , to continue long (class.). Lit. : quibus quisque in locis miles…

invĕtĕrātĭo.opening: invetero , inveterateness; hence, an inveterate disease , Cic. Tusc. 4, 37, 81 .

in-vĕtĕro.opening: v. a. , to render old , to give age or duration to a thing. Lit. : aquam, Col. 12, 12 : allium, cepamque, Plin. 19, 6, 34, § 115 .— Pass. , to become old , to acquire age or durability; to abide , endure (class. but…

invĭcem.opening: , in MSS. and edd. often separately, ( poet. in tmesi: inque vicem, Verg. G. 4, 166 ; id. A. 12, 502 ; Ov. M: 6, 631; 9, 525; id. Her. 17, 180 ; Stat. Th. 2, 149 ; 7, 817 al. ), adv. in-vicis . Prop., by turns , in turn…

invictrix.opening: adj. invictus , unconquerable (post-class.): invictricis Fortunae filius, Inscr. ap. Grut. 1065, 6.

in-victus.opening: adj. 2. in , unconquered , unsubdued , not vanquished; hence unconquerable , invincible; constr. with ab , in and abl. or acc. , ad , contra , adversum , the simple abl. , with gen. and inf. (class.). With ab : invictum…

invĭdens.opening: P. a. , v. invideo fin. D. 1.

in-vĭdens.opening: adj. , not seeing , without vision : animalia, App. Mag. 51, p. 307, 4 .

invĭdentĭa.opening: invideo , an envying , envy : invidentiam esse dicunt aegritudinem susceptam propter alterius res secundas, quae nihil noceant invidenti, Cic. Tusc. 4, 8, 17 ; cf. id. ib. 3, 10, 21 ; Scrib. Ep. § 9; Cael. Aur. Tard. 4,…

invĭdĭa.opening: invidus , envy , grudge , jealousy , act. and pass.; cf.: ut effugiamus ambiguum nomen invidiae, Cic. Tusc. 3, 9, 20 : quoniam invidia non in eo qui invidet solum dicitur, sed etiam in eo cui invidetur, id. ib. 4, 7, 16…

invĭdĭōsus.opening: adj. invidia . Full of envy , envious , invidious , hostile (i. q. invidus; class.): illa peraeque Prae se formosis invidiosa dea est, Prop. 2, 28, 10 (3, 24, 10): vetustas, Ov. M. 15, 234 .— Enviable : possessiones,…

invĭdus.opening: adj. invideo , envious (class.): neque ambitiosus imperator neque invidus, Cic. Mur. 9, 20 : invida me spatio natura coercuit, Ov. Tr. 2, 531 : Lycus, Hor. C. 3, 9, 23 .— Subst. : , , , an envious person , a hater :…

in-vĭgĭlo.opening: v. n. , to watch or be awake in , at , over , or on account of any thing; to be watchful over or on account of; to be intent on , pay attention to , bestow pains upon. —With dat. (mostly poet. ): rei publicae, Cic.…

in-vīlesco.opening: v. n. inch. , not to become bad , Not. Tir. p. 66 .

in-vīlĭto.opening: v. a. , to account very bad , to despise : invilitat = εὐτελίζει, Gloss. Philox.

in-vincĭbĭlis.opening: adj. Invincible , unconquerable (post-class.): invincibile et insuperabile malum, Tert. adv. Herm. 11 . — Irrefutable : gravia et invincibilia dicere, App. Mag. p. 297 .— Adv. : , irrefutably , App. Flor. p. 360, 31 .

invinctus.opening: adj. 1. in-vincio , fettered (post-class.): aliquem invinctum habere (al. in vinculis), Dig. 48, 15, 6, § 2 .

invīnĭus.opening: adj. 2. in-vinum , that abstains from wine (post-class.), App. M. 11, p. 268, 26 .

in-vĭo.opening: v. a. , to tread upon , set foot upon : depavita, Sol. 2, 4 .

in-vĭŏlābĭlis.opening: adj. , invulnerable , imperishable ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): inviolabile telis servabant sacrumque caput, Sil. 16, 16 : inviolabilia haec ne credas forte vigere, Lucr. 5, 305 : elementum, App. Mund. 1, p. 57 :…

in-vĭŏlābĭlĭtas.opening: inviolability (eccl. Lat.), Rustic. c. Aceph. p. 1249.

in-vĭŏlātus.opening: adj. Unhurt , inviolate (class.): invulnerati inviolatique, Cic. Sest. 67, 140 : corpus omnium civium, id. Rab. Perd. 4, 11 : amicitia, id. Sull. 17 : vita, i. e. happy, pleasant, Sil. 13, 875 : terra, i. e. unploughed,…

in-vĭŏlentus.opening: adj. , not violent , Cassiod. Inst. Div. Lit. 20 ; Not. Tir. p. 88 .

in-vĭŏlo.opening: v. a. , not to violate , Not. Tir. p. 88 .

in-viscĕro.opening: v. a. , to put into the entrails (post-class.). Lit. : aliquid canibus, Nemes. Cyn. 214 . — Trop. : caritas inviscerata in cordibus nostris, deeply rooted, Aug. Serm. 24 .

in-visco.opening: v. a. viscum , to ensnare , capture with birdlime (late Lat.), Fulg. Serm. 69 . † , , v. a. id. , to besmear with birdlime , Not. Tir. p. 160 .

in-vīsĭbĭlis.opening: adj. , invisible , unseen (post-Aug.): foramina, Cels. praef.: terra, Tert. adv. Herm. 29 init. : deus, Lact. 7, 9 ; Paul. Nol. Carm. 35, 208 ; Tert. Carn. Chr. 12 : ea in nobis sunt meliora, quae sunt invisibilia, Aug.…

in-vīsĭtātus.opening: adj. , not seen. Unseen , invisible : sidera, Vitr. 9, 1, 4 : (potestatum) forma invisitata, vis cognita, App. Flor. p. 348, 16 . — Not visited : nulla civitas, Quint. Decl. 12, 18 . — Unseen , unknown : quae est enim…

in-vīso.opening: v. a. To look after , to go to see , to visit a person or place: ad meam majorem filiam inviso domum, Plaut. Stich. 1, 2, 9 : ad fratrem modo ad captivos alios inviso meos, id. Capt. 2, 3, 85 Brix: huc intro ad me…

invīsor.opening: invideo , one that envies , an envier (post-class.), App. Flor. 1, p. 375, 1 ; Ambros. Ep. 46, 1 .

in-vīsus.opening: adj. Unseen : sacra maribus non invisa solum, sed etiam inaudita, Cic. Har. Resp. 27, 57 : morbus, unknown, Cato, R. R. 141, 2 : invisus atque inaccessus in id tempus saltus, Flor. 4, 12, 27 .— Adv. : , without being…

invītābĭlis.opening: adj. invito , inviting , attractive , alluring (post-class.): sermones, Gell. 13, 11, 4 .

invītāmentum.opening: id. , an invitation. Lit. (post-class.): filia invitamento matris suae circumlata, App. Mag. p. 322, 39 ; id. M. 1, p. 103, 40 .— Trop. , an allurement , incitement , inducement : invitamenta naturae, Cic. Fin. 5, 6, 17…

invītātĭo.opening: id. , an invitation , incitement , challenge (class.): aderat et hospitum invitatio liberalis, Cic. Phil. 9, 3, 6 : in Epirum invitatio quam suavis! id. Att. 9, 12, 1 : quaedam ad dolendum, id. Tusc. 3, 34, 82 : fit…

invītātĭuncŭla.opening: dim. invitatio , a little invitation (post-class.): vini, little drinking-matches, Gell. 15, 2 in lemm.

invītātor.opening: invito , one who invites , an inviter ( poet. and post-class.), Mart. 3, 23 lemm.; Sid. Ep. 9, 13 ; Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 25 : aeternae vitae invitator, Christus, id. ib. — Esp., the officer charged with invitations at…

invītātōrĭus.opening: adj. invitator , of or belonging to invitation , inviting (postclass.): operatio, Tert. Anim. 57 : scripta, Hier. Ep. 1, 15 .

invītātrix.opening: id. , she that invites (post-class.), Symm. Ep. 1, 59 .

invītātus.opening: (only in abl. sing. ) [invito], an inviting , invitation (rare), Cic. Fam. 7, 5, 2 .

in-vĭtĭābĭlis.opening: adj. , inviolable , incorruptible , imperishable (post-class.): aevum, Prud. Psych. 626 .

invīto.opening: (invitassitis for invitaveritis, Plaut. Rud. 3, 5, 31 ), v. a. perh. for invicito; root vec-; Sanscr. vak-, speak; vak'as, word; cf.: vox, convicium; Gr. ϝεπ- in εἶπον, ὄψ , to invite , treat , feast , entertain (cf.…

in-vĭtŭpĕrābĭlis.opening: adj. , unblamable , Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 10 ; 4, 1 al.

invītus.opening: adj. perh. for in-vicitus; cf. Sanscr. va?*!-, to will; ava?*!as, unwilling; Gr. ἑκών, ἀ-έκων , against one ' s will , unwilling , reluctant (syn. coactus; class.). Of persons: invitus me vides, Plaut. Cas. 2, 4, 23 :…

invĭus.opening: adj. 2. in-via , without a road , impassable (syn.: inaccessus, devius; not in Cic. or Cæs.). Lit. : lustra, Verg. A. 4, 151 : longa via, id. ib. 3, 383 : saltus, Liv. 9, 14 : per invias atque ignotas rupes iter, id.…

invŏcātĭo.opening: invoco , an invoking , invocation (post-Aug.): deorum, Quint. 6, 1, 33 : dearum, id. 6, 1, 48 .— Absol. , Quint. 9, 2, 104 ; 11, 3, 115 ; Macr. S. 1, 16 .

invŏcātus.opening: adj. 2. in-voco . Uncalled (class.): imagines rerum, Cic. N. D. 1, 38, 108 : ego ad subsellia rei occurro, id. Fam. 8, 8, 1 .— Uninvited : invocatus soleo esse in convivio, Plaut. Capt. 1, 1, 2 : ut mihi ... invocato…

in-vŏcātus.opening: (only in abl. sing. ), a non-summoning : si injussu atque invocatu meo (verba) venerint, without my summons , Fronto ad Verum, ep. 1.

in-vŏco.opening: v. a. , to call upon , invoke (cf. imploro), esp. as a witness or for aid. Lit. With living beings as objects: alium invocat, cum alio cantat, Naev. ap. Isid. Orig. 1, 26 : invoco vos, Lares viales, Plaut. Merc. 5, 2,…

invŏlātor.opening: involo , a robber : κλέπτης, fur, involator, Gloss. Gr. Lat.

invŏlātus.opening: (only in abl. sing. ) [id.], a flying , flight : ex alitis involatu, Cic. Fam. 6, 6, 7 .

in-volentĭa.opening: , for involuntas, unwillingness , Salv. de Gub. Dei, 7.

invŏlĭto.opening: v. n. freq. [involo], to fly over a place. Lit. , with dat. : nec minus involitat terris, Prud. 13, 100 . — Transf. , of inanim. things, to flow or float over or upon : umeris involitant comae, Hor. C. 4, 10, 3 .

in-vŏlo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
in-vŏlo.opening: v. n. and a. , to fly into or to a place; to fly at , rush upon. Lit. (class.). With in and acc. : in villam columbae, Varr. R. R. 3, 7, 1 : vix me contineam, quin involem in capillum, from flying at his hair, Ter. Eun.…

in-vŏlŭcer.opening: adj. , unable to fly , unfledged (post-class.): pulli, Gell. 2, 29, 5 .

invŏlūcrum.opening: involvo , that in which something is wrapped , a wrapper , covering , case , envelope (class.). Lit. : candelabri, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 28, § 65 : clipei causa involucrum, vaginam autem gladii ... esse generata, id. N. D.…

invŏlūmen.opening: involvo , a wrapper , cover : involumen, ἐνείλημα, Gloss. Philox.

invŏlūmentum.opening: id. , a wrapper , covering , envelope , for involucrum (eccl. Lat.), Aug. Civ. Dei , 4, 8; Vulg. Sap. 7, 4 .

in-vŏluntārĭus.opening: adj. , involuntary (post-class.): emissio urinae, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 3, 18 ; 2, 5, 24 sq.— Adv. : , involuntarily , Boëth. Arist. Top. 4, 2.

in-vŏluntas.opening: unwillingness (eccl. Lat.): ex involuntate delinquere, Tert. Apol. 45 .

invŏlūtē.opening: adv. , v. involvo, P. a. fin.

invŏlūtĭo.opening: involvo , a rolling up , gathering of itself together : corporis spirae similis sive canina involutio, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 11, 103 ; concr., that which is inwrapped or infolded , Vitr. 10, 11 .

invŏlūto.opening: v. a. freq. [id.], to inwrap , infold (post-class.), Apic. 2, 1 .

in-volvo.opening: v. a. , to roll to or upon any thing. Lit. : Ossae frondosum involvere Olympum, Verg. G, 1, 282 : montes, Ov. M. 12, 507 : silvas, armenta secum, to sweep away with it, Verg. A. 12, 689 : miser involvitur In caput, id.…

involvŭlus.opening: ( ), , involvo , a worm or caterpillar that wraps itself up in leaves , Plaut. Cist. 4, 2, 63 .

in-vulgo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to bring before the public , to publish , make known : disciplinas acroaticas libris foras editis, Gell. 20, 5, 7 ; cf. id. 4, 9, 9 .— Absol. : quo die Allobroges involgarunt, to give evidence, make a…

invulnĕrābĭlis.opening: adj. , invulnerable : hostis, Sen. Ben. 5, 5, 1 .— Transf. : cum animum virtus induravit, undique invulnerabilem praestat, Sen. Cons. ad Helv. 13, 2 ; id. Ep. 9, 2 .

in-vulnĕrātus.opening: adj. , unwounded : invulnerati inviolatique, Cic. Sest. 67, 140 .

Iōb.opening: , and , , , Job , Prud. Psych. 103 ; Vulg. Job, 1, 1 et saep.

iŏhĭa.opening: , false read. for ohe, Plaut. Merc. 4, 3, 31 ; v. Ritschl ad h. l.

Iol.opening: the former name of the city of Cæsarea in Numidia , now Ser-Sel , Plin. 5, 2, 1, § 20 ; Mel. 1, 6 .

Iollas.opening: A Trojan , Verg. A. 11, 640 .— A shepherd , Verg. E. 2, 57 ; 3, 76 . — A Greek writer on medicine , Plin. 34, 10, 22, § 104 al.

Iprasturgi.opening: a town of Bætica , Plin. 3, 1, 3, § 10 (Jahn reads Ipra, Isturgi).

ipse.opening: ( , Cato, R. R. 70 ; 71 ; Plaut. Ps. 4, 7, 43 ; id. Trin. 2, 2, 40 ; 3, 1, 10 et saep.; Ter. And. 3, 2, 15 ; id. Eun. 3, 4, 8 , id. Hec. 3, 5, 5 ; Jusjur. Milit. ap. Gell. 16, 4, 4 al. ), a, um (ipsud, Gloss. Philox.);…

ipsullices.grammar: bracteae in virilem muliebremque speciem expressae

Irĭātes.opening: the inhabitants of Julia Iria, in Liguria , near Dertona (now Voghierro ), Liv. 31, 10 (cf. Plin. 3, 5, 7, § 49 ).

Irĭnē.opening: a small island in the Argolic Gulf , the modern Ypsili, Plin. 4, 12, 19, § 56 .

irpex.opening: ( ), , , = ἅρπαξ, a large rake with iron teeth , used for the same purpose as our harrow (still called erpice by the Italians), Cato, R. R. 10, 2 ; Varr. L. L. 5, § 136 Müll.; Serv. Verg. G. 1, 95 .

irpus.opening: Sabine , a wolf : (lupus) quem irpum dicunt Samnites, Paul. ex Fest. p. 106 Müll.; Serv. ad Verg. A. 11, 785 .

irrădĭo.opening: ( ), , v. a. and n. 1. inradio , to illumine , irradiate; to beam forth , cast forth rays ( poet. and post-class.). Act. Lit. : hoc undique gemmae irradiant, Stat. Th. 6, 64 .— Trop. : artes Romanis floribus, Claud.…

irrādo.opening: ( ), , v. a. 1. in-rado . To scrape into : eodem silphium irradito, Cato, R. R. 157, 7 ; cf. § 8.— To scrape , shave , make smooth : caput irrasum, shaved, bald, Plaut. Rud. 5, 2, 16 .

irrāsus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inrado , unshaved , unpolished , not smooth ( poet. ): aptabat dextris irrasae robora clavae, Sil. 8, 584 .

irrătĭōnābĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. , without reason , irrational (post-class.; not in Quint., v. Spald. ad Quint. 2, 16, 16 ): error, App. Dogm. Plat. p. 21 : motus, Amm. 31, 12, 15 .— Of musical intervals, = logica, proportional , harmonic :…

irrătĭōnālis.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-rationalis , without reason , irrational (postAug.): animal, Quint. 7, 3, 3 ; 24 ; Sen. Ep. 113, 17; 118, 14; 124, 23: usus, mechanical exercises, Quint. 10, 7, 11 : anima, Tert. Poen. 12 .— Subst. : ,…

irraucesco.opening: ( ), , v. inch. n. [1. in-raucus], to become hoarse : si paulum irrauserit, Cic. de Or. 1, 61, 259 .

irraucus.opening: adj. id. , hoarse : vox, Plin. Val. 1, 2 .

irrĕcĭtābĭlĭter.opening: adv. 2. in-recito , unutterably , unspeakably , Venant. Carm. 3, 9, 49.

irrĕcōgĭtātĭo.opening: ( ), , 2. inrecogitatio , inconsiderateness , thoughtlessness (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Exhortat. ad Cast. 4 .

irrĕcordābĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inrecordabilis , not to be remembered (postclass.): oblitteratio, Arn. 2, 62 .

irrĕcŭpĕrābĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inrecupero , irrecoverable , irreparable , unalterable (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Pud. 14 .

irrĕcūsābĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inrecusabilis , not to be refused (post class.): occasio, Cod. Just. 3, 1, 13 ; Hier. Ep. 60, 14 . —Hence, adv. : , without possibility of refusal , Rustic. c. Aceph. p. 1218.

irrĕdĭvīvus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inredivivus , irreparable , that cannot be restored , Cat. 17, 3 .

irrĕdux.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-redux , that does not bring back : via, Luc. 9, 408 .

irrĕformābĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inreformo , unalterable (late Lat.), Tert. Verg. Vell. 1 ; adv. Valent. 29.

irrĕfrāgābĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inrefragor , irrefragable (eccl. Lat.), Pseudo ug. ad Fr. Erem. Serm. 35 .—Hence, adv. : , inviolably : Catholici dogmatis fundamenta observare, Ven. Fort. Vit. Hilar. 1 praef. 1.

irrĕfūtābĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-refuto , irrefutable (post-class.), Arn. 4, 139 . — , adv. : , Jul. ap. Aug. c. Sec. Resp. Jul. 1, 48.

irrĕfūtātus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inrefutatus , unrefuted (eccl. Lat.), Lact. 5, 16 fin.

irrĕgĭbĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-regibilis , ungovernable , unmanageable (postclass.), Veg. Vet. 2, 3 : laxitas corporis (i. e. very large , = immoderata), Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 14, 107 .

irregressĭbĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inregressio , from which there is no return (eccl. Lat.): transgressio, Aug. Civ. Dei , 8, 22.

irrĕlĭgātus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inreligatus , unbound : croceas irreligata comas, Ov. A. A. 1, 530 : ratis, not moored , Pedo Albin. 2, 5 .

irrĕlĭgĭo.opening: ( ), , 2. in-religio , impiety , irreligion (post-class.), App. Trismeg. p. 91 (but not in Auct. Her. 2, 21 ).

irrĕlĭgĭōsĭtas.opening: ( ), , irreligiosus , irreligion , impiety (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Apol. 24 ; Salv. Gub. Dei , 6, 15: inexpiabilis, Hilar. in Matt. 5, 13; id. Trin. 1, 36 al.

irrĕlĭgĭōsus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inreligiosus , irreligious , impious (not anteAug.): irreligiosum ratus, sacerdotes pedibus ire, etc., Liv. 5, 40 fin. : cujus (templi) dedicationem differre longius irreligiosum est, Plin. Ep. 4, 1, 5 ;…

irrĕmĕābĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-remeabilis , from which one cannot return , irremeable ( poet. ): error, Verg. A. 5, 591 : via, Sen. Herc. Fur. 548 : unda, i. e. the Styx, Verg. A. 6, 425 : litus, Sil. 5, 41 .

irrĕmĕdĭābĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inremediabilis , incurable , irremediable , beyond cure (post-Aug.). Lit. : in vino cicuta, Plin. 25, 13, 95, § 152 .— Trop. In gen.: scelus, Plin. 11, 53, 115, § 279 : summa malorum, Salv. Gub. Dei, 4,…

irrĕmissĭbĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inremissibilis , unpardonable , irremissible (eccl. Lat.): peccata, Tert. Pudic. 2 : blasphemia, Hier. Ep. 42, 1 .

irrĕmūnĕrābĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-remuneror , that cannot be compensated , not to be remunerated (post-class.): beneficium, App. M. 3, p. 139 ; 11 , p. 269.

irrĕmūnĕrātus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-remuneratus , unrewarded , unremunerated (late Lat.): suboles, Cassiod. Var. 2, 11 : militia, id. ib. 2, 28 .

irrĕpărābĭlis.opening: ( ), adj. 2. in-reparabilis , irreparable , irrecoverable , irretrievable ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): tempus, Verg. G. 3, 284 ; id. A. 10, 467 : vita, Sen. Ep. 123, 10 : fuga temporis, Col. 11, 1, 29 .

irrĕpercussus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-repercutio , not retorted , not refuted , Tert. Apol. 16 .

irrĕpertus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inreperio , not found , undiscovered : aurum, Hor. C. 3, 3, 49 : puer, Sen. Med. 648 .

irrĕplētus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inrepleo , not filled , Paul. Nol. Carm. 17, 60 .

irrēpo.opening: ( ), , v. n. 1. in-repo , to creep in , into , upon , or to a place. Lit. , with ad : draconem repente irrepsisse ad eam, Suet. Aug. 94 .— With dat. : (salamandra) si arbori irrepsit, Plin. 29, 4, 23, § 74 .— Absol. :…

irrĕposcĭbĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inreposcibilis , that cannot be demanded back (post-class.), App. Mag. p. 332, 18 ; Sid. Ep. 8, 15 .

irrĕprĕhensĭbĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-reprehendo , unblamable , irreprehensible (post-class.), Arn. 2, 53 (with inculpabiles): mandatum, Tert. Res. Carn. 23 ; Vulg. 1 Tim. 6, 14 .— Adv. : , unblamably , Claud. Mam. Stat. Anim. 1, 3, 7 .

irrĕprĕhensus.opening: ( ), , adj. id. , blameless , without blame ( poet. ): probitas, Ov. Tr. 5, 14, 22 : responsa, true, id. M. 3, 340 .

irreptĭo.opening: ( ), , irrepo , a creeping in (late Lat.), Aug Ep. 107.

irrepto.opening: ( ), , v. n. and a. [id.], to creep into or to a place, to creep or crawl upon ( poet. ). With dat. : nemus Lycurgo, cover, Stat. Th. 4, 386 : umeris avi, id. S. 3, 177 .— With acc. : Mycenas, Stat. Th. 11, 731 .

irreptor.opening: ( ), , id. , one who creeps in or upon , an encroacher : agrorum, Cod. Th. 2, 26, 2.

irrĕquĭēbĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inrequiesco , that cannot be stilled , restless : sitis, that cannot be allayed, Scrib. Comp. 105 ; Marc. Emp. 20 .

irrĕquĭes.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-requies , restless , unresting , always in action or motion (late Lat.): cor, Aus. Idyll. 12, 5 : gens, id. ib. 12, 42 .

irrĕquĭētus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inrequietus , unquiet , restless ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): Enipeus, Ov. M. 1, 579 : illa, id. ib. 5, 443 : Charybdis, id. ib. 13, 730 : agitatio, Sen. Brev. Vit. 10, 6 : circuitus mundi, Plin. 2,…

irrĕquīsītus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-requiro , unsought for (late Lat.), Sid. Ep. 9, 3 .

irrĕsectus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-reseco , uncut , unpared : pollex, Hor. Epod. 5, 47 .

irrĕsŏlūbĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-resolubilis , indissoluble : nexus, App. Dogm. Plat. 2, p. 19, 22 ; Amm. 30, 4 .

irrĕsŏlūtus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inresolvo , unloosed , not loosened : vincula, Ov. P. 1, 2, 21 : nexus, Boëth. Cons. 3; Metr. 2, 4.

irrespīrābĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inrespiro , in which one cannot breathe : hypobrychium, Tert. Idol. 24 .

irrestinctus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inrestinguo , unextinguished : altaria, Sil. 3, 29 .— Trop. , of the feelings: ardor, Mart. Cap. 9, § 915 .

irrētĭo.grammar: īvi or ĭi, ītum, 4 v. a.
irrētĭo.opening: ( ), , v. a. 1. in-rete , to catch in a net , to ensnare , entangle (syn.: illaqueo, implico; class.). Lit. : quid ad illum, qui te captare vult, utrum tacentem irretiat te, an loquentem? Cic. Ac. 2, 29, 94 : solum…

irrĕtortus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inretorqueo , not turned back : oculo irretorto Spectat acervos, without looking back, Hor. C. 2, 2, 23 .

irrĕtractābĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inretracto , irrevocable : sententia, Aug. Conf. 10, 33 . — , adv. : , irrevocably : custodire decreta, Facund. Def. 12, 3.

irrĕvĕrens.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inrevereor , that does not show due respect or veneration , disrespectful , irreverent (postAug.). With gen. : operis, Plin. Ep. 8, 21, 3 .— With dat. : matri, Spart. Carac. 2 . — With in and acc. : in…

irrĕvĕrentĭa.opening: ( ), , irreverens , want of due respect or reverence , irreverence , disrespect (post-Aug.): coalitam libertate irreverentiam prorupisse, Tac. A. 13, 26 : juventutis, id. ib. 3, 31 : adversus, fas nefasque, id. H. 3, 51…

irrĕvŏcābĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inrevocabilis , that cannot be recalled , irrevocable. Lit. : vulgus, uncontrollable, Luc. 1, 509 : praeterita aetas, Lucr. 1, 468 : in casum irrevocabilem se dare, unalterably, Liv. 42, 62, 3 : semel…

irrĕvŏcandus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. in-revoco , not to be recalled , irrevocable : error, Claud. B. G. 122 .

irrĕvŏcātus.opening: ( ), , adj. id. , not called back. * Not asked to repeat a thing; without an encore : cum loca jam recitata revolvimus irrevocati, Hor. Ep. 2, 1, 223 .— That cannot be called or kept back : ab acri caede lupus, Ov. M.…

irrīdĕo.grammar: rīsi, rīsu , 2 v. n. and a.
irrīdĕo.opening: ( ), , v. n. and a. [1. in-rideo] (collat. form , , M. Brutus ap. Diom. p. 378 P.). Neutr. , to laugh at a person or thing, to joke , jeer : irrides in re tanta, Ter. Heaut. 5, 2, 29 ; id. And. 1, 2, 33 : tam aperte,…

irrīdĭcŭlē.opening: ( ), adv. 2. in-ridicule , unwittily : non irridicule quidam ex militibus dixit, i.e. wittily, Caes. B. G. 1, 42, 6 .

irrīdĭcŭlum.opening: ( ), , irrideo , a laughing-stock : irridiculo habere, to make a laughing-stock of, Plaut. Poen. 5, 4, 10 : irridiculum esse, to be a laughing-stock, id. Cas. 5, 2, 3 .

irrĭgātĭo.opening: ( ), , irrigo , a watering , irrigating : quos (pulvinos) irrigationes abluunt, Varr. R. R. 1, 35, 1 : agrorum, Cic. Off. 2, 4, 14 : agri, id. de Sen. 15, 53 .— With gen. subj. : irrigatione fluminis diluere aliquid,…

irrĭgātor.opening: ( ), , id. , a waterer (late Lat.), Aug. Ep. 95, 7 .

irrĭgo.opening: ( ), , v. a. 1. inrigo , to lead or conduct water or other liquids to a place. Lit. : amurcam ad arbores, Cato, R. R. 36 : aquam in areas, id. ib. 151 : imbres (plantis), Verg. G. 4, 115 .— Transf. To water , irrigate :…

irrĭgŭus.opening: ( ), , adj. 1. in-riguus , supplied with water. Lit. Pass. , watered , well-watered , irriguous; full of water , wet , swampy : herba, Plaut. Trin. 1, 1, 9 : hortus, Hor. S. 2, 4, 16 : pratum, Prop. 1, 20, 37 : campus,…

irrīmor.opening: ( ), , v. dep. 1. in-rimor , to explore : incultos sinus, Pac. ap. Non. 382, 9 .

irrīsĭbĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. irrideo , laughable , ridiculous , Aug. Serm. 87, 7 (9).

irrīsĭo.opening: ( ), , id. , a deriding , mocking , mockery : liber a tali irrisione Socrates, Cic. Ac. 2, 39, 123 : stultitiae, Auct. Her. 1, 6, 10 : irrisio omnium, Cic. de Or. 1, 12, 50 : cum irrisione audientium, id. de Off. 1, 38,…

irrīsīvē.opening: adv. id. , mockingly , ironically , Amm. 16, 12, 67 ; Schol. Juv. 4, 13 ; 13, 33 .

irrīsor.opening: ( ), , id. , a derider , mocker , scoffer : hujus orationis et sententiae, Cic. Par. 1, 3, 13 ; Prop. 1, 9, 1 .

irrīsōrĭus.opening: ( ), , adj. irrisor , scornful : versutia, Mart. Cap. 8, § 809 .— Adv. : , ironically , Serv. Verg. E. 7, 27 .

irrīsus.opening: ( ), , irrideo , a scoffing , mocking , mockery , derision : irrisu coarguere aliquid, Plin. 28, 8, 29, § 114 : irrisum pueri sperans, Tac. A. 13, 15 : irrisui esse, to be a laughing-stock, Caes. B. C. 2, 15 : hostibus…

irrītābĭlis.opening: ( ), , adj. 1. irrito . Easily excited or enraged , irritable : irritabiles esse animos optimorum saepe hominum, Cic. Att. 1, 17, 4 : genus vatum, Hor. Ep. 2, 2, 102 ; Amm. 18, 6, 18 .— * Act. , easily exciting :…

irrītābĭlĭtas.opening: ( ), , irritabilis , irritability , App. Doctr. Plat. 1, p. 11, 28 .

irrītāmen.opening: ( ), , 1. irrito , an incitement , incentive , provocative ( poet. ): opes, animi inritamen avari, Ov. M. 13, 434 : amoris, id. ib. 9, 133 .—In plur. : cum (taurus) sua terribili petit inritamina cornu Poeniceas vestis,…

irrītāmentum.opening: ( ), , id. , an incitement , incentive , provocative (not before the Aug. period, and most freq. in plur. ; syn.: incitamentum, invitamentum, illecebra): irritamentis iras militum acuere, Liv. 40, 27 : certaminum…

irrītātē.opening: adv. , v. 1. irrito, P. a. fin.

irrītātĭo.opening: ( ), , 1. irrito , an incitement , incentive , provocative , irritation , stimulant (not ante-Aug.). Physical: tenesmos est irritatio ultimae partis directi intestini, Scrib. 142 init. : tamquam edendi irritationes…

irrītātor.opening: ( ), , 1. irrito , an inciter , instigator : cum irritator accesserit, Sen. Ep. 108, 8 ; Vulg. Ezech. 2, 7 .

irrītātrix.opening: ( ), , irritator , she who incites , Vulg. Interpr. Ezech. 24, 3 .

irrītātus.opening: ( ), , 1. irrito , an inciting , instigating : irritatu suo, Paul. Sent. 1, 15, 3 .

irrīto.opening: ( ), ( perf. subj. inritassis for inritaveris, Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 298 ), v. a. cf. ἔρις, ἐρέθω, ἐρεθίζω, Georg Curtius Gr. Etym. p. 342, ed. 4 , to incite , excite , stimulate , instigate , provoke , exasperate ,…

irrĭto.opening: ( ), , v. a. 1. irritus , to make void , invalidate (late Lat.), Cod. Th. 3, 12, 2.

irrĭtus.opening: ( ), , adj. 2. inratus , invalid. Lit. Undecided , unfixed , void , of no effect : quod modo erat ratum, irritum est, Ter. Phorm, 4, 7, 58 : testamentum irritum facere, Cic. Phil. 2, 42, 109 : testamentum pro irrito…

irrōbŏrasco.opening: ( ), , v. inch. n. [in-roborasco], to acquire strength , take root , become confirmed : verbi significatio irroboravit, Gell. 1, 22, 1 .

irrŏgātĭo.opening: ( ), , in-rogatio , an imposing , adjudicating : multae, Cic. Rab. Perd. 3, 8 : dupli vel quadrupli, Plin. Pan. 40, 5 .
