jĕcuscŭlum.opening: dim. jecur , a little liver , Cic. Div. 2, 14, 33 ; Plin. 11, 37, 76, § 196 ; or , Plin. l. l., Jahn; Apic. 4, 2 .

jējūnātor.opening: id. , a faster (eccl. Lat.), Aug. Ep. 86 ; Hier. in Jov. 2, 16 .

jējūnĭōsus.opening: adj. com. intens. form, from jejunus , fasting, hungry : neque jejuniosiorem (diem) nec magis ecfertum fame vidi, Plaut. Capt. 3, 1, 6 .

jējūnĭtas.opening: id. , a fasting, emptiness of stomach . Lit. : jejunitatis plenus, anima foetida, Plaut. Merc. 3, 3, 13 . — Transf. , dryness : calida umoris, Vitr. 2, 6, 4 ; 7, 4, 3 .— Trop. Of speech, dryness, poverty, meagreness :…

jējūnĭum.opening: id. , a fast-day, fast . Lit. : jejunium Cereri instituere, Liv. 36, 37 : illos longa domant inopi jejunia victu, Ov. M. 1, 312 : solvere, id. ib. 5, 534 : ponere, id. F. 4, 535 : jejunia indicere, Hor. S. 2, 3, 291 :…

jējūno.opening: v. n. id. , to fast (late Lat.): Abraham peregrinis prandentibus cibos jejunaturus apposuit, Hier. Ep. 66, 11 : cum jejunas laeta sit facies tibi, id. ib. 22, 27 .— With dat., to abstain from a thing: Adam salvus…

jējūnus.opening: adj. kindr. to Sanscr. yam, refrenare, cohibere; intens. yanyam, Bopp. Gloss. p. 276, a , fasting, hungry, abstinent, not partaking of food . Lit. : in scenam qui jejunus venerit, Plaut. Ps. prol. 12 : sic expletur…

jentācŭlum.opening: jento , a breakfast , taken immediately after rising, by children, valetudinarians, etc. (whereas the prandium was not taken till towards noon): epulas interdum quadrifariam dispertiebat: in jentacula et prandia et…

jentātĭo.opening: id. , a breakfasting, breakfast , Firm. Math. 2, 10.

jento.opening: v. n. contr. for jejunito from jejunus , to breakfast : quod pulli jentent, Varr. ap. Non. 126, 14 ; Afran. ib.; Suet. Vit. 7 : ut jentes, sero venis, Mart. 8, 67 .

Jērĕmīas.opening: (scanned īĕrĕmīas, Prud. Ham. 450 : Jērĕmĭās, Juvenc. Ev. Hist. 3, 269 ), , , the Hebrew prophet Jeremiah : sermo Domini quem locutus fuerat per os Jeremiae, Vulg. 2 Par. 36, 22 ; id. Jer. 27, 1 et saep.; called , Lact.…

Jerĭcho.opening: indecl., the Hebrew city Jericho , Vulg. 2 Reg. 10, 5 al.

Jēsus.opening: (also , trisyl.), , , = Ἰησοῦς , a Hebrew name; esp., Jesus : venturum praemisso nomine Jesum, Sedul. 1, 153 ; Lact. 4, 12, 6 ; Arat. Act. Apost. 1, 274: Nazara, cui felix patria est et nomen lësus, Juvenc. 2, 106 .—…

Jōannes.opening: (trisyl. and quadrisyl.) and , , , = Ἰωάννης . John the Baptist , Lact. 4, 15, 2 ; Vulg. Matt. 3, 1 .— Nom. Joannis, Prud. Cath. 7, 46 .— John the Evangelist , Vulg. Matt. 4, 21 ; Prud. Apoth. 9 .— Nom. Joannis, Prud.…

jŏcābundus.opening: adj. jocor , sportive, jocular (post-class.): juventus, Val. Max. 2, 4, 4; Lact. 2, 7, 11 : satura, Mart Cap. 6, § 576.

jŏcālĭter.opening: adv. jocus , for joculariter, jestingly, in joke , Amm. 15, 12, 3 dub. (al. joculariter, al. localiter).

jŏcātĭo.opening: jocor , a joking, joke (class.): nunc venio ad jocationes tuas, Cic. Fam. 9, 16, 7 ; id. Att. 2, 8, 1 ; Auct. Her. 3, 14, 25 .

jŏcĭnor.opening: (jocineris, Plin. 22, 22, 38, § 80 ), the liver : morbus jocinoris, Cels. 2, 8 ; v. jecur.

jŏcor.opening: v. dep. n. and a. [jocus], to jest, joke (class.): tu hanc jocari credis? faciet, nisi caveo, Ter. Heaut. 4, 4, 7 : duplex jocandi genus, Cic. Off. 1, 29, 104 ; cf.: voluit Fortuna jocari, Juv. 3, 40 .— In partic., to…

jŏcōsus.opening: adj. jocus , full of jesting, jocose, humorous, droll, facetious (class.). Of persons: homo humanus et jocosus, Varr. R. R. 2, 5 : Maecenas, Hor. Epod. 3, 20 : Musa, Ov. Tr. 2, 354 .— Of inanim. and abstr. things: res,…

jŏcŭlāris.opening: adj. joculus , facetious, jocular, laughable, droll (class.): audacia, Ter. Phorm. 1, 2, 84 : joculare istuc quidem, Cic. Leg. 1, 20 : licentia, id. Fat. 8 .— Subst. : , , plur., jests, jokes : ut qui jocularia ridens…

jŏcŭlārĭus.opening: adj. id. , ludicrous, droll ( poet. ): malum, Ter. And. 4, 4, 43 .

jŏcŭlātĭo.opening: joculor , a jest, joke (post-class.): joculationes cantusque exercebant, Firm. Math. 5, 5.

jŏcŭlātor.opening: id. , a jester, joker (rare but class.): huic joculatorem senem illum interesse sane nolui, Cic. Att. 4, 16, 3 . — Plur. : scenici, Firm. Math. 8, 22.

jŏcŭlātōrĭus.opening: adj. joculator , jesting, jocular .—In plur. subst., jests, jokes : joculatoria quaedam, Diom. p. 486 P. (but in Cic. Att. 4, 16, 3 , the better reading is joculatorem; v. the preced. art.).

jŏcŭlor.opening: joculus , to jest, joke; only in part. pres. : incondita quaedam joculantes, Liv. 7, 10, 13 .—Hence, adv. : , jestingly, jokingly : compellare, Sid. Ep. 1, 2 .

jŏcŭlus.opening: dim. jocus , a little jest or joke (a favorite word of Plautus): per joculum et ludum oblectare aliquem, Plaut. Truc. 1, 2, 11 ; usu. in abl. manner : joculo dicere aliquid, to say a thing in jest, id. Merc. 5, 4, 33 :…

jŏcus.opening: ( plur. also , ; so always in Cic.), perh. akin to Sanscr. root div, ludere; cf. jucundus , a jest, joke (class.): joci causa magistrum adhibes, for the sake of the joke, Cic. Phil. 2, 17, 42 : defensio redundabat…

Joppē.opening: or , , Ἰόπη , Joppa, a seaport of Palestine , now Jaffa , Plin. 5, 13, 14, § 68 .—Hence, , , adj., of Joppa , Plin. 5, 14, 15, § 70 .

Jordānes.opening: and , , , the Jordan, the principal river of Palestine , Tac. H. 5, 6 ; Lact. 4, 15, 2 ; Plin. 5, 15, 15, § 71 .

Jōsēph.opening: or , Son of the patriarch Jacob , Just. 36, 2, 6 ; Vulg. Gen. 30, 24 al. — The husband of Mary, the mother of Jesus , Vulg. Matt. 1, 16 ; Juvenc. 1, 272 .— An inhabitant of Arimathea , Juvenc. 4, 720 ; Vulg. Matt. 27,…

Jōsēphus.opening: , i. , a Jewish historian, taken prisoner by Flavius Vespasian, of whom he prophesied that he would become emperor , Suet. Vesp. 5 .

Jŏvĭālis.opening: adj. Jovis, Juppiter , of or pertaining to Jupiter (post-class.): stella, Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 19 : incontinentia, Arn. 5, 162 .

Jŏvis-jūrandum.opening: a swearing by Jupiter; for jus-jurandum, Enn. ap. App. de Deo Socr. p. 45, 4 (but Vahl. reads jusjurandum Jovis, Trag. Fragm. v. 410).

Jŏvĭus.opening: a surname of the emperor Diocletian .— Derivv. , , adj., of or belonging to Diocletian : cohors, a legion of honor instituted by Diocletian, Claud. B. Gild. 418 .— , , adj. , the same; hence, subst. : , soldiers of…

jŭba.opening: the flowing hair on the neck of an animal, the mane . Lit. : equi, Cic. Div. 1, 33, 73 : huic equus ille jubam quatiens, Cic. N. D. poet. 2, 43, 111: equorum jubae, Caes. B. G. 1, 48 ; Plin. 37, 10, 54, § 142 :…

Jŭba.opening: the name of two Numidian-kings . Juba I., king of Numidia and a part of Mauretania, who joined the party of Pompey, gained a victory over Cæsar's legate Curio, and put an end to his own life after the battle of Thapsus…

jŭbar.opening: ( : albus jubar, Enn. ap. Prisc. p. 658 P.; Auct. Aetna, 332), 1. juba , the radiance of the heavenly bodies, light, splendor, brightness, sunshine . Lit. : it portis jubare exorto delecta juventus, Verg. A. 4, 130 ;…

jŭbātus.opening: adj. id. , having a mane or crest, crested : devolant angues jubati deorsum in inpluvium duo, Plaut. Am. 5, 1, 56 : stella, Varr. L. L. 6, § 6 Müll.: anguis, Liv. 41, 21 fin. : cervix, id. 41, 21 : leones, Plin. 8, 16,…

jŭbĕo.opening: (jusso for jussero, Verg. A. 11, 467 ; Sil. 12, 175 : justi for jussisti, Ter. Eun. 5, 1, 15 .— Inf. : jusse, Ter. Heaut. 5, 2, 48 : jussitur for jubetur, Cato, R. R. 14 ), , v. a. perh. = jus habere, to regard as…

jūbĭlaeus.opening: ( ; , incorrectly), , ἰωβηλαῖος; Hebr. jōbēl , the year of jubilee among the Jews , in which all slaves were set free and all lands reverted to their former possessors; it took place every fifty years: quinquagesimus…

jūbĭlātĭo.opening: jubilo , a shouting , App. M. 8, p. 209, 11 .

jūbĭlo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
jūbĭlo.opening: v. n. and a. [jubilum], to shout, to raise a shout of joy : quiritare, jubilare, Varr. L. L. 6, § 68 Müll.: aliquem, to call out to a person: io buccol quis me jubilat? Poet. ib.: jubilate Deo, Vulg. Psa. 99, 4 : in…

jūbĭlum.opening: a wild cry, shout, shepherd's song : audivit jubila Cyclops, Sil. 14, 475 : montana jubila, Calp. Ecl. 1, 80 .

jūcundĭtas.opening: jucundus , agreeableness, pleasantness, delight, enjoyment (class.): corporis morbis vitae jucunditas impeditur, Cic. Fin. 1, 18, 59 : agri, id. Agr. 2, 29, 79 : epistola plena jucunditatis, id. Q. Fr. 2, 10, 2 ; with…

jūcundo.opening: v. a. id. , to please, delight; mid., jucundari, to feel delighted, take delight (post-class.): consolationes Dei jucundant animam, Aug. de Gen. ad Litt. 12, 34 ; ex Psa. 94, 19: quotidie autem jucundabar ante faciem…

jūcundus.opening: ( ), , adj. jocus , pleasant, agreeable, delightful, pleasing (syn.: gratus, blandus; class.): est mihi jucunda in malis et grata in dolore vestra erga me voluntas, Cic. Cat. 4, 1, 1 : comes, id. ib. 4, 6, 11 : id vero…

Jūdaea.opening: (post-Aug.; in inscrr. and coins IVDEA, Cohen, Descr. Hist. Monn. 1, 310 sqq.), , , = Ἰουδαία , the country of the Jews, Judea, Palestine , Plin. 5, 14, 15, § 70 ; Suet. Tit. 4 ; Tac. H. 2, 79 ; 5, 9 .— Derivv. , , adj.…

Jūdăīzo.opening: v. n. , to live in the Jewish manner , Vulg. Gal. 2, 14 .

Jūdas.opening: , or , , = Ἰούδας . Judah, son of Jacob and patriarch of one of the tribes of Israel : istae sunt familiae Juda, Vulg. Num. 1, 26 : dixit Judas fratribus suis, id. Gen. 37, 26 .— Transf. , the tribe of Judah,…

jūdex.opening: ( : et sumus, ut fateor, tam saevā judice sontes, Luc. 10, 368 ; cf. 227; Ov. M. 2, 428 ; 8, 24 ; Cic. Ac. 2, 28, 91 ; Petr. poët. 122, v. 174 al.) [jus-, 2. dico], a judge (class.). Lit. : judex, quod judicat acceptā…

jūdĭcābĭlis.opening: adj. judico , that may be judged of (post-class.), Mart. Cap. 5, § 461 ; also judicial, befitting a judge : judicabili vigore et censoria auctoritate, Ambros. in Psa. 37 .

jūdĭcātĭo.opening: judico . A judging, investigating (class.): longi subsellii, Cic. Fam. 3, 9, 2 ; hence, an inquiry into an accusation, a judicial examination of a cause, id. Inv. 1, 13, 18 : consilium est ratio quaedam habens in se et…

jūdĭcātō.opening: adv. , v. judico, P. a. fin .

jūdĭcātōrĭus.opening: adj. judicator , of or pertaining to a judge, judicial (eccl. Lat.): rigor, Aug. Ep. 54 .

jūdĭcātrix.opening: id. , she that judges or decides (post-Aug.): ars inventrix, et judicatrix, Quint. 2, 15, 21 .

jūdĭcātus.opening: judico , a judgeship, the office of a judge (rare but class.): isti ordini judicatus lege Julia non patebit, Cic. Phil. 1, 8, 20 : judicatu illo solvi, Gell. 14, 2, 25 .

jūdĭcĭālis.opening: adj. judicium , of or belonging to the courts of justice, judicial : jus, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 47, § 103 : annus, i. e. the year in which Pompey altered the form of trials, id. Brut. 69, 243 : molestia, id. Att. 13, 6, 3 :…

jūdĭcĭārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to the courts, judiciary (class.): lex, Cic. Pis. 39, 94 : quaestus, id. Clu. 26, 72 : controversia, Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 2, § 5 : leges, Suet. Aug. 56 : Lex Julia judiciaria, Gai. Inst. 4, 104 .

jūdĭcĭŏlum.opening: dim. id. , a weak or feeble judgment (post-class.): juste, an secus, non judicioli est nostri, Amm. 27, 11, 1 ; 28, 4, 14 .

jūdĭcĭum.opening: judex , a judgment , i. e. a judicial investigation, trial; a judicial sentence (class.). Lit. : omnia judicia aut distrahendarum controversiarum aut puniendorum maleficiorum causā reperta sunt, Cic. Caecin. 2 :…

jūdĭco.opening: (judicassit for judicaverit, Cic. Leg. 3, 3, 6 ), v. a. judex , to examine judicially, to judge, be a judge, pass judgment, decide (syn.: judicium facio, reddo; class.). Lit. : si recte et ordine judicaris, Cic. Rosc.…

jŭgābĭlis.opening: adj. jugo , that may be joined together (post-class.): competentia, Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 6, 24 .

jŭgālis.opening: adj. jugum , of or belonging to a yoke, yoked together . Lit. : equi jumentaque, Curt. 9, 10, 22 : equi et currus jugalis, Macr. S. 5, 17, 2 .— Subst. : , a team : gemini, Verg. A. 7, 280 . — Transf. ŏS, a bone above…

jŭgārĭus.opening: adj. jugum , yoked together , Hyg. Fab. 183 : Vicus Jugarius, a place in Rome where stood an altar to the foundress of marriage, Liv. 35, 21, 6 ; 27, 37, 13 .— Subst. : , , , an ox-herd , Col. 1, 6, 6 .

Jŭgātīnus.opening: jugo , the god of marriage , Aug. Civ. Dei , 6, 9.

jŭgātĭo.opening: id. , a binding (e. g. of a vine) to rails , Varr. R. R. 1, 8 ; Cic. de Sen. 15, 53 .— A kind of land-measure , Cod. Th. 10, 48, 1.

jŭgātor.opening: id. , one who yokes (post-class.): boum, Arn. 5, 174 .

jūgĕrālis.opening: adj. jugerum , of or belonging to an acre, acre- (post-class.): tabula, Pall. 3, 9, 9 .

jūgĕrātĭo.opening: id. . A dividing of land into acres , Front. Col. p. 146 .— A measure of land , Cod. Th. 12, 1, 33.

jūgĕrum.opening: (in sing. acc. to the second, in plur. mostly acc. to the third declension; gen. plur. always jugerum; cf. Lachm. in Rhein. Mus. 1845, pp. 609-612), , an acre , or rather juger of land, measuring 28,800 square feet, or…

jūgĭflŭus.opening: adj. 2. jugis-fluo , ever-flowing (post-class.), Paul. Nol. Carm. 35, 439 .

jūgis.opening: ( gen. plur. jugerum for jugium, Lucil. ap. Charis. p. 40 P.; with the first syll. short, Sedul. 1, 18 ), adj., continual, perpetual; esp. of running water, always flowing, perennial (class.): thesaurus jugis, Plaut.…

jūgĭtas.opening: 2. jugis , continuance, duration (post-class.): lacrimarum, Marc. Emp. 8 : temporis, Cod. 5, 17, 7; 12, 1, 186.

jūglans.opening: i. q. Jovis glans = Gr. Διὸς βάλανος , a walnut; a walnut-tree : haec glans optima, et maxima, ab Jove et glande juglans appellata est, Varr. L. L. 5, § 102 Müll.: juglandium putamina, Cic. Tusc. 5, 20, 58 : juglandium…

jŭgo.opening: v. a. jugum , to bind to laths or rails . Lit. : furcas vel palos perticis jugare, Col. 12, 39 ; 12, 15, 1 : vineam, id. 4, 26, 1 .— Transf. , to marry ( poet. ): cui pater intactam dederat, primisque jugarat Ominibus,…

jugo.opening: v. n. , to utter the note of the kite (milvus), Varr. ap. Non. 179, 2 ; cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 104 Müll., and jugit ικτὶν βοᾷ , Gloss. Philox.

jŭgōsus.opening: adj. jugum , mountainous ( poet. ): silvae, Ov. Am. 1, 1, 9 ; id. H. 4, 85 .

Jŭgŭla.opening: , and , , jugulus , the three stars which form Orion's belt; also, the whole constellation Orion , Varr. L. L. 7, § 50 Müll.: neque Jugulae neque Vesperugo neque Vergiliae occidunt, Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 119 .— Two stars in…

jŭgŭlātĭo.opening: jugulo , a cutting of one's throat, a killing, murdering , Auct. B. Hisp. 16; 18; 22.

jŭgŭlātor.opening: id. , a cutthroat, slayer, murderer (late Lat.), Salv. ad Eccl. 3 ; cf. jugulator, φονεύς, σφάκτης , Gloss. Philox.

jŭgŭlo.opening: v. a. jugulum , to cut the throat, to kill, slay, murder (class.). Lit. : cum jugulatur sus, Cic. Tusc. 5, 40, 116 : cives optimos jugulari jussit, id. Phil. 3, 2, 4 : se alicui tradere jugulandum, id. Mil. 11, 31 :…

jŭgŭlum.opening: , and , , jug, jungo , the collar-bone , which joins together the shoulders and the breast, Cels. 8, 1, § 70 : uni homini juguli, humeri: ceteris armi, Plin. 11, 43, 98, § 243 .— Transf. , hence, the hollow part of the…

jŭgum.opening: kindred to Sanscr. yuga from yug-, jungere; Gr. ζυγόν; v. jungo , a yoke for oxen, a collar for horses. Lit. : nos onera quibusdam bestiis, nos juga imponimus, Cic. N. D. 2, 60, 151 : leones jugo subdere, et ad currum…

jŭgūmento.opening: ( ), , v. a. 1. jugo , to fasten together , Vitr. 2, 1 .

jŭgūmentum.opening: ( ), , id. , a cross-beam, lintel, threshold (ante-class.), Cato, R. R. 14 .

Jŭgurtha.opening: the nephew and successor of Micipsa, king of Numidia, conquered by Marius in the war with the Romans; v. Sall. J. 5 sqq.; Flor. 3, 1 .—Hence, , , adj., of or belonging to Jugurtha, Jugurthan : conjuratio, Cic. N. D. 3,…

jŭgus.opening: adj. 1. jugo , belonging together (ante-class.): vasa, Cato, R. R. 10 .

Juliacum.opening: a city of Gallia Belgica , now Juliers , Amm. 17, 4 .

Jūlĭānus.opening: Julian, a Roman proper name . M. Didius Severus Julianus Augustus, a Roman emperor, who was put to death after a reign of 66 days , A. D. 193.— Julianus Augustus Apostata, an emperor who turned from Christianity to…

Jūlĭensis.opening: adj. Julius , of or belonging to Julius, Julian , an appellation given to cities or colonies, Plin. 3, 3, 4, § 23 ; 3, 5, 8, § 52 ; 3, 19, 23, § 130 .

Jūlĭō^brĭga.opening: a town in Hispania Tarraconensis , Plin. 3, 3, 4, § 27 .—Hence, , , , an inhabitant of Juliobriga , Plin. 4, 20, 34, § 110 .

Jūlĭus.opening: (in poets also , quadrisyll.), a, adj., name of a Roman gens; especially celebrated, C. Julius Cæsar and his adopted son, C. Julius Cæsar (Octavianus) Augustus: unde domus Teucros Julia tangit avos, Ov. F. 4, 40 :…

jūmentārĭus.opening: adj. jumentum , of or belonging to draught-cattle (postclass.): mola, worked by draught-cattle, Dig. 33, 7, 26, § 1 : contubernium, App. M. 10, p. 222, 34 .

jūmentum.opening: contr. from jugimentum, from jungo : jumenta ducunt, Plaut. Ep. 2, 2, 27 ; a beast used for drawing or carrying, draught-cattle, a beast of bur- den, esp. a horse, mule , or ass (class.): cum illam curru vehi jus esset,…

juncētum.opening: juncus , a place full of rushes , Varr. R. R. 1, 8, 3 .

juncĕus.opening: adj. id. . Made of rushes, rush- : sporta, Col. 12, 6 : vincula, Ov. F. 4, 870 : cratis, Plin. 21, 14, 49, § 84 .— Comically: nam mihi jam intus potione junceā onerabo gulam, with a rush-drink , i. e. with a rope of…

juncĭnus.opening: adj. id. , made from rushes, rush- : oleum, Plin. 15, 7, 7, § 30 .

juncōsus.opening: adj. id. , full of rushes : ager, Plin. 18, 6, 8, § 46 : litora, Ov. M. 7, 231 .

junctio.opening: jungo , a joining, uniting, union , Cic. Tusc. 1, 29, 71 .

junctūra.opening: id. , a joining, uniting; a juncture, joint ( poet. and post-Aug.). Lit. : boum, Col. 2, 2 22: genuum, Ov. M. 2, 823 : ut umor teneat juncturas, i. e. the commissures, joints, Plin. 16, 40, 79, § 214 : quadrato saxo…

junctus.opening: jungo , a joining (ante-class.): Carinarum, Varr. L. L. 5, § 47 , Müll.

juncus.opening: a rush . Lit. : murteta juncis circumvincire, Plaut. Rud. 3, 4, 27 : palustres, Ov. M. 8, 336 : acutā cuspide junci, id. ib. 4, 299 .— A twig resembling a rush , Plin. 26, 8, 46, § 72 .

jungo.opening: v. a. Sanscr. jug, junagmi, to unite; juk, joined; Goth. juk; O. H. Germ. joh, joch; Gr. ζυγ, ζεύγνυμι, ζυγός, ζυγόν , to join or unite together, connect, attach, fasten, yoke, harness . Lit. In gen. With acc. :…

Jūnĭānus.opening: adj. Junius , of or belonging to a Junius, Junian : judicium, Cic. Clu. 1, 1 : cerasa, Plin. 15, 25, 30, § 103 .

jūnĭpĕrĕus.opening: adj. juniperus , of juniper , Cic. Fl. de Cond. Agr. p. 4 Goes.

jūnĭpĕrus.opening: (also , in Plin. passim), , , the juniper-tree , Plin. 8, 31, 51, § 99 ; 16, 18, 30, § 73 ; Verg. E. 7, 53 ; 10, 76 .

Jūnĭus.opening: name of a Roman gens: e. g. M. and D. Junius Brutus.—Hence, , , adj., Junian : familia, Tac. A. 3, 24 : domus, Liv. 2, 5 : lex, proposed by Junius, Cic. Att. 2, 9, 1 ; 4, 16, 5 : mensis, the sixth month, June, id. ib.…

jūnix.opening: , or uncontr. , , juvenix , a young cow, a calf, heifer : tot tibi cum in flammas junicum omenta liquescant, Pers. 2, 47 .—In the form juvenix, of a maiden (cf.: δάμαλις , juvenca): quam mox horsum ad stabulum juvenix…

Jūno.opening: the goddess Juno, daughter of Saturn, sister and wife of Jupiter, and the guardian deity of women; as the foundress of marriage, she is also called pronuba Juno; and as the protecting goddess of lying-in women , Juno…

laetisco.opening: v. n. inch. [laetus], to rejoice , Sisenn. ap. Non. 133, 2 .

laetĭtĭa.opening: id. , joy , esp. unrestrained joyfulness, gladness, pleasure, delight (cf.: gaudium, hilaritas). Lit. : laetitia opinio recens boni praesentis, in quo efferri rectum esse videatur, Cic. Tusc. 4, 7, 14 : laetitia dicitur…

laetĭtūdo.opening: id. , ante-class. for laetitia, joy : me excitasti ex luctu in laetitudinem, Att. ap. Non. 132, 12 : affecti laetitudine, id. ib. 13 (Trag. Fragm. v. 61, 259 Rib.).

laeto.opening: v. a. id. , to make joyful, to delight, cheer, gladden . Lit. (ante- and post-class.): oculos specie laetavisti optabili, Liv. Andron. ap. Non. 132, 32 : te ut triplici laetarem bono, Att. ib.: frontem alicujus serena…

laetor.opening: v. dep. n. [lit. pass. of laeto], to rejoice, feel joy, be joyful or glad at any thing (syn. gaudeo); constr. with abl. , with in, de, ex , or super and abl. , with neutr. acc. , with acc. and inf. , poet. with gen.…

Laetōrĭus.opening: adj., the name of a Roman gens, Mart. 12, 26, 13 (but lex Plaetoria is the true reading, Cic. Off. 3, 15, 61 : id. N. D. 3, 30, 74 ; Cod. Th. 8, 12, 2).

laetus.opening: , in late Lat., a foreign bondman who received a piece of land to cultivate, for which he paid tribute to his master, a serf , Amm. 20, 8, 13 ; Eum. Pan. 21, 1 .—Hence, , , , the land so cultivated , Cod. Th. 7, 20,…

laeva.opening: the left hand , v. laevus, I. B. 1.

Laevi.opening: ( ), , , the Lævi, an ancient people of Liguria, between the Po and the Ticinus , Liv. 33, 37, 6 ; 5, 35, 2 ; Plin. 3, 17, 21, § 124 .

Laevīnus.opening: laeva , a Roman surname in the gens Valeria, Plin. 35, 2, 2, § 8 . Esp. M. Valerius Laevinus, consul during the second Punic war , Liv. 26, 40 .— C. Valerius Laevinus, prætor and consul about B. C. 180, Liv. 40, 44, 2 ;…

Laevĭus.opening: a Roman poet of the ante-clussical period , Gell. 2, 24, 8 ; 19, 9, 7 ; Aus. Edyll. 13 .—Hence, , , adj., of or belonging to the poet Lævius, Lævian : carmen, Gell. 19, 7, 2 : verba, id. 19, 7, 12 .

laevorsum.opening: and , adv. laevus-versum , on the left hand, to or towards the left (post-class.): laevorsum vel dextrorsum, App. Flor. 1, p. 340, 41 ; cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 117 Müll.; Amm. 14, 3, 2 : laevorsus flexus itinere, id. 31,…

laevus.opening: adj. cf. Gr. λαιός , left, on the left side (mostly poet. ; syn.: sinister, scaevus). Lit. : ut idem nunc sit laevus; et e laevo sit mutua dexter, Lucr. 4, 301 (325): manus, Cic. Ac. 2, 47, 145 : ab laeva manu, Plaut.…

lăgănum.opening: , = λάγανον , a kind of cake made of flour and oil , Hor. S. 1, 6, 115 ; Cels. 8, 7, § 23 al. : lagana azyma, Vulg. Exod. 29, 2 ; id. Num. 6, 15 .

Lagarīna.opening: plur. (sc. vina), a kind of wine , Plin. 14, 6, 8, § 69 .

lăgēna.opening: (also , , and ), , , = λάγηνος , a large earthen vessel with a neck and handles, a flask, flagon, bottle : quasi tu lagenam dicas, ubi vinum solet Chium esse, Plaut. Curc. 1, 1, 78 ; Cic. Fam. 16, 26, 2 ; Quint. 6, 3,…

lăgēos.opening: , = λάγειος , a Greek species of vine : et passo Psithia utilior, tenuisque Lageos, Verg. G. 2, 93 ; Isid. Orig. 17, 5, 16 .— , , adj. : vitis, Plin. 14, 3, 4, § 39 : Macr. S. 2, 16, 7 .

lago.opening: a plant , otherwise called schite; and scammonia tenuis, Plin. 24, 15, 89, § 139 .

lăgōis.opening: , = λαγωΐς , a kind of bird , perh. heath-cock, grouse (or the same as lagopus, white grouse ): peregrina, Hor. S. 2, 2, 22 ; Schol. Cruq. ad loc.

Lāgōn.opening: name of a boy : nos facimus Bruti puerum, nos Lagona vivum, Mart. 9, 51, 5 (al. Langona).

lăgŏnŏpŏnos.opening: , false reading for adligato raphano, Plin. 20, 4, 13, § 24 .

lăgophthalmos.opening: , = λαγωφθαλμός (hare-eye), a person afflicted with a disease of the eye, in which the upper lid does not cover the eye , Cels. 7, 7, 9, § 93 sqq.

lăgōpūs.opening: , = λαγώπους , hare'sfoot . An Alpine bird , perh. white grouse , Plin. 10, 48, 68, § 133 (see also glaucopis, Mart. 7, 87 ).— The herb hare's-foot , Plin. 26, 8, 34, § 53 .

Lagos.opening: a city in Great Phrygia , Liv. 38, 15, 2 .

lăguncŭla.opening: dim. lagena , a small flask, small bottle , Col. 12, 38, 6 ; 8 ; Plin. Ep. 2, 6, 2 ; 1, 6, 3 : novae, Vulg. Job, 32, 19 ; id. Jer. 13, 12 ; 48, 12 .

lăguncŭlāris.opening: adj. laguncula , of or belonging to a small bottle : pix, Marc. Emp. 36 .

lăguncŭlus.opening: a kind of pastry (al. lucunculus), Stat. S. 1, 6, 17 .

Lāgus.opening: the father of Ptolemy I. king of Egypt : regia Lagi, Luc. 10, 527 : famosa moenia Lagi, Juv. 6, 83 : flumina Lagi, i. e. Nilus, Sil. 17, 592 .—Hence, , , adj., of or belonging to Lagus, Lagian , poet. for Egyptian :…

lāĭcus.opening: adj. , = λαϊκός , of or belonging to the people or laity, not priestly, not consecrated : non habeo laicos panes, loaves not consecrated, Vulg. 1 Reg. 21, 4 .— Subst. : , , , a layman, laic, one not belonging to the…

Lāïs.opening: , = Λαΐς , the name of two courtesans of Corinth celebrated for their beauty . Lais, who flourished during the Peloponnesian war: dicitur et multis Lais amata viris, Ov. Am. 1, 5, 12 ; Cic. Fam. 9, 26, 2 ( acc. Laida);…

Lāĭus.opening: or , ( voc. Lai, Stat. Th. 7, 355 ), , = Λάιος , son of Labdacus, king of Thebes, and father of Œdipus , Cic. Tusc. 4, 33, 71 ; id. Fat. 13, 30 ; Stat. Th. 2, 7 ; 66 . —Hence, , , , a male descendant of Laius , i. e.…

Lălăgē.opening: , = Λαλαγή , the name of a girl , Hor. C. 1, 22, 10 ; 23 ; 2, 5, 16 ; of a woman : LIVIA LALAGE, Inscr. ap. Mur. 1367, 1.

Lălētānĭa.opening: a region in Hispania Tarraconensis, where the vine was cultivated , Ep. Pompei ad Senat. 5; Sall. Hist. Fragm. 2, 96, 5 Dietsch; Mart. 1, 50, 22 .— Hence, , , adj., of or belonging to Laletania, Laletanian : vina, Plin.…

lālīsĭo.opening: (African), the foal of a wild ass , Plin. 8, 44, 69, § 174 ; Mart. 13, 97 .

lallo.opening: v. n. , to sing lalla or lullaby, to sing as a nurse to a child : iratus mammae, lallare recusas, will not let yourself be sung to sleep, Pers. 3, 17 ; Hier. Ep. 14, 3 : lallare βαβάζειν , Gloss. Philox.

lallum.opening: , or , , lallo , a singing lalla or lullaby (post-class.), Aus. Ep. 16, 91 .

lāma.opening: (cf.: lacus, lacer). A slough, bog, fen : lacuna id est aquae collectio, quam alii lamam, alii lustrum, Paul. ex Fest. p. 117 Müll.: viribus uteris per clivos, flumina, lamas, Hor. Ep. 1, 13, 10 .— A kind of mastic :…

lambĕro.opening: v. a. , to tear to pieces (ante-class.): lamberat scindit ac laniat, Paul. ex Fest. p. 118 Müll.—Prov.: lepide, Charine, meo me ludo lamberas, you beat me at my own game, pay me in my own coin, Plaut. Ps. 2, 4, 53 .

lambĭto.opening: v. freq. a. lambo , to lick, lap up : Aegyptii canes e Nilo numquam nisi currentes lambitant, Sol. 15, 12 .

lambĭtus.opening: id. , a licking : lupam primo lambitu pueros detersisse, Aur. Vict. Orig. Gentis R. 20 .

lambo.opening: ( perf. lambuerunt, Vulg. Jud. 7, 7 al. ), , v. a. root lap-; Gr. λάπτω, λαφύσσω; Lat. labrum, labium; Germ. Löffel, spoon; Eng. lip , to lick, lap; to touch (class.; cf.: lingo, sugo, ligurio). Lit. : hi canes, quos…

Lambrīca.opening: a town in Hispania Tarraconensis, Mel. 3, 1 .

Lambrus.opening: a small river in northern Italy, a tributary of the Po , Plin. 3, 19, 23, § 131 al.

lāmella.opening: dim. lamina , a small plate of metal , Vitr. 7, 3 : paucae lamellae argenti, a few small silver coins, Sen. Vit. Beat. 21, 3 ; id. Brev. Vit. 12, 2 : stella e lamella aerea, Paul. ex Fest. p. 351 .

lāmellŭla.opening: dim. lamella , a small plate of metal : glebulas emi, lamellulas paravi, Petr. 57, 6 .

lāmenta.opening: (collat. form of lamentum, q. v.): lamentas, fletus facere, Pac. ap. Non. 132, 28 (Trag. Fragm. v. 175 Rib.).

lāmentābĭlis.opening: adj. lamentor , mournful, lamentable (class.). Full of sorrow, expressing sorrow : afflictus et jacens, et lamentabili voce deplorans, Cic. Tusc. 2, 13, 32 : carmen, Stat. S. 5, 3, 1 .— Causing sorrow, deplorable :…

lāmentārĭus.opening: adj. lamentum , mournful, causing tears : aedes, Plaut. Capt. 1, 1, 28 .

lāmentātĭo.opening: lamentor , a wailing, moaning, weeping, lamenting, lamentation (class.; cf.: querela, questus, lamentum, plangor, planctus): lamentatio (est) aegritudo, cum ejulatu, Cic. Tusc. 4, 8, 18 : aegritudo, lacrumae,…

lāmentātrix.opening: lamentator , she who bewails , Vulg. Jer. 9, 17 .

lāmento.opening: v. n. (collat. form of lamentor), Vulg. Matt. 11, 17 ; id. Luc. 7, 32 .

lāmentor.opening: v. dep. n. and a. [lamentum], to wail, moan, weep, lament (class.). Neutr. : lamentari, cruciari, Plaut. Mil. 4, 2, 40 : quod nunc lamentari, id. Pers. 1, 3, 94 : praeter ceteras lamentari, Ter. And. 1, 1, 94 : lapides…

lāmentum.opening: perh. for clamentum, from clamo , a wailing, moaning, weeping, lamentation, lament (class., only in plur. ): virum, Lucr. 6, 242 Lachm.: negat se velle mortem suam dolore amicorum et lamentis vacare, Cic. de Sen. 20, 73…

lămĭa.opening: , = λαμία . A witch who was said to suck children's blood, a sorceress, enchantress : neu pransae lamiae vivum puerum extrahat alvo, Hor. A. P. 340 ; App. M. 1, p. 110, 3 ; 5 , p. 164, 6.— Transf. : lamiae turres,…

Lămĭa.opening: , = Λαμία , a city in Phthiotis , now Zeitun , Liv. 27, 30, 1 ; 32, 4, 3 ; Plin. 4, 7, 14, § 28 .

lāmĭna.opening: or , and sync. (e. g. Hor. C. 2, 2, 2 ; id. Ep. 1, 15, 36 ; Val. Fl. 1, 123 ; Vitr. 7, 9 ; also, lamina, id. 5, 3 ), , , a thin piece of metal, wood, marble , etc., a plate, leaf, layer, lamina [root la, = ἐλα - of…

lamnŭla.opening: dim. lamina for lamella, a little plate of metal (eccl. Lat.): triumphi laurea lamnulis ornatur, Tert. Coron. Mil. 12 dub. (al. lamnis).

lampābĭlis.opening: adj. lampo , shining (eccl. Lat.), Cassiod. in Psa. praef. 17.

lampădārĭus.opening: lampas , a lampbearer, torch-bearer (post-class.), Cod. Just. 12, 60, 10 ; Inscr. Orell. 2930 ; 2845 (called in Suet. Aug. 29 , servus praelucens).

lampădĭas.opening: , = λαμπαδίας , a comet resembling a blazing torch , Plin. 2, 25, 22, § 90 .

Lampadio.opening: the name of a slave , Plaut. Cist. 2, 3, 50 .

Lampădiscus.opening: the name of a slave , Plaut. Cist. 2, 3, 2 .

lampădo.opening: , i. q. bulbus, Theod. Prisc. de Diaeta, 9.

lampăs.opening: (late Lat. also , , Jul. Val. Rer. G. Alex. 3, 28 : lampadarum, Vulg. Ezech. 1, 13 ), , = λαμπάς , a light, torch, flambeau (mostly poet. ; cf.: lucerna, lychnus, laterna). Lit. : lampades ardentes, Plaut. Men. 5, 2, 86…

Lampĕtĭē.opening: , = Λαμπετίη , a daughter of the sun-god and sister of Phaëthon, who was changed into a tree , Ov. M. 2, 349 ; Hyg. Fab. 154 ; Prop. 3, 12 (4, 11), 29.

Lampīa.opening: or , , , a town in Arcadia , Stat. Th. 4, 290 .

lampo.opening: v. n. lampas , to shine (eccl. Lat.); only trop. of eloquence, Cassiod. Inst. Div. Litt. 21 .

Lampon.opening: , = Λάμπων , the name of a horse , Sil. 16, 334 .

Lamprĭdĭus.opening: Aelius, a Roman historiographer, one of the Scriptores Historiae Augustae, Vopisc. Prob. 2 fin. ; cf. Teuffel, Gesch. der Röm. Lit. § 397, 4.— A Latin orator of the fifth century , Sid. Ep. 8, 11 ; cf. Teuffel, Gesch.…

Lampsăcum.opening: , and ( ), , , = Λάμψακος , a city of Mysia, on the Hellespont , now Lamsaki . —Form Lampsacum, Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 24, § 63 ; Mel. 1, 19 .—Form Lampsacus, Val. Fl. 2, 624 ; Ov. Tr. 1, 10, 26 .—Hence, , , adj., of or…

Lampus.opening: One of Actæon's hounds , Hyg. Fab. 181 .— One of the four horses of the sun , Fulg. Myth. 1, 11 .

Lămus.opening: , = Λάμος . A mythic king of the Læstrygonians, a son of Neptune, and the founder of Formiæ , Hor. C. 3, 17, 1 ; Sil. 8, 530 ; hence, urbs Lami, i. e. Formiæ, Ov. M. 14, 233 .— A son of Hercules and Omphale , Ov. H. 9,…

lămўrus.opening: , = λάμυρος , a seafish , Ov. Hal. 120 ; Plin. 32, 11, 53, § 149 (Jahn, larinus).

lāna.opening: Gr. λάχνη, λάχνος, λῆνος, Dor. λᾶνος; cf. λάοιος, and v. Varr. L. L. 5, § 113 Müll. , wool , Plaut. Men. 1, 2, 12 ; Varr. R. R. 2, 2, 18 ; Cic. de Or. 2, 68, 277 ; Col. 7, 2, 4 : lanam cārĕre, to card wool, Plaut. Men.…

lānāris.opening: adj. lana , woolly, woolbearing (ante-class.): pecus, Varr. R. R. 2, 9, 1 .

lānārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to wool, wool- (post-Aug.; cf.: lanifer, laniger, lamificus, lanatus). Adj. : herba, fuller's-weed, soapwort, Plin. 24, 18, 105, § 169 ; so, radix, Col. 11, 2, 35 .— Substt. , , , a worker in…

Lānārĭus.opening: the surname of P. Calpurnius, Cic. Off. 3, 16, 66 .

lānātus.opening: adj. lana , furnished with wool, bearing wool, woolly (mostly poet. and post-Aug.). Lit. : lanatae oves, i. e. unshorn, Col. 7, 3, 2 : pelles, id. 6, 2, 4 : de lanata pelle, Veg. 3, 7, 1 ; 5, 42, 2 : animalia, Juv. 15,…

Lānātus.opening: a surname in the gens Menenia, Liv. 4, 13 .

lancĕa.opening: λόγχη, acc. to Paul. ex Fest. p. 118 Müll.; acc. to Varr. ap. Gell. 15, 30 fin., of Spanish origin , a light spear, with a leather thong fastened to the middle of it, a lance, spear (cf.: telum, spiculum, hastile,…

lancĕātus.opening: adj. lancea , made into a lance, lance-formed : armabitur ferro et ligno lanceato, Vulg. 2 , Reg. 23, 7.

lancĕo.opening: v. a. lancea , to wield or handle a lance (eccl. Lat.), Tert. adv. Jud. 9 ; id. adv. Marc. 13 .

lancĕŏla.opening: ( ), , dim. id. , a small lance , Capitol. Maxim. jun. 4; App. M. 8, p. 214, 7 .

lancĕŏlātus.opening: adj. lanceola , armed with a little lance or point, lanceolated, lanceolate : plantago, Macer de Plantagine, 5.

Lancĭa.opening: a city of Hispania Tarraconensis, now Castro , Flor. 4, 12 ; cf. Mann. Hispan. p. 358.—Hence, , , , the inhabitants of Lancia , Plin. 3, 3, 4, § 28 .— A city of the same name in Lusitania, whose inhabitants were called…

lancĭārĭus.opening: ( ), , lancea , a lancer (post-class.), Amm. 21, 13, 16 ; Cassiod. Hist. 6, 35 ; Vulg. Act. 23, 23 .

lancĭcŭla.opening: dim. lanx , a small dish or platter (post-class.), Arn. 2, 59 .

lancĭnātor.opening: lancino , one that tears to pieces, a render, lacerater : gregum, Prud. στεφ . 10, 1057.

lancĭno.opening: v. a. cf. lacer , to tear to pieces, to rend, mangle, lacerate ( poet. and post-Aug.). Lit. : alium ira in cubili suo confodit ... alium intra leges celebrisque spectaculum fori lancinavit, Sen. de Ira, 1, 2, 2: morsu…

lancŭla.opening: ( , Varr. L. L. 5, 25, 34 ), , dim. lanx , a small balance , Vitr. 10, 8 .

lanerum.grammar: vestimenti genus ex lana sucida confectum

lānestris.opening: adj. lana , woollen, of wool (post-class.): pallium, Vop. Aur. 29, 1 .

lānĕus.opening: adj. id. , woollen, of wool . Lit. : pallium, Cic. N. D. 3, 34, 83 : culcita ob oculos, Plaut. Mil. 4, 4, 42 : infula, Verg. G. 3, 487 : thorax subuculae, Suet. Aug. 82 : coma flaminis, i. e. his woollen fillet, Stat.…

langa.opening: Celtic , a kind of lizard, from whose urine the stone called langurium (lyncurium) was said to be produced , Plin. 37, 2, 11, § 34 .

Langŏbardi.opening: a people of northern Germany, west of the Elbe , Tac. G. 40 ; id. A. 2, 45 ; 11, 17 : gens etiam Germana feritate ferocior, Vell. 2, 106, 2 .

languĕfăcĭo.opening: v. a. langueo-facio , to make faint, weary, languid : incitare languentes et languefacere excitatos, Cic. Leg. 2, 15, 38 .

languens.opening: Part. and P. a. , v. langueo fin.

languĕo.opening: v. n. root lag-; Gr. λαγαρός, λάγνος, lewd; Lat. laxare, lactes; cf. Sanscr. lang-a, prostitute; Gr. λαγώς, hare, λαγόνες, the flanks, womb , to be faint, weary, languid (cf.: languesco, marceo, torpeo). Lit. In gen.:…

languesco.opening: v. inch. n. [langueo], to become faint, weak, languid (class.; syn.: torpesco, marcesco). Lit. In gen.: corpore languescit, Cic. Fin. 4, 24, 65 : orator metuo ne languescat senectute, id. de Sen. 9, 28 : corpora, Ov.…

languĭdŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [languidus], withered, faded . * Lit. : coronae, Cic. Fragm. ap. Quint. 8, 3, 66 .—* Transf. : somnus, proceeding from faintness, languid, Cat. 64, 332 .

languĭdus.opening: adj. langueo , faint, weak, dull, sluggish, languid (class.; cf.: lassus, fessus, fatigatus, defessus). Lit. In gen.: homines vino languidi, Cic. Cat. 2, 5, 10 ; cf.: vino vigiliisque languidus, Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 12, §…

languĭfĭcus.opening: adj. langueofacio , that makes faint or feeble : Leo, Aus. Ecl. in Versib. Q. Cic. 6 .

languor.opening: langueo , faintness, feebleness, weariness, sluggishness, languor, lassitude . Lit. In gen. (class.; cf.: torpor, torpedo, veturnus): ubi saepe ad languorem tua duritia dederis octo validos lictores. Plaut. As. 3, 2, 28…

langūrĭum.opening: a kind of amber , also called lyncurium, Plin. 37, 2, 11, § 34 ; cf. langa.

lănĭāmentum.opening: lanio , a tearing to pieces , August. Ep. 2, 26 .

lănĭārĭus.opening: adj. lanius , pertaining to a butcher .—Only as subst. , , , a butcher's stall (anteclass.), Varr. R. R. 2, 4, 3 .— , , , a butcher , Inscr. Grut. p. 1035 , n. 4.

lănĭātĭo.opening: 1. lanio , a tearing in pieces, a mangling, lacerating (postAug.): caedes hominum et laniationes, Sen. Clem. 2, 4, 2 .

lănĭātor.opening: id. , μακελλάριος , a butcher , i. q. lanius, Gloss. Philox.

lănĭātōrĭum.opening: μακελλεῖον, κρεωπωλεῖον , a butcher's stall , i. q. laniena, Gloss. Philox.

lănĭātus.opening: 1. lanio , a tearing in pieces, a mangling, lacerating . Lit. (rare but class.): ferarum, * Cic. Tusc. 1, 43, 104 : avium, Amm. 24, 2, 8 .—In plur. : avium ferarumque laniatibus objectus, Val. Max. 1, 6, 11 : quid…

lānĭcĭus.opening: adj. lana , of wool, woolly, fleecy : grex, Arn. 5, 174 .—Hence, subst. : or , , (anteclass. collat. form or , , , Laber. ap. Non. 212, 22 ; Com. Fragm. v. 67 Rib.; post-class. collat. form or , , , Tert. adv. Marc. ap.…

lānĭcŭtis.opening: adj. lana-cutis , woollyskinned : aries, Laber. ap. Tert. Pall. 1 .

lānĭēnus.opening: adj. lanius , of a butcher, butcher's : tabernae, Varr. ap. Non. 532, 20 .—Hence, subst. : , , A butcher's stall : per myropolia et lanienas, Plaut. Ep. 2, 2, 15 : lanienae et tabernae conjunctae, Liv. 44, 16 fin. — A…

lānĭfer.opening: adj. lana-fero , wool-bearing , i. e. cotton-bearing : arbores, Plin. 13, 14, 28, § 90 .

lānĭfĭcĭum.opening: lanificus , the working of wool , i. e. spinning, weaving , etc. (ante-class. and post-Aug.): de lanificio neminem metuo, una aetate quae sit, Plaut. Merc. 3, 1, 22 : lanificii curam suscipere, Col. 12 praef. § 9: usum…

lānĭfĭcus.opening: adj. lana-facio , wool-working, that works in wool , i. e. spinning, weaving , etc. ( poet. ): manus, Tib. 2, 1, 10 : ars, Ov. M. 6, 6 ; Claud. in Eutr. 2, 382 : sorores, the spinning sisters , i. e. the Fates , Mart.…

lānĭger.opening: adj. lana-gero , wool-bearing, fleecy ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): pecus, Att. ap. Cic. Div. 1, 22, 44 : greges, Verg. G. 3, 287 : arbores, i. e. cottontrees, Plin. 12, 10, 21, § 38 : fertilitas, of insects. id. 11,…

lănĭo.opening: 1. lanio , a butcher (post-class.): lanionis instrumentum, Dig. 33, 7, 18 ; 1, 2, 2, § 24 : quis tibi tunc, lanio, cernenti talia sensus, Sedul. Carm. 2, 127 .

lănĭŏlum.opening: dim. lanius , a little butcher's stall , Fulg. Myth. 1 praef.

lănĭōnĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to a butcher (post-Aug.): mensa, a butcher's stall, Suet. Claud. 15 .

lānĭpendens.opening: σταθμοῦχος, γυνὴ ἡ τὸν σταθμὸν παρέχουσα ταῖς ἄλλαις , one who weighs out wool for spinning, a spinning-mistress , Gloss. Philox.; cf. Inscr. Orell. 2820 .

lānĭpendĭum.opening: lana-pendo , the distribution of wool (late Lat.), Caes. Aul. Reg. ad Verg. 30 .

lānĭpendĭus.opening: (collat. form † , Inscr. ap. Spon. Miscell. Antiq. p. 223; Inscr. Don. Cl. 8, 57 ), , adj. id. , that weighs out wool, portions it out for spinning (post-class.); only as subst. , , , one who weighs out wool :…

lānĭpēs.opening: lana-pes , with wool on the feet (i. e. wrapped round), woolfooted : senex, Cass. ap. Quint. 5, 11, 24 .

lănista.opening: a trainer of gladiators, fencing-master (class.; cf.: gladiator, athleta, pugil). Lit. : num ille lanista omnino jam a gladiatore recessisse videtur, Cic. Rosc. Am. 40, 118 : reus, tamquam clemens lanista, id. Att. 1,…

lănistātūra.opening: lanista , the profession of a lanista, Inscr. Tab. Aen. Heracl. ap. Mazoch. p. 424, 49.

lănistīcĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to a trainer of gladiators : familia, Petr. Fragm. Trag. 45, 4 .

lănĭus.opening: 1. lanio , a butcher (cf. macellarius): lanii, qui concinnant liberis orbas ovīs, Plaut. Capt. 4, 2, 39 ; id. Ps. 1, 2, 63 : cetarii, lanii, coqui, Ter. Eun. 2, 2, 26 ; Plaut. Trin. 2, 4, 6 ; cf. Cic. Off. 1, 42, 150 :…

lannae.opening: λοβοί , ear-flaps , Gloss. Philox. (sync. for laminae; v. lamina).

lāno.opening: ἐριοφορέω , Gloss. Philox., to bear or wear wool .

lānōsus.opening: adj. lana , full of wool, woolly (post-Aug.): uterus, Col. 7, 3, 7 : vellus, App. M. 8, p. 214, 29 .

lanterna.opening: (ante-class. and later ), , Gr. λαμπτήρ, root in λάμπω; cf. Lat. limpidus, lepor, lepidus, lĕpus , a lantern, lamp, torch : a portu illic nunc cum laterna huc advenit, Plaut. Am. prol. 149 : laterna Punica, id. Aul. 3,…

lanternārĭus.opening: lanterna , a lantern-bearer, guide : Catilinae, Cic. Pis. 9, 20 .

lānūgĭnĕus.opening: adj. lanugo , for lanuginosus, woolly, downy (post-class.): folia, App. Herb. 62 .

lānūgĭno.opening: v. n. lanugo , to be of wool (late Lat.): lanuginans trama, Aug. in Job, 38.

lānūgĭnōsus.opening: adj. lanugo , woolly, downy (Plinian): araneus, Plin. 29, 4, 27, § 85 : vermiculus, id. 30, 15, 47, § 139 : lanuginosa et aspera folia, id. 25, 8, 45, § 83 . — Comp. : herba lanuginosior, Plin. 22, 20, 24, § 50 .

lānūgo.opening: cf. Gr. λάχνη, Lat. lāna , woolly substance, down , of plants, of the cheeks, etc. ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : flaventem primā ianugine malas Dum sequeris Clytium, Verg. A. 10, 324 ; so, primaque par sacrae…

lānŭla.opening: dim. lana , a little wool, a small lock of wool (perh. only in Celsus), Cels. 6, 9 fin. ; 7, 27, 1 .

Lānŭvĭum.opening: ( ), , , a town of Latium, on the Via Appia, now Cività Lavinia , Cic. Agr. 2, 35, 96 ; id. Mil. 10, 27 ; 17, 45 ; id. Div. 1, 44, 99 ; Liv. 3, 29 ; cf. Mann. Ital. 1, p. 635.—Hence, ( ), , adj., of or belonging to…

lanx.opening: cf. λέκος, λεκάνη , a plate, platter, charger, dish (class.; cf.: patina, patella, magis, scutula). In gen.: in lancibus, Plaut. Curc. 2, 3, 45 : in filicatis lancibus, Cic. Att. 6, 1, 13 : pomum de caelata sumere…

Lāŏcŏon.opening: ( ), , , = Λαοκόων , a son of Priam and Hecaba, priest of the Thymbrean Apollo, who was killed, with his two sons, at the altar by two serpents , Verg. A. 2, 41 ; 201 ; Hyg. Fab. 135 : sicut in Laocoonte, in the statue…

Lāŏdămīa.opening: , = Λαοδάμεια , a daughter of Acastus; she followed her husband Protesilāus, who had been slain by Hector, to the Lower World , Hyg. Fab. 243 ; Ov. P. 3, 1, 110 ; id. H. 13, 2 ; Cat. 68, 74 .

Lāŏdĭcē.opening: , = Λαοδίκη . A daughter of Priam, who married Helicāon, son of the Thracian king, Antenor , Hyg. Fab. 80 .— A woman , otherwise unknown, Ov. H. 19, 135 .— The wife of Antiochus , Val. Max. 9, 14, 1 ext .

Lāŏdĭcēa.opening: , = Λαοδίκεια , the name of several cities . In Cœle-Syria, near Lebanon , now Jusy , Mel. 1, 12 .— In Phrygia Major , also called , and , now Eski Hissar , Cic. Fam. 2, 17, 4 ; 15, 4, 2 ; Plin. 5, 28, 29, § 105 ; Vulg.…

Lāŏmĕdon.opening: , = Λαομέδων , the father of Priam and Ganymede, king of Troy , Cic. Tusc. 1, 26, 65 ; Prop. 2, 14 (3, 6), 2; Hor. C. 3, 3, 22 ; Ov. M. 6, 96 ; id. F. 6, 729 ; Hyg. Fab. 89 .—Hence, , , adj. , = Λαομεδόντειος , of or…

lăpăthum.opening: , and , , ( , Lucil.; v. infra . Ante-class. collat. form , , Varr. ap. Non. 550, 17 ; id. L. L. 5, § 103 Müll.), , = λάπαθον or λάπαθος , sorrel. —Form lapathum, Plin. 20, 21, 85, § 231 .—Form lapathus, Col. poët. 10,…

Lăpăthüs.opening: a fort or castle in Thessaly, at Tempe , Liv. 44, 2 ; 6 .

lăpĭcīda.opening: ( ), , lapiscaedo , a quarryman, stone-cutter : qui lapides caedunt, lapicidas dici, Varr. L. L. 8, § 62 Müll.; Liv. 1, 59, 10 : lapidicida, Sid. Ep. 3, 12 .

lăpĭcīdīnae.opening: († LAPICAEDINAE, Inscr. Orell. 1243 .—Collat. form lapidicinae; v. infra ), , id. , stone-quarries (class.): in lapicidinas facite deductus siet, Plaut. Capt. 3, 5, 78 ; 5, 1, 24 : in Chiorum lapidicinis, Cic. Div. 1,…

lăpĭcīdīnārĭus.opening: a superintendent of stone-quarries , Inscr. Orell. 3246 ; cf.: †lapicidinarius, λαξευτής , Gloss. Philox. —Collat. form: †lapidicinarius, λιθοξόος , Gloss. Philox.

lăpĭdāris.opening: adj. lapis , of stone, stone- : TERMINI, Inscr. Orell. 4334 .

lăpĭdārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to stones, stone- (ante-class. and post-Aug.): latomiae, stone-quarries, Plaut. Capt. 3, 5, 65 : navis, that carries stones, Petr. 117 : lapidariae litterae, cut in stone, id. 58 : †OPIFICES,…

lăpĭdātĭo.opening: lapido , a throwing of stones, a stoning (class.). Lit. : fit magna lapidatio, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 43, § 95 : magna, id. de Or. 2, 47, 197 ; id. Dom. 6, 14 ; Aur. Vict. Vir. Ill. 73 .—In plur. : lapidationes persaepe…

lăpĭdātor.opening: id. , a stoner, thrower of stones : percussor, lapidator, Cic. Dom. 5, 13 .

lăpĭdesco.opening: v. inch. n. [lapis], to become stone, turn to stone, to petrify (Plinian): spongiae ipsae lapidescunt, Plin. 24, 13, 73, § 120 : in balano lapidescit duritia, id. 16, 6, 8, § 21 ; 32, 2, 11, § 22 .

lăpĭdĕus.opening: adj. id. . Of stone, consisting of stones, stone- . Lit. (class.): flumen marginibus lapideis, Varr. R. R. 3, 5, 9 ; Cic. Leg. 2, 18, 45 : imber, a shower of stones, id. Div. 2, 28, 60 ; so, pluit lapideo imbri, Liv.…

lăpĭdo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
lăpĭdo.opening: v. a. and n. lapis , to throw stones at a person or thing, to stone ( = lapidibus obruo, percutio; not ante-Aug.). With personal object: exercitus imperatorem lapidavit, Flor. 1, 22 ; Petr. 93 : eum lapidare coeperunt,…

lăpĭdōsĭtas.opening: lapidosus , a stony hardness (post-class.), Tert. Hab. Mul. 6 .

lăpĭdōsus.opening: adj. lapis , full of stones, stony . Lit. : lapidosa terra, Varr. R. R. 1, 9 : montes, Ov. M. 1, 44 : ager, id. ib. 8, 799 : fluvius, id. ib. 15, 23 .— Transf. , hard as stone, stony : panis, Hor. S. 1, 5, 91 : corna,…

lăpillisco.opening: ( ), , v. inch. n. [lapillus], to become stone, turn to stone; trop., to become hard, be distended (eccl. Lat.), Tert. ad Nat. 2, 12 .

lăpillŭlus.opening: dim. id. , a very little stone, gravel-stone (late Lat.), Sol. 10, 12 .

lăpillus.opening: dim. lapis , a little stone, a pebble (perh. not ante-Aug.). In gen.: invitat somnos crepitantibus unda lapillis, Ov. M. 11, 604 ; Plin. 10, 23, 30, § 59 sq. —Lucky days were marked with white, and unlucky ones with…

lăpĭo.opening: v. a. lapis , to turn into stone, make hard like stone, to petrify, harden (ante-class.): lapit significat obdurefacit et lapidem facit. Pacuvius Periboea: lapit cor cura, Non. 23, 7 sq. ( Pac. Fragm. Trag. v. 276…

lăpis.opening: ( abl. lapi, Enn. ap. Prisc. 708 P.; gen. plur. lapiderum, C. Gell. ap. Charis. p. 40 P.), ( : tanto sublatae sunt augmine tunc lapides, Enn. ap. Non. 211, 9 ) [etym. dub.; perh. from same root with rupes; cf. Corss.…

Lăpĭtha.opening: , and , , , a Lapitha; plur. : , , , = Λαπίθαι , the Lapithæ , a rude tribe of mountaineers in Thessaly, about Olympus, who fought with the Centaurs at the wedding of Pirithŏüs, king of the Lapithæ, Ov. M. 12, 261 ; 536…

lappa.opening: a bur , Verg. G. 1, 153 ; Ov. P. 2, 1, 14 ; Plin. 18, 17, 44, § 153 ; 21, 17, 64, § 104 al. — , , , a Roman surname; e. g. Rubrenus Lappa, a tragedian , Juv. 7, 72 .

lappācĕus.opening: adj. lappa , burshaped, bur-like : capita, Plin. 22, 17, 19, § 41 .

lappāgo.opening: id. , a plant resembling a bur , Plin. 26, 10, 65, § 102 .

Laprĭus.opening: a surname of Jupiter , Enn. ap. Lact. 1, 22, 23 ( Eutr. p. 173 Vahl.).

lapsăna.opening: ( ), , (also , , , Hier. ap. Reg. S. Pachom. 52), = λαψάνη and λαμψάνη , an edible plant, charlock , Sinapis arvensis, Linn.; Plin. 20, 9, 37, § 96 ; Varr. R. R. 3, 16, 25 ; Cels. 2, 25 .—Prov.: lapsanā vivere, to live…

lapsĭo.opening: 1. labor , a sliding; trop., an inclination, tendency : haec in bonis rebus facilitas nominetur, in malis proclivitas, ut significet lapsionem, Cic. Tusc. 4, 12, 28 .

lapso.opening: v. freq. n. [id.], to slip, slide, stumble, fall . Lit. ( poet. and in postAug. prose): (Priamum) in multo lapsantem sanguine nati, Verg. A. 2, 551 : sanguine suo et lubrico paludum lapsantes (equi), Tac. A. 1, 65 :…

lapsus.opening: 1. labor , a falling, fall; a slipping, sliding, gliding, running, flowing, flying, flight , etc. (class.). Lit. : ac celeri ferme percurrunt fulmina lapsu, Lucr. 6, 324 : atque ea, quae lapsu tandem cecidere vetusto,…

lăquĕar.opening: (or , Verg. Cul. 62 ; cf. Prisc. p. 691 P.; and: laqueare, συνίθωμα , Gloss. Philox.: , , acc. to Isid. Orig. 19, 12 ), kindr. with laqueus and lacunar , a panelled or fretted ceiling ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose;…

lăquĕārĭus.opening: laquear , one that makes panelled ceilings, a ceiling-maker (late Lat.): architecti, laquearii, Cod. Th. 13, 4, 2.— Perh. a kind of gladiator; v. the foll. art.

lăquĕātor.opening: laqueus , an ensnarer , a kind of gladiator who attempted to catch his adversary with a noose, acc. to Isid. Orig. 18, 56 (al. laquearius).

lăquĕo.opening: (or ), , v. a. laquear , to adorn with a panelled or fretted ceiling (perh. only in the part. ): tectis caelatis lacuatis, panelled, fretted , Enn. ap. Cic. Tusc. 1, 35, 85 (Trag. v. 121 Vahl.); Serv. Verg. A. 1, 726 :…

lăquĕus.opening: cf. Gr. ἕλκω, draw, ὁλκός; Lat. lacio; perh. Germ. locken , a noose, snare (class.; cf. tendicula). Lit. , Plaut. Truc. 2, 4, 41 : saxa laqueis vinciebat, Sall. J. 94 : laqueis falces avertebant, Caes. B. G. 7, 22 :…

Lăra.opening: , and , , , daughter of the river-god Almo, a nymph whose tongue was cut out by Jupiter on account of her talkativeness, and who was worshipped in Rome under the name of Tacita or Muta: Lara, Ov. F. 2, 599 sq. :…

Lărālĭa.opening: 1. Lares , a festival in honor of the Lares , celebrated on the first of May; the festival of the Lares , Paul. ex Fest. p. 253 Müll.

lărārĭum.opening: id. , a part of the interior of a Roman house, in which the tutelar deities (Lares) were placed, the chapel of the Lares , Lampr. Alex. Sev. 29, 2 ; 31, 4 sq.

Larcĭus.opening: T. Larcius Flavus, a Roman dictator, Cic. Rep. 2, 32, 56 ; Liv. 2, 18, 5 .

lardārĭus.opening: lardum for laridum , a pork-butcher, pork-seller , Inscr. Grut. 647, 4 .

Lārentĭa.opening: ( , Lact. 1, 20 init. ), , (also called Acca Larentia), acc. to the myth, the wife of Faustulus, and mother of the twelve Arval Brothers, who suckled and reared the twins Romulus and Remus , Ov. F. 3, 55 ; Liv. 1, 4, 7…

Lăres.opening: a city in Numidia , Sall. J. 90 Kritz N. cr .

Larga.opening: the name of a woman of bad repute , Juv. 14, 25 .

largĭfĭcus.opening: adj. largus-facio , bountiful , Lucr. 2, 627 : grando mixta imbri largifico, Pac. ap. Cic. de Or. 3, 39, 157 (Trag. Fragm. v. 414 Rib.).

largĭflŭus.opening: adj. large-fluo , flowing copiously, copious (ante-class.): fons, Lucr. 5, 598 .

largĭlŏquus.opening: adj. large-loquor , talking copiously, talkative (Plautin.): largiloquae sumus: plus loquimur, quam sat est, Plaut. Cist. 1, 2, 2 : lingua, id. Mil. 2, 3, 47 .

largīmentum.opening: largior , for largitas, bounty, gift , Fulg. Myth. praef. 1.

largĭor.opening: (ante-class. and poet. ; collat. form of the imperf. largibar, Prop. 1, 3, 25 ; fut. largibere, Plaut. Bacch. 4, 7, 30 ; inf. largirier, id. As. 5, 2, 82 .— Act. collat. form, v. fin. ), v. dep. 1. largus , to give…

largĭtas.opening: 1. largus , abundance, bounty, liberality (rare but class.): largitas nimia, opp. parsimonia, Ter. Heaut. 3, 1, 32 : quae istaec subita est largitas? id. Ad. 5, 9, 28 : tui muneris, Cic. Brut. 4, 16 : terra fruges cum…

largītĭo.opening: largior , a giving freely, a granting, bestowing, dispensing, distributing, imparting . Lit. In gen. (class.): largitio, quae fit ex re familiari, fontem ipsum benignitatis exhaurit, Cic. Off. 2, 15, 52 : largitione…

largītĭōnālis.opening: adj. largitio, II. , of or belonging to the imperial treasury : officiales, treasury-officers, masters of the treasury , Cod. Th. 12, 6, 13; also subst. : , , , a treasury-officer , Vop. Carin. 19 .

largītor.opening: largior , a liberal giver, a bestower, granter, dispenser, distributer, imparter . In gen. (rare; not in Cic.): multarum rerum ac maxume pecuniae largitor, Sall. J. 95 : largitor voluntarius repente senatus factus, Liv.…

largĭtūdo.opening: 1. largus , liberality (for largitas): largitudo nusquam invenitur, nisi apud Nepotem, Charis. p. 78 P.

largĭuscŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [1. largus], rather copious : haustus, Sol. 7, § 4 .

largus.opening: adj. perh. for lasgus; Sanscr. root lash, desire; Gr. λᾶ- in λιλαίομαι, λῆμα; cf. Lat. lascivus , abundant, copious, plentiful, large, much . In gen. (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose): pabula, abundant, Lucr. 5, 869…

Largus.opening: a Roman surname , esp. in the gens Scribonia, Cic. Fam. 6, 8, 1 ; id. de Or. 2, 59, 240 : P. Largus Caecina, Tac. A. 11, 33 .—Hence, , , adj., of or belonging to a Largus, Largian : senatusconsultum, Just. Inst. 3, 7…

lārĭdum.opening: , and sync. (collat. form, , , , sc. caro, Cod. Th. 8, 4, 17), , kindr. with λαρός, λαρινός, fattened, fat , the fat of bacon, lard .—Form laridum: quanta pernis pestis veniet! quanta labes larido! Plaut. Capt. 4, 3, 3…

lărĭfŭga.opening: 2. lar-fugio , a vagabond : larifuga nescio quis, Petr. 57, 3 .

lărignus.opening: adj. larix , of the larch-tree, larch- : materies, Vitr. 2, 9, 15 .

Lārīnum.opening: a town of Samnium, in the territory of the Frentani, near Teanum, now Larino , Cic. Att. 7, 13, 7 ; 7, 13, 6 ; id. Clu. 8, 27 ; Mel. 2, 4 .—Hence, , , adj., of or belonging to the town of Larinum : Larinas socrus, Cic.…

Lārissa.opening: , = Λάρισσα , the name of several cities . In Thessaly, on the Peneus , now Yeni-shehr or Larissa , Mel. 2, 3 ; Plin. 4, 8, 15, § 29 ; Caes. B. C. 3, 80 ; Hor. C. 1, 7, 11 ; Luc. 6, 355 .— Hence, , , adj., of or…

Larissus.opening: ( ), , , a river in Achaia , now Mana , Liv. 27, 31 .

Lārĭus.opening: a lake in Gallia Cisalpina, on which Comum lay , now Lago di Como , Verg. G. 2, 159 ; Plin. Ep. 9, 7, 1 ; Plin. 3, 19, 23, § 131 .—Hence, , , adj., of Larius, Larian : Larium litus, Cat. 35, 4 .

lărix.opening: , ĭcis ( Vitruv., v. infra ), = λάριξ , a larch, larch-tree , Plin. 16, 10, 19, § 43 ; Vitr. 2, 9, 14 ; Luc. 9, 920 .

Lartidĭus.opening: , prop. name, an imitator of Ulysses , Cic. Att. 7, 1, 9 .

lărus.opening: ( ), , , = λάρος , a ravenous sea-bird , perh. the mew , Vulg. Lev. 11, 16 ; id. Deut. 14, 15 ; cf.: larus, λάρος , Gloss. Philox.

larva.opening: (ante-class. as trisyl. ), , 2. lar , a ghost, spectre : larvae stimulant virum, Plaut. Capt. 3, 4, 66 : amator qui me et uxorem ludificatust larva, id. Cas. 3, 4, 2 ; id. Aul. 4, 4, 15 : cum mortuis non nisi larvas…

larvālis.opening: ( ), , adj. larva , like a ghost, ghostly (post-Aug.): habitus, Sen. Ep. 25 ; so, si larvali habitu processeris, Lex ap. Paul. Sent. 3, 4 , b, 2: macies larŭalis, Auct. Priap. 32, 13 .

larvo.opening: , no perf. , ātum ( part. ante-class. ), , v. a. larva , to bewitch, enchant (ante- and post-class., and used almost exclusively in the part. perf. ): artus larvari, Firm. Math. 3, 14.— P. a. as subst. : , , , an…

Larymna.opening: the name of a small town in Bœotia , Mel. 2, 3 ; Plin. 4, 7, 12, § 26 .

lăsănum.opening: , = λάσανον , a utensil . Perh. a cooking-utensil, cooking-pot , Hor. S. 1, 6, 109 .— A chamber utensil, closestool , Petr. 41, 9 .

lăsarpīcĭfer.opening: adj. lasarpicium for laserpicium-fero , bearing or producing assafœtida , Cat. 7, 4 .

lascīvĭa.opening: lascivus , sportiveness, playfulness, frolicsomeness, jollity . In a good sense (class.): adulescens plenus amoris ac lasciviae, Plaut. Trin. 3, 3, 23 : hilaritas et lascivia, Cic. Fin. 2, 20, 65 : laeta (agrestium),…

lascīvībundus.opening: adj. lascivio , wanton, full of petulance , Plaut. Stich. 2, 1, 16 (Ritschl and Fleck. lixabundus, q. v.).

lascīvĭo.opening: v. n. lascivus , to be wanton, petulant, sportive, to sport, frisk, frolic (not freq. till after the Aug. per.). Lit. : licet lascivire, dum nihil metuas, * Cic. Rep. 1, 40, 63 : Ap. Claudius ait, lascivire magis plebem…

lascīvĭtas.opening: id. , wantonness (post-class.): Asiana, Firm. 1, 1; Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 8 .

lascīvŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [lascivus], a little or somewhat wanton : manus, Laev. ap. Prisc. p. 903 P.

lascīvus.opening: adj. Sanscr. lash-āmi, desire; las-āmi, play; Gr. la- in λάω, λιλαίομαι; cf. Goth. lustus; also Lat. largus , wanton, petulant, sportive, playful, frolicsome, frisky , (syn.: petulans, procax). In a good sense: nova…

lāser.opening: ( ), , , the juice of the plant laserpitium, assafœtida . Lit. : laser e silphio profluens, Plin. 22, 23, 49, § 101 ; cf.: cujus sucum vocant laser, id. 19, 3, 15, § 38 : laser Cyrenaicum vino diluere, Col. Arb. 23…

lāsĕrātus.opening: adj. laser , flavored with laser. Adj. : acetum, Plin. Val. 1, 21 .— Subst. : , , , a condiment made from laser, Apic. 1, 30 in lemm .

lāserpīcĭārĭus.opening: adj. laserpicium , of or belonging to laserpicium: de laserpiciario mimo, Petr. 35 dub. (in Bip.: de laserpitio et minio).

lāserpīcĭātus.opening: adj. id. , prepared or flavored with laserpicium: acetum, Cato, R. R. 116 ; Plin. 18, 30, 73, § 308 .

lāserpīcĭum.opening: ( ), , , a plant, also called silphium, from which the laser was obtained , Plaut. Rud. 3, 2, 16 ; id. Stich. 2, 3, 11 ; Col. 6, 17, 7 ; Plin. 19, 3, 15, § 38 ; also the juice of the silphium, id. 20, 13, 51, § 141 .

Lasĭa.opening: a name of the island of Lesbos , Plin. 5, 31, 39, § 139 ; also of a small island near Lycia , id. 5, 31, 35, § 131 .

lassesco.opening: v. inch. n. [lassus], to become tired, to grow weary (post-Aug.): ne lassescat fortuna, Plin. 7, 40, 41, § 130 ; 14, 2, 4, § 33 : victo lassescere visu, Prud. in Symm. 2, 101 : lassescere sub lorica, Hier. Ep. 22, 39 :…

lassĭtūdo.opening: id. , faintness, weariness, heaviness, lassitude (class.): exercitationis finis esse debet lassitudo, quae citra fatigationem est, Cels. 1, 2 : omnia membra lassitudo mihi tenet, Plaut. Stich. 2, 2, 12 : lassitudinem…

lasso.opening: v. a. lassus , to render faint or languid, to tire, weary, fatigue, to deprive of vigor (syn.: fatigo, languefacio; perh. not ante-Aug.): aliquem, Cels. 1, 3, 1 : laevam, Curt. 9, 5, 1 : longior infirmum ne lasset…

lassŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [id.], somewhat wearied : lassulae nimio e labore, Cat. 63, 35 .

lassus.opening: adj. etym. dub.; acc. to Bopp, Gloss. 112, 6, for glassus from glasnus; kindred to Sanscr. glasnu, fessus, defessus, lassus; but more prob. collat. form of laxus; cf. langueo , faint, languid, weary, tired, exhausted…

lastaurus.opening: , = λάσταυρος , a lewd person, debauchee , Suet. Gramm. 15 .

lătē^bra.opening: lateo , a hiding-place, lurking-hole, covert, retreat (class.; most freq. in plur. ; v. infra , II. B.). Lit. : (aurum) in latebris situm est, Plaut. Aul. 4, 2, 2 : itaque in totis aedibus tenebrae, latebrae, id. Poen.…

lătē^brĭcŏla.opening: latebra , one who dwells in lurking-places or brothels , Plaut. Trin. 2, 1, 14 .

lătē^brōsus.opening: adj. latebra , full of lurking-holes or coverts, hidden, retired, secret . Lit. (rare but class.): loca, lurking-places, disreputable haunts, Plaut. Bacch. 3, 3, 26 : via, * Cic. Sest. 59, 126 : locus, Liv. 21, 54 :…

lătens.opening: Part. and P. a. , from lateo.

lătenter.opening: adv. , v. lateo, P. a. fin .

lătĕo.opening: v. n. Sanscr. root rah-, forsake; rahas, loneliness, concealment; Gr. ΛΑΘ λανθάνω , to lurk, be or lie hid or concealed, to skulk (class.). Lit. In gen.: ubi sunt, ubi latent, Plaut. Ps. 1, 2, 69 : cochleae in occulto…

lăter.opening: Sanscr. root prath-, widen; prathas, breadth; Gr. πλατύς, πλάτος , a brick, tile . Lit. : nil mirum, vetus est maceria, lateres si veteres ruunt, Plaut. Truc. 2, 2, 49 sqq.: in latere aut in caemento, ex quibus urbs…

lătĕrālis.opening: adj. 2. latus , of or belonging to the side, lateral . Adj. (ante- and post-class.): lateralis dolor, Enn. ap. Victor. p. 1963 P. (Ann. v. 601 Vahl.; for which: lateris dolor, Plin. 21, 21, 89, § 155 ): cingula, Calp.…

lătĕrāmen.opening: later , any thing made like bricks : lateramina vasi, the earthen-ware, Lucr. 6, 233 .

Lătĕrānus.opening: later , the god of the hearth (because hearths were made of bricks), Arn. 4, 130 .

lătĕrārĭus.opening: adj. 2. latus , of or belonging to the sides; only subst. : , , (sc. tigna), side-beams , Vitr. 10, 20 .

lătercŭlensis.opening: laterculum , one who keeps the register of offices, a secretary , Cod. 12, 34, 5.

lătercŭlum.opening: later , a register of all the offices and dignities in the Roman empire , Cod. 1, 27, 1, § 7.— In gen., a register, list , Tert. adv. Val. 29 .

lătercŭlus.opening: ( , Caes. B. C. 2, 9, 2 ), , dim. id. . A small brick or tile : hanc contignationem laterculo astruxerunt, Caes. l. l.: sacellum factum crudis laterculis, Plin. 30, 7, 20, § 63 : observationes siderum coctilibus…

lătĕrensis.opening: adj. 2. latus , of or belonging to the side.—Subst. : , , , an attendant, body-guard, satellite (post-class.), Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 43 .

Lătĕrensis.opening: a Roman surname in the gens Juventia; e. g. M. Juventius Laterensis, a legate of Lepidus, Cic. Planc. 1 sq. ; id. Fam. 10, 21 ; 23 ; id. Att. 2, 18 ; 24 saep.

lătĕrīcĭus.opening: or , , adj. later , made or consisting of bricks : turris, Caes. B. C. 2, 10 ; 2, 14 : muri, id. ib. 2, 15 : opus, brickwork, Col. 9, 6, 4 : urbs, built of bricks, Suet. Aug. 28 : paries, Plin. 18, 30, 73, § 301…

lătĕrīna.opening: id. , a brickkiln (postclass.), Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 43 .

lătĕrĭtāna.opening: or , , (pira), a good sort of pears , Col. 5, 10, 18 ; 12, 10, 4 ; also, , Plin. 15, 15, 16, § 54 ; and , Macr. S. 2, 15 . (Perhaps pears from Laterium, in Arpinum; v. Laterium).

Lătĕrĭum.opening: a villa of Q. Cicero in Arpinum , Cic. Att. 4, 7, 3 ; 10, 1, 1 .

lătesco.opening: v. inch. n. [lateo], to hide one's self, lie hid, be concealed : hic Equus a capite et longa cervice latescit, Cic. Arat. 385 .

lātesco.opening: v. inch. n. [2. latus], to grow broad, to widen (not ante-Aug.): napi non in ventrem latescunt, Col. 2, 10, 24 : ossa paulatim latescentia, Cels. 8, 1 : bis sex latescit fascia partes, Manil. 1, 680 .

lătex.opening: ( , Att. ap. Prisc. p. 658 P.), a liquid, fluid (mostly poet. ).—So esp. of water: latices simulatos fontis Averni, Verg. A. 4, 512 : Lethaei ad fluminis undam Securos latices et longa oblivia potant, id. ib. 6, 715 :…

lathўris.opening: (collat. form, , Ser. Samm. 1099 ), = λαθυρίς , a plant, a kind of wolf's-milk , Plin. 27, 11, 71, § 95 .

lathўros.opening: , = λάθυρος , a plant, also called leontopodion, App. Herb. 7 .

Lătĭālis.opening: , e; , , āris; , e; , v. Latium, II. D.

lătĭbŭlor.opening: v. dep. n. [latibulum], to be concealed, to lie hid, to lurk (ante-class.): nocte ut opertus amictu latibuletur, Naev. ap. Non. 133, 9 ; Att. ib. 10 (acc. to Perott. Cornucop. also used by Varro in the act. form: vide,…

lătĭbŭlum.opening: lateo , a hiding-place, lurking-hole, covert, den , of animals. Lit. : cum etiam ferae latibulis se tegant, Cic. Rab. Post. 15, 42 : serpens e latibulis, id. Vatin. 2, 4 ; id. Off. 1, 4, 11 : furibunda ferarum, Cat. 63,…

lātĭclāvĭālis.opening: adj. laticlavius , for laticlavius: †TRIBVNVS, Inscr. Grut. 180, 3 .

lātĭclāvĭus.opening: adj. 1. latus-clavus, II. 4. , having a broad purple stripe, broad-striped . Adj. : mappa, Petr. 32 : tunica (a mark of distinction borne by senators, military tribunes of the equestrian order, and the sons of…

lātĭclāvus.opening: id. , a broad stripe on the toga of senators (v. clavus and laticlavius; late Lat.), Cod. Th. 6, 4, 17.

lātĭfĭco.opening: πλατύνω , to make wide, to widen , Gloss. Philox.

lātĭfundĭum.opening: 1. latus-fundus , a large landed property, large estate or farm (not ante-Aug.), Plin. 18, 6, 7, § 35 : nisi latifundiis vestris maria cinxistis, Sen. Ep. 89, 20 : metiri me geometres docet latifundia, id. ib. 88, 10 :…

Lătīnae.opening: (sc. feriae); , adv. , and , , v. Latium, II. B.

Lătīnĭensis.opening: , e. Latin , v. Latium, II. C.— A Roman surname : Q. Caelius Latiniensis, Cic. de Imp. Pomp. 19, 58 .

Lătīnĭgĕna.opening: Latium-gigno , one born in Latium , Prisc. 1285 P.

lătīnĭtas.opening: Latinus . Pure Latin style, Latinity : latinitas est, quae sermonem purum conservat, ab omni vitio remotum. Vitia in sermone, quominus is latinus sit, duo possunt esse: soloecismus et barbarismus, etc., Auct. Her. 4,…

Lătīnĭus.opening: a Roman proper name : Latinius Latiaris, Tac. A. 4, 68 : Latinius Pandus, id. ib. 2, 66 .

lătīnīzo.opening: v. a. 1. Latinus , to translate into Latin (late Lat.), Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 1, 8 ; id. Tard. 5, 4 .

lătīno.opening: v. a. id. , to express in Latin, translate into Latin , Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 4, 77 (dub.; al. latinizavimus).

Lătīnus.opening: a king of the Laurentians, who favorably received Æneas and gave him his daughter Lavinia in marriage , Liv. 1, 2 ; Just. 43, 1 ; Verg. A. 7, 45 sq. : urbs Latini, i. e. Laurentum, id. ib. 6, 891 .

lātĭo.opening: fero , a bearing, bringing (only in the trop. signif.). * In gen.: auxilii, a rendering of assistance, Liv. 2, 33 . 1.— In partic. (cf. fero). Suffragii latio, a voting or right of voting , Liv. 9, 43 , 24; 38, 36, 7;…

lātĭpēs.opening: adj. 1. latus-pes , broadfooted : anas, Avien. Prog. Arat. 358 .

lătĭtābundus.opening: adj. latito , lying hid, skulking , Sid. Ep. 1, 6 fin.

lătĭtātĭo.opening: id. , a hiding, lurking , Quint. 7, 2, 46 ; Dig. 42, 4, 7 .

lătĭtātor.opening: id. , one who lies hid , Aug.

lātĭtĭa.opening: 1. latus , breadth, width (late Lat.): fines in latitia breviores, Auct. Rei Agrar. p. 222 Goes.; opp. longitia, Inscr. ap. Marin. Iscriz. Alb. p. 119.

lătĭto.opening: v. freq. n. [lateo], to be hid or concealed, to lie hid, hide, lurk (rare but class.). In gen.: ille ignavissimus Mihi latitabat, Plaut. Trin. 4, 2, 83 : latitans Oppianicus, Cic. Clu. 13, 38 : latitans aper, Hor. C. 3,…

lātĭtūdo.opening: 1. latus , breadth, width of any thing (class.). Lit. : in hac immensitate latitudinum, longitudinum, altitudinum, Cic. N. D. 1, 20, 54 : fossae, Caes. B. G. 2, 12 : castra amplius milibus passuum VIII. in latitudinem…

Lătĭum.opening: 2. lătus; Sanscr. root prath-, to spread or widen; cf. Lat. later, etc.; prop., the plains or flat-land; by the ancients referred to latēre, because here Saturnus lay concealed from his son, Ov. F. 1, 238; Verg. A. 8,…

Latmus.opening: , = Λάτμος , a mountain in Caria, at the mouth of the Mæander, where Luna (Selene) kissed the sleeping Endymion , Cic. Tusc. 1, 38, 92 ; Mel. 1, 17 ; Plin. 5, 29, 31, § 113 .— Hence, , , adj., of or belonging to Mount…

Latobius.opening: an almost unknown deity , Inscr. Orell. 2019 .

Latobrigi.opening: a Gallic people, neighbors of the Helvetians, situated probably on the Rhine , Caes. B. G. 1, 5 ; 1, 28 sq.

Lātōna.opening: (old gen. sing. Latonas, Liv. Andron. ap. Prisc. p. 679 P.; Gr. form , , Varr. Sat. Mon. 83, 1 ), , = Λητώ ; Dor. Λατώ ; Aeol. Λάτων , daughter of the Titan Cœus and Phœbe, and mother of Apollo and Diana, whom she…

lātor.opening: latum, v. fero , a bearer , i. e. a mover or proposer of a law (class.): lator legis Semproniae, Cic. Cat. 4, 5, 10 : legis, id. N. D. 3, 38, 90 ; Quint. 12, 10, 5 ; 3, 2, 4 ; cf.: legis ambitus, Cic. Mur. 2 ; Quint. 3,…

lātrābĭlis.opening: adj. 1. latro , barking : vox, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 11, 103 : animal, Mythogr. Lat. 3, 9, 3: bestia, Boëth. ap. Porphyr. 1, p. 52.

lātrātor.opening: id. , a barker (perh. not ante-Aug.). Lit. , poet. for a dog : Molossi, Mart. 12, 1 : Anubis (who is represented with the head of a dog), Verg. A. 8, 698 ; Ov. M. 9, 690 .— Transf. , a bawler, brawler : a viro bono in…

lātrātōrĭus.opening: adj. latrator , brawling, noisy : lingua, Isid. Orig. 19, 23, 6 .

lātrātus.opening: 1. latro , a barking (not ante-Aug.), Plin. 8, 40, 61, § 142 : apros Latratu turbabis agens, Verg. G. 3, 411 .—In plur. : venator cursu canis et latratibus instat, Verg. A. 12, 751 : latratus edere, Ov. M. 4, 450 :…

latrīa.opening: , = λατρεια , service, worship , Cassiod. de Amic. 36 .

lātrīna.opening: (collat. forms , , and , , , Lucil. and Laber. ap. Non. 212, 10 sq. ; cf. Lachm. ad Lucr. 2, p. 393 ), contr. from lavatrina, Varr. L. L. 5, § 118 Müll.; 9, § 68 ib. . A bath : qui in latrina languet, Lucil. ap. Non.…

Lātris.opening: λάτρις, a maid-servant, handmaid , a female proper name : deliciaeque meae Latris, Prop. 4 (5), 7, 75.

lātro.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
lātro.opening: v. n. and a. [cf. Gr. λοιδορέω and λατράζειν = βαρβαρίζειν , Hesych.], to bark (cf. baubor). Lit. : si canes latrent, Cic. Rosc. Am. 20, 56 ; Lucr. 5, 1066 : ne latret canis, Hor. S. 1, 2, 128 : quasi feta canes sine…

lā^tro.opening: Gr. λάτρις, root λα-, λαϝ-, in λάω, λεία; cf. lucrum , a hired servant, hireling, mercenary, satellite, bodyguard , etc. (only ante-class.): haec effatus ibi, latrones dicta facessunt, Enn. ap. Non. 306, 23 (Ann. v. 60…

Lā^tro.opening: a Roman surname. So M. Porcius Latro, a famous orator from Spain, a friend of the elder Seneca , Sen. Contr. 1 praef. ; Quint. 10, 5, 18 ; 9, 2, 91 ; Plin. 20, 14, 57, § 160 .—Hence, , , adj., of or belonging to Latro,…

lā^trōcĭnālis.opening: adj. 2. latro, II. , of or belonging to robbers, robber- (post-class.): manus, a band of robbers, App. M. 2, p. 125, 5 : castra, Amm. 27, 2 .—Hence, adv. : , after the manner of a robber, like a robber : aliquem…

lā^trōcĭnātĭo.opening: latrocinor , a robbing, highway-robbery : multitudinis saeva, Plin. 19, 4, 19, § 59 .

lā^trōcĭnĭum.opening: id. . * Military service for pay: apud regem in latrocinio fuisti, Plaut. ap. Non. 134, 28 .— Transf. Freebooting, robbery, highway-robbery, piracy (class.): cum illum ex occultis insidiis in apertum latrocinium…

lā^trōcĭnor.opening: v. dep. 2. latro . To perform military service for pay, to be a hired soldier (ante-class.): ibit aliquo Latrocinatum, Plaut. Trin. 2, 4, 198 ; id. Mil. 2, 6, 19 : qui regi latrocinatus decem annos Demetrio, id. Fragm.…

lā^truncŭlārĭus.opening: adj. latrunculus , of or belonging to draughts or chess : tabula, a chess-board, Sen. Ep. 117, 30 .

lā^truncŭlātor.opening: latrunculus, I. , one who tries cases of robbery, a larceny judge , Dig. 5, 1, 61 fin. ; Jul. Ep. Nov. c. 15, 60.

lā^truncŭlus.opening: dim. 2. latro . A highwayman, robber, freebooter, brigand : mastrucati latrunculi, Cic. Prov. Cons. 7, 15 : hostes sunt, quibus bellum publice populus Romanus decrevit, vel ipsi populo Romano, ceteri latrunculi vel…

lātūra.opening: fero , a bearing, carry ing of burdens (late Lat.), Aug. Serm. 345, 3 ; Sen. Apoc. 14, 3 : latura, φόρετρον , Gloss. Philox.

lātūrārĭus.opening: latura , a carrier, porter (late Lat.), Aug. Serm. 18, 4 ; 38, 9 ; 60, 8 .

lătus.opening: cf. Gr. πλατύς; Lat. lăter, Latium, plautus or plotus , the side, flank of men or animals. Lit. : ego vostra faciam latera lorea, Plaut. Mil. 2, 1, 2 : quid conminatu's mihi? Con. Istud male factum arbitror, quia non…

lătuscŭlum.opening: dim. 2. latus , a little side ( poet. and rare): laneum, Cat. 25, 10 : speculorum, Lucr. 4, 335 .

laudābĭlis.opening: adj. laudo , to be praised, praiseworthy, laudable (class. and freq.). Lit. : laudabile est, quod conficit honestam et praesentem et consequentem commemorationem, Auct. Her. 3, 4, 7 : honestum, etiam si a nullo…

laudābĭlĭtas.opening: laudo , laudability, excellency , a title of the Comes Metallorum: tua, Cod. Th. 10, 19, 3.

laudātĭo.opening: laudo , a praising, praise, commendation; a eulogy, panegyric . In gen.: quam lauream cum tua laudatione conferrem? with your eulogy , i. e. that pronounced by you , Cic. Fam. 15, 6, 1 : felicitatem ipsam deorum…

laudātīvus.opening: adj. id. , in rhet. lang. of Quintilian, of or relating to praise, laudatory : est unum genus, quo laus et vituperatio continetur, sed est appellatum a meliore parte laudativum: idem alii demonstrativum vocant: utrumque…

laudātor.opening: id. , a praiser; a eulogizer, panegyrist (class.). In gen.: integritatis et elegantiae, Cic. Att. 6, 2, 8 : auctores et laudatores voluptatis, id. Sest. 10, 23 : rerum mearum gestarum laudatores, id. Red. in Sen. 6, 16…

laudātōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to praise, laudatory (late Lat.), Fulg. Myth. init.

laudātrix.opening: laudator , she who praises (rare): vitiorum laudatrix fama popularis, Cic. Tusc. 3, 2, 4 : Venus, Ov. H. 17, 126 .

laudātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from laudo.

Laudĭcēni.opening: , collat. form of Laodiceni, v. Laodicea, II. B.—Hence, In a pun, of parasites [laudo-cena], dinnerchanters, who give applause for a dinner , Plin. Ep. 2, 14, 5 .

laudo.opening: v. a. laus , to praise, laud, commend, extol, eulogize, approve (cf.: celebro, praed co). Lit. In gen.: omnes mortales sese laudarier optant, Enn. ap. Aug. Trin. 13, 6 (Ann. v. 551 Vahl.): coram in os te laudare, to…

laurāgo.opening: laurus , a plant of the laurel kind , App. Herb. 58 .

laurĕātus.opening: adj. laurea , crowned or decked with laurel, laureate : imago, Cic. Mur. 41, 88 : lictores, id. Att. 7, 10, 1 : fasces, id. Div. 1, 28, 59 : legiones, Liv. 45, 39 : litterae, a letter announcing a victory (so called…

Laurentum.opening: a maritime town in Latium, between Ostia and Lavinium , now Torre Paterno , Mel. 2, 4, 9 .—Hence, , , adj. Of or belonging to Laurentum, Laurentian : Laurens Thybris, Verg. A. 5, 797 : arva, id. ib. 7, 661 : Turnus, id.…

laurĕŏla.opening: dim. laurea , lit., a little laurel crown or garland; hence, transf., a little triumph : quod esset ad laureolam satis, Cic. Fam. 2, 10, 2 .—Prov.: laureolam in mustaceo quaerere (a laurel branch in a laurel cake), i.…

Laurĕŏlus.opening: a notorious robber, who is said to have been crucified and torn to pieces by wild beasts; hero of a play by the mimographer Q. Lutatius Catulus , Juv. 8, 187 ; Mart. Spect. 7 ; Suet. Calig. 57 .

Laurētum.opening: ( ), , laurus , a laurel-grove : tale, Suet. Galb. 1 .— Esp., Lauretum or Laurel-grove , a place on the Aventine Hill, Varr. L. L. 5, § 152 Müll.—Form Loretum, Plin. 15, 30, 40, § 138 .

laurĕus.opening: adj. id. , of laurel, laurel- . Adj. : vectes laurei, Cato, R. R. 31 : folia, id. ib. 76 : corona, Liv. 23, 11 : in nitidā laurea serta comā, Ov. Tr. 2, 172 : oleum, laurel-oil, Plin. 20, 13, 51, § 137 : ramus, id. 15,…

laurex.opening: ( ), , (Balearic), a young rabbit cut out from the mother, or taken from her teats , Plin. 8, 55, 81, § 217 .

laurĭcŏmus.opening: adj. laurus-coma , laurel-haired, covered with laurels : montes, Lucr. 6, 152 .

laurĭfer.opening: adj. laurus-fero . Laurel-bearing : tellus, Plin. 15 , 30, 40, § 134.— Laurel-crowned : juventa, Luc. 8, 25 : currus, id. 5, 332 .

laurĭger.opening: adj. laurus-gero , laurel-bearing, crowned or decked with laurel : Phoebus, Ov. A. A. 3, 389 : manus, Prop. 4 (5), 6, 54. cuspis, a lance wound round with laurel, Mart. 7, 6, 6 : avis, Sil. 5, 422 .

laurīnus.opening: adj. laurus , of laurel, laurel- : folium, Plin. 12, 8, 18, § 34 : oleum, id. 23, 4, 43, § 86 .

laurĭōtis.opening: adj. , = Λαυριῶτις , from Laurion, in Attica , where there were silver mines; hence, spodos, the ashes which, in smelting silver, remain in the furnace, dross, scoria, Plin. 34, 13, 34, § 132 .

laurĭpŏtens.opening: laurus-potens , lord of laurels, laurel-ruler , an epithet of Apollo, Mart. Cap. 1, § 24 .

Laurŏlāvīnĭum.opening: a later name of the city Lavinium, after (about the time of the Antonines) the inhabitants of Laurentum were transplanted thither , Front. de Colon. p. 105 Goes.; Serv. ad Verg. A. 7, 59 . —Hence, , , , an inhabitant of…

Laurōn.opening: a city in Hispania Tarraconensis, Flor. 3, 22, 7 ; 4, 2, 86 .— Hence, , , adj., Lauronian : vina, Plin. 14, 6, 8, § 71 .

laurus.opening: ( gen. laurūs, Plin. 15, 30, 39, § 132 ; 14, 16, 19, § 112 ; Col. 6, 7, 3 codd.; abl. lauru, Hor. C. 2, 7, 19 ; but lauro, id. ib. 3, 30, 16 ; nom. plur. laurus, Verg. A. 3, 91 ; acc. plur. laurus, id. E. 6, 83 al. ;…

laus.opening: ( gen. plur. laudium, Sid. Carm. 23, 32 ), for claus, from clavid, kindred to cluo and the Greek κλέϝος , praise, commendation, glory, fame, renown, esteem (cf.: gloria, praeconium, elogium). Lit. : in laude vivere,…

Laus.opening: the name of several cities .—Esp., a city in Cisalpine Gaul, northwest of Placentia , now Lodi Vecchia , Cic. Q. Fr. 2, 15, 1 ; also called Laus Pompeia, Plin. 3, 17, 21, § 124 .

Lausus.opening: Son of Numitor and brother of Rhea Silvia , Ov. F. 4, 55 .— The son of Mezentius, whom Æneas slew , Verg. A. 7, 649 ; 10, 790 .

lautĭa.opening: (in Plutarch λαύτεια , Quaest. Rom. 45; old form: dautia quae lautia dicimus et dantur legatis hospitii gratia, Paul. ex Fest. p. 68 Müll.), , lautus, v. lavo fin. , the entertainment furnished in Rome to foreign…

lautĭtas.opening: πολυτέλεια , Gloss. Philox.; cf. the foll. art.

lautĭtĭa.opening: lautus , elegance, splendor, magnificence in one's style of living, in one's house, furniture, food, etc. In gen., Sen. Ep. 114, 9 : fama ad te de mea nova lautitia veniet, Cic. Fam. 9, 16, 8 : esse in lautitiis, Petr.…

lautĭuscŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [id.], somewhat splendid or magnificent : vestis, App. M. 7, p. 191, 22 .

Lautŭlae.opening: ( ), , lavo . A place in Rome where there were warm baths , Varr. L. L. 5, § 156 Müll. Acc. to Servius, the place where the Sabines, in pursuit of the Romans, were stopped by the gushing forth of a hot spring , Serv.…

lautŭmĭae.opening: ( and ), , , = λατομία , a stone-quarry . In gen.: vel in lautumiis vel in pistrino mavelim Agere aetatem, quam, etc., Plaut. Poen. 4, 2, 5 : latomiae lapidariae, id. Capt. 3, 5, 65 .— In partic., a prison cut out of…

lautŭmĭus.opening: adj. lautumiae , of or belonging to a stone-quarry : carcer, Sen. Cons. ad Marc. 17 ; cf. the preced. art. II.

lautŭmus.opening: or , , , a stonecutter , Vulg. 3 , Reg. 5, 15; id. 1 Par. 22, 15 .

lautus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from lavo.

lăvābrum.opening: lavo; fuller form of labrum , a bathing-tub : si calidis cunctare lavabris, Lucr. 6, 799 ; cf. Mar. Victorin. 2457 P.

lăvācrum.opening: ( , Ven. Carm. 5, 5, 96), , lavo , a bath (post-class.), Gell. 1, 2, 2 : lavacra pro sexibus separavit, Spart. Hadr. 18 : lavacra in modum provinciarum exstructa, Amm. 16, 10, 14 ; Tert. Cor. 3 : ferventia, Cael. Aur.…

lăvandārĭa.opening: id. , things to be washed : lavandaria dicit, quae ad lavandum sint data, Laber. ap. Gell. 16, 7, 5 (Inc. Fab. XVII. Rib.).

lăvātĭo.opening: id. , a washing, bathing, bath . In abstr.: quid ea messis attinet ad meam lavationem? Plaut. Most. 1, 3, 4 ; Cic. ap. Col. 12, 3, 2 : lavatio calida et pueris et senibus apta est, Cels. 1, 3, § 71 ; 79 ; cf.: boves…

lăvātōrium.opening: πλύσιμον , locus ad lavandum, Gloss. Philox.

lăver.opening: a water-plant , Plin. 26, 8, 32, § 50 ; called also sion, id. 22, 22, 41, § 84 .

Lăverna.opening: the patron goddess of gain (lawful or unlawful), and hence especially of rogues and thieves , Nov. ap. Non. 483, 21 (Com. Fragm. v. 105 Rib.); Plaut. Aul. 3, 2, 31 : mihi, Laverna, in furtis celerassis manus, id. Fragm.…

lăvernĭōnes.grammar: fures antiqui dicebant, quod sub tutela deae Lavernae essent, in cujus luco obscuro abditoque solitos furta praedamque inter se luere

Lăvernĭum.opening: a place in Campania , otherwise unknown, Cic. Att. 7, 8, 4 ; id. Fragm. ap. Macr. S. 2, 12 (in Cic. IV. 2, p. 235 Orell.).

Lāvīnĭa.opening: the daughter of Latinus and wife of Æneas , Liv. 1, 1 sq. ; Varr. L. L. 5, § 144 Müll.; Verg. A. 6, 764 ; Ov. M. 14, 449 ; 570 .

Lāvīnĭum.opening: a city of Latium, near the sea-coast, six Roman miles distant from Laurentum, founded by Æneas in honor of his wife Lavinia , now Pratica , Liv. 1, 1, 11 ; Varr. L. L. 5, § 144 Müll.; id. R. R. 2, 4, 18 ; Ov. M. 15, 728…

lăvĭto.opening: v. freq. a. lavo , to wash, bathe : se lacrimis falsis, Pompon. ap. Calp. Pis. ap. Merul. Fragm. Ennii, p. 308 (dub.; v. Com. Fragm. Pompon. v. 164 Rib.).

lăvo.opening: (in class. prose, perf. lāvi; sup. always lavātum; perf. part. lautus; the other forms of the first conj. Also, pres. lavĕre; second pers. lavis, ante-class. and poet. ; cf. Diom. 1, p. 377 ; v. Neue, Formenl. second…
