lax.opening: cf. Gr. λέχρις; Lat.: licinus, luxus , fraud, deception : lacit decipiendo inducit. Lax etenim fraus est, Paul. ex Fest. p. 116 .

laxāmentum.opening: laxo , an extending, widening . Lit. (post-Aug.): ventus laxamentum sibi parat, Sen. Q. N. 6, 18, 3 : cellae, Vitr. 4, 7 fin. : ventris, an evacuating, purging, Macr. S. 7, 11 .— Transf. (in concr.), a wide space, room…

laxātĭo.opening: id. , a widening, wide space, width, breadth (post-Aug.). Lit. : duorum digitorum laxatio, Vitr. 4, 7, 4 .— A relief, mitigation , Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 1, 52 al.

laxātīvus.opening: adj. id. , mitigating, assuaging : cataplasmata, Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 3, 67 ; id. Acut. 3, 17, 151 .

laxātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from laxo.

laxĭtas.opening: laxus , width, roominess, spaciousness, extent . Lit. (rare but class.), of a house, Cic. Off. 1, 39, 139 : loci, Sall. ap. Non. 132, 23 : laxitas appellatur Propontis, angustiae Thracius Bosporus, the wide part, Plin.…

laxo.opening: v. a. (rarely ; v. I. B. 2. β . and II. B. β . infra) [id.], to stretch out, extend, to make wide or roomy, to expand . Lit. : forum, Cic. Att. 4, 16, 8 : manipulos, to open the ranks, Caes. B. G. 2, 25 : lilium ab…

laxus.opening: adj. cf. languidus, languor, lactes , wide, loose, open; spacious, roomy; opp. adstrictus (not freq. till after the Aug. per.). Lit. : laxius agmen, Sall. ap. Non. 235, 16 : casses, Verg. G. 4, 247 : circli, id. ib. 3,…

lĕa.opening: leo , a lioness ( poet. for leaena): panthera et lea, Varr. ap. Philarg. ad Verg. E. 2, 63 ; * Lucr. 5, 1318 : pectus et ora leae, Ov. M. 9, 648 : hirsutae, id. F. 5, 176 ; id. M. 14, 255 : saeva, id. ib. 4, 102 .

lĕaena.opening: , = λέαινα , a lioness : statuerunt aeream leaenam, Cic. ap. Philarg. ad Verg. E. 2, 63 ; Plin. 8, 16, 17, § 45 ; Gell. 13, 7, 1 ; Tib. 3, 4, 90 ; Verg. E. 2 , 63; id. G. 3, 245 ; 4, 408 ; Ov. M. 4, 97 ; 514 ; 9, 615 ;…

Lĕaena.opening: , = Λέαινα , an heroic courtesan of Athens, in the time of Harmodius and Aristogīton , Plin. 7, 23, 23, § 87 ; 34, 8, 19, § 72 ; Lact. 1, 20 .

Lēander.opening: ( , Mart. Spect. 25 ; voc. Leandre, Ov. H. 19, 1 al. ), , , = Λείανδρος , a young man of Abydos, who, in order to visit Hero in Sestos, swam nightly across the Hellespont, until he was drowned in a storm , Ov. H. 18 and…

Lĕarchus.opening: , = Λέαρχος , the son of Athamas and Ino, whom Athamas, in a fit of madness, killed , Ov. M. 4, 515 ; id. F. 6, 479 ; Hyg. Fab. 1, 2 .—Hence, , , adj., of Learchus : umbrae, Ov. F. 6, 491 .

Lĕbădĭa.opening: ( , Stat. Th. 7, 345 ), , , = Λεβαδεία, Λεβαδία , a Bœotian city near Mount Helicon, and above which was situated the cave of Trophonius, with a temple , now Livadhia , Cic. Div. 1, 34, 74 ; Liv. 45, 27, 8 ; Gell. 12, 5…

Lĕbĕdus.opening: ( ), , , = Λέβεδος , a city on the coast of Ionia, north of Colophon; where every year great theatrical games were celebrated in honor of Bacchus , Hor. Ep. 1, 11, 6 sq. ; Mel. 1, 17, 2 ; Plin. 5, 29, 31, § 116 .

lĕbes.opening: , = λέβης , among the Greeks, a copper basin, kettle, caldron , for cooking, frequently given as an honorary reward or prize: tertia dona facit geminos ex aere lebetas, Verg. A. 5, 266 : Dodonaei, id. ib. 3, 466 ; Ov.…

Lĕbynthos.opening: ( , or ), , , = Λέβινθος , one of the Sporadic Isles , now Lenitha , Mel. 2, 7 ; Ov. A. A. 2, 81 ; id. M. 8, 222 .

Lĕchaeum.opening: , and , , , = Λέχαιον , the port of Corinth, on the Corinthian Gulf , Liv. 32, 23, 11 ; Stat. S. 2, 2, 34 ; Prop. 3, 20 (4, 21), 19; Stat. Th. 2, 381 : Corinthiacus hinc, illinc Saronicus appellatur sinus: Lechaeae…

lectārĭus.opening: κλινοποιός ( a couch-maker ), Gloss. Philox.; so, FABER LECTARIVS, Inscr. Orell. 4183 .

lectē.opening: adv. , v. 2. lego, P. a. fin .

lectīca.opening: Lit. , a litter, sedan , used at first only on journeys, but afterwards also, for the sake of convenience, in the city: lecticā octophoro ferebatur, Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 11, § 27 : lecticae usum alicui adimere, Suet. Caes.…

lectīcārĭŏla.opening: dim. lecticarius , a chairman's mistress , a comically formed term of reproach, Mart. 12, 58, 2 .

lectīcārĭus.opening: lectica , a litterbearer, sedan-bearer, chairman , Cic. Rosc. Am. 46, 134 ; Sulp. ap. Cic. Fam. 4, 12, 3 : lecticarii cum asseribus in auxilium accucurrerunt, with their poles, Suet. Calig. 58 : inter urbana ministeria…

lectīcŭla.opening: dim. lectica , a small litter or sedan . In gen.: lecticulā in curiam esse delatum, Cic. Div. 1, 26, 55 : Scipio lecticulā in aciem illatus, Liv. 24, 42 . — In partic. A bier : elatus est in lecticula sine ulla pompa…

lectĭo.opening: lego . A gathering, collecting . In gen. (post-Aug. and rare): lectio lapidum, Col. 2, 2, 12 : florum, Arn. 5, 173 .—* In partic., a picking out, selecting : judicum, Cic. Phil. 5, 6, 16 . — A reading, perusal; a…

lectisternĭātor.opening: lectisternium , one who arranged the couches and placed the cushions on them for reclining on at table : propera, abi intro; tu esto lectisterniator, Plaut. Ps. 1, 2, 29 ; cf.: lectis sternundis studuimus, id. Stich. 5,…

lectisternĭum.opening: 2. lectus-sterno , a feast of the gods . Lit. , an offering in which the images of the gods, lying on pillows, were placed in the streets, and food of all kinds set before them; these banquets were prepared by the…

lectĭto.opening: v. freq. a. 2. lego . To gather or collect eagerly or often (postclass.): conchulas et calculos in litore lectitasse, Val. Max. 8, 8, 1 : flores, Arn. 5, 183 . — To read often, with eagerness , or with attention…

lectĭuncŭla.opening: dim. lectio , a short or light reading : matutina tempora lectiunculis consumpseris, Cic. Fam. 7, 1, 1 .

lecto.opening: v. freq. [2. lego], = lectito, Vet. Schol. Hor. S. 1, 6, 122 ; cf. Charis. 142 P.

Lecton.opening: ( ), , , = Λέκτον , a promontory on the coast of Troy , now C. Baba , Liv. 37, 37 ; Plin. 5, 32, 32, § 123 ; 9, 17, 29, § 62 .

lector.opening: 2. lego , one who reads . Lit. In gen., a reader : cum enim Brutus duos lectores excitasset, et alteri orationem legendam dedisset, etc., Cic. de Or. 2, 55, 223 : nihil est aptius ad delectationem lectoris, quam…

lectrix.opening: lector , a female reader , Inscr. ap. Fabr. p. 311, n. 347; cf. Cledon. p. 1893 P.; Serv. Verg. A. 12, 159 .

lectŭālis.opening: adj. 2. lectus , of or belonging to the bed : morbus, which confines one to his bed, Spart. Hadr. 23 dub. (al. letalis).

lectŭārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to the bed, bed- (late Lat.): lectuaria (lecticaria) sindon, Non. 537, 21 .

lectŭlus.opening: dim. id. , a cosey couch, a bed . In gen.: qui sese illa ipsa nocte me in meo lectulo interfecturos pollicerentur, Cic. Cat. 1, 4, 9 : philosophi in suis lectulis plerumque moriuntur, id. Fin. 2, 30, 97 : a ducenda…

lectŭrĭo.opening: v. desid. a. [2. lego], to desire to read, be inclined to read (late Lat.), Sid. Ep. 9, 7 ; 2, 10 .

lectus.opening: 2. lego , a reading , Prisc. 1221 P.— = 2. lectus, q. v.

lēcўthĭnus.opening: adj. λήκυθος , of or belonging to an oil-flask : oleum lecythinum, oil from the flask (al. legitimo or lecythi), Petr. 21 .

lēcўthus.opening: , = λήκυθος , a flask, cruise , Vulg. 3 Reg. 17, 12 .

Lēda.opening: , and , , , = Λήδα , the daughter of Thestius, and wife of Tyndarus; she bore by Jupiter, who visited her in the form of a swan, two eggs, from one of which came Pollux and Helen, and from the other Castor and…

Lēdās.opening: the name of a man , Juv. 6, 63 .

Lēdŭs.opening: a river in Gallia Narbonensis, now Lez , Sid. Pan. 813 ; Mel. 2, 5 .

lēgālis.opening: adj. lex , of or belonging to the law, legal (post-Aug.): genus quaestionis, Quint. 3, 5, 4 ; cf. id. 3, 6, 86 sq. : quaestiones, id. 3, 6, 46 : status, id. 3, 6, 45 : tractatus, id. 3, 8, 4 : vita, according to the…

lĕgārĭum.opening: 2. lego , pulse, legumes , Varr. R. R. 1, 32 .

lēgātārĭus.opening: adj. legatum , enjoined by a last will or testament (postclass.). Adj. : editiones, Tert. Spect. 6 . — Subst. , , , one to whom something is left by will, a legatee , Suet. Galb. 5 ; Dig. 41, 3, 14 ; Gai. Inst. 2, 195 :…

lēgātĭo.opening: 1. lego , the sending of an ambassador; hence, the office of an ambassador, an embassy, legation . Lit. In gen.: cum legatione in provinciam esset profectus, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 5, § 9 : legationem obire, id. Ac. 2, 2, 5 :…

lēgātīvus.opening: adj. 1. lego . Of or relating to an embassy (post-class.): viaticum, or absol. , , , an ambassador's expenses : viaticum, quod legativum dicitur, Dig. 50, 4, 18, § 12 : his, qui non gratuitam legationem susceperunt,…

lēgātor.opening: id. , one who leaves something by will, a testator : voluntas legatoris, Suet. Tib. 31 .

lēgātōrĭus.opening: adj. legatus , of or belonging to a deputy : provincia, one given to a senator as deputy or lieutenant , Cic. Att. 15, 9, 1 B. and K. (dub.; Orell. locatoria).

lĕgĭbĭlis.opening: adj. 2. lego , that may be read, legible (post-class.): si legibilia sunt inconsulto deleta, Dig. 28, 4, 1 .

lēgĭfer.opening: adj. lex-fero , lawgiving ( poet. ). Adj. : Minos, Ov. Am. 3, 10, 41 : legifera Ceres (as the foundress of the social life of mankind), Verg. A. 4, 58 . — Subst. : , , , a law-giver , applied to Moses, Lact. 4, 17, 7 ;…

lĕgĭo.opening: 2. lego (prop., a selecting, choosing; hence), transf., a body of soldiers : legio, quod leguntur milites in delectu, Varr. L. L. 5, § 87 Müll. Lit. , a Roman legion . It consisted of 10 cohorts of foot-soldiers and 300…

lĕgĭōnārĭus.opening: adj. legio , of or belonging to a legion, legionary : miles, Asin. Poll. ap. Cic. Fam. 10, 32, 5 ; cf.: legionarii milites legionis decimae, Caes. B. G. 1, 42 : cohortes, id. ib. 3, 11 ; id. B. C. 1, 73 ; Sall. J. 41 :…

lēgĭrŭpa.opening: lex-rumpo , a lawbreaker (ante- and post-class.): perjure, legirupa, pernicies adolescentum, Plaut. Ps. 1, 3, 130 ; cf. id. Rud. 3, 2, 38 ; id. Ps. 4, 2, 19 : legirupam damnare, id. Pers. 1, 2, 16 ; Prud. Ham. 239 ; cf.…

lēgis-doctor.opening: (also written separately), , , a doctor or teacher of the law , Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 25 ; Vulg. Act. 5, 34 .

lēgislātio.opening: lex-latum, sup. of fero , the giving of the law , Vulg. Rom. 9, 4 .

lēgis-lātor.opening: and (in class. authors usu. written separately; v. lator), , , a law-giver, legislator : noster legumlator, Liv. 34, 31 ; Quint. 7, 8, 13 ; id. Decl. 329 ; 334 : legislator, Val. Max. 6, 5 , n. 3 ext. : non satis in ea…

lēgis-pĕrītus.opening: one learned in the law, a lawyer (late Lat.), Vulg. Luc. 7, 30 .

lēgĭtĭmus.opening: adj. lex; cf. Cic. Top. 8, 36 , fixed or appointed by law, according to law, lawful, legal, legitimate . Lit. Adj. : dies is erat legitimus comitiis habendis, Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 52, § 128 : legitimum imperium habere, id.…

lĕgĭto.opening: v. freq. a. , to read often , Prisc. p. 825 P.

lĕgĭuncŭla.opening: dim. legio , a small legion , Liv. 35, 49, 10 .

lēgo.opening: (archaic perf. legassit for legaverit, Fragm. XII. Tab. ap. Cic. Inv. 2, 50, 148 ), , v. a. lex; and therefore qs. lege creare , a publicist's and jurid. t. t. A publicist's t. t. To send with a commission or charge, to…

lĕgo.opening: ( gen. plur. part. legentum, Ov. Tr. 1 . 7, 25), , v. a. Gr. λέγω, λόγος, λογάς, etc.; Lat. legumen, di-leg-ens, neg-leg-o, etc.; cf. Germ. lesen , to bring together, to gather, collect . Lit. In gen.: oleam, Cato, R.…

legŭla.opening: a flap : auris, the earflap (late Lat.): aurium legulae, Sid. Ep. 1, 2 : Legula, μύτρον , Gloss. Philox.

lēgŭlēïus.opening: lex , a pettifogging lawyer, pettifogger , one who depends on legal technicalities for getting the better of his opponent: leguleius quidam cautus et acutus, Cic. de Or. 1, 55, 236 : formularii, vel ut Cicero ait,…

lĕgŭlus.opening: 2. lego , a gatherer, collector; esp. one who picked up the fallen olives (opp. strictor, he who beat or shook them from the tree; ante- and post-class.): ab legendo leguli, qui oleam aut qui uvas legunt, Varr. L. L. 6,…

lĕgūmen.opening: id. , pulse, any leguminous plant . In gen., Varr. R. R. 1, 23, 32 ; Plin. 18, 17, 46, § 165 ; Col. 2, 7, 1 ; 2, 10, 1 ; 18, 7, 10 : terra feta frugibus et vario leguminum genere, Cic. N. D. 2, 62, 156 ; Caes. B. C. 3,…

lĕgūmĭnārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to pulse : NEGOTIATRIX LEGVMINARIA, dealing in pulse, Inscr. Orell. 3093 . — Subst. : , ὀσπριοπώλης , Gloss. Philox.

leiostrĕa.opening: ( ), , , = λειόστρεον , an oyster with a smooth shell , Lampr. Heliog. 19, 6 .

Lĕlĕges.opening: , = Λέλεγες , a Pelasgic tribe who lived scattered over several parts of Asia Minor and Greece (in Caria, lonia, Mysia, Thessaly, Locris, Megara), Plin. 4, 7, 12, § 27 ; 5, 30, 33, § 127 ; Verg. A. 8, 725 ; Ov. M. 9,…

lēma.opening: , = λήμη , a humor or rheum that gathers in the corner of the eye (also called grāmiae), Plin. 23, 1, 24, § 49 .

Lĕmannus.opening: (with or without lacus), the Lake of Geneva .—Without lacus: deseruere cavo tentoria fixa Lemanno, Luc. 1, 396 ; cf. Plin. 2, 103, 106, § 224 .—With lacus: Rhodanus, Lemanno lacu acceptus tenet impetum, Mel. 2, 5, 5 ;…

lembŭlus.opening: dim. lembus , a small boat, a wherry , Prud. στεφ . 5, 455.

lembus.opening: , = λέμβος , a small fastsailing vessel with a sharp prow, a pinnace, yacht, cutter : lembus genus navicellae velocissimae, quod et dromonis nomine appellamus, Fulg. Exp. Serm. 564, 6 ; Att. ap. Non. 534, 5 : celerare…

lemma.opening: , = λῆμμα , a subject for consideration or explanation, a theme, matter, subject, contents (not ante-Aug.; in Cic. only written as Greek). Lit. : lemma sibi sumpsit, quod ego interdum versibus ludo, Plin. Ep. 4, 27, 3…

lemniscātus.opening: adj. lemniscus , adorned with pendent ribbons : corona, Serv. Verg. A. 5, 269 ; 6, 772 : palma, lit., a palm-branch ornamented with ribbons , the highest reward of a victor; hence, transf., for highest reward : palma…

lemniscus.opening: , = λημνίσκος . A pendent (purple?) ribbon , fastened to a victor's crown, at first of linden-bast or wool, afterwards of gold. A crown adorned with such a ribbon was the highest reward of a victor: tenuissimae earum…

Lemnos.opening: and , , , = Λῆμνος , the island of Lemnos, in the Ægean Sea; in mythology, the abode of Vulcan; it was also here that Philoctetes was left behind; now Lemno or Stalimeni , Plaut. Truc. 2, 4, 4 ; Ter. Phorm. 5, 7, 49 ;…

Lemonĭa trĭbus.opening: a rustic tribe on the Via Latina, Cic. Planc. 16, 38 ; id. Phil. 9, 7, 15 ; cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 115 Müll.

lēmōnĭum.opening: and , , , = λειμώνιον , the wild beet , Plin. 25, 9, 61, § 108 (al. molenonium); id. 20, 8, 28, § 72 .

Lĕmŏvīces.opening: a people of Aquitanian Gaul, neighbors of the Arverni; their name, as applied to their ancient capital, is preserved in the modern form of Limoges , Caes. B. G. 7, 4, 6 ; 7, 75, 3 ; Plin. 4, 19, 33, § 109 .

Lemovĭi.opening: a Germanic people on the Baltic, bordering on the Rugii : Rugii et Lemovii, Tac. G. 43 .

Lĕmŭres.opening: shades, ghosts of the departed. Lit. : Lemures animas dixere silentum, Ov. F. 5, 483 .— Transf. , in gen., ghosts, spectres : lemures larvae nocturnae et terrificationes imaginum et bestiarum, Non. 135, 15 sq. : somnia,…

lēna.opening: leno , a bawd, procuress . Lit. : lenas eas dicimus, quae mulieres quaestuarias prostituunt. Lenam accipiemus et eam, quae alterius nomine hoc vitae genus exercet, Dig. 23, 2, 43 : omnes sunt lenae levifidae, Plaut.…

Lēnaeus.opening: A surname of a king , otherwise unknown, Ov. Ib. 331 .— A name of Roman slaves , e. g. Cn. Pompeius Lenaeus, a freedman of Pompey , Suet. Gram. 15 ; Plin. 15, 30, 39, § 127 .

lēnīmen.opening: lenio , a softening or soothing remedy; an alleviation, mitigation, solace ( poet. ): testudo laborum Dulce lenimen, Hor. C. 1, 32, 14 : sollicitae lenimen dulce senectae, Ov. M. 6, 500 : addidit illis hoc quoque…

lēnīmentum.opening: id. , a softening or soothing remedy; an alleviation, mollification (post-Aug.). Lit. , Plin. 25, 5, 24, § 59 .— Trop. : addito honestae missionis lenimento, Tac. H. 2, 67 .

lēnĭo.opening: ( imperf. lenibant, Verg. A. 4, 528 : lenibat, id. ib. 6, 468 ; fut. lenibunt, Prop. 3, 20 (4, 21), 32), v. a. and n. 1. lenis . Act., to make soft or mild, to soften, mollify, alleviate, mitigate, assuage, soothe, calm…

lēnis.opening: adj. cf. lentus , soft, smooth, mild, gentle, easy, calm . Lit. : sensus judicat dulce, amarum: lene, asperum, Cic. Fin. 2, 12, 36 ; id. N. D. 2, 58, 146 : vehemens fricatio spissat, lenis mollit, Plin. 28, 4, 14, § 53…

lenis.opening: a kind of vessel , Afran. and Laber. ap. Non. 544, 31 .

lēnĭtas.opening: 1. lenis , softness, smoothness, gentleness, mildness . Lit. : vini, opp. asperitas, Plin. 14, 19, 24, § 120 : lini, id. 13, 12, 26, § 82 : Arar in Rhodanum influit incredibili lenitate, slowness, Caes. B. G. 1, 12 :…

lēnĭtĭes.opening: 1. lenis , mildness, gentleness : non sine lenitie, Schol. Ambros. ad Cic. Or. ap. Clod. et Cur. p. 20 Mai.

lēnĭtūdo.opening: id. , softness, mildness, gentleness, calmness (very rare): orationis, Pac. ap. Cic. Tusc. 5, 16, 46 (Trag. Fragm. v. 247 Rib.): mira lenitudine ac suavitate abundat, Turp. ap. Non. 132, 3 (Com. Fragm. v. 189 Rib.):…

lēno.opening: lenio , a pimp, pander, procurer . Lit. : perjurus leno, Plaut. Capt. prol. 57 : leno me peregre militi Macedonico Minis viginti vendidit, id. Ps. 1, 1, 49 : importunus, id. Merc. prol. 44 : leno sum, fateor, Ter. Ad.…

lēnōcĭnāmentum.opening: lenocinor , an allurement (late Lat.), Sid. Ep. 7, 9 .

lēnōcĭnātĭo.opening: id. , flattery (late Lat), Cassiod. in Ps. 15 .

lēnōcĭnātor.opening: id. , one who obtains any thing by flattery : gratiae lenocinator, Tert. adv. Marc. 1, 22 fin.

lēnōcĭnĭum.opening: leno , the trade of a pander, pimping, pandering . Lit. : ait praetor: Qui lenocinium fecerit. Lenocinium facit, qui quaestuaria mancipia habet. Sed et qui in liberis hunc quaestum exercet, in eadem causa est, etc.,…

lēnōcĭnor.opening: v. dep. 1. leno; lit., to pander; hence, transf. . To flatter, entice, allure, wheedle, cajole (syn.: blandior, adulor): tibi serviet, tibi lenocinabitur, Cic. Div. in Caecil. 15, 48 : gloriae alicujus, Sen. Contr. 1 :…

lēnōnĭcē.opening: adv. id. , like a pimp : quae lenonice faceret, Lampr. Commod. 15 (al. lenonie).

lēnōnĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or pertaining to pimping or pandering : non periclumst nequid recte monstres. Ba. Non lenoniumst (sc. recte monstrare), Plaut. Ps. 1, 3, 53 : aedes, id. Truc. 1, 1, 30 ; id. Men. 3 . 3, 29: servitus, id.…

lens.opening: ( nom. lentis, acc. to Prisc. p. 764 P.— Acc. lentim, Cato, R. R. 35 ; 116 ; Varr. ap. Charis. p. 101 P.: lentem, Col. 2, 10, 15 .— Abl. lenti, Titin. ap. Non. 210, 5 .— Plur. lentes, Scrib. Comp. 114 ), ( masc. ,…

lentĕo.opening: v. n. lentus , to proceed slowly : lentet opus, Lucil. ap. Prisc. p. 800 P.

lentesco.opening: v. inch. n. [lentus], to become viscous or sticky; to become pliant, soft (perh. not ante-Aug.). Lit. : salix, si minus lenta est, in stercore obruenda, ut lentescat, Col. 11, 2, 92 : sed picis in morem ad digitos…

lentĭcŭla.opening: dim. 2. lens , a lentil. Lit. : faba vel lenticula, Cels. 2, 18 : hoc mense lenticulam seres, Pall. 3, 4 .— Transf. The shape of a lentil, lentilshape , Plin. 37, 12, 75, § 196 .— A vessel shaped like a lentil : vasa…

lentĭcŭlāris.opening: adj. lenticula , like a lentil : ampulla lenticulari formā, lentilshaped , App. Flor. n. 9, p. 346, 26.

lentīgĭnōsus.opening: adj. lentigo , full of freckles, freckled : vir lentiginosi oris, Val. Max. 1, 7, 6 ext .

lentīgo.opening: 2. lens , a lentil-shaped spot . In gen.: stellio plenus lentigine, Plin. 29, 4, 28, § 90 : chartae, id. 13, 12, 25, § 81 .— In partic., a freckly eruption, freckles, lentigo : lentiginem habere, Plin. 30, 2, 6, § 16 :…

Lentīnus.opening: the name of a man , Mart. 3, 43 .

lentĭpēs.opening: adj. lentus-pes , slowfooted, slow-paced : comes, Aus. Ep. 21, 40 .

lentiscĭfer.opening: adj. lentiscus-fero , bearing mastic-trees : Linternum, Ov. M. 15, 713 .

lentiscĭnus.opening: adj. lentiscus , of or from the mastic-tree : oleum, Plin. 23, 2, 32, § 65 : resina, id. 24, 6, 22, § 36 ; Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 37, 197 al.

lentiscus.opening: the mastic - tree , Pistacia lentiscus, Linn. Lit. : viridis semperque gravata Lentiscus, Cic. poët. Div. 1, 9, 15.— Transf. Mastic-oil , Cato, R. R. 7, 4 ; Varr. R. R. 1, 60 ; Plin. 15, 6, 6, § 21 .— A toothpick of…

lentĭtĭa.opening: ( , , Auct. Aetn. 540 ), lentus , pliancy, flexibility, toughness, viscosity, stickiness : virgas sequacis ad vincturas lentitiae, Plin. 16, 37, 68, § 174 ; 16, 40, 77, § 210 : lactucae lentitiam pituitae digerunt, id.…

lentĭtūdo.opening: id. , slowness, sluggishness, inactivity . Lit. : conjuratorum, Tac. A. 15, 51 ; Vell. 2, 11, 2 .— Trop. : dulness, apathy, insensibility , Cic. Tusc. 4, 19, 43 : omnino non irasci est non solum gravitatis, sed…

lento.opening: v. a. id. , to make flexible, to bend ( poet. and in postclass. prose). Lit. : arcus lentare et fundere glandes, i. e. to draw a bow, Stat. Achill. 1, 436 ; so, arcus, id. Th. 1, 703 : Gortynia cornua, id. ib. 3, 587 .—…

Lento.opening: lentus, sluggard , a Roman surname : Caesennius Lento, Cic. Phil. 11, 6, 3 ; 12, 9, 23 .

lentor.opening: lentus , pliancy, flexibility; toughness, stickiness, viscosity (Plinian; cf. lentitia): ad rotarum axes lentore fraxinus utilis, Plin. 16, 43, 84, § 229 : lentor resinosus, id. 13, 6, 12, § 54 : picis, id. 16, 11 , 22,…

lentŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [lentus], rather slow : lentulus aut restrictus, Cic. Att. 10, 11, 2 .

Lentŭlus.opening: a surname of a distinguished family in the gens Cornelia. Cn. Cornelius Lentulus Clodianus, consul 682 A. U. C., Cic. Balb. 8, 19 ; 14, 33 ; Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 39, § 95 .— Cn. Cornelius Lentulus Marcellinus, consul 698 A.…

lentus.opening: adj. cf. lenis , pliant, flexible, tough, tenacious, sticky, viscous (syn.: flexilis, tardus, serus). Lit. : viburna, Verg. E. 1, 26 : vitis, id. ib. 3, 38 : genistae, id. G. 2, 12 : rami, id. ib. 4, 558 : flagellum,…

lēnullus.opening: dim. 2. leno , a little pimp , Plaut. Poen. 2, 1, 25 (ap. Prisc. p. 614 P., lenulus).

lēnuncŭlārĭus.opening: 2. lenunculus, for lembunculus , one who sails in a small vessel , Inscr. Orell. 3248 ; 4054 ; 4104 .

lēnuncŭlus.opening: dim. for lembunculus, from lembus , a small sailingvessel, a bark, skiff : pauci lenunculi conveniebant, Caes. B. C. 2, 43 : in lenunculo piscantes, Sall. Fragm. ap. Non. 534, 32 : occursu lenunculorum, Tac. A. 14, 5 :…

lĕo.opening: Gr. λέων, λίς , a lion . Lit. : validus, Lucr. 5, 985 : fulvus, Ov. H. 10, 85 : ferus, id. M. 7, 373 : magnanimus, id. Tr. 3, 5, 33 : leoni praecipua generositas, Plin. 8, 16, 17, § 42 : Gaetulus, Verg. A. 5, 351 :…

Lĕo.opening: ; only plur. : , , the priests of the Persian god Mithras : Leones Mithrae, Tert. adv. Marc. 1, 13 .

Lĕōcŏrĭon.opening: , = Λεωκόριον , a temple in Athens , reared in honor of the three daughters of Leos, who suffered themselves to be sacrificed in order to avert a famine: Leoidum est delubrum Athenis, quod Leocorion nominatur, Cic. N.…

Lĕōĭdes.opening: the daughters of Leos , Cic. N. D 3, 19, 50 Wyttenb. (Lambin., Leo natarum; B. and K., Leocorion, q. v.).

Lĕon.opening: , = Λέων . The name of a town near Syracuse , now Magnisi; acc. Leonta, Liv. 24, 39, 13 .— A ruler of Phlius , Cic. Tusc. 5, 3, 8 .— A celebrated painter , Plin. 35, 11, 40, § 141 .

Lĕōnĭdas.opening: ( nom. , Just. 2, 11, 2 ), , , = Λεωνίδας . A king of Sparta, who fell at Thermopylæ , Cic. Fin. 2, 30, 97 ; 2, 19, 62 ; id. Tusc. 1, 42, 101 ; 1, 49, 116 ; Nep. Them. 3 .— The name of a slave , Plaut. As. 1, 1, 43 al.…

Lĕōnĭdes.opening: An instructor of Alexander the Great , Plin. 12, 14, 32, § 62 ; Quint. 1, 1, 9 .— A teacher of the younger Cicero at Athens , Cic. Att. 14, 16, 3 ; 15, 16 , A; id. Fam. 16, 21, 5 .

lĕōnīnus.opening: adj. 2. leo , of or belonging to a lion, a lion's . Lit. : concede audacter ab leonino cavo, Plaut. Men. 1, 2, 47 : species, a lion-like appearance, Varr. R. R. 2, 9, 3 : pellis, Plin. 37, 10, 54, § 142 : jubae, id. ib.…

Lĕōnīnus.opening: adj., of or belonging to the emperor Leo, Leonine : lex, Cod. Just. 1, 3, 50 .

Leonnātus.opening: one of Alexander's generals , Nep. Eum. 2 ; Plin. 6, 23, 26, § 97 .

Lĕontĕus.opening: the name of a warrior , Stat. Th. 9, 133 .

lĕontĭcē.opening: , = λεοντική , a plant, called also cacalia, Plin. 25, 11, 85, § 135 ; v. cacalia.† † , , adj. , = λεοντικός , of or belonging to a lion : SACRA, the offerings made to Mithras, who was represented under the form of a…

Lĕontīni.opening: , = Λεοντῖνοι , a very ancient town on the eastern side of Sicily , now Lentini , Mel. 2, 7, 16 ; Plin. 3, 8, 14, § 89 ; Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 66, § 160 ; Liv. 24, 7, 2 .—Hence, , , adj., of or belonging to Leontini,…

lĕontĭos.opening: , = λεόντιος , a precious stone of the color of a lion , otherwise unknown, Plin. 37, 11, 73, § 190 .

Lĕontĭum.opening: , = Λεόντιον , an Athenian hetæra, a friend of Epicurus , Cic. N. D. 1, 33, 93 .

lĕontŏcăron.opening: , = λεοντόκαρον , a plant , otherwise unknown, App. Herb. 57 .

lĕontŏpĕtălon.opening: , = λεοντοπέταλον , a plant, lion's-leaf : Leontice leontopetalum, Linn.; Plin. 27, 11, 72, § 96 .

lĕontŏphŏnos.opening: , = λεοντοφόνος (lion-killer), a small animal whose urine was said to be fatal to lions , Plin. 8, 38, 57, § 136 .

lĕontŏpŏdĭon.opening: , = λεοντοπόδιον , i. q. leontopetalon, a plant, lion's-foot , Plin. 26, 8, 34, § 52 ; App. Herb. 7 .

lĕŏpardīnus.opening: adj. leopardus , of a leopard : adeps, Marc. Emp. 28 .

lĕŏpardus.opening: λεόπαρδος , a leopard : leopardi Libyci, Vop. Prob. 19 ; Lampr. Heliog. 21 .

Lĕōtўchĭdes.opening: , = Λεωτυχίδης , brother of Agesilāus , Nep. Ages. 1 .

lĕpas.opening: ( , Non. 551, 5 ), , , = λεπάς , a kind of shell-fish that adheres closely to rocks, a limpet : lopades genus conchae marinae, Non. l. l.: lepadas (lopadas, acc. to Non.), ostreas, captamus, Plaut. Rud. 2, 1, 8 ; id.…

lĕpĭdĭum.opening: , = λεπίδιον , a plant, garden-cress, pepperwort : Lepidium sativum, Linn.; Plin. 19, 8, 51, § 166 ; Col. 11, 3, 16 ; 41 ; 12, 8, 3 .

lĕpĭdōtis.opening: λεπιδωτός, scaly , a precious stone , otherwise unknown, Plin. 37, 10, 62, § 171 .

lĕpĭdŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [1. lepidus], rather pleasant, rather witty (post-class.): infacetus et impar lepidulis, Mart. Cap. 7, § 726 ; 8, § 807 .

lĕpĭdus.opening: adj. lepos , pleasant, agreeable, charming, fine, elegant, neat (esp. freq. in Plaut. and Ter.; in Cic. very rare). In gen.: fui ego bellus, lepidus, Plaut. Capt. 5, 2, 3 : nugator, id. Curc. 4, 1, 1 : virgo, id. ib. 1,…

Lĕpĭdus.opening: a surname in the gens Aemilia; e. g. M. Aemilius Lepidus, consul 675 A. U. C., an enemy of Sylla , Cic. Cat. 3, 10, 24 ; Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 91, § 212 .—Another M. Aemilius Lepidus, triumvir with Antony and Octavius , Cic.…

lĕpis.opening: , = λεπίς , a scale (pure Lat. squama): similiter squamae aeris, quam vocant lepida, Plin. 34, 11, 24, § 107 .

lĕpista.opening: ( and ), , , = λεπαστή , a drinking - vessel, goblet : lepista genus vasis aquarii, Paul. ex Fest. p. 115 Müll.: lepistae aut fictiles aut aëneae, Varr. ap. Non. 547, 26 : ferunt pulchras crateras aureasque lepistas,…

Lēpontĭi.opening: , = Ληπόντιοι , a people of Cisalpine Gaul, on the Ticinus; their territory is the modern Val Leventina , Caes. B. G. 4, 10 ; Plin. 3, 20, 24, § 134 ; cf. Mann. Ital. 1, p. 181 sq.—Hence, * , , , a Lepontian , Sil. 4,…

lĕpor.opening: and , , perh. root lamp-; Gr. λάμπω, λαμπρός; cf. Lat. limpidus, lanterna , pleasantness, agreeableness, attractiveness, charm . In gen.: quasi salsa muriatica esse autumantur sine omni lepore et sine suavitate, Plaut.…

lĕpŏrārĭus.opening: adj. lepus , of or belonging to a hare, hare- : lageos (vitis) est, quae Latine leporaria dicitur: nam λαγὼς lepus, Serv. Verg. G. 2, 93 .— Subst. : , , , a place where hares and other wild animals are kept; a preserve,…

lĕpŏrīnus.opening: adj. lepus , of a hare, hare- : coagulum, Varr. R. R. 2, 11, 4 ; Cels. 5, 5 : cinis, Plin. 28, 11, 46, § 166 : lana, Dig. 32, 70, 9 .

lē^pra.opening: , = λέπρα , the leprosy . Sing. (late Lat.): plaga leprae, Vulg. Lev. 13, 9 al. ; Scrib. Comp. 250 ; Juvenc. 1 .— Plur. : , (class.): lepras sedare, Plin. 24, 8, 33, § 48 : curare, id. 20, 21, 86, § 234 : emendare, id.…

Leprĕum.opening: or ( or ), , , and ( ), , , = Λέπρεον , a sea-coast town in Elis, south of Pylos; its ruins are near the modern town Strobitza , Cic. Att. 6, 2, 3 ; Plin. 4, 5, 6, § 14 ; cf. Mann. Griechenland, p. 525 sq.

lĕprōsus.opening: adj. lepra , leprous (late Lat.). Lit. : viri, Sedul. 4, 191 .— Trop. : nil tam leprosum aut putridum, Prud. στεφ . 2, 285.

Lepta.opening: λεπτός, weak , a Roman surname : Q. Lepta, praefectus fabrūm, Cic. Fam. 3, 7, 4 ; cf. id. ib. 5, 20, 4 . To him are addressed the letters, Cic. Fam. 6, 18 and 19.

Leptis.opening: ( abl. Lepte, Cod. Just. 1, 27, 2, § 1 ), , = Λέπτις , the name of two cities on the coast of Africa . Leptis Magna, situated on the Great Syrtis , now Lebdah , Mel. 1, 7, 5 ; Plin. 5, 4, 3, § 25 ; Sall. J. 19, 3 ; 77,…

leptŏmĕres.opening: , = λεπτομερές , consisting of fine particles , Theod. Prisc. de Diaeta, 10.

leptŏmĕrĭcus.opening: adj. , = λεπτομερικός , consisting of fine particles : virtus, Theod. Prisc. de Diaeta, 10.

lepton centaurĭum.opening: ( ), , = λεπτὸν κενταύριον , the lesser centaury : centaureum minus, Plin. 25, 6, 31, § 68 .

leptŏphyllon.opening: , = λεπτόφυλλον , a species of the herb tithymalus, Plin. 26, 8, 45, § 71 .

leptopsēphos.opening: , = λεπτόψηφος , a kind of porphyry with white spots , Plin. 36, 7, 11, § 57 .

leptŏrax.opening: , = λεπτόραξ , a kind of grape-vine with very small berries (like our Levant currants), Plin. 14, 1, 3, § 15 .

leptyntĭcus.opening: adj. , = λεπτυντικός , making thin or meagre : caeparum virtus leptyntica, Theod. Prisc. de Diaeta, 10.

lĕpus.opening: ( , Varr. R. R. 3, 12 ; Plin. 8, 55, 81, § 217 ; v. infra ) [cf. Aeol. and Sicil. λέπορις , collat. form of λαγώς , Varr. L. L. 5, § 101 Müll.; id. R. R. 3, 12 ; but Curt. compares lepor, lepidus, root in Gr. λάμπω ], a…

lĕpuscŭlus.opening: (contr. acc. plur. lepusclos, Poët. ap. Lampr. Alex. Sev. 38 ), dim. lepus , a young or little hare, leveret, a hare . Lit. : in qua (insula) lepusculos vulpeculasque saepe vidisses, Cic. N. D. 1, 31, 88 ; Col. 9, 9…

Lerna.opening: , and , , , = Λέρνη , a forest and marsh near Argos, through which flowed a stream of the same name; the abode of the Lernæan Hydra, which Hercules slew with the help of Iolāus, and then drained the marsh : belua…

Lesbĭa.opening: the name of a woman , one of the dramatis personae in Ter. And.

Lesbos.opening: ( ), ( acc. Lesbum, Tac. A. 2, 54 ), , = Λέσβος , a celebrated island in the Ægean Sea, off the coast of Troy and Mysia, the birthplace of Pittacus, Alcæus, Arion, Sappho, and Theophrastus, and famous for its wine; now…

lessus.opening: acc. um (only in acc. sing. ), , a wailing, cry, funeral lamentation : mulieres genas ne radunto, neve lessum funeris ergo habento, Cic. Leg. 2, 23, 59 ; but a false reading for pausam, Plaut. Truc. 4, 2, 18 .

Lĕsūra.opening: ( , Sid. Carm. 24, 44 ), , A mountain in Gaul that produced excellent cheese , now La Lozère , Plin. 11, 42, 97, § 240 .— , a small river in Belgium, that runs into the Moselle , Aus. Mosell. 365 .

lētābĭlis.opening: adj. letum , deadly, fatal : lues, Amm. 19, 4, 7 .

lētālis.opening: ( ), , adj. id. , deadly, fatal, mortal (mostly poet. and late Lat.): vulnus, Verg. A. 9, 580 ; Suet. Caes. 82 : harundo, Verg. A. 4, 73 ; ensis, Ov. M. 13, 392 : serpens, Stat. Th. 6, 40 : dapes, Val. Fl. 2, 155 :…

Lēthaea.opening: the wife of Olĕnus, who, on account of her pride, was turned into stone , Ov. M. 10, 70 .

lēthargĭa.opening: , = ληθαργία , drowsiness, lethargy , Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 6, 49 ; 2, 9, 45 .

lēthargĭcus.opening: adj. , = ληθαργικός , drowsy, lethargic : morbus, Plin. 23, 1, 6, § 10 : somnus, Aug. Ep. 48 ad Vincent.; Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 3, 38 al. — Subst. : , , , one affected with lethargy, a lethargic person : ut lethargicus…

lēthargus.opening: adj. , Gr. λήθαργος , drowsy, lethargic : morbus, Plin. 23, 1, 6, § 10 ; Schol. Juv. 6, 613 .—Esp. as subst. , , (sc. morbus), drowsiness, lethargy (in Cels. 3, 20 , written as Greek): lethargo grandi est oppressus,…

Lēthē.opening: , = Λήθη (forgetfulness), the river Lethe, in the infernal regions, from which the Shades drank and obtained forgetfulness of the past : pocula Lethes, Ov. P. 2, 4, 23 : da mihi hebetantem pectora Lethen, id. ib. 4, 1,…

lētĭfer.opening: ( ), , adj. letum , death-bringing, death-dealing, deadly, fatal ( poet. ): arcus, Verg. A. 10, 169 : ictus, Ov. M. 8, 362 : dextra, id. ib. 12, 606 : vestis, id. ib. 9, 166 : anguis, Stat. Th. 5, 628 : certamen, Cat.…

lēto.opening: ( ), , v. a. id. , to kill, slay : Lycurgiden letavit, Ov. Ib. 505 : Paris hunc letat, Verg. Cul. 323 : letata corpora, Ov. M. 3, 55 (the conjectural reading letatus, Cic. Leg. 3, 8, 19 , is very dub.; v. Orell. ad…

lētum.opening: (sometimes written , from a supposed connection with λήθη ), , acc. to Varr. L. L. 7, § 42 Müll., and Paul. ex Fest. p. 115 Müll., from λήθη; more prob. acc. to Prisc. p. 665 and 898 P., from leo, whence also deleo;…

Letus.opening: a mountain in Liguria , Liv. 41, 18 ; Val. Max. 1, 5 . †† ( ), , a Celtic word, whence the Fr. lieue , a Gallic mile of 1500 Roman paces, a league : Λεύκη μέτρον τι Γαλακτικόν , Hesych.: leuca finitur passibus mille…

Leuca.opening: a town in Calabria, near the Iapygian promontory , now S. Maria di Leuca : secretaque littora Leucae, Luc. 5, 376 .

leucăcantha.opening: , and , , , = λευκάκανθα . The white thorn , form leucacantha, Plin. 22, 16, 18, § 40 ; form leucacanthos, id. 21, 16, 56, § 94 .— A plant , called also phalangites and leucanthemon, Plin. 27, 12, 98, § 124 .

Leucădĭa.opening: , and , , , = Λευκαδία , an island (previously a peninsula) in the Ionic Sea, opposite Acarnania, with a famous temple of Apollo , now S. Maura , Mel. 2, 7, 10 ; Plin. 4, 1, 2, § 5 ; Liv. 33, 17, 8 ; acc. Leucada, Ov.…

Leucaethĭŏpes.opening: , = Λευκαιθίοπες , the white Ethiopians of Libya , Plin. 5, 8, 8, § 43 (Jahn, Leucoe Aethiopes); called also Leucoaethiopes, Mel. 1, 4, 4 .

leucanthĕmon.opening: or , , , = λευκάνθεμον , the name of three plants . The chamomile , called also anthemis, leucanthemis, etc., Plin. 22, 21, 26, § 53 .— A plant , called also phalangites and leucacantha, Plin. 27, 12, 98, § 124 .— A…

leucanthus.opening: , = λεύκανθος , a plant , otherwise unknown, App. Herb. 92 .

Leucas.opening: , = Λευκάς . For Leucadia, v. h. v.— The capital of the island Leucadia; v. Leucadia, B.— The promontory Leucata; v. Leucata.

leucaspis.opening: † , , adj. f. , = λεύκασπις , armed with a white shield : phalanx, Liv. 44, 41 .

Leucaspis.opening: one of the companions of Æneas , Verg. A. 6, 334 .

Leucāta.grammar: ae ēs is ae ădis f. n. m. f.
Leucāta.opening: , and , , ( , , , Serv. Verg. A. 3, 279 .— , , , Claud. B. G. 185 .— , , , Ov. H. 15, 172 ; Sen. Herc. Oet. 732 ), a promontory in the island of Leucadia , now Capo Ducato , Cic. Tusc. 4, 18, 41 ; Liv. 26, 26 ; 44, 1 :…

Leucē.opening: , = Λευκή . The name of several islands . Near Crete, over against Cydonia , now Fort Suda , Plin. 4, 12, 20, § 61 .— In the Euxine Sea, near the mouth of the Borysthenes , also called Achillea and Achillis insula, now…

leucēŏron.opening: , = λευκήορον , a plant , called also leontopodion, Plin. 26, 8, 34, § 52 ; App. Herb. 7 .

Leuci.opening: , = Λεῦκοι , a people of Gallia Belgica, adjacent to the Lingones, whence, perh., the mod. Liège , Caes. B. G. 1, 40, 10 ; Plin. 4, 17, 31, § 106 ; Tac. H. 1, 64 . —Collect., in sing. : , , , Luc. 1, 424 .

Leucippē.opening: , = Λευκίππη . The daughter of Thestor , Hyg. Fab. 190 .— The wife of Ilus, and mother of Laomedon , Hyg. Fab. 250 .— The wife of Thestius , Hyg. Fab. 14 .— A Roman surname : AVRELIA LEVCIPPE, Inscr. ap. Grut. 761, 7.

Leucippus.opening: , = Λεύκιππος . The father of Phœbe and Hilaira, who were carried off by Castor and Pollux , Ov. F. 5, 709 .—Hence, , , , a daughter of Leucippus , Prop. 1, 2, 15 : te rapuit Theseus, geminas Leucippidas illi, Ov. H.…

leucochrȳsos.opening: , = λευκόχρυσος . A precious stone, a species of chrysolite , Plin. 37, 9, 44, § 128 .— A white precious stone, clear as crystal , Plin. 37, 10, 62, § 172 .

leucŏcŏmos.opening: or , , adj. , = λευκόκομος (white-haired; hence), having white leaves or blossoms : (mala) erythrocomis et leucocomis, Plin. 13, 19, 34, § 113 .

leucŏgaea.opening: , = λευκόγαια (of white earth), a precious stone almost unknown , Plin. 37, 10, 59, § 162 .

leucŏgaeus.opening: adj. , = λευκόγαιος , of white earth : colles, a chain of hills in Campania, where chalk was dug, Plin. 18, 11, 29, § 114 ; 35, 15, 56, § 174 .—Here were the leucogaei fontes, Plin. 31, 2, 8, § 12 .

leucogrăphĭa.opening: , = λευκογραφία , a precious stone , called also leucogaea, Plin. 37, 10, 59, § 162 ; al. leucographitin.

leucogrăphis.opening: , = λευκογραφίς , a kind of St. Mary's thistle , Carduus leucographus, Linn., which was used as a remedy for spitting blood , Plin. 27, 11, 78, § 103 .

leucŏĭon.opening: (trisyl. leucoja, Col. poët. 10, 97), , , = λευκόϊον , the white violet , Col. 9, 4, 4 : candida leucoia, id. 10, 97 .

Leucōn.opening: The name of one of Actæon's hounds , Ov. M. 3, 218 .— A king of Pontus , Ov. Ib. 312 .

Leucŏnĭcus.opening: adj., of or belonging to the Leucŏnes (a people in Gaul), Leuconic : lanae, Mart. 11, 56, 9 dub.: sagae, id. 14, 159, 2 , also dub.— Subst. : , , , Leuconic wool , Mart. 11, 21, 8 .

leucŏnŏtus.opening: , = λευκόνοτος , the ( white , i. e. clear, dry ) south wind , more precisely, the south-southwest wind , Vitr. 1, 6, 10 ; Sen. Q. N. 5, 16, 6 : leuconotus Libs, Aus. Technopaegn. de Deis, 12.

Leucŏpĕtra.opening: , = Λευκοπέτρα (white rock), a promontory in the territory of the Bruttii, near Rhegium , now Capo dell' Armi , Cic. Phil. 1, 3, 7 ; id. Att. 16, 6, 1 ; 16, 7, 1 .

leucŏphaeātus.opening: adj. leucophaeus , clothed in dark gray or ash-colored garments , Mart. 1, 97, 5 .

leucŏphaeus.opening: adj. , = λευκόφαιος , ash - colored, dun - colored : pannus, Plin. 32, 10, 38, § 114 : vellera, Vitr. 8, 3 med.

Leucŏphrўna.opening: , = λευκοφρύνη (with white eyebrows), a surname of Diana in Magnesia , Tac. A. 3, 62 ; Arn. 6, 6 .

leucophthalmos.opening: , = λευκόφθαλμος (white eye), a precious stone , Plin. 37, 10, 62, § 171 .

leucōpis.opening: , = λευκῶπις , a plant , called also artemisia, App. Herb. 10 .

leucŏpoecĭlos.opening: , = λευκοποίκιλος (spotted with white), a precious stone , otherwise unknown, Plin. 37, 10, 62, § 171 .

Leucŏsĭa.opening: , = Λευκοσία , a small island off the coast of Lucania, near Pæstum , now Licosa : Leucosiamque petit, tepidique rosaria Paesti, Ov. M. 15, 708 ; called also Leucothĕa, Mel. 2, 7, 18 (Jahn reads Leucasia, Plin. 3, 7,…

Leucŏsўri.opening: , = Λευκόσυροι , the white Syrians on the shores of the Euxine, afterwards called Cappadocians , Plin. 6, 3, 3, § 9 ; Curt. 6, 4, 17 ; Nep. Dat. 1, 1 .

lĭcenter.opening: adv. , v. licet, P. a. fin .

lĭcentĭātus.opening: licentia , freedom, license : meo licentiatu, Laber. ap. Non. 212, 6 (Com. Fragm. v. 71 Rib.).

lĭcentĭōsus.opening: adj. licentia , full of freedom or license, over-free, unbridled, unrestrained, wanton, licentious (post-Aug.): (ebor dicere) non minus est licentiosum, quam si sulfuri et gutturi subicerent in genitivo litteram o…

Lĭcentĭus.opening: the name of a Christian poet , Paul. Nol. Epist. 47, 51 .

lĭcĕo.opening: v. n. Sanscr. root rik-, riktas, empty; Gr. λιπ-, λείπω, leave; Lat. lic-, linquo, licet, liceor; cf. Germ. leihen, verleihen , to be for sale; to have a price put upon it, to be valued, esteemed at so much. Lit. (rare…

lĭcĕor.opening: v. dep. n. and a. [root lic-; v. 1. liceo], to bid on goods at an auction (class.). Absol. : licetur Aebutius, Cic. Caecin. 6, 16 : liciti sunt usque adeo, quoad, etc., Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 33, § 77 : digito liceri…

Lĭcerĭānus.opening: adj., of or belonging to the city of Licerium (in Aquitania), Licerian : pira, Plin. 15, 15, 16, § 54 .

lĭcet.opening: (old form, licessit for licuerit, Plaut. As. 3, 3, 13 ; imp. liceto, Lex ap. Inscr. Grut. 202, 508 al. ), v. n. and impers. [root lic-; Gr. λιπ- ; v. 1. liceo], it is lawful, it is allowed or permitted; one may or can,…

lĭchănos.opening: , = λίχανος , a note on the tetrachord , Vitr. 5, 4, 5 .

līcĭātōrĭum.opening: , ii. licium , a weaver's beam (late Lat.): liciatorium texentium, Vulg. 1 Reg. 17, 7 al.

līcĭātus.opening: adj. licium; laid, leashed, like a web; hence, trop. , begun, commenced (late Lat.): ut ita dicam liciatum videtur, quod nondum est, Aug. Civ. Dei , 22, 14; id. Gen. ad Litt. 3, 14 .

līcĭnĭo.opening: v. a. licium , to show through, disclose , of a thin texture: membrorum voluptatem, App. M. 10, p. 254, 11 .

līcĭnĭum.opening: id. , lint for dressing wounds (late Lat.), Veg. Vet. 2, 22, 2 ; 2, 48, 6 .

Lĭcĭnĭus.opening: name of a Roman gens. The tribune C. Licinius Crassus, Varr. R. R. 1, 2, 9 ; Cic. Lael. 25, 96 .— The triumvir M. Licinius Crassus, Cic. Div. 2, 9, 22 ; Ov. F. 6, 465 .— L. Licinius Crassus, the famous orator , Cic. de…

lĭcĭnus.opening: adj., bent or turned upward : Licini boves (i. e. qui sursum versum reflexa cornua habent), Serv. and Philarg. on Verg. G. 3, 55 .

Lĭcĭnus.opening: a surname in the gens Fabia and Porcia.—Also, the name of a barber and freedman of Augustus, celebrated for his wealth , Hor. A. P. 301 ; Mart. 8, 3, 6 ; Varr. Atac. in Anth. Lat. T. 1, p. 205 . — Plur. : ego possideo…

lĭcĭtātĭo.opening: licitor , an offering of a price, a bidding for any thing, at sales and auctions: exquisitis palam pretiis et licitationibus factis, Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 53, § 133 ; id. Att. 11, 15, 4 : praedam ad licitationem dividere, to…

lĭcĭtātor.grammar: ōris, an old erroneous reading for illicitator

lĭcĭtē.opening: and , advv. , v. licet fin. B.

lĭcĭtor.opening: v. dep. liceor , to offer a price, to bid for any thing (ante- and postclass.). Lit. : ut ne licitare advorsum animi mei sententiam, Plaut. Merc. 2, 3, 104 .— Transf. , to contend, fight : licitati in mercando sive…

līcium.opening: the thrum or leash , the ends of a web to which those of the new piece are fastened. Lit. : licia telae Addere, i. e. to weave, Verg. G. 1, 285 : adnectit licia telis, Tib. 1, 6, 79 : plurimis liciis texere, quae…

lictor.opening: (pronounced līctor, Gell. 12, 3, 4 ), , 1. ligo; cf. Gell. 12, 3, 1 sqq. , a lictor , i. e. an attendant granted to a magistrate, as a sign of official dignity . The Romans adopted this custom from the Etrurians:…

lictōrĭus.opening: adj. lictor , of or belonging to a lictor (post-class.): virga lictoria, Flor. 1, 26, 3 : DECVRIA LICTORIA, Inscr. Orell. 2676 : fasces, Aur. Vict. Vir. Ill. 20, 1 .

Lĭcus.opening: a river in Vindelicia, a tributary of the Danube , now the Lech , Ven. Vit. S. Mart. 4, 641 .

lĭēn.opening: , and , , ( gen. plur. lienum, Plin. 23, 7, 63, § 121 ) [for plien; Sanscr. plīhan; Gr. σπλήν ], the milt or spleen . Lit. : lienes turgent, Cato. R. R. 157: seditionem facit lien (of a stitch in the side), Plaut. Merc.…

lĭēnĭcus.opening: adj. lien , = σπληνικός , splenetic.—Subst. , , , splenetic persons , Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 4, 56 ; 57 ; 64 .— , , , remedies for spleen , Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 4, 58 .

lĭēnōsus.opening: adj. id. , splenetic : cor lienosum, Plaut. Cas. 2, 6, 62 .— Plur. as subst. : tactu lienosis medebatur, Plin. 7, 2, 2, § 20 .

līentĕrĭcus.opening: adj. λειεντερία; cf. Cels. 2, 1 , troubled with looseness or diarrhœa, lienteric : dantur coeliacis ... sic et lientericis, Plin. 29, 3, 11, § 44 .

lĭgāmen.opening: 1. ligo , a band, tie, bandage ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): Sidoniae nocturna ligamina mitrae, Prop. 2, 22, 15 ; Ov. M. 14, 230 : ligamina vitium, Col. 11, 2, 92 : ligamina herbarum, id. 12, 8, 1 .—In sing. : papyri…

lĭgāmentum.opening: id. , a band, tie, bandage (post - Aug.): aurium ligamenta, Quint. 11, 3, 144 : vulneribus ligamenta parare, Tac. A. 15, 54 .

Lĭgārĭus.opening: name of a Roman gens. So, Q. Ligarius, whom Cicero defended in an oration still extant , Quint. 11, 1, 80 ; Auct. B. Afr. 64, 1; Cic. Lig. 1, 1 .—Hence, , , adj., of or belonging to Ligarius, Ligarian : oratio…

lĭgātĭo.opening: 1. ligo , a binding , Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 37, 195 ; Scrib. Comp. 255 .

lĭgātūra.opening: id. , a band, ligature (post-class.). Lit. : ligatura in vitibus, Pall. 1, 6, 11 .— In partic., an amulet (bound about one), Aug. in Joann. 7 ; cf. Isid. Orig. 8, 9 .— A bunch, cluster : duas ligaturas uvae passae,…

Lĭgauni.opening: a people of Gallia Narbonensis, Sil. 4, 206 .

Lĭgella.opening: the name of a woman , Mart. 10, 90 .

Lĭger.opening: a river forming the boundary between Gallia Lugdunensis and Aquitania, now the Loire : quod Liger ex nivibus creverat, Caes. B. G. 7, 55, 10 ; Tib. 1, 7, 12 : cum ad flumen Ligerim venissent, Caes. B. G. 7, 5, 4 :…

lignātĭo.opening: lignor , a felling or procuring of wood . Lit. : qui lignationis munitionisque causā in silvas discessissent, Caes. B. G. 5, 38 : quae maxime necessaria est ad cibum excoquendum, Vitr. 5, 9 fin. — Transf. , concr., a…

lignātor.opening: id. , a wood-cutter, one sent to get wood : oppressis lignatoribus, Caes. B. G. 5, 26 : legio tertia, quae pabulatores et lignatores tueretur, Liv. 41, 1, 7 .

lignĕŏlus.opening: adj. dim. [ligneus], wooden , of small objects: scuta, Lucil. ap. Prisc. 3 fin. : lychnuchus, Cic. Q. Fr. 3, 7 : figurae, App. de Mundo, p. 70, 19.

lignĕus.opening: adj. lignum , of wood, wooden . Lit. : ponticulus, Cic. Tusc. 5, 20, 59 : turres, Caes. B. C. 3, 9 : materia, wood, Cic. Inv. 2, 57, 170 : deus, Tib. 1, 11, 20 : piscinas, Plin. 34, 12, 32, § 123 : Fabii Maximi oppida,…

Lĭgurra.opening: the name of a woman , Mart. 12, 61 .

līlĭācĕus.opening: adj. lilium , of or from lilies : oleum, oil of lilies, Pall. 6, 14 in lemm .

līmĭcŏla.opening: limus-colo , a dweller in the mud : ostreae, Aus. Ep. 7, 36 .

limnĭcē.opening: , = λιμνική , the pond-lily, sword-lily , App. Herb. 78 .

limpĭdus.opening: adj. Gr. λάμπω; cf. lepor, O-lymp-us , clear, bright, pellucid, transparent, limpid (poet and in post-Aug. prose): lacus, Cat. 4, 24 : limpidior aqua fiet, Vitr. 8, 7 : vinum limpidissimum, Col. 12, 28, 3 : limpidae…

linctus.opening: lingo , a licking : nectaris, Lucr. 6, 971 (v. Lachm. ad h. l.), Plin. 31, 9, 45, § 104 ; 35, 15, 50, § 177 .

Lindus.opening: ( ), , , = Λίνδος , a town in the island of Rhodes, founded by Lindus, brother of Ialysus, with a temple of Minerva , now Lindo , Mel. 2, 7, 4 ; Plin. 5, 31, 36, § 132 ; Cic. N. D. 3, 21, 54 .—Hence, , , adj., of or…

līnĕa.opening: ( ), , linum , a linen thread, a string, line . Lit. : nectere lineas, restes, funes, Varr. R. R. 1, 23, 6 : linia longinqua per os religata, Plin. 9, 17, 26, § 59 : ligato pede longā lineā gallina custoditur, Col. 8,…

līnĕālis.opening: adj. linea , consisting of lines, made with lines, lineal (post-class.): ambitus lineales, Amm. 22, 16, 7 .—Hence, adv. : , in the manner of lines, by means of lines : quos (circulos) linealiter feci, Mart. Cap. 8, §…

līnĕāmentum.opening: ( ), , linea , a line or stroke made with a pen, with chalk, etc., a mark, line . Lit. : in geometria lineamenta formae, etc., lines, Cic. de Or. 1, 41, 187 : lineamentum, longitudinem latitudine carentem, id. Ac. 2,…

līnĕāris.opening: (or ), adj. id. , of or belonging to lines, consisting of lines, linear : pictura, the art of drawing with lines, without colors, Plin. 35, 3, 5, § 16 : ratio, the science of lines, geometry, Quint. 1, 10, 36 :…

līnĕārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to lines, line- : limes, a narrow pathway between fields, Hyg. de Limit. p. 152 Goes.

līnĕātĭo.opening: id. , the drawing of a line, a line : solis radii paribus lateribus lineationibus extenduntur, Vitr. 9, 4 .— A feature, lineament : corporis, Firm. Math. 1, 4.

līnĕo.opening: v. a. id. , to reduce to a straight line, to make straight or perpendicular . Lit. : dolabit, lineabit, secabitque materiam, Cato, R. R. 14, 3 : bene lineata carina, Plaut. Mil. 3, 3, 40 : radios, Vitr. 9, 4, 13 .—…

līnĕŏla.opening: dim. id. , a little line , Gell. 10, 1, 9 .

līnĕus.opening: adj. linum , of flax or lint, flaxen, linen- : vincula, Verg. A. 5, 510 : terga, the linen lining of a shield, id. ib. 10, 784 : vestes, Plin. 12, 6, 13, § 25 : lanugo, id. 32, 10, 44, § 126 : pannis lineis involvere,…

lingo.opening: ( Prisc. 881 ), , v. a. Sanscr. lih, rih, to lick; Gr. λιχ-, λείχω, λιχανός; cf. ligurio , to lick, lick up : mel mihi videor lingere, Plaut. Cas. 2, 8, 21 : crepidas carbatinas, Cat. 98, 5 : sulphur linctum, Plin. 35,…

Lingŏnes.opening: a people in Celtic Gaul , whence the modern name of their chief city, Langres , Caes. B. G. 1, 26 ; Plin. 4, 17, 31, § 106.—Afterwards dwelling on the Po, Liv. 5, 35, 2 .—Hence, , , adj., Lingonian : bardocucullus, a…

lingua.opening: (ante-class. form dingua, like dagrima for lacrima, Mar. Victorin. p. 2457 and 2470 P.; cf. the letter D), , Sanscr. jihvā; original Lat. form. dingua; A. -S. tunga; Germ. Zunge; Engl. tongue. Not from the root lih,…

linguārĭum.opening: lingua , tonguemoney; a comic expression to denote a penalty for rash sayings: linguarium dare, Sen. Ben. 4, 36, 1 .

linguātŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [linguatus], somewhat gifted with a tongue, sub-eloquent , Tert. ad Nat. 1, 8 .

linguātus.opening: adj. lingua , gifted with a tongue, eloquent (post-class.): civitas, Tert. Anim. 3 ; Vulg. Eccl. 8, 4 ; 25, 27 .

lingŭlāca.opening: lingula . Comm., a gossip, chatterbox : ea (uxor) lingulaca est nobis: numquam tacet, Plaut. Cas. 2, 8, 62 : lingulacae obtrectatores, Varr. ap. Non. 26, 18 ; Gell. 1, 15 .— Fem. A kind of fish, a sole , Varr. L. L. 5,…

lingŭlātus.opening: adj. id. , tongueshaped, lingulate : tubi, Vitr. 8, 7 : calcei, Isid. Orig. 19, 34, 13 .

lingŭlus.opening: adj. id. , talkative, quarrelsome , Poët. ap. Wernsdorf. Poet. Lat. Min. 2, p. 237.

linguōsĭtas.opening: lingua , loquacity , (late Lat.), Rust. c. Aceph. init.

linguōsus.opening: adj. id. , talkative, loquacious . Lit. : durae buccae fuit, linguosus, Petr. 43, 3 ; 63, 2 : adulescentula, Hier. Ep. 108 , n. 20.— Transf. , expressive : orchestarum linguosi digiti, Cassiod. Var. 4, 51 .

līnĭfer.opening: linum-fero . Flaxbearing : arbores, Plin. 13, 14, 28, § 90 .— A surname of Silvanus, Inscr. ap. Murat. 70. 6.

līnĭger.opening: adj. linum gero , linen-wearing, clothed in linen; of Isis and her priests: turba, Ov. M. 1, 747 : neu fuge linigerae Memphitica templa juvencae, id. A. A. 1, 77 : grege linigero circumdatus, Juv. 6, 532 .

lĭnīmen.opening: lino , grease : pro linimine adhibere, Theod. Prisc. 1, 18 .

lĭnīmentum.opening: id. , smearing-stuff, liniment : dolii, Pall. 11, 14 fin. : limpidum, Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 1, 34 .

lĭnītus.opening: linio , a smearing, anointing : potu et linitu, Plin. 20, 12, 47, § 118 .

lĭno.opening: (līvi), lĭtum, 3, and , , ītum. 4 (contr. form of the inf. perf. lisse for livisse. Spart. Hadr. 4 : perf. livi, Cato, R. R. 69; Col. 12, 50, 17 : levi, Hor. C. 1, 20, 3 : lini for livi, acc. to Prisc. p. 898 P.), v. a.…

lĭnostema.opening: , est vestis ex lana linoque contexta: et dicta linostema, quia in stamine linum in trama lanam habet, Isid. Orig. 19, 22 .

lĭnostrŏphon.opening: , = λινόστροφον , a plant, called also marrubium, Plin. 20, 22, 89, § 241 .

lĭnozōstis.opening: , = λινόζωστις , a plant, called also mercurialis, Plin. 25, 5, 18, § 38 ; 26, 12, 76, § 124 ; 26, 14, 89, § 150 .

linquo.opening: ( part. lictus, Capitol. M. Aurel. 7 dub.), v. a. Gr. λιπ- in λείπω, λοιπός; cf. Lat. licet . To leave, quit, forsake, depart from something (cf.: destituo, desero): urbem exsul linquat, Plaut. Most. 3, 1, 69 : terram,…

lintĕāmen.opening: linteum , a linen cloth : lotum, Lampr. Heliog. 26 : candidum, App. M. 11, p. 261, 35 : mollia, Hier. Ep. 108, 15 ; Vulg. Luc. 24, 12 al.

lintĕārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or pertaining to linen, linen- . Negotiatio, Dig. 14, 4, 5, § 15 .— Subst. : , , , a linen-weaver : linteariorum corpus, Cod. Th. 10, 20, 16; so Dig. 14, 4, 5, § 4 ; Inscr. Orell. 8 ; 4215 .

lintĕātus.opening: adj. id. , clothed in linen : senex, Sen. de Vit. Beat. 26, 8 ; cf.: legio, a legion of Samnites, containing picked men, Liv. 10, 38, 12 (v. the context): cohortes, id. 10, 41, 10 : pallio deae Isidis linteata, Tert.…

lintĕo.opening: id. , a linen-weaver , Plaut. Aul. 3, 5, 38 ; Serv. ad Verg. A. 7, 14 : linteones Apollinis, Inscr. Grut. 38, 15 .

lintĕŏlum.opening: dim. linteum , a small linen cloth , Plaut. Ep. 2, 2, 46 : rosae folia tusa in linteolo, Plin. 14, 16, 19, § 106 ; 31, 9, 45, § 100 ; Vulg. Ezech. 30, 21 .— Transf. , a lamp-wick : ebrium, Prud. Cath. 5, 18 .

lintĕŏlus.opening: adj. dim. [linteus], linen- : palliolum, Prud. στεφ . 3, 180.

linter.opening: ( nom. lintris, Sid. Carm. 5, 283 ), ( , Tib. 2, 5, 34 ) [old form lunter for plun-ter; root πλύνω , to wash; cf. pluvia; hence] Lit. , a wash-tub; or in gen., a trough, vat, tray, tub , for wine, Cato, R. R. 11, 5 ;…

lintĕum.opening: linum , a linen cloth . Lit. : linteum cape atque exterge tibi manus, Plaut. Most. 1, 3, 110 : uncto linteo, id. Bacch. 3, 3, 42 : linteum extersui, id. Curc. 4, 4, 22 : merces linteis et vitro delatae, Cic. Rab. Post.…

lintĕus.opening: adj. id. , linen- : lintea vestis, Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 56, § 146 ; Plin. 19, 1, 2, § 8 : tunica, Liv. 9, 40 : Lintei libri, an ancient chronicle of the Roman people, which was written on linen, and preserved in the temple…

lintrārĭus.opening: linter , a boatman, waterman , Dig. 4, 9, 1, § 4 ; Inscr. Orell. 4245 .

lintrĭcŭlus.opening: dim. id. , a small boat or wherry , Cic. Att. 10, 10, 5 .

līnum.opening: Gr. λίνον; Goth. lein; Germ. Leinwand; Engl. linen , flax. Lit. : reticulum, tenuissimo lino, Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 11, § 27 : urit lini campum seges, Verg. G. 1, 77 ; cf. Plin. 19 prooem. § 2; 19, 1, 1, § 9: lino legato tam…

Lĭnus.opening: ( ), , , = Λίνος , Linus . A son of Apollo and Psammate, daughter of Crotopus, king of the Argives; he was given by his mother to the care of shepherds, and one day, being left alone, was torn to pieces by dogs;…

līnўphus.opening: ( ), , ( ), , and ( ), , , = λινόϋφος, λινοϋφής ( λίνυφος , Gloss.), a linen-weaver (post-class.): Scythopolitani linyphi, Cod. Th. 10, 20, 8: alii linyphiones sunt, Hadr. in Ep. ap. Vop. Sat. 8 : corpus linyphiariorum,…

līo.opening: v. a. , = λειόω, λειῶ , to make smooth, plaster over : cisternam liare, Tert. Idol. 5 ; Apic. 5, 1, § 186 .

līŏthăsĭus.opening: ( ), , adj. , = λεῖοσ-Θάσιος , a kind of turnip , which perh. came from Thasus, and was more delicate than the others, Plin. 19, 3, 25, § 75 .

Lĭpăra.opening: , and , , = Λιπάρη , one of the Æolian isles, to the north of Sicily, with a city of the same name , now Lipari .—Form Lipara, Mel. 2, 7, 18 ; Plin. 3, 9, 14, § 93 .—Form Lipare, Verg. A. 8, 417 ; Val. Fl. 2, 96 .—…

lĭpărĕa.opening: a precious stone , otherwise unknown, Plin. 37, 10, 62, § 172 ; Isid. 16, 15, 22 .

Lĭpăris.opening: , = Λιπαρίς , a Cilician river near the town of Soli, the water of which is of an oleaginous quality , Vitr. 8, 3, 8 .

lĭpăris.opening: , a false reading for lelepris, Plin. 32, 11, 53, § 149 .

lĭpĭo.opening: v. n. , to croak , of the kite: milvus lipit, Auct. Carm. Philom. 24.

lippesco.opening: v. n. , to become blear-eyed (eccl. Lat.), Hier. in Sophon. 3, 49 .

lippĭdus.opening: γλαμώδης (i. q. lippus), Gloss. Gr. Lat.

lippĭo.opening: v. n. lippus , to haw watery or inflamed eyes, to be blear-eyed . Lit. : cum leviter lippirem, has litteras dedi, * Cic. Att. 7, 14, 1 : ne omnino lippiatur, Plin. 28, 8, 27, § 94 : calor adjuvat lippientes, Cels. 1, 9…

lippĭtūdo.opening: id. , blearedness, rheum or inflammation of the eyes : ab lippitudine usque siccitas ut sit tibi, Plaut. Rud. 3, 2, 18 ; id. Poen. 1, 2, 182 : diuturna, Cic. Tusc. 4, 37, 8 : molestior, id. Att. 8, 12, 1 : sicca, Plin.…

lippus.opening: adj. Sanscr. lip, to smear; Gr. λίπα, λίπος, fat; ἄλειφα, salve; whence adeps , blear-eyed, bleared, inflamed . Lit. : num tibi lippus videor, Plaut. Mil. 2, 3, 21 : (matrem) cubare in navi lippam atque oculis turgidis,…

lĭquābĭlis.opening: adj. liquo , that may be melted or dissolved (post-class.): cera, App. Mag. 293, 3 : saxum, i. e. the pillar of salt into which Lot's wife was turned, Prud. Ham. 744 .

lĭquāmen.opening: id. , a liquid mixture : eo liquamine tonsa ovis imbuitur, Col. 7, 4, 7 .— In partic. A sauce made of fish-fat, fish-sauce (cf. garum), Col. 6, 2, 7 ; Pall. 3, 25, 12 .— = lixivium, lye , Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 13, 167 .

lĭquāmentum.opening: id. , a mixture, concoction , Veg. Vet. 3, 66, 5 .

lĭquāmĭnārĭus.opening: γαροπώλης ( one who prepares or sells fish-sauce ), Gloss. Philox.

lĭquāmĭnātus.opening: adj. liquamen , furnished with gravy, having gravy : porcellus, Apic. 8, 7 .

lĭquāmĭnōsus.opening: adj. id. , full of gravy : res, Marc. Emp. 5 , fin.

lĭquārĭus.opening: adj. liquo , of or pertaining to liquids : mensurae, measures for liquids, liquid measures, Inscr. Orell. 4344 .

lĭquātōrĭum.opening: id. , a filter, strain er , Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 39, 229 .

lĭquĕfăcĭo.opening: v. a. , and pass . ( e long, Sil. 1, 178 ), factus, fĭĕri [liqueo-facio], to make liquid, to melt, dissolve, liquefy (class.; but in act. very rare). Lit. : glacies liquefacta, Cic. N. D. 2, 10, 26 : legum aera…

lĭquĕfactĭo.opening: , = liquatio (late Lat.), Inc. Auct. de Tripl. Habit. 2.

Lĭquentĭa.opening: a river in Venetia , now the Livenza , Plin. 3, 18, 22, § 126 ; Serv. Verg. A. 9, 679 ; Cod. Th. 11, 10, 2.

lĭquĕo.opening: v. n. Sanscr. rik-, riktas, empty; Zend, ric-, to pour out; Gr. λιπ- in λείπω; cf. linquo , to be fluid or liquid . Lit. (only in the part. pres. ): lac est omnium rerum liquentium maxime alibile, Varr. R. R. 2, 11, 1 :…

lĭquesco.opening: v. inch. n. [liqueo], to become fluid or liquid, to melt . Lit. : tabes nivis liquescentis, Liv. 21, 36 : haec ut cera liquescit, Verg. E. 8, 80 ; Ov. M. 5, 431 : volnificusque chalybs vastā fornace liquescit, Verg. A.…

lĭquĭdĭtas.opening: liquidus , liquidity : aëris, App. de Mundo, p. 57, 13.

lĭquĭdĭuscŭlus.opening: adj. comp. dim. [id.], somewhat more fluid or soft : liquidiusculusque ero, quam ventus est Favonius, Plaut. Mil. 3, 1, 71 ; v. Brix ad loc.

lī^quĭdus.opening: (the first syll. usually short; long in Lucr. 1, 349 ; 3, 427 ; while in the line id. 4, 1259 it is used both as long and short; v. infra ), adj. liqueo , flowing, fluid, liquid . Lit. : aqua bona et liquida, Cato, R.…

lĭquĭrītĭa.opening: corrupted fr. γλυκυρρίζα = glycyrrhiza, q. v. , liquorice , Theod. de Diaet. 9; Veg. Vet. 4, 9 .

līquis.opening: adj. the simple word, whence obliquus , oblique , Front. Expos. Form. p. 32 Goes.

lĭquo.opening: v. a. , to make liquid, to melt, dissolve, liquefy . Lit. : pila, Luc. 7, 159 : vitrum, Plin. 36, 26, 66, § 194 : lapis liquatur igni, id. 36, 8, 13, § 62 : liquatum aes, id. 34, 13, 36, § 134 : liquatae guttae, Cic.…

līquor.opening: ( inf. liquier, Att. Trag. Brut. 28 ), v. dep. n. [liqueo], to be fluid or liquid, to flow, melt, dissolve ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : tum toto corpore sudor Liquitur, Verg. A. 9, 813 : huic (arbori) atro…

lĭquor.opening: (lī, Lucr. 1, 454 ), liqueo , fluidness, fluidity, liquidity . Lit. : liquor aquai, Lucr. 1, 454 ; Cic. N. D. 2, 10 : causae, quae vim habent frigoris et caloris, concretionis et liquoris, id. Univ. 14 : vomica liquoris…

līra.opening: perh. fr. lisa; O. H. Germ. Leisa; Germ. Geleise, a track or rut; cf. delirus , the earth thrown up between two furrows, a ridge : liras rustici vocant easdem porcas, cum sic aratum est, ut inter duos latius distantes…

līrātim.opening: adv. lira , by furrows : liratim serere, Col. 11, 3, 20 .

Līrīnus.opening: ( , ae), , = Ληρίνη , an island on the coast of Gallia Narbonensis, opposite to Antipolis (the modern Antibes), now St. Honorat (one of the islands De Lérins ), Plin. 3, 5, 11, § 79 ; Sid. Carm. 16, 104 . —Hence, ,…

Līrĭŏpē.opening: a fountain-nymph, the mother of Narcissus by Cephisus , Ov. M. 3, 342 .

Līris.opening: a river between Latium and Campania , now Garigliano , Hor. C. 1, 31, 7 ; Mel. 2, 4, 9 ; Plin. 2, 103, 106, § 227, 3, 5, 9, § 56 ; Cic. Leg. 2, 3, 6 ; Luc. 2, 424 .— Acc. : Lirem, Cic. Leg. 2, 3, 6 : Lirim, Liv. 26, 9 :…

līro.opening: v. a. lira , to plough or harrow in the seed. Lit. : terram cum primum arant, proscindere appellant: cum iterum, offringere dicunt: tertio cum arant jacto semine, lirare dicuntur, Varr. R. R. 1, 29, 2 ; cf.: haec…

līroe.opening: ( ) = λῆροι , trifles, bagatelles : gerrae germanae, atque edepol liroe liroe, Plaut. Poen. 1, 1, 9 .

līs.opening: (old form stlis, stlitis, like stlocus for locus; cf. Quint. 1, 4, 16 ), root star-, in sterno; cf. Germ. streiten, to contend , a strife, dispute, quarrel . In gen.: si quis pugnam expectat, litis contrahat, Plaut.…

Lissus.opening: , and , , , = Λισσός , a city in southern Dalmatia, on the borders of Macedonia , now Alessio , Caes. B. C. 3, 26, 4 ; Plin. 3, 22, 26, § 144 ; Liv. 43, 20 ; 44, 30 .

lĭtābĭlis.opening: adj. lito , fit for sacrifice, with which a successful offering can be made (post-class.): victima, Lact. 1, 21, 25 : hostia, Min. Fel. 32, 2 : litabilior victima, Lact. Epit. 7 .

lĭtāmen.opening: id. , a sacrifice : extrema litamina divum, Stat. Th. 10, 610 : cujus litamen sordet, Prud. Hamart. praef. 50.

Lĭtāna silva.opening: , or absol. , , , , a forest in Gallia Cisalpina, which extended through Liguria and Etruria , now Selva de Luogo , Liv. 23, 24, 7 ; 34, 22, 4 ; 34, 42, 2 ; Front. Strat. 1, 6 .—Form Litana, Cic. Tusc. 1, 37, 89 .

lĭtănīa.opening: , = λιτανεία , a public form of prayer to God, a litany : litanias facere, Sid. Ep. 5, 7 ; Cod. 1, 5, 6.

lĭtātĭo.opening: lito , a fortunate or successful sacrifice , Plaut. Ps. 1, 3, 100 : per dies aliquot hostiae majores sine litatione caesae, diuque non impetrata pax deorum, Liv. 27, 23, 4 : sacrificare, id. 41, 15, 4 ; Inscr. Fratr.…

lĭtātō.opening: abl. absol. , v lito, I. A.

Līternum.opening: ( ), , , a city of Campania, situated to the north of the mouth of the river Liternus , now the village of Patria , Mel. 2, 4, 9 ; Plin. 3, 5, 9, § 61 ; Liv. 22, 16 ; Ov. M. 15, 714 ; Sil. 6, 654 ; 8, 533 .— Hence, , ,…

lĭthānĭcus.opening: λιθιάω , one suffering from the stone , Plin. 20, 22, 87, § 239 .

lĭthargўrus.opening: ( ), , , = λιθάργυρος , the spume of silver, litharge, the semivitreous protoxide of lead (pure Lat.: spuma argenti), Plin. 26, 10, 64, § 101 .

lĭthīzon.opening: , = λιθίζων (stonelike): lithizontes, a reading for lignyizontes, in Plin. 37, 7, 25, § 95 .

lĭthospermon.opening: , = λιθόσπερμον , a plant, stone-crop, gromwell , Plin. 27, 11, 74, § 98 .

lĭthostrōtus.opening: adj. , = λιθόστρωτος , inlaid with stones, mosaic : pavimentum, Varr. R. R. 3, 1, 10 .—Hence, Subst. : , , , mosaicwork , Varr. R. R. 3, 2, 4 ; Plin. 36, 25, 60, § 184 ; Capitol. Gord. 32, 6 .

lĭthŏtŏmĭa.opening: , = λιθοτομία , lithotomy, the cutting out of a stone from the bladder , cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 4, 77.

lĭtĭcen.opening: lituus-cano , a clarionblower, trumpeter : tubicines a tuba et canendo, similiter liticines, Varr. L. L. 5, § 91 Müll.: liticines et tubicines, Cato ap. Gell. 20, 2 : notus Hectoris armis, i. e. Misenus, Stat. S. 4, 7,…

lītĭgans.opening: Part. and subst. , v. litigo fin.

lītĭgātĭo.opening: litigo , a dispute, quarrel (post-class. for lis, jurgium, certatio): omissis litigationibus (al. litigatoribus), Lact. 3, 8 init. dub. (al. litigatoribus): litigatio μάχη ἡ διὰ λόγων , Gloss. Philox.

lītĭgātor.opening: id. , one engaged in a dispute, a disputant . In gen., Plin. praef. § 32: litigatores furiosi, Lact. 3, 8 init. (al. litigationes, v. litigatio).— In partic., a party in a lawsuit, a litigant : litigator rusticus…

lītĭgātus.opening: id. , a lawsuit, process : in hoc litigatu, Quint. Decl. 6, 19 .

lītĭger.opening: adj. lis-gero , belonging to legal process : fasces (consulum), Anthol. Lat. 6, 86 (295), 19.

lītĭgĭōsus.opening: adj. litigium , full of disputes, quarrelsome . Lit. : fora, Ov. F. 4, 188 : disputatio, Cic. Fin. 5, 26, 76 .— Fond of disputes, contentious, litigious : homo minime litigiosus, Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 14, § 37 : duae anus,…

lītĭgĭum.opening: litigo , a dispute, quarrel, strife (ante-class.): nam ego aliquid contrahere cupio litigii inter eos duos, Plaut. Cas. 3, 2, 31 : cum viro litigium natum, id. Men. 5, 2, 15 : litigium tibist cum uxore, id. ib. 1, 2, 42…

lītĭgo.opening: v. n. litem ago , to dispute, quarrel, strive . In gen.: qua de re litigatis inter vos? Plaut. Rud. 4, 4, 16 : Hirtium cum Quinctio acerrime litigasse, Cic. Att. 13, 37, 2 ; Juv. 6, 35 .—Prov.: litigare cum ventis, to…

lĭto.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
lĭto.opening: v. n. and a. , to make an offering which exhibits favorable prognostics, to sacrifice under favorable auspices, to obtain favorable omens . Lit. Neutr. : si istuc umquam factum est, tum me Juppiter Faciat, ut semper…

lītŏrālis.opening: adj. 3. litus , of or belonging to the sea-shore : dii litorales, that guard the shore, gods of the sea-shore, Cat. 4, 22 : pisces, Plin. 9, 17, 30, § 65 : Indi, Just. 12, 10, 6 .

lītŏrārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to the shore : harena, Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 11, § 134 : moratio, on the shore, id. ib. 3, 5, 74 .

lītŏrĕus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to the sea-shore, shore-, beach- : harena, Ov. M. 15, 725 : cancer, id. ib. 10, 127 : aves, Verg. A. 12, 248 : Cupra, a town of the Piceni, lying on the sea-shore, Sil. 8, 434 .

lītŏrōsus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to the shore, on the shore : callais litoroso mari similis, Plin. 37, 10, 56, § 151 . — Sup. : ager litorosissimus, next the shore , Fab. Maxim. ap. Serv. Verg. A. 1, 3 .

littĕra.opening: (less correctly ), , lino, q. v. , a letter, a written sign or mark signifying a sound . Lit. : cubitum hercle longis litteris signabo jam usquequaque, si quis, etc., Plaut. Rud. 5, 2, 7 : quid hae locuntur litterae?…

littĕrālis.opening: ( ), , adj. littera , of or belonging to letters or writing (postclass.): commercium, epistolary correspondence, Symm. Ep. 4, 52 : lectio, the reading of books, Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 5 : grammatica litteralis dicta, quod…

littĕrātus.opening: ( ), , adj. littera , lettered , i. e. Lit. , marked with letters, branded : ensiculus, Plaut. Rud. 4, 4, 112 : securicula, id. ib. 115 : urna, id. ib. 2, 5, 21 : laminae, App. M. 3, p. 137, 7 : laciniae auro…

littĕrĭo.opening: ( ), , litterae , a language-master , in a contemptuous sense: appellare (aliquem) loquacem talpam, et purpuratam simiam, et litterionem Graecum, Amm. 17, 11, 1 ; so, Graecus, Aug. adv. Leg. et Proph. 1, § 52.

littĕrōsus.opening: ( ), , adj. id. , literary, learned in letters : homo mere litterosus, Cass. Hem. ap. Non. 133, 6 .

littĕrŭla.opening: ( ), , dim. littera . A little letter , Cic. Att. 6, 9, 1 : accepi tuam epistolam vacillantibus litterulis, id. Fam. 16, 15, 2 .— Transf. : litterulae, ārum. A short letter, a note : hoc litterularum exaravi, Cic. Att.…

līturgus.opening: , = λειτουργός , one who fills a public office, a servant of the state , Cod. Th. 11, 24, 6.— In gen., an attendant , Mart. Cap. 2, 45 .

lĭtūro.opening: v. a. litura , to rub or blot out, erase : liturasse aliqua, Sid. Ep. 9, 3 ; Inscr. Orell. 4405 .

lĭtus.opening: lino , a smearing, besmearing, anointing : litu, Plin. 33, 6, 35, § 110 ( Cels. 6, 6, 20 , instead of litum we should read lenitum; v. Targa, ad loc.).

lītus.opening: (not ), , cf. λίμνη, λειμών, λιμήν; and lino , the sea-shore, seaside, beach, strand (opp. ripa, the bank of a river: ora, the coast of the sea; cf. Ov. M. 1, 37 sqq.; Verg. A. 3, 75 ): litus est, quousque maximus…

lĭtŭus.opening: ( gen. plur. lituum, Luc. 1, 237 ; Val. Fl. 6, 166 ; Sil. 13, 146 ), prob. Etruscan; prim. signif. crooked . Lit. The crooked staff borne by the augurs, an augur's crook or crosier, augural wand : dextra manu baculum…

līvēdo.opening: liveo , blueness, lividness , produced by bruises, blows, etc.: homunculi vibicibus livedinis totam cutem depicti, App. M. 9, p. 222, 26 .

līvens.opening: Part. and P. a. , from liveo.

līventer.opening: adv. , v. , P. a. , A. fin.

līvĕo.opening: v. n. for pliveo; Gr. πελιός, πελλός, dark-blue; cf.: pullus, pallidus , to be of a bluish color, black and blue, livid : livent rubigine dentes, Ov. M. 2, 776 : livere catenis, Prop. 4 (5), 7, 65. — Trop. , to be…

līvesco.opening: v. n. , to turn black and blue, become livid : digiti, Lucr. 3, 528 ; Scrib. Comp. 181 .—* Trop. , to envy, be envious : nec enim livescere fas est, Claud. Rapt. Pros. 3, 27 .

līvĭdinans.opening: adj. lividus , envious : ipse Paris dearum lividinantium judex, Petr. 138 dub. (al. libidinantium; al. litigantium).

līvĭdo.opening: v. a. id. , to render livid : pallore vultum, Paul. Nol. Carm. 21, 619 .

līvĭdŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [id.], somewhat envious : quibus invideas si lividulus sis, Juv. 11, 110 .

līvĭdus.opening: adj. liveo , of a blue or leaden color, bluish, blue . Lit. : vada, Verg. A. 6, 320 : lividissima vorago, Cat. 17, 11 : racemi, Hor. C. 2, 5, 10 .— Esp., produced by beating, bruising, etc., black and blue, livid :…

Līvilla.opening: dim. Livia , the daughter of Germanicus and Agrippina, and sister of Caligula , Suet. Calig. 7 .

līvor.opening: liveo , bluish color, leaden color, a black and blue spot . Lit. : jam livorem tute scapulis istoc concinnas tuis, Plaut. Truc. 4, 3, 19 : livore decoloratum corpus mortui, Auct. Her. 2, 5, 8 : ostendere nigram in facie…

lix.opening: ashes, lye : lix est cinis vel umor cineri admixtus: nam etiamnum id genus lixivium vocatur, Non. 62, 11 .

lixa.opening: perh. linquo , a sutler : non lixa sequebatur, Liv. 39, 1 : lixae modo sine insignibus, sine lictoribus, profectum, id. 21, 63 : lixarum in modum negotiari, id. 5, 8 : lixae ac negotiatores, Tac. A. 2, 62 .— Transf. In…

lixābundus.opening: lixa , journeying at pleasure : iter libere ac prolixe faciens, Paul. ex Fest. p. 116 Müll.; cf.: lixabundus ambulat, qui voluptatis causā ambulat, Gloss. Isid.: Pinacium tam lixabundum currere, Plaut. Stich. 2, 1, 15…

lixio.opening: id. , a sutler, camp-follower : lixiones aquarum portitores, Gloss. Isid.

lixīvĭus.opening: adj. lix , made into lye : cinere lixivio abluere, lye-ashes, Plin. 28, 18, 75, § 244 .— Subst. : , , , lye : lixivia cineris, Col. 12, 16 ; 12, 50 . —Also, , , , lye : ossa prunorum lixivio sunt maceranda, Pall. 12, 7,…

lixīvus.opening: adj. id. , made into lye : cinis lixiva, Scrib. Larg. 216 ; 230 ; Varr. ap. Plin. 36, 27, 69, § 202 ; 15, 17, 18, § 67 : mustum lixivum, the must which flows from the grapes before they are pressed, Cato, R. R. 23 .—…

lixo.opening: ἕψω , to boil, seethe , Gloss. Philox.

lŏba.opening: The haulm or straw of Indian millet , Plin. 11, 7, 10, § 55 .— Nightshade, also called strychnos, App. Herb. 74 .

lŏcālis.opening: adj. locus , of or belonging to a place, local (late Lat.): determinatio, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 34 : locale universali opponit, id. ad Scapul. 3 : aerumnae, Amm. 14, 7, 5 : adverbia, adverbs of place, Charis. p. 182…

lŏcālĭtas.opening: id. , locality , as a necessary quality of bodies, Claud. Mam. Stat. Anim. 3, 3 ; 4 .

lŏcātōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to letting or hiring out : locatorius, μισθωσιμαῖος , Gloss. Philox.: locatoria provincia, where one will be a mere letter out, Cic. Att. 15, 9, 1 ; Orell. N. cr .

Lochīa.opening: , = λοχεία (midwife), a surname of Diana , Inscr. ap. Grut. 1011, 3.

lŏcĭto.opening: v. freq. a. loco , to let or hire out : agelli hic est sub urbe paulum, quod locitas foras, Ter. Ad. 5, 8, 26 .

lŏcūtĭo.opening: ( ), , loquor , a speaking . Lit. In gen., a speaking, speech, discourse : sermo est oratio remissa et finitima quotidianae locutioni, Auct. Her. 3, 13, 23 : ex locutione, ex reticentia, Cic. Off. 1, 41, 146 : quamquam…

lŏgŏdaedălĭa.opening: , = λογοδαιδαλία , an excessive nicety in one's words, affectation in selecting expressions , Aus. Idyll. 12, 1 .

lŏgŏgrăphus.opening: , = λογογράφος , an accountant , Dig. 15, 4, 18 ; Cod. Just. 10, 69 .

lŏgos.opening: ( ), , , = λόγος , a word . In gen.: non longos logos, Plaut. Men. 5, 2, 29 ; Petr. 126 .— In partic. Mere words, empty talk : dabuntur dotis tibi sescenti logei atque Attici omnes, Plaut. Pers. 3, 1, 66 ; Ter. Phorm.…

lŏlĭācĕus.opening: adj. lolium , of darnel, darnel- : farina, Varr. R. R. 3, 9, 20 .

lonchōton.opening: , = λογχωτός , a kind of copperas , Plin. 34, 12, 32, § 124 .

lonchus.opening: ( ), , , = λόγχος , a lance , Tert. Cor. Mil. 11 .

longănon.opening: (also and , or , , , ), the straight gut , Veg. Vet. 1, 42, 1 ; 1, 49 ; 1, 56, 17 ; Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 22, 220 ; id. Tard. 2, 1, 11 .— Transf. , a sausage , Varr. L. L. 5, § 11 Müll.; Arn. 7, 229 .

Longānus.opening: adj., inhabitant of Longula , Plin. 3, 5, 9, § 69 (al. Longulani).

longĭlŏquĭum.opening: longus-loqui , a long speech , Don. ad Ter. Eun. 2, 2, 34 ; Isid. 1, 33, 8 .

longĭtĭa.opening: ( ), , longus , length (late Lat.), Auct. de Limit. p. 271; Goes. Veg. Vet. 6, 2, 2 (Schneid. longitudo).

longĭtūdo.opening: longus , length . Lit. : in hac immensitate latitudinum, longitudinum, altitudinum, Cic. N. D. 1, 20, 54 : itineris, id. Phil. 9, 1, 2 : pontis, Caes. B. G. 6, 29 : longitudines et brevitates in sonis, Cic. Or. 51, 173…
