Longuntĭca.opening: a city in Hispania Tarraconensis, Liv. 22, 20, 6 .

longŭrĭo.opening: longus , a tall fellow, a long-shanks , Varr. ap. Non. 131, 29 .

longŭrĭus.opening: id. , a long pole : inter singulas equas a praesepibus intericere longurios, Varr. R. R. 2, 7, 10 ; 1, 14, 2 : falces praeacutae insertae affixaeque longuriis, Caes. B. G. 3, 14 ; 4, 17 .

longus.opening: adj. cf. λαγγάζω, λογγάζω , long. Lit. In gen.: longo interjecto intervallo, Cic. Off. 1, 9, 30 : longissima epistula, id. Att. 16, 11 : Rhenus longo spatio citatus fertur, Caes. B. G. 4, 9 : proficisci longissimo…

Lopadusa.opening: an island on the coast of Africa , Plin. 5, 7, 7, § 42 .—The same as , Plin. 3, 9, 15, § 92 Jan. (al. Lepidose).

lŏquācĭtas.opening: loquax , talkativeness, loquacity , Cic. Fam. 6, 4, 4 : Macri loquacitas, id. Leg. 1, 2, 7 : Graeci alicujus, id. de Or. 1, 23, 105 : quo quaeque accuratius celantur, eo facilius loquacitate regiorum ministrorum…

lŏquax.opening: adj. loquor , talkative, prating, chattering, loquacious, full of words . Lit. : quae (ars) in excogitandis argumentis muta nimium est, in judicandis nimium loquax, Cic. de Or. 2, 38, 160 : senectus est naturā…

lŏquēla.opening: (incorrectly written ), , id. , speech, language, words, discourse . Lit. : commoda loquelam tuam, Plaut. Cist. 4, 2, 76 : fuditque has ore loquelas, Verg. A. 5, 842 : nutricis blanda loquela, Lucr. 5, 230 .— Transf. *…

lŏquēlāris.opening: adj. loquela , of or belonging to speech : praepositiones loquelares, in the grammarians, the inseparable prepositions , as re, se, dis, etc., Val. Prob. p. 1427 P.: am praepositio loquelaris significat circum, Paul. ex…

lŏquentĭa.opening: loquor , a talking, discoursing, readiness in speaking, fluency of speech (post-Aug.): Julius Candidus non invenuste solet dicere, aliud esse eloquentiam, aliud loquentiam, Plin. Ep. 5, 20, 5 ; satis loquentiae,…

lŏquĭtor.opening: v. freq. dep. n. [id.], to speak much, talk : loquitatusne es gnato meo male, reviled, Plaut. Bacch. 4, 7, 5 : meditari condiscere, loquitari dediscere, App. Flor. p. 352, 18 .

lŏquor.opening: (quūtus), lŏqui ( inf. loquier, Naev. ap. Gell. 1, 24, 2 ), v. dep. n. and a. [Sanscr. lap-, to talk, whisper; Gr. λακ-, ἔλακον, λάσκω ], to speak, talk, say (in the lang. of common life, in the tone of conversation;…

lŏra.opening: a small or thin wine made of the husks of grapes, after-wine : loram bibere, Cato, R. R. 57 : expressi acinorum folliculi in dolia coniciuntur, eoque aqua additur, ea vocatur lora, quod lota acina: ac pro vino operariis…

lōrāmentum.opening: lorum , a thong : capita loramentorum, Just. 11, 7, 16 : gladio loramenta caedit, id. ib. —Also, any fastening : loramentum ligneum, Vulg. Eccl. 22, 19 .

lōrārĭus.opening: id. , a harness-maker . Lit. , Inscr. ap. Maff. Mus. Ver. 295, 3 (cf. Inscr. Orell. 4302 ).— Transf. , a flogger, chastiser , who scourged slaves with thongs: qui (magistratus) dicebantur lorarii, et, quos erant jussi,…

lōrātus.opening: adj. id. , bound with thongs : juga, Verg. Mor. 122 .

lŏrĕa.opening: , for 1. lora, wine of the second press, after-wine : postquam adbibere aures meae tuae loream orationis, Plaut. Mil. 3, 3, 10 Brix ad loc.: erit lorea familiae, quod bibat, Cato, R. R. 25 : bibere solitus esse, Gell.…

lōrĕus.opening: adj. lorum , of thongs, made of thongs . Lit. : funes, Cato, R. R. 3, 5 ; 12 ; 63 .— Transf. : ego vostra faciam latera lorea. I will cut your hide into strips , Plaut. Mil. 2, 2, 2 .

lōrīca.opening: id. , a leather cuirass, a corselet of thongs (opp. thorax, a brazen breastplate). Lit. : pro lorica malacum capiam pallium, Plaut. Bacch. 1, 1 , 37: lata insignisque lorica, Cic. Mur. 26, 52 : ambulat cum lorica, id.…

lōrīcārĭus.opening: adj. lorica , of or pertaining to cuirasses : loricaria fabrica, Veg. Mil. 2, 11 .— Subst. : † , θωρακοποιός , a maker of cuirasses , Gloss. Philox.

lōrīcātĭo.opening: id. , a clothing in armor, an arming; hence, transf., duplex, a double flooring, double pavement , Vitr. 7, 1 ; so, loricationes, Paul. Dig. 50, 16, 79 fin.

lōrīco.opening: v. a. lorica , to clothe in mail, to mail, to harness . Lit. : statua loricata, Liv. 23, 19 : equites loricati, id. 37, 40 : ornatus loricatusque elephantus cum esset, ubi pluribus coriis se loricavit, Plin. 8, 24, 36,…

lōrīcŭla.opening: dim. id. , a small breastplate; hence, transf., a small breastwork : quorum frontes viminea loricula munirentur, Hirt. B. G. 8, 9, 3 : loricula urbem esse circumdatam, Veg. Mil. 4, 28 .

lŏrĭŏla.opening: dim. 1. lora , wine of the second press, after-wine : loriolam nominabant, cum ex uvis expressum erat, et ad folliculos reliquos et vinacea adiciebant aquam, Varr. ap. Non. 551, 30 .

lōrĭpēs.opening: adj. lorum-pes , strapfooted , i. e. limber-footed, lithe-legged; acc. to others, crook-footed, bandy-legged : proci loripedes, tardissimi, Plaut. Poen. 3, 1, 7 : loripedem rectus derideat, Juv. 2, 23 : juvenis, id. 10,…

lōrum.opening: ( , , , Petr. 57, 8 ; App. M. 3, p. 135, 13 ; Schol. ap. Juv. 6, 480 ), for vlorum, from a ground-form vlārom; Gr. εὔληρα, reins; root perh. val-; cf. volvo , a thong . Lit. : vincire vis? en ostendo manus: tu habes…

Lōryma.opening: , = τὰ Λώρυμα , a seaport in Carta , Liv. 37, 17 ; 45, 10 ; Plin. 5, 28, 29, § 104 .

Lōt.opening: , = Λώτ , Lot, son of Haran, and nephew of Abraham , Prud. Psych. praef. 32; Alcim. 2, 405 ; Vulg. Gen. 11, 27 .

lōtaster.opening: lotos , the wild lotus, of which javelins were made , Grat. Cyn. 131 Wernsd.

lōtĭōlentē.opening: adv. lotium , foully, impurely , Titin. ap. Non. 131, 32 (lotilente, v. 137 Rib.).

Lōtis.opening: , and , , , = Λωτίς, Λωτός , a nymph, daughter of Neptune, who was changed into the lotus-tree : Lotis, Ov. M. 9, 347 ; id. F. 1, 415 : Lotos, Serv. ad Verg. G. 2, 84 .

lōtĭum.opening: urine : brassica alvum bonam facit lotiumque, Cato, R. R. 156 ; Suet. Vesp. 23 .—Prov.: non valet lotium suum, of a good-for-nothing fellow, Petr. 57, 3 .

lōtŏmētra.opening: , = Λωτομήτρα , a species of lotus , Plin. 22, 21, 28, § 56 .

Lōtŏphăgi.opening: Gr. gen. Lotophagōn, Plin. 5, 4, 4, § 20 , , = Λωτοφάγοι (lotus-eaters), an African people on the Lesser Syrtis, to whom fable ascribes great hospitality , Mel. 1, 7, 5 ; Ov. R. Am. 789 ; Verg. Cul. 124 ; Sil. 3, 310 ;…

Lōtŏphăgītis.opening: , = Λωτοφαγῖτις , the island of the lotus-eaters , Plin. 5, 7, 7, § 41 .

lōtos.opening: and , , ( , Mart. 8, 51, 14 ), = λωτός . The name of several plants . The Egyptian water-lily , Plin. 13, 17, 32, § 104 .— A tree on the northern coast of Africa, the food of the Lotophagi, the lotustree, edible…

lōtūra.opening: lavo , a washing, bathing (post-Aug.): pompholyx loturā se paratur, spodos illota est, Plin. 34, 13, 33, § 128 ; Mart. 2, 52 .

Loxĭas.opening: Λοξίας , a surname of Apollo, on account of his obscure ( λοξοῖς ) oracles , Macr. S. 1, 17, 31 .

Lŭa.opening: luo , also called Lua Mater and Lua Saturni, a goddess who expiated the blood shed in battle; to her were devoted the arms taken from an enemy , Liv. 8, 1 ; 45, 33 ; Varr. L. L. 8, § 36 Müll.; Gell. 13, 23, 1 ; Inscr.…

lūbrĭco.opening: v. a. lubricus , to make smooth or slippery, to lubricate (postclass.). Lit. : qui Lacedaemonium pytismate lubricat orbem, Juv. 11, 175 : lubricatus lapis, Arn. 1, 22 ; Prud. στεφ . 11, 38.— To be slippery , Vulg.…

lūbrĭcus.opening: adj. Gr. λιτός, λισσός, smooth; from root γλιτ; cf. γλίσχρος, glittus, and ὀλιβρός, slippery , slippery . Lit. : loculi, Plaut. Mil. 3, 2, 38 : testudini injecta imbris in modum lubrico fastigio innoxia ad imum…

Lūcăgŭs.opening: the name of a warrior , Verg. A. 10, 575 .

Lūcāni.opening: a people in Lower Italy , Varr. L. L. 7, § 39 Müll.; Liv. 8, 19 and 25; 9, 20 et saep.— Transf. , the territory inhabited by them , Caes. B. G. 1, 30 ; Liv. 8, 17, 9 ; Juv. 8, 180 .—Hence, , , adj., Lucanian : ager,…

lūcar.opening: lucus , a forest-tax for the support of players : lucar appellatur aes, quod ex lucis captatur, Paul. ex Fest. p. 119 Müll. N. cr.; cf.: lucaris pecunia, quae in luco erat data, ib.: lucar θεατρικὸν ἀργύριον μισθὸς ἀπὸ…

lūcāris.opening: adj. lucus , of or belonging to a grove : lucaris pecunia, quae in luco erat data, forest-tax , Paul. ex Fest. p. 119, 6 Müll.; v. lucar.—Hence, subst. : , , , the grove-festival : lucaria festa in luco colebant Romani,…

Lūcās.opening: , = Λουκᾶς , St. Luke, the third evangelist , Vulg. Col. 4, 14 ; Prud. Apoth. 1002 et saep.

Luccēĭus.opening: a Roman name . So esp., Q. Lucceius, of Rhegium, a witness against Verres , Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 64, § 165 .— L. Lucceius, son of Marcus, a friend and correspondent of Cicero, and a supporter of the aristocracy , Cic. Att.…

lūcĕ.opening: abl. adv., by day , etc.; v. lux, I. 2. b.

Luceium.opening: a castle or fortress in Galatia , Cic. Deiot. 6 ; 7 .

lŭcellum.opening: dim. lucrum , a small gain, slight profit : lucelli aliquid dare, Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 30, § 72 : facere aliquid lucelli, id. ib. 2, 3, 44 , § 106: tecum partita lucellum, Hor. S. 2, 5, 82 ; trop.: hujus diei lucellum tecum…

lūcens.opening: Part. and P. a. , from luceo.

lūcĕo.opening: v. n. Sanscr. ruk, to be bright; Gr. λύχνος, λευκός, ἀμφιλύκη; Lat. lux, lumen, lucidus, luna; O. H.-Germ. liŏht; Germ. Licht; cf. also illustris , to be light or clear, to shine, beam, glitter (syn.: splendeo, fulgeo).…

Lū^cĕres.opening: (also , or perh. , Paul. ex Fest. p. 119, 10 ), , , an Etruscan tribe, whose union with the Ramnes (Latins) and Taties (Sabines) gave rise to the oldest Roman state. Romulus named after them one of his three centuries…

Lūcĕrĭa.opening: an ancient city of Apulia , now Lucera , Cic. Fam. 15, 15, 4 ; id. Att. 7, 12, 2 ; 8, 11 , a; id. Clu. 69, 197 ; Liv. 22, 9 ; Hor. C. 3, 15, 14 et saep.—Hence, , , adj., Lucerian : finis, Liv. 10, 35 .—In plur. subst. :…

lŭcerna.opening: luc-erna, from luceo, q. v.; with double suffix like caverna, laverna, lanterna, etc.; cf. Gr. κέ-αρνον, σκέπαρνον , a lamp, oil-lamp . Lit. : lucerna dicta a luce, aut quod id vocant Graeci λύχνον , Varr. L. L. 5, §…

lŭcernārĭa.opening: the plant verbascum (acc. to Adelung's Lex. Manuale), Marc. Emp. 20 .

lŭcernāris.opening: adj. lucerna , of or belonging to a lamp : herba, candle-grass, Isid. 17, 9, 73 .

lŭcernārĭum.opening: id. , the time when the lamps are lighted, candle-light , Aug. ap. Reg. Cleric.— A lamp , Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 9, 38 fin.

lŭcernātus.opening: adj. lucerna , furnished , i. e. lighted with a lamp : janua, Tert. ad Uxor. 2, 6 .

lŭcernŭla.opening: dim. id. , a small lamp : accensa lucernula, Hier. Ep. 107 , n. 9; 117, n. 12.

lūcesco.opening: and , , v. inch. n. [luceo], to begin to shine . Lit. In gen.: sol lucescit, Verg. E. 6, 37 : quorum caput flavo capillorum crine lucescat, Firm. Math. 4, 13.— In partic., of the break of day, to grow light, break, dawn…

lūcet.opening: v. impers. , v. luceo, I. A. 2. β .

Lūcĕtĭus.opening: , and , , lux , light-bringer, a surname of Jupiter and of Juno : Lucetium Jovem appellat, Naev. ap. Gell. 5, 12, 6 ; cf. Serv. Verg. A. 9, 570 ; Macr. S. 1, 15 ; cf. also: Lucetium Jovem appellabant, quod eum lucis…

lūcī.opening: abl. as adv. , v. lux init. and I. 2. b.

lūcĭbĭlis.opening: φωτεινός , bright, clear , Gloss. Philox.; cf.: luceus est, quod aliunde illuminatur, lucibile, quod per se patet, Serv. Verg. A. 6, 725 .

lūcĭdus.opening: adj. lux , containing light, full of light, clear, bright, shining (syn.: luminosus, luculentus; as an adj. not in Cic.). Lit. : aër, Lucr. 4, 315 : sidera, Hor. C. 1, 3, 2 : gemma, Ov. H. 15, 74 : amnis, Quint. 12, 10,…

lūcĭfer.opening: adj. lux-fero , light-bringing : itaque ut apud Graecos Dianam, eamque Luciferam, sic apud nostros Junonem Lucinam in pariendo invocant, Cic. N. D. 2, 27, 68 : pars Lunae, Lucr. 5, 726 : equi, the horses of Luna, Ov. H.…

lūcĭfĭco.opening: v. a. lux-facio , to make bright, to brighten : lucificare exitum alicujus aetati, Lab. ap. Gell. 10, 17 fin.

lūcĭfĭcus.opening: adj. id. , light-making, light-giving : sol, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 9, 45 .

lūcĭflŭus.opening: adj. lux-fluo , lightstreaming, light-beaming, brilliant . Lit. : lucifluus solis ortus, Juvenc. 3, 294 .— Trop, light-beaming, glorious : sermo, Juvenc. 4, 120 .

lūcĭfŭga.opening: lux-fugio , lightfleeing, light-shunning . Lit. : maritus, i. e. Cupid (who visited Psyche only at night), App. M. 5, p. 167, 5 ; id. Mag. p. 284, 38 .— Transf. , one who turns night into day : turba lucifugarum, Sen.…

lūcĭfŭgax.opening: adj. lux-fugax , lightshunning : noctua, Auct. Carm. Philomel. 40: natio, Min. Fel. Octav. 8 .

lūcĭfŭgus.opening: adj. lux-fugio , light-shunning . Lit. : blattae, Verg. G. 4, 243 ; Isid. 12, 8, 7 .— Trop. : lucifugus, nebulo, Lucil. ap. Non. 19, 1 : homines, Cic. Fin. 1, 18, 61 : natio, Min. Fel. 8, 4 .

Lūcīlĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens, whose most celebrated members were, The poet C. Lucilius, a native of the Campanian Suessa, formerly Aurunca (hence, Auruncae alumnus, Juv. 1, 19 ), the father of Roman satire , Cic. de Or. 1,…

lūcĭpărens.opening: adj. lux-parens , light-bearing, light-producing : nox (because day follows it), Avien. Phaen. 853 .

lūcĭpĕtus.opening: adj. lux-peto , seeking light (opp. lucifigus): musca, Isid. 12, 8, 7 .

lūcĭsător.opening: lux-sator , lightproducer, author of light : lucisator Omnipotens, Prud. Cath. 3, 1 .

Lūcĭus.opening: lux; of the day , a Roman prænomen, usually represented by L.: Crepusci, qui eo tempore erant nati, ut Lucii prima luce, Varr. L. L. 6, § 5 Müll.; cf.: qui luci natus est Lucius, id. ib. 9 , § 60 Müll.; and: Lucius…

lūcĭus.opening: a fish , perh. the pike , Aus. Mosell. 123 .

lū^crātĭo.opening: lucror , a gaining, gain : spes lucrationis, Tert. ad Uxor. 2, 7 .

lū^crātīvus.opening: adj. id. , gaining, attended with gain . In gen., gainful, profitable, lucrative (rare but class.): apricatio in illo lucrativo sole, Cic. Att. 7, 11, 1 B. and K.: opera, Quint. 10, 7, 27 ; Spald. N. cr. : lucrativa in…

lū^crātor.opening: lucror , he who gains, the acquirer : multarum gentium lucratores, i. e. the apostles, Arn. in Psa. 88 : hominum, Hier. Comm. ad Tit. 1, 11 .

Lū^crētĭlis.opening: a mountain in the Sabine territory , now Monte Genaro , Hor. C. 1, 17, 1 ; cf.: Lucretilis mons in Sabinis, Paul. ex Fest. p. 119 Müll.—Hence, , , adj., of or near the mountain Lucretilis, where Atticus had a villa :…

Lū^crētĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens. Masc. The poet T. Lucretius Carus, an Epicurean in philosophy, author of the poem De rerum natura, Cic. Q. Fr. 2, 11, 4 ; Quint. 10, 1, 87 ; 12, 11, 27 ; Ov. Am. 1, 15, 23 ; Stat. S. 2, 7, 76…

lū^crīcŭpīdo.opening: lucrum-cupido , the passion for gain , App. Doctr. Plat. 2, p. 20, 24 .

lū^crĭfăcĭo.opening: , and in pass. , , (also separately: licet lucri dotem faciat, Dig. 11, 7, 29 : me esse hos trecentos Philippos facturum lucri, Plaut. Poen. 3, 5, 26 ; id. Most. 2, 1, 7 ; id. Pers. 4, 4, 117 ; id. Truc. 3, 2, 22 ; usu.…

lū^crĭfĭcābĭlis.opening: adj. lucrifico , gainful, profitable : dies, Plaut. Pers. 4, 7, 2 .

lū^crĭfĭco.opening: v. a. lucrum-facio , to gain, win : Paulum factum omnibus esse omnia, ut omnes lucrificaret, Tert. Praescr. 24 .

lū^crĭfĭcus.opening: adj. id. , gainful, profitable : Fortuna, Plaut. Pers. 4, 3, 46 .

lū^crĭfŭga.opening: lucrum-fugio , gain-fleeing, gain-shunning : quom ea (Venus) homines huc ad me adigit lucrifugas, Plaut. Ps. 4, 7, 33 .

Lū^crīnus.opening: , with or without lacus, the Lucrine Lake, on the coast of Campania, in the neighborhood of Baiæ (now Lago Lucrino ), Mel. 2, 4, 9 ; Cic. Att. 4, 16, 1 ; Hor. C. 2, 15, 3 . Cæsar, or, acc. to Suetonius, Augustus,…

lū^crĭo.opening: lucrum , one fond of gain : κέρδωνα , quem nos quoque lucrionem vocamus, Paul. ex Fest. p. 56 Müll.

lū^crĭpĕta.opening: lucrum-peto , a gainseeker, one fond of lucre : lucripeta fenerator, Argum. Most. Plaut. 6 .—Collat. form in plur. : , , , Cassiod. Var. 12, 11 .

lū^crĭus.opening: adj. lucrum , of or pertaining to gain : di Lucrii, gods of gain, Arn. 4, 132 .

lū^cror.opening: v. dep. a. [id.], to gain, win, acquire, get, make (as profit). Lit. : cum lucrari impune posset auri pondo decem, Cic. Par. 3, 1 : ut locupletes suum perdant, debitores lucrentur alienum, id. Off. 2, 24, 84 :…

lū^crōsus.opening: adj. lucrum , gainful, profitable, lucrative : voluptas, Ov. Am. 1, 10, 35 ; Tac. Agr. 19 : fraus lucrosior, Plin. 37, 12, 75, § 197 : id peraeque etiam lucrosissimum, id. 18, 31, 74, § 320 .—Hence, adv. : , profitably,…

lū^crum.opening: root laf-; Gr. λάω, ἀπολαύω; Goth. Laun; Germ. Lohn; cf. Laverna , gain, profit, advantage (syn.: quaestus, compendium; cf.: commodum, fructus). Lit. : rem gero et facio lucrum, Plaut. Pers. 4, 3, 34 : quoi di sunt…

lucta.opening: root lug-; cf. λυγίζω, to writhe, ligare , a wrestling, wrestling-match (post-class.): exercebat cum militibus ipse luctam, Capitol. Maxim. 6 : certamen luctae, Aus. Ep. 93 .— Trop. : perseverans quodammodo lucta…

luctāmen.opening: id. , a wrestling . Lit. , Lampr. Alex. Sev. 30 .— Transf. A struggling, struggle , Lampr. Alex. Sev. 30, 4 .— Toil, exertion, contest, fight : remo ut luctamen abesset, Verg. A. 8, 89 : Veneris luctamen anhelum…

luctātĭo.opening: luctor , a wrestling . Lit. : sine adversario nulla luctatio est, Cic. Fat. 13, 30 : quid prodest multos vincere luctatione vel caestu, ab iracundia vinci, Sen. Ep. 88, 19 ; Hyg. Fab. 273 ; Scrib. 101 .— Transf. , a…

luctātor.opening: luctor , a wrestler . Lit. : fortior in fulva novus est luctator arena, Ov. Tr. 4, 6, 31 : luctator ter abjectus perdidit palmam, Sen. Ben. 5, 3, 1 ; id. Ep. 88, 18 ; Quint. 2, 8, 7 ; 12, 2, 12 .— Esp. a wrestler…

luctātus.opening: id. , a wrestling , Plin. 29, 1, 8, § 26 ; id. 8, 12, 12, § 33 .—In plur. , Tert. Spect. 29 .

luctĭfer.opening: adj. luctus-fero , grief - bringing, mournful : illic luctifer bubo gemit, ill-boding, Sen. Herc. Fur. 687 : annus, Val. Fl. 3, 454 .

luctĭfĭcābĭlis.opening: adj. luctus - facio , sorrowful, afflicted : cor, Pers. 1, 78 .

luctĭfĭcus.opening: adj. id. , causing sorrow or lamentation, doleful, woful, baleful : clades, Cic. poët. Tusc. 2, 10, 25: Alecto, Verg. A. 7, 324 : pavor, Sil. 6, 557 : jubar, Val. Fl. 3, 292 .— Neutr. as adv. : luctificum clangente…

luctĭsŏnus.opening: adj. luctus-sonus , sad-sounding, mournful, doleful : mugitu, Ov. M. 1, 732 .

luctĭto.opening: v. freq. n. [lucto], to wrestle violently , acc. to Prisc. p. 797 P.

luctor.opening: ( part. gen. plur. luctantūm, Prop. 4 (5), 22, 9 ; act. collat. form: viri validis viribus luctant, Enn. ap. Non. 472, 8 : plurimum luctavimus, Plaut. ap. Non. 468, 32 ; Varr. L. L. 5, 10, § 61 Müll.: dum luctat, Ter.…

luctŭōsus.opening: adj. luctus , full of sorrow . Causing sorrow, sorrowful, lamentable, doleful, mournful : o diem illum rei publicae luctuosum, Cic. Sest. 12, 27 : fuit hoc luctuosum suis, acerbum patriae, id. de Or. 3, 2, 8 : misera…

luctus.opening: ( gen. lucti, Att. ap. Non. 485, 30 and 32), lugeo , sorrow, mourning, grief, affliction, distress, lamentation , esp. over the loss of something dear to one. Lit. : filius luctu perditus, Cic. Rosc. Am. 8, 23 : orat,…

lūcū.opening: abl. adv. , v. lux, I. 2. b.

lūcū^brātĭo.opening: lucubro , a working by lamp-light, night-work, nocturnal study, lucubration. Lit. : per hiemem lucubratione haec facito, Cato, R. R. 37 : lucubrationes detraxi, Cic. Div. 2, 68, 142 : ista sunt tota commenticia, vix…

lūcū^brātĭuncŭla.opening: dim. lucubratio , a working by night, sitting up at night (post-Aug.). Lit. , Marc. Aur. ap. Front. ad Ep. M. Caes. 1, 3 Mai.— Transf. , night-work, lucubration , Gell. N. A. praef. § 14.

lūcū^brātōrĭus.opening: adj. lucubro , of or belonging to a night-student : lecticula, Suet. Aug. 78 .

lūcū^bro.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
lūcū^bro.opening: v. n. and a. [lux], to work by lamp-light, work at night. Neutr. : (Lucretiam) deditam lanae inter lucubrantes ancillas inveniunt, Liv. 1, 57, 9 : sin lucubrandum est, non post cibum id facere, sed post concoctionem,…

lūcŭbrum.opening: , quod luceat in umbra. Est enim modicus ignis, qui solet ex tenui stuppa ceraque formari, Isid. Orig. 20, 10, 8 .

lūcŭlentĭa.opening: luculentus , brilliancy, beauty (post-class.): verborum luculentiae, Arn. 3, 103 (p. 111 Orell.).— Sing. : scriptorum, Oros. 5, 15 .

lūcŭlentĭtas.opening: id. , excellence, splendor, magnificence : luculentitate captus, Lab. ap. Non. 135, 2 (Com. Rel. v. 71 Rib.): alicujus, Caecil. ib. (Com. Rel. v. 90 Rib.).

lūcŭlentus.opening: adj. lux , full of light, bright, splendid. Lit. : vestibulum et ambulacrum, Plaut. Most. 3, 2, 132 : camino luculento uti, i. e. brightly burning, having a good fire in it, Cic. Fam. 7, 10, 2 .— Trop. Distinguished,…

Lūcullus.opening: a family name in the gens Licinia. The most celebrated is L. Licinius Lucullus, the conqueror of Mithridates, famous for his great wealth and luxury , Cic. Imp. Pomp. 8, 20 sq. ; id. Ac. 2, 1 sq. ; Hor. Ep. 1, 6, 40 ;…

lūcŭlus.opening: dim. lucus , a small grove , Suet. Vit. Hor. fin.

lŭcŭmo.opening: or , and sync. or , , Etrusc. Lauchme , orig., one possessed, an inspired person : lucumones quidam homines ob insaniam dicti, quod loca ad quae venissent, infesta facerent, Paul. ex Fest. p. 120 Müll. — Transf. An…

lŭcuncŭlus.opening: dim. lucuns , a kind of pastry , Afran. ap. Non. 131, 28 : molles caseoli lucunculique, Stat. S. 1, 6, 17 ; App. M. 10, p. 245, 1 ; Petr. 66 : lucunculus, τηγανίτης , Gloss. Philox.

lŭcuns.opening: root lic or luc, crooked, as in obliquus, luxus; Gr. λοξός; cf.: licinus, limus , a kind of pastry , Varr. ap. Non. 131, 24 ; cf.: lucuntem genus operis pistorii, Paul. ex Fest. p. 119 Müll.

lūcus.opening: , i. q. lux, light : cum primo lucu, at daybreak, Ter. Ad. 5, 3, 56 (dub.; Fleck. and Ussing, luci): noctu lucuque, Varr. L. L. 5, 19, § 99 Müll. (ex conj.; al. noctulucus).

Lūcus.opening: 1. lucus , the name of several cities in Gaul and Spain, of which the most important was Lucus, a city of the Vocontii , also called Lucus Augusti, now Lucim , Tac. H. 1, 66 ; Plin. 3, 4, 5, § 37 .

lūdĭa.opening: 1. ludius . An actress, a female stage-dancer , Mart. 5, 25, 10 .— A female gladiator, a gladiator's wife or mistress : quid vidit, propter quod ludia dici Sustinuit, Juv. 6, 103 : quae ludia sumpserit umquam hos…

lūdĭārĭus.opening: adj. 1. ludius, ludus , of or belonging to players : pecunia, the money appropriated by the state for the getting up of plays, Inscr. Orell. 2601 .

lūdī^brĭōsus.opening: adj. ludibrium , full of mockery or scorn, mocking, scornful (post-class.): probra ludibriosa, Gell. 7, 11 : auspicia, Amm. 15, 5, 25 .—Hence, adv. : , scornfully , Amm. 26, 6 ; Tert. Res. Carn. 61 .

lūdī^brĭum.opening: ludus and, perh., fero , a mockery, derision, wantonness. Lit. : quodsi ridicula haec ludibriaque esse videmus, Lucr. 2, 47 : ne per ludibrium interiret regnum, by wantonness, Liv. 24, 4, 2 . — With gen. subj. : ille…

lūdī^brōsus.opening: adj. ludibrium , ridiculous : habitus, Hilar. in Psa. 41, 1.

lūdĭbundus.opening: adj. ludo , playful, sportive, frolicsome, wanton . Lit. : Sic palliolatim amictus hac incessi ludibundus, Plaut. Ps. 5, 1, 30 : milites ita ludibundi Beneventum rediere, ut ab epulis reverti viderentur, Liv. 24, 16 :…

lūdĭcer.opening: or ( nom. sing. m. is not used), , adj. ludus , that serves for sport, done in sport, sportive : ars, Plaut. Aul. 4, 3, 3 : exercitatio, Cic. N. D. 1, 37, 102 : sermones, id. Ac. 2, 2, 6 : ludicrae artes sunt, quae ad…

lūdī^cror.opening: v. dep. ludicrum , to joke, jest , Front. ad Amic. 1, 15 Mai.

lūdĭfăcĭo.opening: v. a. collat. form of ludifico , to make game of, make sport of : aliquem de aliqua re, Plaut. Ep. 5, 2, 41 .

lūdĭfĭcābĭlis.opening: adj. ludifico , with which one makes game of a person: ludi, Plaut. Cas. 4, 1, 2 .

lūdĭfĭcātĭo.opening: id. , a making game, a rallying, jeering, derision, mocking : cum omni morā, ludificatione, calumniā senatūs auctoritas impediretur, * Cic. Sest. 35, 75 : exactā prope aestate per ludificationem hostis, Liv. 22, 18 :…

lūdĭfĭcātor.opening: id. , one who makes game of another, a mocker : ludificator meus, Plaut. Most. 5, 1, 18 .

lūdĭfĭcātōrĭus.opening: adj. ludificator , that makes game of one, mocking, deceptive, false : phantasmatum imaginatio ludificatoria, Aug. Civ. Dei , 11, 26: ubi fuit procuratoris ludificatoria, inanis et nulla persona, Vet. Jureconsult. 3, 2…

lūdĭfĭcātus.opening: ludifico , a mocking, mockery, derision : habere aliquem ludificatui, Plaut. Poen. 5, 5, 2 .

lūdĭfĭco.opening: ( inf. pass. ludificarier, Plaut. Capt. 3, 1, 27 ), , v. a. and n. ludus-facio , to make sport of, make game of, make a fool of; to delude, chouse, cozen, deceive : erum meum ut ego hodie lusi lepide! ut ludificatus…

lūdĭfĭcor.opening: v. dep. n. and a. [id.] ( inf. ludificarier, Plaut. Mil. 4, 4, 25 ), to make game, to mock; to make game of, make sport of, turn into ridicule; to delude, deceive. Lit. Neutr. : aperte ludificari et calumniari, to mock,…

lūdīmăgister.opening: (better separately, ), , ludus-magister , a school-master, school-teacher : cum agellus eum non satis aleret, ut opinor, ludi magister fuit, Cic. N. D. 1, 26, 72 : Dionysius ludimagistrum professus pueros in trivio…

lūdĭo.opening: ludus , a stage-player, pantomimist : ludiones ex Etruria acciti, Liv. 7, 2, 4 : ludionum oblectamenta, id. 39, 6 ; App. Flor. 4, 18, p. 359, 8 ; cf. 1. ludius, I.

lūdĭus.opening: ludus . A stageplayer, pantomimist : fite caussā meā ludii barbari, Plaut. Curc. 1, 2, 63 : ipse ille maxime ludius, non solum spectator, sed actor et acroama, Cic. Sest. 54, 116 ; id. Har. Resp. 11 ; Plaut. Aul. 2, 9,…

Lūdĭus.opening: , a false reading for S. Tadius, Plin. 35, 10, 37, § 116 .

lūdĭvăgus.opening: adj. ludus-vagus , sportive (late Lat.), Cassiod. in Psa. 1, 6 .

lūdo.opening: ( inf. ludier, Ter. Ad. 4, 3, 16 ), , v. a. and n. root lud- for loid-, from Sanscr. krīd, to play; cf. laus and cluere from Sanscr. root cru- , to play. Lit. , to play, play at a game of some kind: tesseris, Ter. Ad.…

lūdor.opening: ludo , a player , Schol. ad Juv. 6, 105 .

lūdus.opening: id. , a play. Lit. In gen., a play, game, diversion, pastime : ad pilam se aut ad talos, aut ad tessaras conferunt, aut etiam novum sibi aliquem excogitant in otio ludum, Cic. de Or. 3, 15, 58 : datur concessu omnium…

lŭella.opening: or , , luo , an expiation, a punishment : scelerisque luela Carcer, Lucr. 3, 1015 .

lŭes.opening: cf. λύω , that which is not bound; hence, fluid, water not frozen : paulo ante lues, jam considenda jacebat, Petr. 123 .

Lugdūnum.opening: (orig. form LVGVDVNVM, v. Rhein. Mus. 1854, vol. 9, p. 445 sq.), , , a city of Gaul, at the confluence of the Arar and Rhodanus , now Lyons , Plin. 4, 18, 32, § 107 ; Suet. Calig. 20 ; Tac. A. 3, 41 ; id. H. 2, 65 ; 4,…

lūgĕo.opening: (luxti for luxisti, Cat. 66, 21 ; dep. lugeri, Prisc. 1251 ), v. n. and a. [akin to Gr. λυγρός, λοιγός ; Sanscr. root lū, to cut; cf. lues], to mourn, lament, bewail, deplore (syn. ploro). Lit. Neutr. : luget senatus,…

lūgū^bris.opening: ( , Lucr. 4, 547 ), , adj. lugeo and fero , of or belonging to mourning, mourning- . Lit. : lamentatio, over the dead, Cic. Tusc. 1, 13, 30 : vestis, mourning apparel, Ter. Heaut. 2, 3, 45 ; cf. cultus, Tac. A. 13, 32 :…

lŭĭtĭo.opening: luo , a paying, payment , Dig. 49, 15, 15 ; Paul. Sent. 3, 7 : de luitione pignoris, the redemption of a pledge by paying the money lent, Cod. Just. 8, 31 .

lūma.opening: A thorn : luma genus herbae vel potius spinae, Paul. ex Fest. p. 120 Müll.— A kind of cloak : luma, sagum quadrum, Glos. Isid.

lūmārĭus.opening: adj. luma, I. , of or for thorns : falces, for cutting down thorns, Varr. L. L. 5, § 137 Müll.

lumbāgo.opening: lumbus , lumbago : vitium et debilitas lumborum, Paul. ex Fest. p. 120 Müll.

lumbāre.opening: id. , an apron for the loins , Hier. in Jer. 13, 1 ; id. Ep. 7, 3 ; cf. Isid. Orig. 19, 22, 25 .

lumbellus.opening: dim. id. , a little loin , Apic. 7, 1, § 259 .

lumbĭfrăgĭum.opening: lumbus-frango , a breaking of the loins , Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 298 .

lumbrīcōsus.opening: adj. lumbricus , full of intestinal worms , Cael. Aur.

lumbrīcus.opening: an intestinal worm, maw-worm, stomach-worm . Lit. : si teniae et lumbrici molesti erunt, Cato, R. R. 126 ; Col. 6, 25 ; cf. id. 6, 30, 9 : nec lumbricis ulli sunt (oculi), Plin. 11, 37, 52, § 140 ; Cael. Aur. Acut. 7, 8…

lumbŭlus.opening: dim. lumbus , a little loin , Plin. 28, 11, 47, § 109 ; Apic. 7, 8, § 292 .

lumbus.opening: a loin . Lit. : At Edepol nos (velimus) tibi in lumbos linguam atque oculos in solum (decidisse), Plaut. Poen. 3, 1, 68 : exporgi meliust lumbos, id. Ps. prol. 24 (1); id. Ep. Grex, 2: lumborum tenus, Cic. Arat. 82 :…

lūmectum.opening: luma, I. , a thicket of thorns : lumariae (falces) sunt, quibus secant lumecta, Varr. L. L. 5, § 137 Müll.

lūmen.opening: contr. from lucmen, from the root luc; v. luceo , light . Lit. : quasi lumen de suo lumine accendat, Enn. ap. Cic. Off. 1, 16, 51 (Fragm. v. 388 Vahl.): solis, Cic. Div. 2, 42, 91 : tabulas bene pictas conlocare in bono…

lūmĭnāre.opening: lumen , that whieh gives light, a light-giver (mostly in plur. ). A luminary, a heavenly body : fecitque Deus duo luminaria magna, Vulg. Gen. 1, 16 .— A light, lamp , burned in the Jewish temple and in Christian…

lūmĭnātor.opening: lumino , a giver of light (late Lat.), Aug. c. Faust. Manich. 20, 12.

lūmĭnātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , v. lumino.

lūmĭno.opening: v. a. lumen , to light up, brighten, illumine (post-class.): tu luminas solem, regis mundum, App. M. 11, p. 269, 40 : tellus floribus luminata, Marc. Cap. 1, § 27; § 66: locus fenestris luminatus, Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 9…

lūmĭnōsus.opening: adj. id. , full of light, light, luminous . Lit. : aedificia, Vitr. 6, 9 : oleum luminosius, Aug. Ep. 137 fin. — Trop. , bright, conspicuous, prominent, remarkable : partes orationis, Cic. Or. 36, 125 .— Sup. :…

lūna.opening: ( gen. lunai, Lucr. 5, 69 ), contr. for luc-na, from root luc; v. luceo , the moon . Lit. : dimidiata, Cato, R. R. 37 : extrema et prima, Varr. R. R. 1, 37 : solis annuos cursus spatiis menstruis luna consequitur, Cic.…

Lūna.opening: a city of Etruria , now Luni , Mel. 2, 4, 9 ; Plin. 3, 5, 8, § 50 ; Liv. 39, 21, 5 ; 43, 11 ; Mart. 13, 30, 1 ; Sil. 8, 482 .— Hence, or , , adj., of or belonging to Luna : caseus Luniensis, remarkable for its size,…

lūnāris.opening: adj. 1. luna , of or belonging to the moon, lunar .— Lit. : dies, Varr. R. R. 1, 37 : horae, id. L. L. 9, § 26 Müll.: cursus, Cic. Rep. 6, 18 : equi, Ov. F. 5, 16 : ratio, Plin. 16, 39, 74, § 190 : cornua, Ov. M. 10,…

lūnātĭcus.opening: adj. id. . Living on the moon : homines, Lact. 3, 23, 13 .— = σεληνιακός, σεληνόπληκτος , epileptic, lunatic, moon-struck, crazy : mancipium, Dig. 21, 1, 43, § 6 ; Vulg. Matt. 4, 24 ; 17, 14 ; Acron. ad Hor. A. P. 454 ;…

lūnātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , v. luno.

lūno.opening: v. a. 1. luna , to bend like a half-moon or crescent, to crook like a sickle (rare in the verb. finit.; freq. in the P. a. ): lunavit fortiter arcum, Ov. Am. 1, 1, 23 : acies geminos in arcus, Prop. 4 (5), 6, 25.…

lūnŭla.opening: dim. 1. luna , a little moon , an ornament worn by women: aurea, Plaut. Ep. 5, 1, 33 : lunulae sunt ornamenta mulierum in similitudinem lunae, bullulae aureae dependentes, Isid. Orig. 19, 31, 17 ; Tert. Cult. Fem. 2, 10…

Lūnus.opening: luceo , the Moon-god , worshipped at Carræ, Spart. Caracall. 6, 6 ; 7, 3 ; cf. Tert. Apol. 15 .

lŭo.opening: (no sup. , but fut. part. act. luiturus, Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 16 ; Claud. VI. Cons. Hon. 140 ; Prud. Psych. 535 ; v. Neue, Formenl. 2, p. 585), , v. a. root lu, to loose, let go; Gr. λύω; cf. λυτήρ, λύτρον; Lat. solvo,…

lŭpa.opening: lupus , a she-wolf . Lit. : rabidae tradis ovile lupae, Ov. A. A. 3, 8 ; Liv. 1, 4, 6 : ab agro rava decurrens lupa Lanuvino, Hor. C. 3, 27, 3 : quem nutrit dura papilla lupae, Prop. 5, 4, 54 : lupa Romuli, Quint. 2, 4,…

lŭpānar.opening: lupa, II. A. , a house of ill-repute : qui in lupanari accubat, Plaut. Bacch. 3, 3, 50 : deprehensus in lupanari cum alienā uxore, Quint. 7, 3, 6 : intrare, Juv. 6, 121 : virorum, Mos. et Rom. Leg. Coll. 5, 3, 2.—As a…

lŭpānāris.opening: adj. lupanar , belonging to or characteristic of a lewd woman : infamia, App. M. 9, p. 229, 7 .

lŭpānārĭum.opening: id. , i. q. lupanar, Dig. 5, 3, 27 al.

lŭpārĭae.opening: brothels , Sext. Ruf. Reg. 2 ; Inscr. ap. Gud. 33, 1.

lŭpārĭus.opening: lupus , a wolf-hunter , Serv. Verg. G. 1, 139 ; cf.: luparius, λυκοθήρας , Gloss. Philox.

lŭpātus.opening: adj. id. , furnished with wolf's teeth , i. e. iron prickles shaped like a wolf's teeth. Adj. : Gallia nec lupatis Temperet ora frenis, curbs studded with jagged points, Hor. C. 1, 8, 6 . — Subst. (sc. freni or frena):…

Lŭperca.opening: v. Lupercus , a goddess of the old Romans, the wife of Lupercus, identified with the deified she-wolf that suckled Romulus , Arn. 4, 128 ; cf. Liv. 1, 4 ; Lact. 1, 20 .

Lŭpercal.opening: Lupercalis , a grotto on the Palatine Hill, sacred to the Lycean Pan (Lupercus) : gelidā monstrat sub rupe Lupercal, Verg. A. 8, 342 ; v. Serv. ad loc.: quamquam Velia non est vilior quam Lupercal, Cic. Fam. 7, 20, 1 :…

Lŭpercus.opening: lupus, and perh. arceo . The Roman name of the Lycean Pan (so called because he protected the flocks from wolves), Just. 4, 3, 1 .—Far more freq., A priest of the Lycean Pan : nudi Luperci, Verg. A. 8, 663 ; Ov. F. 2,…

Lupĭa.opening: ( ), , , a river in the north-west of Germany , now the Lippe , Mela, 3, 3, 3; Vell. 2, 10, 5 ; Tac. A. 1, 60 ; 2, 7 ; id. H. 5, 22 .

Lū^pĭae.opening: plur., a town of Calabria , Paul. Nol. 30, 85 ; cf. Mel. 2, 4 .

Lŭpĭcīnus.opening: the name of a man , Paul. Petr. Vit. S. Mart. 1, 369 .

lŭpillus.opening: dim. 2. lupinus , a small lupine , Plaut. Stich. 5, 4, 9 .

lŭpīnācĕus.opening: adj. id. , of or made of lupines : lomentum, App. Herb. 21 .

lŭpīnārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or for lupines : labrum, Cato, R. R. 10 and 11.— Subst. : , , , dealers in lupines , Lampr. Alex. Sev. 33, 2 .

lŭpīnus.opening: , and , , , a lupine : ibi lupinum bonum fiet, Cato, R. R. 34, 2 ; cf. Col. 12, 10, 1 sq. ; Plin. 18, 14, 36, § 133 ; Pall. 1, 6, 14 ; 7, 3, 2 : fetus viciae tristisque lupini, Verg. G. 1, 75 : tunicam mihi malo lupini,…

Lūpŏdūnum.opening: a German town near the sources of the Danube , now Ladenburg or Lupff , Aus. Mosell. 423 .

lŭpor.opening: v. dep. n. [lupa, II.], to associate with lewd women : cum meretrice per vias lupantur, Atta ap. Non. 133, 11 (Com. Rel. v. 3 Rib.): impune lupari, Lucil. ib. 15 .

lŭpŭla.opening: dim. id. , a little she-wolf , transf., a witch, hag , App. M. 5, p. 164, 3 .

lŭpus.opening: kindred with λύκος; Sanscr. vrika, and our wolf , a wolf . Lit. : torva leaena lupum sequitur, lupus ipse capellam, Verg. E. 2, 63 ; Plin. 10, 63, 88, § 173 ; 8, 22, 34, § 80 : Martialis lupus, sacred to Mars, Hor. C.…

Lŭpus.opening: a surname in the gens Rutilia, e. g. P. Lutilius Lupus, a rhetorician in the time of Augustus; v. Rutilius; cf. Cic. N. D. 1, 23, 63 .

lūra.opening: ( ), , from same root as lorum, q. v. , prop. a thong; hence, the mouth of a skin or leathern bag , which was closed by a thong: lura os cullei vel etiam utris: unde lurcones capacis gulae homines et bonorum suorum…

lurchĭnābundus.opening: ( and ), , adj. 1. lurco , voracious , Cat. ap. Quint. 1, 6, 42 ; cf. Spald. ad loc.

lurco.opening: ( , Serv. ad Verg. A. 6, 4 ; Prob. p. 1455 P.), , , a gormandizer, glutton .— Lit. : lurco, edax, furax, fugax, Plaut. Pers. 3, 3, 16 : vivite lurcones, comedones, vivite ventres, Lucil. ap. Non. 11, 9 : lastaurum et…

Lurco.opening: a Roman surname . Esp., M. Aufidius, who was the first to fatten peacocks for the table , Varr. R. R. 3, 6, 1 ; Plin. 10, 20, 23, § 45 .—So of M. Perpenna Lurco, Inscr. Grut. 237, 8 .— Transf. , a voluptuary, debauchee…

lūrĭdātus.opening: adj [luridus], besmeared, defiled , Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 8 .

lūrĭdus.opening: adj. luror , pale yellow, sallow, wan, ghastly, lurid . Lit. : luridi supra modum pallidi, Paul. ex Fest. p. 120 ; cf.: luridus, ὠχρός, πέλιος, ἰκτερικός, ὑπώπιος , Gloss. Philox.: luridus Orcus, Hor. C. 3, 4, 74 :…

lūror.opening: etym. dub.; cf.: pullus, lividus , a yellowish color, sallowness, paleness , Lucr. 4, 308 : luror permanat in herbas, Claud. Rapt. Pros. 3, 238 : lurore buxeo foedatus, App. M. 9, p. 222, 31 .

luscĭnĭa.grammar: ae ĭi i f. m. m.
luscĭnĭa.opening: ( , , , Phaedr. 3, 18, 2 and 11; Sen. Ep. 76, 7 ; and, † , , , = ἀηδών , Gloss. Lat. Gr.) [for clus-cinia; Sanscr. root cru, to hear; Gr. κλύω ; Lat. clueo, to be famous, akin to gloria and cano; hence, the melodious or…

luscĭnĭŏla.opening: dim. luscinia , a little nightingale : aves cantrices, ut lusciniolae ac merulae, Varr. R. R. 3, 5, 14 ; cf. id. L. L. 5, § 76 Müll.—Prov.: So. Pol magis metuo mihi in monendo ne defuerit optio. Ba. Pol ego metuo…

luscĭnĭus.opening: adj. luscinus , blinded, one-eyed , applied by Commodus to persons one of whose eyes he had destroyed, Lampr. Commod. 10, 6 ; cf. the foll. art.

Luscĭnus.opening: a Roman surname : C. Fabricius Luscinus, Val. Max. 4, 3, 6 ; Liv. 33, 42 and 43; 37, 4.

luscĭtĭo.opening: luscus , dimness of sight , Dig. 21, 1, 10, § 4 : vitium oculorum, quod clarius vesperi quam meridie cernit, Paul. ex Fest. p. 120, 17 Müll.

luscĭtĭōsus.opening: and , , adj. i. e. luscitionosus, from luscitio , that cannot see in the dusk or by lamp-light, dim-sighted, purblind: Pa. Quid jam? Sce. Quia luscitiosus. Pa. Verbero, edepol tu quidem caecus, non luscitiosus, Plaut.…

luscus.opening: adj. root luc of lux; with fundamental idea to glimmer; cf. Gr. λυγη, gloom , one-eyed: Le. Oculum ego ecfodiam tibi, si verbum addideris. Sc. Hercle qui dicam tamen: nam si sic non licebit, luscus dixero, Plaut. Trin.…

lūsĭo.opening: ludo , a playing, play : in ludum discendi, non lusionis, Cic. Q. Fr. 3, 4, 6 : pueri lusionibus vel laboriosis delectantur, id. Fin. 5, 20, 55 : in ipsā lusione (pilae), in the act of playing, id. de Or. 1, 16, 73 :…

Lūsĭtānĭa.opening: the western part of Spain , the mod. Portugal and a part of the Spanish provinces of Estremadura and Toledo , Caes. B. C. 1, 38, 2 ; Liv. 21, 43, 8 ; 27, 20 ; Mel. 2, 6, 3 sq. ; 3, 1, 6 ; 3, 6, 2 ; Liv. Ep. 52 ; Plin.…

lūsĭto.opening: v. freq. n. [ludo], to play often or habitually (ante- and post-class.): aut coturnices dantur, quibuscum lusitent, Plaut. Capt. 5, 4, 6 : alea festiva et honesta lusitabamus, Gell. 18, 13, 1 : in labellis morsicatim,…

Lusĭus.opening: a river of Arcadia , Cic. N. D. 3, 22, 57 .

lūsor.opening: ludo , one who plays at a game; a player . Lit. : sic ne perdiderit, non cessat perdere lusor, Ov. A. A. 1, 1, 451 ; Sen. Ben. 2, 17, 3 : furtum factum domi et eo tempore quo alea ludebatur, licet lusor non fuerit qui…

lūsōrĭus.opening: adj. lusor , of or belonging to a player . Lit. : pila, a playing-ball, Plin. 7, 56, 57, § 205 : alveus cum tesseris, id. 37, 2, 6, § 13 .—Hence, Subst. : , , , a place where shows of gladiators and wild beasts were…

lustrābĭlis.opening: adj. lustro , conspicuous , περίβλεπτος (i. e. spectabilis), Gloss. Philox.

lustrāgo.opening: perh. from lustrum , a plant, also called verbenaca, App. Herb. 3 .

lustrālis.opening: adj. 2. lustrum , relating to purification from guilt or the appeasing of the gods, lustral . Lit. : sacrificium, a sacrifice of purification, a propitiatory offering, Liv. 1, 28 : aqua, lustral water, holy water, Ov.…

lustrāmen.opening: lustro , a means of purification , Val. Fl. 3, 442 ; 409 .

lustrāmentum.opening: lustror , an incentive to lust : si quis lustramenti causā dederit cantharides, Dig. 48, 8, 3 .

lustrātĭo.opening: lustro , a purification by sacrifice, a lustration . Lit. : lustrationis sacro peracto, Liv. 40, 6 ; 40, 13, 2 sq.; Col. 2, 22, 5 .— Transf. [v. lustro, II.], a going or wandering about : lustrationesque (ferarum), Cic.…

lustrātor.opening: id. . A purifier, cleanser : Gallus sacerdos ac lustrator, Schol. Juv. 6, 542 .— A wanderer through a place, a traverser : Hercules lustrator orbis, App. Mag. p. 288, 25 .

lustrĭcus.opening: adj. 2. lustrum , of or belonging to purification : dies, the eighth (or ninth ) day after a child's birth, on which it was purified by a sacrifice and received a name , Suet. Ner. 6 ; Macr. S. 1, 16 ; Arn. 3, 102 ;…

lustrĭfĭcus.opening: adj. 2. lustrumfacio , purifying : cantus, Val. Fl. 3, 448 .

lustro.opening: , i. q. vagus, wanderer, vagabond , Naev. in Lex. Vatic. tom. 8, p. 313; cf. Klussman, Naev. p. 232 , and Com. Rel. v. 118 sq. Rib.

lustror.opening: v. dep. n. [1. lustrum], to frequent places of ill-repute : circum oppida, Lucil. Sat. 30, 68 : lustrantur, comedunt quod habent, Plaut. Ps. 4, 7, 6 : ubi fuisti, ubi lustratus, id. Cas. 2, 3, 29 .

lustrum.opening: 2. luo , a purificatory sacrifice, expiatory offering, lustration , made by the censors for the whole people once in five years, after completing the census, and in which a swine, a sheep, and a bull were offered…

lūsus.opening: ludo , a playing, play, game (not in Cic.). Lit. : virgineis exercent lusibus undas Naides, Ov. M. 14, 556 : aleae, Suet. Calig. 41 : calculorum, Plin. Ep. 7, 24 : nec me offenderit lusus in pueris, Quint. 1, 3, 10 ;…

lŭtāmentum.opening: 1. luto , that which is made of mud or clay, a mud or clay wall , Cato, R. R. 128 .

lŭtārĭus.opening: adj. 2. lutum , of or be longing to mud . Living in mud : testudines, Plin. 32, 4, 14, § 32 .— Living on mud : mullus, Plin. 9, 17, 30, § 65 .

Lŭtātĭus.opening: ( ), , the name of a Roman gens. So, Q. Lutatius Catulus, consul A. U. C. 652, Cic. Mur. 17, 36 ; id. Cael. 29, 70 ; a younger man of the same name, consul A. U. C. 676, id. Cat. 3, 10, 24 ; id. Balb. 15, 34 .—Hence, (…

lūtĕa.opening: 1. lutum , a false reading for uvam, Plin. 33, 5, 26, § 87 .

lŭtensis.opening: adj. 2. lutum , found or living in mud : genus purpurarum, Plin. 9, 37, 61, § 131 .

lūtĕŏlus.opening: adj. dim. [1. luteus], yellowish : mollia luteolā pingit vaccinia calthā, Verg. E. 2, 50 : violae, Col. 9, 4, 4 : olivae, id. 12, 47, 9 .

lūtēr.opening: , = λουτήρ , a hand-basin, laver , Hier. in Jov. 1 , n. 20; Vulg. 3 Reg. 7, 26 al.

lŭtesco.opening: v. inch. n. [2. lutum], to turn to mud, become muddy : litora, quae limo caenoque lutescunt, Col. 8, 17, 9 : cava terra lutescit, Furius Antias ap. Gell. 18, 11 ; id. ap. Non. 133, 26 .

Lutetĭa.opening: a city in Gallia Lugdunensis, now Paris , Caes. B. G. 7, 57 ; Amm. 15, 11, 3 al. ; called also Lutetia Parisiorum, Caes. B. G. 6, 3 .

lūtĕus.opening: adj. 1. lutum , prop. of or belonging to the yellow-weed; hence, in gen., of the color of lutum . Golden-yellow, saffron-yellow, orange-yellow . chrysocolla, Plin. 33, 5, 27, § 91 ; Varr. ap Non. 549, 22 : pallor, Hor.…

lŭtĕus.opening: adj. 2. lutum , of mud or clay . Lit. : defingit Rheni luteum caput, Hor. S. 1, 10, 37 : opus, of a swallow's nest, Ov. F. 1, 157 : aedificium, Plin. 7, 56, 57 . § 194: toreuma, Mart. 4, 46, 16 : homo, i. e. Adam, Prud.…

lūtĭto.opening: v. freq. a. 1. luto , to bedaub; only trop., to bring into contempt, to asperse : nam hi mores majorum laudant, eosdem lutitant quos conlaudant, Plaut. Trin. 2, 2, 15 Brix ad loc.

lŭto.opening: v. a. 2. lutum , to bedaub with mud or clay . Lit. , Cato, R. R. 92 : nidosque reversa lutabit hirundo, Calp. Ecl. 5, 17 : lutati tituli statuarum, Lampr. Elag. 14 .— Transf. , to bedaub, besmear : ne lutet immundum…

lūto.opening: v. freq. a. for luito, from luo; cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 116, 5 Müll.: litatum ... quasi luitatum , to pay : lutavi, Varr. ap. Non. 131, 21 .

lūtor.opening: luo , a washer, fuller : † lutor, πλύτης ἡλιαστής , Gloss. Philox.; Inscr. Gud. 17, 2 .

lŭtōsus.opening: adj. 2. lutum , full of mud or loam, muddy, miry, dirty : terra, Cato ap. Plin. 18, 19, 49, § 176 : ager, Col. 2, 45 : rapa, id. 12, 54 (56), 1.

lūtra.opening: ( ), , luo , an otter , Plin. 8, 30, 47, § 109 ; 32, 11, 53, § 144 ; form lytra, Varr. L. L. 5, § 79 Müll.

lŭtŭlentus.opening: adj. 2. lutum , muddy . Lit. : sus, bedaubed with mud, Hor. Ep. 2, 2, 75 : diluvio tellus lutulenta recenti, Ov. M. 1, 434 : amnis, id. Am. 3, 6, 95 : mula, Mart. 9, 23, 13 .—* Transf. , besmeared with ointment: et…

lŭtŭlo.opening: v. a. id. , to bespatter with mud; trop., to asperse; old reading, Plaut. Trin. 2, 2, 15 ; for lutito, q. v., cf. Ritschl, Prol. ad Plaut. p. lxxiv.

lūtum.opening: a plant used in dyeing yellow, yellow-weed. dyer's-weed, weld : jam croceo mutabit vellera luto, Verg. E. 4, 44 ; Plin. 33, 5, 26, § 87 ; Vitr. 7, 14 .— Transf. , a yellow color, yellow , Verg. Cir. 316 : nimius luto…

lŭtum.opening: ( , , , Quadrig. ap. Non. 212, 17 ) [luo], mud, mire . Lit. : volutari in luto, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 24, § 53 : cratesque luto integuntur, Caes. B. C. 2, 15 ; Quadrig. ap. Non. 212, 17 : imbre lutoque Aspersus, Hor. Ep. 1,…

lux.opening: (adverb. abl. luce, luci, and lucu, and in these old forms also used as ; v. infra ; in Plaut. lux is usually ; Brix ad Plaut. Capt. 5, 4, 11 ), luceo , light . Lit. In gen., the light of the sun and other heavenly…

luxātĭo.opening: στρέμμα , i. q. luxatura, a dislocation, luxation , Gloss. Philox.

luxātūra.opening: luxo , a dislocation, luxation , Marc. Emp. 36 .

luxo.opening: v. a. Gr. λοξός, slanting, akin to obliquus, limus, licinus , to put out of joint, to dislocate . Lit. : luxatum si quod est, sanum faciet, Cato, R. R. 157 : luxata in locum reponere, Sen. Ep. 104, 18 : articulis…

luxor.opening: v. dep. luxus , to riot, revel, live luxuriously : luxantur a luxu dictum, id est luxuriantur, Paul. ex Fest. p. 120 Müll.; cf. Non. 55, 15 : luxantur, lustrantur, Plaut. Ps. 4, 7, 5 Fleck.

luxŭrĭa.opening: , and , (v. Zumpt, Verr. 2, 2, 3, § 7, and 2, 5, 31, § 80; Roby, Gram. § 342; old gen. luxurii, Gracch. ap. Gell. 9, 14 ; the dat. of the fifth decl. is not in use, and the abl. is doubtful; v. Neue, Formenl. 1, 382…

luxŭrĭo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 ātus, 1 v. n. v. dep.
luxŭrĭo.opening: v. n. , and , , v. dep. (cf. Quint. 9, 3, 7 ) [luxuria], to be rank, luxuriant, abound to excess (not in Cic. or Cæs.). Lit. : ager assiduā luxuriabat aquā, Ov. F. 4, 644 : luxuriat Phrygio sanguine pinguis humus, id.…

luxŭrĭōsus.opening: adj. luxuria , rank, luxuriant, exuberant . Lit. : frumenta, Cic. Or. 24, 81 : seges, Ov. F. 1, 690 : vitis valida et luxuriosa, Col. 5, 6, 36 : vitis, id. 4, 21, 2 .— Trop. Immoderate, excessive : luxurioso otio esse,…

luxus.opening: ( dat. luxu, Sall. J. 6 ; Tac. A. 3, 34 ; id. H. 2, 71 ) [root luc-; cf. pol-luceo, pol-lucte; v. Corss. Ausspr. 1, 368 sq.]. Excess, extravagance in eating and drinking, luxury, debauchery : adulescens luxu perditus,…

Lўaeus.opening: , = Λυαῖος , Lyæus, the relaxer, unbender, deliverer from care . A surname of Bacchus : patri Lyaeo, Verg. A. 4, 58 : corniger Lyaeus, Ov. Am. 3, 15, 17 ; id. M. 4, 11 ; 8, 274 ; 11, 68 ; Verg. G. 2, 229 al. — Transf. ,…

Lўcăbas.opening: , = Λυκάβας . A Tuscan who fled from his country on account of a murder, and who, for a slight shown to Bacchus, was changed into a dolphin , Ov. M. 3, 624 .— An Assyrian , Ov. M. 5, 60 .— A Centaur , Ov. M. 12, 302 .

Lўcaeus.opening: , = Λυκαῖος , a mountain in Arcadia (now Dhiaforti ), where Jupiter and Pan were worshipped , Plin. 4, 6, 10, § 21 ; Verg. G. 4, 539 ; Ov. M. 1, 217 ; Aug. Civ. Dei , 18, 17; Serv. Verg. A. 8, 343 and 344: saxa Lycaei,…

Lўcambes.opening: , = Λυκάμβης , a Theban who promised his daughter to Archilochus, and afterwards refused her; for which he was pursued by the poet with such bitter sarcasm that he hung both himself and his daughter : qualis Lycambae…

Lўcāon.opening: , = Λυκάων , a king of Arcadia, father of Callisto, whom Jupiter, because he had defiled his altar with human sacrifices, turned into a wolf; acc. to Ovid, because he had tried to murder Jupiter himself, who was his…

lўcāon.opening: , = λυκάων , an animal of the wolf kind , Mela, 3, 9, 2; Plin. 8, 34, 52, § 123 ; Sol. 3 .

Lўcāŏnes.opening: , = Λυκάονες , the Lycaonians, a people of Asia Minor, between Cappadocia, Cilicia, and Pisidia , Mel. 1, 2, 5 ; Plin. 5, 29, 29, § 105 .—Hence, , , adj., Lycaonian : Lycaoniumque Ericeten, Verg. A. 10, 749 .— Subst. :…

Lўcāŏnĭus.opening: , v. 1. Lycaon, II. A. and Lycaones.

Lўcaūnŭs.opening: the name of a warrior , Sil. 4, 203 .

Lўcē.opening: , = Λύκη , the name of a woman , Hor. C. 4, 13, 1 .

lychnĭcus.opening: adj. , = λυχνικός , luminous, shining : lapis, a kind of white marble, also called lychnites, Hyg. Fab. 223 .

Lychnĭdum.opening: , and , , , = Λυχνιδός , a city of Illyria, near the Haliacmon, in the territory of the Dessaretes , Liv. 27, 32 ; 43, 9 ; 10 ; 21.

lychnis.opening: adj. f. , = λυχνίς , lightgiving, shining . Lit. : lychnides puellae, girls with lamps , Fulg. Myth. prooem. 1.— Subst. : , , A kind of rose of a fiery red , Plin. 21, 4, 10, § 18 .— Lychnis agria, another plant, Plin.…

lychnītes.opening: , = λυχνίτης , a kind of white marble , which was quarried in the Isle of Paros by lamp-light, Plin. 36, 5, 4, § 14 .

lychnītis.opening: , = λυχνῖτις , a plant from which wicks were made , Plin. 25, 10, 74, § 121

lychnŏbĭus.opening: , = λυχνόβιος , one who lives by lamp-light, who turns night into day , Sen. Ep. 122, 17 ; v. lucifuga.

lychnūchus.opening: , = λυχνοῦχος , a lamp-stand, candlestick, chandelier : ligneolus, Cic. Q. Fr. 3, 7, 2 : pensiles, Plin. 34, 3, 8, § 14 ; Suet. Dom. 4 ; id. Caes. 37 .

lychnus.opening: (old Latinized form lucinus, Enn.; cf. Ritschl in Rhein. Mus. 10, p. 448 sq.), , , = λύχνος , a light, a lamp : pendentes lychni, Lucr. 5, 295 : lux alia est solis et lychnorum, Cic. Cael. 28, 67 ; Verg. A. 1, 726 ;…

Lўcĭa.opening: ( , Plaut. Curc. 3, 73 Fleck.), , , = Λυκία , a country of Asia Minor, between Caria and Pamphylia, where was the volcano Chimæra , Mel. 1, 2, 6 ; 1, 15, 1 ; 2, 7, 4 ; Plin. 5, 27, 27, § 97 : Chimaerifera Lycia, Ov. M.…

Lўcĭdas.opening: , = Λυκίδας , one of the Centaurs, who endeavored to carry off Hippodamia from Pirithoüs , Ov. M. 12, 310 .— The name of a beautiful boy , Hor. C. 1, 4, 19 .— The name of a shepherd , Verg. E. 7, 67 ; 9, 12 .

Lўcīmnĭa.opening: ( ), , , the name of the wife of a king of Lydia , Verg. A. 9, 546 (al. Licymnia).

Lўcimnĭus.opening: adj., of or belonging to the town of Lycimna (in Argolis), Lycimnian : stagna, Stat. Th. 4, 734 .

Lўcinna.opening: the name of a girl , Prop. 3, (4), 13, 6.

Lўcisca.opening: , and , , The name of a bitch , Verg. E. 3, 18 ; Ov. M. 3, 220 .— A vile woman , Juv. 6, 122 .

lўciscus.opening: , = λυκίσκος , a wolfdog : lycisci dicuntur canes nati ex lupis et canibus, cum inter se forte miscentur, Isid. Orig. 12, 2 .— , the name of a beautiful boy , Hor. Epod. 11, 24 .— A boy whose statue was made by…

Lўcīum.opening: (less correctly , v. Ellendt ad Cic. de Or. 1, 21, 98 ), , , = Λύκειον , a gymnasium very near Athens, in which Aristotle taught , Cic. de Or. 1, 21, 98 ; id. Ac. 1, 4, 17 ; id. Div. 1, 13, 22 ; Liv. 31, 24, 18 ; Gell.…

Lyco.opening: a Peripatetic philosopher, a follower of Strato of Lampsacus , Cic. Tusc. 3, 32, 78 .

Lўcŏmēdes.opening: , = Λυκομήδης , a king of the Isle of Scyros, with whom Achilles concealed himself disguised in female attire, and whose daughter Deidamia bore to the latter Pyrrhus or Neoptolemus , Cic. Lael. 20, 75 (where Neoptolemus…

Lўcōnĭdēs.opening: the name of a man , Plaut. Aul. 4, 10, 49 .

lўcŏphon.opening: a plant, also called scelerata, App. Herb. 8 .

Lўcŏphōn.opening: the name of a warrior , Stat. Th. 2, 610 .

lўcŏphōs.opening: , = λυκόφως , the morning twilight , Macr. S. 1, 17, 37, p. 292 Bip.; Paul. ex Fest. p. 121 Müll.

Lўcŏphron.opening: , = Λυκόφρων , Lycophron of Chalcis, in Eubœa, the author of Cassandra, an Alexandrine grammarian and tragedian of the time of Ptolemy Philadelphus : utque cothurnatum periisse Lycophrona narrant, Ov. Ib. 531 : latebrae…

lўcophthalmos.opening: , = λυκόφθαλμος (wolf's-eye), a precious stone , Plin. 37, 11, 72, § 187 ; cf. Isid. 16, 15, 20 .

lўcopsis.opening: (al. ), , , = λυκοψίς , the wild bugloss , a plant resembling the alkanet, Plin. 27, 11, 73, § 97 .

Lycōreus.opening: a son of Apollo , Hyg. Fab. 161 .

Lўcōrĭas.opening: , = Λυκωριάς , a seanymph, daughter of Nereus and Doris , Verg. G. 4, 339 ; Hyg. Fab. praef.

Lўcōris.opening: ( acc. -orida, Ov. A. A. 3, 537 ; voc. Lycori, Verg. E. 10, 42 ; Mart. 1, 102, 1 ), , also called Cythere, a freedwoman of the senator Volumnius Eutrapelus, the mistress of Cornelius Gallus, and afterwards of Marc…

Lўcormas.opening: , = Λυκόρμας , a river of Ætolia , Ov. M. 2, 245 ; afterwards called Chrysorrhoas, Hyg. Fab. 242 .

Lўcortas.opening: , = Λυκόρτας , a general (strategos, στρατηγός ) of the Achæan League , Liv. 39, 35 ; 36 .

lўcos.opening: , = λύκος , a kind of spider : araneus, et maxume qui lycos vocatur, Plin. 30, 6, 17, § 52 ; acc. lycon, id. 30, 11, 30, § 104 .

Lўcōtas.opening: one of the Centaurs at the wedding of Pirithoüs , Ov. M. 12, 350 .— A fictitious name of a man , probably meaning Postumius, Prop. 4 (5), 3, 1 .

Lўcŏtherses.opening: a king of Illyria, whom his wife Agave, the daughter of Cadmus, murdered, in order to give the kingdom to her father , Hyg. Fab. 184 ; 340 ; 254 .

Lyctus.opening: or , , , = Λύκτος , a city of Crete, east of Gnossus, a colony of the Lacedæmonians , Mel. 2, 7, 12 ; Plin. 4, 12, 20, § 59 .—Hence, , , adj., of or belonging to Lyctus, Lyctian, Cretan : Lyctius Idomeneus, Verg. A. 3,…

Lўcurgus.opening: , = Λυκοῦργος . Son of Dryas, king of the Edones, who prohibited the worship of Bacchus to his subjects, and ordered all the vines to be destroyed , Ov. M. 4, 22 ; Prop. 4, 16, 23 ; Stat. Th. 4, 386 ; Hor. C. 2, 19, 16…

Lўcus.opening: or , , , = Λύκος . Son of Pandion, king of Lycia , Mela, 1, 15, 1.— A Theban, who, when Hercules descended into the Lower World, took possession of the sovereignty in Thebes , Hyg. Fab. 31 and 32. — One of the Centaurs…

Lȳdē.opening: , = Λύδη , the wife of the poet Antimachus of Claros, who attempted to console himself for her death by an elegiac poem which he named Lyde : Clario Lyde dilecta poëtae, Ov. Tr. 1, 6, 1 .— The name of a female…

Lȳdĭa.opening: , = Λυδία , a country in Asia Minor, the capital of which was Sardis, the fabled original land of the Etruscans , Plin. 5, 29, 30, § 110 ; Varr. R. R. 3, 17, 4 ; Cic. Fl. 27, 65 ; Liv. 38, 39, 16 et saep.—Hence, , ,…

Lygdămus.opening: a slave of Cynthia, the mistress of Propertius , Prop. 3, 4 (4, 5), 2; 4 (5), 7, 43.

lygdĭnus.opening: adj. , = λύγδινος , of white marble : horoscopus, Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. M. 1, 3 .—Esp.: lygdinus lapis, a dazzling white marble found in the island of Paros, Plin. 36, 8, 13, § 62 ; Isid. Orig. 16, 5, 8 (the same…

lygdos.opening: , = λύγδος , a white stone , = lygdinus lapis: candida, Mart. 6, 13, 3 : vacua, id. 6, 42, 21 .

lўgos.opening: , = λύγος , a plant, the chaste tree, agnus castus, Abraham's balm (in late Lat. vitex), Plin. 24, 9, 38, § 59 .

Lўgos.opening: , = Λύγος , an ancient name of Byzantium : oppidum Byzantium ... antea Lygos dictum, Plin. 4, 11, 18, § 46 ; Aus. de Clar. Urb. Carm. 1, 14 .

lympha.opening: νύμφη , water; esp. clear river or spring water ( poet. ): lymphae puteales, Lucr. 6, 1178 : fluviali spargere lympha, Verg. A. 4, 635 ; Ov. M. 2, 459 : vulnera lymphis abluere, id. ib. 13, 531 .— Also, the water in…

lymphācĕus.opening: adj. lympha , clear as water, clear as crystal , Mart. Cap. 6, § 569 .

lymphātĭcus.opening: adj. lympha; cf. hydrophobia; hence, in gen. , distracted, frantic, panic-struck : pavor, a panic, Liv. 10, 28, 10 ; 7, 17, 3 : metus, Sen. Ep. 13, 9 : somnia, Plin. 26, 8, 34, § 52 : elleborum medetur melancholicis,…

lympho.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
lympho.opening: v. a. and n. lympha . To water, dilute with water : admixto vino lymphato, id est, aqua temperato, Cael. Aur. Tard. 4, 3, 68 .— To drive out of one's senses, to distract with fear, to make mad : urbem, Val. Fl. 3, 47 :…

lymphor.opening: id. , water : impermixtum lymphorem, Lucil. ap. Non. 212, 4 .

Lyncaestē.opening: one of Actæon's hounds , Hyg. Fab. 181 .

Lyncestae.opening: , = Λυγκησταί , a people in the south-western part of Macedonia , Liv. 45, 30, 6 ; Plin. 4, 10, 17, § 35 .— Hence, , , adj., Lyncestian : amnis, Ov. M. 15, 329 ; v. Sen. Q. N. 3, 20 fin. — , , adj., Lyncestian : aqua,…

Lynceus.opening: ( ), ( gen. Lyncei, dissyl., Hor. S. 1, 2, 90 Orell. ad loc.; voc. Lynceu, Prop. 3, 32, 9 ), , = Λυγκεύς , a Messenian, and one of the Argonauts, brother of Idas, and son of Aphareus, famed for the sharpness of his…

lyncūrĭon.opening: or , , , = λυγκούριον , a hard, transparent gem, which, according to the opinion of the ancients, was formed of lynxes' urine; prob. the hyacinth or tourmaline , Plin. 8, 38, 57, § 137 ; 37, 2, 11, § 34 ; 37, 3, 13, §…

Lyncus.opening: , = Λύγκος . Masc., a Scythian king, who attempted the life of his guest, Triptolemus, and was changed by Ceres into a lynx , Ov. M. 5, 650 ; Hyg. Fab. 259 .— Fem., a city of Macedonia, the capital of the Lyncestae (q.…

lynx.opening: , = λύγξ , a lynx : lynces Bacchi variae (Bacchus was drawn by a team of lynxes), Verg. G. 3, 264 : maculosae tegmine lyncis, id. A. 1, 323 : lyncibus ad caelum vecta Ariadna tuis, Prop. 3, 15, 8 (4, 16, 18): colla…

lўo.opening: v. a. λύω , to make liquid, to liquefy : ptisanam, Apic. 4, 4 : pulpa lyata, id. 5, 1 .

lўra.opening: , = λύρα , a lute, lyre , a stringed instrument resembling the cithara, fabled to have been invented by Mercury and presented to Apollo, Hyg. Astr. 2, 7 : curvae lyrae parens, Hor. C. 1, 10, 6 : Threiciam digitis…

Lyrcēĭus.opening: or , , adj., Lyrcean, of or near the Mount Lyrceum ( Λύρκειον ) between Arcadia and Argolis : tellus, Val. Fl. 4, 355 : Lyrcea arva, Ov. M. 1, 598 .

Lyrcīus.opening: or ( ), , , a fountain in the Peloponnesus : aret Lyrcius (Lyrceus), Stat. Th. 4, 711 .

lўrĭcen.opening: lyra-cano , a luteplayer, lyrist : fidicen, lyricen, cornicen, liticen, Aug. de Gramm. p. 1977 P.; cf.: lyricen, λυρῳδός , Gloss. Philox.

lўrĭcus.opening: adj. lyra , of or belonging to the lute or lyre, lyric : lyrici soni, Ov. F. 2, 94 : vates, Hor. C. 1, 1, 35 : senex, i. e. Anacreon, Ov. Tr. 2, 364 : regnator lyricae cohortis, i. e. Pindar, Stat. S. 4, 7, 5 .— Subst.…

lўristes.opening: , = λυριστής , a luteplayer, lyrist : audisses lectorem, vel lyristen, Plin. Ep. 1, 15, 2 ; 9, 17, 3 ; 9, 36, 4 ; Sid. Ep. 8, 11 .

Lyrnēsus.opening: ( ), , , = Λυρνησός , a town in Troas, the birthplace of Briseis , Plin. 5, 30, 32, § 122 : Lyrnessi domus alta, Verg. A. 12, 547 .—Hence, ( ), , adj., Lyrnesian : moenia, Ov. M. 12, 108 ; 13, 176 ; id. H. 3, 45 .— ( ),…

lyron.opening: , = λύρον , a plant, also called alisma, Plin. 25, 10, 77, § 124 .

Lўsander.opening: , = Λύσανδρος . A celebrated Spartan general, conqueror of the Athenians , Cic. Off. 1, 22, 76 ; 1, 30, 109 ; Nep. Lys. — An ephor in Sparta, banished for injustice , Cic. Off. 2, 23, 80 .

lysas.opening: a plant, also called artemisia, App. Herb. 10 .

Lўsĭădes.opening: , = Λυσιάδης , an Athenian, son of the philosopher Phædrus , Cic. Phil. 5, 5, 13 .

Lўsĭas.opening: , = Λυσίας . Son of Cephalus, a famous orator of Athens : tum fuit Lysias, quem jam prope audeas oratorem perfectum dicere, Cic. Brut. 9, 35 ; cf. id. ib. 85, 293 ; id. de Or. 1, 54, 231 ; id. Or. 9, 29 ; Quint. 10, 1,…

lysĭmăchĭa.opening: , = λυσιμαχία , a plant , Lysimachia vulgaris, Linn.; Plin. 26, 12, 82, § 131 ; 26, 14, 87, § 141 .

Lȳsĭmăchīa.opening: , or , = Λυσιμάχεια , a city in Thrace , now Examili , Mela, 2, 2, 6; Plin. 4, 11, 18, § 48 ; Liv. 32, 34, 6 al. —Hence, , , , the Lysimachians , Liv. 33, 38, 12 .

lȳsĭmăchos.opening: , = λυσίμαχος , a precious stone with golden veins , Plin. 37, 10, 62, § 62 .

Lȳsĭmăchus.opening: , = Λυσίμαχος , one of the generals of Alexander the Great, afterwards king of Thrace, and founder of Lysimachia , Cic. Tusc. 1, 43, 102 ; 5, 40, 117 ; Plin. 8, 16, 61, § 143 ; Just. 17, 1 .— An Acarnanian, instructor…

Lўsĭnŏē.opening: , = Λυσινόη , a city of Pisidia , Liv. 38, 15 .

Lȳsippus.opening: , = Λύσιππος , a celebrated brass-founder of Sicyon, to whom alone Alexander the Great gave permission to cast a statue of him , Cic. Fam. 5, 12, 7 ; id. Brut. 86, 296 ; Hor. Ep. 2, 1, 240 ; Plin. 7, 37, 38, § 125 ; 34,…

lўsis.opening: , = λύσις . A loosening, rupture : trabes frangunt suā lysi structuras, Vitr. 6, 11 .— A talon, ogee , Vitr. 3, 4, 5 ; 5, 6, 6 .

Lȳsis.opening: a small river in Asia Minor , Liv. 38, 15, 3 .

Lўsis.opening: , = Λύσις , a Pythagorean of Tarentum, instructor of Epaminondas , Cic. de Or. 3, 34, 139 ; id. Off. 1, 44, 155 ; Nep. Epam. 2 .

Lȳsistrătus.opening: the brother of Lysippus, who first made statues of gypsum , Plin. 34, 8, 19, § 91 ; 35, 12, 44, § 153 .

Lȳsĭtĕlēs.opening: the name of a man , Plaut. Trin. 5, 2, 28 .

Lystra.opening: , or , , a city in Lycaonia, north-west of Iconium , Vulg. Act. 14, 8; 14, 21.—Hence, , , , the inhabitants of Lystra, Lystrenes , Plin. 5, 32, 42, § 147 .

lytrōtes.opening: , = λυτρωτής , one of the Æons of Valentinus , Tert. adv. Val. 9 .

lytrum.opening: , false read. for lustra; v. 2. lustrum, II. E.

lytta.opening: , = λύττα , a worm under a dog's tongue, said to cause madness , Plin. 29, 5, 32, § 100 .

M.grammar: the twelfth letter of the Latin alphabet
M.opening: (J not being distinguished from I in the class. period), corresponds in form and sound to the Greek M; the Latin language, however, does not combine an initial m with n , as in the Greek μνᾶ, μνῆμα, μνίον, μνόος , etc.;…

Macae.opening: , = οἱ Μάκαι (Herod. 4, 175), a people of Africa in the regio Syrtica, Mela, 3, 8, 6; Plin. 5, 5, 5, § 34 ; Sil. 3, 275 ; 15, 670 .— Sing. : , Sil. 9, 222 . — Acc. Macen, Sil. 2, 60 .

macaerinthē.opening: μάκαιρα , another name for rosmarinus: rosmarinum prophetae macaerinthen, Latini salutarem, App. Herb. 79 .

Măcăreus.opening: ( ), , , = Μακαρεύς . A son of Æolus, who lived in incest with his sister Canace , Ov. H. 11, 21 ; id. Ib. 564 ; Hyg. Fab. 242 .—Hence, , , , = Μακαρηΐς , daughter of Macareus, Isse; acc. Græc. , Macarēïda, Ov. M. 6,…

măcărĭŏtēs.opening: , = μακαριότης (happiness), one of the Æons of Valentinus , Tert. adv. Val. 8 .

Macātus.opening: a Roman surname : M. Livius Macatus, Liv. 27, 34 .

maccis.opening: a fictitious spice , Plaut. Ps. 3, 2, 43 (al. macis).

Maccius.opening: name of a Roman gens. —Hence, T. Maccius Plautus, the celebrated Roman comic poet; v. Plautus.

maccus.opening: cf. Sanscr. mūkas, dumb; Gr. μῶκος, mockery; also Μῶμος , a buffoon, punchinello, macaroni , in the Atellane plays: in Atellana Oscae personae inducuntur, ut maccus, Diom. p. 488 P.; cf. Inscr. Orell. 2621 .— Transf. ,…

Măcĕdo.opening: the name of a usurer , Dig. 14, 6, 1 init. —Hence, , , adj., relating to the usurer Macedo : senatusconsultum, a decree forbidding usurers to recover loans from heirs after they inherited their estates, Dig. 14, 6, 1 .—…

Măcĕdŏnes.opening: ( Gr. acc. Macedonas, Auct. Her. 4, 32, 43 ; Liv. 26, 24, 5 et saep.; Sen. Ben. 5, 6, 1 ; Flor. 2, 8, 5 ; v. Neue, Formenl. 1, 328), , = Μακεδόνες , the Macedonians , Mel. 2, 3, 1 ; Cic. Off. 2, 22, 76 ; Auct. Her. 4,…

Macella.opening: , = Μάκελλα , a town in Sicily, on the Crimisus , Liv. 26, 21 .

măcellārĭus.opening: adj. macellum , of or belonging to the meat-market or provision-market : taberna, Val. Max. 3, 4, 4 : negotiator artis macellariae, Inscr. Grut. 647, 5 : ARS, Inscr. Orell. 4302 .—Hence, Subst. : , , , a meat-seller,…

Măcellīnus.opening: id. , an epithet of the emperor M. Opilius Macrinus, who killed his slaves in his own house , Capit. Macr. 13 .

măcellum.opening: ( , , , Mart. 10, 96, 9 ), root μαχ-; cf. Gr. μάχομαι, to fight; cf. μάχαιρα, μάχη, and mactāre; prop. butcher's stall, shambles; hence, transf. , meat-market, provision-market (where flesh, fish, and vegetables were…

măcĕo.opening: v. n. 1. macer , to be lean, meagre : quia ossa atque pellis totust: ita cura macet, Plaut. Aul. 3, 6, 28 ; cf. Non. 509, 11 .

măcer.opening: adj. Sanscr. root mak, to crush; Gr. μάσσω, knead; μαγεύς, baker; Germ. mager , lean, meagre . Lit. , of living beings (most freq. of animals): taurus, opp. pinguis, Verg. E. 3, 100 : boves, Varr. R. R. 2, 5, 12 ; Juv.…

Măcer.opening: a Roman surname . C. Licinius Macer, an historian , Cic. Leg. 1, 2, 7 ; id. Brut. 67, 238 ; Liv. 4, 7, 12 . — Aemilius Macer, a poet and a friend of Virgil and Ovid , Ov. Tr. 4, 10, 44 ; v. Aemilius.

mācĕrātĭo.opening: macero , a steeping, soaking, maceration : diuturna, Vitr. 6, 2 .— A making soft or tender , Arn. 4, 152 .

māceresco.opening: v. inch. n. [id.], to make soft or tender , Cato, R. R. 92 .

mācĕrĭa.opening: (post-class. form, , only nom. and acc. , Afran. ap. Non. 138 ; Varr. R. R. 3, 5, 11 ; Prud. Hamart. 227 ; Inscr. Grut. 611, 13 ; Inscr. Orell. 4057 ), from macero, to soften; orig. a wall built of soft clay; cf. Gr.…

mācĕrĭātus.opening: adj. maceria , enclosed, walled in : SEPVLCRVM, Inscr Mur 1644, 14.

măcĕrĭes.opening: f [1. macer], distress, affliction (ante-class.), Afran. ap. Non. 138, 13 .

mācĕrĭŏla.opening: dim. maceria , a small enclosure, wall , Inscr. Mur. 492, 2.

mācĕro.opening: v. a. prob. from root μαγ-, μάσσω, to knead; through an adj. mācerus; v. Corss. Ausspr. 1, 395; cf. also măcer , to make soft or tender, to soften by steeping, to soak, steep, macerate (not in Cic. or Cæs.). Lit. :…

măcesco.opening: v. inch. n. [maceo], to grow lean or thin, to become meagre (anteand post-Aug.): (apes) propter laborem asperantur et macescunt, Varr. R. R. 3, 16 ; 1, 55, 1 : constat, arva segetibus ejus (hordei) macescere, become…

Măcĕtae.opening: ( ), , , = Μακέται . (As a less usual form for Μακεδόνες ,) Macedonians : Macetae locupletissimo imperio aucti, Gell. 9, 3, 1 .— Gen. plur. Măcĕtūm. Stat. S. 4, 6, 106 ; Sil. 14, 5 ; Luc. 2, 647 ; Claud. ap. Rufin. 2,…

Machabaeus.opening: a surname of Judas , Vulg. 1 Macc. 1, 2 et saep.—Hence, , , , the Maccabees , Aug. Civ. Dei , 18, 36; Hier. Ep. 7, 6 .

măchaera.opening: , = μάχαιρα , a sword (ante-class. and post-Aug.): machaera atque hasta, Enn. ap Fest. s. v. redhostire, p. 270 Müll. (Trag. v. 212 Müll.): succincti corda machaeris, id. ap. Serv. ad Verg. A. 9, 678 (Ann. v. 392 ib.):…

măchaerĭum.grammar: ii, a false reading for machaeris

măchaerŏphŏrus.opening: , = μαχαιροφόρος , a sword-wearer, a satellite : machaerophoris centum sequentibus, i. e. soldiers armed in the Greek manner, Cic. Q. Fr. 2, 10, 2 .

măchaerŏphyllon.opening: , = μαχαιρόφυλλον (sword-leaf), a plant (al. macrophyllon). App. Herb. 78 .

Măchāon.opening: , = Μαχάων , son of Æsculapius, a famous surgeon of the Greeks before Troy , Cels. praef.; Prop. 2, 1, 61 ; Verg. A. 2, 263 ; Ov. P. 3, 4, 7 al. — Transf. , in plur., surgeons, physicians : quid tibi cum medicis?…

māchilla.opening: dim. machina , a little machine : e machillā sustuli, Petr. 74, 13 dub. (al. e machina illam sustuli).

Machĭmus.opening: , = Μάχιμος , the name of one of Actæon's hounds , Hyg. Fab. 181 .

māchĭna.opening: = μηχανή , a machine , i. e. any artificial contrivance for performing work, an engine, fabric, frame, scaffolding, staging, easel, warlike engine, military machine , etc. Lit. In gen.: moles et machina mundi, Lucr. 5,…

māchĭnālis.opening: adj. machina , of or belonging to machines (post-Aug.): scientia, Plin. 7, 37, 38, § 125 : saxa machinali pondere, Aus. Ep. 21, 34 .

māchĭnāmen.opening: machinor , a contrivance, device , Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 9, 14 .

māchĭnāmentum.opening: id. , a machine, engine; an instrument, organ (perh. not ante-Aug.; not in Cic. or Cæs.). Lit. : machinamenta alia quatiendis muris portabant, military engines, Liv. 24, 34 : suspensum et nutans machinamentum, Tac. H.…

māchĭnārĭus.opening: adj. machina , of or belonging to machines, machine- (postclass.). Adj. : mola, which is worked by an animal by means of a machine, App. M. 7, p. 194, 20 : asinus, Dig. 33, 7, 12 : mensor, a surveyor, ib. 11, 6, 7 :…

māchĭnātĭo.opening: machinor , artificial contrivance, mechanism, machinery (class.). Lit. : cum machinatione quadam moveri aliquid videmus, ut sphaeram, Cic. N. D. 2, 38, 97 : data est quibusdam bestiis machinatio quaedam, et sollertia,…

māchĭnātor.opening: machinor , a maker of machines, a machinist, an engineer, architect (class.). Lit. , of Archimedes: inventor ac machinator bellicorum tormentorum, Liv. 24, 34 : machinatores, qui pegmata per se surgentia excogitant,…

māchĭnātrix.opening: machinator , an inventress : malorum facinorum, Sen. Med. 266 .

māchĭnātus.opening: machinor , a contrivance, artifice, device (post-class.): suo machinatu, App. Mag. p. 321, 33 ; Sid. Ep. 5, 6 .

māchĭnor.opening: v. dep. a. [machina], to contrive skilfully, to devise, design, frame, invent (class). In gen.: incredibile est, quantā operā machinata natura sit, Cic. N. D. 2, 59, 149 : qui haec machinatus est, id. Univ. 3 : haec duo…

māchĭnōsus.opening: adj. id. , skilfully constructed : navigium, Suet. Ner. 34 .

māchĭnŭla.opening: dim. id. , a little machine , Paul. Nol. Carm. 26, 458 ; Paul. ex Fest. p. 107, 3 ; p. 147, 2.

māchĭo.opening: id. , one who works on a scaffold, a mason : machiones dicti a machinis, quibus insistunt propter altitudinem parietum, Isid. Orig. 19, 8, 2 (hence, Fr. macon; Engl. mason).

Machlўes.opening: a fabled people of Africa : supra Nasamonas confinesque illis Machlyas androgynos esse utriusque naturae, Plin. 7, 2, 2, § 15 .

macĭa.opening: a plant, called by the Greeks ἀναγαλλίς , pimpernel , Marc. Emp. 1 .

măcĭes.opening: maceo , leanness, thinness, meagreness (class.). Lit. Of living beings and the parts of their bodies: profectus est (ad bellum) Hirtius consul: at quā imbecillitate? quā macie? Cic. Phil. 7, 4, 12 ; id. Agr. 2, 34, 93 :…

măcĭlentus.opening: adj. macies , lean, thin, meagre (ante- and post-class.): macilento ore, Plaut. Capt. 3, 4, 114 : macilentis malis, id. As. 2, 3, 20 : macilenti, macie tenuati, Paul. ex Fest. p. 125 Müll.: solum, poor, barren, Pall.…

măcĭo.opening: v. a. id. , to make lean, thin , or meagre, to reduce (post-class.): Caspii maris fauces mirum in modum maciantur imbribus, crescunt aestibus, Sol. 15, 18 ; cf.: macio διακναίω , Gloss. Philox.

macir.opening: , = μάκερ , a kind of red spicy bark brought from India , Plin. 12, 8, 16, § 32 .

măco.opening: v. a. cf. macellum , to maul, beat, hack : namque nullum Pejus macit homonem quamde mare saevum, Naev. ap. Paul. ex Fest. p. 397 Müll. ad loc.: ut nunc saepe boves lucae ferro male mactae Diffugiunt, Lucr. 5, 1339 Munro…

măcor.opening: maceo , leanness, meagreness (ante-class. for macies): corpus meum tali maerore, aegrore, macore senet, Pac. ap. Non. 137, 1 (Trag. Rel. v. 275 Rib.); cf. Prisc. 699 P.

Mā^cra.opening: A river in Italy, between Liguria and Etruria , now Magra , Plin. 3, 5, 7, § 48 ; Liv. 39, 32, 2 ; 40, 41, 3 .— Macra Cōmē, Gr. Μακρὰ κώμη , a town in Locris, on the border of Thessaly , Liv. 32, 13, 10 .

mā^cresco.opening: v. inch. n. [1. macer], to grow lean, meagre : algor eas et famis macrescere cogit, Varr. R. R. 2, 5, 15 ; 3, 5, 3 : macrescit pecus, Col. 6, 3, 1 : macrescunt animalia, Veg. Vet. 1, 7, 2 : invidus alterius macrescit…

Macri Campi.opening: (also , Varr. R. R. 2 praef. § 6, and Liv. 41, 18 ), = Μακροὶ Κάμποι , a region in Gallia Cispadana, on the river Macra, in the vicinity of Parma and Modena , Varr. R. R. 2 praef. § 6; Col. 7, 2, 3 ; Liv. 41, 18, 5 ;…

Macria.opening: a small island near Eubœa , Plin. 2, 88, 90, § 204 .

macrĭcŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [1. macer], lean , Varr. L. L. 8, 40, § 79 Müll.

Mā^crīnus.opening: the name of a man . A friend of the poet Persius , Pers. 2, 1 .— A Roman emperor , Aus. Caes. 23 .

Mā^cris.opening: , = Μακρις , the name of several islands . In the Ægean Sea, near Ionia , Liv. 27, 13 ; 28 ; 29 .— An ancient name of the island of Eubœa , Plin. 4, 12, 21, § 64 .— Of Chios , Plin. 5, 31, 38, § 136 . — Of Icarus ,…

măcrĭtas.opening: 1. macer , leanness, poorness, thinness (post-Aug. and rare for macies): arenae, Vitr. 2, 4 : soli, Pall. Oct. 1, 2 .

mā^crĭtūdo.opening: id. , leanness, thinness, meagreness (for macies): ossa atque pellis sum, miser macritudine, Plaut. Capt. 1, 2, 26 Weise (1, 2, 32 Brix and Fleck., who read aegritudine; acc. to Non. 136, 2 ).

Macrŏbĭi.opening: ( , Schol. Juv. 10, 150 ), , , = Μακρόβιοι (longlived). A people of Æthiopia , Mel. 3, 9, 1 ; Plin. 6, 30, 35, § 190 ; 7, 2, 2, § 28 ; Val. Max. 8, 13, 5 ext. — The inhabitants of Apollonia, in Macedonia , Plin. 4, 10,…

Măcrŏbĭus.opening: , = Μακρόβιος (living long): Aurelius Macrobius Ambrosius Theodosius, a Roman grammarian at the end of the fourth century, author of a commentary on Cicero's Somnium Scipionis, and of a treatise entitled Convivia…

Macrŏcĕphăli.opening: , = Μακρο, κέφαλοι (i. e. people with great heads ), a people of Pontus , Mela, 1, 19, 11; Plin. 6, 4, 4, § 11 .

macrŏchēra.opening: , = μακρόχειρα , having long sleeves, long-sleeved : tunica, Lampr. Alex. Sev. 33, 4 .

Măcrŏchīr.opening: , = Μακρόχειρ , Longhand , = Lat. Longimanus, a surname of king Artaxerxes , Nep. Reg. 1, 3 sq. ; Amm. 30, 8, 4 .

măcrŏcōlum.opening: and , , , = μακρόκωλον , large-sized paper, royal paper , Cic. Att. 16, 3, 1 ; 13, 25, 3 ; Plin. 13, 12, 24, § 80 .

Macrocremnii montes.opening: a chain of mountains near the Dniester , Plin. 4, 12, 26, § 82 .

macrŏlŏgĭa.opening: , = μακρολογία , tediousness in speech (Lat. longiloquium), Pomp. Gram. Com. in Donat. de Barb. 3, 1, p. 293 Keil (as Greek, trans., longior quam oportet sermo, Quint. 8, 3, 53 ).

mactātĭo.opening: id. , a slaying, killing (post-class.): innoxiorum animantium mactatio, Arn. 7, 213 ; Isid. Orig. 6, 19, 31 .

mactātor.opening: id. , a slayer, murderer : mactator senum, Sen. Troad. 1002 .

mactātus.opening: id. , a slaying, killing : mactatu parentis, Lucr. 1, 99 .

macto.opening: (old form of perf. subj. mactassint, Enn., Afran., and Pompon. ap. Non. 342, 12 sq. ), v. freq. a. macto, kindr. to Sanscr. makh, mah; intens. māmahyata, to slaughter, sacrifice; maha, victim; the ct in macto like…

mactus.opening: P. a. of maco, q. v., and cf. macto fin.

măcŭla.opening: for malocula, malcula, dim.; cf. Sanscr. mala, dirt , a spot, mark, stain (class.). Lit. In gen., Plin. 37, 10, 56, § 155 : (bos) maculis insignis et albo, i. e. with white spots, Verg. G. 3, 56 : maculis albis equus,…

Măcŭla.opening: a Roman surname , e. g. of Q. Pompeius, Cic. Fam. 6, 19, 1 .

măcŭlātĭo.opening: maculo , a spotting; a spot, stain (post-class.). Lit. : cutem maculationibus convariare, App. Mag. p. 306, 14 .— Trop. : aliquā infamiae maculatione pollutus, stain , Firm. Math. 3, 15, 3.

măcŭlo.opening: v. a. 1. macula , to make spotted, to spot, speckle, variegate . Lit. In gen. (only poet. ), to stain, tinge, dye : telas maculare ostro, Val. Fl. 4, 368 : et multo maculatum murice tigrim, id. 6, 704 .— In partic., to…

măcŭlōsus.opening: adj. id. , full of spots, spotted, speckled, dappled, mottled, variegated . Lit. In gen. ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): maculosae tegmine lyncis, Verg. A. 1, 323 : color, Col. 6, 37, 6 : marmor, Plin. 36, 6, 5, § 44 :…

Mădărus.opening: , = μαδαρὀς (bald), a surname jestingly given to C. Matius, on account of his baldness , Cic. Att. 14, 2, 1 ; cf. Calvena.

Madaura.opening: , and , , , a city in Numidia , now Ayedrah , Aug. Conf. 2, 3 .

Madaurensis.opening: adj., of or belonging to the city of Madaura (on the borders of Numidia and Gætulia, not the city mentioned in the preced. art.), Madauran : Appuleius Madaurensis, Aug. Ep. 49 .—Hence, subst. : , , , an inhabitant of…

mădĕfăcĭo.opening: v. a. ; in pass. : , madeo, facio , to make wet, to wet, moisten, to soak, drench, water , etc. In gen.: lanam aceto et nitro, Plin. 32, 7, 25, § 77 : amarantus madefactus aquā revirescit, id. 21 , 8, 23, § 47: radix in…

mădĕfacto.opening: v. freq. a. madefacio , to wet, moisten, water, irrigate (post-class.): humum, Ven. Carm. 1, 21, 26.

Madena.opening: a district of Great Armenia, between the rivers Cyrus and Araxes , Eutr. 8, 3 ; Sex. Ruf. Brev. 16 al.

mădĕo.opening: v. n. Gr. μαδάω, to drip; cf. Sanscr. mad-, to be merry; Gr. μαστός and μεστός , to be wet or moist, to drip or flow with any thing (class.). Lit. In gen.: natabant pavimenta vino, madebant parietes, Cic. Phil. 2, 41,…

mădesco.opening: v. inch. n. [madeo], to become moist or wet ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : semiusta madescunt Robora, Verg. A. 5, 697 : tellus Nubibus assi duis pluvioque madescit ab austro, Ov. M. 1, 66 : multā terra madescit…

mădĭdo.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
mădĭdo.opening: v. a. and n. madidus , to make wet or moist, to wet, moisten (post-class.). In gen. Act. : proluvie linerent et madidarent se suā, Arn. 2, 70 : madidari ex imbribus arva, id. 1, 3 : madidatae spongiae, App. M. 8, p.…

mădĭdus.opening: adj. madeo , moist, wet, soaked, drenched (rare until after the Aug. per.). Lit. In gen.: fasciculus epistolarum aquā madidus, * Cic. Q. Fr. 2, 12, 4 : spiritus, Plin. 31, 7, 39, § 79 : madidi myrrhā capilli, Ov. M. 5,…

mădor.opening: madeo , moisture, wetness (very rare; not in Cic. or Cæs.): ingens terror erat, ne ex latere nova munimenta madore infirmarentur, Sall. Fragm. ap. Non. 138, 6 (Hist. 3, 26): terrae, Arn. 5, 185 : quoad me urinae madore…

mădos.opening: , or , , , = μάδος . A kind of grape-vine, white grape , = vitis alba, Plin. 23, 1, 16, § 21 .— A reading in Plin. 25, 7, 37, § 75 , for mallon, q. v.

mădulsa.opening: madeo , a drunken man : nunc probe abeo madulsa, Plaut. Ps. 5, 1, 7 ; cf.: madulsa, ebrius, a Graeco μαδᾶν deductum, vel quia madidus satis a vino, Paul. ex Fest. p. 126, 5 Müll.

Madytos.opening: ( ), , , = Μαδυτός , a seaport town in the Thracian Chersonese , now Maitos , Mel. 2, 2, 7 ; Liv. 31, 16 ; 33, 38 .—Hence, , , , the inhabitants of Madytos , Liv. 38, 40 .

Maeander.opening: ( or ), , , = Μαιανδρος , a river, proverbial for its winding course, which rises in Great Phrygia, flows between Lydia and Caria, and falls, near Miletus, into the Icarian Sea , now Mendere Su; nom. Maeander, Liv. 38,…

Maecēnas.opening: Tuscan, perh. Maecnatial; v. Sil. 10, 40; Müll. Etrusk. 1, p. 404; 415 : C. Cilnius Maecenas, a Roman knight, descended, on the mother's side, from the Arretinian gens of the Maecenates (and on the father's side from…

Maecĭus.opening: ( ), , , the name of a place in Latium : nec procul ab Lanuvio (ad Maecium is locus dicitur) castra oppugnare est adortus, Liv. 6, 2, 8 (dub.; Weissenb. ad Mecium).—Hence, , , , a tribe , Liv. 8, 17, 11 ; 29, 37 ; Cic.…

Maedi.opening: ( ), , , = Μαῖδοι , a Thracian people on the borders of Macedonia , Plin. 4, 1, 1, § 3 ; 4, 11, 18, § 40 ; Liv. 26, 25, 6 ; 28, 5 ; Eutr. 5, 7 .—Hence, ( ), , adj. , = Μαιδικός , of or belonging to the Mædi.—Subst. : ,…

Maelĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens, of which the most celebrated member is Sp. Maelius, who, under suspicion of aiming at kingly power, was slain, at the command of the dictator L. Quinctius Cincinnatus, by the magister equitum…
