mălĕdictĭo.opening: maledico , an evil-speaking, reviling, abuse (very rare): maledictio nihil habet propositi praeter contumeliam, Cic. Cael. 3, 6 ; Arn. 4, 147 . — Esp., the act of cursing, a curse, malediction (freq. in eccl. Lat.):…

mălĕdictĭto.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to revile or abuse vehemently or repeatedly , Plaut. Trin. 1, 2, 62 (also separately, male dictitatur).

mălĕdictor.opening: a reviler, slanderer : maledictores dicebantur ab antiquis, qui nunc maledici, Paul. ex Fest. p. 152, 8 ; Tert. p. 154 Müll.

mălĕdictus.opening: P. a. , v. maledico, fin. B.

mălĕdĭcus.opening: adj. maledico , foul-mouthed, abusive, scurrilous, slanderous (class.): conviciator maledicus, Cic. Mur. 6, 13 : homines, Auct. Her. 2, 8, 12 : maledicum esse in aliquem, Quint. 4, 1, 10 . — Transf. , of inanim. and…

mălĕ-făber.opening: adj. malefaber , contriving evil, cunning, crafty, insidious (post-class.): suadelae, Prud. Ham. 716 .

mălĕfăcĭo.opening: (or separately, ), , v. n. male-facio , to do evil, harm, mischief to any one, to injure : alicui, Plaut. Mil. 2, 2, 11 : neque tu verbis solves umquam, quod mi re male feceris, Ter. Ad. 2, 1, 10 : tibi, Vulg. 1 Reg.…

mălĕfactĭo.opening: malefacio, properly, an injuring; hence , syncope, fainting, swooning , Macer. de Herb. Carm. 2, 4.

mălĕfactor.opening: id. , an evildoer, malefactor (Plautin. and post-class.): malefactorem amitti satiu'st quam relinqui beneficum, i. e. it is better to let a malefactor go unpunished than to be ungrateful towards a benefactor, Plaut.…

mălĕfĭcentĭa.opening: maleficus , an evil-doing, ill-conduct towards any one, mischievousness; harm, injury (post-Aug.). (tursiones) maxime rostris canicularum maleficentiae assimulati, Plin. 9, 9, 11, § 34 : neque ex beneficentia dei…

mălĕfĭcĭum.opening: maleficus , an evil deed, misdeed, wickedness, offence, crime . Lit. In gen. (class.): ne conscii sint ipsi malefici suis, Plaut. Rud. 4, 7, 21 : conscientia maleficiorum, Cic. Phil. 5, 6, 15 : committere, admittere, to…

mălĕfĭcus.opening: (in MSS. also ), , adj. malefacio , evil-doing, nefarious, vicious, wicked, criminal . Lit. In gen. (class.): homo natura maleficus, et injustus, Cic. Tusc. 5, 20, 57 : malefici sceleratique homines, Cic. Verr. 2, 5,…

mălĕ-fīdus.opening: adj., unfaithful, faithless , Boëth. Cons. Phil. 1, 1; 1, 17. (In class. Lat. always separately, as, capiti male fido, Ov. Ib. 85 .)

mălĕfīo.opening: or , , v. n. malefio , to be injured (late Lat.), Cael. Aur. Signif. Diaet. Pass. 89 .

mălĕsuādus.opening: adj. male-suadeo , ill-advising, seductive ( poet. ): Illa hanc corrumpit mulierem viti malesuada plena, Plaut. Most. 1, 3, 56 Lorenz ad loc. (al. vitilena): interpres, Sid. Ep. 7, 5 .— Transf. , of inanim. and abstr.…

Mălĕventum.opening: ancient name of Beneventum, in the Samnite territory , Liv. 9, 27, 14 ; v. Beneventum.

mălĕvŏlens.opening: ( ), , adj. male-volens , ill-disposed, disaffected, envious, spiteful, malevolent (very rare, and in posit. ante-class.): est miserorum ut malevolentes sint, Plaut. Capt. 3, 4, 51 : ingenium, id. Bacch. 4, 3, 4 .— Sup.…

mălĕvŏlentīa.opening: ( ), , malevolens , ill-will, evil disposition towards any one, dislike, hatred, envy, malevolence (class.): malevolentia est voluptas ex malo alterius sine emolumento suo, Cic. Tusc. 4, 9, 20 : malevolentia in ceteros,…

mălĕvŏlus.opening: ( ), , adj. male-volo , ill-disposed towards any one, disaffected, envious, spiteful, malevolent . Adj. with dat. , or in with acc. (class.): si omnibus est malevolus, Cic. Fam. 2, 17, 7 : Cato in me turpiter fuit…

Mālĭăcus Sĭnus.opening: a gulf south of Thessaly , now Gulf of Zeitouni , Mel. 2, 3, 6 ; Plin. 4, 7, 12, § 27 ; Liv. 27, 30, 3 .— Hence, , , adj., Malian : ager, Liv. 42, 40, 6 .— , , adj., Malian : lympha, Cat. 68, 54 .

mālĭcŏrĭum.opening: malum-corium , the rind of a pomegranate , Plin. 23, 6, 57, § 107 ; Petr. 47 .

mālĭfer.opening: adj. malumfero , apple-bearing ( poet. ): Et quos maliferae despectant moenia Abellae, Verg. A. 7, 740 .

mălignans.opening: P. a. of maligno, q. v.

mălignĭtas.opening: malignus . ill-will, spite, malice, envy, malignity (not in Cic. or Cæs.).— Lit. : malignitati falsa species libertatis inest, Tac. H. 1, 1 : malignitas multo veneno tincta, Sen. Vit. Beat. 18, 2 : interpretantium,…

măligno.opening: v. a. , and , , v. dep. id. , to do or contrive maliciously, to malign (post-class.). Form maligno: consilium super populum tuum, Vulg. Psa. 83, 4 : venena malignantes, i. e. maliciously ejecting, Amm. 22, 15, 26 .—…

mălignōsus.opening: adj., active in mischief , = κακεντρεχής , Gloss. Gr. Lat.

mălignus.opening: adj. for maligenus, malus, and gen-, root of gigno; cf. the opp. benignus , of an evil nature or disposition, ill-disposed, wicked, mischievous, malicious, spiteful, envious, malignant, malign ( poet. and post-Aug.;…

mălĭlŏquax.opening: adj. male-loquax , evil-speaking, slanderous : lingua est maliloquax mentis indicium malae, P. Syrus in Mim. (cf. id. Sent. App. v. 267 Rib.).

mălĭlŏquĭum.opening: male-loquor , an evil-speaking, slander (post-class.), Tert. Spect. 2 ; id. Apol. 45 .

mălĭlŏquus.opening: adj. id. , evilspeaking, slanderous (post-class.): lingua, Hier. Ep. 148, 16 ; Arn. in Psa. 11 .

mālĭnus.opening: adj. , = μήλινος , of or belonging to an apple-tree : pruna, Plin. 15, 13, 12, § 42 .— Of the color of apples, apple-green , Plin. 22, 21, 26, § 53 Jan.

mălĭtas.opening: malus; cf. bonitas , evil, harm (post-class.): timor majoris malitatis (al. majoris mali), Dig. 4, 2, 5 ; cf. κακία , malitas, Gloss. Philox.

mălĭtĭa.opening: malus , bad quality, badness . Lit. (post-class.): terrae malitia, Pall. 1, 6 : arboris, unfruitfulness, id. 11, 8 .— Trop. , ill-will, spite, malice (class.): virtutis contraria est vitiositas: sic enim malo, quam…

mălĭtĭōsĭtas.opening: malitiosus , wickedness, knavishness (eccl. Lat.), Tert. adv. Marc. 3, 15 fin.

mălĭtĭōsus.opening: adj. malitia , full of wickedness, wicked, knavish, crafty, malicious . In gen. (class.): homo, Cic. Off. 3, 13, 57 : malitiosissimus, Front. ad M. Caes. 4, 3 .—Of things: juris interpretatio, Cic. Off. 1, 10, 33 .— As…

mallĕātor.opening: malleo, -āre, obs.; v. malleus , a hammerer, hammer-man : balucis, Mart. 12, 57, 9 : malleatores monetae Caesaris, Inscr. Orell. 3229 ; Vulg. Gen. 4, 22 .

mallĕātus.opening: adj. malleo, -āre, obs.; v. malleus , wrought or beaten with a hammer, hammered (post-Aug.): spartum, Col. 12, 19, 4 : libri, Dig. 32, 1, 52, § 5 .

mallĕŏlāris.opening: adj. malleolus , of or belonging to vine-shoots or to young vines (post-Aug.): virga, Col. Arbor. 3, 3 .

mallĕŏlus.opening: dim. malleus , a small hammer or mallet . Lit. , Cels. 8, 3, 29 ; Vulg. Jud. 4, 21 : verba mea sunt quasi malleus conterens petram, id. Jer. 23, 29 .— Transf. A hammershaped slip, a mallet-shoot for planting: malleolus…

mallĕus.opening: a hammer, mallet, maul . Lit. : (navis) excussa malleo, Plaut. Men. 2, 3, 52 : malleorum rostra, Plin. 34, 14, 41, § 144 : stuparius, a swingle-staff, id. 19, 1, 3, § 17 .—Of the maul or axe for felling animals to be…

Mallĭus.opening: cf. Manlius , a Roman proper name . Mallius Glaucia, Cic. Rosc. Am. 7, 18 ; 34, 96 .— Cn. Mallius Maximus, Cic. Planc. 5, 12 ; id. Mur. 17, 36 ; cf. Sall. J. 114 .

mallo.opening: , = μαλλός . The stem of onions (post-class.): mallonem caeparum, id est calamos siccos, unde fasces dependent, Veg. Vet. 2, 60 ; 1, 63 .— A kind of tumor on the knees in animals, Veg. Vet. 2, 48, 1 .

mallon.opening: the Bœotian name for the plant Nymphæa , Plin. 25, 7, 37, § 75 (al. madon).

Mallos.opening: and , , , = Μαλλός , a city in Cilicia , Mel. 1, 13, 1 ; Luc. 3, 227 .— Hence, and , , , = Μαλλώτης and Μαλώτης , an inhabitant of Mallus , Varr. R. R. 1, 1, 8 ; Suet. Gram. 2 .

mallus.opening: , = μαλλός , a lock of wool , Cato, R. R. 157 .

mallŭvĭae.opening: manus - lavo , water for washing the hands , Paul. ex Fest. p. 161 Müll.; v. the foll. art.

malluvĭum.opening: id. , a wash-handbasin : malluvium dicitur, quo manus lavuntur malluviae quibus manus sunt lautae (i. e. water to wash the hands in ), perinde ut quibus pedes pelluviae, Paul. ex Fest. p. 160 Müll.

mālo.opening: (old forms, mavolo for malo, Plaut. As. 5, 1, 18 ; id. Curc. 2, 3, 41 ; id. Poen. 1, 2, 88 ; 90 ; id. Rud. 5, 3, 57 ; Ter. Hec. 4, 1, 25 : mavolunt for malunt, Naev. ap. Fest. s. v. stuprum, p. 317 Müll.: mavoluit for…

mālŏbăthrātus.opening: adj. malobathron , anointed with malobathron (postclass.): satrapae pumicati, malobathrati, Sid. Ep. 8, 13 .

mālŏbā^thrĭnus.opening: adj. , = μαλοβάθρινος , made of betel : oleum, Cael. Aur. Acut 3, 3, 24 ; id. Tard. 5, 1, 12 .

mālŏbăthron.opening: ( ), , , = μαλόβαθρον . Lit. , an Indian or Syrian plant, from which a costly oint ment was prepared , perh. betel or base cin namon , Plin. 12, 26, 59, § 129 ; Sid. Carm. 2, 415 .— Transf. , the oil procured from this…

mālŏgrānātum.opening: (better ), , 2. malum-granatum , a pomegranate , Plin. 26, 8, 31, § 49 ; Hier. Com. ad Aggen. 2, 20 ; Vulg. Num. 20, 5 .

mālŏpē.opening: mallows : majorem (malvam) Graeci malopen vocant in sativis, Plin. 20, 21, 84, § 222 (v. malva).

maltha.opening: , = μάλθα , a kind of thick, fatty petroleum from Samosata, fossil tar , the flame of which could be extinguished only with earth, Plin. 2, 104, 108, § 235 .— Transf. , a kind of varnish or cement made of slaked lime…

Malthīnus.opening: (al. ), , maltha, II. , a fictitious name , Hor. S. 1, 2, 25 .

maltho.opening: v. a. id. , to cement, to varnish (post-Aug.), Plin. 36, 24, 58, § 181 , Schol. Juv, 5, 48 Cramer.

Malūgĭnensis.opening: a Roman surname in the gens Cornelia, e. g. M. Cornelius Maluginensis, Liv. 4, 21 .

mālum.opening: , = μῆλον (Doric μᾶ λον ), an apple , i. e. any tree-fruit fleshy on the outside, and having a kernel within (opp. nux); hence, applied also to quinces, pomegranates, peaches, oranges, lemons, etc. In gen., Plin. 15,…

mălus.opening: adj. Sanscr. mala, dirt; Gr. μέλας, black; cf. macula; Germ. mal in Mutter-mal, etc. .— Comp. : pējor, pejus.— Sup. : pessimus, a, um, bad , in the widest sense of the word (opp. bonus), evil, wicked, injurious,…

mālus.opening: by some referred to root mac-; Gr. μακρος; Lat. magnus; but perh. the same word with 2. malus , an upright mast, pole , or beam . In gen.: malos exaequantes altitudinem jugi surrexit, Front. Strat. 3, 8, 3 .— Esp. A…

malva.opening: μαλάχη , mallows : in magnis laudibus malva est utraque, et sativa, et silvestris. Duo genera earum amplitudine folii discernuntur: majorem Graeci malopen vocant in sativis. Alteram ab emoliendo ventre dictam putant…

malvācĕus.opening: adj. malva , of or belonging to mallows, like mallows, mallowshaped (post-Aug.): caulis, Plin. 21, 4, 10, § 19 .

Māmercīnus.opening: of or belonging to a Mamercus, Mamercine , a Roman surname, e. g. L. Aemilius Mamercinus, Liv. 7, 1 .

Māmercus.opening: Mamers for Mars , an Oscan prænomen : Mamercus praenomen Oscum est, ab eo, quod hi Martem Mamertem appellant, Paul. ex Fest. p. 130 Müll.— A Roman surname in the Æmilian gens, who claimed Numa as their ancestor : ridere…

Māmers.opening: the Oscan name for Mars : Mamers Mamertis facit, id est lingua Osca Mars Martis, Paul. ex Fest. p. 131 Müll.; cf. id. s. v. Mamertini, p. 158 ib. The Sabines also gave to Mars the name of Mamers, acc. to Varr. L. L. 5,…

Mămilĭus.opening: root mar-, the shining, splendid one; cf. marmor , name of a Roman gens. Octavius Mamilius, a prince of Tusculum , Liv. 1, 50 .— C. Mamilius Limetanus, a tribune of the people , Sall. J. 40, 1 .— C. Mamilius Vitulus, a…

mămilla.opening: (incorrectly ; cf. Lachm. ad Lucr. vol. 2, p. 36), , dim. mamma , a breast, pap, nipple, teat . Lit. , Vell. 2, 70, 5 ; Juv. 6, 400 : laeva in parte mamillae Nil salit juveni, id. 7, 159 : scrofa triginta clara…

mămillānus.opening: adj. mamilla, having breasts; hence, transf. , full, swelling, protuberant : ficus, Plin. 15, 18, 19, § 69 .

mămillāre.opening: id. , a breast-cloth, stomacher , Mart. 14, 66 in lemm .

mămillāris.opening: adj., of or in the breast : tumores, Dyn. 2, 96.

mamma.opening: , = μάμμα , a breast, pap , esp. of females, rarely of males; also, a teat, dug of animals. Lit. : puero isti date mammam, give him the breast, suckle him, Plaut. Truc. 2, 5, 1 ; id. Trin. 5, 1, 16 : puer in gremio…

Mammaea.opening: the mother of the emperor Alexander Severus , Lampr. Alex. Sev. 3, 1 .—Hence, , , adj., of or belonging to Mammæa, Mammæan , Lampr. Alex. Sev. 57, 7 .

mammālis.opening: adj. mamma , of or for the breasts (post-class.): herba, good for diseases of the breasts, App. Herb. 26 .

mammātus.opening: adj. mamma, having breasts; hence, transf. , furnished with little pipes (post-Aug.), Plin. 35, 12, 46, § 159 , v. Sillig. ad h. l.

mammĕātus.opening: adj. id. , for mammosus, having large breasts, largebreasted, full-breasted (Plautin.): amica Plin. Poen. 1, 2, 181 ; cf. Non. 137, 20 .

mammĭcŭla.opening: dim. id. , a little breast , i. e. a man's breast : ubi mamma mammicula opprimitur, Plaut. Ps. 5, 1, 17 .

mammo.opening: v. n. mamma , to give suck (late Lat.): vae tunc praegnantibus et mammantibus, S. S. Marc. 13, 17, ap. Aug. in Psa. 95, 14 .

mammōnas.opening: , or , , or , , , = μαμμωνᾶς [properly, Syr. ], riches, mammon : non potestis servire Deo et Mammonae, Vulg. Matt. 6, 24 ; id. Luc. 16, 9 ; Aug. Serm. Domin. 2, 14 : mammona iniquitatis prodere, Aug. Civ. Dei , 1, 10, 3.

mammōnĕus.opening: adj. mammonas , greedy of gain, self-interested (eccl. Lat.): fides, Prud. Ham. 429 .

mammōsus.opening: adj. mamma , having large breasts, full-breasted . Lit. : non mammosa, non annosa, non bibosa, Laber. ap. Gell. 3, 12 .—Of animals: canes feminae, Varr. R. R. 2, 9, 5 .— Transf. , full, protuberant : pira, Plin. 15, 15,…

mammothreptus.opening: , = μαμμόθρεπτος , nourished by a nurse , Aug. in Psa. Conc. 30 .

mammŭla.opening: dim. mamma , a little breast or teat . Lit. , Varr. R. R. 2, 3, 2 ; Cels. 7, 26, 1 .— Transf. , in the language of children, little mamma, mammy , Inscr. Orell. 4849 ; 4671 ; cf. mamma, II. B.

Mammŭla.opening: a Roman proper name : M. Cornelius Mammula, Liv. 42, 6 .

mamphūla.opening: a kind of Syrian bread : mamphula appellatur panis Syriaci genus, quod, ut ait Venius, in clibano, antequam percoquatur, decidit in carbones cineremque, Paul. ex Fest. p. 142 Müll.

mamphur.grammar: appellatur loro circumvolutum mediocris longitudinis lignum rotundum, quod circumagunt fabri in operibus tornandis
mamphur.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 132 Müll., a bow-drill [acc. to Scalig. mutilated from μαννοφόρον , wearing a collar].

Māmū^rĭus.opening: , in full, Mamurius Veturius, the maker of the ancilia; v. ancile, Paul. ex Fest. p. 131 Müll.; Ov. F. 3, 391 ; Prop. 4 (5), 2, 61 .(where Müll. Mamurri).—Varro explains in an entirely different manner the expression,…

Māmurra.opening: a Roman knight of Formiæ , praefectus fabrūm in Gaul under Cæsar, who was the first in Rome to cover the walls of his house on the Mons Cœlius with marble, and had none but marble columns in his house , Plin. 36, 6, 7,…

Māna.opening: , and , , , ancient Roman goddesses who presided over the submanes , Mart. Cap. 2, § 164 ; Plin. 29, 4, 14, § 58 .

mānābĭlis.opening: adj. mano , flowing, running; hence, trop., penetrating : frigus, Lucr. 1, 534 .

mānăchus.opening: and , , , = μήναχος , Dor. μάναχος , the ecliptic on a sundial, Vitr. 9, 8 (Schneid. reads menaeus).

mānālis.opening: adj. mano , flowing (ante-class.): manalem fontem dici pro eo, quod aqua ex eo semper manet, Paul. ex Fest. p. 128 Müll.; cf. id. p. 157 ib.: manalem vocabant lapidem etiam (cf. another signif. in the foll. art.) petram…

Mānālis.opening: adj. Manes , of or belonging to the Manes : Manalem lapidem putabant esse ostium Orci, per quod animae inferorum ad superos manarent, qui dicuntur manes, Paul. ex Fest. p. 128, 14 Müll. (perhaps from the same origin as…

mānāmen.opening: mano , a flowing : bivio refluus manamine pontus, i. e. in ebb and flood, Aus. Mosell. 32 .

mānātĭo.opening: id. , a flowing, flowing out (post-Aug.), Front. Aquaed. 65 ; 110 ; 122 .

manceps.opening: manus-capio , a purchaser of any thing at a public auction, a renter, farmer, contractor , etc. (syn.: redemtor, exactor). Lit. : manceps dicitur, qui quid a populo emit conducitve, quia manu sublata significat se…

Mancĭa.opening: a Roman surname , e. g. Q. Mucius Mancia, Cic. Off. 1, 30, 109 .

Mancīnus.opening: a Roman proper name , e. g. C. Hostilius Mancinus, a consul who was delivered up to the Numantines, on the refusal of the Roman people to ratify the dishonorable treaty of peace which he had made with them , Cic. Rep.…

mancĭŏla.opening: dim. manus , a little hand (ante-class.), Laev. ap. Gell. 17, 7 .

mancĭpātĭo.opening: ( ), , mancipo , a making over, delivery, transfer of a thing to another; one of the modes of acquiring possession by the Roman civil law; hence, also, for purchase : qui mancipio accipit, apprehendere id ipsum, quod ei…

mancĭpātus.opening: mancipo . A sale (post-Aug.): in mancipatum venire, Plin. 9, 35, 60, § 124 .— The office or business of a public farmer (in jurid. Lat.), Cod. Th. 8, 5, 36; so ib. 7, 9 .

mancĭpĭum.opening: ( ), (the contr. form of the gen. , mancipi, like imperi, ingeni, etc., predominates in jurid. lang.), manceps , a taking by hand; hence, law t. t., the formal acceptance, the taking possession of a purchase and sale…

mancĭpo.opening: ( ), , v. a. manceps . To make over or deliver up as property by means of the formal act of purchase (mancipium; v. mancipium init. ), to dispose of, transfer, alienate, sell (not in Cic.; for the true reading ap. Cic.…

mancus.opening: adj. Sanscr. man-āk, little; cf. Germ. mangeln , maimed, infirm (class.). Lit. , in a limb or member, esp. in the hand: sciendum, scaevam non esse morbosum, praeterquam si, imbecillitate dextrae, validius sinistra…

mandātārĭus.opening: mandatum , one to whom a charge or commission is given, an attorney, agent, mandatory (jurid. Lat.), Dig. 17, 1, 10, § 11 dub. (al. mandatores).

mandātēla.opening: id. , a charge, the intrusting of a commission , Gai. Inst. 2, 104 ; Prisc. 622 P.

mandātĭo.opening: 1. mando , a charge, commission (jurid. Lat.): mandatione, Dig. 41, 1, 37 init. (dub.; al. traditione).

mandātīvus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to a charge or command, mandative : modus, a name given by some grammarians to the future used imperatively (e. g. leges for lege), Diom. p. 330 P.

mandātor.opening: id. , one who gives a charge or commission, a mandator . Lit. (post-class.): quod extra mandatum egit, non praejudicet mandatori, Gai. Inst. 1, 17 fin. ; Dig. 3, 2, 20 ; 17, 1, 22 ; Tert. adv. Marc. 3, 2 : caedis, Paul.…

mandātōrĭus.opening: adj. mandator , of or belonging to a mandator, mandatory (post-class.): nomine, Cod. Just. 8, 41, 19 al.

mandātrix.opening: id. , she that charges or commands (post-class.): operum, Claud. IV. Cons. Hon. 235 .

mandātus.opening: (only in abl. sing. ), 1. mando , a command, mandate (class.): mandatu Caesenniae, Cic. Caecin. 7, 19 : Sullae, id. Sull. 23, 65 : praetoris, Suet. Caes. 7 : creditorum, Dig. 17, 1, 32 : agitur mandatu meo, Cic. Fam. 2,…

Mandēla.opening: a town in the Sabine territory, near the Digentia , Hor. Ep. 1, 18, 105 .—Hence, , , adj., of or belonging to Mandela : MASSA, Inscr. Orell. 104 .

mandĭbŭla.opening: , or , , 2. mando , a jaw (post-class.), Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 6, 69 : cibaria confecta mandibulis, id. S. 7, 4, 14 ; Isid. 11, 1, 45 .

mando.opening: 2. mando , a glutton, gormandizer : mandonum gulae, Lucil. ap. Non. 17, 16 ; cf. manduco.

Mandŏnĭus.opening: , = Μανδόνιος , a general in Spain, who sided with the Romans in the second Punic war , Liv. 22, 21 ; 28, 31 sq.

mandra.opening: , = μάνδρα , a stall or pen for cattle , etc. ( poet. ). Lit. : mulorum, Mart. 5, 22, 7 .— Transf. A herd of cattle : stantis convicia mandrae, abuse from the herd penned up or stopped , i. e. from the drovers, Juv. 3,…

mandrăgŏras.opening: , = μανδραγόρας , a plant, mandrake : mandragoras illitus, Plin. 25, 13, 110, § 175 ; so id. 25, 13, 94, § 147 ; Col. 10, 20 .

Mandrŏpŏlis.opening: , = Μανδρόπολις , a city in Great Phrygia , Liv. 38, 15 .

Mandūbĭi.opening: a people of Gallia Celtica, whose chief city was Alesia, Caes. B. G. 7, 68 ; 78 .

mandūcātĭo.opening: 1. manduco , a chewing (eccl. Lat.), Aug. Tract. in Joann. 27 .

mandūcātor.opening: id. , a chewer (eccl. Lat.), Aug. Tract. in Joann. 27 .

mandūco.opening: 1. manduco , a glutton, gormandizer (post-class.), Pompon. ap. Non. 17, 15 (Com. Rel. v. 112 Rib.); App. M. 6, p. 186, 41 .

mandūcus.opening: 1. manduco , a glutton (ante-class.). Lit. , Pompon. ap. Non. 17, 15 .— Transf. , a ludicrous masked figure representing a person chewing , used in processions and in comedies to excite merriment: manduci effigies in…

Mandūrĭa.opening: a city of the Salentines, in Lower Italy, between Aletium and Tarentum , still called Manduria , Plin. 2, 103, 106, § 226 ; Liv. 27, 15, 4 .

māne.opening: (archaic abl. mani, like luci, vesperi: a mani ad vesperum, Plaut. Most. 3, 2, 80 ; id. Poen. 3, 3, 37 ), old Lat. manus, good; whence immanis; cf. Manes . The morning, morn. As subst. , mostly poet. and in post-Aug.…

manentĭa.opening: maneo , permanency (eccl. Lat.): substantia habet manentiam quandam ut ita dicam, Aug. Ep. 11, 3 .

mănĕo.opening: (contr. perf. mansti for mansisti, Lucil. ap. Gell. 18, 8 ), , v. n. and a. [root man, to think; whence the notion of hesitating leads to that of waiting; cf. Gr. μένω, μένος, μιμνήσκω, μάντις ; and Lat. memini, moneo,…

Mānes.opening: ( fem. , Inscr. ap. Fea, Var. di Notiz. p. 174; Inscr. Grut. 786, 5 ), manus, good; v. mane , with or without di. The deified souls of the departed, the ghosts or shades of the dead, the gods of the Lower World,…

Manĕtho.opening: , or , , , Μανέθων and Μανέθως , a priest of Heliopolis, who wrote a history of Egypt in Greek .

mango.opening: μάγγανον , a dealer, monger in slaves or wares, to which he tries to give an appearance of greater value, by adorning them (post-Aug.): mangones quicquid est quod displiceat, aliquo lenocinio abscondunt, etc., Sen. Ep.…

mangōnico.opening: ( ), , v. a. mango , to set off, deck, adorn an article for sale (post-Aug.): ita pueros mangonicavit saepe obstetrix, Plin. 32, 10, 47, § 135 . —In part. perf. : mangonicatae villae, Plin. 9, 54, 79, § 168 .— In gen.,…

mangōnĭcus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to a dealer (post-Aug.): venalicii, Plin. 21, 26, 97, § 170 : quaestus, Suet. Vesp. 4 .

mangōnĭum.opening: id. , a setting off, displaying of wares (post-Aug.), Plin. 10, 50, 71, § 140 .

mănĭa.opening: , = μανία , madness (syn.: furor, insania, v. Cic. Tusc. 3, 5, 11 ), Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 12, 107 .—As a disease of cattle, Veg. Vet. 3, 2, 19 Gesn. (Schneid. insania).

mănĭcae.opening: manus , the long sleeve of a tunic , reaching to the hand, and which therefore supplied the place of our glove . Lit. : et tunicae manicas (habent), Verg. A. 9, 616 : partem vestitus superioris in manicas non extendunt,…

mănĭcārĭus.opening: manicae a manacler , a gladiator who sought to manacle his opponent; cf. LAQVEATOR, Inscr. Orell. 2566 .

mănĭcātus.opening: adj. id. , furnished with long sleeves (class.): tunica, Cic. Cat. 2, 10, 22 : pelles, Col. 1, 8, 9 ; 11, 1, 21 .

Mănichaei.opening: a heretical Christian sect , Prud. Apoth. 1025 ; Mos. et Rom. Leg. Coll. 15, 3, 4.—In sing. : , , , Cod. Just. 1, 5, 4 .

manicleātus.opening: adj. manicae , furnished with long sleeves , for manicatus: tunica, Isid. Orig. 19, 22, 8 .

mānĭco.opening: v. n. mane , to come in the morning (eccl. Lat.): omnis populus ad eum, Vulg. Luc. 21, 38 al.

mănĭcon.opening: , = μανικόν , a plant, the juice of which maddens , Plin. 21, 31, 105, § 179 .

mănĭcŭla.opening: dim. manus . Lit. , a little hand , Plaut. Rud. 4, 4, 125 .— Transf. (cf. Engl. handle), the handle of a plough, plough-tail , Varr. L. L. 5, § 136 Müll. (al. manibula).

mănĭfestārĭus.opening: adj. manifestus , palpable, plain, clear, evident, manifest (ante- and post-class. for manifestus): fur, Plaut. Aul. 3, 4, 10 : moechus, id. Bacch. 4, 8, 77 : teneo hunc manifestarium, id. Trin. 4, 2, 50 .—Of things:…

mănĭfestātĭo.opening: 2. manifesto , a manifesting, manifestation (post-class.): suae praesentiae, Aug. Civ. Dei, 20, 30: tantae virtutis, Sulp. Sev. Dial. 3, 4 .

mănĭfestātor.opening: id. , a discoverer, shower, manifester (post-class.): alicujus rei, Non. 14, 6 ; Acron ad Hor. C. 1, 9, 21 .

mănĭfesto.opening: v. a. manifestus , to make public, discover, show clearly, exhibit, manifest ( poet. and postclass.): aliquem latentem, Ov. M. 13, 105 : gratam voluntatem, Just. 24, 6, 10 .—In pass. : quod vel ex eo manifestari, quod,…

mănĭfestus.opening: , old form (v. Lachm. ad Lucr. 2, 867 ), a, um. adj. manus and fendo; cf.: defendo, offendo, i. e. that one hits by the hand; hence , palpable, clear, plain, apparent, evident, manifest . In gen. (class.): manifesta res…

mănĭfŏlĭum.opening: a kind of burdock , also called personata, App. Herb. 36 .

Mānīlĭus.opening: name of a Roman gens. So, C. Manilius, a tribune of the people A. U. C. 687, Cic. Imp. Pomp. 24, 69 ; Q. Cic. Pet. Cons. 13, 51 .— A. Manilius, the astronomer and poet, author of the poem Astronomica.— In fem. : * , , a…

mānĭŏlae.opening: dim. maniae , little bugaboos for children, acc. to Paul. ex Fest. p. 128 Müll.

mănĭŏpoeos.opening: , = μανιοποιός (making mad), a term applied to henbane , App. Herb. 4 .

mănĭōsus.opening: adj. 2. mania , full of madness, utterly crazed , Amm. 28, 4, 16 dub. (al. famosus).

mănĭpŭlāris.opening: or (sync. and ), , adj. manipulus , with miles , or absol., of or belonging to a maniple or company, manipular (class.): pertica suspensos portabat longa maniplos: Unde maniplaris nomina miles habet, Ov. F. 3, 117 :…

mănĭpŭlārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to a maniple or to a common soldier (post-Aug.): manipulario habitu, in the dress of a private, Suet. Calig. 9 .

mănĭpŭlātim.opening: adv. id. . By handfuls, in bundles , Plin. 12, 13, 28, § 48 .— Milit., by maniples : manipulatim resistere hostibus, Sisenn. ap. Non. 141, 27 : manipulatim structa acies, Liv. 8, 8 ; Tac. H. 1, 8, 2 .—Comically:…

mănĭpŭlus.opening: (sync. , in poets; plur. : inter manipula, Spart. Hadrian. 10 ), , manus-pleo, plenus , a handful, a bundle . Lit. : de his (herbis) manipulos fieri, Varr. R. R. 1, 49 : manipulos obligare, Col. 11, 2, 40 : vincire, id.…

Mānĭus.opening: , and , , mane , a Roman prænomen , usually abbreviated M'., Varr. L. L. 9, § 61 Müll.; cf.: Manius praenomen dictum est ab eo, quod mane quis initio natus sit, ut Lucius, qui luce, Paul. ex Fest. p. 148 Müll.

Manlĭus.opening: name of a Roman gens. So esp. M. Manlius Capitolinus, who saved the Capitol in the Gallic war, but afterwards, suspected of aspiring to royal power, was thrown from the Tarpeian Rock , Liv. 5, 47, 4 sq. ; 6, 11 sq.;…

manna.opening: neutr. indecl. , and , , Hebrew , the manna of the Hebrews.— Neutr. : Filii Israël dixerunt ad invicem, Manhu, quod significat, Quid est hoc? Vulg. Exod. 16, 15 : sume vas unum, et mitte ibi man, quantum, etc., id. ib.…

mannŭlus.opening: dim. 1. mannus , a Gallic pony (post-Aug.), Plin. Ep. 4, 2, 3 ; Mart. 12, 24, 8 .

mannus.opening: Celtic , a kind of small Gallic horse, a coach-horse, cob (used esp. for pleasure-drives): agens mannos, Lucr. 3, 1063 : si per obliquum similis sagittae (serpens) Terruit mannos, Hor. C. 3, 27, 6 ; id. Ep. 1, 7, 77 :…

Mannus.opening: Germ. Mann, ἄνθρωπος , a god of the ancient Germans, son of Tuisco , Tac. G. 2 .

māno.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
māno.opening: v. n. and a. [prob. for mad-no; Sanscr. madas, drunkenness; Gr. μαδαρός , flowing; cf.: madeo, madidus; also Gr. μᾶνός ], to flow, run, trickle, drop, distil , etc. Lit. Neutr. : manat omni corpore sudor, Enn. ap. Macr.…

mānon.opening: , = μανόν , a kind of soft sponge , Plin. 9, 45, 69, § 148 ; called also, , , : (spongearum genus) spissum et mollius manos, id. 9, 45, 69, § 149 Jan. (al. mana).— Plur. , : maximae fiunt manoi, Plin. 9, 45, 69, § 149 .

mansĭo.opening: maneo , a staying, remaining, stay, continuance . Lit. (class.): is saepe mecum de tua mansione, aut decessione communicat, Cic. Fam. 4, 4, 5 : mansio Formiis, id. Att. 9, 5, 1 : excessus e vita et in vita mansio, id.…

mansĭōnārĭus.opening: adj. mansio , of or belonging to a dwelling or lodging (post-class.): conjugium, Fulg. Myth. 3, 6 .

mansĭto.opening: v. freq. n. [maneo], to stay, remain, tarry, abide, dwell (post-Aug.): pygargus in oppidis mansitat, Plin. 10, 3, 3, § 7 : sub eodem tecto, Tac. A. 14, 42 : una, to pass the night, id. ib. 13, 44 ; cf. maneo, B.;…

mansĭuncŭla.opening: dim. mansio , a little dwelling (late Lat.): mansiunculas in arca facies, chambers, Vulg. Gen. 6, 14 .

mansor.opening: maneo , a sojourner, indweller, guest (late Lat.): faciat (Deus nos) tanto mansore capaces, Sedul. 5, 294 .

mansōrĭus.opening: adj. mansor , abiding, permanent (opp. transitorius): non quasi mansoria dilectio atque delectatio, sed transitoria potius, ut viae, Aug. Doctr. Chr. 1, 35, 39 .

mansŭēfăcĭo.opening: v. a.; pass. , mansuetus-facio , to make tame, to tame (class.). Lit. : mansuefacimus animalia? indomita nascuntur, Quint. 9, 4, 5 : uri assuescere ad homines et mansuefieri, ne parvuli quidem excepti, possunt, grow or…

mansŭēfactĭo.opening: mansuefacio , the taming : bestiarum, Aug. de Nat. et Grat. 15, 16 .

mansŭēs.opening: adj. manussuesco , tamed, tame (ante- and post-class. for mansuetus, v. mansuesco fin. ): mansues pro mansueto, dixit Cato in epistola ad filium, Cato ap. Fest. p. 154 Müll.; cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 152, 125 Müll.: leonem…

mansŭesco.opening: v. inch. a. and manus-suesco; lit., to accustom to the hand; hence , Act., to tame, to make tame (in the verb. finit. ante- and post-class.; but cf. infra, mansuetus). Lit. : silvestria animalia, Varr. R. R. 2, 1, 4 :…

mansŭētārĭus.opening: mansuetus , a tamer of wild beasts (post-class.), Lampr. Heliog. 21 ; Firmic. 8, 17.

mansŭēto.opening: v. freq. a. mansuetus , to make tame, to tame (late Lat. for mansuefacio): mansuetabatur ignis, Vulg. Sap. 16, 18 .

mansŭētūdo.opening: id. , tameness . Lit. (post-class.): elephanti, Just. 15, 4, 19 .— Trop. In gen., mildness, gentleness, clemency (class.): uti clementiā ac mansuetudine in aliquem, Caes. B. G. 2, 14 : imperii, Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 44, §…

mansŭētus.opening: Part. and P. a. , v. mansuesco.

mansus.opening: , um. Part. , from 2. mando.— Part. , from maneo.

mantēle.opening: ( ), , , and ( ), , manus and tela, properly a cloth for the hand , a towel, napkin . Lit. : mantelium, ubi manus terguntur, Varr. L. L. 6, § 85 Müll.: tonsisque ferunt mantelia villis, Verg. A. 1, 702 (v. l. mantilia);…

mantēlum.opening: and , , i. q. mantele, q. v. , a cloth, napkin , Lucil. ap. Serv. Verg. G. 4, 377 ; Paul. ex Fest. p. 133, 33 ; Inscr. Orell. 2271 .— A cloak, mantle; trop.: nec mendaciis subdolis mihi usquam mantelum est meis, Plaut.…

mantīa.opening: , = μαντεία , the name of the blackberry-bush among the Dacians, App. Herb. 87 .

mantĭca.opening: manus , a bag for the hand, wallet, cloak-bag, portmanteau : mantica cui (mulo) lumbos onere ulceret, Hor. S. 1, 6, 104 : umero exuere, to take off from the shoulder, App. M. 1, p. 110, 27 .—Prov.: non videmus, manticae…

mantĭcē.opening: , = Μαντική , the goddess of prescience : divinationem quam Graeci Μαντικὴν appellant, id est, praesensionem et scientiam rerum futurarum, Cic. Div. 1, 1, 1 ; cf. id. Leg. 2, 13, 32 : Mantice Pronoës filia, Mart. Cap.…

mantĭchō^ra.opening: , = μαντιχώρας and μαντιχόρας , a fabulous Indian beast, with a human face, a lion's body, and a scorpion's tail , Plin. 8, 21, 30, § 75 ; 8, 30, 45, § 107 ; Calp. Ecl. 7, 58 .

mantĭcĭnor.opening: v. dep. μάντιςcano , to predict, prophesy, divine (comically formed, in imitation of vaticinor): nisi ego manticinatus probe ero, Plaut. Capt. 4, 2, 115 .

mantĭcŭla.opening: dim. mantica , a small wallet, purse, pouch , Paul. ex Fest. p. 133 Müll.

mantĭculārĭa.opening: obsol. adj. manticularius , handy little things, things in constant use : dicuntur ea, quae frequenter in usu habentur, et quasi manu tractantur. Frequens enim antiquis ad manus tergendas usus fuit mantelorum, unde haec…

mantĭcŭlātor.opening: manticulor , a pickpocket, sharper , Pac. ap. Fest. p. 133 Müll. (Trag. Rel. v. 376 Rib.).

mantĭcŭlor.opening: v. dep. manticula; lit., to be busied with purses; hence , to steal (ante- and post-class.): cum utrem ventosissimum manticularentur, App. Mag. 55, p. 309, 36 .— Transf. , to act slyly, go cunningly to work :…

Mantinēa.opening: , = Μαντίνεια , a city of Arcadia, celebrated for the victory of Epaminondas over the Spartans , Plin. 4, 6, 10, § 20 ; Nep. Ep. 9, 1 ; Cic. Fam. 5, 12, 5 ; id. Fin. 2, 30, 97 .

mantīsa.opening: ( ), , Tuscan . Lit. , a worthless addition, makeweight : mantisa additamentum dicitur lingua Tusca, quod ponderi adicitur, sed deterius et quod sine ullo usu est. Lucilius: mantisa obsonia vincit, Paul. ex Fest. p.…

mantiscĭnor.opening: , a false read. for man ticinor, Plaut. Capt. 4, 2, 115 .

manto.opening: v. freq. n. and a. [maneo]. Neutr., to stay, remain, wait (ante-class.): in eādem mantat malitiā, Caecil. ap. Non. 505, 27 (Com. Rel. v. 87 Rib.): manta, Plaut. Ps. 1, 3, 49 ; id. Rud. 2, 4, 26 : usque mantant, id.…

Manto.opening: , = Μαντώ . The daughter of Tiresias, a prophetess, and mother of the seer Mopsus , Ov. M. 6, 157 ; Mel. 1, 17, 2 ; Hyg. Fab. 128 ; Stat. Th. 7, 758 ; 10, 679 .— An Italian nymph who had the gift of prophecy, the mother…

Mantŭa.opening: a city of Gallia Transpadana, on the Mincius, in whose vicinity was Andes, the birthplace of Virgil , still called Mantua , Plin. 3, 19, 23, § 130 ; Liv. 24, 10, 7 ; Verg. A. 10, 200 : Mantua Vergilio gaudet, Ov. Am. 3,…

mantŭēlis.opening: adj. mantelum , cloakshaped, mantle-like (post-class.), Treb. Claud. 17, 6 .

mantum.opening: a Spanish cloak : mantum Hispani vocant, quod manus tegat tantum: est enim breve amictum, Isid. Orig. 19, 24, 15 .

Manturna.opening: maneo , the goddess of matrimony, who was invoked to render the marriage lasting , Aug. Civ. Dei , 6, 9.

Mantus.opening: the Etruscan Pluto, the god of the under-world , Serv. Verg. A. 10, 199 .

mănŭa.opening: manus , a handful : manuae feni, Schol. Juv. 8, 154 : manua, δράγμα , Gloss.

mănŭālis.opening: adj. 1. manus , of or belonging to the hand, for the hand, that is held in or fills the hand, hand- . Adj. (mostly post-Aug.): manuales lapides, that can be thrown with the hand , Sisenn. ap. Non. 449, 2 : saxa, Tac. A.…

mănŭārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to the hand, for the hand, that fills the hand (ante- and post-class.): mola, a hand-mill, Dig. 33, 7, 26 : vas, Charis. p. 95 P.: aes, won with the hand at gaming, money won at dice, Gell.…

mănŭātus.opening: adj. id. , furnished with hands , Mart. Cap. 4, § 378 ; v. also manuor.

mănŭballistārĭus.opening: manu-ballista , one who carries or uses a hand-ballista (post-class.), Veg. Mil. 3, 14 ; 4, 21 .

mănŭbĭae.opening: (in sing. , v. infra , II.), 1. manus . In milit. and legal lang. Lit. : money obtained from the sale of booty (opp. praeda, the booty itself). Of this money, one part was put into the Ærarium, one was given to the…

mănŭbĭālis.opening: adj. manubiae , of or belonging to booty (post-Aug.): pecunia, derived from the sale of booty : de manubiis, Suet. Aug. 30 ; cf. manubiae, I. A.

mănŭbĭārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to booty; transf.: amicus manubiarius, i. e. that brings one profit, Plaut. Truc. 4, 4, 27 .

mănŭbĭus.opening: adj. , v. manubiae, I. B. 1 fin.

mănūbrĭātus.opening: adj. manubrium , furnished with a handle (post-class.): manubriatae serrulae, Pall. 1, 43, 2 : magistri manubriatos cultros dexteris manibus gestabant, Amm. 25, 1, 15 .

mănūbrĭŏlum.opening: dim. id. , a little handle or haft (post-Aug.): scalpelli, Cels. 7, 6 fin.

mănūbrĭum.opening: ( ), , 1. manus , that which is grasped or held in the hand; hence, a handle, hilt, haft (class.): trulla excavata, manubrio aureo, Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 27, § 62 : manubria, quorum optima sunt ilignea, Col. 11, 2, 92 :…

mănŭcĭŏlum.opening: ( ), , dim. manucium , a small bundle , = manipulus, Petr. 63, 8 .

mănŭcĭum.opening: ( ) [manus], = χειρίς , a glove, muff , Gloss. Philox.

mănŭfactĭlis.opening: adj. 1. manus-facio , made by hand of man (eccl. Lat.): Deum manufactilem, Hier. in Psa. 118 .

mănŭfactus.grammar: a, um, more correctly written as two words

mănŭinspex.opening: manus-inspicio , = χειροσκόπος , a hand-inspector, student or practitioner of palmistry , Gloss. Vet.

mănŭlĕa.opening: (al. leg. ap. Vitr. mănucŭla or mănucla), , 1. manus . * A long sleeve reaching to the hand, i. q. manica: quid tu amicam times ne te manulea cajet? Plaut. Fragm. ap. Fulg. Contin. Verg. p. 163 Muncker; v. cajo, and cf.…

mănŭlĕārĭus.opening: manulea , a maker of sleeves or muffs for women (anteand post-class.), Plaut. Aul. 3, 5, 37 ; Inscr. Rein. 2 , n. 83.

mănŭlĕātus.opening: adj. manulea , furnished with long sleeves , which were regarded as a proof of effeminacy (ante-class. and post-Aug.): manuleatus et armillatus in publicum processit, Suet. Calig. 52 : tunicam, Plaut. Ps. 2, 4, 48 .

mănŭlĕus.opening: id. , the long sleeve of a tunic (ante-class. and post-Aug. for manica): actoribus manuleos, baltea, machaeras, Att. ap. Non. 194, 19 : laxiores, Front. Ep. 4, 3 bis; cf. manulea, I.

mănūmissĭo.opening: manumitto , the freeing of a slave, manumission . It was effected either per censum (when the person to be freed was registered in the census), or per testamentum, or per vindictam (v. vindicta, and Cic. Top. 2, 10 );…

mănūmissor.opening: id. , one who gives a slave his freedom, a liberator, emancipator (post-class.), Dig. 37, 15, 3 ; Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 4 .

mănūmitto.opening: (also as two words, v. infra ; and ante-class. , v. emitto, I. B.), , v. a. 1. manus-mitto , to release from one's power (manus), to set at liberty, to enfranchise, emancipate, make free a slave (v. manumissio): quos…

mănŭor.opening: , ätus , v. dep. manus , to steal : Laberius in mimis scripsit, manuatus est pro furatus est, Gell. 16, 7, 2 .

mănŭprĕtĭōsus.opening: adj. manupretium , precious, valuable, costly : vestimentum, Cato ap. Gell. 13, 23, 1 .

mănŭprĕtĭum.opening: ( ; and as two words, and ; v. Weissenb. ad Liv. 34, 7, 4 ), , 1. manus-pretium , a workman's or artist's pay, wages. Lit. : manupretium dabo, Plaut. Men. 3, 3, 17 : in auro, praeter manus pretium, nihil intertrimenti…

mănus.opening: ( dat. manu for manui: alternae manu, Prop. 1, 11, 12 ; 2, 1, 60 ), root man-, ma-, to measure; Sanscr. ma, measure, moon; cf. Germ. Mond, moon, and O. H. Germ. mund, hand; Angl.-Sax. mund , a hand. Lit. : quam vero…

mānus.opening: , i. q. bonus, Varr. L. L. 6, 2, 4 ; Macr. S. 1, 3, 13 ; Isid. 5, 30, 14 ; Serv. Verg. A. 1, 139 ; 2, 286 ; v. † cerus manus.

mănŭtergĭum.opening: 1. manustergeo , a towel : manutergium a tergendo manus vocatur, Isid. Orig. 19, 26 .

mănŭtĭgĭum.opening: 1. manus-tango , a touching or feeling with the hand ( = manuum contactus; cf. Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 18, 177 ; post-class.), Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 4, 121 .

manzer.opening: ( ), , adj. comm. [Heb. ], illegitimate, bastard (eccl. Lat.), Sedul. Carm. 5, 256 : agmina manzera, Ven. Carm. 5, 5, 75.—As subst. : , , , a bastard : non ingredietur manzer, hoc est de scorto natus, in Ecclesiam…

măpālĭa.opening: Punic , huts, cottages of the Africans: mapalia casae Punicae appellantur, Paul. ex Fest. p. 146, 25 Müll.; so ib. p. 147 ; cf.: aedificia Numidarum agrestium, quae mapalia illi vocant, oblonga, incurvis lateribus…

mappa.opening: Punic, Quint. 1, 5, 57 , a napkin, table-napkin; a towel . Lit. : Varius mappa compescere risum Vix poterat, Hor. S. 2, 8, 63 : laticlavia, Petr. 32 ; Mart. 4, 46, 17 : rubra detergere vulnera mappa, Juv. 5, 27 .—…

mappŭla.opening: dim. mappa , a small napkin (late Lat.): mappulam apponere, Hier. Ep. 108, 28 (al. matulam).

Maracanda.opening: the capital of Sogdiana , now Samarcand , Curt. 7, 6, 16 ; 7, 9, 20 .

Mărăthon.opening: ( , Mel. 2, 3, 6 ), = Μαραθών , a town (now Vrana ) on the eastern coast of Attica, famed for the death of Icarus, the victory of Theseus over the Marathonian bull, and that of Miltiades over the Persians , Mel. 2, 3, 6…

Mărăthos.opening: or , , , = Μάραθος , an ancient Phœnician city, opposite the island of Arados , near the modern Ainel-Hye , Mel. 1, 12, 3 ; Plin. 5, 20, 17, § 78 ; Curt. 4, 1, 6 .—Hence, , , adj., of or from Marathos, Marathene :…

mărăthrītes.opening: , = μαραθρίτης (sc. οἶνος ), wine flavored with fennel, fennelwine : vinum absinthiten, et hyssopiten, et marathriten sic condire oportet, Col. 12, 35 init.

mărăthrus.opening: or , , , or , , , = μάραθρον , fennel , called in pure Lat. feniculum, Plin. 8, 27, 41, § 99 : marathros (v. l. marathrus), Ov. Med. Fac. 91 .

Marcellus.opening: dim. of Marcus , a Roman family name in the plebeian gens Claudia: inter Marcellos et Claudios patricios, Cic. de Or. 1, 39, 176 : generosior Marcellis, Juv. 2, 145 .— Esp., M. Claudius Marcellus, the taker of Syracuse…
