massŭla.opening: dim. 1. massa , a little lump or mass (post-Aug.), Col. 12, 38, 2 : salis, id. 12, 48, 5 .

Massŭrĭus.opening: ( ) , a celebrated jurist in the time of the emperor Tiberius , Dig. 1, 2, 2 fin. ; Gell. 3, 16 fin. ; 5, 19 al. : Masuri rubrica vetavit, Pers. 5, 90 . —Hence, , , adj., of or pertaining to Massurius : deliramenta, M.…

Massȳli.opening: , = Μασσύλιοι , a people in Africa, to the east of the Massaesyli, Plin. 5, 4, 4, § 30 ; Verg. A. 6, 60 ; Sil. 4, 512 ; 16, 171 ; Prud. στεφ . 4, 46; called Maesuli, Liv. 24, 48, 13 .—Hence, and , , adj., of or…

Mastarna.opening: an ancient (Tuscan) name of Mons Coelius, Oratio Claudii Aug. ap. Grut. 502.

Mastaurenses.opening: the inhabitants of the city of Mastaura in Lydia , Plin. 5, 29, 31, § 120 .

mastĭcātĭo.opening: mastico , a chewing, mastication (post-class.): cibum masticatione exercere, Cael. Aur. Tard. 4, 3, 70 .

mastĭchātus.opening: ( ), , adj. mastiche , furnished or seasoned with mastic (post-class.), Lampr. Heliog. 19, 4 .

mastĭchē.opening: ( ), , , = μαστίχη , mastic, an odoriferous gum from the mastic-tree , Plin. 12, 17, 36, § 72 ; 21, 16, 56, § 96 ; 14, 20, 25, § 122 ; Capitol. Gord. 19 .— Post-class. collat. forms: , , , Marc. Emp. 26 ; ( ), , , Pall.…

mastĭchĭnus.opening: ( ), , adj. , = μαστίχινος , of or belonging to mastic, mastic- (post-class.): oleum, Pall. Mart. 9, 3 .

mastĭco.opening: v. a. , to chew (post-class.): aliquid, Pelag. Vet. 30; App. Herb. 79 : portulaca mastucata, Theod. Prisc. de Diaeta, 10.

mastīgĭa.opening: , = μαστιγίας , a scoundrel, rascal, rogue . Lit. (anteclass.), Plaut. Curc. 4, 4, 11 ; id. Capt. 3, 4, 69 ; 3, 5, 1 ; id. Cas. 2, 6, 9 ; 2, 8, 10 ; id. Most. 1, 1, 1 ; 3, 1, 71 ; id. Poen. 1, 2, 108 ; 177 ; 178 ; id.…

mastīgo.opening: v. a. , = μαστιγόω , to whip, scourge , Cypr. Serm. de Rat. Circumcis. p. 489 .

mastīgŏphŏrus.opening: , = μαστιγοφόρος , a whip-bearer , i. e. a beadle, policeman , an officer whose duty it was to maintain order at the public shows (post-class.), Prud. adv. Symm. 2, 516 ; Dig. 50, 4, 18, § 17 ; Arn. 2, 23 .

mastos.opening: , = μαστός , a plant good for the breast , Plin. 26, 15, 92, § 163 .

mastrūca.opening: ( ), , Sardinian; v. infra , a garment made of skins, a sheepskin, a skin : mastrucam, quod Sardum est, inridens Cicero ex industria dixit, Quint. 1, 5, 8 : mastruca vestis Sardonica ex pelliculis ferarum, de qua Cicero…

mastrūcātus.opening: adj. mastruca , clothed in a mastruca or in skins : latrunculi, Cic. Prov. Cons. 7, 15 .

masturbātor.opening: masturbor , one who defiles himself (post-Aug.), Mart. 14, 203, 2 .

masturbor.opening: v. dep. perhaps from manus-stupro , to defile one's self (postAug.), Mart. 11, 104, 13 ; 9, 42, 7 ; cf. in the act. form masturbat, δέφει, δέφεται , Vet. Gloss.

mătella.opening: or , , dim. matula , a pot, a vessel for liquids. In gen.: matella aquae, Plaut. Fragm. ap. Non. 543, 17 ; Varr. ib. 19 ; Cato, R. R. 10 ; 11 .—Prov.: mus in matella, of a person in difficulty, Petr. 58, 9 .— In…

mătellĭo.opening: dim. matula; cf. Varr. L. L. 5, § 119 Müll.; Paul. ex Fest. p. 126 ib. , a pot, vessel (class.), Varr. ap. Non. 547, 7 : Corinthius, Cic. Par. 5, 2, 38 .

matĕŏla.opening: , perh. a kind of mallet or beetle : si (talea) parum descendet, malleolo aut mateola adigito, Cato, R. R. 45, 2 ; 46, 2 (also ap. Plin. 17, 18, 29, § 126 ).

māter.opening: root ma-; Sanscr. and Zend, to make, measure, like Gr. μήτηρ, the maker, akin with Dor. μάτηρ; Germ. Mutter; Engl. mother; cf.: materies, manus , a mother ( dat. sing. matre, Corp. Inscr. Lat. 177; dat. plur. matris,…

mātercŭla.opening: dim. mater , a little mother (class.): tune igitur mea matercula? Plaut. Fragm. ap. Prisc. p. 601 P.: materculae suae festivus filius, * Cic. Fl. 36, 91 ; Hor. Ep. 1, 7, 7 .

mātĕrĭa.opening: ( gen. materiāi, Lucr. 1, 1051 ), and , (only in nom. and acc. sing. , and once gen. plur. materierum, Lact. 2, 12, 1 ; v. Neue, Formenl. 1, p. 383), from same root with mater, q. v. , stuff, matter, materials of which…

mātĕrĭālis.opening: adj. materia , of or belonging to matter, material (post-class.): influxio, Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 12, 7 ; 10 ; Ambros. de Virg. 3, 1, 1 .—Hence, adv. : , according to the occasion (postclass.): in pectore viri iracundia…

mātĕrĭārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to stuff, matter, wood, timber . In gen. (ante-class. and post-Aug.): fabrica, carpentry, Plin. 7, 56, 57, § 198 : FABER, a carpenter, Inscr. Grut. 642, 6 : NEGOCIATOR, a timber-merchant,…

mātĕrĭātĭo.opening: materia , woodwork , as beams, rafters , etc., Vitr. 4, 2, 1 .

mātĕrĭātūra.opening: id. , a working in wood : materiatura fabrilis, carpenter's work, Vitr. 4, 2, 2 .

mātĕrīnus.opening: adj. materia , hard, solid : terra, Cato, R. R. 34, 2 dub.

mātĕrĭo.opening: (no perf. ), , v. a. id. , to build of wood (rare but class.): eaque aedificia minime sunt materianda propter incendia, Vitr. 5, 12, 7 : aedes male materiatae, of bad wood-work, Cic. Off. 3, 13, 54 .

mātĕrĭŏla.opening: dim. id. , a small matter (post-class.), Tert. Baptism. 17 .

mātĕrĭor.opening: v. dep. id. , to fell or procure wood : erat eo tempore et materiari et frumentari necesse, Caes. B. G. 7, 73 init.

matĕris.opening: or ( ), , and , , Celtic , a Celtic javelin, pike : nonnulli inter carros rotasque mataras ac tragulas subiciebant nostrosque vulnerabant, Caes. B. G. 1, 26, 3 : humero matari trajecto, Liv. 7, 24, 3 : materis…

māternus.opening: adj. mater , of or belonging to a mother, maternal (class.): sanguis, Enn. ap. Non. 292, 16 (Trag. v. 184 Vahl.): paternus maternusque sanguis, Cic. Rosc. Am. 24, 66 : animus, Ter. Heaut. 4, 1, 24 : nomen, Cic. Clu. 5,…

Māternus.opening: a Roman surname : Curiatius Maternus, Tac. Or. 2 .

mātertĕra.opening: for materitera, mater and an obsol. fem. noun found in neutr. i-terum; cf. al-tera, a second mother , a mother's sister, an aunt by the mother's side: amita est patris soror: matertera est matris soror, Dig. 38, 10, 10,…

măthēmătĭcus.opening: adj. , = μαθηματικός , of or belonging to mathematics, mathematical (class.). Adj. : mathematica nota, Vitr. 1, 1 : artes, Plin. 30, 1, 1, § 2 : cogitatio, Macr. Somn. Scip. 2, 2 : disciplinae, i. e. geometry,…

măthēsis.opening: (with the second syll. short: involvit măthĕsi, Prud. adv. Symm. 2, 893 al. ; Sid. Carm. 5, 131 ), , = μάθησις (lit., knowledge, science; hence, in partic.). The mathematics, mathesis (late Lat.): quadrifariae mathesis…

Mătho.opening: a rich speculator, afterwards a bankrupt , Juv. 1, 32 ; 7, 129 .

Matilĭca.opening: a city in Umbria , the modern Matelica , Front. de Colon. p. 100 Goes.—Hence, , , , the inhabitants of Matilica , Plin. 3, 14, 19, § 113 .

Mătīnus.opening: a mountain or promontory in Apulia, near the foot of Mount Garganus , now Matinata , Luc. 9, 185 ; Schol. Cruq. ad Hor. C. 1, 28, 3 .—Hence, , , adj., of or belonging to Mount Matinus, Matinian : apis Matinae More, Hor.…

Matisco.opening: a city of the Æduans, in Gallia Lugdunensis, on the Arar, the modern Maçon , Caes. B. G. 7, 90, 7 .

Mătĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens. So, Cn. Matius, a poet and translator of the Iliad , Gell. 6, 6, 5 ; 9, 14, 14 ; Varr. L. L. 7, 5, § 96 Müll.; perh. the same with C. Matius, a friend of Cæsar and Cicero, Cic. Fam. 6, 12, 2 ;…

Matrae.opening: ( dat. plur. MATRABVS, for Matris, Inscr. Grut. 29, 1 ), or , more freq. , the protecting goddesses of a country, city , or place : MATRIS AVGVSTIS D. D., Inscr. Grut. 90, 1 ; so ib. 2 sq.

mātrālis.opening: adj. mater , pertaining to a mother : Matralia festa, Ov. F. 6, 533 , or simply Matralia, the festival of Mater Matuta, i. e. Ino, celebrated annually on the 11 th of June : Matralia Matris Matutae festa, Paul. ex Fest.…

mātresco.opening: v. inch. n. [id.], to become a mother, to become like one's mother (ante-class.): utinam nunc matrescam ingenio, Pac. ap. Non. 137, 7 dub. (Trag. Rel. v. 139 Rib., maturescam): matrescere, μητράζειν , Onomast. Vet.

mātrīcālis.opening: adj. matrix , of or belonging to the womb or matrix (post-class.): herba, App. Herb. 65 : vena, Veg. Vet. 1, 10, 7 .

mātrĭcīda.opening: (scanned matrĭcĭda, Sid. Carm. 5, 291 ), , mater-caedo , a mother's murderer, a matricide (rare but class.): quem scribis certissimum matricidam, Cic. Q. Fr. 1, 2, 2 ; Nep. Alc. 6, 2 : cantavit Oresten matricidam, Suet.…

mātrĭcīdĭum.opening: matricida , the murder of one's mother, matricide : accusari matricidii, Cic. Inv. 1, 13, 18 .

mātrīcŭla.opening: dim. matrix , a public register, list, roll (post-class.), Veg. Mil. 1, 26 ; 2, 2 ; 5 ; Cod. Just. 12, 20, 3 .

matricŭlus.opening: an unknown fish , App. Mag. p. 162 .

mātrĭmōnĭālis.opening: adj. matrimonium , of or belonging to marriage, matrimonial (post-class.): tabulae, Firm. Math. 7, 17: lectulus, Quint. Decl. 1, 13 .

mātrĭmōnĭum.opening: mater , wedlock, marriage, matrimony . Lit. (class.): ire in matrimonium, i. e. to be married, Plaut. Trin. 3, 3, 4 : in matrimonium dare, opp. in concubinatum, id. ib. 3, 2, 65 : alicujus tenere, to be one's spouse :…

mātrimus.opening: (the quantity of the i is doubtful), a, um, (collat. form: matrimes ac patrimes dicuntur, quibus matres et patres adhuc vivunt, Paul. ex Fest. p. 126 Müll.), adj. id. , that has a mother living : decem ingenui, decem…

mātrix.opening: id. , a mother in respect to propagation (in lit. signif. not used of women). Lit. , a breeding-animal : of breeding-cows , Varr. R. R. 2, 5, 12 ; of breeding-ewes , Col. 7, 3, 12 ; of laying-hens , id. 8, 2, 6 ; 8, 5,…

mātrōna.opening: id. , a married woman, wife, matron (whether she was in manu or not; consequently more general in its application than mater familias, which always denoted one who was in manu). In gen.: matronam dictam esse proprie,…

Matrŏna.opening: ( , Aus. Mos. 462 ; Sid. Pan. 812 ), a river in Gaul , now the Marne , Caes. B. G. 1, 1, 2 ; Amm. 15, 11, 3 ; Aus. Mos. 462 ; Sid. Carm. 5, 208 .

mātrōnālis.opening: adj. 1. matrona , of or belonging to a married woman or matron, womanly, matronly (not in Cic.): oblitae decoris matronalis, of womanly honor, Liv. 26, 49 fin. : jam illi anilis prudentia, matronalis gravitas erat,…

mātrōnātus.opening: id. , the dress of a matron or lady of rank , App. M. 4, p. 153, 9 .

Matrōum.opening: , = Μητρῶον , a false read. for Matrem, Plin. 16, 27, 50, § 115 .

mātrŭēlis.opening: mater , a mother's brother's son, a cousin-german, first-cousin on the mother's side (cf. patruelis, a father's brother's son; post class.), Dig. 48, 9, 1 ; Vict. de Orig. Gentis Rom. 13, 8.

matta.opening: a mat made of rushes, Aug. contr. Faust. 5, 5; Schol. Juv. 5, 8 ; 6, 117 (also v. l. for lata, Ov. F. 6, 679 ).

Mattārĭus.opening: matta , one who sleeps on a mat (late Lat.), a name applied by the orthodox to a sect of Manichæans: quia in mattis dormiunt, Mattarii appellantur, Aug. contr. Faust. 5, 5; id. de Haeres. 46 .

mattĕa.opening: ( , ), , , = ματτύα (v. Varr. L. L. 5, 22, § 112 Müll.), a dainty dish, dainty, delicacy , Suet. Calig. 38 ; Sen. Contr. 4, 27 ; Petr. 65 : to mattea sola juvat (al. juvant, assuming a collat. form, , , ), Mart. 10, 59,…

mattĕŏla.opening: ( , ), , dim. mattea , a little delicacy, dainty (post class.), Arn. 7, 231 .

Matthaeus.opening: , = Ματθαῖος , or (eu diph.), St. Matthew the evangelist : publicanus, Vulg. Matt. 10, 3 : Mattheus, as a dissyl., Prud. Apoth. 982 .

Mattĭăcus.opening: adj., of or belonging to Mattiacum (the mod. Wiesbaden ): Mattiaci fontes, the warm mineral springs of Wiesbaden, Plin. 31, 2, 17, § 20 : aquae, Amm. 29, 4, 3 : pilae, soap-balls for coloring the hair, Mart. 14, 27 :…

Mattici.grammar: cognominantur homines malarum magnarum atque oribus late patentibus
Mattici.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 126 Müll. [ ματύαι , i. q. γνάθοι , acc. to Hesych.].

mattĭŏcŏpa.opening: ματτύα-κόπτω , prop. a cutter of dainties; hence, a skinflint (late Lat.), Amm. 15, 5, 4 .

Mattĭum.opening: a city of Germany, the capital of the Chatti; acc. to some, Marburg; acc. to others, the town of Maden , near Fritzlar, Tac. A. 1, 56 .

mattus.opening: or , , adj. Sanscr. mad, to be drunk; cf. madidus , drunk, intoxicated , Petr. 41 fin.

mătŭla.opening: a vessel, pot for liquids (ante- and post-class.). In gen.: continentur mundo muliebri specula, matulae, unguenta, vasa unguentaria, Dig. 34, 2, 25, § 10 . As a term of abuse, a simpleton, noodle (cf. Engl. colloq., a…

Mātūra.opening: maturus , a goddess that presides over the ripening of fruits , Aug. Civ. Dei , 14, 8 (al. Matuta).

mātūrātĭo.opening: maturo , a hastening, accelerating , Auct. Her. 3, 2, 3 .

mātūrātor.opening: id. , one who urges on, a hastener (late Lat.): itineris inchoati, Ven. Fort. Mauril. 15.

mātūrĕfăcĭo.opening: v. a. maturus-facio , to make ripe, to ripen, mature (post-class.), Theod. Prisc. de Diaeta, 14.

mātūresco.opening: v. inch. n. [maturus], to become ripe, ripen, to come to maturity (class.). Lit. , of fruits: cum maturescere frumenta inciperent, Caes. B. G. 6, 29, 4 ; id. B. C. 3, 49 : fructus maturescens, Plin. 16, 26, 44, § 107 .—…

mātūrĭtas.opening: id. . Ripeness, maturity (class.). Lit. : frugum, Cic. Tusc. 1, 28, 68 : neque multum a maturitate aberant (frumenta), Caes. B. C. 1, 48, 5 ; frumentorum, id. ib. 3, 49 fin. : celerius occidere festinatam maturitatem,…

mātūro.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
mātūro.opening: v. a. and n. id. . Act., to make ripe, ripen, to bring to ma turity (class.). Lit. , of fruits: uvas, Tib. 1, 4, 19 : pomum, Plin. 16, 25, 41, § 102 . — Pass. : maturari, to grow ripe, ripen, to come to maturity :…

mātūrus.opening: ( sup. usually maturissimus; less freq. maturrimus, Tac. A. 12, 65 ; cf. the adv. ), adj. root, Sanscr. ma-, measure, time, whence mane, matutinus; cf.: manus, modus; hence, timely, ready in time , ripe, mature…

Mātūta.opening: root ma- of mane, maturus, q. v. . Matuta, the goddess of the morning or dawn , identical with Aurora, Lucr. 5, 656 .— A name of Ino (Gr. Λευκοθέα ), called by the Romans also Mater Matuta, Cic. Tusc. 1, 12, 28 ; id. N.…

mātūtīnālis.opening: adj. matutinus , of or belonging to the morning, early, morning- (post-class.): tempus, Auct. Carm. Phil. 15.

mātūtīnus.opening: adj. Matuta; cf.: mane, manus, maturus , of or belonging to the morning, morning- (class.): tempora, the morning hours, Cic. Fam. 7, 1, 1 : frigora, Hor. S. 2, 6, 45 : dies, the morning, Col. 6, 2, 3 : equi, i. e.…

maurella.opening: a plant , otherwise unknown, Macer. Cam. 2, 34.

Mauri.opening: ( Μαῦροι ), the Moors, Mauritanians, the inhabitants of Mauritania: proxime Hispaniam Mauri sunt, Sall. J. 18, 10 sqq.; Plin. 5, 2, 1, § 17 ; 13, 15, 29, § 91 ; Liv. 21, 22, 3 ; Mel. 1, 4, 4 .—In sing. : , , , a Moor ,…

Mausōlus.opening: , = Μαύσωλος , a king of Caria, husband of Artemisia , Cic. Tusc. 3, 31, 75 ; Gell. 10, 18, 1 sqq.; Mel. 1, 16, 3 . —Hence, , , adj., of or belonging to Mausolus, Mausolean . Lit. : sepulcrum, Prop. 3 (4), 1, 59. or…

Māvors.opening: from mah, magh, to cut; Gr. μάχη, μάχαιρα, and vor, root of vortere; i. e. the turner of the battle , old and poetic name for Mars (q. v.), the god of war, etc. Prop.: urbs Mavortis, i. e. Rome, Verg. A. 6, 872 ; 8, 630…

Maxentĭus.opening: a Roman emperor , Eutr. 10 ; Aur. Vict. Epit. 54 .—Hence, , , adj., of or belonging to the emperor Maxentius : milites, Lact. Mort. Pers. 44, 3 .

maxilla.opening: dim. of a ground-form magsula (whence māla; root mag of μάσσω, to knead; μαγεύς. baker, etc.; cf. axilla, ala, from ago) , the jawbone, jaw (postAug.). Lit. : quam litteram (X) etiam e maxillis et taxillis et vexillo…

maxillāris.opening: adj. maxilla , of or belonging to the jaw, maxillary (post-Aug.): dentes, the maxillary teeth, grinders, Cels. 6, 9 ; Plin. 11, 37, 63, § 166 ; 32, 7, 26, § 80 ; 32, 10, 50, § 139 .

maxĭmĭtas.opening: ( ), , maximus , greatness, magnitude (ante- and post-class.): immanis, Lucr. 2, 498 : se in maximitatem producere, Arn. 6, 204 .

māza.opening: , = μάζα , frumenty , for feeding dogs, Grat. Cyn. 307 .

Māzăca.opening: , = Μάζακα , the chief city of Cappadocia , now Kaisariyeh , Auct. B. Alex. 66, 4; Plin. 6, 3, 3, § 8 ; Eutr. 7, 6 . —Also, , , , Vitr. 8, 3, 9 ; Plin. 2, 108, 112, § 244 ; and , , , Plin. 6, 3, 3, § 8 .

Māzăces.opening: A people of Numidia , afterwards called Mazacenses: Mazacum turba, Suet. Ner. 30 .—In sing. collect. : , Luc. 4, 681 ; Claud. Laud. Stil. 1, 356 .— A people near the Palus Mæotis , Plin. 6, 7, 6, § 21 .

Mazĭces.opening: , = Μάζικες , a people of Numidia , the same with Mazaces, q. v., Amm. 29, 25, 21 sqq.

māzŏnŏmus.opening: (acc. to others, , , ; the form corresponds with the Greek word μαζονομος , sc. κύκλος ), a dish, charger , Varr. R. R. 3, 4, 3 : deinde secuti Mazonomo pueri magno discerpta ferentes Membra gruis, etc., Hor. S. 2, 8,…

mĕābĭlis.opening: adj. meo . * Pass., passable, that can be passed through : transitus vel bubus meabilis, Plin. 6, 1, 1, § 2 .— * Act., passing through, penetrating : aër per cuncta rerum meabilis, Plin. 2, 5, 4, § 10 .

mĕācŭlum.opening: id. , a course, passage = meatus: vos, superi caelestesque, vestra recensebitis meacula, Mart. Cap. 8, § 813 .

mĕāmet.opening: , for mea or mea ipsius: culpa, Plaut. Poen. 1, 3, 37 .

meapte.opening: , for mea or mea ipsius: causa, Ter. Heaut. 4, 3, 8 .

mĕātim.opening: adv. meus , in my manner , analog. to tuatim, after thy manner; acc. to Prisc. p. 949 P.; Donat. p. 1759 P.

mĕātor.opening: meo , a passenger, traveller, wanderer : DOLE MEATOR QVISQVIS HOC LEGIS CARMEN, Inscr. ap. Guarin. in Prosod. Lat. Fundam. p. 133: INTERPRES DIVVM COELI TERRAEQVE MEATOR, of Mercury, as the messenger of the gods, Inscr.…

mĕātus.opening: id. , a going, passing, motion, course ( poet. and post-Aug.). Lit. : solis lunaeque meatus, Lucr. 1, 128 : caeli, Verg. A. 6, 850 : aquilae, flight, Tac. H. 1, 62 : spiritus, i. e. the breathing, respiration, Quint. 7,…

mēchănēma.opening: , = μηχάνημα , a piece of mechanism, a trick (post-class.), Sid. Ep. 1, 9 .

mēchănĭcus.opening: adj. , = μηχανικός , of or belonging to mechanics, mechanical (ante-class. and post-Aug.). Adj. : disciplina, Gell. 10, 12 : opera, Lampr. Alex. Sev. 2, 2 : ars, Firm. Math. 6, 31.— Subst. , , , a mechanic , Lucil. ap.…

mēchănisma.opening: mechanical contrivance, mechanism , for mechanema (post-class.), Cassiod. Var. 1, 45 .

Mechir.opening: the name of an Egyptian month, answering nearly to the Roman January and a part of February , Plin. 6, 23, 26, § 106 .

mēcon.opening: , = μήκων , a sort of poppy : tertium genus est tithymalon, mecona vocant, Plin. 20, 19, 80, § 209 ; App. Herb. 53 ; 91 .

mēcōnis.opening: , = μηκωνἰς , a kind of lettuce with a milky juice of a soporiferous quality, like the poppy , Plin. 19, 8, 38, § 126 ; 20, 7, 26, § 67 .

mēcōnītes.opening: , = μηκωνίτης , a precious stone resembling a poppy , otherwise unknown, Plin. 37, 10, 63, § 173 .

mēcōnĭum.opening: , = μηκώνιον . Poppy-juice , Plin. 20, 18, 76, § 202 ; 25, 12, 91, § 142 .— A plant, called also peplis, Plin. 27, 12, 93, § 119 .— The excrements of new-born children , Plin. 28, 4, 13, § 52 .

mēcum.opening: , i. e. cum me, with me , like tecum, secum, etc., v. ego.

meddix.opening: ( ), , from the root med-, medeor; cf. Homeric μέδοντες , he who cares for, attends to, a curator , the title of a magistrate among the Oscans : meddix apud Oscos nomen magistratūs est. Ennius: summus ibi capitur…

Mēdēa.opening: (arch. gen. Medeaï, Enn. ap. Cic. Tusc. 3, 26, 63 ; v. Enn. p. 127, v. 292 Vahl.; nom. , acc. to id. p. 130, v. 311 Vahl.), and , , = Μήδεια , a celebrated sorceress, daughter of Æetes, king of Colchis. She assisted her…

mĕdēla.opening: ( , Lachm. ad Lucr. p. 204 ; Schol. Bob. ad Cic. Red. ad Quir. p. 251, 8 Bait.), , medeor , a healing, cure, a remedy (post-class.). Lit. : facere medelam, Gell. 12, 5, 3 : facere medelarum miracula, id. 16, 11, 2 :…

Medĕon.opening: , = Μεδεών . A city in Dalmatia , Liv. 44, 23 .— A city in Bœotia , Plin. 4, 7, 12, § 26 .

mĕdĕor.opening: v. dep. n. [root madh, to be wise; Zend, madha, the healing art; cf. μάθος , also medicus, re-med-ium], to heal, cure, be good for or against a disease (syn.: medico, sano, curo); constr. with dat. , rarely with contra…

Mēdi.opening: , = Μῆδοι , the Medes; poet. also for the Assyrians, Persians, Parthians , Mel. 1, 2, 5 ; Cic. Off. 2, 12, 41 ; Hor. C. 1, 2, 51 ; 2, 16, 6 ; Luc. 8, 386 ; Pers. 3, 53 .—In sing. : Medusque et Indus, Hor. C. 4, 14, 42 :…

mĕdĭālis.opening: adj. : medialem appellabant hostiam atram, quam meridie immolabant, Paul. ex Fest. p. 124 Müll.; cf. meridies init.

mĕdĭānus.opening: adj. medius , that is in the middle, middle (except Vitr., only post-class.): columnae, Vitr. 3, 2, 6 : acroteria, id. 3, 5, 12 : capita leonina, id. 3, 5, 15 : digitus, Veg. Vet. 2, 40, 3 : filius, Hier. Ep. 73, 3 :…

mĕdĭastīnus.opening: id. , a common servant, drudge , employed in all kinds of menial occupations (class.): tu illi mediastinus, Cato ap. Non. 143, 9 : atque bubulcus, Lucil. ib. 7 : exercitus collectus ex senibus desperatis, ex agresti…

mĕdĭātĕnus.opening: adv. mediā tenus, like hactenus , as far as the middle, half way over , Mart. Cap. 6, § 683 ; 8, § 873 init.

mĕdĭātor.opening: medius , a mediator (post-class., esp. in eccl. Lat.): tot mediatorum praesentia, App. M. 9, 36, p. 202 : mediator unius non est, Vulg. Gal. 3, 20 ; cf. v. 19; id. Heb. 8, 6 : mediator advenit, id est Deus in carne,…

Mēdĭca.opening: , = Μηδική [Media], an excellent kind of clover introduced from Media; Burgundy-clover, lucern (Medicago sativa), Verg. G. 1, 215 ; Plin. 18, 16, 43, § 144 ; Varr. R. R. 1, 42 .

mĕdĭca.opening: a female physician; v 1. medicus, II. B.

mĕdĭcābĭlis.opening: adj. medicor . Pass., that can be healed or cured, curable ( poet. and not ante-Aug.): nullis amor est medicabilis herbis, Ov. M. 1, 523 ; id. H. 5, 149 : vulnus, Sil. 10, 416 .— Act., healing, curative, medicinal…

mĕdĭcābŭlum.opening: id. , a healthy place (post-class.): aegris medicabula, App Flor. p. 353, 6 .

mĕdĭcāmen.opening: id. , a drug, medicament , in a good and a bad sense, meaning both a healing substance, remedy, medicine , and, as also medicamentum and the Gr. φάρμακον , a poisonous drug, poison (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose;…

mĕdĭcāmentārĭus.opening: adj. medicamentum , of or belonging to drugs or to poisons; only subst. , , A druggist, apothecary , Plin. 19, 6, 33, § 110 .— A preparer of poisons : homicida vel medicamentarius, Cod. Th. 3, 16, 1.— , , , a female…

mĕdĭcāmentōsus.opening: adj. id. , that has a healing power, medicinal (perh. only ἅπαξ εἰρημ .; in Cato, R. R. 157, 2 dub.; al. medicamento): aqua, Vitr. 8, 3, 4 .

mĕdĭcāmentum.opening: medicor , a drug, remedy, physic, medicine, medicament . Lit. : medicamentum alicui dare ad aquam intercutem, Cic. Off. 3, 24, 92 : haurire, Plin. 24, 19, 113, § 174 : sumere, to take, Curt. 3, 6, 3 : componere, to…

mĕdĭcātĭo.opening: id. , lit., a healing, cure; hence, in agriculture, a besprinkling with vegetable juices , e. g., of lentils, to preserve them from the corn-worm, Col. 2, 10, 16 .

mĕdĭcātor.opening: id. , a physician (post-class.): annunciari Christum medicatorem, Tert. adv. Marc. 3, 17 ; Avien. Arat. 216 .

mĕdĭcātus.opening: medicor , a charm ( poet. ), Ov. H. 12, 165 .

mĕdĭcīnālis.opening: adj. medicina , of or pertaining to medicine, medical, medicinal (not ante-Aug.): ars, Cels. praef.: cucurbitulae, cupping-glasses, Plin. 32, 10, 42, § 123 : mortarium, id. 36, 22, 43, § 157 : scalprum, Scrib. Compos.…

mĕdĭcīnus.opening: adj. 1. medicus , of or belonging to a physician or surgeon, medical (as adj. only ante- and post-class.; as subst. class.). Adj. : ars, the healing art, medicine, Varr. L. L. 5, § 93 Müll.; Hyg. Fab. 274 ; Aug. Conf.…

mĕdĭco.opening: v. a. 1. medicus , to heal, cure ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose for the class. medeor). Lit. With acc. : ego istum lepide medicabo metum, Plaut. Most. 2, 1, 40 : (apes) odore galbani, Col. 9, 13, 7 : vulneris aestus,…

mĕdĭcor.opening: v. dep. a. [id.], to heal, cure . Lit. ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). With dat. : senibus medicantur anhelis, Verg. G. 2, 135 .— With acc. : cuspidis ictum, Verg. A. 7, 756 .— Trop. , to cure, relieve (ante-class.):…

mĕdĭcōsus.opening: adj. id. , healing (post-class.): fomentationes, Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 1 .

mĕdĭcus.opening: medeor , of or pertaining to healing, healing, curative, medical (as adj. , poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Adj. : medicas adhibere manus ad vulnera, Verg. G. 3, 455 : ars, Ov. Tr. 5, 6, 12 : potus, Nemes. Cyn. 222 :…

mĕdĭĕtas.opening: medius , the middle, place in the middle, midst (in Cic. only as transl. of the Gr. μεσότης ; elsewhere postclass.). Lit. : vix audeo dicere medietates, quas Graeci μεσότητας appellant, Cic. Univ. 7, 20 : narium, Lact.…

mĕdĭlūnĭus.opening: adj. mediusluna , in the middle of the month, having half a disk, half-orbed (post-class): (luna) primo est corniculata, deinde medilunia, Mart. Cap. 7, § 738 .

mĕdimnum.opening: , and , , , = μέδιμνος , a Greek measure of corn, a Greek bushel (containing six modii): primus, secundus, tertius medimnus, Lucil. ap. Non. 213, 21 ; so in masc. form, Nep. Att. 2 fin. : medimnum tritici seritur, Cic.…

mĕdĭo.opening: v. a. medius , to halve, divide in the middle (post-class.), Apic. 3, 9 . — Neutr., to be in the middle : melius Juno mediante, Pall. Mart. 10, 32 .

mĕdĭō^crĭcŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [mediocris], rather middling : exercitus, Cato ap. Fest. p. 154 , and Paul. ex Fest. p. 155 Müll.

mĕdĭō^cris.opening: (ō usually; rarely ŏ), adj. medius , in a middle state between too much and too little, middling, moderate, tolerable, ordinary; sometimes also, not remarkable, indifferent, mediocre . In gen. (class.). Lit. , of size,…

mĕdĭō^crĭtas.opening: mediocris . A middle state, a medium, mean; moderateness, moderation (class.): mediocritatem illam tenere, quae est inter nimium et parum, Cic. Off. 1, 25, 89 ; 1, 39, 140 : in dicendo, mediocrity, id. de Or. 1, 25, 117…

Mĕdĭōlānum.opening: or , , A city in Gallia Cisalpina, the capital of the Insubres , the mod. Milan . Form Mediolanum, Plin. 3, 17, 21, § 124 ; Just. 29, 5, 8 ; Tac. H. 1, 70 ; Aus. de Clar. Urb. 4, 1 . Form Mediolanium, Liv. 5, 34, 9 ;…

Mĕdĭōmātrĭci.opening: a people of Gaul, on the Moselle, in the neighborhood of Metz , Caes. B. G. 4, 10 .—Hence, , , adj. —In sing. , Inscr. Grut. 731, 12 ; and in fem. , Inscr. Orell. 3523 .

Mĕdĭon.opening: a city of Acarnania , Liv. 36, 11, 10 ; 36, 12, 1 ; 44, 23, 3 .— Hence, , , adj., of or belonging to Medion.—Plur. subst. : , , , the inhabitants of Medion , Liv. 36, 12, 3 .

mĕdĭoxĭmus.opening: ( ), , adj. superlative of an obsolete mediox for medius . In the middle, middlemost : medio actum modo, Non. 141, 4 : medioximus, μέσος , Gloss. Philox. (anteand post-class.): medioxumam quam duxit uxorem, Plaut. Cist.…

medipontus.opening: a kind of thick rope (ante-class.): medipontos privos loreos (al. melipontos), Cato, R. R. 3, 5 ; 12 .

mĕdĭtābundus.opening: adj. meditor , earnestly meditating, designing; with acc. (post-class.): Romanum meditabundus bellum, Just. 38, 3, 7 .

mĕdĭtāmen.opening: id. , a thinking of any thing, a preparation ( poet. ): meditamina belli, Sil. 8, 326 : rerum, Prud. Psych. 234 .

mĕdĭtāmentum.opening: id. , a thinking of any thing, a preparation . In gen.: belli, Tac. H. 4, 26 ; id. A. 15, 35 : arietum meditamenta, thoughtfully prepared battering-rams, Amm. 23, 4, 10 .— * In partic.; plur. : puerilia, rudiments…

mĕdĭtātĭo.opening: meditor , a thinking over any thing, contemplation, meditation (class.). Lit. (very rare): stultam esse meditationem futuri mali, aut fortasse ne futuri quidem, Cic. Tusc. 3, 15, 32 . — Transf. Preparation for any thing…

mĕdĭtātĭuncŭlā.opening: dim. of meditatio , a small or trifling preparation , Claud. Mam. de Stat. Anim. 1, 3 .

mĕdĭtātīvus.opening: adj. meditor , meditative (post-class.): meditativa verba, which signify a desire to perform an action , also called desiderativa (as lecturio, etc.), Diom. p. 336 P.; Prisc. 825 ib.

mĕdĭtātor.opening: id. , one who thinks or plans, a meditator (post-class.): meditator (al. meditatus), Prud. στεφ . 5, 265.

mĕdĭtātōrĭum.opening: meditator . A preparation (eccl. Lat.): meditatorium Evangelii, Hier. Ep. 78 .— A place of preparation , Hier. in Jovin. 2, 12 .

mĕdĭtātus.opening: meditor , a thinking, meditating upon any thing, a meditation , i. q. meditatio (post-class.), App. M. 3, p. 135, 31 .

mĕdĭ-terrānĕus.opening: adj. mediusterra , midland, inland, remote from the sea, mediterranean (opp. to maritimus). Adj. (class.): nascitur ibi plumbum album in mediterraneis regionibus, in maritimis ferrum, Caes. B. G. 5, 12, 5 : locus (opp.…

mĕdĭterrĕus.opening: id. , inland, remote from the sea , another form of the preceding word: mediterream melius quam mediterraneam Sisenna dici putat, Paul. ex Fest. p. 123, 22 Müll.

mĕdĭtor.opening: v. dep. a. and Sanscr. madh-a, wisdom; Gr. μάθος, μανθάνω, μήδομαι; cf.: medeor, re-med-ium, etc. ; act., to think or reflect upon, to muse over, consider, meditate upon; neutr., to think, reflect, muse, consider,…

Mĕdĭtrīna.opening: medeor, with fem. suffix -tri-, as in nutrix, genetrix; v. Corss. Ausspr. 2, 522 , the goddess of Healing; v. the foll. art.

Mĕdĭtrīnālĭa.opening: Meditrina , a festival celebrated on the 11 th of October in honor of Meditrina (on which occasion a libation of new wine was made for the first time): Octobri mense Meditrinalia dies dictus a medendo, quod Flaccus…

mĕdĭtullĭum.opening: medius and tollus, old form of tellus, q. v. , the middle (ante- and post-class.): in finitimo, legitimo, aeditimo non plus inesse timum, quam in meditullio, tullium, Serv. ap. Cic. Top. 8, 36 : in ipso meditullio…

mĕdĭus.opening: adj. Sanscr. madhya, the same; Gr. μέσος; Angl. - Sax. midd; Germ. Mitte; cf. dimidius, meridies (medi-), etc. , that is in the middle or midst, mid, middle (class.). Adj. Lit. : terra complexa medium mundi locum, Cic.…

Medobrēga.opening: ( , ), , , a city in Lusitania , now Portalegre , Auct. B. Alex. 48, 4.—Hence, , , , the inhabitants of Medobrega , Auct. B. Alex. 48; Plin. 4, 22, 35, § 118 ; al. Medubricenses.—Also written † MEIDVBRIGENSES, Inscr.…

Mĕdon.opening: , = Μέδων . A Centaur , Ov. M. 12, 303 .— Son of Codrus, king of Athens, the first archon; hence, , , , his descendants , Vell. 1, 2, 2 .— One of Penelope's suitors; acc. Medonta, Sabin. Ep. 1, 47.

Mĕdŭli.opening: a people in Aquitanian Gaul, whose coast was famous for its oysters , in the mod. Medoc , Aus. Ep. 4, 2 ; 7, 1 .—Hence, or , , adj., of or belonging to the Meduli, Medulian , Plin. 32, 6, 21, § 62 .— , , adj., Medulian…

mĕdulla.opening: medius , the marrow of bones; the pith of plants (class.). Lit. , Hor. Epod. 5, 37 : cumque albis ossa medullis, Ov. M. 14, 208 : ossa regum vacuis exsucta medullis, Juv. 8, 90 : per media foramina a cerebro medullā…

mĕdullāris.opening: adj. medulla , situated in the marrow or inmost part (post-class.): dolor, App. M. 7, p. 193, 26 .

mĕdullātus.opening: adj. id. , possessed of marrow, marrowy; hence, rich, fat, abounding in richness (post-class.): convivium pinguium medullatorum, Vulg. Isa. 25, 6 ; cf. id. ib. 34, 6 .

Mĕdulli.opening: an Alpine people in Sabaudia, Inscr. ap. Plin. 3, 20, 24, § 137 ; Vitr. 8, 3, 20 .—Hence, , , adj., of or belonging to the Medulli, Medullian : Medullini te feret aura noti, i. e. Alpine wind, Aus. Ep. 5, 27 .

Medullĭa.opening: , or , , , a little town in Latium , near the modern Monte Verde , Liv. 1, 33, 4 ; Plin. 3, 5, 9, § 68 . —Hence, , , adj., of or belonging to Medullia, Medullian; as subst. , , , a Roman surname; e. g. L. Furius…

mĕdullĭtus.opening: adv. medulla , in the marrow, to the very marrow, in the inmost part (ante- and post-class.). Lit. : medullitus aquiloniam intus servat frigedinem, Varr. ap. Non. 139, 9 .— Trop. , inwardly, from the heart, thoroughly :…

mĕdullo.opening: v. a. id. , to fill with marrow (post-class.): cura nimia medullatos artus magni facit, App. Dogm. Plat. 2, 16, p. 21, 13 : quando ossa incipiunt medullari, Aug. Anim. 4, 5 ; Ven. Carm. 3, 7 fin.

mĕdullōsus.opening: adj. id. , full of marrow, marrowy (post-Aug.): umerus, Cels. 8, 1, 102 sq.

Medullus.opening: a mountain in Hispania Tarraconensis, Flor. 4, 12, 50 ; Oros. 6, 21 .

Mēdus.opening: , = Μῆδος , a small river of Persia, a tributary of the Araxes, now the Polwar , Curt. 5, 4, 7 ; v. also Medi.

Mĕdūsa.opening: , = Μέδουσα , daughter of Phorcus; she captivated Neptune with her golden hair, and became by him the mother of Pegasus. Minerva, as a punishment, turned her hair into serpents, and gave to her eyes an enchanted power…

Mĕgăbocchus.opening: and , , —Caius, a prætor in Sardinia , Cic. Scaur. § 40; id. Att. 2, 7, 3 Orell.

Mĕgăbyzus.opening: , = Μεγάβυζος . A priest of Diana at Ephesus , Plin. 35, 10, 36, § 93 .— One of Darius's generals , Just. 7, 3, 7 .— The name of a Persian eunuch , Quint. 5, 12, 21 .

Mĕgaera.opening: , = Μέγαιρα . One of the Furies , Verg. A. 12, 846 ; Claud. Rapt. Pros. 3, 387 .— Transf. , a fury : Megaera quaedam mortalis, Amm. 14, 1, 2 .

Mĕgălē.opening: , = Μεγάλη (the great, exalted), a surname of the Magna Mater, Calend. Verrii Fl. in Inscr. Orell. 2, p. 389 ; v. the foll. — Derivv. ( ), , adj. Of or belonging to the Magna Mater (only postAug.): ludorum Megalesium…

Mĕgălensĭa.opening: or , , and , v. Megale, II. A.

Mĕgālĭa.opening: a small island of Campania , the modern Castel dell' Ovo , Stat. S. 2, 2, 80 ; called also Megaris, Plin. 3, 6, 12, § 82 .

mĕgălīum.opening: ( ), , , = μεγάλειον , a kind of ointment : postea multo successit propter gloriam appellatum megalium, ex oleo balanino, balsamo, calamo, junco, xylobalsamo, casia, resina, Plin. 13, 1, 2, § 13 .

mĕgălŏgrăphĭa.opening: , = μεγαλογραφία , the painting of large or grand subjects (opp. ῥυπαρογραφία , the painting of small subjects), Vitr. 7, 4, 4 ; 7, 5, 2 .

Mĕgălŏbūsus.opening: ( ), , , = Μεγαλόβυζος , the father of Theotimus , Plaut. Bacch. 2, 3, 74 .

Mĕgălŏpŏlis.opening: , or ( acc. ), , = Μεγαλόπολις or Μεγάλη πόλις , a city of Arcadia, the birthplace of Polybius .—Form Megalopolis, Liv. 36, 31, 6 ; 45, 28, 4 .—Form Megale polis, Plin. 4, 6, 10, § 20 ; Liv. 32, 5, 5 ; 35, 36, 10…

Mĕgăpenthes.opening: , = Μεγαπένθης , a son of Prœtus , Hyg. Fab. 244 .

Mĕgăra.opening: wife of Hercules, whom, in his madness, he destroyed, together with her children , Hyg. Fab. 31 .

Mĕgărensis.opening: adj. 2. Megara , of or belonging to the city of Megara : Nicias, of Megara, Plin. 7, 56, 57, § 196 : homines Gell. 6, 10, 3 .

Mĕgărēus.opening: ( ), , adj. = Μεγαρεῖος , of or belonging to the city of Megara (in Megaris), Megarean (class.): Euclides Socratis discipulus, Megareus, Cic. Ac. 2, 42, 129 .

Mĕgărēa.opening: plur. , for Megara (a city of Sicily), or for Megarensia , sc. arva, Ov. F. 4, 471 .

Mĕgăreus.opening: ( ), , , = Μεγαρεύς , a son of Neptune, and father of Hippomenes , Hyg. Fab. 157 and 185; Ov. M. 10, 605 .—Hence, , , adj., of or belonging to Megareus, Megareian ( poet. ): heros, i. e. Hippomenes, Ov. M. 10, 659 .

Mĕgărĭcus.opening: adj. , = Μεγαρικός , of or belonging to the city of Megara, Megaric : ager, Plin. 17, 7, 4, § 42 : Megaricus sinus, a part of the Saronic Gulf, near Megara, id. 4, 12, 19, § 57 : signa, i. e. of marble from Megara, Cic.…

Mĕgăris.opening: , = Μεγαρίς . A country of Greece, between Attica and Phocis , Mel. 2, 3, 4 ; Plin. 4, 7, 11, § 23 .— A city of Sicily, also called Megara, Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 25, § 63 ; Plin. 3, 8, 14, § 89 .

Mĕgărus.opening: adj. 2. Megara , of or belonging to the city of Megara, Megarean ( poet. ): sinus, Verg. A. 3, 689 .

Mĕgas.opening: , = μέγας , a surname; e. g. Demetrius Megas, Cic. Fam. 13, 36, 1 .

Mĕges.opening: , = Μέγης , son of Phyleus, one of Helen's suitors , Hyg. Fab. 97 .

mĕgistānes.opening: , = μεγιστᾶνες the grandees of a kingdom, the magnates who were in the king's suite, Sen. Ep. 21, 4 ; Tac. A. 15, 27 ; Suet. Calig. 5 .

Mĕgistē.opening: , = Μεγίστη , a Roman name given to slaves , Inscr. Fabr. p. 189 , n. 433.

Mĕgistō.opening: , = Μεγιστώ , daughter of Ceteus , Hyg. Astr. 2, 1 .

mēio.opening: v. n. for migio, kindred with Sanscr. mih, effundere; whence also mingo; cf. Gr. ὀμιχέω, ὀμίχλη , to make water : sacer est locus, extra Meiite, Pers. 1, 114 : HOSPES AD HVNC TVMVLVM NE MEIAS, Inscr. Orell. 4781 : mala…

mĕl.opening: ( abl. sing. melli, Plaut. Truc. 2, 4, 20 .— Gen. and dat. plur. obsol. acc. to Prisc. p. 744 P.), Gr. μέλι, honey; μέλισσα, bee; cf. mulsus , honey . Lit. : hoc est melli dulci dulcius, Plaut. Truc. 2, 4, 20 (Spengel,…

Mĕla.opening: prob. from μέλας , a Roman proper name , Cic. Phil. 13, 2, 3 : Pomponius Mela, a Roman geographer, a native of Spain, under the emperor Claudius; v. Teuffel, Röm. Litt. § 291.

Melae.opening: a town in the Samnite country , Liv. 24, 20 ; called also , , Liv. 27, 1 .

Melambĭum.opening: a place in Thessaly, near Scotussa , Liv. 33, 6 .

mĕlamphyllon.opening: , = μελάμφυλλον , a plant, also called acanthus and paederos, Plin. 22, 22, 34, § 76 .

Mĕlampūs.opening: , = Μελάμπους . Son of Amythāon, a celebrated physician and soothsayer , Cic. Leg. 2, 13, 33 ; Verg. G. 3, 550 ; Stat. Th. 3, 452 .— Son of Atreus , Cic. N. D. 3, 21, 53 .— Name of a dog , Ov. M. 3, 206 .

mĕlănăĕtos.opening: , = μελανάετος , the black eagle; a small species of eagle, Plin. 10, 3, 3, § 6 .

Mĕlanchaetes.opening: , = Μελαγχαίτης , black-hair , the name of a dog, Ov. M. 3, 232 .

mĕlanchŏlĭcus.opening: adj. , = μελαγχολικός , having black bile, atrabilious, melancholy : Aristoteles quidem ait, omnes ingeniosos melancholicos esse, Cic. Tusc. 1, 33, 80 ; cf. id. Div. 1, 37, 81 : insania, Plin. 22, 25, 64, § 133 :…

mĕlancŏrўphos.opening: , = μελαγκόρυφος (having a black crown), the black cap , the name of a kind of snipe, Plin. 10, 29, 44, § 86 : genus avium, quae Latine vocantur atricapillae, eo, quod summa eorum capita nigra sunt, Paul. ex Fest. p.…

mĕlancrānis.opening: , = μελάγκρανις (black-head), a kind of rush with black seeds , Plin. 21, 18, 69, § 112 .

mĕlandrўum.opening: , = μελάνδρυον , a piece of salted tunny-fish : ceterā parte plenis pulpamentis sale asservantur melandrya vocantur, caesis quercus assulis simillima, i. e. like the black heart of oak, Plin. 9, 15, 18, § 48 ; Mart. 3,…

Mĕlăneus.opening: ( ), , , = Μελανεύς . Name of a Centaur , Ov. M. 12, 306 .— Name of a dog , Ov. M. 3, 223 .

mĕlănĭa.opening: , = μελανία ( μέλας , Cels. 5, 28, 19 ), blackness, black spots , of the skin (post-Aug.), Plin. 24, 8, 29, § 44 ; 26, 14, 88, § 149 Sillig. (Jan. malandrias).

Mĕlănippē.opening: , = Μελανίππη . Daughter of Desmon or Æolus, the mother by Neptune of Bœotus and Æolus, the founders of Bœotia and Æolia , Hyg. Fab. 186 ; Varr. R. R. 2, 5, 5 .— Acc. plur. : Melanippas, Arn. 4, 26 . She was the subject…

Mĕlănĭus.opening: a Roman proper name , Inscr. Mur. 858, 5.

mĕlantērĭa.opening: ( gen. sing. melanterias), = μελαντηρία , blacking , Scrib. Comp. 208 .

mĕlanthĕmum.opening: , a reading in Plin. 22, 21, 26, § 53 , for melanthion.

mĕlanthĭum.opening: ( ), , , = μελάνθιον , the plant gith, cultivated fennel-flower : gith e Graecis alii melanthion, alii melaspermon, vocant, Plin. 20, 17, 71, § 182 ; Col. poët. 10, 245; also chamomile , Plin. 22, 21, 26, § 53 .—Called…

Mĕlanthĭus.opening: , = Μελάνθιος . A goatherd of Ulysses , Ov. H. 1, 95 .— A celebrated painter , Plin. 35, 7, 32, § 50 ; 35, 10, 36, § 76 .

Mĕlanthō.opening: , = Μελανθώ , a seanymph, daughter of Neptune , Ov. M. 6, 120 ; cf. Serv. ad Verg. A. 5, 373 .

Mĕlanthus.opening: , = Μέλανθος . A river in Sarmatia , Ov. P. 4, 10, 54 .— One of the seamen whom Bacchus changed into dolphins , Ov. M. 3, 617 .— The father of the Athenian king Codrus , Vell. 1, 2, 1 .— Hence, ( ), , adj., of or…

Melantĭas.opening: , = Μελαντιάς , a town of Thrace, between the Propontis and the Pontus Euxinus , Amm. 30, 11, 1 .

mĕlănūrus.opening: , = μελάνουρος (black-tail), a kind of sea-fish , Enn. ap. App. Mag. p. 299 (Heduph. v. 7 Vahl.); Ov. Hal. 113 ; Col. 8, 16, 8 ; Plin. 32, 2, 8, § 17 ; 32, 11, 53, § 149 .

mēlăpĭum.opening: , = μηλάπιον , an apple-pear , a kind of apple resembling a pear (al. melapia, melappia), Plin. 15, 14, 15, § 51 .

Mĕlas.opening: , = Μέλας (black). The name of several rivers. A river of Bœotia , now Mavropotami , Plin. 2, 103, 106, § 230 ; Sen. Q. N. 3, 25, 3 ; Stat. Th. 7, 273 .— A river of Thrace , now Kavatch , Liv. 38, 40, 5 ; Mela, 2, 2, 8;…

mĕlas.opening: , = μέλας , a black spot on the skin , Cels. 5, 28, 18 ; cf. melania.

mĕlaspermon.opening: , = μελάνσπερμον , the plant gith, cultivated fennel-flower (v. melanthium), Plin. 20, 17, 71, § 182 .

melcŭlum.opening: , and , , dim. mel; v. melliculus , a term of endearment, = melliculum, Plaut. ap. Prisc. p. 610 P. (where some read melliculum); applied to a male person, in the voc. melcule: vale mel gentium, melcule, ebur ex…

Meldi.opening: a people of Gallia Celtica, between the Seine and Marne; their chief town answered to the modern Meaux , Caes. B. G. 5, 5 ; Plin. 4, 18, 32, § 107 .

mĕlē.opening: , Gr. plur. of melos, v. 1. melos.

Mĕlĕăger.opening: and ( ), , , = Μελέαγρος , son of the Calydonian king Œneus and Althæa, one of the combatants at the Calydonian boar-hunt. His life depended on the preservation of an extinguished brand; this his mother burned, out of…

mēles.opening: ( ) and ( ), , , a marten or badger , Varr. R. R. 3, 12, 3 ; Plin. 8, 38, 58, § 138 ; Grat. Cyneg. 340 .

Mĕles.opening: plur., a village in the Samnite territory , Liv. 27, 1, 1 .

Melessi.opening: a people in Hispania Baetica, Liv. 28, 3 .

Mĕlĕtē.opening: , = Μελέτη . One of the Muses , Cic. N. D. 3, 21, 54 .— A Roman surname : PORCIA MELETE, Inscr. Grut. 357, 7.— The name of a plant, called also chamaeleon, App. Herb. 25 .

Meletīdes.opening: a foolish Athenian , App. Mag. p. 289, 26 .

Mĕlĭboea.opening: , = Μελίβοια , a maritime town of Thessaly, at the foot of Mount Ossa, the birthplace of Philoctetes , now Kastri , Mel. 2, 3 ; Plin. 4, 7, 16, § 32 ; Liv. 36, 13, 6 ; 44, 13 .—Hence, Derivv. , , adj., Melibœan :…

mēlĭca.opening: , perh. a kind of vessel (ante-class.), Varr. ap. Non. 545, 4 ; 12 and 23.

mĕlĭcēris.opening: , = μελικηρίς , a kind of tumor, meliceris (the yellow matter of which looks like honey): melilotos contra meliceridas efficax, Plin. 21, 20, 87, § 151 .—In sing. , Veg. Vet. 2, 30 (in Cels. 5, 26, 20 , called μελίκηρα…

Mĕlĭcerta.opening: and , , , = Μελικέρτης , son of Ino and the Theban king Athamas. His mother, pursued by her husband in his madness, threw herself into the sea with Melicerta, who became a seagod, called by the Greeks Palaemon, and by…

mĕlichlōros.opening: , = μελίχλωρος , a precious stone yellow as honey , Plin. 37, 11, 73, § 191 .

mĕlichros.opening: , = μελίχρως , a precious stone of the color of honey , Plin. 37, 11, 73, § 191 .

mĕlĭcus.opening: adj. , = μελικός , musical, tuneful, melodious : sonores, Lucr. 5, 334 .— In partic., lyric, lyrical : poëma, Cic. Opt. Gen. Or. 1, 1 .— Subst. : , , , a lyric poet : Simonides melicus, Plin. 7, 24, 24, § 89 ; 7, 56,…

Mēlĭcus.opening: adj. , in vulg. lang. for Medicus, Median : gallinae, Varr. R. R. 3, 9, 19 ; Col. 8, 2, 4 ; Plin. 10, 21, 24, § 48 .

Mĕlĭē.opening: , or , , , = Μελία . A sea-nymph : Hestiaea, Melie, Ianthe, Hyg. Fab. praef.— A Bithynian nymph, beloved by the river-god Inachus , Ov. Am. 3, 6, 25 .

mĕlĭlōtos.opening: , = μελίλωτος , a kind of clover, melilot, also called sertula Campana: pars meliloton amant, Ov. F. 4, 440 ; cf. Plin. 21, 11, 37, § 63 ; 21, 7, 18, § 39 .

mĕlĭmēla.opening: plur. , = μελίμηλα , honey-apples , previously called mustapples (mustea mala): quae antea mustea vocabant, nunc melimela appellant, Varr. R. R. 1, 59 ; cf.: mustea a celeritate mitescendi, quae nunc melimela dicuntur a…

mēlīnus.opening: adj. 1. meles , of or belonging to the marten; only subst. (sc. crumena): , , , a purse or wallet of marten-skin , Plaut. Ep. 1, 1, 20 .

mĕlĭnus.opening: adj. mel , of or belonging to honey, honey-; only subst. : , , , mead : melinam promere, Plaut. Ps. 2, 4, 51 (al. mellinam); id. Ep. 1, 1, 21 (al. mellina).

mēlĭnus.opening: adj. , = μήλινος , of or belonging to quinces, quince-; quinceyellow; only as subst. : , , (Sc. oleum.) Quince-oil , Plin. 13, 1, 2, § 11 ; 23, 6, 54, § 103 .— (Sc. unguentum.) Quince-ointment , Plin. 13, 1, 2, § 5 .—…

Mēlĭnus.opening: adj. Melos , of or belonging to the island of Melos, Melian; subst. : , , , a kind of white color, Melian white : pigmentum, or simply Melinum, Plaut. Most. 1, 3, 106 Lorenz ad loc.; cf. Plin. 35, 6, 17, § 36 ; Vitr. 7,…

mĕlĭor.opening: cf. μᾶλλον, for μάλιον , v. bonus.

mĕlĭōrātĭo.opening: melioro , a bettering, improvement, melioration (post-class.), Cod. Just. 4, 66, 2 ; 2, 19, 24 .

mĕlĭōresco.opening: v. inch. n. , to begin to improve, grow better; βελτιοῦμαι , Gloss. Philox.

mĕlĭōro.opening: (no perf. ), , v. a. melior , to make better, to better, improve (postclass.): meliorare proprietatem, Dig. 7, 1, 13 : melioratum praedium, Cod. Just. 5, 71, 16 ; Cassiod. Var. 9, 3 .

mĕlisphyllum.opening: and , , , = μελίφυλλον and μελισσόφυλλον (honey-leaf, bee-leaf), an herb of which bees are fond, balm-gentle, balm (also called apiastrum): trita melis phylla, et cerinthae ignobile gramen, Verg. G. 4, 63 ; Plin. 20,…

Mĕlissa.opening: , = Μέλισσα . A nymph who is said to have invented the art of keeping bees , Col. 9, 2, 3 .— Daughter of the Cretan king Melissus, who, together with her sister Amalthea, fed Jupiter with goats' milk , Lact. 1, 22, 19 sq

Mĕlissus.opening: , = Μέλισσος . (Also called , = Μελισσεύς .) A king of Crete, father of Melissa and Amalthea , Lact. 1, 22, 19 ; ib. § 28.— A grammarian and comic poet, librarian to Augustus , Ov. P. 4, 16, 30 ; cf. Suet. Gram. 21 .— A…

Mĕlĭta.opening: , or , , , = Μελίτη . The isle of Malta , Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 46, § 103 ; Plin. 3, 8, 14, § 92 .— An island off the coast of Dalmatia , now Meleda , Plin. 3, 26, 30, § 152 ; Ov. F. 3, 567 .— A city of Ionia , Vitr. 4, 1 .—…

Mĕlĭtaeus.opening: adj. , = Μελιταῖος , of or belonging to the Dalmatian island Melita, Melitæan : catuli, Plin. 30, 5, 14, § 43 .

Mĕlĭtānus.opening: adj., of or belonging to Melita, Melitan , Inscr. Grut. 751, 3 .

Mĕlĭtensis.opening: adj. Melita , of or belonging to the isle of Malta, Melitan, Maltese : vestis, Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 72, § 176 : rosa, id. ib. 2, 5, 11 , § 27.—In plur. subst. : , (sc. vestimenta), Melitan garments , Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 74, §…

Mĕlĭtēsĭus.opening: adj. id. , Melitan, Maltese : Melitesia Coralia (al. Melitensia), Grat. Cyn. 404 .

mĕlĭtĭnus.opening: adj. , = μελίτινος , of or belonging to honey, mixed with honey (post-class.): cera, Plin. Val. 3, 26 .— Lapis, a kind of precious stone , Plin. 36, 19, 33, § 140 .

Mĕlĭtīnus.opening: a Roman proper name , Inscr. Visc. Opt. Varr. t. 1, p. 182; Inscr. Fabr. p. 45 , n. 255.

mĕlĭtītes.opening: , = μελιτίτης , a honey-drink made of honey and must , Plin. 14, 9, 11, § 85 (but a false read. for melitinus, Plin. 36, 19, 33, § 140 ).

mĕlittaena.opening: ( ), , , = μελίτταινα . A plant, also called marrubium, App. Herb. 45 .— A plant, also called melissophyllon, Plin. 21, 20, 86, § 149 .

mĕlitturgus.opening: , = μελιττουργός , a bee-keeper , Varr. R. R. 3, 16, 3 .

mĕlĭus.opening: comp. adj. and adv. , v. bonus.

Mēlĭus.opening: adj. 2. Melos , of or belonging to the isle of Melos, Melian : Diagoras Melius, dwelling in Melos, Cic. N. D. 1, 1, 2 .

mĕlĭuscŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [melius], somewhat better, rather better (anteclass. and post-Aug.).—Of a convalescent: qui meliusculus esse coepit, Cels. 3, 22 ; Ter. Hec. 3, 2, 19 .—Of things: si eris verax, ex tuis rebus feceris…

mella.opening: mel , perh. for mellea (sc. aqua), honey-water (post-Aug.), Col. 12, 11, 1 ; 12, 49, 3 .

Mella.opening: a Roman surname in the gens Annaea, e. g. M. Annaeus Mella, the father of Lucan.

mellācĕum.opening: mel , must (postclass. for sapa): sapa, quod nunc mellaceum dicimus, mustum ad mediam partem decoctum, Non. 551, 21 .

Mellāria.opening: a city in Hispania Baetica, Plin. 3, 1, 3, § 7 —Hence, , , adj., of or belonging to Mellaria; in plur. subst. : , , , the inhabitants of Mellaria , Inscr. Grut. 321, 10 .

mellārĭus.opening: adj. mel , of or belonging to honey, honey- (post-Aug.): vasa mellaria, Plin. 21, 14, 49, § 82 .—Hence, subst. , , , a bee-keeper, beemaster (ante-class.), Varr. R. R. 3, 16, 17 .— , , , a beehive, apiary , Varr. R. R.…

mellātĭo.opening: mello , a honeying, honey-gathering, taking of honey from the hive , Col. 11, 2, 50 : aestiva, Plin. 11, 15, 15, § 41 .

mellĕus.opening: adj. mel , of or belonging to honey, honey- (post-Aug.). Lit. : sapor, Plin. 15, 14, 15, § 51 : color, id. 11, 16, 16, § 48 : sardonyches, id. 37, 6, 23, § 89 : sucus, id. 36, 19, 33, § 140 : crustum, Aus. Eph. Parecb.…

mellĭcŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [id.], honey-sweet, honeyed : corpusculum melliculum! a coaxing epithet, Plaut. Cas. 4, 4, 23 . — Subst. : , , , honey-pet, honey-kin. Plaut. Cas. 4, 4, 14 .—Collat. form melculum, q. v.

mellĭfer.opening: adj. mel-fero , honey-bearing, honey-producing, melliferous (pcet.): apes, Ov. M. 15, 383 : exercitus, Claud. Rapt. Pros. 2, 127 .

mellĭfex.opening: mel-facio , i. q. mellarius, 1., a honey-maker , i. e. a keeper of bees : ubicunque saltus idonei sunt mellifici, Col. 9, 8, 8 ; better referred to mellificus, q. v.

mellĭfĭcĭum.opening: id. , the making of honey : ad mellificium aptissimum est thymum, Varr. R. R. 3, 16, 4 ; Col. 9, 13, 13 .

mellĭfĭco.opening: v. a. mellificus , to make honey (poet and in post-Aug. prose): sic vos non vobis mellificatis apes, Verg. ap Don. Vit. Verg. (but ap. Plin. 11, 18, 19, § 59 , mella faciunt; v. Sillig).

mellĭfĭcus.opening: adj. mel-facio , honey-making, fit for making honey (postAug.): opus, Col. 9, 13, 14 : saltus, id. 9, 8, 8 ; v. mellifex.

melliflŭens.opening: adj. mel-fluo , honey-dropping; trop., mellifluous , of a speaker: Nestor, Aus. Epist. 16, 14 .

melliflŭus.opening: adj. id. , flowing with honey, honey-dropping (post-class.). Lit. : antra, Avien. Perieg. 468 .— Trop. , mellifluous : Homerus melliflui oris, Boëth. Metr. 5, 2, 2.

mellĭgĕnus.opening: adj. , a false read. for melliginis, Plin. 16, 7, 10, § 28 .

mellĭger.opening: adj. mel-gero , honey-bearing (late Lat.), Aldh. Laud. Virgin. 4 .

mellīgo.opening: mel . A honey-like juice , sucked by the bees from flowers, but not yet made into honey, bee-glue, bees'rosin, hive-dross (post-Aug.), Plin. 11, 6, 5, § 14 ; 16, 7, 10, § 28 .— The juice of unripe grapes : uvae, Plin.…

mellilla.opening: dim. 2. melinus , a term of endearment, little honey, little sweetheart : mea vita, mea mellilla, Plaut. Cas. 1, 1, 47 dub.

mellĭnĭa.opening: mel , sweetness, deliciousness, delight : hoc nimio magnae melliniae mihist, Plaut. Truc. 4, 1, 6 Spengel (al. mellinae).

mellītŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [mellitus], honey-sweet, darling (ante- and post-class.): corpusculum mellitulum! (al. melliculum), Plaut. Cas. 4, 4, 19 : puella, Hier. Ep. 79, 6 . — Subst. : , , , little honey : mea mellitula, App. M. 3,…

mellītus.opening: adj. mel , of honey, honey-. Lit. : melliti favi, Varr. R. R. 3, 16, 22 : bellaria, id. ap. Gell. 13, 11 : absorptio, Suet. Ner. 27 .— Sweetened with honey, honey-sweet : placenta, Hor. Ep. 1, 10, 11 .— Trop. ,…

mello.opening: v. a. id. , to make or collect honey , Pall. 7, 7, 1 dub.

Mellōna.opening: id. , the goddess of bees and honey , Aug. Civ. Dei , 4, 24.—Called also , Arn. 4, 131 .

Mellŏproxĭmus.opening: , vox hibr. [ μέλλω- proximus], one who comes next in rank to the Proximus; v. h. v. under propior, Cod. Th. 6, 26, 16; Cod. Just. 12, 19, 5 ; 7 ; 14 .

mellōsus.opening: adj. mel , of or from honey, honey-, honey-like (post-class. for melleus): mellosa dulcedo, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 29, 151 .

mellum.opening: a dog's collar , Varr. R. R. 2, 9, 15 Schneid. N. cr. (al. melium and maelium).—Also, , i: millus collare canum venaticorum, factum ex corio confixumque clavis ferreis eminentibus adversus impetum luporum, Paul. ex…

Mēlo.opening: , old Latin name for the Nile: Melo nomine alio Nilus vocatur, Paul. ex Fest. p. 124 Müll.; cf. id. p. 7 and p. 18; Serv. Verg. G. 4, 291 : Melonis alba filia, i. e. the paper-reed growing in the Nile, Aus. Epist. 4, 75…

mēlo.opening: , = μῆλον , an apple-shaped melon , for melopepo, Pall. 4, 9, 6 ; Vop. Carin. 17 .

mēlōcarpon.opening: a plant, also called aristolochia, App. Herb. 19 .

mĕlōdes.opening: , = μελῴδης , a pleasing, charming singer (post-class.): Proculus melodes insonare pulsibus (al. melodis) Sid. Ep. 9, 15 .—Also in fem. : , a Roman surname , Inscr. Grut. 1157, 3 .

mĕlōdĭa.opening: , ae. , = μελῳδία , a pleasant song, melody , Mart. Cap. 9, § 905 : melodiae compositor, Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 1, 2 .

mĕlōdĭcus.opening: adj. , = μελωδικός , melodious : suavitas, Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 8, 6 .

mĕlōdĭna.opening: melodia , a melody (ante-class.), Varr. ap. Non. 49, 33 dub.

Melodūnum.opening: a city of the Senones , the modern Melun , Caes. B. G. 7, 58, 2 ; 7, 60, 1 .

mĕlōdus.opening: adj. , = μελῳδός , pleasantly singing, melodious (post-class.): virgines, Aus. Prof. 15, 8 : carmen, Prud. Cath. 9, 2 .—Hence, subst. : , , , a melody : lyricae melodae, Ven. Carm. 9, 7, 13.

mēlŏfŏlĭa.opening: , vox hibr. [ μῆλον- folium], apples with a leaf on the side , Plin. 15, 14, 15, § 52 .

mēlŏmĕli.opening: ( ), , = μηλόμελι , the sirup of preserved quinces , Col. 12, 45, 3 .

mēlŏpĕpo.opening: , = μηλοπέπων , an apple-shaped melon, cucumber-melon , not eaten till fully ripe, Plin. 19, 5, 23, § 67 .

mēlophyllon.opening: a plant, also called millefolium, App. Herb. 88 .

mĕlŏpoeĭa.opening: , = μελοπολὶα , musical composition : melopoeia est habitus modulationis effectae, Mart. Cap. 9, § 965 al.

mĕlos.opening: (Greek plur. mele, Lucr. 2, 412 .—In masc. : quosdam melos, Cato ap. Non. 213, 17 ; so Pac. and Varr. ib.), = μέλος , a tune, air, strain, song, lay (ante-class. and poet. ): suave summum melos, Naev. ap. Non. 213, 11 :…

Mēlos.opening: , = Μῆλος , an island in the Ægean Sea, one of the Cyclades , now Milo , Mel. 2, 7, 11 ; Plin. 4, 12, 23, § 70 ; Paul. ex Fest. p. 124 Müll.—Hence, , , adj., of Melos : Diagoras Melius, Cic. N. D. 1, 1, 2 .— , , v. 4.…

melosmos.opening: a plant, also called polion, App. Herb. 57 .

mēlōta.opening: , or , , , = μηλωτή , a sheepskin (with the wool on): circumierunt in melotis, in pellibus caprinis, Vulg. Heb. 11, 37 ; Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 4, 76 . —Collat. form, , Isid. 19, 24, 19 ; and , , , Ambros. Ep. 15, 9 .

mēlōthron.opening: (or , Plin. 21, 9, 29, § 53 ), , , = μήλωθρον , a plant, the white bryony , called, in pure Lat., vitis alba, Plin. 23, 1, 16, § 21 ; 21, 9, 29, § 53 .

mēlōtris.opening: , = μηλωτρίς , a probe or sound , mostly for the ears, Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 4, 63 .

Melpŏmĕnē.opening: Μελπομένη (the songstress), the muse of tragic and lyric poetry : Melpomene, cui liquidam pater Vocem cum citharā dedit, Hor. C. 1, 24, 3 ; Mart. 4, 37, 1 ; Aus. Idyll. 20, 2 .

Memacēni.opening: a people of Asia, beyond the Caspian Sea , Curt. 7, 6 .

membrāna.opening: membrum , the skin or membrane that covers parts of the body (class.). Lit. : natura oculos membranis tenuissimis vestivit, Cic. N. D. 2, 57, 142 : cerebri, the membrane of the brain, meninges, Cels. 8, 4 : membranis…

membrānācĕus.opening: and , , adj. membrana , of skin or membrane, skinny, membranaceous (post-Aug.). Lit. : vespertilio, cui membranaceae pinnae uni, Plin. 10, 61, 81, § 168 : PVGILLARES, of parchment, Inscr. Grut. 174, 7 .— Like a skin or…

membrānārĭus.opening: id. , a parchment-maker (post-class.), Edict. Dioclet. p. 20; cf. membranarius, διφθεροποιός , Gloss. Philox.

membrānĕus.opening: adj. id. , of parchment (post-Aug.): pugillares membranei, Mart. 14, 7 in lemm. : codices, Dig. 32, 50, 1 .

membrānŭla.opening: dim. id. , a little skin or membrane. Lit. : membranula, quae sub cute calvariam cingit, Cels. 8, 4 : oculi, membrane of the eye, id. 7, 7, 13 . — Transf. A parchment : iisque imperes, ut sumant membranulam, Cic. Att.…

membrānŭlum.opening: dim. id. , for membranula, a little skin or membrane , App. M. 6, p. 184, 20 .

membrātim.opening: adv. membrum , by limbs or members, in the limbs, limb by limb, from member to member. Lit. : membratim vitalem deperdere sensum, Lucr. 3, 527 : nunc peractis malis, quae membratim sentiuntur, dicemus de his, quae totis…

membrātūra.opening: membro , the formation of the limbs, constitution of the body , Vitr. 8, 5, 1 .

membrĭpŏtens.opening: adj. membrum-potens , ruling in the members (eccl. Lat.), Jul. ap. Aug. c. Sec. Resp. Jul. 2, 11.

membro.opening: v. a. membrum , to form limb by limb, to furnish with limbs : quinque et triginta diebus infans membratur, Censor. de Die Nat. 11 ; Dracont. Hex. 220 .

membrōsus.opening: adj. id. , large membered : hortorum custos membrosior aequo, i. e. majori mentula praeditus, Auct. Priap. prooem.

membrum.opening: etym. dub.; perh. for mems-trum; cf. Sanscr. māmsa, flesh , a limb, member of the body (class.). Lit. : jam membrorum, id est partium corporis, alia videntur propter eorum usum a natura esse donata, ut manus, crura,…

mēmĕcўlon.opening: , = μημέκυλον, μιμαίκυλον , the edible fruit of the strawberrytree , Plin. 15, 24, 28, § 99 .

mēmet.opening: acc. of ego with met, v. ego and met.

mĕmĭni.opening: v. n. Sanscr. man, think; upaman = Gr. ὑπομένειν, await; Gr. μεν- in μένω, Μέντωρ; μαν- in μαίνομαι, μάντις; μνᾶ- in μιμνήσκω, etc.; cf.: maneo, moneo, reminiscor, mens, Minerva, etc. , to remember, recollect, to think…

Memmius.opening: name of a Roman gens. mox Italus Mnestheus, genus, a quo nomine Memmi, Verg. A. 5, 117 . So C. Memmius, a public man, who, being adjudged guilty of ambitus, went into exile to Athens , to him Cicero addressed several…

Memnon.opening: , = Μεμνων , son of Tithonus and Aurora, and king of the Ethiopians; he went to the aid of the Trojans, and was slain by Achilles : nigri Memnonis arma, Verg. A. 1, 489 .— When burned on the funeral pile he is said to…

mĕmor.opening: (anciently memoris, memore, acc. to Prisc. p. 772 P.; comp. memorior, id. p. 699 P.), adj. Sanscr. root smar-, in smarti, memory; smara, love; Gr. μάρτυς, witness; μέριμνα, care; cf.: memoria, mora, etc., not from…

mĕmŏrābĭlis.opening: adj. memoro , memorable, remarkable, worthy of being remembered; heard of, conceivable; worthy to be mentioned, fit to be spoken of (class.): vir, Liv. 38, 53 .— Comp. : memorabilior, Liv. 38, 53 : auctores, Col. 1, 1 :…

mĕmŏrācŭlum.opening: id. , a monument (post-class.), App. Mag. p. 311, 3 .

mĕmŏrālis.opening: , false read. for memorialis, ap. Arn. 6, p. 196 .

mĕmŏrālĭter.opening: adv. memoria , serving to make mention , Ven. Fort. Carm. 4, 20.

mĕmŏrālĭus.opening: memoro , a recorder, notary : ὑπομνηματογράφος , actuarius, memoralius, Gloss. Gr. Lat.

mĕmŏrandus.opening: P. a. , v. memo ro fin. B.

mĕmŏrātor.opening: id. , one who mentions or recounts, a relater ( poet. ): tui casūs memorator, Prop. 3 (4), 1, 33.
