mercātor.opening: id. , a trader, merchant , esp. a wholesale dealer (opp. to caupo, a retailer; class.). Lit. : venalicii mercatoresque, Cic. Or. 70, 232 : multi ad eos mercatores ventitant, Caes. B. G. 4, 3 . — Transf. A dealer,…

mercātōrĭus.opening: adj. mercator , mercantile (ante-class.): navis mercatoria, a merchant-vessel, Plaut. Bacch. 2, 3, 2 .

mercātūra.opening: mercor , trade, traffic, commerce (class.). Lit. : mercatura autem, si tenuis est, sordida putanda est; sin magna et copiosa, non est admodum vituperanda, Cic. Off. 1, 42, 151 : mercaturas facere, to follow the pursuits…

mercātus.opening: id. , trade, traffic, buying and selling (class.): apud aedem Veneris mercatus meretricius, Plaut. Poen. 1, 2, 129 : turpissimus mercatus, Cic. Phil. 2, 3, 6 : domesticus, id. ib. 3, 12, 30 .— Transf. , a place for…

mercēdārĭus.opening: merces , he who pays wages : ostende mercedarios tuos, Sen. Contr. 5, 33, 5 and 25; cf. Gloss. Isid. s. v., † 1. mercedonius.

mercēdŏnĭus.opening: adj. 1. merces-do , of or belonging to the payment of wages : Mercedonios (dies) dixerunt a mercede solvendā, on which wages are paid, pay-days , Paul. ex Fest. p. 124 Müll.— Subst. : , , , a payer of wages, paymaster :…

Mercēdŏnĭus.opening: or , = Μερκηδόνιος, Μερκεδῖνος , mensis, an intercalary month of 22 or 23 days, inserted every two years in the calendar of Numa , Vet. Kalend. Rom. ap. Grut. 133; cf. so Laur. Lyd. de Mens. 4, 92.

mercēdŭla.opening: dim. 1. merces . Small wages, poor pay (class.): infimi homines mercedula adducti, Cic. de Or. 1, 45, 198 : isto modo nec medico quicquam debere te nisi mercedulam dicis nec praeceptori, Sen. Ben. 6, 15, 1 .— Hire,…

mercēnārĭus.opening: (in old MSS. written mercennarius), , adj. id. , that does any thing for reward or pay; hired for money, wages , or pay; paid, hired, mercenary (opp. to gratuitus, without pay, gratuitous). Adj. Of persons: comes, Cic.…

mercĭmōnĭum.opening: merx , goods, wares, merchandise (ante-class. and postAug.): in vostris mercimoniis Emundis vendundisque, Plaut. Am. prol. 1 ; id. Most. 3, 3, 9 ; 12 : quid agit meum mercimonium apud te? id. Curc. 4, 4, 8 : videre…

mercor.opening: (archaic form, mercassitur for mercatus fuerit, Inscr. Grut. 512, 20 .— Inf. mercarier for mercari, Hor. S. 2, 3, 24 ), v. dep. n. and a. [id.], to trade, traffic, deal in commodities ( absol. , Plaut. Merc. prol. 82 ),…

Mercŭrĭālis.opening: adj. Mercurius , of or belonging to the god Mercury : caduceum, App. M. 11, p. 262 : unde frequentia Mercuriale Imposuere mihi cognomen compita, called me Mercury (as being a skilful man of business), Hor. S. 2, 3, 25…

Mercŭrĭŏlus.opening: dim. id. , a little image of Mercury , App. Mag. p. 314, 16 ; 315, 4 .

Mercŭrĭus.opening: , = Ἑρμῆς , Mercury, the son of Jupiter and Maia, the messenger of the gods; as a herald, the god of dexterity; in speaking, of eloquence; the bestower of prosperity; the god of traders and thieves; the presider over…

merda.opening: etym. dub.; cf. Gr. μορύσσειν, to defile , dung, ordure, excrement : corvorum, Hor. S. 1, 8, 37 ; Mart. 3, 17, 6 ; Veg. 2, 8, 4 ; Phaedr. 4, 17, 25 .

merdācĕus.opening: adj. merda , defiled with excrement (post-class.), Auct. Priap. 69, 8 ; Anthol. Lat. 3, 160, 6 .

merdālĕus.opening: adj. id. , = merdaceus, q. v., Auct. Priap. 68, 8 .

mĕrenda.opening: mereo, q. v. , an afternoon luncheon , taken between four and five o'clock (ante- and post-class.): merendam antiqui dicebant pro prandio, quod scilicet medio die caperetur, Paul. ex Fest. p. 123 Müll.: merenda dicitur…

Merenda.opening: a Roman surname : T. Antonius Merenda, a consul , A. U. C. 304, Liv. 3, 35 .

mĕrendārĭus.opening: 1. merenda , one who takes an afternoon luncheon (postAug.), Sen. Contr. 5, 33 fin. dub. (al. mercenarios).

mĕrendo.opening: v. n. id. , to take an afternoon luncheon (late Lat.): merenda est cibus, qui declinante die sumitur, quasi post meridiem edenda: Hinc merendare, quasi meridie edere, Isid. Orig. 20, 2, 12 .

mĕrens.opening: Part. and P. a. of mereo, q. v.

mĕrĕo.grammar: ŭi, ĭtum, 2 ĭtus, 2 v. a. v. dep.
mĕrĕo.opening: v. a. , and , , v. dep. cf. Gr. μέρος, μείρομαι, μόρος, etc.; hence, to receive one's share; cf. II. below , to deserve, merit, to be entitled to, be worthy of a thing; constr. with acc. , with ut , with ne , with inf.…

mĕrĕtrīcābĭlis.opening: , and , , adj. meretrix , = meretricius, Cassiod. de Amic. 22, 46 ; id. ib. prol. § 55.

mĕrē^trīcĭus.opening: adj. meretrix , of or pertaining to harlots or prostitutes, meretricious . Adj. (class.): meretricia ornamenta, Plaut. Truc. 2, 2, 63 : quaestus, Cic. Phil. 2, 18, 44 : disciplina, Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 3, § 6 : domus, a…

mĕrĕtrīcor.opening: v. dep. id. , to deal with harlots : meretricor ἑταιρεύω , Gloss. Philox.

mĕrē^trīcŭla.opening: dim. id. , a public prostitute, courtesan (class.): meretricula Leontium, Cic. N. D. 1, 33, 93 ; Hor. S. 2, 7, 46 ; Quint. 11, 3, 74 .

mĕrē^trix.opening: ( gen. plur. meretricium, Plaut. Cas. 3, 3, 22 : meretricum, id. Ep. 2, 2, 29 ; Ov. A. A. 1, 435 ), mereo; she who earns moncy; hence , a prostitute, harlot , courtesan : ita sunt hic meretrices omnes elecebrae…

mergae.opening: root marg-, to clear away; cf.: ἀμέργω, ἀμέλγω, mulgo, amurca , a two-pronged pitchfork , with which corn, when cut, was made into heaps: mergae furculae, quibus acervi frugum fiunt, dictae a volucribus mergis, quia, ut…

mergĕs.opening: mergae . A sheaf : cerealis mergite culmi, Verg. G. 2, 517 .— I. q. mergae, a two-pronged pitchfork , Plin. 18, 30, 72, § 296 .

mergĭto.opening: v. a. freq. [mergo], to dip in, immerse : ter mergitamur, i. e. baptizamur (al. mersitamur), Tert. de Cor. Milit. 3 .

mergo.opening: v. a. cf. Sanscr. madsh-, majan, to dip; Zend, masga, marrow; Germ. Mark; Engl. marrow , to dip, dip in, immerse; absol . also to plunge into water, to sink . Lit. (class.): eos (pullos) mergi in aquam jussit, Cic. N.…

mergŭlus.opening: dim. mergus , a diver, a kind of bird , Vulg. Lev. 11, 17 ; id. Deut. 14, 17 .

mergus.opening: mergo . A diver , a kind of water-fowl, Varr. L. L. 5, § 78 Müll.: praesagiunt pluviam mergi, Plin. 18, 35, 87, § 362 : mergi maria fugientes, id. ib. ; Ov. M. 8, 625 ; cf.: aequor amat; nomenque tenet, quia mergitur…

mĕrĭbĭbŭlus.opening: adj. merumbibulus , wine-bibbing (eccl. Lat.): puella, Aug. Conf. 9, 8 .

merica.opening: ( ), sc. vitis or uva, an unknown kind of vine , v. l. ap. Col. 3, 2, 27 ; Plin. 14, 2 . 4, § 35 (al. metica; Jan. mettica).

mĕrīdĭālis.opening: adj. meridies , of midday (post-class.): ventus (al. meridionalis), Gell. 2, 22, 14 : temperatura, Tert. Anim. 25 .

mĕrīdĭānus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to mid-day, mid-day- . (Class.) Tempus, mid-day, noon , Cic. de Or. 3, 5, 17 : sol, Plin. 12, 19, 42, § 86 : somnus, id. Ep. 9, 40, 2 ; Lact. 2, 9, 9 .—Hence, as subst. : , sc. gladiatores,…

mĕrīdĭātĭo.opening: meridio , a midday nap, siesta (class.): et lucubrationes detraxi, et meridiationes addidi, Cic. Div. 2, 68, 142 .

mĕrīdĭes.opening: ( ap. Amm. 26, 1, 9 ) [for medidies from medius-dies], mid-day, noon . Lit. : meridies ab eo, quod medius dies, Varr. L. L. 6, § 4 Müll.: ipsum meridiem cur non medidiem? credo, quod erat insuavius, Cic. Or. 47, 158 ;…

mĕrīdĭo.opening: v. n. , and , , v. dep. meridies , to take a mid-day nap or siesta : jube, ad te veniam meridiatum, Cat. 32, 3 : meridiari ante cibum, Cels. 1, 2 : dum ea meridiaret, Suet. Calig. 38 : inter acervos eorum meridiati…

mĕrīdĭōnālis.opening: adj. id. , southern, meridional (post-class.): plaga, Lact. 2, 9 (dub.; al. meridiana): signum, Firm. Math. 2, 12.

mĕrīdĭōnārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to mid-day, meridional (postclass.): gloria quoius lemulcatus (lemniscatus) meridionaria, Tit. ap. App. de Orthogr. p. 130 Mai.

Merīnas.opening: adj., of or belonging to the city of Merinum, in Apulia : Merinates ex Gargano, Plin. 3, 11, 16, § 105 .

Mērĭŏnes.opening: , = Μηριόνης , a charioteer of Idomeneus, who piloted his ships from Crete to Troy , Ov. M. 13, 359 ; Hor. C. 1, 6, 15 ; 1, 15, 26 .

mĕrĭto.opening: v. freq. a. mereo . * To earn, gain : vilicus, qui sestertia dena meritāsset, Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 50, § 119 : Roscius histrio HS. D. annua meritāsse proditur, Plin. 7, 39, 40, § 129 .— To serve for pay, to serve as a…

mĕrĭtōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to the earning of money, by which money is earned, for which money is paid, that brings in money (class.). In gen.: vehicula, Suet. Calig. 39 : balinea, Plin. Ep. 2, 17 : cenaculum, Suet. Vit.…

mĕrĭtus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from mereo, q. v. fin. B.

Mermĕros.opening: , = Μέρμερος , one of the Centaurs present at the wedding of Pirithoüs , Ov. M. 12, 305 .

Mermessĭus.opening: adj., of or belonging to the city of Mermessus, in Phrygia, Mermessian : quicquid Mermessia dixit, i. e. the Hellespontine Sibyl, Tib. 2, 5, 67 (Müller, Marpesia).

Mĕro.opening: merum , the wine-bibber , a nickname bestowed on the emperor Tiberius Claudius Nero, in allusion to his drinking propensities: propter nimiam vini aviditatem, pro Tiberio Biberius, pro Claudio Caldius, pro Nerone Mero…

mĕrōbĭbus.opening: adj. merum-bibo , that drinks wine unmixed (which among the ancients was the practice only of drunkards): anus multibiba atque merobiba, Plaut. Curc. 1, 1, 77 .

Mĕrŏē.opening: , = Μερόη , a large and celebrated island of the Nile, in Ethiopia , now the province of Atbar , Mela, 1, 9, 2; Plin. 2, 73, 75, § 184 ; Ov. F. 4, 570 ; Luc. 10, 303 ; Juv. 6, 528 .— Transf. , in a lusus verbb. with…

mĕrŏis.opening: , = μεροΐς , a plant growing in Meroë , Plin. 24, 17, 102, § 163 .

Mĕrŏpē.opening: , = Μερόπη , the mythic name of several persons . A daughter of Atlas and Pleione, one of the Pleiades, whose star is more obscure than the rest, because she wedded Sisyphus, a mortal , Ov. F. 4, 175 . — A daughter of…

Mĕrops.opening: , = Μέροψ . A king of Ethiopia, husband of Clymene, and reputed to be the father of Phaëthon , Ov. M. 1, 763 ; id. Tr. 3, 4, 30 .— A king of the isle of Cos, from whose name its inhabitants in early times were called…

mĕrops.opening: , = μέροψ , a bird that devours bees; hence also called apiastra, the bee-eater , Verg. G. 4, 14 ; cf. Plin. 10, 33, 51, § 99 .

mĕrōsus.opening: adj. merus , pure, unmixed (post-class.): vinum, Agroet. de Orthogr. p. 2273 P.

mersĭo.opening: mergo , a dipping in, immersion : mersio, βύθισις , Gloss. Philox.

mersĭto.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to dip in, immerse (post-class.): nares in bibendo, Sol. 45, 18 .

merso.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to dip in, immerse ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : balantumque gregem fluvio mersare salubri, Verg. G. 1, 272 : balneo infertur, calida aqua mersatur, Tac. A. 15, 69 .— Trop. , to overwhelm :…

merthryx.opening: , a false reading for myrtis, Plin. 26, 11, 68, § 108 .

merto.opening: v. freq. a. mergo , a collat. form of merso, to immerse, overwhelm (anteclass.): mertat pro mersat dicebant, Paul. ex Fest. p. 124 Müll.; cf. Quint. 1, 4, 14 : quos hic non mertet metus, Att. ap. Non. 138, 33 ; 138, 2 .

mĕrŭla.opening: (post-class. collat. form , , , Auct. Carm. Philom. 13), a blackbird, ousel, merle . Lit. : evolare merulas, Cic. Fin. 5, 15, 42 : ut merula, quia sola volat, quasi mera volans nominaretur, Quint. 1, 6, 38 ; cf. Plin.…

Mĕrŭla.opening: a river of Liguria , now Arosia , Plin. 3, 5, 7, § 48 .

mĕrŭlentus.opening: adj. merum , drunken, intoxicated (post-class.): Pierides, Fulg. Myth. praef.

Mĕrŭlīnus.opening: a Roman surname , Inscr. Raym. Guarin. Comm. 7, p. 41.

mĕrus.opening: adj. root mar-, to gleam; cf.: μάρμαρος, marmor, mare; hence, bright, pure , pure, unmixed, unadulterated , esp. of wine not mixed with water: merum antiqui dicebant solum: at nunc merum purum appellamus, Paul. ex Fest.…

merx.opening: ( nom. sing. merces, Sall. Fragm. ap. Charis. p. 27 P.), mereo , goods, wares, commodities, merchandise (class.): invendibili merce oportet ultro emptorem adducere: Proba merx facile emptorem reperit, Plaut. Poen. 1, 2,…

mĕsa.opening: , = μέση , middle , pure Lat. media (post-Aug.).—Of hemp: tria ejus (cannabis) genera: laudatissima est e medio, quae mesa vocatur, the middle sort, Plin. 19, 9, 56, § 174 .† † , , ( , , ), = μεσάγκυλον , a javelin,…

mesauloe.opening: ( ), , , = μέσαυλοι .—In archit., narrow passages between two rooms or walls : inter duo autem peristylia itinera sunt, quae mesauloe dicuntur, Vitr. 6, 7 (10), 5; cf. andron.

mĕsē.opening: , = μέση , the middle note, the note A, Vitr. 5, 4, 5 ; 5, 5, 2 .

Mĕsembrĭa.opening: , = Μεσημβρία , a city in Thrace, on the Black Sea , now Missiori , Mel. 2, 2, 5 ; Plin. 4, 11, 18, § 45 .— Hence, , , adj., Mesembrian , Ov. Tr. 1, 10, 37 .

Mĕsēnē.opening: , = Μεσήνη , the midland, a name of the district of Babylonia , Plin. 6, 27, 31, § 129 ; Amm. 24, 3, 12 .

mĕses.opening: , = μέσης , the northnortheast wind, between boreas and caecias, Plin. 2, 47, 46, § 120 .

mĕsŏbrăchys.opening: , = μεσόβραχυς (sc. pes), a poetical foot of five syllables, of which only the middle one is short (e. g. pulcherrĭmarum; opp. to mesomacros), Diom. p. 479 P.

mĕsŏchŏrus.opening: , = μεσόχορος , one who stands in the middle of a chorus (of dancers or singers) to lead it, a chorusleader (post-class.): cum mesochorus dedit signum, Plin. Ep. 2, 14, 7 ; Sid. Ep. 1, 2 ; Schol. Juv. 11, 172 .

Mĕsŏgītes.opening: a sort of wine from Mesogis ( Messogis ), a mountain of Lydia , Plin. 14, 7, 9, § 75 .

mĕsŏīdes.opening: , = μεσοειδής , a musical modulation (post-class.): mesoides, quae tonos aequales, mediosque custodit, Mart. Cap. 9, § 965 sq.

mĕsŏlăbĭum.opening: , = μεσολάβιον , a mathematical instrument for finding mean proportional lines, a mesolabe , Vitr. 9, 3, 14 .

mĕsŏleucos.opening: , = μεσόλευκος . A black precious stone with a white stripe , Plin. 37, 10, 63, § 174 .— A plant , Plin. 27, 11, 77, § 102 .

mĕsŏmăcros.opening: , = μεσόμακρος (sc. pes), a poetical foot of five syllables , of which only the middle one is long (e. g. avidissimus; opp. mesobrachys), Diom. p. 478 P.

mĕsŏmĕlas.opening: , = μεσομέλας , a white precious stone with a black stripe , Plin. 37, 10, 63, § 174 .

mĕsŏnauta.opening: , = μεσοναύτης , a seaman who ranked between the pilot and the rowers , Pomp. ap. Ulp. Dig. 4, 9, 1, § 2 .

mĕsŏnyctĭus.opening: adj. , μεσονύκτιος , of midnight : afflatus, Isid. 5, 30, 4 .— Hence, subst. : , , , = μεσονύκτιον , midnight (post-class.): CVIVS MESONYCTIVM FACTVM EST V. ID. DEC., i. e. midnight apparition , Inscr. Mur. 333.

Mĕsŏpŏtămĭa.opening: , = Μεσοποταμία , a country of Asia, between the Euphrates and Tigris , now called Al-Jezireh , Cic. N. D. 2, 52, 130 ; Isid. 13, 21, 10 ; Mel. 1, 11, 1 ; Plin. 5, 12, 13, § 66 ; Sall. H. 4, 51 Dietsch. —Hence, , , adj.…

mĕsosphaerum.opening: , = μεσόσφαιρον , a kind of nard with middle-sized leaves (v. hadrosphaerum and microsphaerum), Plin. 12, 12, 26, § 44 .

mespĭlum.opening: , = μέσπιλον . A medlar , Plin. 15, 20, 22, § 84 ; Pall. Mart. 10, 19 and 22.— A medlar-tree , Pall. Insit. 69 .

mespĭlus.opening: , or , , , = μεσπίλη , a medlar-tree , Plin. 17, 10, 13, § 67 ; Pall. 3, 25, 32 .— A medlar , Pall. de Insit. 69 and 105.

Messālīna.opening: or , , The profligate wife of the emperor Claudius, daughter of M. Valerius Messalla Barbatus, Suet. Claud. 17 ; 26 ; Tac. A. 11, 1 sq. ; Juv. 10, 333 ; cf. id. 6, 116 al. — The wife of the emperor Nero , Suet. Ner. 35…

Messalla.opening: (less correctly ), , , a Roman surname in the gens Valeria: Corvinus primus Messanam vicit, et pri mus ex familiā Valeriorum, urbis captae in se translato nomine, Messana appellatus est: paulatimque vulgo permutante…

Messāna.opening: , = Μεσσήνη . A Sicilian city, situated on the strait between Italy and Sicily , the mod. Messina , Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 8, § 17 ; Caes. B. C. 2, 3 ; Mel. 2, 7, 16 : incumbens Messana freto, Sil. 14, 194 .— Another name for…

Messāpĭa.opening: ( ), , , the old name of a part of Lower Italy (Apulia and Calabria): Messapia Apulia a Messapo rege appellata, Paul. ex Fest. p. 125 Müll.; cf. Plin. 3, 11, 16, § 99 .—Hence, ( ), , adj., of or belonging to Messapia,…

Messāpus.opening: ( ), , , a mythic prince in Messapia , Verg. A. 7, 691 ; cf. Paul. ex Fest. s. v. Messapia, p. 125 Müll.

Messēis.opening: , = Μεσσηίς , a fountain in Thessaly , Plin. 4, 8, 15, § 30 .—As adj., of or belonging to the fountain Messēis : Messeides undae, Val. Fl. 4, 374 .

Messēnē.opening: , or ( ), , , = Μεσσήνη , the capital of Messenia, in the Peloponnesus, on the river Pamisos , now Maura-Matia , Mel. 2, 3, 4 ; Plin. 4, 5, 7, § 15 ; Nep. Ep. 8 ; id. Pel. 4 ; Liv. 36, 31, 1 ; 32, 21, 23 ; Ov. M. 6, 417…

Messĭa.opening: messio , the goddess of reaping , Tert. Spect. 8 .

Messĭa Silva.opening: a wooded hill on the right bank of the Tiber, south-west of Veii , Liv. 1, 33, 9 Hertz (Weissenb. Maesia), Plin. 8, 58, 83, § 225 Jan. (al. Mesia).

Messīas.opening: Heb., the Anointed, Gr. Χριστός , the Messiah, Christ , Vulg. Johan. 4, 25 ; Lact. 4, 7 , and in the eccl. fathers saepiss.

messĭo.opening: 2. meto , a reaping : frumenti tria genera sunt messionis, Varr. R. R. 1, 50, 1 ; Vulg. Job, 29, 19 ; id. Jer. 51, 33 ; id. 2 Sam. 21, 9.

messis.opening: ( acc. sing. messim, Cato, R. R. 134 ; Plaut. Most. 1, 3, 5 ; id. Ep. 5, 2, 53 ; Varr. R. R. 3, 2, 6 ; v. Neue, Formenl. 1, p. 200), ( masc. : non magno messe, Lucil. ap. Non. 213 fin. ) [id.], a reaping and ingathering…

messor.opening: id. , a reaper (class.). Lit. , Cic. de Or. 3, 12, 46 : durus, Ov. M. 14, 643 : feniseca, a mower, Col. 2, 18 : dura messorum ilia, Hor. Epod. 3, 4 : parce messoribus illis qui saturant urbem, Juv. 8, 117 .—…

messōrĭus.opening: adj. messor , of or belonging to a reaper (class.): messoria corbis, a reaper's basket, Cic. Sest. 38, 82 : falces, Pall. 1, 43 : opera, Col. 2, 13, 2 .

messŭārĭus.opening: adj [messura], for messorius, of or belonging to reapers (post-class.): corbis, Serv. Verg. E. 8, 82 .

messūra.opening: 2. meto , a reaping (post-class.), Primas. ap. Gall. c. 6: messuram dicimus, non metitionem, Diom. p. 374 P. (dub.)

Mestria.opening: a Roman surname , Inscr. Fabr. p. 621, 181 .

Mestriānus.opening: a Roman surname , Inscr. Malvas. Marm. Felsin. p. 253.

met.grammar: a pronominal suffix attached to substantive and
met.opening: (less freq.) adjective personal pronouns; Engl. self : egomet, mihimet, memet, nosmet, nobismet, tutemet, tibimet, vosmet, meamet; v. ego, tu, and meus.

mēta.opening: root ma-, measure, whence Gr. μέτρον; Lat. manus, mane, etc. (q. v.), properly, that which marks a measured space, hence , any mark at a boundary or limit , esp., The conical columns set in the ground at each end of the…

mĕtăbŏlē.opening: , = μεταβολή , the transition to another key or set of tones , Fulg. Myth. 3, 9, p. 128 Muncker: cf. written as Greek, Quint. 9, 4, 50 .

Mĕtăbus.opening: A king of the Volsci, father of Camilla , Verg. A. 11, 540 ; Hyg. Fab. 252 .— A son of Sisyphus, the founder of Metapontum , Serv. ad Verg. A. 11, 540 .

mĕtăcismus.opening: for mytacismus, = μυτακισμός, from μῦ , a frequent repetition of the letter M, Mart. Cap. 5, § 514 ; also the pronunciation of M at the close of a word before a word beginning with a vowel, metacism , Diom. p. 448 P.

Mĕtăgōgeu͡s.opening: , = μεταγωγεύς , he who leads around; Lat. circumductor, one of the aeons of Valentinian, Tert. adv. Valent. 10 .

Mĕtăgon.opening: , = Μετάγων , the name of a dog , Grat. Cyn. 209 .

Metalces.opening: , = Μεταλκής , one of the fifty sons of Ægyptus, slain by his wife Cleopatra , Hyg. Fab. 170 .

metălepsis.opening: , = μετάληψις , in rhetoric, the use of one word for another which it suggests by association , as, the cause for the effect, or the reverse; especially when a second substitution is made, as when aristae is said for…

mētālis.opening: adj. meta, III. 3 , conical (post-class.): forma, Paul. ex Fest. s. v. tutulum, p. 335 Müll.—Hence, adv. : , conically (post-class.): majus corpus ejus quo umbra metaliter jacitur, quam umbra ipsa, Mart. Cap. 8, § 859 ;…

mĕtallārĭus.opening: , and , , metallum , a man or a woman that works in a mine, a miner (post-class.), Cod. Just. 11, 6, 7 .

mĕtallĭcus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to metal, metallic (post-Aug.). Adj. : molybdaena metallica, Plin. 34, 18, 53, § 173 : natura, id. 27, 4, 5, § 15 .— Subst. : , , A digger of metals, a mine-digger, miner : lavant eas arenas…

mĕtallĭfer.opening: adj. metallum-fero , yielding or abounding in metal, metalliferous ( poet. ): terra, Sil. 15, 500 : Luna, Stat. S. 4, 4, 23 .

Metallinensis.opening: , or , , adj. Metallinum , of or belonging to the town of Metallinum (in Lusitania), Metallinian : colonia, Plin. 4, 21, 35, § 117 .

mĕtallum.opening: , = μέταλλον , a mine or quarry , of gold, silver, iron, or stone; voc. metalle, as if from metallus, Spart. Pesc. Nig. 126 . Lit. , the place where metals are dug, a mine : metalla vetera intermissa recoluit, et nova…

mĕtămĕlos.opening: , = μετάμελος , repentance (ante-class.): metamelos, filius inconstantiae, Varr. ap. Non. 79, 23 (Büch. § 239).

mĕtămorphōsis.opening: , = μεταμόρφωσις , a transformation, metamorphosis; in plur. : , -ĕōn, the Metamorphoses, a well-known poem of Ovid; in Gr. acc. plur. Metamorphoseis, Tert. adv. Val. 12 : censeo eam rem ad metamorphosis Ovidi…

mĕtaphŏra.opening: , = μεταφορά , a rhetorical figure, metaphor, a transferring of a word from its proper signification to another (called by Cic. de Or. 3, 38, 155 , verbi translatio; post-Aug.), Quint. 8, 6, 18 ; (as Greek), id. 8, 6, 4…

mĕtaphŏrĭcē.opening: adv. metaphora , metaphorically, figuratively (post-class.), Acron. ad Hor. Ep. 1, 20, 1 .—Also , μεταφορικῶς , Acron. ad Hor. Ep. 1, 3, 29 sq. ; Schol. Juv. 7, 103 .

mĕtăphrĕnum.opening: , = μετάφρενον , the upper part of the spine , Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 16, 129 (as Greek, id. ib. 2, 29, 151 ; id. Tard. 3, 2, 31 ).

Mĕtăpīnus.opening: etym. dub. , Metapinic , an epithet of the second or middle of the three principal mouths of the Rhone: cujus ora appellata ... alterum Metapinum, Mart. Cap. 6, § 635 ; Plin. 3, 4, 5, § 32 .

mĕtaplasmus.opening: , = μεταπλασμός , a grammatical change, irregularity, metaplasm , e. g. in declension (post-Aug.): metaplasmus enim, et schematismos et schemata vocamus, Quint. 1, 8, 14 ; Mart. Cap. 3, § 326 .

mĕtaplastĭcōs.opening: adv. , = μεταπλαστικῶς , metaplastically, by the use of metaplasm : metaplasticos dicitur apud poëtas usurpari id quod propter necessitatem metri mutare consueverunt, Paul. ex Fest. p. 153 Müll.

Mĕtăpontum.opening: a town of Lucania, where Pythagoras lived and died , now Torre a Mare , Cic. Fin. 5, 2, 4 ; Liv. 1, 18, 8 ; Mela, 2, 4, 3; Plin. 3, 11, 15, § 97 .—Hence, , , adj., Metapontine : ager, Liv. 24, 20 .—In plur. : , , , the…

mētārĭus.opening: adj. meta , of or belonging to limits or boundaries (post-class.): metaria circumscriptio, a limiting by boundaries, Arn. 2, 70 .

mĕtastăsis.opening: , = μετάστασις , a rhet. figure. A refusing , Agn. Roman. de Fig. 16, p. 155.— = metabasis, a passing over, transition , Julian. Rufin. de Schem. 23, p. 243 .

mĕtăsyncrĭtĭcus.opening: adj. , = μετασυγκριτικός , belonging to the discharge of peccant humors : adjutoria, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 16, 134 : cyclus, id. Tard. 1, 1, 24 ; 2, 1, 49 .

mĕtăthĕsis.opening: , = μετάθεσις , a transposition of the letters of a word , Diom. 2, p. 437 P.

mētātĭo.opening: metor , a measuring or meting out, a marking off a place (postAug.): vinearum, Col. 7, 15, 1 .

mētātor.opening: id. , one who metes out or marks off a place, a divider and fixer of boundaries (class.). Lit. : castrorum antea metator, nunc, ut sperat, urbis, Cic. Phil. 11, 5, 12 ; cf. id. ib. 14, 4, 10 : templi, Lact. 4, 11 .—…

mētātōrĭus.opening: adj. metator , of or pertaining to measuring out , transf. (post-class.): pagina, a letter relative to the providing of quarters, Sid. Ep. 8, 11 .

mētātūra.opening: metor , a measuring out, marking off a place (eccl. Lat.), Lact. 4, 11, 13 .

Mĕtaurensis.opening: adj. Metaurus , of or belonging to the river Metaurus, in Umbria : AGER, Inscr. Oliv. Marm. Pisaur. n. 30.— Subst. : , , , the inhabitants of that region, Metaurians , Plin. 3, 14, 19, § 114 .

Mĕtaurus.opening: , = Μέταυρος , the name of several rivers . A river in Umbria, celebrated for the defeat of Hasdrubal, the brother of Hannibal , now Meturo , Liv. 27, 43 sq. ; Sil. 8, 486 .—Hence, , , adj., of Metaurus : Metaurum…

mĕtaxa.opening: or , , , = μέταξα and μάταξα , raw silk , the web of silkworms. Lit. , Dig. 39, 4, 16 ; Cod. Just. 11, 7, 10 .— Transf. , a rope : lini metaxa, Lucil. ap. Fest. s. v. rodus, p. 265 Müll.; Vitr. 7, 3 .

mĕtella.opening: (prob. adj. , sc. machina), a basket filled with stones, which the besieged threw down on the heads of the besiegers (post-class.): ut de ligno crates facerent, quas metellas vocaverunt, lapidibusque complerent, etc.…

Mĕtellīnus.opening: adj. Metellus , of or belonging to a Metellus, Metelline : oratlo Metellina, i. e. against Metellus, Cic. Att. 1, 13 fin.

Mĕtellus.opening: etym. dub.; metellus = μισθιος, hired, i. e. a hired servant, Gloss. Philox.: metelli dicuntur in re militari quasi mercenarii, Attius in Annalibus: calones famulique metellique caculaeque; a quo genere hominum…

mĕtempsȳchōsis.opening: , = μετεμψύχωσις , the transit of the soul, its transmigration from one body to another , a doctrine of the Pythagoreans, Porphyr. ad Hor. Ep. 2, 1, 52 .

mĕtensōmătōsis.opening: , = μετενσωμάτωσις , a removing from one body into another, a change of body (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Anim. 31 and 32.

mĕtĕōrĭa.opening: , = μετεωρία , forgetfulness , M. Aurel. ap. Front. ad M. Caes. 4, 7 (as Greek, Suet. Vit. Claud.).

Mĕtĕrēa turba.opening: a people dwelling about the Danube and the Black Sea , Ov. Tr. 2, 191 .

Mēthīon.opening: the father of Phorbas , Ov. M. 5, 74 .

mĕthŏdĭcē.opening: , = μεθοδική , the methodical part of grammar (post-Aug.): grammaticae partes duae, id est ratio loquendi, et enarratio auctorum: quarum illam methodicen, hanc historicen vocant, Quint. 1, 9, 1 .

mĕthŏdĭcus.opening: adj. , = μεθοδικός , methodical, belonging to a particular school (post-Aug.): medicina, Tert. Anim. 6 : disciplina, Cael. Aur. Tard. 4, 1, 6 : medici, Cels. praef. § 13.

mĕthŏdĭum.opening: , = μεθόδιον , a witty conceit, a jest, joke (post-Aug.): Trimalchio ejusmodi methodio laetus, Carpe, inquit, etc. (al. metōdīum, i. e. μετωδεῖον , an inserted song ), Petr. 36, 5 .

mĕthŏdus.opening: and , , , = μέθοδος , a way of teaching, mode of proceeding, method (post-class.), Vitr. 1, 1, 4 ; Aus. Idyll. 11, 67 ; Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 1, 49 (as Greek, Cels. praef. § 91); cf. methodicus.

Mēthymna.opening: , = Μήθυμνα , a city in the island of Lesbos, famous as the birthplace of the poet Arion, and for its excellent wine , now Molivo , Mel. 2, 7, 4 ; Liv. 45, 31, 14 : quot habet Methymna racemos, Ov. A. A. 1, 57 .—Hence.…

Metĭa Porta.opening: , a false read. in Plaut.; cf. Ritschl ad Plaut. Ps. 1, 3, 97 .

mĕtĭcŭlōsus.opening: adj. metus , full of fear . Fearful, timid (ante- and postclass.): nullus est hoc meticulosus aeque, Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 137 ; Dig. 4, 2, 7 : lepus, App. Flor. p. 341, 9 .—* Frightful, terrible : res, Plaut. Most. 5, 1, 52…

Metilius.opening: a Roman family name : M. Metilius, Liv. 5, 11 .—Hence, , , adj., of or belonging to a Metilius : Metilia lex, Plin. 35, 17, 57, § 197 .

Metina.opening: an island near the coast of Gaul, opposite the mouth of the Rhone , Mart. Cap. 6, § 643 .

mētĭor.opening: (post-class. metītus, Dig. 32, 1, 52 ), , v. dep. Sanscr. ma, to measure; cf. Gr. μέ-τρον, Lat. modus , to measure, mete (lands, corn); also, to measure or mete out, to deal out, distribute by measure (class.). Lit. :…

Mĕtĭōsēdum.opening: a city in Gaul , now Meudon , Caes. B. G. 7, 61 .

Metiscus.opening: a charioteer of Turnus , Verg. A. 12, 469 .

mētītĭo.opening: metior , = mensura, but not in use; v. Diom. 374 P.

Metĭus.opening: or (also ), , , an Italian proper name . Metius (Mettius) Curtius, a Sabine chief , Liv. 1, 12 fin. ; Varr. L. L. 5, § 149 Müll.— Metius Fufetius (acc. to others, Mettus Fufetius), an Alban general, who was put to death…

mēto.opening: (no perf. ), ātum, 1, v. a. , to measure; v. metor fin.

mĕto.grammar: messŭi messum, 3 v. a. and n.
mĕto.opening: (Cato ap. Prisc. p. 903 P.; Mart. Cap. 3, § 319 ), , v. a. and n. root ma-; Gr. ἀμάω, mow, reap; ἄμη, sickle; cf. messis, messor , to reap, mow, crop; of the vintage, to gather, gather in, collect; and poet. of the…

mĕtŏchē.opening: , = μετοχή , a participle (late Lat.), Aus. Epigr. 6, 7 .

mĕtoecus.opening: , = μέτοικος , a stranger, sojourner, denizen, resident alien dwelling in a city without the rights of citizenship (post-class.), Eum. Pan. Flavens. Nom. Dict. 4 fin. : ager militi metoeco (al. modico) est assignatus,…

Mĕton.opening: or , , , = Μέτων , a celebrated Athenian astronomer, who discovered the cycle of nineteen years, at the end of which the new and full moons again fall on the same days , Avien. Prognost. 48 ; Aus. Epis. 2, 12 .—Hence…

mĕtōnўmĭa.opening: , = μετωνυμία , a figure by which one name is changed for another, a change of names, metonymy (pure Lat. denominatio), Paul. ex Fest. p. 153 Müll.; Charis. p. 244 P. al.

mĕtōnўmĭcōs.opening: adv. , = μετωνυμικῶς , metonymically, by metonymy , Porphyr. ad Hor. Epod. 13, 16 ; id. ad Hor. Ep. 1, 18, 9 sqq. al.

mĕtŏpa.opening: , = μετόπη , the space between two hollows; in architecture, the space between two dentils or two triglyphs, a metope (only in Vitr.): inter denticulos et inter triglyphos quae sunt intervalla, metopae nominantur, etc.,…

mĕtōpĭon.opening: or , , (also , , Sol. 40 ), = μετώπιον . The gum of an African tree, also called ammoniacum, Plin. 12, 23, 49, § 107 ; Sol. 27, 47 . — Oil of bitter almonds, almond-oil , Plin. 15, 7, 7, § 26 (Jahn, neopum).— An…

mĕtōposcŏpus.opening: or , , , = μετωποσκόπος , a forehead inspector, one who tells fortunes by examining the forehead, a metoposcopist (post-Aug.), Suet. Tit. 2 ; cf. Plin. 35, 10, 36, § 88 .

mētor.opening: v. dep. meta , to measure, mete; to measure off, mark out (not in Cic.). In gen.: stadium Hercules pedibus suis metatus est, Gell. 1, 1, 2 : caelum, Ov. F. 1, 309 : Indiam, Plin. 6, 17, 21, § 57 . — Poet. , to traverse,…

mĕtrēta.opening: , = μετρητής , an Athenian measure for liquids, containing 12 congii ( χόες ) and 144 κοτύλαι (3/4 of the Attic medimnus, about 9 gallons English ): picis liquidae metreta, Col. 12, 22, 1 : se vendidisse navem, metretas…

mē^trĭcus.opening: adj. , = μετρικός , of or relating to measuring or measure (postAug.). In gen.: leges metricae, Plin. 11, 37, 88, § 219 .— In partic., of or relating to metre, metrical : metrici pedes, Quint. 9, 4, 52 ; 48 .— Subst. :…

mētrŏcōmĭa.opening: , = μητροκωμία , a village from which other villages have derived their inhabitants, a mother-village (post-class.), Cod. Th. 11, 24, 6; Cod. Just. 8, 10, 19 .

Mētrŏdōrus.opening: , = Μητρόδωρος . Metrodorus Lampsacenus or Atheniensis, an Epicurean , Cic. Tusc. 2, 3, 8 ; 2, 6, 17 ; 5, 9, 27 .— M. Scepsius (from Scepsis, a city of Mysia ), a rhetorical and Academic philosopher, famous for his…

mētrŏpŏlis.opening: , = μητρόπολις , a city from which other cities have been colonized, a mother-city; also, the chief city, metropolis of a province (post-class.). Lit. , Cod. Just. 11, 21 ; Cod. Th. 13, 3, 11.— Trop. : metropolis et arx…

Mētrŏpŏlis.opening: , = Μητρόπολις , the proper name of several cities , e. g. in Thessaly, between Pharsalus and Gomphi , Caes. B. C. 3, 80 ; Liv. 32, 13, 11 .— , , , the inhabitants of Metropolis , Caes. B. C. 3, 81 ; cf. of others,…

mētrŏ-pŏlīta.opening: , = μητροπολίτης , a bishop in a chief city, a metropolitan (post-class.): metropolita sacer, Ven. Carm. 3, 6, 20.

mētrŏpŏlītānus.opening: adj. 1. metropolis , of or belonging to a metropolis, metropolitan (post-class.): nomen, Cod. Just. 11, 21, 1 .—Esp. subst. : , , , a metropolitan, the bishop of a metropolitan church , Sid. Ep. 7, 9 .

Mētrŏpŏlītānus.opening: adj. 2. Metropolis , of or belonging to the city of Metropolis : campus, Liv. 38, 15 .

mē^trum.opening: , = μέτρον , a measure; in partic., a poetical measure, metre; a verse (post-Aug.): rhythmi, id est numeri, spatio temporum constant: metra etiam ordine: ideoque alterum esse quantitatis videtur, alterum qualitatis,…

mettĭca.opening: an unknown species of vine , Col. 3, 2, 27 ; Plin. 14, 2, 4, § 35 (Sillig. Metica).

Mettus.opening: ( ), , , a Sabine prænomen , prob. the title of a magistracy among the Albans (cf. medix, meddix), e. g. Mettus Curtius, Liv. 1, 12 ; 1, 23 sqq.; v. Metius.

mĕtŭens.opening: Part. and P. a. , v. metuo fin.

mētŭla.opening: dim. meta , a small pyramid, obelisk (post-Aug.), Plin. Ep. 5, 6, 35 .

mĕtŭo.opening: (cf.: nimis ante metutum, Lucr. 5, 1140 ), , v. a. and n. metus , to fear, be afraid of a person or thing; to hesitate, not to venture, not to wish (syn.: vereor, formido, timeo); with inf. , with ne, to fear lest; with…

mĕtus.opening: ( fem. : nulla in me est metus, Enn. ap. Paul. ex Fest. p. 123 Müll.: metus ulla, id. ap. Non. 214, 11 ; cf. Ann. v. 537, and Trag. v. 179 Vahl.; dat. metu, Tac. A. 11, 32 ; 15, 69 ), fear, dread, apprehension, anxiety;…

mēum.opening: , = μῆον , an umbelliferous plant, bear-wort , Plin. 20, 23, 94, § 253 .

mĕus.opening: ( voc. meus for mi: proice tela manu, sanguis meus, Verg. A. 6, 835 : Lolli meus, Sid. Ep. 1, 9 ; and: domine meus, id. ib. 4, 10 ; gen. plur meūm for meorum: pietas majorum meūm, Plaut. Cas. 2, 6, 66 : meapte, Ter.…

Mēvānĭa.opening: a city in Umbria , now Bevagna , Liv. 9, 41, 13 ; Col. 3, 8, 3 ; Sil. 6, 647 : nebulosa, Prop. 4 (5), 1, 123. — Hence, , , comm., of or belonging to the city of Mevania Mevanas Varenus, Sil. 4, 546 .— Subst. : , , , the…

Mēvĭa.opening: a woman fond of masculine sports , Juv. 1, 22 .

Mezentĭus.opening: (not , , , , or ; cf. Rib. in Rhein. Mus. 1857, vol. 12, p. 418 sq.), , , a male proper name [of Oscan origin], a tyrant of Cære or Agylla , Liv. 1, 2 ; Paul. ex Fest. s. v. oscillum, p. 194 Müll.: contemptor divom…

mi.opening: . Dat. from ego.— Voc. from meus; v. h. vv.

Mĭa Chărĭtōn.opening: = Χαρίτων μία , one of the Graces , Lucr. 4, 1162 ; v. Charites.

mīca.opening: root smic-; Gr. σμικρός, μικρός; cf. micula; O. Germ. smahan, to belittle , a crumb, little bit, morsel, grain ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : mica panis, Petr. 42 : auri, Lucr. 1, 839 : marmoris, Plin. 33, 4,…

mĭcans.opening: Part. and P. a. , from mico.

mīcārĭus.opening: adj. mica , of or belonging to crumbs or little bits (post-Aug.): homo frugi, et micarius, a crumb-gatherer , i. e. frugal, economical , Petr. 73, 6 .

mĭcātĭo.opening: mico , a quick motion : micatio λαχμός , Gloss. Philox.

mĭcātus.opening: id. , a quick motion (post-class.): linguarum micatibus, Mart. Cap. 4, § 331 .

Miccotrōgus.opening: , = Μικκότρωγος , the fictitious name of a parasite, Smallbiter , Plaut. Stich. 1, 3, 88 .

micĕo.opening: v. n. , to bleat , of a hegoat (al. mutire), Auct. Phil. 58.

Michāēl.opening: , a Hebrew name, Vulg. Num. 13, 14 al. —Esp., Michael, the archangel , Vulg. Dan. 10, 13 .

Michăēlĭum.opening: , = Μιχᾳηλεῖον , the church of St. Michael , Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 2, 19 .

mīcĭdus.opening: adj. mica , thin, poor , Innocent. Agrar. p. 231 Goes.

Micio.opening: name of a man , Ter. Ad. 5, 3, 7 .

Mĭcipsa.opening: son of Masinissa, and king of Numidia , Sall. J. 5 sq. ; Flor. 3, 1 . —In plur. , poet. for Numidians, Africans , Juv. 5, 89 .

mĭco.opening: ( pf. subj. micaverit, Sol. 53 ), , v. n. Sanscr. mish-, to wink , to move quickly to and fro, to have a vibrating or tremulous motion, to quiver, shake, tremble , e. g. of the pulse; to beat, palpitate; to spring forth…

Mĭcon.opening: , = Μίκων , the name of a shepherd : cum me arbustum videre Miconis ... incidere falce, Verg. E. 3, 10 : ramosa Micon vivacis cornua cervi, id. ib. 7, 30 .—So, forte Micon senior, Canthusque Miconis alumnus, Calp. Ecl.…

micrŏcosmus.opening: , = μικρόκοσμος , a little world, world in miniature, microcosm , Isid. Orig. 3, 22, 2 .

micropsȳchus.opening: adj. , = μικρόψυχος , little-minded, narrow-minded (postAug.), Plin. 22, 24, 51, § 110 : Novius, Mart. 1, 87 lemm .

mictĭlis.opening: adj. mingo , that deserves to be defiled; hence, transf., despicable, worthless, bad (ante-class.): merx, Lucil. ap. Non. 137, 31 .

mictōrĭus.opening: adj. mingo , that promotes urine, urinative, diuretic (postclass.): medicamenta, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 8, 86 .

mictŭālis.opening: adj. id. (only post class). Relating to the passing of urine, wrinary : via, Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 10, 91 : viae, id. ib. 5, 10, 121 .—Hence, subst. : , , , the urinary passage , Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 4, 65 .— That promotes…

mictŭrĭo.opening: v. desider. n. [mingo], to go to make water, to make water (only in Juvenal): micturiunt hic, Juv. 6, 309 ; 16, 46 .

mictus.opening: id. , a making water, urinating (post-class.): sanguinis mictus, Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 3, 59 ; 2, 1, 12 .

mīcŭla.opening: dim. mica , a little crumb, little grain, little bit (post-Aug.), Cels. 2, 5 : exiguae, Arn. 2, 77 .

Midaium.opening: , = Μιδάειον , a city of Phrygia , Plin. 5, 32, 41, § 145 .—Hence, subst. : , , , the inhabitants of Midaium , Cic. Fam. 3, 8, 3 .—Also called , , , Plin. 5, 29, 29, § 105 .

Mīdāmus.opening: one of the fifty sons of Ægyptus, who was slain by his wife , Hyg. Fab. 170 .

Mĭdas.opening: or , , , = Μίδας , son of Gordius, and king of Phrygia. At his request he received from Bacchus, who wished to prove his gratitude for the hospitality Midas had accorded him, the boon that everything he touched should…

Mīdē.opening: a city in Bœotia , Stat. Th. 7, 331 .

Mīdea.opening: , = Μίδεια , a city in Lycia , Stat. Th. 4, 45 .

Mīdĭas.opening: , = Μειδιας , the name of a Messenian, who invented the cuirass , Plin. 7, 56, 57, § 200 .

Mīdīnus.opening: adj. Midas , of or belonging to Midas : Arcadicum ac Midinum sapis, i. e. after the manner of an ass, Mart. Cap. 6, § 577

Migdĭlybs.opening: μιγδην-λύψ , a mixed Libyan , i. e. of Libyan (African) and Tyrian descent , as the Carthaginians were, Plaut Poen. 5, 2, 73.

migma.opening: , = μίγμα , a mixture, mixed provender, meslin : commistum mig ma, Vulg. Isa. 30, 24 .

mī^grātĭo.opening: migro , a removal, a changing of one's habitation, migration (class.). Lit. : haec migratio nobis misera, Liv. 5, 53 : migrationem esse mortem in eas oras, quas, qui vitā excesserunt, incolunt, Cic. Tusc. 1, 41, 98 ;…

mī^grātor.opening: id. , a wanderer : migrator μετανάστης , Gloss. Gr. Lat.

mī^gro.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
mī^gro.opening: (migrassit for migraverit, Cic. Leg. 3, 4, 11 ), v. n. and a. [etym. dub.; cf. Sanscr. root mā, exchange; also meo]. Neutr., to remove from one place to another, to depart, flit, migrate (class.). Lit. : migrare e fano…

mihipte.opening: , i. q. mihi ipsi, v. ego.

Mīlănĭon.opening: , = Μειλανίων , the husband of Atalanta : flēsse Milaniona, Ov. A. A. 2, 188 ; id. Am. 3, 2, 29 ; Prop. 1, 1, 9 .

milĕon.opening: the name of a plant, also called scelerata, App. Herb. 8 .

mīlĕs.opening: (MEILES, Inscr. Mur. 582; late form, milex, Gromat. Vet. p. 246, 19), , Sanscr root mil-, to unite, combine; cf.: mille, milites, quod trium millium primo legio fiebat, ac singulae tribus Titiensium, Ramnium, Lucerum…

Mīlētis.opening: Miletus . The daughter of Miletus, Byblis , Ov. M. 9, 634 .— A Milesian woman , Caecil. ap. Diom. p. 378 P.

Mīlētŏpŏlis.opening: , = Μιλητόπολις , a city in European Sarmatia, founded by the Milesians, otherwise called Olbia Borysthenis or Olbiopolis, now Oczakow , Plin. 4, 12, 26, § 82 .

Mīlētus.opening: ( ), , , = Μίλητος , the city of Miletus, in Caria, the birthplace of Thales , Mel. 1, 17, 1 ; Plin. 5, 29, 31, § 112 ; Cic. Att. 9, 9, 2 .—Esp., as a proverb for luxury and wantonness: paupertas Romana perit, hinc…

Mileum.opening: ( ), , , and , , , a city in Numidia , Aug. adv. Don. 6, 20 .—Hence, , , adj., of or belonging to the city of Mileum , Aug. Ep. 34 .

mĭlĭăcĕus.opening: adj. milium , of millet, millet puls, Paul. ex Fest. s. v. forma, p. 83, 12 Müll.

mĭnūtātim.opening: adv. id. , piecemeal, in little bits; piece by piece, little by little; gradually, by degrees; singly, one by one (class.): nasturtium consectum minutatim, Varr. R. R. 3, 10, 6 : cribrare terram, to sift small, Plin.…

mĭnūtē.opening: adv. , v. minuo, P. a. fin .

mĭnūtĭa.opening: minutus , smallness, fineness, minuteness (post-Aug.): donec ad minutiam redigantur, to make quite small, reduce to powder, Sen. Ep. 90, 23 : pulveris minutiae, little particles , Lact. Ira Dei, 10, 9.— Plur.,…

mĭnūtĭ-lŏquĭum.opening: minutus-loquor , brevity of speech (eccl. Lat.): Aristotelis, Tert. Anim. 6 ; Boëth. Myth. 1 praef. fin.

mĭnūtim.opening: adv. , v. minuo, P. a. fin .

mĭnūtĭo.opening: minuo , a lessening, diminishing (post-Aug.); trop., opp. incrementum, Quint. 8, 4, 28 : rerum, id. 6, 3, 52 : capitis, i. e. deminutio, Gell. 1, 12, 9 ; Dig. 4, 5, 1 ; 4, 5, 5 : sanguinis, blood-letting, bleeding, Veg.…

mĭnūtīvus.opening: adj. minuo , adapted for diminution, diminishing , opp. auctivus, Fortun. Art. Rhet. 3, 20 .

mĭnūtŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [minutus], very little; very paltry (ante- and post-class.): pueri, Plaut. Poen. prol. 28 : argenteos Philippeos minutulos, Vop. Aur. 9 fin. : quaestiones, Macr. S. 7, 3 .

mĭnūtus.opening: Part. and P. a. , v. minuo fin.

Mĭnўae.opening: , = Μινύαι , the Minyans, Argonauts, the companions of Jason, so called from their ancestor Minyas, a king in Thessaly : Minyae dicti Argonautae, quod plerique eorum ex filiis Minyae fuerant orti, Paul. ex Fest. p. 122…

minyanthes.opening: , = μινυανθές , a kind of large-leaved clover , Plin. 21, 9, 30, § 54 ; 21, 21, 88, § 152 .

minyas.opening: a plant : idem (Pythagoras) minyada appellat, nomine alio Corinthiam, Plin. 24, 17, 100, § 157 .

Mĭnȳēĭas.opening: , = Μινυηϊάς , the daughter of Minyas , Ov. M. 4, 1 .

Mĭnўēĭdĕs.opening: ( ), = Μινυηΐδες , the daughters of Minyas, who were changed into bats for slighting the festival of Bacchus , Ov. M. 4, 32 ; cf. Minyeïdăs, id. ib. 4, 425 .

Mĭnўēĭus.opening: adj. , = Μινυήϊος , of or belonging to Minyas ( poet. ): Minyeia proles, Ov. M. 4, 389 .

Mĭnўēus.opening: ( ), , or , , , = Μινυεῖος , an old name of the river Orchomenos, in Thessaly : Orchomenus, Minyius antea dictus, Plin. 4, 8, 15, § 29 .

mĭo.opening: v. a. , to make water , Inscr. Zaccaria, Marm. Salonit. p. 10, n. 15.

mīrābĭlĭārĭus.opening: mirabilis , a wonder-worker, worker of miracles (eccl. Lat.), Aug. Tract. in Joann. 13 .

mīrābĭlis.opening: ( sup. mirabilissimus, Col. 6, 36, 3 MSS.), , adj. miror , to be wondered at, wonderful, marvellous, extraordinary, admirable, strange, singular (class.): nimium mirimodis mirabilis, Plaut. Trin. 4, 2, 86 : nec hoc tam…

mīrābĭlĭtas.opening: mirabilis , wonderfulness, admirableness, admirable quality (eccl. Lat.): operum, Lact. 7, 4 init.

mīrābundus.opening: adj. miror , wondering, astonished, full of wonder or astonishment (mostly Livian and post-class.): nova res mirabundam plebem convertit, quidnam incidisset, cur, etc., Liv. 3, 38 : Poeni mirabundi, unde, etc., id. 25,…

mīrācŭla.opening: miror , a marvellously ugly woman (ante-class.): diobolares, miraculae, Plaut. Fragm. ap. Varr. L. L. 7, § 64 Müll.: miraculae a miris, id est, monstris, Varr. ib.

mīrācŭlum.opening: id. , a wonderful, strange , or marvellous thing, a wonder, marvel, miracle; wonderfulness, marvellousness (class.; syn.: prodigium, portentum): miracula, quae nunc digna admiratione dicimus, antiqui in rebus turpibus…

mīrātĭo.opening: miror , wonder, admiration : mirationem facere, Cic. Div. 2, 22, 49 .

mīrātor.opening: id. , an admirer ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): formae honestae, Prop. 2, 13, 9 : rerum, Ov. M. 4, 640 ; Hor. S. 1, 2, 36 : inanium, Plin. 14, 4, 5, § 51 : sui, Sen. Vit. Beat. 8, 3 .

mīrātrix.opening: mirator , wondering, admiring; she that wonders or admires ( poet. ): miratrix turba, Juv. 4, 62 : fama, Sen. Hippol. 742 : vetustas sui, Luc. 4, 655

mīrĭfĭcentĭa.opening: mirificus , wonder, admiration (eccl. Lat.): mirabilium, Chrys. Serm. 63.

mīrĭfĭco.opening: v. a. id. , to exalt, make wonderful, magnify (eccl. Lat.): mirifica misericordias tuas, Vulg. Psa. 17, 7 ; 4, 3 .

mīrĭfĭcus.opening: adj. mirus-facio , causing wonder or admiration, wonderful, marvellous, extraordinary, singular, strange (class.). Of persons: voramus litteras cum homine mirifico ... Dionysio, Cic. Att. 4, 11, 1 : homo in doctrinis…

mīrĭmŏdīs.opening: adv. mirus-modus; cf. multimodis; v. Lorenz ad Plaut. Most. 3, 2, 98 , in an astonishing manner : nimium mirimodis mirabilis, Plaut. Trin. 4, 2, 86 ; Claud. Mam. Stat. Anim. 3, 12 .

mīrĭo.opening: mirus . * A singularly or defectively formed person , Att. ap. Varr. L. L. 7, § 64 Müll.—* A wonderer, admirer , Tert. Praescr. 3 .

mirmillo.opening: ( , ), , μορμύλος , a kind of gladiator that used to fight with a Thracian (Threx), or a net-fighter (retiarius), and wore a Gallic helmet, with the image of a fish for a crest (whence the name): retiario pugnanti…

mirmillōnĭcus.opening: ( ), , adj. mirmillo , of or belonging to a mirmillo: genus armaturae, of the mirmillones, Paul. ex Fest. s. v. retiario, p. 284 and 285 Müll.; v. mirmillo: myrmillonica scuta dicebant, cum quibus de muro pugnabant,…

mīro.opening: v. a. , to wonder (ante-class. collat. form of miror): quid miras? Varr. ap. Non. 480, 30 : aut ambos mira aut noli mirare de eodem, id. ib. 32 : si studium mirabis, Pompon. ib. 474, 25 (Com. Rel. v. 108 Rib.).— Part. :…

mīror.opening: ( act. collat. form, v. miro), v. dep. a. and Sanscr. smi, smile; Gr. μειδάω; cf.: mirus, nimīrum , to wonder or marvel at, to be astonished or amazed at a thing; to admire; constr. with acc., acc. with inf. , with…

mīrus.opening: adj. Sanscr. smi; v. miror , wonderful, marvellous, astonishing, extraordinary (class.): mirum et magnum facinus, Plaut. Ps. 1, 5, 97 : mirum me desiderium tenet urbis, Cic. Fam. 2, 11, 11 : miris modis odisse aliquem,…

mis.opening: , an archaic form for meis; v. meus init.

Mīsăgĕnes.opening: a son of Masinissa , Liv. 42, 29 ; 62 sq.

Mīsargўrĭdes.opening: , = μισαργυρια , money-hater , a name comically formed by Plautus to signify usurer , Plaut. Most. 3, 1, 41 .

miscellānĕus.opening: ( ), , adj. miscellus , mixed, miscellaneous (postAug.): turba, of all sorts, App. M. 3, p. 129 fin. — Subst. : , , A hash of different sorts of broken meat, a gallimaufry, hodge-podge , the coarse diet of gladiators,…

miscellĭōnes.grammar: appellantur, qui non certae sunt sententiae, sed variorum mixtorumque judiciorum sunt

miscellus.opening: ( , Mart. Cap. 9, § 997 ), , adj. misceo , mixed (anteclass. and post-Aug.): uvae, Cato, R. R. 23 : genus (i. e. of tame and wild pigeons), Varr. R. R. 3, 7 : ludi, composed of games of several kinds, Suet. Calig. 20 :…

miscĕo.opening: (mistum is found in many MSS. and edd., but is probably a corruption of copyists, representing the weakened sound of x in later times; v. Neue, Formenl. 2, p. 556), , v. a. root mik-, mig-; Sanscr. micras, mixed; Gr.…

miscillĭo.opening: one who is undecided in opinion, Paul. ex Fest. p. 123, 7 Müll.; cf. miseix.

miscipulo.opening: v. n. , to smack : miscipulat, ποππύζει , Gloss. Philox.

miscĭtātus.opening: Part. from the unused miscito, v. freq. from misceo , mixed, mingled , Auct. de Limit. p. 267 Goes.

miscix.opening: adj. misceo , changeable, inconstant : inconstans, Petr. 45, 6 dub. (al. mittix).

mĭsellus.opening: adj. dim. [miser], poor, wretched, unfortunate (rare, and with Cic. only in the epistolary style): homo, Cic. Att. 3, 23, 6 ; id. Fam. 14, 4, 3 : o miselle passer, Cat. 3, 16 .—As subst. : , , , a wretch, miserable…

Mīsēnum.opening: , = Μισηνόν , a promontory, town, and harbor in Campania , now Punta di Miseno , Mel. 2, 4, 9 ; Cic. de Or. 2, 14, 60 ; id. Imp. Pomp. 12, 33 ; Plin. Ep. 6, 20 ; Suet. Aug. 49 ; Tac. A. 4, 5 ; 14, 13 ; cf.: Misenum…

mĭser.opening: adj. prob. Sanscr. root mi-; cf. minuo; akin to Gr. μῖσος; Lat. maestus, maereo , wretched, unfortunate, miserable, pitiable, lamentable , etc. (cf.: infelix, calamitosus). Of persons: nihil est tam miserabile, quam ex…

mĭsĕrābĭlis.opening: adj. miseror , worthy of pity, pitiable, miserable, deplorable, lamentable, wretched, sad (class.): nihil est tam miserabile, quam ex beato miser, Cic. Part. Or. 17, 57 : fiet ultro miserabilis, Quint. 11, 1, 64 ; 9, 4,…

mĭsĕrāmen.opening: id. , pity, commiseration : parvi miseramina panis (al. mihi fragmina panis), Juvenc. 4, 285 .

mĭsĕrātĭo.opening: miseror , a pitying, pity, compassion, commiseration (class.). Lit. : cum quādam miseratione delectare, Cic. Fam. 5, 12, 5 : miserationem commovere, Quint. 6, 1, 46 : miseratione mens judicum permovenda, Cic. Or. 38,…

mĭsĕrātor.opening: id. , one who pities, a commiserator (post-class.), Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 11 ; Juvenc. 2, 295 ; Vulg. Psa. 85, 15 .

mĭsĕrĕo.opening: v. n. and , ( inf. pres. misererier, Lucr. 5, 1023 ; ante- and post-class. part. perf. misertus for miseritus, Scip. Afric. ap. Macr. S. 2, 10 ; Hyg. Fab. 58 ), v. dep. miser , to feel pity, have compassion, to pity,…

mĭsĕresco.opening: v. inch. n. [misereo]. To feel pity, have compassion (only poet. ): his lacrimis vitam damus et miserescimus ultro, Verg. A. 2, 145 : miserescite regis, id. ib. 8, 573 : generis miseresce tui, Stat. Th. 1, 280 .—…

mĭsĕrĕvīvĭum.opening: a plant, also called proserpinaca, App. Herb. 18 .

mĭsĕrĭa.opening: miser , wretchedness, unhappy condition, misfortune, misery; affliction, distress , etc. Lit. (Class.) Nam invidere alii bene esse, tibi male esse, miseriast, Plaut. Truc. 4, 2, 31 : Proloqui Caelo atque terrae Medeaï…

mĭsĕrĭcordĭa.opening: misericors , tender-heartedness, pity, compassion, mercy . Lit. (class.): misericordia est aegritudo ex miseriā alterius injuriā laborantis, Cic. Tusc. 4, 8, 18 : (Stoici) misericordiam, cupiditatem, metum, morbos animi…

mĭsĕrĭcors.opening: adj. misereo-cor , tender-hearted, pitiful, compassionate, merciful (class.).—Of persons and things: credc misericors est, Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 141 : misericordem se praebere, Cic. Caecin. 10, 26 : misericors et mansuetus,…

mĭsĕrĭmōnĭum.opening: ( ), , miser , wretchedness, misery (ante-class. for misera), Laber. ap. Non. 214, 20 .

mĭsĕrĭtūdo.opening: miser . * For miseria, wretchedness, misery , Att. ap. Non. 136, 18 (Trag. Rel. v. 185 Rib.).— For miseratio, pity, compassion , Att. ap. Non. 136, 20 (Trag. Rel. v. 79 Rib.).

mĭsĕrĭtus.opening: and , Part. , from misereor, v. misereo.

mĭsĕro.opening: v. , act. collat. form of miseror (ante-class.): ut miserarent mala, Att. ap. Non. 470, 23 (Trag. Rel. v. 195 Rib.).

mĭsĕror.opening: v. dep. ( act. collat. form, v misero) [miser]. To lament, bewail, deplore : miseratur is, qui conqueritur aliena incommoda: miseretur is, qui miserum sublevat, Paul. ex Fest. p. 123 Müll. (class.): quis illaec est…

mĭsertor.opening: syncop. for miserator, from miseror , a pitier, compassionater : miserande misertor, Ven. Vit. S. Mart. 478 .

mĭsĕrŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [miser], wretched, unfortunate (ante-class.): animula miserula, Ser. ap. Non. 517, 4 ; Afran. ap. Non. 217 : ut illius conmiserescas miserulae orbitudinis, Turp. ap. Non. 146, 18 (Com. Rel. v. 211 Rib.):…

misisŭla.opening: a crust of bread hollowed out in the shape of a spoon : misisula, μυστίλη , Gloss. Philox.

missa.opening: mitto , the mass (eccl. Lat.), Ambros. Ep. 5, 33 .

missīcĭus.opening: or , , adj. mitto , discharged from military service (postAug.): praetorianus, Suet. Ner. 48 ; Inscr. Orell. 3579 ; 3582 .

missĭcŭlo.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to send often : ad me litteras Missiculabas, Plaut. Ep. 1, 2, 29 .

missĭlis.opening: adj. id. , that may be hurled or cast, that is thrown or hurled, missile (not in Cic. or Cæs.): lapides missiles, slingstones, Liv. 1, 43 : telum, id. 22, 37 : ferro, quod nunc missile libro, a javelin, Verg. A. 10, 421…

missĭo.opening: id. . In gen., a letting go, sending away, a sending, despatching; a throwing, hurling (class.): litterarum, Cic. Att. 1, 5, 3 : legatorum, id. Phil. 7, 1, 1 : extra telorum missionem, beyond the range of missiles,…

missĭto.opening: v. freq. a. mitto , to send repeatedly, to send (not in Cic. or Cæs.): supplicantes legatos, Sall. J. 38, 1 : auxilia, Liv. 9, 45, 5 : litteras, Front. de Eloq. p. 234 Mai.: codicillos missitatos, Plin. 33, 1, 4, § 12 .

missor.opening: id. , one who sends, throws , or shoots, an archer (very rare): hic missore vacans fulgens jacet una sagitta (al.: hic misso revocans), Cic. Arat. 84 .

missōrĭum.opening: id. , a dish, charger , for serving up food (post-class.): aurata missoria, Ven. Vit. S. Germ. 13; cf.: lances, missoria, Gloss. Isid.

missum.opening: id. , a prize : ἆθλον , missum, Gloss. Gr. Lat.; also called , , , Schol. Juv. 8, 227 .

missus.opening: mitto , a sending away, a sending, despatching . Lit. missu Caesaris ad Ambiorigem ventitare consueverat, Caes. B. G. 5, 27 : duas venisse legiones missu Caesaris, id. ib. 6, 7 : Archippi regis missu, Verg. A. 7, 752 :…

mistārĭus.opening: or , , misceo , a vessel in which wine was mixed with water, a mixing-vessel , Lucil. ap. Non. 546, 30 .

mistīcĭus.opening: ( ) or , , adj. id. , of mixed race, mongrel, born of parents of different nations; a transl. of the Gr. σύμμικτος (eccl. Lat.), Hier. 5 , in Jer. 25, 19.

mistĭo.opening: ( ), , misceo , a mixing (post-Aug.): aliam mixtionem habet genus avium, Vitr. 1, 4, 7 ; plur. , id. 1, 4, 6 ; 11 .— Transf. , concr., a mixture , Pall. 1, 34, 5 ; 12, 7, 1 .

mistūra.opening: ( ), , id. , a mixing, mingling (ante-class. and post-Aug.). Lit. : mistura immoderata, Varr. ap. Non. 490, 28 : rerum, Lucr. 2, 978 : unguentorum, Plin. 13, 1, 2, § 4 .— In partic., carnal intercourse, copulation ,…

mistūrātus.opening: ( ), , adj. mistura , mixed, mingled (post-class.), Pelag Veter. 6.

mistus.opening: ( ), (only in the abl. sing. ), misceo , a mixing, mingling (post-Aug.): seminis mistu, Col. 6, 37, 7 dub.

Mistyllus.opening: μιστύλλω, to cut up , the name of a cook , Mart. 1, 51, 1 .

Misulāni.opening: ( ), , , a people of Numidia , Plin. 5, 4, 4, § 30 ; called also , Tac. A. 2, 52 ; 4, 24 .

mĭsy.opening: (in the gen. also misys, Scrib. Comp. 34 ; and, misy, Cels. 6, 7, 2 ; 5, 19, 15 ; Veg. 6, 16, 1 ), , = μίσυ . A kind of mushroom or truffle , Plin. 19, 3, 12, § 36 .— A mineral , perh. a vitriolic ore, copperas, sory ,…

mĭtella.opening: dim. mitra , a headband , a kind of turban . Lit. : nobiles adulescentes Neapoli cum mitellā saepe vidimus, Cic. Rab. Post. 10, 26 (dub.): copa Syrisca caput Graia redimita mitella, Verg. Cop. 1 : mitellā textili…

mītesco.opening: ( ), , v. inch. n. [mitis], to become mild or mellow, to grow ripe (of fruits, to lose their roughness or harsh flavor; class.). Lit. : nec grandiri frugum fetum posse nec mitescere, Pac. ap. Non. 343, 16 (Trag. Rel. v.…

Mĭthras.opening: and , , , = Μίθρας . The sun-god of the Persians, Stat. Th. 1, 717 ; Curt. 4, 13, 12 ; Mart. Cap. 2, § 191 ; Claud. Laud. Stil. 1, 63 .— The proper name of a priest of Isis , App. M. 11, p. 267, 35 .— A Roman surname ,…

mithrax.opening: or , , , = μίθραξ , a Persian precious stone , Plin. 37, 10, 63, § 173 ; also called , Sol. 37 .

Mĭthrĭdātes.opening: ( dat. -dati, Gell. 15, 1, 6 ), , = Μιθριδάτης . Mithridates the Great, king of Pontus, who waged war with the Romans, was at last conquered by Pompey, and stabbed himself , Cic. Ac. 2, 1, 3 ; id. Mur. 15, 32 sq. ; id.…

mītĭfĭco.opening: v. a. mitis-facio , to make mild or mellow, to mature, ripen; to make tame, to tame (mostly postAug. for the class. mitigo, q. v.). Lit. : in omne corpus diviso et mitigato cibo, well digested, distributed as nutriment…

mītĭfĭcus.opening: adj. mitifico , mild, soft, gentle ( poet. and post-class.): vapores, Prud. Ham. 963 : mens, Sil. 12, 474 .

mītĭgābĭlĭter.opening: adv. mitigo , mildly, gently (post-class.), Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 4, 32 .

mītĭgātĭo.opening: mitigo , a soothing, mitigating, mitigation (rare but class.), Cic. de Or. 3, 30, 118 : multis mitigationibus lenire, Auct. Her. 4, 37, 49 : quae non indiget mitigationis, id. ib. 4, 37, 50 : si est lingua curationis,…

mītĭgātīvus.opening: adj. id. , soothing, mitigative (post-class.): curatio, Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 5, 45 : cataplasma, id. Tard. 2, 1, 52 ; 5, 2, 37 .

mītĭgo.opening: v. a. mitis-ago , to make mild, soft , or tender, make ripe or mellow; to make tame, to tame (class.). Lit. : cum aestivā maturitate alia mitigaverit, alia torruerit, Cic. Rep. 4, 1, 6 (cited ap. Non. 343, 21 ): mitiget…

mĭtĭlo.opening: v. n. , to cry like the acredula: acredula tunc mitilans (al. trutilans, truculans), Auct. Carm. Philom. 16.

mītis.opening: adj. etym. dub.; cf. Sanscr. mith-, to associate; Lat. mutuus , mild, mellow, mature, ripe; of the soil, mellow, light, kindly, fruitful; of a river, calm, gentle, placid (class.; syn.: lenis, placidus, comis). Lit. :…

mītĭuscŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [mitior], rather mild, mildish (post-class.): febres, Cael. Aur. Acut. praef. § 18.

mī^tra.opening: , = μίτρα . A headband, coif, turban of the Asiatics; in Greece and Rome worn only by women, except occasionally by effeminate young men: P. Clodius a crocotā, a mitrā ... est factus repente popularis, Cic. Har. Resp.…

mī^trātus.opening: adj. mitra , wearing a turban, turbaned : mitrati chori, Prop. 4 (5), 7, 42. Arabes, Plin. 6, 28, 32, § 162 : caput, Sid. Carm. 9, 2, 199 ; Sol. 33, 16 .

mitrŭla.opening: dim. id. , a little headband, band, bandage (post-class.): alba mitrula, Sol. 27, 51 .

mittendārĭus.opening: mitto , a public officer who was sent into the provinces to collect the taxes (post-class.): e numero mittendariorum, Impp. Gratian. Valent. et Theod. Cod. Th. 6, 30, 2; ib. 8 and 9.

mitto.opening: (contr. form, misti for misisti, Cat. 14, 14 : archaic inf. pass. mittier, Plaut. Capt. 2, 3, 78 ), v. a. etym. dub.; cf. Sanscr. math-, to set in motion , to cause to go, let go, send, to send off, despatch , etc. In…

mītŭlus.opening: and ( ), , , = μύτυλος, a kind of mussel, seamussel , Plin. 9, 51, 74, § 160 ; 32, 9, 36, § 111 ; also, mutulus, Cato, R. R. 158 ; Hor. S. 2, 4, 28 .

Mitys.opening: or , , a river of Macedonia , Liv. 44, 7 .

mī^ūrus versus.opening: μίουρος, μείουρος , a hexameter that has at the end an iambus instead of a spondee , Ter. de Metr. p. 2425 P.; Serv. Centim. p. 1824 P.

mius.opening: adj. , an old form for meus, Diom. p. 319 P.: v. meus.

Mnasĕas.opening: , = Μνασἐας, an author who wrote De Re Rustica, Varr. R. R. 1, 1, 9 ; Col. 1, 1, 9 ; Plin. 37, 2, 11, § 38 .

Mnēmon.opening: , = Μνήμων (having a good memory). A surname of king Artaxerxes , Nep. Reg. 1, 3 .— A Roman surname , Inscr. Mur. 819, 2.

Mnēmŏnĭdes.opening: the Muses, daughters of Mnemosyne , Ov. M. 5, 268 ; 280 .

Mnēmŏsўnē.opening: , = Μνημοσύνη (remembrance). The mother of the Muses , Ov. M. 6, 114 ; Cic. N. D. 3, 31, 54 ; Phaedr. 3 prol. 18: natae Mnemosynes, the Muses, Aus. Ep. 4, 64 .— In plur. : , , , the Muses , Aus. Idyll. 11, 30 .

mnēmŏsȳnon.opening: , = μνημοσυνον, a memorial : mnemosynon mei sodalis, Cat. 12, 13 .

Mnēsarchus.opening: , = Μνήσαρχος . Acc. to some, the father of Pythagoras , App. Flor. 2, p. 55 Oud.— A Stoic philosopher , Cic. de Or. 1, 11, 45 ; 1, 18, 83 al.

mnēster.opening: , = μνηστήρ, a wooer, suitor , pure Lat. procus: ad mnesteras, Hyg. Fab. 126 .

Mnēster.opening: a Roman surname : M. Lepidus Mnester, a pantomime, favorite of Caligula, Suet. Calig. 36 ; 55 ; 57 .

Mnestheus.opening: ( ), , , = Μνησθεύς, a Trojan : Mnesthea vocat, Verg. A. 4, 288 .—On account of the metre, also Menestheus (trisyl.): fratre Menestheo, Verg. A. 10, 129 .

Mnēvis.opening: , = Μνεῦις, a black ox consecrated to the sun-god at Heliopolis : Mnevidis regia, Plin. 36, 8, 14, § 65 ; cf. Macr. S. 1, 21 ; Amm. 22, 14, 7 .

Mōab.opening: indecl., the mountainous region on the eastern coast of the Dead Sea, extending from Zoar to the river Arnon , Vulg. Gen. 36, 35 ; 48, 15 and 20, etc.—Hence, , , , an inhabitant of Moab, a Moabite , Vulg. 1 Chron. 11,…

mōbĭlis.opening: adj. for movibilis, from moveo , easy to be moved, movable; loose, not firm (class.). Lit. : sum pernix pedibus manibus mobilis, Plaut. Mil. 3, 1, 36 : mobiles turres, Curt. 8, 11, 32 : oculi, Cic. N. D. 2, 57, 142 :…

mōbĭlĭtas.opening: mobilis , movableness, mobility, activity, speed, rapidity, quickness (class.). Lit. : animal mobilitate celerrimā, Cic. N. D. 2, 15, 42 : linguae, volubility, id. de Or. 1, 28, 127 : equitum, agility, rapidity (opp.…

mōbĭlĭto.opening: v. a. mobilis , to make movable, to make quick (ante-class.): omnia mobilitantur, Lucr. 3, 248 : laetitia me mobilitat, Caecil. ap. Non. 4, 346, 14 : mobilitatā mente, Laber. ap. Non. 137, 27 (Com. Rel. v. 91 Rib.).

Mōcilla.opening: a Roman surname , e. g. L. Julius Mocilla, Nep. Att. 11 .

mōcōsus.grammar: a, um, a false reading for inotiosus
mōcōsus.opening: Quint. 11, 3, 183 ; and for morosus, Cic. Att. 1, 13, 2 .

mŏdĕrābĭlis.opening: adj. moderor , moderate : nihil moderabile suadere, Ov. Am. 1, 6, 59 .

mŏdĕrāmen.opening: id. , a means of managing or governing , e. g. a rudder, helm ( poet. and in post-class. prose). Lit. Innixus moderamine navis, Ov. M. 15, 726 ; so in plur. , id. ib. 3, 644 .— Management, direction, control : equorum,…

mŏdĕrāmentum.opening: id. , a means of guidance, a guide : accentus moderamenta vocum, Gell. 13, 6, 1 .

mŏdĕranter.opening: adv. id. , with control : moderanter habere habenas, = moderari habenas, Lucr. 2, 1096 Munro ad loc.

mŏdĕrātim.opening: adv. moderatus , in due measure, gradually : crescere, Lucr. 1, 323 .

mŏdĕrātĭo.opening: moderor . A moderating, moderation in any thing; moderateness, temperateness of the weather (Ciceron.): dummodo illa praescriptio moderatioque teneatur, Cic. Cael. 18, 42 : moderatio et continentia, id. Att. 6, 2, 4 :…

mŏdĕrātor.opening: id. , a manager, ruler, governor, director. Lit. (class.): rector et moderator tanti operis, Cic. N. D. 2, 35, 90 : dierum, id. Tusc. 1, 28, 70 : equorum, Ov. M. 4, 245 : arundinis, an angler, id. ib. 8, 856 : pectinis…

mŏdĕrātrix.opening: moderator . She who moderates or allays; a directress, mistress, governess (mostly Ciceron.): sibi, Plaut. Cist. 2, 2, 3 .— That which rules, guides, controls , etc.: temperantia est moderatrix omnium commotionum, Cic.…

mŏdernus.opening: adj. from modo, just now; like hodiernus from hodie , modern (post-class.); as subst. : , , , things or institutions of the present : antiquorum diligentissimus imitator, modernorum nobilissimus institutor, Cassiod.…

mŏdĕro.opening: v. a. modus , to moderate a thing (in verb. fin. only anteand post-class.). Lit. With acc. : neque tuum te ingenium moderat, Pac. ap. Non. 471, 7 .— With dat. : ego voci moderabo meae, Plaut. Mil. 2, 2, 115 .— Transf. ,…

mŏdĕror.opening: ( inf. moderarier for moderari, Lucr. 5, 1298 ), v. dep. modus , to set a measure, set bounds to a thing (syn.: tempero, rego, guberno). Lit. , to moderate, mitigate, restrain, allay, temper, qualify; with dat.…

mŏdestĭa.opening: modestus , moderateness, moderation; esp. in one's behavior, unassuming conduct, modesty (opp. immodestia, superbia, licentia; class.). In gen.: eam virtutem Graeci σωφροσύνην vocant: quam soleo equidem tum…

Mŏdestīnus.opening: a Roman surname , Inscr. Marin. Frat. Arv. 36; Inscr. Grut. 712, 2 .—So, Herennius Modestinus, a celebrated lawyer under Alexander Severus , Lampr. Alex. Sev. 68 .

mŏdestus.opening: adj. modus , keeping due measure, moderate; esp. in behavior, modest; as respects anger, calm, gentle, dispassionate; towards others, kind, forbearing, temperate, mild; in morals, honest, virtuous, sober, discreet,…

mŏdĭālis.opening: adj. modius , containing a modius or Roman peck (ante- and postclass.): aulae, calicesque, Plaut. Capt. 4, 4, 8 : figura, Tert. ad Nat. 2, 8 .

mŏdĭātĭo.opening: id. , a measuring by modii (post-class.), Cod. Th. 11, 24, 2.

mŏdĭcellus.opening: adj. dim. [modicus], very moderate, very little (post-Aug.): modicella culcita, Suet. Ner. 48 dub. (al. modica; v. Oud. ad loc.).

mŏdĭcus.opening: adj. modus , having or keeping a proper measure, moderate (cf. mediocris); esp. in behavior, modest, temperate; also, of size, moderate-sized; middling, ordinary, mean, bad (class.; syn.: moderatus, mediocris). In a…

mŏdĭfĭcātĭo.opening: modificor , a measuring, measure (post-Aug.): versuum lex ac modificatio, Sen. Ep. 88, 3 : verborum, Gell. 10, 3, 15 ; cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 160, 10 Müll.

mŏdĭfĭcātor.opening: id. , one who gives the proper measure to a thing, a moderator, manager (post-class.): tibicen omnis modi peritus modificator, App. Flor. p. 341 .

mŏdĭfĭco.opening: v. n. and a. [modusfacio]. Neutr., to limit, set limits to : alicui in aliquā re intercedere aut modificare, Front. Ep. ad M. Caes. 4, 3 Mai.— Act., to control, regulate : vitalis motus, Aug. de Music. 6, 17, 58 .—…

mŏdĭfĭcor.opening: v. dep. ( act. collat. form, v. modifico), a. and modificus , to measure off, measure a thing (post-class. in verb. finit. ). Lit. : comprehensa mensura Herculani pedis, quanta longinquitas corporis ei mensurae…

mŏdĭfĭcus.opening: adj. modus-facio , measured (post-class.): mela modifica, Aus. Parent. 27, 2 .

mŏdimpĕrātor.opening: for modi imperator , the president or chairman of a convivial party , who prescribes the quantity to be drunk (the magister bibendi, the Greek συμποσίαρχος ): potandi modimperatores, Varr. ap. Non. 142, 7 .

mŏdĭŏlum.opening: dim. of modium, v. modius , the yolk : quinque ovorum modiola, Plin. Val. 1, 64 .

mŏdĭŏlus.opening: dim. modius , lit., a small measure; hence, transf., A kind of drinking-vessel , Dig. 34, 2, 37 .— A bucket on a water-wheel, Vitr. 10, 9 : modioli gemelli, the boxes or cylinders of a forcing-pump, id. 10, 13 .— The…

mŏdĭus.opening: ( gen. plur. modiūm: qui CCCC. modium quinque milia, Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 36, § 83 : modiorum, Plaut. Mil. 4, 2, 72 ), ( neutr. collat. form: , , , Cato, R. R. 58 ; so in plur. : modia vicena, Plin. 18, 16, 43, § 145 )…

mŏdŏ.opening: (scanned mŏdō, Plaut. Ps. 2, 3, 23 ; Lucr. 2, 11, 35 ; Cic. poët. N. D. 2, 42, 107; v. Corss. Ausspr. 2, p. 480; Lachm. ad Lucr. 2, p. 140 ), adv. orig. abl. of modus, q. v. . Qs., by measure, expressing, like tantum, a…

mŏdŭlābĭlis.opening: adj. modulor , that can be sung or played ( poet. ): carmen, Calp. Ecl. 4, 63 .

mŏdŭlāmen.opening: id. , melody, euphony (post-class.): (Cicero) in secundā (in Verrem, i. e. Verr. 2, 2, 78, § 191) simili usūs modulamine, manifesto peccatu inquit, non peccato, Gell. 13, 21 (20), 16: caeli ac siderum, Macr. Somn. Scip.…

mŏdŭlāmentum.opening: id. , melody, euphony (post-class.): modulamenta orationis M. Tullii, Gell. 1, 7, 19 .

mŏdŭlātĭo.opening: modulor , a regular measure (post-Aug.). In gen.: operis modulationes, Vitr. 5, 9, 3 : dorica, id. 5, 9, 2 : incedendi, a marching to time, Gell. 1, 11, 18 .— In partic., a rhythmical measure, modulation; hence, singing…

mŏdŭlātor.opening: id. , one who measures by rule, a director of music, a musician ( poet. and post-Aug. prose).— Absol. : optimus est modulator, Hor. S. 1, 3, 130 : vocis et cantūs, Col. 1 prooem. § 3.

mŏdŭlātrix.opening: modulator , she that regulates (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Bapt. 3 .

mŏdŭlātus.opening: modulor , a modulating ( poet. ): canoro saxa modulatu trahens, music, a playing on the lute, Sen. Herc. Fur. 263 .

mŏdŭlor.opening: v. dep. modulus , to measure off properly, to measure; to manage properly, to regulate . In gen. (only post-Aug.): in modulanda statūs longitudinisque ejus praestantiā, Gell. 1, 1, 1 ; cf.: quanta longinquitas corporis…

mŏdŭlus.opening: dim. modus , a small measure, a measure (not in Cic. or Cæs.). Lit. : relinquitur de numero, quem faciunt alii majorem, alii minorem, nulli enim hujus moduli naturales, Varr. R. R. 2, 2, 20 : ab imo Ad summum moduli…

mŏdus.opening: root med-, measure, weigh; Gr. μέδομαι, μέδοντες, μήστωρ, μέδιμνος; cf.: modius, modestus, moderor , a measure with which, or according to which, any thing is measured, its size, length, circumference, quantity (freq.…

moechīle.opening: moechus , a place where adultery is committed (post-Aug.): moechile (al. cubile), Petr. 113 .

moechillus.opening: id. , an adulterer, paramour : moechilli, facto, v. l. ap. Cat. 113, 2 dub. for mucillam.

moechĭmēnĭum.opening: id. , adultery , Laber. ap. Gell. 16, 7, 2 (also ap. Non. 140, 31 ).

moechisso.opening: v. a. id. , to ravish (anteclass.): aliquam, Plaut. Cas. 5, 4, 6 .

moechŏ-cĭnaedus.opening: moechuscinaedus , a man abandoned to lewdness , Lucil. ap. Non. 493, 26 .

moechor.opening: v. dep. moechus , to commit adultery ( poet. and late Lat.), Cat. 94, 1 ; Hor. S. 1, 2, 49 ; Mart. 6, 91, 2 ; Mos. et Rom. Leg. Coll. 4, 1, 1.

Moenis.opening: the River Main, in Germany , Mel. 3, 3, 3 .—Called also , , Tac. G. 28 ; Plin. 9, 15, 17, § 45 ; Amm. 17, 1, 6 .

Moera.opening: the name of one of the Fates , Gell. 3, 16, 11 .

moerica.opening: ( ), , a sort of grape-vine , otherwise unknown, Plin. 14, 2, 6 ; Col. 3, 2, 27 .

Moeris.opening: the name of a shepherd and sorcerer , Verg. E. 8, 96, 98 ; 9, 1 ; 53, 54 , etc.

Moesa.opening: the grandmother of Heliogabalus , Lampr. Heliog. 10 .

Moesi.opening: the Mœsians, a people in the modern Bulgaria and Servia , Plin. 3, 26, 29, § 149 ; 4, 11, 18, § 41 ; Tac. A. 15, 6 ; Juv. 9, 143 ; Inscr. Orell. 4984 .—Hence, , , , the country of the Mœsi, Mœsia , the modern Bulgaria…

moesīlēum.opening: , corrupted from mausoleum, a tomb, mausoleum , Front. de Limit. Agror. p. 43 Goes.

Mogontĭăcum.opening: a city of Germany , the mod. Mayence , or Mainz , Eutr. 7, 8 .—Called also , Tac. H. 4, 15 ; 24 ; 25 ; 33 al.: , , , Amm. 15, 11, 8 ; and , , , Ven. Fort. 9, 9.

mŏla.opening: cf. μύλη, μύλος, mill, millstone; μύλαι, grinders, molar-teeth; cf. molaris , a millstone; and usu. plur. molae, a mill (driven by slaves, animals, or water): verbera, compedes, molae, Plaut. Men. 5, 6, 9 : molarum…

Molae.opening: , in the relig. lang. of the Italic people, perh. the daughters of Mars, the protectresses of mills , Gell. 13, 22 .

mŏlāris.opening: adj. mola , of or belonging to a mill or to grinding, mill- . Adj. (post-Aug.): molaris lapis, Plin. 36, 19, 30, § 137 ; Isid. 19, 10, 10 : petrae molares, Grom. Vet. 401, 20: saxum, id. ib. 212, 9 : lapis molaris,…

mŏlārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to a mill or to grinding, mill- (anteclass.): asinus molarius, a mill-ass, an ass that turns a mill, Cato, R. R. 11, 4 ; Varr. R. R. 1, 19, 3 .

mŏlaxo.opening: v. a. , for malaxo, Pelag. Vet. 5.

molemonĭum.opening: a plant that promotes vomiting , Plin. 26, 7, 25, § 40 .

mŏlendārĭus.opening: adj. 1. molo , of or belonging to a mill or to grinding, mill- (post-class.): asina molendaria, Dig. 33, 7, 18, § 2 : meta (al. molendinaria), ib. § 5.

mŏlendīnārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to a mill, mill- (post-class.). Adj. : molendinariae metae, Amm. 17, 4, 15 : molendinaria meta (al. molendaria), Dig. 33, 7, 18, § 5 .— Subst. : , , , a miller , Inscr. Grut. 1114, 6 .

mŏlendīnum.opening: id. , a millingplace, mill-house (eccl. Lat.), Aug. in Psa. 132, 4 ; 36, 2 .

mōles.opening: prob. for mog-les; root magh-; cf. magnus; Gr. μόχθος, μογεῖν, μόγις; cf.: μοχλός, molīri, molestus; Germ. Mühe , a shapeless, huge, heavy mass, huge bulk . Lit. In gen. ( poet. ): Chaos, rudis indigestaque moles, Ov.…

mŏlestĭa.opening: molestus , trouble, troublesomeness, irksomeness, uneasiness, annoyance, molestation, vexation, disgust, dislike , etc. (class.). Lit. In gen.: sine molestiā, Cato, R. R. 154 ; cf.: sine molestiā tuā, without trouble to…

mŏlesto.opening: v. a. id. , to trouble, annoy, molest : aliquem, Petr. Fragm. ap. Fulg. p. 566, 28 ; id. Sat. 58 ; App. Herb. 71 : neminem molestari volo nomine debiti, Dig. 34, 3, 20 .— Absol. : uva raro valde molestat, is…

mŏlestus.opening: adj. moles , troublesome, irksome, grievous, annoying (class.; cf. importunus): abscede hinc, molestus ne sis! Plaut. As. 2, 4, 63 : provincia, Cic. Mur. 8, 18 : operosus ac molestus labor, id. N. D. 2, 23, 39 : alicui…

mŏletrīna.opening: 1. molo , a mill (ante-class.), Cato ap. Non. 63, 26 .

mŏlīle.opening: mola , the drawing-ropes or traces of an ass in a mill, Cato, R. R. 10 and 11.

mōlīmen.opening: molior , a great exertion, effort, endeavor, attempt, undertaking (mostly poet. , not in Cic.): ventus Trudit agens magnam magno molimine navem, Lucr. 4, 902 : revellere Annosam pinum magno molimine, Ov. M. 12, 357 :…

mōlīmentum.opening: molior , a great exertion, effort, endeavor, attempt, undertaking (good prose, but not in Cic.): magno cum molimento procedunt, Sisenn. ap. Non. 142, 5 : neque se exercitum sine magno commeatu atque molimento in unum…

mŏlīnus.opening: adj. mola , of or belonging to a mill, mill- (eccl. Lat.): saxum, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 35 .—Hence, as subst. , , , a mill , Amm. 18, 8, 11 . — , , , a mill , Cassiod. Inst. Div. Litt. 29 .

mōlĭo.opening: ( act. collat. form of molior). To build, erect (post-Aug.): neque quis quid molit, S. C. ap. Front. Aquaed. 129 .— In a pass. signif., to set in motion, start : jam sospitatricis deae peculiaris pompa moliebatur, App.…

mōlĭor.opening: ( inf. molirier for moliri, Lucr. 5, 934 ), v. dep. n. and a. [moles]. Neutr. To set one's self or one's powers in motion, to make exertions, exert one's self, to endeavor, struggle, strive, toil , etc. (rare but…

mōlītĭo.opening: molior , a putting in motion, moving, removing; a laborious undertaking, preparation, contrivance (rare but class.): molitio agrorum, a working, ploughing, digging , Col. prooem.: terrena, id. 11, 2, 98 : facilis…

mŏlĭtĭo.opening: molo , a grinding (late Lat.), Ambros. Serm. 29 .

mōlītor.opening: molior , one who undertakes to do a thing, an attempter, author, framer, contriver (class.): effector mundi molitorque deus, Cic. Univ. 5 : ratis, Ov. M. 8, 302 : caedis, Tac. A. 11, 29 : novarum rerum, Suet. Dom. 10 :…

mŏlĭtor.opening: 1. molo , a miller (post-class.). Lit. , Dig. 33, 7, 12, § 15 . — Transf. , in mal. part., Aus. Ep. 90, 3 .

mōlītrix.opening: 1. molitor , she who attempts, frames, contrives (post-Aug.): novarum rerum, Suet. Ner. 35 .

mŏlĭtūra.opening: 1. molo , a false read. for moluntur, Plin. 15, 23, 25, § 52 .

mollĕo.opening: v. n. mollis , to be soft , Theod. Prisc. 1, 28 .

mollesco.opening: v. inch. n. [molleo], to become soft, to soften ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose; cf. liquesco). Lit. : rura colit nemo: mollescunt colla juvencis, Cat. 64, 38 : ebur, Ov. M. 10, 283 : tactu, Plin. 12, 17, 37, § 76 .—…

mollĭcellus.opening: adj. dim. [mollis], soft, tender, delicate ( poet. ): nates, Cat. 25, 10 .

mollĭcīna.opening: mollis , a kind of soft garment (post-class.), Nov. ap. Non. 540, 22 .

mollĭcŏmus.opening: adj. mollis-coma , soft-haired (post-class.): herbae, Avien. Perieg. 1082 .

mollĭcŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [mollis]. Lit. , soft, tender, delicate ( poet. ): escae, Plaut. Cas. 2, 8, 58 : meus molliculus caseus, id. Poen. 1, 2, 154 .— Trop. , voluptuous : versiculi, Cat. 16, 4 ; cf. adulescentulus, Charis. 183 P.

Mollĭcŭlus.opening: a Roman surname , e. g. Ti. Minucius Molliculus, Liv. 40, 35 .

mollĭfĭco.opening: v. a. mollis-facio , to make soft, to soften, mollify , Caesar. Epist. Hortat. ad Virgg.; cf.: mollifico, ἁπαλύνω, μαλάσσω , Gloss. Lat. Gr.

mollĭfĭcus.opening: adj. mollifico , making soft, softening (post-class.): phlebotomia est mollifica corporis, Cael. Aur. Tard. 4, 1, 9 .

mollīmentum.opening: mollio , a means of softening or mitigating (post-Aug.): calamitatum, Sen. Tranq. 10 . 2.

mollĭo.opening: (mollibat for molliebat, Att. ap. Non. 347, 16 ; Ov. M. 6, 21 : mollirier for molliri, Ter. Phorm. 4, 3, 27 ), v. a. mollis , to make soft, pliant, flexible , or supple, to soften (class.). Lit. : frigoribus durescit…

mollĭ-pes.opening: adj. mollis-pes , softfooted ( poet. ): boves, Cic. poët. Div. 1, 9, 15.

mollis.opening: adj. Gr. μαλακός, ἀμαλός, μῶλυς; cf. βληχρός, perh. Lat. mulier (mollior) , easily movable, pliant, flexible, supple; soft, tender, delicate, gentle, mild, pleasant (class.; syn.: tener, facilis, flexibilis, lentus).…

mollĭtĭa.opening: ( ), , , and ( ), , mollis , movableness, pliability, flexibility, suppleness; softness (class.). Lit. : mollitia cervicum, Cic. Or. 18, 59 : lapidis, Plin. 36, 22, 45, § 162 : lanae, id. 19, 3, 18, § 48 : carnis, id.…

mollĭtōrius.opening: adj. id. , emollient (late Lat.), Auct. de Virt. Herb. 30, p. 137.

mollĭtūdo.opening: id. , suppleness, flexibility, softness (class.). Lit. : mollitudo vocis, flexibility of the voice, Auct. Her. 3, 11, 20 : manuum, Pac. ap. Gell. 2, 26, 13 : assimilis spongiis mollitudo, Cic. N. D. 2, 55, 136 : viarum,…

mollūgo.opening: a variety of the plant lappago, Plin. 26, 10, 65, § 102 ; also called molligo, Marc. Emp. 26 .

molluscus.opening: adj. mollis . Soft : mollusca nux; and absol. : , , , a kind of soft nut with a thin shell , Plaut. ap. Macr. S. 2, 14 ; Plin. 15, 22, 24, § 90 .— Subst. : , , , a fungus that grows on the maple-tree , Plin. 16, 16, 27,…

mŏlo.opening: v. a. mola , to grind in a mill. Lit. : molendum usque in pistrino, Ter. Phorm. 2, 1, 19 : hordeum in subtilem farinam, to grind into fine flour, Plin. 18, 7, 14, § 73 : tolle molam, et mole farinam, Vulg. Isa. 47, 2 .—…

Mŏlo.opening: or , , , a surname of Apollonius of Rhodes, a Greek rhetorician, one of Cicero's teachers, who came to Rome as an ambassador of the Rhodians , Cic. Brut. 70, 245 ; 90, 311 ; id. Att. 2, 1, 9 ; Quint. 12, 6, 7 , etc.

mŏlŏchĭnārĭus.opening: ( ), , id. . A mallow-dyer, one who dyes with the color of mallows (ante- and post-class.), Plaut. Aul. 3, 5, 40 .— A seller of mallowcolored garments , Inscr. Mar. 939, 6.

mōlon.opening: a plant, also called syron, Plin. 26, 7, 19, § 33 .

Mŏlorchus.opening: a poor vine-dresser near Nemea, who hospitably entertained Hercules when about to slay the lion of that place , Stat. S. 3, 1, 29 ; 4, 6, 51 ; id. Th. 4, 160 ; Mart. 4, 64, 30 .— Poet. : Alpheum linquens lucosque…

mŏlorthus.opening: a sounding-lead : gravis molorthus (al. molybdis), Stat. S. 3, 2, 30 .

Mŏlossi.opening: , = Μολοσσοί , the Molossians, a people in the eastern part of Epirus , Plin. 4 prooem.; Cic. Div. 1, 34, 76 ; Nep. Them. 8, 4 .—They were so called from Molossus, the son of Pyrrhus, king of Epirus, and Andromache,…

Mŏlossĭa.opening: , = Μολοσσία , Molossia, the country of the Molossi, in Epirus , Serv. Verg. A. 3, 297 .

mŏlossĭambos.opening: molossus-iambus , a metrical foot consisting of three long syllables and an iambus (e. g. ādmīrābĭlēs), Diom. p. 478 P.

Mŏlossĭcus.opening: adj. Molossus , Molossian (ante- and post-class.): parasiti Molossici (v. Molossus, A.), i. e. as ravenous as Molossian hounds, Plaut. Capt. 1, 1, 18 : carmen, consisting wholly of molossi (———; e. g.: Romani victores…

Mŏlossis.opening: , = Μολοσσίς , Molossis, the country of the Molossi, in the eastern part of Epirus , Liv. 8, 24 .

mŏlossŏ-pyrrhĭchĭus.opening: molossus-pyrrhichius , a metrical foot consisting of a molossus and a pyrrhichius (e. g. ādmīrābĭlĭs), Diom. p. 478 P.

mŏlosso-spondēus.opening: molossusspondeus , a metrical verse consisting of a molossus and a spondee (e. g. cōntūrbātōrēs), Diom. p. 479 P.

Mŏlossus.opening: son of Pyrrhus, king of Epirus, and Andromache, the progenitor of the Molossi, acc. to Serv. Verg. A. 3, 297 .

mŏlū^crum.opening: mola . A millbroom , i. e. a broom for sweeping out a mill : molucrum, quo molae verruntur, quod Graeci μυλήκορον dicunt, Paul. ex Fest. p. 140 Müll.— A handle for turning a mill : molucrum, quo molae vertuntur, Paul.…

Mŏlus.opening: or , , , = Μόλος , the father of Meriones, Hyg. Fab. 97 .
