mōly.opening: , = μῶλυ . A plant with a white flower and a black root , Plin. 25, 4, 8, § 26 .— Another plant, a kind of nightshade , Plin. 21, 31, 105, § 180 .

mŏlybdaena.opening: , = μολύβδαινα . Sulphuret of lead, galena , Plin. 34, 18, 53, § 173 .— The plant leadwort (pure Lat. plumbago), Plin. 25, 13, 97, § 155 .

mŏlybdītis.opening: , = μολυβδῖτις , the spume of lead, lead-ashes , Plin. 33, 6, 35, § 106 .

mŏlybdus.opening: , and , , , = μόλυβδος and μολυβδις , lead (pure Lat. plumbum), Stat. S. 3, 2, 30 ; v. molorthus.

momar.opening: , = μῶμαρ : Siculi stultum appellant, Paul. ex Fest. p. 140 Müll.

mōmen.opening: for movimen, from moveo . Movement, motion : e salso consurgere momine ponti, i. e. from the salt billows, Lucr. 6, 474 ; so also id. 2, 632 , and 4, 179; v. Lachm. (where others read numine); cf. id. 3, 144 .— Weight,…

mōmentālĭter.opening: adv. momentum , in a moment (post-class.), Fulg. Myth. 2, 3 .

mōmentāna.opening: id. , a delicate pair of scales for weighing gold and silver : momentana pro parva modicaque pecunia, Isid. Orig. 16, 25, 4 .

mōmentānĕus.opening: adj. id. , short, of brief duration, momentary (eccl. Lat.): momentaneus ardor gentium, Tert. adv. Marc. 3, 17 dub.: vices rerum, Ambros. Ep. 2, 24 init. : felicitas, Fulg. Myth. 2, 17 ; Hier. Ep. 69 (83), 9; Vulg. 2…

mōmentārĭus.opening: adj. id. , brief, of brief duration, momentary; quick (postclass.): maritus, i. e. who stays but a short time, App. M. 5, p. 164, 21 : vita, id. ib. 2 , p. 127, 24: cura, Dig. 34, 1, 8 .— Transf. , instantaneous :…

mōmentōsus.opening: adj. id. , rapid, momentary : rapina (apis), Ps.- Quint. Decl. 13, 12 .

mōmentum.opening: for movimentum, from moveo , a movement, motion (as an indwelling force; cf.: motio, motus; class.). Lit. : astra forma ipsa figuraque sua momenta sustentant, Cic. N. D. 2, 46, 117 : pisces levi caudae in utrumque…

Mŏna.opening: , = Μόνα , the name of two islands . The Isle of Man , near Britain, Caes. B. G. 5, 13 .— The Isle of Anglesea , Tac. A. 14, 29 ; id. Agr. 14 ; 18 ; Plin. 2, 75, 77, § 187 .

mŏnăcha.opening: , = μοναχή , a nun (eccl. Lat.), Hier. Ep. 39, 4 .

mŏnăchĭcus.opening: adj. , = μοναχικός , monkish (post-class.): certamen, Just. Novell. Constit. 133, 5 .

mŏnăchīum.opening: , = μοναχεῖον , a monastery (post-class.), Impp. Valent. et Marc. Cod. Just. 1, 2, 13 .

mŏnăchus.opening: , = μοναχός (that lives alone), a monk (eccl. Lat.), Rutil. Nam. 1, 441 ; Sid. Ep. 5, 17 ; Hier. Ep. 22, 34 .

Mŏnaeses.opening: a king of the Parthians : Monaeses et Pacori manus, Hor. C. 3, 6, 9 (Monaeses et Pacorus reges Persarum fuere, Schol. Acr.).

mŏnarcha.opening: , = μονάρχης , an absolute ruler, a monarch ( poet. ): caeruli monarcha ponti, Vet. poët. ap. Mar. Victor. p. 2551 P.

mŏnarchĭa.opening: , = μοναρχία , absolute rule, monarchy (post-class. for unius dominatio, imperium singulare, regnum, regalis potestas), Capitol. Max. and Balb. 14; Tert. adv. Prax. 14 ; Lact. 1, 5, 23 .

mŏnārĭus.opening: adj. μόνος , having but one form in inflection: nomen, Gram. Vatic. de Nom. 68 (class., Auct. 5, p. 240 Mai.).

mŏnas.opening: , = μονάς , unity; a unit, monad (post-class.), Macr. Somn. Scip. 1, 6, 7 sqq.; Tert. adv. Val. 37 ; id. Praescr. 49 fin. et saep.

mŏnastērĭālis.opening: adj. monasterium , monastic, monasterial (eccl. Lat.): disciplina, Sid. Ep. 7, 9 .

mŏnastērĭŏlum.opening: dim. id. , a little monastery , Not. Tir. p. 192 ; Hier. Ep. 105, 4 .

mŏnastērĭum.opening: , = μοναστήριον , a monastery (eccl. Lat.), Sid. Ep. 4, 25 ; 7, 17 ; Aug. ad Casul. Ep. 86 .

mŏnaules.opening: , = μοναύλης , a player on the single flute , Not. Tir. p. 173 ; cf. monaulos.

mŏnaulĭter.opening: adv., on a single flute (post-class.): sonare (al. monaliter alone), Mart. Cap. 9, § 906 .

mŏnaulos.opening: or , , , = μόναυλος , a single flute, a flute with a single pipe (post-Aug.): fistulam et monaulum (invenit) Pan Mercurii, Plin. 7, 56, 57, § 204 : saepe monaulon habet, Mart. 14, 64, 2 ; cf. monaules.

mŏnazontes.opening: , = μονάζοντες (who live alone), monks (post-class.), Cod. Th. 12, 1, 63.

mŏnēdŭla.opening: a jackdaw, daw , Corvus monedula, Linn.: examina graculorum monedularum, cui soli avi furacitas auri argentique praecipue mira est, Plin. 10, 29, 41, § 77 ; 17, 14, 22, § 99 . Acc. to the myth, the nymph Arne was turned…

mŏnēla.opening: moneo , a reminding, admonition (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Pat. 8 ; id. adv. Marc. 4, 34 .

mŏnēmĕron.opening: , = μονήμερον , a kind of eye-salve , Marc. Emp. 8 .

mŏnĕo.opening: ( inf. pres. pass. monerier, Plaut. Capt. 2, 3, 36 ; perf. subj. moneris pro monueris, Pac. ap. Non. 507, 24 sq. ; cf. Trag. Rel. p. 66 Rib.; likewise: di monerint meliora, Pac. ap. Non. l. l. p. 74 Rib.), v. a.…

mŏnēris.opening: , = μονήρης (sc. ναῦς ), a vessel with a single bank of oars, a galley , Liv. 38, 38, 8 (cf. Tac. H. 5, 23 ).

Mŏnēta.opening: (archaic gen. Monetas, Liv. Andron. ap. Prisc. p. 679 P.), moneo . The mother of the Muses , a transl. of the Gr. Μνημοσύνη : Μνημοσύνη Moneta, Gloss. Philox.; cf. Cic. N. D. 3, 18, 47 ; Hyg. Fab. praef.: filia Monetas,…

mŏnētālis.opening: adj. moneta , of or belonging to the mint; minted, coined (class.): triumviri monetales, the directors of the mint, Dig. 1, 2, 2, § 30 .—In jest of one who asks for money: monetali ascripsi, quod ille ad me pro consule,…

mŏnētārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to the mint : FAMILIA, Inscr. Orell. 3226 .—Hence, subst. : , , , a master of the mint , Inscr. Mur. 968, 5: monetarii, minters, coiners (post-class.), Aur. Vict. Epit. Eutr. 35 ; Eutr. 9, 14…

mŏnīle.opening: kindr. to Sanscr. mani; Lat. gemma, margarīta; Gr. μάννος, μόννος , a necklace, a collar (esp. of women, but also of boys and of animals), Paul. ex Fest. p. 138 Müll.; cf. Quint. 11, 1, 3 : cum (Eriphyle) vidisset…

mŏnĭtĭo.opening: moneo , a reminding, admonishing, advice, admonition, warning (rare but class.): objurgatio post turpe factum castigatio: monitio vero est ante commissum, Paul. ex Fest. p. 196 Müll.: monitio acerbitate, objurgatio…

mŏnĭto.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to remind, admonish (post-class.), Venant. Vit. S. Mart. 2, 387 ; id. Carm. 5, 5, 23 .

mŏnĭtor.opening: id. , one who reminds one of any thing, an admonisher, monitor (syn.: hortator, auctor). In gen.: nil opus fuit monitore, Ter. Heaut. 1, 1, 119 : monitor et praemonstrator, id. ib. 5, 1, 2 : est enim (hoc praeceptum)…

mŏnĭtōrĭus.opening: adj. monitor , that serves to remind or admonish, monitory (post-Aug.): fulmen, Sen. Q. N. 2, 39, 2 ; id. ib. 2, 49, 1 .

mŏnĭtum.opening: moneo , admonition, advice, counsel (rare but class.): meis consiliis, monitis, etc., Cic. Fam. 5, 8, 2 : tuis monitis praeceptisque, id. ib. 5, 13, 3 : meas aures omnium praeceptis monitisque patuisse, id. Phil. 14, 7,…

mŏnĭtus.opening: moneo , a reminding, warning, admonition . In gen. (only poet. ): monitu nutricis, Ov. H. 18, 115 : finierat monitus, id. M. 2, 103 : laevo monitu pueros producit avaros, Juv. 14, 228 : monitus acres tradere, Val. Fl.…

monnŭla.opening: a darling , a late Lat. term of endearment, Inscr. Mur. 2083, 2.

mŏnŏbĕlus.opening: , = μονόβελος (all shaft): i. q. magno pene praeditus, Heliog. ap. Lampr. Heliog. 8, 7 .

mŏnŏbŏlon.opening: , = μόνοσ-βόλος , a single throw , i. e. leaping alone , a game in which various feats of bodily agility are performed without the aid of a leapingpole; diff. from the contomonobolon, where the performer is furnished…

mŏnŏcĕros.opening: , = μονόκερως , a unicorn : asperrimam autem feram monocerotem, reliquo corpore equo similem, capite cervo, pedibus elephanto, cauda apro, mugitu gravi, uno cornu nigro mediā fronte cubitorum duūm eminente, Plin. 8, 21,…

mŏnŏchordos.opening: adj. , = μονόχορδος , of one string : cithara, Aeron. ad Hor. A. P. 216 .— Subst. : , , , μονόχορδον , the monochord, tonometer , Boëth. Instr. Mus. 1, 27 al.† † , , , = μόνοσ-χόρος , one who dances alone, who executes…

mŏnochrōmăta.opening: , = μονοχρώματα , paintings of but one color (postAug.), Plin. 33, 7, 39, § 117 ; 35, 8, 34, § 56 .

mŏnochrōmătos.opening: adj. , = μονοχρώματος , one-colored, of a single color (post-Aug.): picturam singulis coloribus, et monochromaton dictam, Plin. 35, 3, 5, § 15 ; cf. monochromata.

mŏnochrŏnos.opening: adj. , = μονόχρονος , of one time, of the same time or measure (post-class.): tempus, Mart. Cap. 9, § 982 .

mŏnoclōnos.opening: adj. , = μονόκλωνος , having a single branch or shoot (postclass.): herba monoclonos, App. Herb. 10 .

mŏnocnēmos.opening: , = μονόκνημος , one-legged, a one-legged man , Petr. 83 dub.

mŏnŏcōlus.opening: , = μονόκωλος , onelegged , epithet applied to a fabled race of giants, each with but one leg of prodigious strength (post-Aug.): hominum genus, qui monocoli vocarentur, singulis cruribus, Plin. 7, 2, 2, § 23 ; cf.…

mŏnocrēpis.opening: , = μονοκρηπίς , one-shoed, he that has but one shoe (postclass.): monocrepis, id est uno pede calceatus, Hyg. Fab. 12 .

mŏnŏcŭlus.opening: vox hybr. from μόνος and oculus , one-eyed, a one-eyed man (post-class.), Firm. Math. 8, 19; 8, 22; cf. Gloss. Lab. monoculus = μονόφθαλμος .

mŏnōdĭārĭa.opening: μονῳδία , she that sings alone, a female solo-singer , Inscr. Orell. 2633 .

mŏnōdĭārĭus.opening: id. , a solosinger , Not. Tir. p. 173 .

mŏnōdĭum.opening: , = μονῴδιον , the song of a solo-singer , Diom. p. 489 .—Also called , , , = μονῳδία , Isid. Orig. 6, 19, 6 .

Mŏnŏdūs.opening: μονόδους, onetoothed , a son of Prusias, who had only a solid bone instead of teeth .—So, also, Pyrrhus, king of the Epirotæ , Paul. ex Fest. p. 148 Müll.; cf. Plin. 7, 16, 15, § 69 ; Val. Max. 1, 8, 12 ext.

Mŏnoecus.opening: , = Μόνοικος (that dwells alone), a surname of Hercules; hence, Arx Monoeci, a promontory and harbor in Liguria , the mod. Monaco : portus Herculis Monoeci, Plin. 3, 5, 7, § 47 ; Tac. H. 3, 42 : Arx Monoeci, Verg. A. 6,…

mŏnŏgămĭa.opening: , = μονογαμία , a marrying of but one wife, monogamy (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Monog. 2 sq. ; Hier. in. Jovinian. 1, 14.

mŏnŏgămus.opening: , = μονόγαμος , he who has but one wife (eccl. Lat.), Hier. in. Jovinian. 1, 15; id. Ep. 69, 3 .

mŏnŏgĕnēs.opening: μονογενής , onlybegotten, only , Tert. adv. Valent. 7 sqq.

mŏnogramma.opening: , = μονόγραμμα , a character consisting of several letters, a monogram (post-class.), e. g. = Christus, Paul. Nol. Carm. 26, 618 .

mŏnogrammus.opening: or , , adj. , = μονόγραμμος , lit. of pictures, that consist of lines merely, outlined, sketched; hence transf., Of incorporeal gods, shadowy : Epicurus monogrammos Deos et nihil agentes commentus est, Cic. N. D. 2, 23,…

mŏnŏīdēs.opening: adj. , = μονοειδής , having a single form : luna, Firm. Math. 4 praef.

mŏnŏlĭnum.opening: , = μονόλινον , a necklace consisting of a string of pearls , Capitol. Max. Jun. 1, 8 (al. monolium).

mŏnŏlĭthus.opening: adj. , = μονόλιθος , consisting of a single stone, monolith (ante- and post-class.): columnae, Laber. ap. Non. 544, 33 : postes marmorei monolithi, Ampel. Lib. Mem. 8, 12 ; Inscr. Orell. 1593 .

mŏnŏlōris.opening: adj. vox hybr. μόνοσ- lorum , with one thong : vestes, having a single stripe of purple, Vop. Aur. 46, 6 .

mŏnŏmăchĭa.opening: , = μονομαχία , a single combat, duel (post-class.): cur ad monomachiam recurritis? Cassiod. Var. 3 , 24; Serv. Verg. A. 6, 136 ; Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 2, 18 .

mŏnŏmăchus.opening: , = μονόμαχος , he who fights in single combat , Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 1, 9 ; 4, 37 .

mŏnŏmĕter.opening: adj. , = μονόμετρος , consisting of one metre, monometer , Prisc. Metr. Ter. p. 1320 P.

mŏnŏpŏdĭum.opening: , = μονοπόδιον , a table or stand with one foot , Liv. 39, 6 fin. ; cf. Plin. 34, 3, 8, § 14 .

mŏnŏpōlĭum.opening: , = μονοπώλιον , the exclusive privilege of dealing in or selling a thing, a monopoly (post-Aug.), Suet. Tib. 71 ; 30 ; Plin. 8, 37, 56, § 135 .

mŏnoptĕros.opening: adj. , = μονόπτερος , of buildings, with one wing : aedes, Vitr. 4, 7 .

mŏnoptōta.opening: , = μονόπτωτα , in the later grammarians, nouns which have but one case-ending, monoptotes , Diom. p. 288 P.; Prisc. p. 672 ib. et saep.; Mart. Cap. 3, § 242 al.

mŏnŏsŏlis.opening: adj. vox hibr., from μόνος-solea , single-soled (post-class.), Edict. Diocl.

mŏnostĭchĭum.opening: , = μονοστίχιον , a poem consisting of a single verse (post-class.), Aus. Ecl. 7, 8 .

mŏnostĭchum.opening: , = μονόστιχον , a poem consisting of a single verse (postclass.), Aus. Ecl. 8, 2 .

mŏnŏsyllăbus.opening: adj. , = μονοσύλλαβος , monosyllabic (post-Aug.): VOX, Mart. Cap. 3, § 269 ; 5, § 520 .—As subst., a monosyllable : , , (sc. verbum), Aus. Idyll. Lit. Monosyll. 13 : monosyllaba, sc. verba, Quint. 9, 4, 42 ; Mart. Cap.…

mŏnotrĭglўphus.opening: adj. , = μονοτρίγλυφος , that has only one triglyph , Vitr. 4, 3, 7 .

mŏnotrŏpus.opening: , = μονότροπος , of one kind, single : nosmet inter nos ministremus monotropi, Plaut. Stich. 5, 4, 7 (v. Ritschl ad h. l.).

mŏnoxўlus.opening: adj. , = μονόξυλος , that consists of a single piece of wood (post-Aug.): linter, Plin. 6, 23, 26, § 105 .

mons.opening: (archaic abl. montei, Enn. ap. Non. 222, 33 ; cf. Ann. v. 420 Vahl.), etym. dub., perh. from the root min, whence also, emineo, mentum, minari; cf. minae; lit. a projecting body; hence , a mountain, mount . Lit. :…

monstrābĭlis.opening: adj. monstro , worthy to be shown or noticed, conspicuous, remarkable (post-Aug.): probitate morum monstrabilis, Plin. Ep. 6, 21, 4 .

monstrātĭo.opening: id. , a showing, direction (only in Terence and Vitruv.): defessus sum ambulando: ut, Syre, te cum tuā Monstratione magnus perdat Juppiter, direction, Ter. Ad. 4, 6, 1 : solers et expedita monstratio, indication, hint,…

monstrātor.opening: monstro , a shower, pointer out, introducer, inventor, teacher, informant ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): aratri, i. e. Triptolemus, Verg. G. 1, 19 : sacri iniqui, an introducer of human sacrifices, Ov. Ib. 399 :…

monstrātus.opening: (only in the abl. sing. ), monstro , a showing (post-class.): cujus monstratu, App. M. 1, p. 112, 24 : monstratu Helenae, Aus. Per. Iliad. 3 .

monstrĭfer.opening: adj. monstrum-fero , monster-bearing, that produces monsters ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): campi, Val. Fl. 5, 222 : novercae, i. e. Juno, who sent monsters to Hercules, id. ib. 5, 43 : sinus (i. e. mare), id. ib. 2,…

monstrĭfĭcābĭlis.opening: adj. monstrificus , monstrous, strange (ante-class.): mirum ac monstrificabile, Lucil. ap. Non. 138, 26 .

monstrĭfĭcus.opening: adj. monstrumfacio , monstrous, strange (post-Aug.): artes, i. e. magical, Val. Fl. 6, 152 : natura hyaenae, Plin. 28, 8, 27, § 92 : hominum ingenia, id. 21, 5, 13, § 26 : effigies, id. 2, 3, 3, § 7 ; and so the better…

monstrĭgĕna.opening: monstrumgigno , monster-bearing : monstrigenis fluctibus, Avien. Perieg. 799 .

monstrĭger.opening: adj. monstrum-gero , = monstrifer, II., Salv. Gub. Dei. 5, 8 .

monstro.opening: , (archaic mostro; v. Brix ad Plaut. Trin. 2, 2, 61 ), , v. a. like monstrum, from moneo , to show, point out, to indicate, intimate, inform, advise, teach, instruct, tell any thing (in class. prose very rare, and only…

monstrōsĭtas.opening: monstrosus, -uosus , unnaturalness, monstrosity , Aug. Civ. Dei , 7, 26.

monstrum.opening: moneo . Orig. belonging to relig. lang., a divine omen indicating misfortune, an evil omen, portent (syn.: ostentum, prodigium, portentum): quia ostendunt, portendunt, monstrant, praedicunt, ostenta, portenta, monstra,…

monstrŭōsus.opening: (post-class. ), , adj. monstrum , strange, preternatural, monstrous (class.): monstruosissima bestia, of the ape, Cic. Div. 2, 32, 69 : hominum partus monstrosi, Luc. 1, 557 : ferculum longe monstruosius, Petr. 69 :…

montānĭōsus.opening: adj. mons , for montanus, mountainous (post-class.): locus, Auct. Rei Agrar. p. 239 Goes.; Gromat. Vet. p. 331, 20.

montānus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to a mountain, mountain-; full of mountains, mountainous (class.): locus montanus an planus, Quint. 5, 10, 37 : ager, Varr. R. R. 1, 6 : flumen, Verg. A. 2, 305 : cacumina, i. e. montium, Ov.…

Montānus.opening: a Roman surname . Curtius Montanus, a favorite of the emperor Tiberius , Tac. A. 16, 28 sq. ; id. H. 4, 42 ; Ov. P. 4, 16, 11 ; Juv. 4, 107 ; 131 . — Votienus Montanus, an orator of the reign of Tiberius , Tac. A. 4, 42…

montensis.opening: adj. mons , for montanus, of or belonging to mountains, mountain- : DII, Inscr. Grut. 21, 3 .

montĭcellus.opening: dim. id. , a small mountain, a mount (post-class.), Auct. Rei Agrar. p. 231 Goes. (Gromat. Vet. 306 sq.).

montĭcŏla.opening: mons-colo , a dweller in the mountains, a mountaineer ( poet. ): monticolae Silvani, Ov. M. 1, 193 .

montĭcŭlus.opening: dim. mons , a small mountain : monticulus, ὄριον, βουνός , Gloss. Philox. Donat. Art. Gram. 2, 2, 3 .

montĭfer.opening: adj. monsfero , mountain-bearing : montiferum Titana (al. monstriferum), Sen. Herc. Oet. 1212 .

montĭgĕna.opening: mons-gigno , mountain-born : montigena, ὀρεσιγενής , Gloss. Philox. Anthol. Lat. 1, 53, 1 .

Montīnus.opening: mons , a mountaingod, god of the Mountains , Arn. 4, 132 .

montĭ-văgus.opening: adj. mons-vagus , mountain-roaming, that wanders over mountains (mostly poet. ): Diana, Stat. Ach. 1, 450 : fera, Lucr. 1, 404 : genus ferarum, id. 2, 597 ; 1081 : ac silvestres cursus lustrationesque, Cic. Tusc. 5, 27,…

montŭōsus.opening: or , , adj. mons , mountainous, full of mountains (class.): regio, Cic. Planc. 9, 22 : cum locis ipsis delectemur, montuosis etiam, id. Lael. 19, 68 : loci, id. Part. 10, 36 : frutex, Plin. 12, 13, 28, § 48 .—Form…

mŏnŭbĭlis.opening: adj. moneo , reminding, admonishing (post-class.): columnae, that serve as remembrancers, Sid. Ep. 2, 2 .

mŏnŭmentālis.opening: adj. [monumentum, of or belonging to a monument, monumental (late Lat.): lapis, Auct. de Limit. p. 305 Goes.

mŏnŭmentārĭus.opening: ( ), , adj. id. , of or belonging to a monument or tomb (post-class.): ceraula, who played at tombs, App. Flor. p. 342, 22 .

mŏnŭmentum.opening: ( ), , [moneo), that which preserves the remembrance of any thing, a memorial, a monument; esp. of buildings, statues, galleries, tombs erected to perpetuate the remembrance of a person or thing; cf. Paul. ex Fest. p.…

Monustē.opening: one of the Danaides, who killed her husband Eurysthenes , Hyg. Fab. 170 .

Mōnўchus.opening: , = Μώνυχος , the name of a Centaur , Luc. 6, 388 ; Ov. M. 12, 499 ; Juv. 1, 11 .

Mopsĭāni.opening: or , , , the adherents of Mopsus, in the city of Compsa, during the second Punic war , Liv. 23, 1, 2 ; 3 .

Mopsĭum.opening: , = Μόψιον , a hill in Thessaly, between Tempe and Larissa , Liv. 42, 61 .

Mopsŏpĭus.opening: adj. , = Μοψόπιος , of or belonging to Mopsopia ( Μοψοπία , an old name of Attica), Mopsopian, Attic, Athenian (only poet. ): Mopsopius juvenis, i. e. Triptolemus, Ov. M. 5, 661 : muri, i. e. of Athens, id. ib. 6, 423 :…

Mopsūcrēnae.opening: plur. , = Μόψου κρῆναι (Mopsus-springs), a city in Cappadocia , now Mezanluk Khan , Amm. 21, 15, 2 .

Mopsuhestĭa.opening: or , , , = Μόψου ἑστία (Mopsus-hearth), a city in Cilicia, on the river Pyramus, near the sea, also called Mopsos; now Missis , Cic. Fam. 3, 8, 10 ; Amm. 14, 8, 3 .

Mopsus.opening: , = Μόψος . A soothsayer in Argos , Cic. N. D. 2, 3, 7 ; id. Div. 1, 40, 88 ; id. Leg. 2, 13, 33 .— A soothsayer in Thessaly , Ov. M. 12, 456 ; Hyg. Fab. 14 ; 128 ; 173 .— Another soothsayer, the son of Manto , Val. Fl.…

mŏra.opening: , = μόρα , a division of the Spartan army, consisting of three, five , or seven hundred men : moram Lacedaemoniorum intercepit, the Spartan army, Nep. Iphicr. 2, 3 (but in Cic. Tusc. 2, 16, 37 , the best reading is…

moracillum.opening: dim. from moracius, Titin. ap. Paul. ex Fest. p. 139 Müll.

moracĭus.opening: adj. mora , hard : nuces, Titin. ap. Paul. ex Fest. p. 139 Müll.

mōrālis.opening: adj. mores , of or belonging to manners or morals, moral (a word formed by Cicero; cf. moratus): quia pertinet ad mores, quos ἤθη Graeci vocant, nos eam partem philosophiae de moribus appellare solemus. Sed decet…

mōrālĭtas.opening: moralis , manner, characteristics, character (post-class.), Macr. S. 5, 1 ; morality , Ambros. in Psa. 118 , Serm. 3.

mŏrāmentum.opening: moror , that which causes a delay, a hinderance (postclass.), App. Flor. p. 363, 32 .

mŏrārĭa.opening: a plant, called also statioron or chamaeleon, App. Herb. 25 .

mŏrātim.opening: adv. , moror , slowly , Sol. 3, 1 dub. (al. memoratim).

mŏrātĭo.opening: id. , a delaying, tarrying, a delay , Vitr. 9, 4 : morationibus impediri, id. ib. : litoraria, delay on the coast, Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 5, 74 .

mŏrātor.opening: id. . A delayer, loiterer, malingerer : unus publici commodi, Liv. 2, 44 ; Curt. 4, 10, 10 (but moratorum, Liv. 21, 47, 3 , and 24, 41, 5, is from morati; v. moror).— A talker against time , a sort of advocate who spoke…

mŏrātōrĭus.opening: , a. , adj. morator , delaying, dilatory (post-class.): cunctatio, Dig. 26, 7, 6 : appellationes, Paul. Sent. 5, 35, 2 : ambages, Cod. Just. 4, 31, 14 .

mōrātus.opening: adj. mos . Mannered, of morals , good or bad; constituted, conditioned, circumstanced (class.): nequiquam mulier exornata est bene, si morata est male, Plaut. Most. 1, 3, 132 : condigne pater est ejus moratus moribus,…

mŏrax.opening: adj. moror , fond of delay, dilatory : cogitationes, Varr. ap. Non. 451, 13 .

morbĭdus.opening: adj. morbus . Sickly, diseased (rare and only ante-class. and post-Aug.; syn. aeger, aegrotus): apes morbidae, Varr. R. R. 3, 16, 22 : corpus, Plin. 8, 26, 40, § 96 .— Sickly, unwholesome : vis, Lucr. 6, 1225 : aër, id.…

morbĭfer.opening: or , , adj. morbus-fero , that brings disease (postclass.): labes, Paul. Nol. Carm. 25, 238 .

morbĭfĭco.opening: v. n. morbus-facio , to produce disease (late Lat.), Cael. Aur. Salut. Praec. 19 .

morbōsĭtas.opening: morbosus , sickliness, unhealthiness (post-class.): si provincia, quam colimus, de morbositate suspecta est, Pall. 1, 16 (al. morbis aestate).

morbōsus.opening: adj. morbus , sickly, ailing, diseased . In gen. (only anteand post-class.): morbosum hominem morbo aliquo affectum, Paul. ex Fest. p. 139 Müll.: servus, Cato, R. R. 2 : pecus, Varr. R. R. 2, 1, 21 : equus, Labeo ap.…

Morbōvĭa.opening: (or ), , morbus , the land of disease, sickdom , vulg. in execrations: abire Morboviam jusserat, go to the devil, Suet. Vesp. 14 .

morbus.opening: Sanscr. mar-, die; Gr. βροτός (for μροτός), μαραίνω; cf. morior, marceo , a sickness, disease, disorder, distemper, ailment, illness, malady , of body or mind (class.). Corporeal: morbum appellant totius corporis…

mordācĭtas.opening: mordax , the power of biting or stinging, mordacity (post-Aug.): urticarum foliis inest aculeata mordacitas, Plin. 21, 15, 54, § 91 : vinosa, sharp, like sour wine, id. 21, 18, 72, § 120 .— Transf. , snappishness,…

mordax.opening: adj. mordeo , biting, given to biting, snappish ( poet. and in postAug. prose). Lit. : canis, Plaut. Bacch. 5, 2, 27 : equus, Labeo ap. Gell. 4, 2 : asinus, App. M. 8, p. 213 init. : Memmius, Auct. ap. Cic. de Or. 2,…

mordĕo.opening: (archaic memordi; v. in the foll. ), , v. a. root smard-; Sanscr. mard-, bite; Gr. σμερδνός, σμερδαλέος; (cf. Engl. smart) , to bite, to bite into (class.). Lit. : si me canis memorderit, Enn. ap. Gell. 7, 9, 3 (Sat. v.…

mordex.opening: adj. mordeo , biting, gnawing : asini mordices, v. l., Plaut. Aul. 2, 3, 57 (better mordicus).—As subst. : , , , the biter , i. e. tooth , v. l. ap. App. M. 3, p. 140 (better mordicus, q. v.).

mordĭcātĭo.opening: mordico , a griping (post-class.): ventris mordicatio, Cael. Aur. Acut. 3, 20, 161 ; 2, 18, 105 .

mordĭcātīvus.opening: adj. id. , biting, sharp : acetum, Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 8, 144 .

mordĭcĭtus.opening: adv. a lengthened form for 1. mordicus , with the teeth (ante- and post-class.): asini me mordicitus scindant, Plaut. Aul. 2, 2, 57 dub. (al. mordicibus, from obsol. mordex, a bite; al. mordicus; Non. 139, 30 , has…

mordĭco.opening: v. a. mordax , to bite, sting : est acerrimae atque mordicantis qualitatis, biting, sharp, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 8, 34 .

mordĭcus.opening: adj. id. , biting, snappish : quem equi mordici distraxerunt (al. mordicus, al. mordicibus), Hyg. Fab. 273 .

mordōsus.opening: adj. id. , biting, given to biting : mordosus, δηκτικός , Gloss. Gr. Lat.

mŏrētārĭus.opening: adj. moretum , of or belonging to the dish moretum (postclass.): moretaria condimenta, Apic. 6, 4 . — Subst. : , , , the dish moretum (made of garlic, rue, vinegar, oil, etc.), Don. ad Ter. Phorm. 2, 2, 4 .

mŏrētum.opening: from same root with mordeo, q. v. . A country dish composed of garlic, rue, vinegar, oil , etc., Ov. F. 4, 367 .— , , , the title of a small poem ascribed to Virgil; v. Heyne and Sillig in Verg. Carm. vol. iv. p. 301…

Morgētes.opening: , = Μόργητες , a people who anciently dwelt in Lucania , Plin. 3, 5, 10, § 71 .

mŏrĭbundus.opening: adj. morior . Dying (class.): minus valet, moribundus est, Plaut. Bacch. 2, 2, 15 : jacentem moribundumque vidistis, Cic. Sest. 39, 85 : moribundus procubuit, Liv. 26, 15 : anima, Ov. Tr. 4, 5, 3 .— Transf. : vox, Stat.…

mōrĭgĕrātĭo.opening: morigeror , compliance (ante-class.), Afran. ap. Non. 2, 6 (Com. Rel. v. 381 Rib.).

mōrĭgĕror.opening: v. dep. morigerus , to comply with, gratify, humor, endeavor to please (syn.: obsequor, obtempero; class.): nunc si servitus evenit, ei vos morigerari mos bonus est, to accommodate yourself to it, Plaut. Capt. 2, 1, 4 :…

mōrĭgĕrus.opening: adj. mos-gero , complying, obsequious, obedient (ante- and post-class.): meo me aequom est morigerum patri, Plaut. Am. 3, 4, 21 : male morigerus mihi est danista, id. Ep. 5, 1, 1 : quando una vivis meis morigera…

Morimărūsa.opening: (Dead Sea), the Cimbric appellation of the North Sea , Plin. 4, 13, 27, § 95 .

Mŏrĭni.opening: a people of Belgic Gaul, near the channel , Caes. B. G. 2, 4 ; 3, 9 ; 4, 22 ; Mel. 3, 2 fin. ; Plin. 4, 17, 31, § 106 : extremique hominum Morini, Verg. A. 8, 727 .

mōrĭo.opening: , = μωρός , an arrant fool (post-Aug.): quidam tantae sunt fatuitatis, ut non multum a pecoribus differant: quos moriones vulgo vocant, Aug. Ep. 26 ; Plin. Ep. 9, 17, 1 sq. ; Mart. 8, 13 ; 14, 210 in lemm. — Transf. , a…

mōrĭon.opening: , = μώριον . A narcotic plant, nightshade, also called strychnus: alterum genus (strychni), quod halicacabon vocant ... ab aliis morion, ab aliis moly appellatum, Plin. 21, 31, 105, § 180 .— — The male mandrake : album…

mŏrĭor.opening: ( fut. part. moriturus, a, um, Cic. Arch. 12, 30 ; id. Div. 2, 25, 54 ; 2, 47, 99 ; Liv. 21, 12, 4 ; Verg. A. 4, 308 ; id. ib. 2, 511 et saep.; old forms acc. to the fourth conj.: si vivimu' sive morīmur, Enn. ap.…

Moritasgus.opening: A god of the Senones , Inscr. Orell. 2028 .— A male proper name among the Senones , Caes. B. G. 5, 54, 2 .

mŏrĭtŭrĭo.opening: v. n. desid . [morior], to desire to die , Cic. ap. Aug. de Gramm. p. 2006 P.

mormorion.opening: a kind of darkbrown rock crystal , Plin. 37, 10, 63, § 173 .

mormyr.opening: , = μορμύρος , a sort of fish in Pontus : pictae mormyres, Ov. Hal. 110 ; cf. Plin. 32, 11, 54, § 152 .

mŏrŏchītes.opening: ( ), , , a precious stone of the color of a leek , Plin. 37, 10, 63, § 173 .

mōrŏlŏgus.opening: adj. , = μωρολόγος , speaking foolishly, foolish (Plautinian): sermones, Plaut. Ps. 5, 1, 20 .—As subst., a fool : tibi morologus fio, Plaut. Pers. 1, 1, 50 .

mŏror.opening: v. dep. n. and a. [mora]. Neutr., to delay, tarry, stay, wait, remain, linger, loiter (syn.: cesso, cunctor, haesito; class.); eamus ergo ad cenam: quid stas? Thr. Ubi vis: non moror, i. e. I have no objection, Ter.…

mōror.opening: v. dep. n. [ μωρός ], to be foolish, be a fool (post-Aug.), in the lusus verbb.: morari eum (Claudium) inter homines desiisse, productā primā syllabā, jocabatur, Suet. Ner. 33 .

mōrōsĭtas.opening: morosus . Peevishness, fretfulness, moroseness (rare but class.): si in morositatem inutilem et odiosam incidamus, Cic. Off. 1, 25, 88 : morositas et ea vitia, quae dixi, habent aliquid excusationis, id. Sen. 18, 65 .—…

mōrōsus.opening: adj. mos; cf. Cic. Tusc. 4, 24, 54 , peevish, fretful, wayward, capricious, captious, morose (syn.: tristis, severus, gravis, difficilis; class.): usque eo difficiles ac morosi sumus, ut nobis non satisfaciat ipse…

mŏrōsus.opening: adj. mora , lingering, slow, slow in coming (lato Lat.): cui morosum videtur quodcunque futurum est, Cassiod. in Psa. 34, 20 : iter fieri morosum quod ad celeritatem est inventum, id. Var. 1, 29 .

Morpheus.opening: , = Μορφεύς , the son of Sleep and god of dreams : excitat Morphea, Ov. M. 11, 634 ; 647 .

morphnos.opening: , = μορφνός , a kind of eagle that lives near lakes , Plin. 10, 3, 3, § 7 .

Morrenas.opening: adj. comm., of or belonging to Morrena or Morena (a country of Mysia), Inscr. Grut. 760, 4 .

mors.opening: root mor, v. morior ( dat. morte, Varr. ap. Gell. 24 ), death in every form, natural or violent (syn.: letum, nex). Lit. : omnium rerum mors est extremum, Cic. Fam. 6, 21, 1 : mors ultima linea rerum est, Hor. Ep. 1,…

morsĭcātim.opening: adv. morsico , by biting, by biting the lips together (ante-class.): labellis morsicatim lusitant, Naev. ap. Non. 139, 25 .

morsĭcātĭo.opening: id. , a biting : ciborum, Paul. ex Fest. p. 143, 1 Müll. (al. morsitatio).

morsĭco.opening: v. a. mordeo . To bite continually , Paul. ex Fest. p. 68 Müll.— To bite, to press the lips together as in kissing (post-class.): ore improbo compulsat, et morsicat, App. M. 7, p. 197, 16 : limis et morsicantibus…

morsĭuncŭla.opening: dim. 2. morsus , a little bite; a biting with the lips, a kissing (ante- and post - class.): formicarum, App. M. 8, p. 211, 35 : teneris labellis molles morsiunculae, kisses, Plaut. Ps. 1, 1, 65 .

morsum.opening: mordeo , a bit, little piece , e. g. of wool ( poet. ): lanea morsa, Cat. 64, 316 .

morsus.opening: mordeo , a biting, a bite. Lit. : contra avium minorum morsus munitur vallo aristarum. Cic. Sen. 15, 51 : serpentis, id. Fat. 16, 36 : morsu apprehendere, to bite, Plin. 11, 24, 28, § 84 : morsibus insequi, Ov. M. 13,…

Morta.opening: , = Μορτή , one of the Fates , Liv. Andron. ap. Gell. 3, 16, 11 : tria sunt nomina Parcarum, Nona, Decima, Morta, Caesell. ib.

mortālis.opening: adj. mors , subject to death, liable to die, mortal (class.). Lit. : quid in iis mortale et caducum, quid divinum aeternumque sit, Cic. Leg. 1, 23, 61 : animal, id. N. D. 3, 13, 32 .— Transf. Human, mortal : mucro, of…

mortālĭtas.opening: mortalis , the state of being subject to death, mortality; a dying, death . Lit. (rare but class.): omne, quod ortum sit, mortalitas consequitur, * Cic. N. D. 1, 10, 26 : metu meae mortalitatis, Quint. 6 praef. § 2 :…

mortārĭŏlum.opening: dim. mortarium , a small mortar , Aem. Mac. 1, 8 ; Hier. Ep. 64, 9 ; Vulg. Num. 7, 14 .

mortārĭum.opening: a mortar (mostly ante-class. and post-Aug.). Lit. : mortarium, in quo teruntur quae solvenda sunt, Non. 543, 22 ; Plaut. Aul. 1, 2, 17 ; Cato, R. R. 74 : aerea, Plin. 33, 8, 41, § 123 : plumbea, id. 34, 18, 50, § 168 .—…

mortĭcīnus.opening: adj. mors , dead, that has died , only of animals; hence, of or belonging to an animal that has died of itself, carrion-; as a term of abuse, carrion; and transf., dead (ante-class. and postAug.). Lit. : morticinae ovis…

mortĭfer.opening: (rarely) , , adj. mors-fero , death-bringing, death-dealing, deadly, fatal (class.; syn.: lethalis, funestus): poculum, Cic. Tusc. 1, 29, 71 : morbus, id. Div. 1, 30, 63 : vulnus, id. Leg. 2, 5, 13 : bellum, Verg. A. 6,…

mortĭfĭcātĭo.opening: mortifico , a killing, death (eccl. Lat.), opp. vivificatio, Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 9 .

mortĭfĭco.opening: v. a. mortificus , to kill, destroy (eccl. Lat.): caro mortificatur, Tert. Res. Carn. 37 .— Transf. , to mortify, subject, reduce to weakness : membra, Vulg. Col. 3, 5 : facta carnis, id. Rom. 8, 13 ; cf. id. ib. 7, 4 .

mortĭfĭcus.opening: adj. mors - facio , deadly, fatal (eccl. Lat.): cibus, Tert. Carm. adv. Marc. 4, 5 : mortifico vulnere ictus, v. l. ap. Val. Max. 5, 6, 1 (Halm).

mortĭgĕna.opening: mors-gen-, gigno , the producer of death, death-giver , Inscr. Grut. p. 1163 .

mortŭālĭa.opening: mortuus . (Sc. vestimenta.) Grave - clothes or mourningweeds (ante - class.), Naev. ap. Non. 548, 28 (Trag. Rel. v. 48 Rib.).— (Sc. carmina.) Haec sunt non nugae; non enim mortualia, funeral songs, dirges , referring to…

mortŭārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to the dead (ante-class.): mortuaria glossaria, vocabularies of the dead , a term applied by Cato to the philosophers who talk of dead, and not of existing, things, Gell. 18, 7, 3 .

mortŭōsus.opening: adj. id. , death-like, deadly (post-class.): vultus, Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 3, 38 .— Deadly , Cael. Aur. Acut. 1, 10, 71 .

mortŭrĭo.opening: v. n. desid. [mors], to long for death, desire to die : dictum est a Cicerone de philosophis, morturiunt, mori desiderant, Aug. de Gram. p: 2006 P. ( Cic. Fragm. 50, 29, p. 146 B. and K.).

mŏrŭla.opening: dim. mora , a brief delay (post-class.): tempus nullā morulā extenditur, Aug. Conf. 11, 15 ; App. Fragm. M. 10, p. 71 .

mōrŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [2. morus], black, dark-colored (ante-class): jam pol ego illam pugnis totam faciam ut sit morula, Plaut. Poen. 5, 5, 10 .

mōrum.opening: , = μῶρον and μόρον , a mulberry; a blackberry : nigra mora, Hor. S. 2, 4, 22 ; cf. Plin. 15, 24, 27, § 96 : in duris haerentia mora rubetis, Ov. M. 1, 105 ; cf. Plin. 24, 13, 73, § 117 .

mōrus.opening: , = μῶρα or μορέα , a mulberry-tree : arbor ibi, niveis uberrima pomis, Ardua morus erat, Ov. M. 4, 89 ; cf. Plin. 16, 18, 30, § 74 .

Morvinnĭcus.opening: adj., of or belonging to Morvinnus (a town of the Ædui), Inscr. Giorn. Arcad. t. 28, p. 351.

mos.opening: etym. dub.; perh. root ma-, measure; cf.: maturus, matutinus; prop., a measuring or guiding rule of life; hence , manner, custom, way, usage, practice, fashion, wont , as determined not by the laws, but by men's will…

Mŏsa.opening: a river in Belgic Gaul , now the Meuse or Maas , Caes. B. G. 4, 9 fin. ; 4, 10 init. ; Plin. 4, 14, 28, § 100 ; Tac. A. 2, 6 ; id. H. 4, 28 ; 5, 23 .

Moschi.opening: a people between the Black and the Caspian Seas , Mela, 1, 2, 5; 3, 5, 4; Luc. 3, 270 ; Plin. 6, 4, 4, § 29 .— Hence, , , adj., Moschian , Plin. 5, 27, 27, § 99 ; Mela, 1, 19, 13.— , , adj., Moschian , Mela, 1, 19:…

Moschis.opening: a female proper name , Afran. ap. Non. 318, 5 ; Inscr. Mur. 477, 5.

Moschus.opening: A rhetorician of Pergamus, accused of poisoning , Hor. Ep. 1, 5, 9 .— A Roman surname , Inscr. Mur. 477, 5.

moscilli.opening: or , , dim. mos , little customs or usages : moscillis (al. mosculis) Cato pro parvis moribus dixit, Paul. ex Fest. pp. 158 and 159 Müll.

Mŏsella.opening: and , a river of Belgic Gaul , now the Moselle , Tac. A. 13, 53 ; id. H. 4, 71 ; 77 : largus Mosella, Aus. de Clar. Urb. 4 : placida Mosella, id. Idyll. 10, 73 .—Also called , , , Flor. 3, 10, 14 .—Hence, , , adj., of…

Mōses.opening: or , , (in Vulg. nom. semper Mo︤︥yses; gen. Mo︤︥ysi, Lev. 8, 36; 16, 34; Num. 3, 1; 33, 1, etc.: Mosi, Sedul. 5, 274 ), = Μωσῆς, Μωυσῆς , Moses : Moses, Juv. 14, 102 : Moyses, Tac. H. 5, 4 : Moysen unum exsulum…

Mostellārĭa.opening: mostellum, dim. from monstrum , The Ghost , the name of a comedy of Plautus, also called Phasma ( φάσμα , ghost).

Mostēni.opening: the inhabitants of Mostena or Mostene, a city of Lydia , Tac. A. 2, 47 .

mōtābĭlis.opening: adj. moto , moving, that moves : anima, Vulg. Gen. 1, 21 .

mōtăcilla.opening: the white water-wagtail : motacilla, quod semper movet caudam, Varr. L. L. 5, § 76 Müll.; Plin. 37, 10, 56, § 156 ; Arn. 7, 223 .

mōtātĭo.opening: moto , frequent motion, motion (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Anim. 45 .

mōtātor.opening: id. , a mover (postclass.), Tert. Anim. 12 : motator sali Neptunus, Arn. 3, 118 .

mōtĭo.opening: moveo , a moving, motion; a removing (class.). Lit. : principium motionis, Cic. Fat. 19, 43 : corporum, id. N. D. 2, 58, 145 : ab ordine motio, a removing, Dig. 47, 20, 3 .—Abstr., motion : ipsum animum ... quasi…

mōtĭto.opening: v. freq. a. moto , to move often, move about (post - class.), Gell. 9, 6, 3 dub.

mōtĭuncŭla.opening: dim. motio , a slight motion, shaking; in medicine, an attack of fever (post-Aug.), Sen. Ep. 53, 6 : tentatus in Campaniā motiunculis levibus, Suet. Vesp. 24 init.

mōto.opening: v. freq. a. moveo , to keep moving, move about ( poet. ): Zephyris motantibus, Verg. E. 5, 5 ; cacumina quercūs, id. ib. 6, 28 : lacertos, Ov. M. 11, 674 .— Pass. : fundamenta parietesque quati et motari videntur, Jul.…

mōtor.opening: id. , a mover, that which keeps a thing in motion ( poet. ): cunarum fueras motor, Charideme, mearum, i. e. hast rocked me, Mart. 11, 39, 1 .

mōtōrĭus.opening: adj. motor , moving, that has motion (post-class.). Adj. : modus agendi, a stirring, bustling, noisy style of playing (opp. statarius), Don. Ter. Ad. prol. 24 ; id. ad argum. And.; Prisc. p. 590 P.— Subst. : , , , the…

mōtus.opening: moveo , a moving, motion (freq. and class.). Lit. In gen.: orbes, qui versantur contrario motu, Cic. Rep. 6, 17, 17 : deus motum dedit caelo, id. Univ. 6 : natura omnia ciens et agitans motibus et mutationibus suis, id.…

mŏvens.opening: Part. and P. a. , v. moveo fin. A.

mŏvĕo.opening: ( sync. , mōstis for movistis, Mart. 3, 67, 1 ; mōrunt for moverunt, Sil. 14, 141 ), v. a. and n. Sanscr. mīv, set in motion; Gr. ἀμείβω, change; cf.: momentum, mutare . Act., to move, stir, set in motion; to shake,…

mox.opening: adv. etym. dub.; cf. Sanscr. mankshu, ready, soon , soon, anon, directly, presently; mostly of the future (class.). Lit. In gen.: mox ivero, Plaut. Capt. 1, 2, 91 : mox ego huc revertor, Ter. And. 3, 2, 4 : jussit mihi…

Mŏysītĭcus.opening: adj. Moyses , of or belonging to Moses (post-class.), Venant. Vit. S. Mart. 2, 28 .

mu.opening: interj. , = μῦ , a slight sound made with the closed lips (ante-class.): neque, ut aiunt, mu facere audent, to mutter, make a muttering , Enn. ap. Varr. L. L. 7, § 101 Müll. ( Enn. p. 175 , n. 10 Vahl.): nec mu facere…

mūcēdo.opening: ( ), , mucus , mucus of the nose (post-class.), App. Mag. p. 306 dub. (Hildebr. dulcedo).

mūcĕo.opening: v. n. id. , to be mouldy, musty (ante-class.): vinum quod neque aceat, neque muceat, Cato, R. R. 148 .

mūcesco.opening: v. inch. n. [muceo], to become mouldy or musty (post-Aug.): proprium est vino mucescere, Plin. 14, 20, 26, § 131 .

muchula.opening: the Persian name of the precious stone telicardios, Plin. 37, 10, 68, § 183 .

mūcĭdus.opening: ( ), , adj. mucus . Mouldy, musty : mucida panis frusta, Juv. 14, 128 : vina, Mart. 8, 6, 4 .— Snivelling : homo es, Qui me emunxisti mucidum, Plaut. Epid. 3, 4, 58 : senex, id. Mil. 3, 1, 52 .

mūcĭlāgo.opening: ( ), , muceo , a mouldy, musty juice , Theod. Prisc. 4, 1 .

Mūcĭus.opening: ( , Lact. 5, 13, 13 ), the name of a Roman gens. The most celebrated are, C. Mucius Scaevola, who altempted to assassinate Porsena, and, on being apprehended, burned off his right hand , Liv. 2, 12 ; Cic. Sest. 21, 48 ;…

mūcor.opening: muceo . Mould, mouldiness , in bread (post-Aug.): mucorem contrahere, to become mouldy, Col. 12, 4, 4 .— Mustiness , in wine, vinegar, etc.: mucor (vini), Dig. 18, 6, 4 .—Also, a moisture which flows from vines, and is…

mūcōsus.opening: ( ), , adj. mucus , slimy, mucous (post-Aug.): cruenta et mucosa ventris proluvies, Col. 1, 7, 1 ; 6, 7, 1 ; Paul. ex Fest. p. 158 Müll.: exulceratio, Cels. 5, 28, 15 .— Transf. , = stultus (opp. emunctae naris), Acron.…

mucro.opening: a sharp point or edge; esp., the point of a sword, the sword's point (class.; cf.: acies, cuspis). Lit. : mucro falcis, Col. 4, 25, 1 : dentis, Plin. 8, 3, 4, § 8 : folii, id. 16, 10, 16, § 38 : crystalli, id. 37 , 2,…

mūcrōnātus.opening: adj. mucro , pointed (post-Aug.): piscis mucronato rostro, Plin. 32, 2, 6, § 15 : folia, id. 25, 13, 102, § 161 .

mūcŭlentus.opening: ( ), , adj. mucus , snivelling (post-class.): nares, Prud. στεφ . 13, 282: munctiones, Arn. 3, 107 .

mūcus.opening: ( ), , mug, mungo; cf. also Sanscr. muć, solvere, dimittere , snivel, mucus of the nose: mucusque, et mala pituita nasi, Cat. 23, 17 ; Cels. 4, 18 .

mufrius.opening: a term of abuse : mufrius non magister, Petr. 58 fin.

muger.grammar: dici solet a Castrensium hominibus, quasi mucosus, is, qui talis male ludit
muger.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 158, 27 Müll. (cf. Engl. smuggle; Germ. Schmuggel), a false player.

mūgil.opening: and , , , a sea-fish; acc. to some, the mullet : mugilum natura ridetur, in metu capite abscondito, totos se occultari credentium, Plin. 9, 17, 26, § 59 ; 9, 42, 67, § 144 ; 9, 62, 88, § 185 ; 10, 70, 89, § 193; 32, 11,…

Mugillānus.opening: a Roman surname; as, e. g. Papirius Mugillanus, Liv. 4, 30 .

mūgĭnor.opening: v. dep. , to dally, trifle, hesitate, delay (rare but class.): muginari est nugari et quasi tarde conari, Paul. ex Fest. p. 147 Müll.: muginamur, Lucil. ap. Non. 139, 6 ; Att. ib. 139, 7 : dum tu muginaris, cepi…

mūgĭo.grammar: īvi and ĭi, ītum, 4 v. n.
mūgĭo.opening: v. n. Sanscr. root, muǵ, sonare; Gr. μυκάομαι, μύζω , to low, bellow (syn. boo). Lit. : inde cum actae boves mugissent, Liv. 1, 7 . —Prov.: hic bove percusso mugire Agamemnona credit, Juv. 14, 286 .— Part. pres. subst.…

Mūgĭōnĭa.opening: or , , or ( ), , (porta), a gate of ancient Rome, which was afterwards within the city : in Palatio Mucionis a mugitu, Varr. L. L. 5, § 164 Müll.: Mugionia porta Romae dicta est a Mugio quodam. Paul. ex Fest. p. 144…

mūgītor.opening: 1. mugio , a bellower ( poet. ): mugitor Vesuvius, Val. Fl. 3, 208 .

mūgītus.opening: id. , a lowing, bellowing (class.). Lit. : mugitusque boum, Verg. G. 2, 470 : edere, to utter lowings, to low, Ov. M. 7, 597 : dare, id. F. 1, 560 : tollere, Verg. A. 2, 223 .— Transf. , a bellowing, rumbling, roaring,…

mūla.opening: ( abl. plur. mulabus: data et vehicula cum mulabus ac mulionibus, Capitol. Ver. 5 ; Tert. Uxor. 2, 8 ; Prisc. p. 733 P.), mulus , a she-mule; also, in gen., a mule (used instead of horses for drawing carriages or…

mūlāris.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to mules (post-Aug.): materies, the race of mules, Col. 6, 27, 1 : carpentum, Lampr. Heliog. 4, 4 .

mulc.opening: the Persian name for the precious stone thelycardios , Plin. 37, 10, 68, § 183 ; al. muchala.

mulcātor.opening: mulco , he who handles roughly , Isid. 10, 178 ; Placid. Gloss. p. 483 .

mulcēdo.opening: mulceo , pleasantness, agreeableness (post-class.): Veneris atque Musae, Gell. 19, 9, 7 ; Sid. Ep. 5, 17 .

mulcĕo.opening: (rarely mulctum), , v. a. Sanscr. root marc, take hold of; Gr. μάρπτω, μάρπτις; cf. mulco , to stroke; to touch or move lightly (syn. palpo; poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : manu mulcens barbam, Ov. F. 1, 259 :…

mulcētra.opening: a plant, called also heliotropium, App. Herb. 9 .

Mulcĭber.opening: ( gen. sync. Mulcebri, Cic. poet. Tusc. 2, 10, 23), mulceo; he who softens any thing; v. infra , a surname of Vulcan : Mulciber, Vulcanus, a molliendo scilicet ferro dictus: mulcere enim mollire, sive lenire est, Paul.…

mulco.opening: († , Inscr. Grut. 155, 1 ), āvi, ātum, 1 (mulcassitis, for mulcaveritis, Plaut. Mil. 2, 2, 8 ), v. a. Sanscr. root marc, take hold of; of. Gr. μάρπτω, perh. μορφή , to beat, cudgel; to maltreat, handle roughly, injure…

mulctra.opening: mulgeo , a milkingpail, milk-pail . Lit. : bis venit ad mulctram, Verg. E. 3, 30 : e mulctrā recens caseus, Col. 8, 17, 13 ; cf. mulctrum.— Transf. , the milk in a milk-pail , Col. 7, 8, 1 ; cf. mulctrum.

mulctrārĭum.opening: (coll. form, , , Serv. Verg. E. 3, 30 ), mulgeo , a milking-pail : nivea implebunt mulctraria vaccae, Verg. G. 3, 177 Wagn. N. cr. (Rib. mulctraria; al. multraria, al. mulgaria).

mulctrum.opening: id. , a milking-pail : illic injussae veniunt ad mulctra capellae, Hor. Epod. 16, 49 ; Val. Fl. 6, 145 ; Calp. Ecl. 3, 66 ; 4, 25 ; 5, 33 ; 9, 36; Prud. Cath. 3, 66 : mea, Nemes. Ecl. 2, 35 ; cf. mulctra.

mulctus.opening: (only in abl. sing. ) [id.], a milking (ante-class.), Varr. R. R. 2, 11, 2 .

mulgāre.opening: mulgeo , a milkingpail : tepidi mulgaria lactis, Valg. ap. Serv and Philarg. ad Verg. G. 3, 177 .

mulgĕo.grammar: si, sum or ctum, 2 v. a.
mulgĕo.opening: v. a. Sanscr marǵ, wipe or rub away; Gr. ἀ-μέλγω; Germ. melken; Engl. milk , to milk : oves, Verg. E. 3, 5 : capras, Plin. 10, 39, 56, § 115 .— Absol. : mulgent ad caseum faciendum, Varr. R. R. 2, 11, 4 .—Prov.: mulgere…

mūlicurĭus.opening: v. hibrid. from mulus-κουρεύς , a mule-clipper : mulicurius, ἡμιονόκουρος , Gloss. Philox.

mŭlĭĕbris.opening: adj. mulier , of or belonging to a woman, womanly, female, feminine . Adj. (class.): loci muliebres, ubi nascendi initia consistunt, Varr. L. L. 5, 3 : facinus, Plaut. Truc. 4, 3, 35 : comitatus, Cic. Mil. 10, 28 : vox,…

mŭlĭē^brĭtas.opening: muliebris , womanhood opp. to virginity (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Verg. Vel. 14 .

mŭlĭē^brōsus.opening: adj. mulier , fond of women (Plautin.): genus muliebrosum (al. mulierosum), Plaut. Poen. 5, 5, 24 .

mŭlĭer.opening: mollior, comp. of mollis, q. v. , a woman, a female , whether married or not. Lit. In gen., Plaut. Poen. 1, 2, 36 : mulieres omnes propter infirmitatem consilii, majores in tutorum potestate esse voluerunt, Cic. Mur.…

mŭlĭĕrārĭus.opening: adj. mulier , of or belonging to a woman (mostly postclass.). Adj. : manus, the band sent by Clodia , Cic Cael. 28, 66: voluptas, Auct. ap. Trebell. Trig. Tyrann. 6, 7.— Subst. : , , , a lover of women , Cat. 25, 5…

mŭlĭercŭla.opening: dim. id. , a little woman, mere woman, girl (class.), Lucr. 4, 1279 : qui illo susurro delectari se dicebat aquam ferentis mulierculae, a common working girl, Cic. Tusc. 5, 36, 103 ; 1, 16, 37 ; id. Lael. 13, 45 ; Serv.…

mŭlĭercūlārĭus.opening: muliercula , a lover of women (post-class.), Cod. Th. 3, 16, 1.

mŭlĭĕrĭtas.opening: mulier , womanhood , opp. to maidenhood (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Virg. Vel. 12 (al. muliebritas).

mŭlĭĕro.opening: v. a. id. , to make womanish, render effeminate (ante-class.): Varr. ap. Non. 140, 16 .

mŭlĭĕrōsĭtas.opening: mulierosus , a fondness for women , as a transl. of the Gr φιλογύνεια , Cic. Tusc. 4, 11, 25 .

mŭlĭĕrōsus.opening: adj. mulier , fond of women (class.): homo, Afran. ap. Non. 28, 25 ; Cic. Fat. 5, 10 ; v. l. Plaut. Poen. 5, 5, 24 (v. muliebrosus).

mūlīnus.opening: adj. mulus , of or belonging to a mule : ungula, Vitr. 8, 3 : nares, Plin. 30, 4, 11, § 31 : cor, i. e. stolidum, fatuum (al. Mutinensis), Juv. 16, 23 .

mūlĭo.opening: id. , a mule-keeper, a mule-driver, muleteer; a mule-dealer, mule-hirer (mostly ante-class. and postAug.). Lit. , Varr. L. L. 5, § 159 Müll.; Plaut. Most. 3, 2, 93 : mulionesque cum cassidibus, Caes. B. G. 7, 45 ; Suet.…

mūlĭōnĭcus.opening: or , , adj. 1. mulio , of or belonging to a muledriver (class.): mulioniam paenulam arripuit, Cic. Sest. 38, 82 Halm: tectus cuculione mulionico, Lampr. Heliog. 32, 9 .

mullĕŏlus.opening: adj. dim. [mulleus], reddish (eccl. Lat.): calceus, Tert. Pall. 4 fin.

mullĕus calcĕus.opening: absol. , , , mullus , a reddish or purplecolored shoe , worn only by the three highest magistrates (the consul, prætor, and curule Ædile): mulleos genus calceorum aiunt esse; quibus reges Albanorum primi, deinde…

mullo.opening: v. a. , to sew; v. mulleus.

mullŭlus.opening: dim. mullus , a little red mullet or barbel : barbatulos mullulos exceptans, Cic. Par. 5, 2, 38 dub. (Orell., mullos).

mullus.opening: a kind of fish highly esteemed, the red mullet, barbel , Varr. R. R. 3, 17 ; Plin. 9, 17, 30, § 64 : mulli barbati in piscinis, Cic. Att. 2, 1, 7 ; Juv. 5, 92 ; Sen. Ep. 95, 27 et saep.

mūlŏcĭsĭārĭus.opening: mulus- cisium , one who rides in a carriage drawn by mules : καρουχάριος , mulocisiarius, Gloss. Gr. Lat.

mūlŏmĕdĭcīna.opening: mulus-medicina , the art of curing the diseases of mules , Veg. Vet. praef. 1 and 2.

mūlomĕdĭcus.opening: mulus-medicus , a mule-doctor , Veg. Vet. praef. 1; Firm. Math. 8, 13; Edict. Diocl. 7, 20.

mulsĕus.opening: adj. mulsum, v. mulceo , sweetened with honey; sweet as honey (post-Aug.): mulsea aqua, honey-water, hydromel, Col. 8, 7, 4 ; Plin. 21, 19, 75, § 129 : liquor mulsei saporis, sweet as honey, Col. 12, 45, 3 .

mulsus.opening: Part. and P. a. , v. mulceo fin.

multangŭlus.opening: ( ), , adj. multus-angulus , having many angles, multangular , Lucr. 4, 654 : forma, Mart. Cap. 2, § 138 .

multănĭmis.opening: adj. multus-animus , having much spirit or courage, spirited, courageous , Inscr. Marin. Frat. Arv. p. 690.

multannus.opening: adj. multusannus , of many years, ancient : πολυχρόνιος , multannus, Gloss. Gr. Lat.

multātīcĭus.opening: ( ), or , , adj. 1. multa , of or belonging to fines, fine- : pecunia, fine-money, Liv. 10, 23, 13 : argentum, id. 30, 39, 8 ; 27, 6, 19 .

multātĭcus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to fines, fine- : QVAISTORES AIRE MOLTATICOD DEDERONT, Inscr. Maff. Mus. Ver. 469, 2 : AEDILES AERE MVLTATICO, Inscr. Donat. 263, 1 .

multātĭo.opening: ( ), , 2. multo , a penalty, amercement, fine in any thing (class.): misera est multatio bonorum, Cic. Rab. Perd. 5, 16 : multatio non nisi ovium boumque impendio dicebatur, Plin. 18, 3, 3, § 11 : AEDILIS MVLTATIO,…

multēsĭmus.opening: adj. multus , multesimal , i. e. very small, trifling : pars, Lucr. 6, 651 (also ap. Non. 136, 39 ).

multĭangŭlum.opening: multus-angulus , a polygon , = πολύγωνον , Boëth. de Arithm. 2, 24; cf. multangulus.

multĭbĭbus.opening: adj. multus-bibo , much-drinking (ante- and post-class.): lena, Plaut. Curc. 1, 1, 77 : anus, id. Cist. 1, 3, 1 : heros, Macr. S. 5, 21 .

multĭ-căvātus.opening: adj. multuscavatus , with many hollows or cavities, multicavous (ante-class.): favus, Varr. R. R. 3, 16, 24 .

multĭ-căvus.opening: adj. multuscavus , many-holed : pumex, Ov. M. 8, 561 .

multīcĭus.opening: or , , adj., soft, splendid, transparent , a term applied to garments ( poet. and post-class.). Adj. : dabis Aureliano tunicas multicias viriles decem (al. multilicias), Valerian. Aug. ap. Vop. Aurel. 12 : synthesis,…

multĭcŏla.opening: multus-colo , a many-worshipper, one who worships many , Fulg. adv. Arianos.

multĭcŏlor.opening: adj. multus-color , many-colored (post-Aug.). Adj. : hexecontalithos, Plin. 37, 10, 60, § 167 : Iris, App. de Mundo, p. 64, 18.— Subst. : , a many-colored garment , App. M. 11, p. 258, 20 .

multĭcŏlōrus.opening: adj. id. , manycolored (post-class.): sicuti multijuga dicimus, et multicolora et multiformia, Gell. 11, 16, 4 : prata, Prud. Cath. 3, 104 ; App. de Mundo, 16.

multĭcŏmus.opening: adj. multuscoma , having much hair ( poet. ); transf. of radiant light, abounding in rays : flammae, Paul. Nol. Carm. 26, 418 .

multĭ-cŭpĭdus.opening: adj. multuscupidus , much-desiring, that desires much or many things (ante-class.): juvenilitas, Varr. ap. Non. 123, 7 .

multĭ-făcĭo.opening: v. a. , for magnifacio, to make much of, to esteem or value highly (ante-class.): multifacere dicitur, sicut magnifacere, parvifacere. Cato: Neque fidem, neque jusjurandum, neque pudicitiam multifacit, Paul. ex Fest. p.…

multĭfārĭus.opening: adj. multus , manifold, various, multifarious (the adj. post-class.): militares coronae multifariae sunt, Gell. 5, 6, 1 .—Hence, adv. , in two forms. ( acc. form), on many sides, in many places (class.): multifariam…

multĭ-fer.opening: , féra, , adj. multusfero , bearing much, fruitful (post-Aug.): robora, Plin. 16, 8, 11, § 30 ; 19, 8, 41, § 138 .

multĭfĭdus.opening: adj. multus-findo , many-cleft , i. e. cleft or divided into many parts ( poet. and post-Aug.). Lit. : faces, Ov. M. 7, 259 ; 8, 644 : pedes, Plin. 11, 37, 45, § 128 : dens, i. e. a comb, Mart. 14, 25, 2 .— Transf. , of…

multĭflōrus.opening: adj. multus-flos , abounding in flowers , Isid. 17, 9, 11 .

multiflŭus.opening: adj. multus-fluo , flowing copiously , trop. of speech ( poet. ): verba, Juvenc. 1, 586 .

multĭ-fŏrābĭlis.opening: adj. multus-forabilis , many-holed, perforated with many holes (post-class.): tibiae, App. M. 10, p. 254, 40 ; Sid. Ep. 8, 9 .

multĭ-fŏrātĭlis.opening: adj. multus-foro , many - holed, perforated with many holes (post - class.): tibia, App. Flor. 3, p. 341 med. ; id. M. 10, 32 .

multĭ-fŏris.opening: adj. multus - foris , many-doored, having many entrances, openings , or holes (post - Aug.): specus, Plin. 8, 55, 81, § 218 .

multĭ-formis.opening: adj. multus-forma , many-shaped, multiform; various, diverse, manifold (class.): nuces, Col. 7, 9, 8 : qualitates, Cic. Ac. 1, 7, 26 : multiformes sumus, have a fickle character, Sen. Ep. 120, 23 : artes multiformes et…

multĭformĭtas.opening: id. , multiformity (eccl. Lat.), Aug. Ver. Relig. 21 .

multĭ-fŏrus.opening: adj. multus-foris , having many openings, pierced with many holes ( poet. ): non illos ... multifori delectat tibia buxi, Ov. M. 12, 158 ; Sen. Agam. 346 .

multifructus.opening: adj. multusfructus , = πολύκαρπος , abounding in fruit , Fulg. Myth. 3, 2 ; Mythogr. Lat. 2, 130.

multĭ-gĕnĕris.opening: adj. multus-genus , of many kinds (Plautin.): multis et multigeneribus opus est tibi Militibus, Plaut. Capt. 1, 2, 56 .— Absol. : unguenta multigenerum multa, for multorum generum, id. Stich. 2, 2, 59 .

multĭ-gĕnus.opening: or , , adj. multus-genus , of many kinds, various ( poet. and post-Aug.): multigenis variata figuris, Lucr. 2, 335 : multa haec et multigenera terrestrium volucrumque vita, Plin. 11, 1, 1, § 1 .

multĭ-grūmus.opening: adj. multusgrumus , much heaped up; of waters, greatly swollen (ante class.): fluctus, Naev. ap. Gell. 19, 7, 15 .

multĭ-jŭgus.opening: , and , (the latter form only in Cic. Ait. 14, 9 ), adj. multus - jugum , yoked many together (mostly post-Aug.). Lit. : multijugi equi, Liv. 28, 9, 15 : quadrigae multijugae, Gell. 19, 8, 11 .— Trop. , many, manifold,…

multĭ-laudus.opening: adj. multuslaus , much-praised : vir (al. aemulandus), Amm. 21, 10, 6 .

multĭlīcĭus.opening: adj. multus-licium , consisting of many threads : tunica, Valerian ap. Vop. 12 (al. multicia).

multĭ-lŏquax.opening: adj. multusloquax , that talks much, talkative, loquacious : multiloquaces mulieres (al. multumloquaces), Plaut. Aul. 2, 1, 5 .

multĭ-lŏquĭum.opening: multus-loquor , a much-speaking , Plaut. Merc. prol. 31 ; Ambros. de Job, 1, 6, 20; id. in Psa. 1, § 20 .

multĭ-lŏquus.opening: adj. id. , talkative, loquacious (Plautin.): coquus, Plaut. Ps. 3, 2, 5 : anus, id. Cist. 1, 3, 1 : erit tacitus, qui naturā fuerat multiloquus, Cael. Aur. Acut. 2, 2, 10 .

Multĭmammĭa.opening: multus-mamma , the many-breasted , an epithet of the Ephesian Diana, who was represented with many breasts: Dianam, Hier. Ep. ad Ephes. prooem.

multĭ-mĕter.opening: multus - metrum , many - metred, consisting of many feet or kinds of verse (post-class.): si poëmata illius metiaris, multimeter, argutus, artifex erat, Sid. Ep. 8, 11 .

multĭ-mŏdis.opening: adv. from multi' modis for multis modis , in many ways or modes, variously (very rare, and rejected by Madv. ad Cic. Fin. 2, 26, 82 ): hoc etsi multimodis reprehendi potest, Cic. Fin. 2, 26, 82 B. and K.; cf.: sive…

multĭ-mŏdus.opening: adj. multusmodus , manifold, various : coitio potestatum, App. de Dogm. Plat. p. 4 fin. : ambages, id. M. 10, p. 253 med. (but very dub. in Liv. 21, 3, 4 , where the correct read. seems to be multifariam; v. Fabri ad h.…

multĭ-nōdus.opening: , and , , adj. multus - nodus , having many knots (post-class.): multinodis voluminibus serpens coluber, App. M. 5, p. 166, 19 : flagellis multinodi genere, Prud. Cath. 7, 139 : anfractus, Mart. Cap. 4, § 423 (but in…

multĭ-nōmĭnis.opening: adj. multus-nomen , many-named (post-class.): dea, App. M. 11, p. 268, 6 .

multĭ-nūbentĭa.opening: multus-nubo , a marrying several persons, polygamy (eccl. Lat.): multinubentiae pronus, Tert. adv. Psych. 1 .

multĭ-nūbus.opening: adj. id. , married to several, polygamous (eccl. Lat.): Salomon, Hier. adv. Jovin. 1, 28 : uxor, id. Ep. 123, 10 .

multĭ-nummus.opening: ( ), , adj. multus-nummus , that costs much money, dear, expensive (ante-class.): asini, Varr. R. R. 3, 17, 6 : piscis, id. ap. Non. 3, 152 .

multĭ-partītus.opening: adj. multuspartitus , much divided, divided into many classes (post-Aug.): vita, Plin. 6, 19, 22, § 66 .

multĭpĕda.opening: multus-pes , a multipede , an insect, Plin. 22, 25, 58, § 122 ; 29, 6, 39, § 143 ; v. millepeda.— A measure a number of feet long, Gram. Vet. p. 190, 6.

multĭ-pēs.opening: adj. id. , many-footed, multipede (post-Aug.). Adj. , Plin. 11, 45, 102, § 249 .— Subst. : , , , a multipede, millipede , an insect: multipes vermis terrenus a multitudine pedum vocatus, Isid. Orig. 12, 5, 6 .

multĭ-plex.opening: adj. multus-* plica (multīplex, Lucr. 2, 163 ; 4, 208 ; plur. multiplica, Gell. 19, 7, 16 ), that has many folds (class.). Lit. : alvus est multiplex et tortuosa, Cic. N. D. 2, 54, 136 .— Transf. That has many windings…

multĭplĭcābĭlĭs.opening: adj. multiplico , manifold , a word formed by Cicero in translating a passage of Sophocles (Trach. 1046 sq.): tortu multiplicabili Draconem, Cic. poët. Tusc. 2, 9, 22 (Sophocles has only δράκοντα ).

multĭplĭcātĭo.opening: id. , a making manifold, increasing, multiplying (postAug.). In gen.: frugum, Col. 3, 2, 5 : quinariarum, Front. Aquaed. 34 : temporum, Sen. Ep. 12, 6 .— In partic., multiplication , Col. 5, 2, 1 ; Vitr. 9, 1 ; 10, 16 .

multĭplĭcātor.opening: id. , a multiplier (post-class.): herilium talentorum multiplicator, Paul. Nol. Ep. 44 .—As math. t. t., the multiplier , Boëth. de Music. 2, 27 al.

multĭplĭcĭtas.opening: multiplex , multiplicity, manifoldness : profunda et infinita (sc. memoriae), Aug. Conf. 10, 17 init. ; Boëth. de Music. 1, 4; id. de Arithm. 1, 23.

multĭplĭco.opening: v. a. multiplex , to multiply, increase, augment . In gen. (class.; syn.: augeo, amplifico, amplio): aes alienum. Caes. B. C. 3, 32 : auxiliis multiplicatis. Planc. ap. Cic. Fam. 10, 8, 4 : flumina collectis…

multĭ-plĭcus.opening: adj. id. , variously compounded (for the class. multiplex): quae multiplica ludens composuit (Laevius), Gell. 19, 7, 16 .

multĭ-pŏtens.opening: adj. multum-potens , very powerful, very mighty (Plautin.): frater Jovis, Plaut. Trin. 4, 1, 1 : Venus, id. Cas. 4, 4, 17 : pectus, id. Bacch. 4, 4, 9 ; v. Ritschl ad h. l.

multĭ-rādix.opening: adj. multus-radix , many - rooted, having many roots (postclass.): centaurea minor, App. Herb. 35 .

multĭ-rāmis.opening: adj. multus - ramus , many-branched (post-class.): thyrsus, App. Herb. 4 .

multĭ-scĭus.opening: adj. multumscius , knowing much, of great knowledge (Appul.): etsi minus prudentem, multiscium reddidit, App. M. 9, p. 223, 13 : Homerus, id. Mag. p. 294, 29 : sophista longe multiscius, id. Flor. 4, p. 360, 12 al.

multĭ-sŏnōrus.opening: adj. multumsonorus , loud-sounding ( poet. ): esseda, Claud. Epigr. 1, 18 .

multĭ-sŏnus.opening: adj. multus-sonus , loud-sounding ( poet. ): Atthis, Mart. 1, 53, 9 : sistrum, Stat. S. 3, 2, 103 .

multĭtūdo.opening: multus , a great number, multitude (class.; cf.: copia, vis, magnitudo). In gen.: nationes, quae numero hominum ac multitudine ipsā poterant in provincias nostras redundare, Cic. Prov. Cons. 12, 31 : navium, Nep. Hann.…

multĭ-văgus.opening: adj. multumvagus , that wanders about much (postAug.): avis, Plin. 10, 37, 52, § 109 : flexus lunae, id. 2, 10, 7, § 48 : gradus, Stat. Th. 6, 1 .

multĭ-vĭdus.opening: adj. multum-video , much-seeing (post-class.), Mart. Cap. 2, 27, § 109 Kopp.

multĭ-vĭra.opening: multus-vir , she that has had many husbands (post-class.): alia sacra coronat univira, alia multivira, Min. Fel. Oct. 24, 3 .

multĭ-vĭus.opening: adj. multus-via , having many ways, multivious (Appul.): circuitus, App. M. 9, p. 221, 34 : circumcursio, id. ib. p. 222 fin. (al. multijuga).

multĭ-vŏlus.opening: adj. multusvolo , wishing or longing for many ( poet. ): mulier, Cat. 68, 128 ; Vulg. Eccl. 9, 3 .

multĭ-vŏrantĭa.opening: multus-voro , gluttony (eccl. Lat.): multivorantiae pronus, Tert. adv. Psych. 1 .

multo.opening: (less correctly ), , v. a. 1. multa , to punish one with any thing; used mostly of judicial punishment (class.; cf.: punio, animadverto): accusatorem multā et poenā multavit, Cic. Balb. 18, 42 : vitia hominum atque…

multŏtĭens.opening: and , advv. , [multus]. many times, oftentimes, often (postclass.), Just. Nov 29 praef.

multus.opening: (old form ), , um; comp. plus; sup. plurimus (v. at the end of this art.), adj. etym. dub. , much, great, many , of things corporeal and incorporeal. Posit. In gen.: multi mortales, Cato ap. Gell. 10, 3, 17 : multi suam…

muscellārĭum.opening: mus , a mousetrap : muscellarium, viverrarium, γαλεάγρα , Gloss. Philox.

muscĭdus.opening: , um. adj. muscus , full of moss, mossy (post-class.): pumices, Sid. Ep. 8, 16 .

muscĭpŭlātor.opening: muscipula , a mouse-catcher; trop., a deceiver : muscipulator, deceptor, alterplex, Gloss. Isid.

muscŭla.opening: dim. musca , a little fly (eccl. Lat.): scyniphes musculae sunt brevissimae, Aug. Trin. 7, 3 ; Arn. 2, 74 .

muscŭlōsus.opening: adj. musculus . Muscular, fleshy (post-Aug.): cor naturā musculosum, Cels. 4, 1 : pectora, Col. 8, 2 . — , , a Roman surname , Inscr. Grut. 337 .

muscŭlus.opening: dim. mus , a little mouse . Lit. , Cic. Div. 2, 14, 33 ; Plin. 27, 7, 28, § 52 .— Transf. Of other creatures. A companion of the whale , Plin. 9, 62, 88, § 186 ; called musculus marinus, id. 11, 37, 62, § 165 .— A…

muscus.opening: Moss , Cato, R. R. 6 : musco circumlita saxa, Hor. Ep. 1, 10, 7 : mollis, Ov. M. 8, 562 .— Musk , Hier. in Jov. 2 , n. 8.

mūseiārĭus.opening: and , , , for musivarius, a worker in mosaic (post-class.): marmorarius, musaearius, albarius, Edit. Diocl. p. 19; Inscr. Grut. 586, 3 .

Mūsēus.opening: or , , adj. , = Μουσεῖος , of or belonging to the muses, poetical or musical ( poet. ): musaea mele, Lucr. 2, 412 : musaeo lepōre, id. 1, 934 : vates, i. e. Orpheus, App. M. 2, p. 124 .— For musivus, mosaic , Inscr.…

mūsĭcārĭus.opening: musicus , a musical-instrument maker , Inscr. Grut. 654, 1 .

mūsĭcātus.opening: adj. musica , set to music (post-class.): cantilenae, App. Trism. p. 81, 33 .

mūsĭcus.opening: . , adj. , = μουσικός . Of or belonging to music, musical (class.). Adj. : leges musicae, the rules of music, Cic. Leg. 2, 15, 39 : sonus citharae, Phaedr. 4, 18, 20 : pedes, Plin. 29, 1, 5, § 6 .— Subst . , , , a…

Mūsĭ-gĕna.opening: Musa-gigno , muse-born, son of a muse (post-class.), Rufin. de Compos. et Metr. Orat.

mūsīvus.opening: adj. musa , of or belonging to a muse, artistic : fontem opere musivo exornare, Inscr. Orell. 3323 ; cf. Museus.—As subst. : , , , = μουσεῖον , mosaic work, mosaic (post-class.): pictum de musivo, Spart. Pesc. 6 :…

mussātĭo.opening: musso , a suppression of the voice, silence (post-class.), v. l. ap. Amm. 20, 8, 9 (al. simulatione).

mustārĭus.opening: adj. mustum , of or belonging to must (ante-class.): urceus, Cato, R. R. 11 .

mustēla.opening: or , , mus . A weasel : certum est mustelae posthac numquam credere, Plaut. Stich. 3, 2, 43 ; cf. Plin. 29, 4, 16, § 60 .— A fish; acc. to some, a lamprey; acc. to others, an eelpout , Plin. 9, 17, 29, § 63 : marina,…

mustēlātus.opening: ( ), , adj. mustela , weasel-colored : peplum, App. M. 2, p. 126, 22 dub.

mustrĭcŏla.opening: ( ), , , a shoemaker's last , Paul. ex Fest. p. 147 Müll.; Afran. ib. (Com. Rel. v. 421 Rib.).

mustŭōsus.opening: adj. mustum , full of new wine (late Lat.), Cassiod. ap. Ps. 79, s. f.

mustus.opening: adj., young, new, fresh (as adj. only ante-class.): agna, Cato ap. Prisc. 711 P.: vinum, id. R. R. 115 .— Subst. : , , , new or unfermented wine, must , Cato, R. R. 120 : dulce, Verg. G. 1, 295 : novum, Plin. Ep. 9, 16,…

Musulāmii.opening: ( , ), , , a powerful African tribe, west of the Great Syrtis , Tac. A. 2, 52 ; 4, 24 ; Plin. 5, 4, 4, § 30 ; Aur. Vict. Caes. 4, 2 .

Mūta.opening: a goddess, called also Lara and Larunda, whom Jupiter, on account of her talkativeness, struck dumb , Ov. F. 2, 583 ; Lact. 1, 20 ; id. 1, 35 .

mūtābĭlis.opening: adj. muto , changeable, mutable (class.): omne corpus mutabile est, Cic. N. D. 3, 12, 30 : sidera quae vaga et mutabili erratione (al. ratione) labuntur, id. Univ. 10 : forma civitatis, id. Rep. 2, 23, 43 : varium et…

mūtātor.opening: id. , a changer; an exchanger, barterer ( poet. and post-Aug. prose): mutator circulus anni, i. e. Zodiacus, Luc. 10, 202 : mercis mutator Eoae, i. e. mercator, id. 8, 854 : equorum, i. e. desultor, Val. Fl. 6, 161 :…

mūtātōrĭus.opening: adj. mutator , of or belonging to changing or exchanging (post-class.). Adj. : indumentum, Tert. Res. Carn. 56 .— Subst. : , , A cape, tippet, wimple, change of raiment; Gr. ἀναβόλαιον , Hier. in Isa. 3, 22 ; Vulg. Isa.…

mūtātūra.opening: 1. muto , the exchange of money, paying in exchange , Nov. Majorian. de Curial. 4, 7 , c. 1, § 14; 16.

mūtātus.opening: id. , a change, alteration (eccl. Lat.): incredibili mutatu, Tert. Pall. 4 .

mŭtĭcus.opening: adj. , for mutilus, curtailed, docked (ante-class.): spica, Varr. R. R. 1, 48, 3 .

mŭtĭlāgo.opening: a plant, also called tithymalus, App. Herb. 108 .

mŭtĭlĭtas.opening: mutilus , imperfection, defect (late Lat.), Dion. Exig. Greg. Creat. Hom. 12.

mŭtĭlo.opening: v. a. mutilus , to cut or lop off, to cut short, clip, crop; to maim, mutilate (syn.: trunco, tondeo, amputo). Lit. : naso auribusque mutilatis, Liv. 29, 9 : corpora securibus, Curt. 9, 2, 10 : aures naresque, id. 7, 5,…

mūtŭārĭus.opening: adj. mutuus , mutual (post-class.): operae, exchanges of services, App. Mag. p. 284, 30 .

mȳcētĭas.opening: , = μυκητίας , for mycematias, an earthquake attended with a rumbling noise , App. de Mund. p. 65, 33 .

mўron.opening: or , , , = μύρον , an ointment, unguent , pure Latin, unguentum (eccl. Lat.): myro ungere caput, Hier. praef. in Libr. Reg. fin.

mўrŏ-pōla.opening: , = μυροπώλης , a dealer in ointments, essences, balsams , etc., a perfumer (ante-class.), Naev. ap. Fulg. 565, 17 ; Plaut. Cas. 2, 3, 10 ; id. Trin. 2, 4, 7 .

mўrŏ-pōlĭum.opening: , = μυροπώλιον , a shop where ointments, balsams, essences , etc., were sold, a perfumer's shop (Plautin.), Plaut. Ep. 2, 2, 15 ; id. Am. 4, 1, 3 .

myrtĕŏlus.opening: ( , ), , adj. dim . [myrteus], of the color of myrtle-blossoms : myrteolo modo crine viret (al. murceolo, al. murciolo), Col. poët. 10, 237.

myrtētum.opening: ( ), , (collat. form, , , , Plaut. Fragm. ap. Prisc. p. 625 P.) [myrtus], a place full of myrtles, a myrtle-grove : quasi pineis murteta item ego vos virgis circumvinciam, Plaut. Rud. 3, 4, 27 : collis vestitus oleastro…

myrtĕus.opening: ( ), , adj. id. , of or belonging to myrtles, myrtle- . Lit. : myrtea silva, Verg. A. 6, 443 : corona, Val. Max. 3, 6, 5 ; cf.: myrtea corona (Papirius) usus est, quod Sardos in campis Myrteis superāsset, Paul. ex Fest.…

myrtĭnus.opening: ( ), , adj. , = μύρτινος , of or belonging to myrtles, myrtle- (post-class. for myrteus): oleum, App. Herb. 121 .

myrtŏ-pĕtălon.opening: , = μύρτοσ-πέταλον , myrtle-leaf, a plant, also called polygonon, Plin. 27, 12, 91, § 113 .

myrtum.opening: ( ), , , = μύρτον , the fruit of the myrtle, a myrtle-berry : cruenta myrta, Verg. G. 1, 306 ; cf. Plin. 15, 29, 35, § 118 .

Myscĕlŏs.opening: or , , , the founder of the city of Croton, in Italy , Ov. M. 15, 20 .

Mȳsĭa.opening: , = Μυσία , a country of Asia Minor, divided into Lesser Mysia, on the Hellespont, and Greater Mysia, on the Ægean Sea , Mel. 1, 18, 1 ; Plin. 5, 32, 40, § 143 ; Cic. Or. 8, 25 ; Luc. 3, 203 ; Inscr. Orell. 2274 ; 3664…

mysta.opening: or , , , = μύστης , a priest of the secret rites of divine worship, a priest of the mysteries , Ov. F. 4, 536 ; Aus. Idyll. 1, 2 ; Inscr. Orell. 2362 .

mystăgōgĭca.opening: , = μυσταγωγικά , a treatise on initiation into the mysteries , Paul. ex Fest. p. 363, 30 Müll.

mўstăgōgus.opening: , = μυσταγωγός , one who conducts a person through secret and sacred places as a guide , an initiator, a mystagogue , Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 59, § 132 .— Trop. : amicitiae meae, te mystagogo usus, accessit, the founder, Symm.…

mystrum.opening: , = μύστρον , the fourth part of a cyathus, Rhem. Fan. de Pond. et Mens. 77.
