Nārўcĭa.opening: the city of Locri, founded in Lower Italy by the Ozolian Locrians (from Narycion), Ov. M. 15, 705 .

Nārўcĭon.opening: , = Ναρύκιον , Plin. 4, 17, 12, § 27 ; and , , , = Νάρυξ , a city of the Ozolian Locrians , a colony from which built the city of Locri, in Italy, Plin. 4, 17, 12, § 27 (Jan. Narycum).—Hence, , , adj. , = Ναρύκιος , of…

Năsămōnes.opening: , = Νασαμῶνες , a Libyan people to the south-west of Cyrenaica, extending to the Great Syrtis , Plin. 5, 5, 5, § 33 ; 7, 2, 2, § 14 ; 13, 17, 23, § 104 : tota commercia mundo Naufragiis Nasamones habent (because they…

nascens.opening: Part. and P. a. , from nascor.

nascentĭa.opening: , v. nascor, II. P. a. A. 2.

nascĭbĭlis.opening: adj. nascor , that can be born (post-class.), Tert. adv. Marc. 3, 19 ; 3, 11 .

Nascĭo.opening: the goddess of birth; v. natio, init. , I.

nascor.opening: (ante-class., and in poets of the class. period also gnatus, v. under P. a. B.; part. fut. nasciturus, Pall. Jun. 7, § 8 ; Vulg. Judic. 13, 8 ), , v. dep. from gnascor, gnatus, root gen, whence gigno; cf. Gr. γεννάω ,…

nāsīca.opening: comm. adj. [nasus], who has a large or pointed nose , Arn. 6, 196 ; 3, 108 .

Nāsīca.opening: a surname in the Scipio family . So P. Cornelius Scipio Nasica, who was declared to be the most virtuous man in the state, and on that account was sent to accompany the image of the Mater Idaea to Rome , Liv. 29, 14, 8…

Nāsīdĭēnus.opening: a Roman surname . A wealthy upstart in the time of Horace , Hor. S. 2, 8, 1 sq. — Another person , Mart. 7, 54 .

Nāsĭdĭus.opening: name of a Roman gens. L. Nasidius, a Roman knight , Cic. Phil. 7, 8, 24 .— An adherent of Pompey , Caes. B. C. 2, 3 ; Cic. Att. 11, 17, 3 .—Hence, , , adj., Nasidian : naves, Caes. B. C. 2, 7 .

Nāso.opening: amplif. [nasus, largenosed], a Roman family name in the Otacilian, Octavian, Ovidian, and Voconian gentes. So esp., P. Ovidius Naso, the poet : ingenio perii Naso poëta meo, Ov. Tr. 3, 3, 74 .

Nāsos.opening: or , , , = Νᾶσος, Νῆσος (the island), a part of the city of Syracuse , Liv. 25, 30, 9 sqq.

nassa.opening: or , , no , a wickerbasket with a narrow neck, for catching fish, a weel . Lit. : nassa est piscatorii vasi genus, quo, cum intravit piscis, exire non potest, Paul. ex Fest. p. 169 Müll.; Sil. 5, 47 ; Plin. 9, 37, 61, §…

nassĭterna.opening: ( ), , nasus , a large watering-pot with a large nose or spout : nassiterna est genus vasi aquarii ansati et patentis, quale est quo equi perfundi solent, Paul. ex Fest. p. 169 Müll.; Cato, R. R. 11 ; Varr. ap. Non.…

nassĭternātus.opening: nassiterna , provided with a large-nosed watering-pot , Calp. ap. Fulg. in Expos. Serm. Antiq. p. 563, 31 Merc.

nasturtĭum.opening: nasi-tortium , a kind of cress : nasturtium nomen accepit a narium tormento, Plin. 19, 8, 44, § 155 ; cf. id. 20, 13, 50, § 127 : (Persas) negat Xenophon ad panem adhibere quicquam praeter nasturtium, Cic. Tusc. 5, 34,…

nāsus.opening: (ante - class. , : quīs oculi non sunt neque nasum, Lucil. ap. Non. 215, 4 ; Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 288 ; id. Curc. 1, 2, 18 ; id. Men. 1, 2, 57 ; id. Mil. 4, 6, 41 ), the nose (syn nares). Lit. : nasus ita locatus est, ut…

nāsūtus.opening: adj. nasus , that has a large nose, large-nosed (perh. not anteAug.). Lit. : depygis, nasuta, Hor. S. 1, 2, 93 : manus, the elephant's trunk, Cassiod. Var. 10, 30 .— Trop. , sagacious, witty, satirical, censorious :…

nāta.opening: , v. natus, under , P. a. B. 1.

nătābĭlis.opening: adj. nato , that can swim or float (post-class.): robur, Coripp. Laud. Just. 4, 43 .

nătābŭlum.opening: id. , a place for swimming, a swimming - place , App. Flor. p. 353, 6 : natabula fluminis, Jul. Val. Res Gest. Alex. 2, 9 .

nătābundus.opening: adj., swimming , Jul. Val. Res Gest. Alex. M. 2, 8 (2, 31 Mai.).

Natal.opening: = natale, birthday festival , the name of one of the mimes of Laberius : in mimo, qui inscribitur Natal, Gell. 16, 7, 9 .

nātālīcĭus.opening: adj. 1. natalis , of or belonging to the hour or day of one's birth, birthday, natal (class.): qui haec Chaldaeorum natalicia praedicta defendunt, a casting of nativities, Cic. Div. 2, 42, 89 : sidera, id. ib. 2, 43, 91…

nātālis.opening: adj. natus, nascor , of or belonging to one's birth, birth-, natal : hunc emortualem facere ex natali die, Plaut. Ps. 4, 7, 139 : nunc huic lenonist hodie natalis dies, id. ib. 3, 1, 9 : natali die tuo scripsisti…

Nātālis.opening: a Roman surname , e. g. Antonius Natalis, Tac. A. 15, 50, 54 sq. ; 71 .

nătans.opening: Part. and P. a. , v. nato fin.

nătātìcĭus.opening: adj. nato , that can swim : nataticius, νηκτικός , Gloss. Philox.

nătātĭlis.opening: adj. id. , that can swim (post-class.): animae, Tert. adv. Herm. 33 . — Subst. : , , , swimming creatures : feras, volucres, reptiles, natatiles, Prud. στεφ . 10, 332; App. de Mund. 28 .

nătātĭo.opening: id. , a swimming . Lit. : habeant igitur sibi arma, sibi equos ... sibi pilam, sibi natationes atque cursus. * Cic. Sen. 16, 58 : frigidae natationes, Cels. 3, 24 fin. — Transf. , a place for swimming, swimming - place…

nătātor.opening: id. , a swimmer , Varr. L. L. 5, § 93 Müll.: pugnat in adversas ire natator aquas. Ov. R. Am. 122 ; id. H. 19, 70 ; Stat. Th. 10, 497 .

nătātōrĭus.opening: adj. natator , of or belonging to a swimmer, that serves to swim with, natatory (post-class.): cortex, Isid. Orig. 17, 7, 27 .— Subst. : , , , and , , , a place for swimming, a swimming - place, a bath; a pool , Sid.…

nătātūra.opening: id. , a place for swimming or bathing : natatura, κολυμβήθρα , Gloss. Philox.

nătātus.opening: id. , a swimming (postAug.), Stat. S. 1, 5, 25 : piscium natatu, Pall. 1, 17, 2 : fluvios natatu scindere, Claud. IV. Cons. Hon. 347 ; cf. id. Rapt. Pros. 3, 333 .

nātĭcīdĭum.opening: or † , , natus-caedo , the murdering of one's son or child, child-murder : gnaticidium, τεκνοκτονία , Gloss. Philox.

nătĭnātĭo.opening: a being busy, business : natinatio dicebatur negotiatio et natinatores ex eo seditiosa negotia gerentes, Paul. ex Fest. p. 166 Müll.

nătĭnor.opening: v. dep. , to be busy : audito tumultu Macedoniae Samnites, Lucanos inter se natinari atque factiosos esse, Cato ap. Paul. ex Fest. s. v. natinatio, p. 166 Müll.; v. h. v.

nātĭo.opening: nascor , a being born, birth; hence, transf. Personified, Natio, the goddess of birth : Natio quoque dea putanda est, quae, quia partus matronarum tueatur, a nascentibus Natio nominata est, Cic. N. D. 3, 18, 47 (al.…

nătis.opening: , more freq. in the plur. , , , akin to Gr. νῶτον, back; cf. νόσφι , the rump, the buttocks . Sing. : diffissā nate, Hor. S. 1, 8, 46 ; Auct. Priap. 77, 11 ; 83, 23 : quod ejus natis fulmine icta erat, Paul. ex Fest. s.…

Natiso.opening: , = Νατίσων , a small Italian river near Aquileia , now Natisone , Mel. 2, 4, 3 ; Plin. 3, 18, 22, § 126 .

nătĭto.opening: v. freq. [no], to swim (late Lat.), Anon. (Hilar.) in Job, 1, p. 98.

nātĭuncŭla.opening: dim. natio , a small nation : natio, natiuncula, Not. Tir. p. 79 .

nātīvĭtas.opening: nativus , birth, nativity (post-class.; cf. ortus): municipem aut nativitas aut adoptio facit, Dig. 50, 1, 1 : janua nativitatis, Tert. Anim. 39 : vultum nativitatis, natural face, Vulg. Jacob. 1, 23 . — Plur. , Tert.…

nātīvĭtus.opening: adv. id. , from birth, by birth (post-class.), Tert. Anim. 39 ; so id. ib. 12 .

nātīvus.opening: adj. nascor , that has arisen from or by birth; born (cf. naturalis). Lit. (class.): mundus, made, created, Lucr. 5, 66 : animus, id. 3, 417 : Anaximandri opinio est, nativos esse deos, Cic. N. D. 1, 10, 25 .— Transf.…

năto.opening: v. freq. n. and a. [no], to swim, to float . Lit. : qui neque in Oceano natare volueris studiosissimus homo natandi, Cic. Fam. 7, 10, 2 : natant pisces aequore, Ov. P. 2, 7, 28 : canis, per flumen, carnem dum ferret,…

nā^trix.opening: (once : natrix violator aquae, Luc. 9, 720 ; usually), no . A water-snake : cur deus tantam vim natricum viperarumque fecerit? Cic. Ac. 2, 38, 120 .— Trop. , of a dangerous person: se natricem educare, Suet. Calig. 11…

nātŭla.opening: dim. nata , a little daughter , Inscr. Gud. 335, 12 .

nātūra.opening: nascor , birth. Lit. (very rare): naturā tu illi pater es, consiliis ego, Ter. Ad. 1, 2, 46 ; cf.: naturā pater, id. ib. 5, 7, 4 .— Transf. (freq. and class.; syn.: indoles, ingenium). The nature , i. e. the natural…

nātūrābĭlis.opening: , i. q. naturalis, App. Doct. Plat. 2, p. 19, 6 .

nātūrālis.opening: adj. natura , natural , i. e., By birth, one's own : naturalis pater, opp. to adoptive father, Cic. Phil. 3, 6, 15 : in adoptionem dato redire in familiam liceat, si pater naturalis sine liberis decesserit, Quint. 3, 6,…

nātūrālĭtas.opening: naturalis , naturainess (post-class.): somni naturalitas, Tert. Anim. 43 ; 16 .

nātūrālĭtus.opening: adv. naturalis , by nature (post-class.), Sid. Ep. 9, 11 ; App. M. 1, 12, p. 107 .

nātūrĭfĭcātus.opening: adj. naturafacio , brought into being (post-class.): animae naturificatae, Tert. adv. Valent. 23 .

nātus.opening: (used only in abl. sing. ), nascor , lit. birth; hence, * Of plants, a growing, growth : cupressus natu morosa, slow of growth, Plin. 16, 33, 60, § 139 .— With esp. reference to age, birth, age, years (the class.…

nauarchia.opening: , = ναυαρχία , the command of a vessel , Cod. Th. 13, 5, 20.

nauarchus.opening: (less correctly ), = ναύαρχος , the master of a vessel , Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 24, § 60 ; Tac. A. 15, 51 ; Inscr. Orell. 3615 ; 3624 ; Veg. Mil. 5, 2 .

Naubŏlus.opening: , = Ναύβολος , a king of Phocis, father of Iphitus the Argonaut , Stat. Th. 7, 355 ; Hyg. Fab. 14 .—Hence, , , , the son of Naubolus , i. e. Iphitus , Val. Fl. 1, 362 ; cf. Stat. Th. 7, 354 .

nauclērĭcus.opening: adj. , = ναυκληρικός , of or belonging to a ship-owner or ship-master : facito uti venias (ornatu) ornatus huc nauclerico, in a skipper's dress, Plaut. Mil. 4, 4, 41 (MSS. nauclerioco): nauclerico ornatu, in the dress…

nauclērĭus.opening: , v. l. for nauclericus, q. v. Plaut. As. 1, 1, 54 .

nauclērus.opening: , = ναύκληρος , a shipowner, a ship-master, skipper (syn.: navarchus, gubernator), Plaut. Mil. 4, 3, 17 ; Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 1 ; Vulg. Act. 27, 11 ; Cod. Th. 7, 16, 3; Firm. Math. 8, 20 fin. — , the title of a comedy…

Naucrătes.opening: , = Ναυκράτης , a Greek historian of Erythræ, a pupil of Isocrates , Cic. de Or. 2, 23, 94 ; 3, 44, 173 ; id. Or. 51, 172 ; Quint. 3, 6, 3 .

Naucrătis.opening: , = Ναύκρατις , a town of the Delta in Egypt , now Salhadschar , Plin. 5, 10, 11, § 64 ; 31, 10, 46, § 111 .— Hence, , , adj., of Naucratis, Naucratian : nomos, Plin. 5, 9, 9, § 49 .— , , adj. , Naucratian : ostium…

naucŭla.opening: navicula , a little ship , for navicula (post-Aug.), Plin. Ep. 5, 6, 37 ; 9, 7, 4 ; Paul. Carm. 21, 247 ; cf.: naucula, navicella, navicula, Not. Tir. p. 177 .

naucum.opening: , or , , etym. dub.; cf. nugae , something slight or trivial, a trifle : naucum ait Ateius Philologus poni pro nugis. Cincius, quod in oleae nucis, quod intus sit. Aelius Stilo omnium rerum putamen. Glossematorum autem…

naufrăgābĭlis.opening: adj. naufragium , dangerous to ships (late Lat.), Caes. Ep. 2, p. 1134 .

naufrăgālis.opening: adj. id. , where many shipwrecks occur, dangerous to ships : Capraria naufragalis, Mart. Cap. 6, § 643 ; cf. naufragiosus.

naufrăgātor.opening: naufrago , a shipwrecked person (late Lat.), Aug. Serm. in Spicil. Rom. t. 8.

naufrăgĭōsus.opening: adj. naufragium , full of shipwrecks, dangerous to ships : pelagus, Sid. Ep. 4, 12 ; Claud. Mam. de Stat. Anim. 1, 1 ; cf. naufragalis.

naufrăgĭum.opening: for navifragium, from navis-frango , a shipwreck . Lit. : multi naufragia fecerunt, Cic. Fam. 16, 9, 1 : naufragio perire, id. Deiot. 9, 25 : naufragio interire, Caes. B. C. 3, 27 : naufragio interceptus, Tac. A. 14, 3…

naufrăgo.opening: v. n. naufragus , to suffer shipwreck, be wrecked : omnes naves naufragārunt, Petr. 76, 4 ; Sid. Ep. 4, 21 ; Salv. Gub. Dei , 3, p. 77.

naufrăgus.opening: adj. navis-frango , that suffers shipwreck, shipwrecked, wrecked . Lit. (class.): Marium Africa devicta expulsum et naufragum vidit, Cic. Pis. 19, 43 : corpora, Verg. G. 3, 542 : puppis, Ov. H. 2, 16 : mulier, Tac. A.…

Naulŏcha.opening: ( , , , Suet. Aug. 116 ), a village on the north coast of Sicily, near the promontory of Pelorus , Sil. 14, 265 .

naulum.opening: ( ), , , = ναῦλον , passage-money, fare : perdere naulon, Juv. 8, 97 : in naulis navium, Dig. 30, 39, 1 : ut naulum exsolvatur, ib. 20, 4, 6 ; Vulg. Jonae, 1, 3 .

naumăchĭa.opening: , = ναυμαχία , the representation of a sea-fight, a mock seafight (pure Lat. navale proelium). Lit. : naumachiam commisit, Suet. Claud. 21 : naumachiae spectaculum edere, id. Caes. 44 : naumachiam exhibere, id. Ner. 12…

naumăchĭārĭus.opening: adj. naumachia , of or for a mock sea-fight : pons, Plin. 16, 39, 74, § 190 .—Hence, Subst. : , , , a combatant in a mock sea-fight , Suet. Claud. 21 .

naumăchus.opening: , = ναύμαχος , a naval combatant : nauta, nauticus, naumachus, naumachia, Not. Tir. p. 77 .

Naupactus.opening: ( ), , , and , , , = Ναύπακτος , a city of Ætolia, on the Gulf of Corinth , now Epakto or Lepanto , Caes. B. C. 3, 35 ; Mel. 2, 3, 5 ; Cic. Pis. 37, 91 ; Liv. 36, 30 ; 34 sq.; Plin. 4, 2, 3, § 6 .—Hence, , , adj.,…

naupēgĭārĭus.opening: naupegus , a ship-carpenter , Inscr. Spon. Miscell. p. 67.

naupēgus.opening: , = ναυπηγός , a shipbuilder, shipwright, ship-carpenter : naupego in navi maritimā diurni X sexaginta, Edict. Diocl. p. 19; Dig. 50, 6, 6 ; Firm. Math. 4, 7 med.

nauphўlax.opening: ( , , ), , , = ναυφύλαξ , one who kept watch over the luggage on shipboard , Inscr. Don. 273, 2 ; Inscr. Maff. Mus. Ver. 125, 3 .

Naupĭdămē.opening: , = Ναυπιδάμη , daughter of Amphidamas, and mother of Augeas by Helios , Hyg. Fab. 14 .

Nauplĭus.opening: , = Ναύπλιος , a son of Neptune and Amymone, king of Eubœa, and father of Palamedes. To avenge his son, whom the Greeks had put to death before Troy, he made false signal-fires on the shores of Eubœa as the Greeks were…

nauplĭus.opening: , = ναύπλιος , a kind of shell-fish, which sails in its shell as in a ship , Plin. 9, 30, 49, § 94 ; v. naviger.

Nauportum.opening: a city in Upper Pannonia , the mod. Laybach , Tac. A. 1, 20 ; Vell. 2, 110, 4 .—Near it is the river , , , Plin. 3, 18, 22, § 128 .

nauscit.opening: (qs. naviscit), said of a bean, which opens in the shape of a ship, Paul. ex Fest. p. 168 and 169 Müll.

nausĕa.opening: or , , , = ναυσία , sea-sickness . Lit. : ne nauseae molestiam suscipias aeger, Cic. Fam. 16, 11, 1 : navigavimus sine timore et nauseā, id. Att. 5, 13, 1 : nauseā pressus, Cels. 1, 3 .— Transf. , in gen., sickness,…

nausĕābĭlis.opening: adj. nauseo , that causes nausea or vomiting , Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 2, 18 .

nausĕābundus.opening: adj. id. , inclined to vomit , Sen. Ep. 108, 35 ; 47, 6 .

nausĕātor.opening: id. , one who is apt to feel nausea, who vomits easily : Ulixes nauseator erat, Sen. Ep. 53, 4 .

nausĕo.opening: v. n. nausea , to be sea-sick . Lit. , Hor. Ep. 1, 1, 93 : si sine vomitu nauseavit, Cels. 1, 3 .— Transf. , to be squeamish or qualmish, to vomit : quidlibet, modo ne nauseet, faciat, Cic. Phil. 2, 34, 84 : ructantem…

nausĕŏla.opening: dim. id. , a slight squeamishness , Cic. Att. 14, 8, 2 .

nausĕōsus.opening: adj. id. , that produces nausea, nauseous : radix, Plin. 26, 8, 38, § 59 .

Nausĭcăa.opening: , and , , , = Ναυσικάα , the daughter of Atcinoüs, king of the Phæacians : virgo Nausicaa, Gell. 9, 9, 14 ; cf. Aus. Per. Odyss. 6 ; Hyg. Fab. 125 sq. : Nausicaë patrii horti, Mart. 12, 31, 9 .

Nausĭphănes.opening: , = Ναυσιφάνης , a Grecian philosopher of Teos, instructor of Epicurus , Cic. N. D. 1, 26, 33 .

Nausĭphŏus.opening: the son of Ulysses by Circe , Hyg. Fab. 125 .

Nausistrăta.opening: name of a woman , Ter. Phorm. 5, 7, 94 et passim.

Naustathmos.opening: , = Ναύσταθμος , a seaport in Ionia, near Phocæa , Liv. 37, 31 fin.

naustĭbŭlum.opening: navis , a vessel shaped like a ship : naustibulum vocabant antiqui vas alvei simile, videlicet a navis similitudine, Paul. ex Fest. p. 168 and 169 Müll.

nausum.opening: a kind of Gallic ship : nauso advehi, Aus. Ep. 22 ; id. ib. in carm .

nauta.opening: (ante-class., poet. , and late Lat. ), , for navita, from navis , a sailor, seaman, mariner : ego nautas eum non putabam habiturum, Cic. Att. 9, 3, 2 ; id. Fam. 16, 9, 4 ; nautas gubernatoresque comparari jubet, Caes.…

Nautăca.opening: , = Ναύτακα , a city of Sogdiana, near the river Oxus, probably between the mod. Samarcand and the river Amur , Curt. 8, 2, 9 (ex conject., Zumpt and Mütz. for Naura).

nautālis.opening: adj. nauta , sailor-like : forma, Aus. Idyll. 10, 223 .

nautĕa.opening: , = ναυτία (another form for ναυσία ). * A qualm, nausea : nauteam facere, Plaut. ap. Paul. ex Fest. p. 165 Müll.— An offensive liquid , perh. bilgewater = sentina: nautea est aqua de coriis, vel, quod est verius, aqua…

Nautes.opening: the primogenitor of the Nautii (v. h. v.), Verg. A. 5, 704 ; 728 .

nautĭcārĭus.opening: nauta , a shipmaster , Inscr. Fea Fast. Cons. 40.

nautĭcus.opening: adj. , = ναυτικός , of or belonging to ships or sailors, ship-, nautical : inhibere est verbum totum nauticum, Cic. Att. 13, 21, 3 : exuviae nauticae, id. Imp. Pomp. 18, 54 : scientia nauticarum rerum, Caes. B. G. 3, 8…

Nautĭi.opening: the Nautians, a Roman family, descended from Nautes the Trojan, who brought the image of Minerva to Italy. The sacrifices to Minerva remained in this family, and the goddess herself was called Dea Nautia, Serv. ad Verg.…

nautĭlus.opening: or , , , = ναυτίλος , the nautilus, a shell-fish so called because it sails like a vessel , Plin. 9, 29, 47, § 88 ; cf. nauplius and naviger.

Nautĭus.opening: name of a Roman gens. C. Nautius, a consul , Liv. 2, 52 ; 3, 25 sq.— C. Nautius Rutilus, a consul , Liv. 4, 52 .— Sp. Nautius Rutilus, a military tribune , Liv. 4, 35 .

Nāva.opening: a river of Germany which flows into the Rhine near Bingen , now the Nahe , Tac. H. 4, 70 ; Aus Mosell. 1.

nāvācŭlum.opening: navis , a harbor : navaculum, ναύσταθμον , Gloss. Philox.

nāvālis.opening: adj. navis , of or belonging to ships, ship-, naval : pedestres navalesve pugnae, Cic. Sen. 5, 13 ; Liv. 26, 51, 6 : bellum, id. Imp. Pomp. 10, 28 : apparatus, id. Att. 10, 8, 3 : disciplina et gloria navalis, id. Imp.…

nāvĭa.opening: navis . A corruption of navis, a ship; in the proverb, aut caputa aut naviam for aut caput aut navim (v. caput), Aur. Vict. Orig. Gent. R. 3 ; Paul. Nol. 38, 73 ; cf. Macr. S. 1, 7 .— Transf. , a bark, boat, canoe :…

nāvĭcella.opening: ( ), , dim. navis , a small vessel, a boat, skiff (postclass.): navicellae, quae piscium capiendorum causā paratae sunt, Dig. 33, 7, 17, § 1 (al. naucellae).

nāvĭcŭla.opening: dim. id. , a small vessel, a boat, skiff : nos ad naviculas nostras descendimus, Cic. Ac. 2, 48, 148 ; Afran. ap. Non. 238, 25 ; Caes. B. C. 2, 3 ; cf. id. ib. 3, 104 fin.

nāvĭcŭlāris.opening: adj. navicula , of or relating to the shipping business (postclass.): res, Dig. 50, 4, 1, § 1 .

nāvĭcŭlārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to a small ship, boat , or vessel (late Lat.): onus, Cod. Th. 13, 5, 12: PORTITOR, Inscr. Mur. 984, 1.— Of or belonging to a ship-master : functio, Cod. Just. 11, 2, 3 .—Hence, subst. , , , a…

nāvĭcŭlor.opening: ( ), , v. dep. n. [navicula], to sail in a small vessel : Lucrino nauculatur in stagno, Mart. 3, 20, 20 .

nāvĭfrăgus.opening: adj. navis-frango , causing shipwrecks, dangerous ( poet. ): navifragum Scylaceum, Verg. A. 3, 553 : fretum, Ov. M. 14, 6 : saxa, Stat. Th. 5, 415 ; cf. naufragus, I. B.

nāvĭgābĭlis.opening: adj. navigo , navigable : amnis, Liv. 38, 3 : mare, id. 35, 44 : fossa, Tac. A. 15, 42 : litora, id. ib. 13, 53 : flumen, Col. 1, 2, 3 : fontes magnorum fluminum, Auct. ap. Quint. 8, 3, 76 .

nāvĭgātĭo.opening: id. , a sailing, navigation : ex tuis litteris cognovi cursūs navigationum tuarum, Cic. Fam. 13, 68, 1 : in portum ex longā navigatione venire, id. Sen. 19, 71 : prima navigatio, id. Q. Fr. 2, 6, 3 : navigationi se…

nāvĭgātor.opening: id. , a sailor, mariner , Quint. 5, 10, 27 ; Auct. Quint. Decl. 12, 23; Paul. Nol. ad Cyther. 397 .
