neurospaston.opening: , = νευρόσπαστον , a figure set in motion by strings, a puppet, marionette , Gell. 14, 1, 23 (by others written as Greek).

neuter.opening: ( gen. neutri, Varr. L. L. 9, § 62 , acc. to the MSS.; cf. §§ 55 and 58; Aus. Ep. 50 ; and by grammarians always in the phrase neutri generis, of the neuter gender, Charis. 13 P.; Diom. 277 P. al.; Serv. Verg. A. 1, 449…

ne-utĭquam.opening: (mostly ante-class.; not in Cæs., Quint., Plin., Suet.; very rare in Cic. and Liv.; v. Hand, Turs. 3, p. 182 sq.; by Enn., Plaut., and Ter. written as two words, ), adv., by no means, in nowise; not altogether, not…

ne-utĭquē.opening: adv., by no means (postclass.), Cod. Th. 15, 2, 3.

neutrālis.opening: adj. neuter , in gram., of the gender of substantives, neuter : positio, Quint. 1, 4, 24 : nomina, id. 1, 5, 54 et saep.—Hence, adv. : , as a neuter; Gellius fora navium neutraliter dixit, Charis. p. 55 P.

neutrŭbi.opening: adv. neuter-ubi . * In neither place , Plaut. Aul. 2, 2, 56 .— Neither way : neutrubi proelio inclinato, Amm. 19, 2, 13 ; 24, 2, 14 .

nē-ve.opening: or , adv. , introduces a negative clause containing a purpose, command, or prohibition, esp. after ut, ne, etc., and not, nor, and that not, and lest : utinam ne in nemore, etc.... neve inde, etc., Enn. ap. Auct. Her.…

nex.opening: neco , death (syn.: mors, letum). Lit. A violent death, murder, slaughter (cf.: caedes, occisio): mater terribilem minatur vitae cruciatum et necem, Enn. ap. Cic. de Or. 3, 58, 218 (Trag. v. 44 Vahl.): insidiatori et…

nexābundē.opening: adv. nexo , in a straitened or scanty manner; comp. : victitare nexabundius, Jul. Val. Res Gest. Alex. M. 1, 2 Mai.

nexĭbĭlis.opening: adj. necto , tied or bound together (post-class.). Lit. : membra, Lact. 7, 5, 10 (dub.; al. vexabilia).— Trop. : adversatio, Amm. 29, 2, 11 .

nexĭlis.opening: adj. id. , tied or bound together ( poet. ): vestis, Lucr. 5, 1350 : plagae, Ov. M. 2, 499 : hederae, id. ib. 6, 128 .

nexĭo.opening: necto , a tying or binding together, a fastening (post-class.): vinculorum nexiones, Arn. 5, 156 ; Mart. Cap. 1, § 31 ; 3, § 226 .

nexo.opening: (also of the first conj., acc. to Prisc. 9, 6, 33, p. 860 sq. ; 10, 8, 48 , p. 904; Diom. 1, p. 366 ; and in the reading: nexantem nodis seque in sua membra plicantem, Verg. A. 5, 279 Conington; but here the better…

nexuōsus.opening: nexus , full of windings, much interlaced , Cassiod. Var. 11, 40 Fig.— Sup. : nexuosissimae quaestionem minutiae, excessively involved or complicated , Claud. Mam. Stat. Anim. 2, 6 .

nexus.opening: necto , a tying or binding together, a fastening, joining, an interlacing, entwining, clasping . Lit. (only poet. and in post-Aug. prose): et jam contulerant arto luctantia nexu Pectora pectoribus, Ov. M. 6, 242 ; cf.:…

nī.opening: (old orthography , v. in the foll. ), adv. and conj. [identical with ne and the prim. form, whence nisi, i. e. si ni]. Adv. , like ne, an absolutely negative particle, not. —So only in the combinations, Quid ni? or, in…

nīcā.opening: , = νίκαε, νίκα , conquer! = vincas, a cry with which each party in the circus encouraged its favorite combatant, Inscr. Grut. 338, 2 ; Inscr. Fabr. p. 573 , n. 54.

Nīcaea.opening: ( , Plin. Ep. 10, 48 ), , , = Νίκαια . The name of several cities . A city in Bithynia, on Lake Ascanius, formerly called Antigonia, the mod. Isnik or Nice , Cic. Planc. 34, 84 ; id. Att. 14, 1, 2 ; Cat. 46, 5 ; Plin.…

Nīcaeus.opening: adj. , = Νικαῖος (who grants victory), an epithet of Jupiter : ad templum Jovis, quem Nicaeum vocant, Liv. 43, 21, 8 .

Nīcander.opening: , = Νίκανδρος . A physician, poet, and grammarian of Colophon , Cic. de Or. 1, 16, 69 ; Macr. S. 5, 21, 12 .— A Roman surname , Inscr. Maff. Mus. Ver. 274, 4 .

Nīcānor.opening: , = Νικάνωρ . A grammarian , Suet. Gram. 5 .— A ceiebrated painter , Plin. 35, 11, 39, § 122 .— A roman surname , Inscr. Murat. 26, 3 .

Nīcarchus.opening: , = Νίκαρχος , a Roman surname , Inscr. Grut. 650, 4 .

Nīcărium.opening: , = Νικάριον , a female surname , Inscr. Maff. Mus. Ver. 133, 3 .

Nīcātor.opening: , = Νικήτωρ (victor). An epithet given to the members of King Perseus's body-guard : cohors regia, quos Nicatoras appellant, Liv. 43, 19, 11 .— A surname of the Seleucidæ , Plin. 6, 11, 12, § 31 .

Nīcēphŏrĭum.opening: and , , , = Νικηφόριον . A grove near Pergamum , Liv. 32, 33 and 34.— A city in Mesopotamia , Tac. A. 6, 41 ; Plin. 5, 24, 21, § 86 al.

Nīcēphŏrĭus.opening: ( , , , Plin. 6, 27, 31, § 129 ). The bringer of victory , a surname of Jupiter, Spart. Hadr. 2, 9 .— A river in Armenia, near Tigranocerta , Tac. A. 15, 4 .

Nīcēphŏrus.opening: , = Νικηφόρος (who brings victory), a Roman surname , Cic. Q. Fr. 3, 1, 2, § 4 ; Inscr. Murat. 83, 3 .

Nīcer.opening: the river Neckar , Eum. Pan. Const. 19 ; Aus. Mos. 423 ; Sid. 7, 324 .

Nīcĕros.opening: , = Νικέρως , a perfumer , Mart. 12, 65, 4 .—Hence, , , adj., of Niceros , Mart. 10, 38, 8 ; so id. 6, 55, 3 ; Sid. Carm. 9, 324 .

nīcētērĭum.opening: , = νικητήριον , the prize of victory , Juv. 3, 68 .

Nīcētĭānus.opening: adj., of or belonging to a Nicetius : hereditas, Sid. Ep. 3, 1 .

Nīcĭas.opening: , = Νικίας . A celebrated Athenian statesman and general, who fell in the expedition against Sicily , Nep. Alcib. 3, 1 ; Just. 4, 4, 3 .— Nicias Curtius, a grammarian, a companion of Cicero in Cilicia , Cic. Fam. 9, 10,…

nĭco.opening: v. n. root gnic-, gnig-; Germ. neigen; cf. conivere (for cognigvere), to close (the eyelids), shut fast; v. also nitor, nixus , to beckon , Plaut. Truc. 2, 7, 63 and 64.

Nīco.opening: ( , Inscr. Grut. 656, 5 ), , , = Νίκων . A physician , Cic. Fam. 7, 20, 3.— A famous pirate , Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 30, § 79 .

Nīcocles.opening: , = Νικοκλῆς , a tyrant of Sicyon, overthrown by Aratus , Cic. Off. 2, 23, 81 .

Nīcŏlāus.opening: , = Νικόλαος , a Peripatetic philosopher from Damascus, a friend of Augustus; hence, , , adj., of Nicolaus : dactyli Nicolai, a kind of dates of a larger size than ordinary, Plin. 13, 4, 9, § 45 ; Edict. Diocl. p. 18.

Nīcŏmēdes.opening: , = Νικομήδης . Son of Prusias, a king of Bithynia , Cic. de Or. 2, 61, 229 ; Cic. Verr. 2, 1, 24, § 63 .— The son of the former, who declared himself a freedman of the Roman people , Just. 34, 4 ; 38, 5 ; Suet. Caes. 2…

Nīcŏmēdīa.opening: , = Νικομήδεια , the capital of Bithynia , now Izmid , Plin. 5, 32, 43, § 149 ; Amm. 22, 9, 3 ; Aur. Vict. Caes. 39, 45 .—Hence, , , , the Nicomedians , Plin. et Traj. Ep. 37 (46), 1; Dig. 50, 9, 5 ; Inscr. Grut. 389, 2…

nīcŏphŏros.opening: , = νικόφορος , a kind of bind-weed, withwind : milax quoque, qui et nicophoros nominatur, Plin. 24, 10, 49, § 82 (Jahn, anthophoros).

Nīcŏpŏlis.opening: , = Νικόπολις , the name of several cities , among them a city of Epirus, founded by Augustus to commemorate the battle of Actium , now Prevesa Vecchia , or Paleo-prevesa , Tac. A. 2, 53 ; Suet. Aug. 18 .—Also a city in…

Nīcŏpŏlītānus.opening: adj., of or belonging to Nicopolis, Nicopolitan : civitas, Plin. 4, 1, 2, § 5 .— , , , the Nicopolitans , in Lower Moesia, Inscr. Grut. 527, 7 .

nictātĭo.opening: nicto , a winking with the eyes, Plin. 11, 37, 57, § 156 .

nicto.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1, and ĕre, 3 ātus v. n.
nicto.opening: v. n. , and , , v. dep. n. [1. nico], to move the eyelids . Lit. , to move the eyelids up and down, to wink, blink : plerisque naturale ut nictari (al. nictare) non cessent, Plin. 11, 37, 54, § 144 ; 11, 37, 57, § 156…

nictus.opening: 1. nico , a winking, blinking with the eyes, Caecil. ap. Paul. ex Fest. p. 177 Müll. (but in Ov. M. 3, 460 ; id. A. A. 1, 138 ; and id. F. 1, 418 , the correct read. is nutu).

nīdāmentum.opening: nidus . * The materials for a nest : in nervum ille hodie nidamenta congeret, he will scrape together a nest to get himself a drubbing, Plaut. Rud. 3, 6, 51 .—* Transf. , a nest. blattas nidamenta ponere, Arn. 6, 202 .

nīdĭcus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to a nest : usque ad limina nidica esca vilis, Varr. ap. Non. 336, 10 dub. (a corrupt passage).

nīdĭfĭcĭum.opening: nidifico , a nest , App. M. 8, p. 211, 32 .

nīdĭfĭco.opening: v. n. nidus-facio , to build a nest : nidificant aves, Col. 8, 15, 5 ; 8, 8, 3 : sola piscium nidificat ex algā, Plin. 9, 26, 42, § 81 : turdi luto nidificantes, id. 10, 53, 74, § 147 .—Prov.: sic vos non vobis…

nīdĭfĭcus.opening: adj. nidus-facio , nest-making : ver, when birds make their nests, Sen. Med. 714 .

nīdor.opening: cf. Gr. κνίσσα for κνιδια , a vapor, steam, smell , from any thing boiled, roasted, burned, etc.: nidoris odores, Lucr 6, 987: galbaneus, Verg. G. 3, 415 : pinguescant madidi laeto nidore Penates, Mart. 7, 27, 5 ; Plin.…

nīdōro.opening: v. n. , to give out steam, to steam , Not. Tir. p. 167 .

nīdōrōsus.opening: adj. nidor , steaming, reeking : holocaustomata, Tert. adv. Marc. 5, 5 fin.

nīdŭlor.opening: v. dep. n. and a. [nidus]. Neutr., to build a nest : halcyones hieme in aquā nidulantur, Varr. ap. Non. 145, 7 ; and Gell. 3, 10, 5 ; 2, 29, 4 .—* Act. aliquem, to make a nest for one : contra rigorem hiemis vermiculos…

nīdŭlus.opening: dim. id. , a little nest. Lit. : Ithacam illam, in asperrimis saxulis, tamquam nidulum, affixam, Cic. de Or. 1, 44, 196 ; Gell. 2, 29, 2 .—* Trop. , a place of retirement : senectutis, Auct. ap. Plin. Ep. 6, 10, 1 :…

nīdus.opening: kindred with Sanscr. nīda and the Germ. and Engl. nest , a nest. Lit. : fingere et construere nidos, Cic. de Or. 2, 6, 23 : tignis nidum suspendit hirundo, Verg. G. 4, 307 : facere, Ov. M. 8, 257 : ponere, Hor. C. 4,…

Nĭgellĭo.opening: nigellus, swarthy , a Roman surname , Inscr. Gud. 310, 7 .

nĭgellus.opening: adj. dim. [1. niger], somewhat black, dark (ante-class.): oculi suppaetuli nigellis pupulis, Varr. ap. Non. 456, 8 : amiculum, id. ib. 550, 6 : vina, Pall. 3, 25, 12 : Cadmi nigellae filiae, i. e. the letters of the…

Nĭgellus.opening: a Roman surname , Inscr. Grut. 226, 8 .—In fem. : † , Inscr. Fabr. p. 4 , n. 20.

nĭger.opening: ( gen. fem. nigraï, Lucr. 4, 537 ; comp. nigrior, Ov. H. 18, 7 ), adj., black, sable, dark, dusky (cf.: ater, pullus). Lit. : quae alba sint, quae nigra, dicere, Cic. Div. 2, 3, 9 : quamvis ille niger, quamvis tu…

Nĭger.opening: a river in Africa , Mart. Cap. 6, § 673 ; v. Nigris.

Nĭgĭdĭus.opening: P. Nigidius Figulus, a celebrated Roman scholar, a contemporary of Cicero and Cæsar, the composer of several grammatical works, Gell. 19, 14, 1 ; cf. id. 4, 9, 1 sqq.—Hence, , , adj., of Nigidius : commentationes, Gell.…

nīgīna.opening: , a false read. for nyma. Plin. 27, 12, 82, § 82 .

nī^grēdo.opening: niger , blackness, black color (post-class.): capilli corvinā nigredine, App. M. 2, p. 118, 31 : nigredo ollae, Vulg. Nah. 2, 10 ; Mart. Cap. 2, § 137 : atrae noctis, id. 1, § 67 .

nī^grefacĭo.opening: v. a. 1. niger-facio , to make black, to blacken : nigrefacio, μελανοποιῶ , Vet. Gloss.— Pass. : , to become black , Theod. Prisc. 1, 5 .

nī^grĕo.opening: v. n. 1. niger , to be black (ante-class.): solis occasu nigret, Pac. ap. Non. 144, 11 (Trag. Rel. v. 88 Rib.): nimbis nigret, opp. splendet, Att. ib. 13 (Trag. Rel. v. 260 Rib.).

nī^gresco.opening: v. inch. n. (usu. ī) [id.], to become black, grow dark ( poet. and post-Aug. prose): latices nigrescere sacros, etc., Verg. A. 4, 454 : tenebris nigrescere, id. ib. 11, 824 : nigrescunt sanguine venae, Ov. A. A. 3, 503…

Nī^grĭānus.opening: adj., of or belonging to M. Pescennius Niger, the rival of Septimius Severus , Tert. ad Scap. 3 .

nī^grĭco.opening: v. n. 1. niger , to be blackish (post-Aug.): epimelas fit, cum in candidā gemmā superne nigricat colos, Plin. 37, 10, 58 fin. ; cf. Not. Tir. p. 128 .—Hence, , , P. a., blackish, swarthy : Tyrius color nigricans…

nī^grĭcŏlor.opening: adj. 1. niger-color , = μελάγχροος , of a black color : facies, Sol. 2 .

nī^grĭcŭlus.opening: dim. of niger , blackish, dark, swarthy , Varr. L. L. 8, 40, § 79 .

nī^gridĭus.opening: adj. 1. niger , blackish , Not. Tir. p. 128 .

nī^grĭfĭco.opening: v. a. 1. niger-facio , to make black, to blacken : dentes, Marc. Emp. 35 .

Nī^grīnus.opening: 1. niger, swarthy , a Roman surname : C Pontius Nigrinus, Suet. Tib. 73 .— Fem. : Nigrina, Mart. 4, 75 ; Inscr. Grut. 430, 3 .

Nī^gris.opening: ( , Vitr. 8, 2, 6 ; , Mart. Cap. 6, § 673 ), , a river in the interior of Africa , now the Joliba or Niger , Plin. 5, 4, 4, § 30 ; 8, 21, 32, § 77 .— Hence, , , , the people living near the Niger , Mel. 1, 4, 3 ; 3, 10,…

nī^grĭtĭa.opening: , and , , 1. niger , black color, blackness (post-Aug.): capilli, Plin. 29, 6, 34, § 109 ; 9, 38, 62, § 134 . —Form nigrities, Cels. 8, 4, 19 ; 5, 20, 3 al.

nī^gro.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. n. and a.
nī^gro.opening: v. n. and a. [id.]. Neutr., to be black : ea, quae nigrant nigro de semine nata, Lucr. 2, 733 .— Act., to make black, to blacken . Lit. : mgrāsset sibi planctu lacertos, Stat. S. 2, 6, 83 .— Trop. , to make dark, to…

nī^gror.opening: 1. niger , blackness ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): noctis, Pac. ap. Cic. Div. 1, 14, 24 ; Lucil. ap. Non. 515, 5 : mortis, Lucr. 3, 39 : nigrorem in ulceribus excitat, Cels. 2, 1 : rubidus est rufus, atrore et…

nĭhil.opening: (ante-class. and post-Aug.) contr. , indecl.; and , or contr. , , ne-hilum, not the least; v. hilum . , nothing : nihil est agriculturā melius, nihil uberius, Cic. Off. 1, 42, 151 : de re publicā nihil loquebantur, id.…

nĭhĭlo.opening: nihil , a good-fornothing fellow : οὐδαμινός , nihilo, nugatori. us, gerra, Vet. Gloss.

Nīleus.opening: ( ), , , one of the enemies of Perseus , Ov. M. 5, 187 .

Nīlides lăcus.opening: a lake in Lower Mauritania lacus stagnans quem vocant Niliden, Plin. 5, 9, 10, § 51 ; Mart. Cap. 6, § 676 .

nīlĭos.opening: , = νείλιος , a precious stone, of the color of a dark topaz , Plin. 37, 8, 35, § 114 .

Nīlus.opening: , = Νεῖλος . The river Nile, celebrated for its annual overflow , Lucr. 6, 712 sq. ; Cic. N. D. 2, 52, 130 ; id. Rep. 6, 18, 19 ; Sen. Q. N. 4, 2 ; Plin. 5, 9, 10, § 51 ; 18, 8, 47, § 167 ; Vitr. 8, 2, 6 ; Mart. Cap. 6,…

nimbātus.opening: adj. nimbus , perh. light, trifling, frivolous : quam magis aspecto, tam magis est nimbata et nugae merae, Plaut. Poen. 1, 2, 135 .

nimbĭfer.opening: adj. nimbusfero , storm-bringing, stormy : inter nimbiferas nubes, Avien. Arat. 858 : ignis, Ov. P. 4, 8, 60 (al. nubifer).

nimbōsus.opening: adj. nimbus , full of storms, stormy, rainy (cf.: nubilus, nebulosus): fluctu nimbosus Orion, Verg. A. 1, 535 : ventus, Ov. P. 2, 3, 27 : aër, Luc. 5, 631 : bruma, Stat. S. 1, 3, 89 : montes, Plin. 18, 11, 29, § 109 :…

nimbus.opening: ( gen. plur. nimbūm, Pac. ap. Trag. Rel. 412 Rib.), Sanscr. nabhas, cloud, vapor; Gr. νέφος, νεφέλη; cf.: nubes, nebula , a violent or pouring rain, a rain-storm . Lit. : terra abit in nimbos imbremque, Lucil. ap. Varr.…

nĭmĭĕtas.opening: nimius , a too great number or quantity; a superfluity, redundancy, excess (post-class.): sanguinis, Pall. 6, 7 : prunarum, Eutr. 10, 9 : gaudii, App. M. 3, p. 133, 33 ; Arn. 4, 133 .—In plur. , Pall. 2, 13 med.

nīmīrum.opening: adv. ni, i. q. ne mirum, v. ni, I.; lit. not wonderful; cf., less strong than mirum ni; v. ni, III. A. β; hence , to introduce an assertion as indisputable, without doubt, doubtless, indisputably, certainly, surely,…

nĭmis.opening: adv. ni-, ne-, and root ma-, to measure; cf.: metior, mensa, metare, etc.; hence , too much, overmuch, excessively, beyond measure . Lit. : Chremes nimis graviter cruciat adulescentulum nimisque inhumane, too severely…

nĭmĭus.opening: adj. nimis , beyond measure, excessive, too great, too much . Lit. : quod autem satis est, eo quidquid accesserit nimium est, Cic. Fin. 5, 27, 81 : vitem coërcet, ne in omnes partes nimia fundatur, id. Sen. 15, 52 :…

ningit.opening: or , , v. n. Gr. νίφει; cf. nix, and v. Serv. Verg. A. 4, 250 , it snows . Lit. : ningit, Col. 11, 2, 31 ; Verg. G. 3, 367 : cum ninxerit caelestium molem mihi, Att. ap. Prisc. p. 882 P. (Trag. Rel. v. 101 Rib.).— In…

ningor.opening: ningo , a fall of snow , App. de Mundo, p. 61, 26.

ninguĭdus.opening: adj. ninguis , full of snow, snowy (post-class.): juga, Aus. Ep. 24, 68 : oppida, id. ib. 24, 124 : Boreas, Prud. Apophth. 729 .— Transf. , falling like snow : cibus, i. e. manna, Prud. Cath. 5, 97 .

ninguis.opening: kindr. with nix , snow (ante- and post-class.): albas descendere ningues, Lucr. 6, 736 (but id. 6, 964 , the correct read. is nives, v. Lachm. ad h. l.); so according to Lucil. ap. Charis. p. 71 P.; App. ap. Prisc. p.…

ningŭlus.opening: adj. dim. of noenus, from ne-oenus for unus , nobody : ningulus, nullus, ut Ennius lib. II.: qui ferro minitere atque in te ningulus ..., Paul. ex Fest. p. 177 Müll. (Ann. v. 133 Vahl.): ningulus, nullus. Marcius vates:…

Nī^nī^vē.opening: the ancient capital of Assyria , prob. near the mod. Nebbi Yunus , Aug. Civ. Dei , 16, 3; Vulg. Gen. 10, 11 ; Paul. Nol. Carm. 23, 168 ; Alcim. 4, 357 ; also called Ninus or Ninos, v. Ninus.—Hence, , , , the inhabitants…

Ninnius.opening: the name of a noble Campanian gens, Liv. 23, 8 .—So, L. Ninnius Quadratus, a tribune of the people , Cic. Att. 3, 23, 4 ; id. Sest. 31, 68 .— Ninnius Crassus, who translated the Iliad into Latin , Prisc. 865 P.; cf.…

Nī^nus.opening: , = Νινος , the son of Belus, the first king of Assyria, husband of Semiramis, and builder of Nineveh , Just. 1, 1, 7 sq. ; Curt. 3, 3, 16 : busta Nini, Ov. M. 4, 88 . — Another name of the city of Nineveh , Plin. 6,…

Nĭnўas.opening: or , , , son of Ninus and Semiramis , Just. 1, 1, 10 ; 1, 2, 11 .

Nĭŏba.opening: , and , , , = Νιόβη . The daughter of Tantalus, and wife of Amphion, king of Thebes, whose seven sons and seven daughters were slain by Apollo and Diana, because, on the strength of her numerous progeny, she triumphed…

Nĭphas.opening: , = Νιφάς (snow-storm), a Roman surname , Inscr. Grut. 278, 10 .

Nĭphātes.opening: , = Νιφάτης A part of the Mount Taurus range in Armenia , the mod. Ali-Dagh , etc., Verg. G. 3, 30 ; Hor. C. 2, 9, 20 ; Mel. 1, 15, 2 .— A river that rises in the same , Luc. 3, 245 ; Juv. 6, 409 .

Niphĕtus.opening: , = Νιφετός (snowstorm), a Roman surname , Inscr. Fabr. p. 516 , n. 243.

Niptra.opening: plur. , = Νίπτρα , water for washing , the title of a tragedy of Pacuvius, Cic. Tusc. 2, 21, 48 ; Gell. 13, 29, 3 ; v. the fragments in Trag. Rel. p. 90 sq. Rib.

Nīreus.opening: ( ), , , = Νίρευς , son of Charopus and Aglaia, the handsomest man among the Greeks before Troy , Hor. C. 3, 20, 15 ; id. Epod. 15, 22 ; Prop. 3, 16 (4, 17), 27; Ov. P. 4, 13, 16 ; Hyg. Fab. 113 and 270; Dict. Cret. 4,…

nis.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. s. v. callim, p. 47 Müll.

Nīsa.opening: a female proper name , Verg. E. 8, 26 .

nĭ-sĭ.opening: (archaic forms and , , v. Ritschl, Legis Rubriae pars superstes, Bonnae, 1851, and Rhein. Mus. tom. 8, p. 448 sq.), conj., if not, unless . In gen.: quid tu malum curas, Utrum crudum an coctum-edim? nisi tu mihi es…

Nĭsĭbis.opening: or , , , = Νίσιβις . A city in Mesopotamia , now Nisibin , Plin. 6, 13, 16, § 42 ; Tac. A. 15, 5 ; Amm. 25, 7, 9 ; 25, 8, 27 —Hence, , , , the inhabitants of Nisibis , Amm. 25, 8, 13 .— A city in Aria , Amm. 23, 6, 69 .

nīsus.opening: nitor , a pressing or resting upon or against, a pressure; a striving, exertion, labor, effort (mostly poet. ; nixus in good prose, v. h. v.): pedetentim et sedato nisu, a tread, step , Pac. ap. Cic. Tusc. 2, 21, 48 :…

Nīsus.opening: , = Νῖσος A king of Megara, father of Scylla, who, in order to gain the love of Minos, cut off her father's purple hair, on which the safety of his kingdom depended, whereupon Nisus was changed into a sparrow-hawk, and…

nitălōpĭces.opening: acc. plur. , , perh. Indian foxes , Jul. Val. Res Gest. Alex. M. 3, 17 .

nītēdŭla.opening: a kind of small red mouse, a dormouse , Cic. Sest. 33, 72 : cf.: nitedula mus agrestis rubeus, Serv. ad Verg. G. 1, 181 ; Arn. 2, 47 ( Hor. Ep. 1, 7, 29 , the common read. is volpecula, but Bentley's conjecture,…

nĭtĕfăcĭo.opening: v. a. niteofacio , to make shining (post-class.): ventus mare crispicans nitefacit, Gell. 18, 11, 3 : grato crinem nitefactus olivo, Juvenc. 1, 607 .

nĭtēla.opening: niteo , brightness, splendor (post-class.). Lit. : armorum nitela, Sol. 22, 5 .— Transf. That which shines or glitters, a glittering particle : nitelae pulveris, gold-dust, Sol. 23, 4 . — That which causes to shine, a…

nītella.opening: (contr from nitedula, q. v, sometimes written , but v. Lachm. ad Lucr. 3, 1015 ), a small mouse, a dormouse , Plin. 8, 57, 82, § 224 ; Mart. 5, 37, 8 ; Serv ad Verg. G. 1, 181 .

nītellīnus.opening: adj. nitella , of or belonging to a nitella or dormouse : color, the color of a dormouse : salix, Plin. 16, 37, 69, § 177 .

nĭtens.opening: shining, Part. and P a. , from niteo; v. niteo fin.

nītens.opening: pressing upon or against, Part. from nitor.

nĭtenter.opening: adv. , v niteo, P. a. fin .

nĭtĕo.opening: ( gen. plur nitentūm, Verg. Cir. 523 ), v. n. etym. dub.; cf. nix , to shine, look bright, glitter, glisten (cf., luceo, fulgeo splendeo). Lit. : placatumque nitet diffuso lumine caelum, Lucr. 1, 9 : luna potest solis…

nĭtesco.opening: v. inch. n. [niteo], to begin to shine or glitter, to shine, glitter ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : caelum nitescere, arbores frondescere, Enn. ap. Cic. Tusc. 1, 28, 69 (Trag. v. 192 Vahl.): exiguo qui…

nītĭbundus.opening: adj. nitor , pressing against, straining, striving (post-class.): mentium conspiratu tacito nitibundi, relying upon, Gell. 1, 11, 8 : pondus nitibundum, oppressive weight, weighty pressure, Sol. 25, 12 : caput, id. 27,…

nĭtĭdĭtas.opening: nitidus , splendor, beauty : formae, Att. ap. Non. 143, 29 (Trag. Rel. v. 254 Rib.).

nĭtĭdĭuscŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [nitidus], somewhat more shining (Plautin.): caput, Plaut. Ps. 1, 2, 84 .—Hence, adv. : , a little more finely, sprucely : ut curer, Plaut. Ps. 3, 1, 8 .

nĭtĭdo.opening: v. a. id. , to make bright or shining, to polish, smooth ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). In gen.: ferramenta detersa nitidentur, Col. 12, 3, 9 : post serraturam, plagam ferramentis acutis nitidemus, Pall. 3, 17, 1 :…

nĭtĭdŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [id.], somewhat spruce, rather trim : vidua nitidula, Sulp. Sev. Dial. 2, 8, 3 .

nĭtĭdus.opening: adj. niteo , shining, glittering, bright, polished, clear (class.; syn.: splendidus, lautus). Lit. : facite, sultis, nitidae ut aedes meae sint, Plaut. Stich. 1, 2, 8 : in picturis alios horrida, inculta ... contra…

Nitĭobrīges.opening: a people in Aquitanian Gaul, between the Garumna and the Liger, near the mod. Agen , Caes. B. G. 7, 7 ; 31 ; 35 ; 75; Sid. Ep. 8, 11 .

nītor.opening: ( inf. nitier, Lucr. 1, 1059 ; old form of the part. perf. : gnitus et gnixus a genibus prisci dixerunt, Paul. ex Fest. p. 96 Müll.), 3, v. dep. n. [from gnitor; root gnic- or gnig-; cf.: nico, conivere], to bear or…

nĭtor.opening: niteo , brightness, splendor, lustre, sheen . Lit. : nitor exoriens aurorae, Lucr. 4, 538 : diurnus, the daylight, Ov. H. 18, 78 : herbarum viridis, Lucr. 5, 783 : argenti et auri, Ov. P. 3, 4, 23 : eboris, Plin. 7, 15,…

nĭtrārĭa.opening: nitrum , a place where natron was dug or prepared , Plin. 31, 10, 46, § 109 (ib. saep.).

nĭtrātus.opening: adj. id. , mixed with natron : aqua, Col. 12, 55 ; Mart. 13, 17, 2 .

nī^trĕus.opening: adj. id. , made of natron, of soda : pulvis, Cael. Aur. Tard. 2, 7, 108 .

nitrĭon.opening: a plant, also called daphnoides, App. Herb. 58 .

nĭtrōsus.opening: adj. nitrum , full of natron : aquae frigidae genus nitrosum, Vitr. 8, 3 : lacus, Plin. 31, 10, 46, § 107 .

nĭtrum.opening: , = νίτρον , also called sal nitrum, native mineral alkali, native soda, natron; found chiefly in Media, Egypt, Thrace, and Macedonia, Plin. 31, 10, 46, § 106 : flos nitri, Vitr. 7, 11, 1 ; and used for washing with:…

nĭvālis.opening: adj. nix , of or belonging to snow, snowy, snow- . Lit. : nivalis dies, a snowy day, Liv. 21, 54, 7 : nivalia (sc. loca), Plin. 26, 8, 29, § 46 : Haemonia, Hor. C. 1, 37, 19 : venti, Plin. 2, 47, 48, § 126 : axis, the…

nĭvārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to snow : nivarium colum, a strainer filled with snow, through which generous wines were filtered , whereas the commoner sorts were merely passed through a linen cloth, filled with snow ,…

nĭvātus.opening: adj. id. , cooled with snow : potiones, Sen. Q. N. 4, 13, 10 : aqua, Petr. 31 ; Suet. Ner. 27 .

nīvens.opening: winking (cf. coniveo): niventibus oculis, v. l. ap. Petr. 115 , for umentibus.

nĭvesco.opening: v. inch. n. [nix], to become snow-white , Anth. Lat. tom. 2, p. 406 Burm.; Tert. Pall. 3 med.

nĭvĕus.opening: adj. id. , of or from snow, snowy, snow- ( poet. ) Lit. : aggeribus niveis informis, Verg. G. 3, 354 : aqua, cooled with snow , Mart. 12, 17, 6 ; cf. id. 14, 104 and 117: mons, covered with snow, Cat. 64, 240 .— Transf.…

nĭvĭfer.opening: adj. nix - fero , snow-bearing, covered with snow : niviferae valles, Salv. G. D. 6, 2 .

nĭvit.opening: v. impers. [nix], it snows; poet. transf. of a great quantity of missile weapons: sagittis, plumbo et saxis grandinat, nivit, Pac. ap. Non. 507, 27 (Trag. Rel. v. 4 Rib.).

Nīvŏmăgus.opening: a city of the Treveri, otherwise called Noviomagus, now Neumagen , Aus. Mos. 11 .

nĭvōsus.opening: adj. nix , full of snow, snowy : hiems gelida ac nivosa, Liv. 5, 13, 1 : tantum nivosae grandinis, id. 21, 59, 8 : Strymon, Ov. Tr. 5, 3, 22 : Scythia, id. H. 12, 27 : loca praegelida ac nivosa, Col. 2, 9, 7 : Pliadum…

nix.opening: cf. Gr. νίφα (acc.), snow; Lat. ningit, ninguit , snow. Lit. : Anaxagoras nivem nigram dixit esse, Cic. Ac. 2, 23, 72 : pars terrarum obriguit nive pruināque, id. N. D. 1, 10, 24 : miles nivibus pruinisque obrutus, Liv.…

nixābundus.opening: adj. nixor , striving to support one's self : illā deā, Jul. Val. Res Gest. Alex. M. 1, 11 .

nixor.opening: dep. n. [1. nitor], to lean or rest upon; to strive, endeavor ( poet. ). Lit. , Lucr. 6, 836 ; 3, 1001 : pars vulnere clauda retentat Nixantem (serpentem), Verg. A. 5, 279 Wagner N. cr. — Trop. , to depend upon :…

nixŭrĭo.opening: v. a. desid. [nixus, from nitor], to wish to lean or rest upon : nixurit qui niti vult et in conatu saepius aliquā re perpellitur, Nigid. 144, 20 .— Transf. , for parturio, to wish to bring forth : nixurio, φιλοτοκέω ,…

nixus.opening: 1. nitor , a pressure (the same as nisus, v. 2, nisus). Lit. : astra se nixu suo conglobata continent, revolution, course , * Cic. N. D. 2, 46, 117 . — Transf. , a striving, exertion, effort : hic ad summum non pervenit…

no.opening: v. n. νέω , to swim, float. Lit. : alter nare cupit: alter pugnare paratu'st, Enn. ap. Paul. ex Fest. p. 166 Müll. (Ann. v. 258 Vahl.): pueris, qui nare discunt, scirpea induitur ratis, Plaut. Aul. 4, 1, 9 ; cf. below,…

No.opening: an Egyptian city , perh. Alexandria; acc. to Bochart, Thebes , Hier. ad Ezech. 30, 14 .

Nōa.opening: (more freq.) , , = Νῶε , Noah : perfidus (corvus) Noae, Sedul. Carm. 1, 158 : arca Noë, Gromat. Vet. 373, 6; Tert. adv. Marc. Carm. 3, 42 ; Alcim. Avit. 4, 178 ; Vulg. Gen. 6, 8 ; 8, 1 al. — Fem., daughter of Zelophehad…

Nōbĭlĭor.opening: nobilis , a family name in the gens Fulvia, e. g. M. Fulvius Nobilior, the vanquisher of the Ætolians and the friend of Ennius , Liv. 37, 47 ; 39, 5 ; 40, 45 .

nōbĭlis.opening: (old collat. form : nobilem antiqui pro noto ponebant, et quidem per g litteram, ut Plautus in Pseudolo: peregrina facies videtur hominis atque ignobilis, et: oculis meis obviam ignobilis obicitur. Attius in Diomede:…

nōbĭlĭtas.opening: nobilis . Celebrity, fame, renown (very rare): eam nobilitatem amittundam video, Plaut. Mil. 4, 8, 14 : praedicationem nobilitatemque despicere, Cic. Arch. 11, 26 : repentina, Liv. 1, 34 ; cf.: aliquem nobilitate…

nōbĭlĭto.opening: v. a. nobilis . To make known, to render famous or renowned : disciplinā militari nobilitatus est, Nep. Iphic. 1, 1 : poëtae post mortem nobilitari volunt, Cic. Tusc. 1, 15, 34 : spectata ac nobilitata virtus, id. Fl.…

nŏcenter.opening: adv. , v. noceo, P. a. fin .

nŏcentĭa.opening: nocens , guilt, transgression (post-class.): deus innocentiae magister, nocentiae judex, Tert. Apol. 40 ; id. adv. Marc. 2, 13 .

nŏcĕo.opening: ( inf. pres. pass. nocerier, Plaut. Curc. 2, 3, 73 ; gen. plur. nocentūm, Ov. P. 1, 8, 19 ; perf. subj. noxit: ne boa noxit, Lucil. ap. Paul. ex Fest. s. v. Fama, p. 360 Müll.; Fronto ad M. Caesarem, 3, 13 Mai.), v. n.…

nŏcīvus.opening: adj. noceo , hurtful, injurious, noxious (not ante-Aug., and very rare), Phaedr. 1, 28, 3 : pecori nociva, Plin. 20, 2, 6, § 12 ; Vulg. 1 Tim. 6, 9 .

noctanter.opening: adv. nox , by night , Cassiod. Hist. Eccl. 6, 31 .

noctesco.opening: v. n. inch. [id.], to draw towards night, to grow dark : omnia noctescunt, Furius ap. Non. 145, 11 ; and Gell. 18, 11, 3 (where the word is censured).

noctĭcŏla.opening: nox-colo , fond of the night : lndus, who, on account of the excessive heat of the day, is fond of the night, Prud. Ham. 636 .

noctĭcŏlor.opening: adj. nox-color , nightcolored, black : nocticolor Memnon (as being an Ethiopian), Laev. ap. Gell. 19, 7, 6 : Styx, Aus. Monos. de Diis, 11.

noctĭfer.opening: nox-fero, the nightbringer , the evening-star , Cat. 62, 7 ; Calp. Ecl. 5, 121 .

noctĭlūca.opening: nox-luceo , that shines by night; hence, The moon : Luna quod sola lucet noctu: itaque ea dicta noctiluca in Palatio; nam ibi noctu lucet templum, Varr. L. L. 5, § 68 Müll.: canentes Rite crescentem face noctilucam,…

noctĭsurgĭum.opening: nox-surgo , a getting up in the night : nyctegresia, quasi noctisurgium, Paul. ex Fest. s. v. egretus, p. 78 Müll.

noctĭvăgus.opening: adj. nox-vagus; cf. Quint. 1, 5, 68 , night-wandering; that wanders about by night ( poet. ): noctivagae faces caeli, Lucr. 5, 1191 : currus (sc. Phoebes), Verg. A. 10, 216 : deus, i. e. sleep, Stat. Th. 10, 158 : iter,…

noctĭvĭdus.opening: adj. nox-video , night-seeing; that sees by night; of the night-owl, Mart. Cap. 6, § 571 .

noctŭa.opening: nox , a night-owl, an owl , a bird sacred to Minerva: noctua, quod noctu canit ac vigilat, Varr. L. L. 5, § 76 Müll.; Paul. ex Fest. pp. 174 and 175 ib.; Plaut. Men. 4, 2, 90 : noctuarum dimicatio, Plin. 10, 17, 19, §…

Noctŭa.opening: a Roman surname : Q. Caedicius Noctua, a consul with M. Valerius Corvinus A. U. C. 465.

noctŭābundus.opening: adj. noctu , having travelled all night (cf. noctivagus): noctuabundus ad me venit cum epistulā tuā tabellarius, Cic. Att. 12, 1, 2 .

noctŭīnus.opening: adj. 1. noctua , of or belonging to night-owls : noctuini oculi, owls' eyes, Plaut. Curc. 1, 3, 35 .

Noctulĭus.opening: a deity of the Brixians , Inscr. Spon. Miscell. Antiq. p. 115; Inscr. Murat. 98, 4 .

noctūlūcus.opening: nox-luceo , watching, waking , or seeing at night , Varr. L. L. 5, 19, § 99 Speng.

nocturnālis.opening: adj. nox , nocturnal (post-class.): cucullus, Sid. Ep. 7, 16 : habitatio, Alcim. Ep. 33 .

nocturnus.opening: adj. from the adv. noctu, analog. to diurnus from diu , of or belonging to the night, nocturnal (class.): labores diurnos nocturnosque suscipere, Cic. Sen. 23, 82 ; opp. diurnus, id. Mil. 3, 9 : nocturnum praesidium…

noctūvĭgĭlus.opening: ( ), , adj. nox-vigilo , night-watching : Venus, Plaut. Curc. 1, 3, 40 .

nŏcŭus.opening: adj. noceo , hurtful, injurious, noxious (very rare), Ov. Hal. 128 ; Ser ib. Comp. 114 .

nōdābĭlis.opening: adj. nodo , knotty (late Lat.), Vict. Tunon. de Poenit. 3.

nōdāmen.opening: id. , a knotting, knot : lori, Paul. Nol. Carm. 26, 593 .

nōdātĭo.opening: id. , knottiness, nodosity : propter nodationis duritiem, Vitr. 2, 9, 7 .

nōdātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from nodo.

nodĭa.opening: or , , , a plant, also called herba mularis, Plin. 24, 19, 115, § 175 .

Nodīnus.opening: a rivulet near Rome, mentioned in prayers , otherwise unknown, Cic. N. D. 3, 20, 52 .

nōdo.opening: v. a. nodus , to furnish or fill with knots . Lit. : ferula nodata, Plin. 13, 22, 42, § 123 : cornus nodata, id. 16, 38, 73, § 186 .— Transf. , to tie in a knot, to knot , Cato, R. R. 32, 2 : crines nodantur in aurum,…

nōdōsĭtas.opening: nodosus , knottiness, nodosity : tortuosissima et implicatissima nodositas, Aug. Conf. 2, 10 .

nōdōsus.opening: adj. nodus , full of knots, knotty (syn. geniculatus). Lit. : stipes, Ov. H. 10, 101 : robur, Val. Fl. 8, 298 : lina, nets, Ov. M. 3, 153 ; so, plagae, id. F. 6, 110 : vitis, Juv. 8, 247 : ossa, the bones of the neck,…

Nōdōtus.opening: ( ), , , a deity who presided over corn, and brought it as far as the knots in the stalk : praefecerunt ergo ... geniculis nodisque culmorum deum Nodutum, Aug. Civ. Dei , 4, 8; Arn. 4, 131 .

nōdŭlus.opening: dim. nodus , a little knot , Plin. 21, 5, 13, § 26 : capilli, App. M. 3, p. 139, 13 .

nōdus.opening: for gnodus; Sanscr. root gadh-, gandh-, grasp; cf. Gr. Χανδάνω, hold; γνάθος, jaw; Lat. pre-hend-o; Germ. Knoten; Engl. knot , a knot (cf. nexus). Lit. : nodus vinculumque, Cic. Univ. 4 : necte tribus nodis ternos,…

Nōē.opening: , = Νῶε (Hebr. ), Noah , Sedul. Carm. 1, 174 , Vulg. Matt. 24, 37 ; 38 ; id. Gen. 6, 13 ; v. Noa.

nœgēum.opening: ( ), , , a garment trimmed with purple; acc. to others, a white upper garment : noegeum quidam amiculi genus praetextum purpura; quidam candidum ac perlucidum, quasi a navo (nauco), quod putamen quorundam pomorum est…

nŏĕrus.opening: adj. , = νοερός , gifted with understanding , Tert. adv. Val. 20 .

Nōla.opening: a city of remote antiquity in Campania, founded by the Ausonians, afterwards conquered by the Tuscans, and colonized by the Chalcidians, still called Nola , Liv. 9, 28 ; 23, 14 ; Plin. 3, 5, 9, § 63 ; Cic. Brut. 3, 12 ;…

nŏla.opening: a little bell : jusserat (canem) in rabido gutture ferre nolam, Avien. Fab. 7, 8 dub. (al. notam).

nōlenter.opening: , a false read. for nocenter, Tert. Apol. 14 .

Nolĭba.opening: a city in Tarraconian Spain , Liv. 35, 22 .

nōlo.opening: (nevis for non vis, Plaut. Trin. 5, 2, 32 Brix ad loc.; id. Most. 3, 2, 75 ; id. Poen. 5, 2, 119 al. : nevolt for non vult, id. Trin. 2, 2, 80 ; id. Most. 1, 2, 29 ; Titin. ap. Non. 144, 7 ; v. Don. ad Ter. Eun. 3, 3, 2…

nōluntas.opening: nolo , unwillingness : noluntas ab eo quod nolumus, sicut voluntas ab eo, quod volumus, Placid. Gloss. ap. Mai. Auct. class. 6, p. 568, a.

Nŏmaeus.opening: adj., of or belonging to the city of Nomæ, in Sicily : viri, Sil. 14, 266 .

Nŏmăs.opening: , = Νομάς (pasturing flocks); in plur. , pastoral people that wander about with their flocks , Nomads , Plin. 5, 3, 2, § 22 .—Hence, In partic., the (wandering) Numidians , Verg. A. 4, 320 ; cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 173…

nŏmē.opening: , = νομή , a corroding sore, eating ulcer : nome intestina, Plin. 31, 8, 44, § 97 .—Usu. in plur. : , , Plin. 20, 9, 36, § 93 : cohibere nomas, id. 26, 14, 87, § 144 ; 23, 4, 46, § 91 : sanare, id. 30, 13, 39, § 115 :…

nōmen.opening: (archaic form of gen. sing. NOMINVS, S. C. de Bacch. Corp. Inscr. Lat. 196, 8), for gnōmen, from root gno, whence gnosco, nosco, co-gnosco , a name, appellation (syn. vocabulum). Lit. : nomen est, quod unicuique…

nōmenclātĭo.opening: nomen-calo , a calling by name (very rare). Of persons, Q. Cic. Petit. Cons. 11, 41 .— Of things: vitium, a list, catalogue, Col. 3, 2, 31 .

nōmenclātor.opening: ( , Mart. 10, 30, 23 ; Suet. Aug. 19 ; id. Calig. 41 ; id. Claud. 34 ), , id. , one who calls a person or thing by name, a nomenclator; among the Romans, a slave who attended his master in canvassing and on similar…

nōmenclātūra.opening: id. , a calling by name, a list of names, nomenclature (Plinian), Plin. H. N. 3 prooem. § 2; id. 21, 9, 28, § 52 .

Nōmentum.opening: a city in the country of the Sabines , now Mentana , Liv. 1, 38 ; 4, 22 ; 32 ; Verg. A. 6, 773 .— Hence, , , adj., of or belonging to Nomentum : ager, Plin. 14, 4, 5, § 48 : vina, Mart. 13, 119 : via, the road leading…

nŏmĭmus.opening: adj. , = νόμιμος , lawful, legitimate , = legitimus: PATER NOMIMVS, Inscr. Orell. 5059 .

nōmĭnālis.opening: adj. nomen , of or belonging to a name, nominal (ante- and postclass.): gentilitas, Varr. L. L. 8, § 4 Müll.— Subst. : , , , the day on which a child received its name, the name-day , Tert. Idol. 16 .—Hence, adv. : , by…

nōmĭnātim.opening: adv. nomino , by name, expressly, one by one, in detail (class.): ibi ego dicam quidquid inerit nominatim, Plaut. Rud. 4, 4, 90 : aliquem nominatim excipere, Cic. Att. 11, 7, 2 : non nominatim, sed generatim, id. ib.…

nōmĭnātĭo.opening: nomino , a naming . * In gen.: consuetudo nominationum, Vitr. 6, 7, 7 .— In partic. In rhet. lang., a figure of speech, whereby a thing which has no name, or an unsuitable one, receives an appropriate name , Auct. Her.…

nōmĭnātīvus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to naming, nominative; in gram.: casus nominativus, the nominative case, Varr. L. L. 10, § 23 Müll.; Quint. 1, 7, 3 ; 7, 9, 13 ; 8, 3, 46 et saep.

nōmĭnātor.opening: id. , a nominator (in jurid. Lat.): nominatores magistratuum, Dig. 27, 8, 1 ; so ib. 27, tit. 7 .

nōmĭnātōrĭus.opening: adj. nominator , of or belonging to naming, naming, containing names (in jurid. Lat.): nominatorii breves, Cod. Th. 1, 10, 8; 11, 28, 3: pericula, having a name, named, Tert. Anim. 13 .

nōmĭnātus.opening: nomino , a naming, a name; in gram., a noun (perh. only in Varr.), Varr. L. L. 8, § 52 Müll.; so id. ib. § 63: quod ad nominatuum analogiam pertinet, id. ib. 9, 52 , § 95; id. ib. 10, 1 .

nōmĭnĭto.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to name (ante- and post-class.): suscipere hunc motum, quem sensum nominitamus, Lucr. 3, 352 ; 4, 51 ; 6, 424 ; Inscr. Murat. 1522, 2 .

nōmĭno.opening: v. a. nomen , to call by name, to name, to give a name to (esp. after, for a person or thing; cf.: appello, voco, dico). In gen.: quae (navis) nunc nominatur nomine Argo, Enn. ap. Auct. Her. 2, 22, 34, 26 : Chaldaei,…

Nŏmĭo.opening: a hymn to Apollo , Paeanem aut Nomionem citarimus, Cic. de Or. 1, 59, 251 B. and K.

nŏmisma.opening: ( ), (also , Ven. Vit. S. Martin. 2, 338), , = νόμισμα , a piece of money, a coin (not ante-Aug.). Lit. In gen.: acceptos, regale nomisma, Philippos, Hor. Ep. 2, 1, 234 : largae nomismata mensae, Mart. 12, 62, 11 :…

Nŏmĭus.opening: and , , and , , , = Νόμιος and Νομίων , the Pasturer , a surname of Apollo, because he tended the flocks of Admetus (cf. Verg. G. 3, 2 ); acc. to Cic. N. D. 3, 23, 57 , it is from νόμος , lex, and denotes the fourth…

nŏmos.opening: m. (and nŏmus), = νομός . A district, province, nome : Thebais dividitur in praefecturas oppidorum, quos nomos vocant, duodecim, Plin. 5, 9, 9, § 49 : substituunt alios nomos, ut Heroopoliten, id. ib. § 50.— In music, a…

nōn.opening: (old collat. forms and , cf. Lachm. ad Lucr. tom. 2, p. 149 sq.: noenum pro non Lucilius lib. XXX.: sed tamen hoc dicas, quid est, si noenu molestum'st. Varro Epistola ad Fusium: si hodie noenum venis, cras quidem,…

Nōna.opening: , = Νῶνα , one of the three Fates : Tria nomina Parcarum sunt, Nona, Decuma, Morta, Caes. Vindex ap. Gell. 3, 16, 11 ; Varr. ap. Gell. 3, 16, 10 .

Nōnācris.opening: , = Νώνακρις , a mountain in Arcadia, at the foot of which lay a city of the same name, and in which the Styx had its source , Vitr. 8, 3, 16 ; Plin. 2, 103, 106, § 131 ; 4, 6, 10, § 21 .— Hence, , , adj., Nonacrian ,…

Nōnae.opening: nonus , the fifth day in every month of the year, except March, May, July, and October, in which it was the seventh; the nones , so called because it was the ninth day before the ides, Varr. L. L. 6, § 28 Müll.: o Nonae…

nōnāgēnārĭus.opening: adj. nonageni , that contains or consists of ninety . In gen.: nonagenarius motus stellae Martis, ninety degrees distant from the sun, Plin. 2, 15, 12, § 60 : fistula, made of a sheet of lead ninety inches wide, Front.…

nōnāgēni.opening: ( gen. pl. nonagenūm, Front. Aquaed. 61 ), adj. distr . [nonaginta], ninety each : porticus ascenduntur nonagenis gradibus omnes, Plin. 36, 13, 19, § 88 .

nōnāgēsĭmus.opening: adj. ord. [id.], the ninetieth : Isocrates quarto et nonagesimo anno scripsisse dicitur, Cic. Sen. 5, 13 .

nōnāgessis.opening: nonaginta-as , a sum of ninety asses , Prisc. 1356 P.; Beda de Num. tom. 1, p. 101.

nōnāgĭes.opening: or , adv. id. , ninety times : nonagies sestertium, ninety times a hundred thousand sesterces, Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 70, § 163 .

nōnāgintā.opening: num. adj., ninety : nonaginta annos natus, Cic. Sen. 10, 34 ; Aus. Ep. 5, 5 .

Nōnālis.opening: adj. Nonae , of or belonging to the nones : Nonalia sacra, offerings made at the Capitol on the nones, Varr. L. L. 6, § 28 Müll.

nōnānus.opening: adj. nona, sc. legio , of or belonging to the ninth legion : miles nonanus, Tac. A. 1, 23 .— Absol. : , , , a soldier of the ninth legion , Tac. A. 1, 30 ; 14, 38 .

nōnārĭus.opening: adj. nonus , of or belonging to the ninth hour .—As subst. : , , (sc. meretrix), a public prostitute (so called because not allowed to show herself before the ninth hour of the day), Pers. 1, 133 .

non-dum.opening: adv., not yet : nondum sex menses, Plaut. Pers. 1, 3, 57 : nondum centum et decem anni sunt, cum, etc., Cic. Off. 2, 21, 75 : nondum Voconiā lege latā, id. Rep. 3, 10, 17 ; id. Div. 2, 6, 16 : nondum Ilium et arces…

noneolae.grammar: vocantur papillae, quae ex faucibus caprarum suppendent
noneolae.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. pp. 174 and 175 Müll.

nongēnārĭus.opening: or , , adj. nongeni, nongenti , containing nine hundred , Prisc. 1355 P.

nongēni.opening: num. adj. distr . [nongenti], nine hundred each , Prisc. 1353 P.

nongenti.opening: ( , Col. 5, 2, 7 ), ae, a, adj. card., nine hundred : ab uno ad nongenta ... a mille ad nongenta milia, Varr. R. R. 3, 49 : Falcidius emerat HS. nongentis milibus, Cic. Fl. 37, 91 .— In sing. : , , , one of nine hundred…

nōnĭes.opening: adv. nonus , nine times : quinquies, sexies, septies, octies, nonies, decies, Not. Tir. p. 100 ; Inscr. Murat. 451, 1 .

nōnĭgēsĭmus.opening: or , , adj. ord. , for noningentesimus, the nine hundredth , Prisc. de Pond. p. 1353 .

nōningentēsĭmus.opening: (or , Aur. Vict. Caes. 15, 4 ), a, um, adj. ord., the nine hundredth , Prisc. de Pond p. 1353 .

nōningentĭes.opening: or , adv. ( ), nine hundred times : noningenties trigesies septies mille, Vitr. 1, 6 .

Nōnĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens. So M. Nonius Suffenas, Cic. Att. 6, 1, 13 .— Nonius Marcellus, a Roman grammarian, whose treatise De Proprietate Sermonis is extant in a very mutilated form .

non-nĕ.opening: adv. , the interrogative non, expecting an affirmative answer, not? In a direct interrogation: nonne ego hic sto? Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 250 : nonne animadvertis? Cic. N. D. 3, 37, 89 : te dejectum debeo intellegere, etiamsi…

non-nēmo.opening: Some, several, many a one , Cic. Mur. 39, 84 ; id. Pis. 5, 10 al. — Some one, a certain person , Cic. Cat. 4, 5, 10 .

non-nullus.opening: (or written separately, , Verg. A. 11, 725 ), a, um, adj., some, several : non nullumst periculum, Plaut. Capt. 1, 1, 23 ; Ter. Ad. 2, 1, 68 : esse nonnullo se Caesaris beneficio affectum, Caes. B. G. 7, 37, 4 :…

non-numquam.opening: or , adv., sometimes; opp. numquam, Cic. Vatin. 2, 5 ; with aliquando, id. Fam. 5, 8, 2 : nonnumquam interdiu, saepius noctu, Caes. B. G. 1, 8 fin.

nonnus.opening: , and , , A monk; a nun , Hier. Ep. 117 , n. 6; id. ib. 22 , n. 16.— A tutor , Inscr. Orell. 4670 .

non-nusquam.opening: adv., in some places , Plin. 14, 19, 24, § 120 : silices quibusdam in locis rubentes, nonnusquam vero et albi, id. 36, 22, 49, § 168 ; Gell. 13, 24, 31 .

nōnuncĭum.grammar: et sescunciam quod magistri ludi appellant, significat dodrantem et dimidium teruncium, quod singula sescuncia uncia et dimidium sit

nōnus.opening: adj. ord. [for novenus, from novem], the ninth : terra nona, Cic. Rep. 6, 18, 18 : accedes opera agro nona Sabino, Hor. S. 2, 7, 118 .— Subst. : , , (Sc. hora.) The ninth hour of the day , i. e. the third before sunset,…

nōnus-dĕcĭmus.opening: adj. ord., the nineteenth (the class. undevicesimus): nonodecimo aetatis anno, Tac. A. 13, 16 ; id. Or. 34 fin. ; Inscr. Grut. 449, 7 .

nōnussis.opening: novem-as , nine asses , Varr. L. L. 5, § 169 Müll.

Nōra.opening: , = Νῶρα . A hill-fort between Lycaonia and Cappadocia , Nep. Eum. 5, 3 .— A very ancient city in Sardinia , now Nori .—Hence, , , adj., of or belonging to Nora , Cic. Scaur. 1, 4 , c.—In plur. : , , , the inhabitants…

Norba.opening: a city of Latium , now called Norma , Liv. 2, 34 .— Hence, , , adj., of or belonging to Norba, Norban : ager, Liv. 8, 19 .—In plur. : , , , the Norbans , Liv. 8, 1 ; 27, 10 ; Plin. 3, 5, 9, § 64 .— , , , a Roman surname…

Nŏrēïa.opening: a town in Noricum , now prob. Neumarkt , Caes. B. G. 1, 5 ; Plin. 3, 19, 23, § 131 .

Nōrĭcum.opening: a country lying between the Danube and the Alps , Tac. H. 1, 70 .—Hence, , , adj., of or belonging to Noricum, Norican : ager, Caes. B. G. 1, 5 : provincia, Tac. A. 2, 63 : ferrum, Plin. 34, 14, 41, § 145 ; cf. Ov. M.…

norma.opening: for gnorima (cf. Gr. γνώριμος); root, gno-; cf. gnarus, nosco , a square , employed by carpenters, masons, etc., for making right angles (cf. regula). Lit. : anguli ad normam respondentes, Vitr. 7, 3 ; 9, 2 ; Plin. 36,…

normālis.opening: adj. norma , made according to the square : normalis angulus, a right angle, Quint. 11, 3, 141 : virgula, a square, Manil. 2, 289 : rigores, Aggen. ap. Comm. in Frontin. p. 53 Goes.—Hence, adv. : , according to the…

normātĭo.opening: id. , a fashioning or adjusting according to the square , Auct. de Limit. p. 217 Goes.

normātūra.opening: id. , a fashioning or adjusting according to the square , Innocent. de Cas. Lit. p. 221 Goes.

normātus.opening: norma , adjusted according to the square : normatus ad perpendiculum, rectangular, Col. 3, 13, 12 .

normo.opening: v. a. id. , to square, to set by the square : basis ad perpendiculum normata, Col. 3, 13, 12 .

normŭla.opening: dim. id. , a small square : norma, normula, Not. Tir. p. 119 ; Bretto, 2 Geometr. p. 1216.

Nortĭa.opening: or , , , a goddess of the Volsinii , prob. Fortuna : quam alii Sortem asserunt, Nemesimque nonnulli, Tychenque quam plures, aut Nortiam, Mart. Cap. 1, § 88 : in templo Nortiae Etruscae Deae, Liv. 7, 3, 7 : si Nortia…

nōs.opening: , etc., the plur. of ego, q. v. ( gen. nostrōrum and nostrārum, for nostrum: nemo nostrorum, Plaut. Poen. 4, 2, 39 : nostrarum quisquam, Ter. Eun. 4, 4, 11 ) [cf. Sanscr. nāu; Gr. νῶϊ ], we : nos, nos, dico aperte,…

noscentĭa.opening: nosco , knowledge , Symm. Ep. 4, 9 ; 6, 11 dub. (al. notitia).

noscĭbĭlis.opening: adj. id. , knowable (eccl. Lat.), Tert. ad Scapul. 2 fin. ; Aug. Trin. 9, 5, 12 .

noscĭto.opening: v. freq. a. nosco , to know, to recognize (not in Cic. or Cæs.). Lit. : noscito hanc, nam videor, nescio ubi, me vidisse prius, Plaut. Ep. 4, 1, 14 : aliquem facie, Liv. 22, 6 : noscitabatur tamen in tantā deformitate,…

nosco.opening: (old form, GNOSCO, GNOVI, GNOTVM, acc. to Prisc. p. 569 P.; inf. pass. GNOSCIER, S. C. de Bacch.; cf. GNOTV, cognitu, Paul. ex Fest. p. 96 Müll.: GNOT (contr. for gnovit) οἶδεν, ἐπιγινώσκει ; GNOTV, γνῶσιν, διάγνωσιν ,…

nŏsŏcŏmīum.opening: , = νοσοκομεῖον , a hospital, infirmary , Cod. Just. 1, 2, 19 ; 22 ; Hier. Ep. 30, 2 .

nŏsŏcŏmus.opening: , = νοσοκόμος , an attendant on the sick, a sick-nurse , Jul. Ep. Nov. c. 111, § 410; c. 115, § 452.

noster.opening: ( gen. sing. f. nostrāï, Vel. Long. p. 2222 P.; gen. plur. nostrum, Plaut. Men. 1, 2, 25 ; v. infra .), pron. poss. [nos], our, our own; ours, of us . In gen. For the poss. gen. of the first person : nostra omnis lis…

Nostĭmus.opening: , = Νόστιμος (returned = redux), name of a Roman slave , Inscr. Don. 427, 18 .

Nostĭus.opening: name of a Roman gens.— Hence, , , , name of a Roman freedman : L. Nostius Zoilus, Cic. Fam. 13, 46 .

nostras.opening: (old form of the nom. sing . nostratis, Cass. Hem. ap. Prisc. p. 943 P.), adj. noster , of our country, native : arma nostratia, Cato ap. Prisc. p. 943 P.: verba nostratia, Cic. Fam. 2, 11, 1 : mirifice capior facetiis,…

nostrātim.opening: adv. nostras; cf. tuatim , in our manner : tuatim Plautus in Amphit. (2, 1, 4): jam tuatim facis: ubi Sisenna, ut nostratim. Significat autem tuo more, Charis. p. 196 P.

Nostos.opening: , = Νόστος (return), name of a Roman slave , Inscr. Fabr. p. 194 , n. 41.

nŏta.opening: nosco , a mark, sign, note (cf.: signum, insigne, indicium): nota alias significat signum; ut in pecoribus, tabulis, libris, litterae singulae aut binae, alias ignominiam, Paul. ex Fest. p. 174 Müll. (v. in the foll.).…

nŏtābĭlis.opening: adj. nota , noteworthy, distinguished, remarkable, extraordinary, memorable, notable (not freq. till the Aug. per.; in Cic. perh. only once; in Cæs. not at all). Prop.: exitus, * Cic. Fam. 5, 12, 5 : rara et notabilis…

nŏtācŭlum.opening: noto , a mark, sign : notaculum corporis, Min. Fel. 31, 8 .

nŏtārĭus.opening: adj. nota , of or belonging to writing in cipher or short-hand writing (post-Aug.).—Only as subst. , , A short-hand writer, stenographer (syn. actuarius), Plin. Ep. 3, 5, 15 ; Quint. 7, 2, 24 ; Mart. 5, 51, 2 ; 14, 208…

nŏtātĭo.opening: noto , a marking, noting. In gen.: tabellarum, i. e. the marking of the voting-tablets with wax of different colors, Cic. Clu. 47, 130 .— In partic. The inflicting of disgrace by the nota censoria; v. nota, II. B. 2.:…

nŏtātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from noto.

nōtesco.opening: v. inch. n. [1. notus], to become known ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): notescatque magis mortuus atque magis, Cat. 68, 47 : nec minus haec nostri notescet fama sepulchri, Prop. 2, 13, 37 (3, 5, 21 M.): malis…

nŏthus.opening: adj. , = νόθος , spurious, not genuine . Lit. Of persons, illegitimate, bastard, born out of wedlock (but of a known father; contra, spurius, of an unknown father : legitimus, born in wedlock ): nothum qui non sit…

nŏtĭa.opening: , = νοτία , a precious stone, said to fall with the rain, also called ombria, Plin. 37, 10, 65, § 176 .— A plant , Plin. 24, 19, 115, § 175 .

nŏtĭālis.opening: adj. 2. notus , southern (post-class.): nubila, Avien. Arat. 550 .

nōtĭfĭco.opening: v. a. 1. notusfacio , to make known (perh. only ante- and post-class.): genus alicui, Pompon. ap. Non. 144, 24 : res est notificata satis, Poët. Lat. Min. t. 6, p. 383 Wernsd.

nōtĭo.opening: nosco , a becoming acquainted, a making one's self acquainted with a person (syn.: cognitio, perceptio, notitia). Lit. * In gen.: quid tibi hanc aditiost? quid tibi hanc notiost, inquam, amicam meam? Plaut. Truc. 2, 7,…

nŏtĭon.opening: a plant, otherwise called cucumis silvaticus, App. Herb. 113 .

nōtĭtĭa.opening: ( gen. sing . notitiāï, Lucr. 2, 124 .—Collat. form , Lucr. 5, 182 ; 1047 ; Vitr. 6 prooem.), 1. notus , a being known, celebrity, note, fame . Lit. (very rare): hi propter notitiam sunt intromissi, Nep. Dion. 9, 4 :…

Notium.opening: a city and promontory near Colophon, in Ionia , Liv. 37, 26 ; 38, 39 ; Plin. 5, 29, 31, § 116 .

nŏtĭus.opening: adj. , = νότιος , southern : notia sidera, Manil. 1, 436 ; so, piscis, id. 1, 427 : polus, Hyg. Astron. 1, 5 ; 4, 11 . According to Pliny, the Tyrrhene Sea was called by some Greek writers Mare Notium, Plin. 3, 5, 10, §…

nŏto.opening: v. a. nota , to mark, to designate with a mark (syn.: signo, designo). Lit. : tabellam cerā, Cic. Verr. 2, 2, 32, § 79 : ungue genas, Ov. Am. 1, 7, 50 : pueri rubor ora notavit, id. M. 4, 329 : rugis uterum, id. A. A.…

nōtor.opening: (collat. form † , v. infra ), , nosco , one who knows a person or thing, a voucher, witness , = cognitor (postAug.): qui notorem dat ignotus est, Sen. Ep. 39, 1 ; Petr. 92 ; Sen. Apoc. med. ; NOTOS (i. e. notor)…

nōtōrĭus.opening: adj. notor , pointing out, making known (post-class.); only subst. , , A notice, advice, intelligence, news : quod notoriā tuā intimāsti, Gall. ap. Treb. Claud. 17 : qui falsam de me notoriam pertulerat, information,…

nŏtŭla.opening: dim. nota , a little mark , Mart. Cap. 1, § 66 .

Nŏtus.opening: and , , Νότος , = auster, the south wind . Lit. : tres Notus hibernas immensa per aequora noctes Vexit me violentus aquā, Verg. A. 6, 355 : madidis Notus evolat alis, Ov. M. 1, 264 : udus, Hor. Epod. 10, 19 :…

nŏvācŭla.opening: novo , a sharp knife . Lit. : cutem raporum novaculā decerpere, Col. 12, 56, 1 ; Plin. 22, 23, 47, § 99 .— Esp. A razor : ut ex novaculā comperistis, tonsor est, Petr. 103 : aream (capitis) novaculā radere, Cels. 6, 4 :…

nŏvālis.opening: adj. novus , in agriculture, that is ploughed anew or for the first time : ager restibilis, qui restituitur ac reseritur quotquot annis: contra qui intermittitur, a novando novalis, Varr. L. L. 5, § 39 Müll.; cf. id.…

nŏvāmen.opening: novo , an innovation (post-class.), Tert. adv. Marc. 1, 20 .

Novānensis vīcus.opening: a village on the Via Appia, not far from Calatia , Inscr. Marin. Fratr. Arv. p. 390.

Nŏvāni.opening: novus , colonists, immigrants, new residents , Inscr. Orell. 101 ; Inscr. Grut. 1022, 12 .

Nŏvātĭāni.opening: the followers of Novatius of Carthage, Novatians, a sect of Christians , Lact. 4, 30, 10 ; Cod. 16, 5, 59 al.

Nŏvātilla.opening: a niece of Seneca the philosopher , Sen. Cons. ad Helv. 18, 7 .

nŏvātĭo.opening: novo , a renewing, renovation (post-class.). Lit. , Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 1 : pudendorum, i. e. shaving, Arn. 5, 182 .— Transf. , a renewal or change of a bond or other evidence of debt : novatio est prioris debiti in…

nŏvātor.opening: id. , a renewer, restorer (post-class.): verborum, i. e. who brings obsolete words again into use, Gell. 1, 15, 18 : stirpis Anniae, Aus. Ep. 16, 32 .

nŏvātrix.opening: novator , she who renews or changes : rerum, Ov. M. 15, 252 .

nŏvātus.opening: novo , a renewing, changing, change (late Lat.), Aus. Idyll. 14, 39 .

nŏvellaster.opening: adj. novellus , rather new : vinum novellastrum, Marc. Emp. 8 .

nŏvellētum.opening: 1. novellus , a place planted with young trees or vines, a nursery-garden (post-class.), Dig. 25, 1, 6 ; cf.: novelletum, νεόφυτον, νεοφυτεῖον , Gloss. Philox.

nŏvellĭtas.opening: id. , newness, novelty (post-class.), Tert. Anim. 28 ; id. adv. Prax. 2 .

nŏvello.opening: v. a. id. , to till new fields, to set out new vines (post-Aug.). Lit. : edixit ne quis in Italiā novellaret, Suet. Dom. 7 .— Trop. : vitam novellantes Deo, dedicating, renewing by devotion, Paul. Nol. Carm. 21, 659 .

nŏvellus.opening: adj. dim. [novus], young, new (esp. freq. in econom. lang.): capra, Varr. R. R. 2, 3 : juvenci, id. ib. 1, 20 : boves, Col. 6, 1, 3 : sues, Plin. 11, 37, 84, § 211 : vineae, Varr. R. R. 1, 31, 1 ; cf.: arbor et novella…

Nŏvellus.opening: a Roman surname : Cn. et L. Gavilii Novelli, Aquileienses, Liv. 41, 5, 1 (but Gronov. regards it as adj., new colonists of Aquileia; cf. Liv. 40, 34, 2 ).

nŏvem.opening: num. adj. card . [kindred to Sanscr. navan; Gr. ἐννέα ; Germ. neun; Engl. nine], nine : novem orbibus, Cic. Rep. 6, 17, 17 : sermo in novem et libros et dies distributus, id. Q. Fr. 3, 5, 1 : milia passuum decem novem,…

Nŏvember.opening: and , , adj. , with or without mensis [novem], the ninth month of the old Roman year (which began with March), November : mense Octobri fecimus: Novembris reliquus erat, Cato ap. Prisc. p. 696 P.: Calendis Novembribus,…

nŏvēnārĭus.opening: adj. novem , consisting of nine : numerus, Varr. L. L. 9, § 86 Müll.: natura, id. ib. ; cf. Macr. Somn. Scip. 2, 2 ; Aus. Idyll. 11 : sulcus, three feet in breadth and three in depth, Plin. 17, 11, 15, § 77 .

nŏven-dĕcim.opening: and , num. adj. card. [novem-decem], nineteen : centum septemdecim milia trecenta novemdecim, Liv. 3, 24 fin. : cum annos novendecim haberet, id. Epit. 18 Weissenb.; v. Drak. ad loc.

nŏvendĭālis.opening: adj. novem-dies , nine-day, of nine days . That lasts nine days, a nine-days' festival , which was solemnized on the occasion of a prodigy announcing misfortune (esp. a shower of stones): novendiale sacrum, Liv. 1, 31 ;…

nŏvennis.opening: adj. novem-annus , of nine years (post-class.): filius, Lact. Mort. Persec. 20, 4 .

Nŏvensĭdes.opening: or , , novus-insideo , the new gods (those received from abroad, in opp. to indigetes, the native gods): Feronia, Minerva, Novensides a Sabinis, Varr. L. L. 5, § 74 Müll. N. cr.; cf., respecting the form with d , Mar.…

nŏvēnus.opening: num. adj. distr. [novem], nine each, nine : ut virgines ter novenae per urbem euntes carmen canerent, Liv. 27, 37 : terga novena boūm, Ov. M. 12, 97 : novenorum conceptu dierum, Plin. 3, 5, 9, § 53 ; in sing. , Stat. S.…

nŏverca.opening: for noverica, qs. νεαρική, the new one , a step-mother, step-dame . Lit. , Afran. ap. Non. 393, 26 : uxor generi, noverca filii, filiae paelex, Cic. Clu. 70, 199 : cum is (Hippolytus) patri suspectus esset de novercā,…

nŏvercālis.opening: adj. noverca , of or belonging to a step-mother (post-class.). Lit. : novercales ibat venator in agros Ascanius, of Dido, Stat. S. 5, 2, 118 : atque novercali sedes praelata Lavino, called after Ascanius's step-mother,…

nŏvercor.opening: v. dep. id. , to act the step-mother to, to treat with harshness : alicui, Sid. Ep. 7, 14 med.

Nŏvesĭum.opening: a city in Gallia Belgica, on the Rhine , the mod. Neuss , Tac. H. 4, 26 ; 33, 35 ; 5, 22 ; its fortifications were restored by Julian A. D. 359, Amm. 18, 2, 4 .

nŏvīcĭŏlus.opening: adj. dim. [novicius], rather new (post-class.), Tert. Apol. 47 ; id. Poen. 6 .

nŏvīcĭus.opening: (late Lat. ), , adj. novus; cf. Varr. L. L. 6, § 59 Müll. , new (mostly confined to technical lang.): novum novicium dicimus et proprium propicium augere atque intendere volentes novi et proprii significationem, Alfen.…

nŏvĭes.opening: ( ), num. adv. [novem], nine times : ter novies, Varr. R. R. 1, 2 fin. : noviens Styx interfusa, Verg. G. 4, 480 : novem novies, Sen. Ep. 58, 31 .

nŏvĭes-dĕcĭes.opening: num. adv., nineteen times , Prisc. 1355 P.

nŏvĭlūnĭum.opening: novus-luna , the new moon (late Lat. for nova luna; cf. interlunium), Vulg. 3 Esdr. 5, 57; 9, 37 al.

Nŏvĭŏdūnum.opening: the name of several cities in Gaul. A city of the Bituriges , near the mod. Nouan , Caes. B. G. 7, 12, 2 ; 7, 55 .— A city of the Æduans, on the Loire , the mod. Nevers , Caes. B. G. 7, 55, 1 . — A city of the Suessones…

nŏvissĭmālis.opening: adj. novissimus , of or belonging to the last, final : particulae (versuum) finales seu novissimales, Mar. Victorin. p. 2519 P.

nŏvĭtas.opening: novus , a being new, newness, novelty . In gen.: rei novitas, Cic. Div. 2, 28, 60 : gratiam novitati similem parant, Quint. 1, 6, 39 : novitatis gratiā, id. 9, 3, 58 : plus novitatis, id. 8, 3, 74 : (figura) ipsā…

Nŏvĭus.opening: the name of a Roman gens. Masc. Novius, a famous writer of Atellane plays, a contemporary of Pomponius, about A. U. C. 650-670: Novius probatissimus Atellanarum scriptor ait, etc., Macr. S. 1, 10, 3 ; Cic. de Or. 2, 63,…

nŏvo.opening: v. a. novus . Lit. , to make new, to renew : ipsi transtra novant, Verg. A. 5, 752 : nullā prole novare viros, Ov. F. 1, 622 : gregem, Stat. Th. 10, 229 : fessa membra, to refresh, Ov. H. 4, 90 : vivāque nitentia lymphā…

nŏvus.opening: adj. Sanscr. navas; Gr. νέος, i. e. νεϝος; cf.: noverca, nuntius, denuo, nuper; Germ. neu; Engl. new , new, not old, young, fresh, recent , etc. (v. antiquus init. ; cf.: recens, novellus). Lit. In gen.: civitates…

nox.opening: (collat. form of the abl. noctu; v. in the foll. : nox, adverb. for nocte; v. fin. ), (once masc. in Cato; v. infra , I.) [Sanscr. nak, naktis, night; Gr. νύξ ; Germ. Nacht; Engl. night; from root naç; cf. neco, νέκυς…

noxa.opening: for noc-sa, from noc-eo, like rixa from ringor , hurt, harm, injury , which one does or suffers (v. Döderl. Synon. 2, p. 153 sqq.; not in Cic., but cf. noxia; syn.: injuria, contumelia). Lit. : QVANDOQVE HICE HOMINES…

noxālis.opening: adj. noxa , of or relating to an injury (jurid. Lat.): noxalis actio, an action on account of an injury committed : noxales actiones appellantur, quae non ex contractu, sed ex noxā atque maleficio servorum adversus nos…

noxĭālis.opening: adj. noxia , injurious, noxious (post-class.): lex noxialis, Prud. Cath. 9, 18 : carcer, id. ib. 14, 1107 .

noxĭōsus.opening: adj. noxia (postAug.). Very hurtful, injurious , or noxious : res, Sen. Ben. 7, 10, 1 : noxiosissimo animali (al. noxissimo s. noxiissimo), id. Clem. 1, 26, 3 .— Full of guilt, vicious, sinful : animi perditi…

noxĭtūdo.opening: noxa , guilt, offence, crime : Pelopidarum, Att. ap. Non. 143, 22 (Trag. Rel. v. 162 Rib.).
