nuncŭpātīvus.opening: id. , so-called, nominal , Ambros. de Fide, 5, 1, 22.—Hence, adv. : , nominally , Hier. in Psa. 26 ; Facund. Def 1, 4.

nuncŭpātor.opening: id. , a namer (post-class.): Pythagoras primus philosophiae nuncupator et conditor, App. Flor. p. 352, 13 .

nuncŭpo.opening: (nuncupassit for nuncupaverit; v. in the foll. ), v. a. nomencapio , to call by name, to call, name (mostly ante-class. and post-Aug.; esp. in jurid. lang.: quem cultrix nomine nostro nuncupat, Ov. F. 1, 246 ; cf. Cic.…

nundĭnālis.opening: adj. nundinae , of or belonging to the nundinae: nundinalis cocus, a bad cook, employed only on marketdays, Plaut. Aul. 2, 4, 45 ; cf. id. Ps. 3, 2, 6 , sqq. (or perhaps nundinalis stands for nundinarius, v. h. v., and…

nundĭnārĭus.opening: adj. id. , of or belonging to a market or fair, market- (postAug.): forum, Plin. 8, 51, 77, § 208 : oppidum, id. 12, 17, 40, § 80 : epulae, given to those who attended the market, Dig. 17, 2, 69 .

nundĭnātīcĭus.opening: or , , adj. nundinor , for sale (post-class.): capita, i. e. the unveiled faces of girls, Tert. Virg. Vel. 3 .

nundĭnātĭo.opening: id. , lit., the holding of a market or fair; hence, a trading, trafficking, buying and selling : fuit nundinatio aliqua, et isti non nova, ne causam diceret, Cic. Verr 2, 5, 5, § 10 : quae libido in jure dicundo fuerit,…

nundĭnātor.opening: id. , a trader, trafficker . Lit. , Paul. ex Fest. s. v. nundinae, p. 173 Müll.: NVNDINATOR, an appellation of Mercury as the patron deity of brokers , Inscr. Rein. cl. 1, n. 80.— Trop. : nundinator salutis publicae,…

nundĭnor.opening: v. dep. nundinae . Lit. , to attend or hold market, to trade, traffic (syn. mercor): in captivorum pretiis, nec victoris animo, nec magni ducis more nundinans, chaffering, Liv. 22, 56 : nefandis nundinandi commerciis,…

nundĭnus.opening: adj. novem-dies , of or belonging to nine days; hence, subst. , , (sc. dea), the goddess who presided over the purification and naming of infants, which took place in the case of boys on the ninth and in that of girls…

nuntĭātĭo.opening: ( ), , nuntio , used only in relig. and jurid. lang. In relig. lang., a declaring, announcing; a declaration, announcement made by the augur respecting what he has observed: nos nuntiationem solum habemus: consules…

nuntĭātor.opening: ( ), , id. (postclass.). A reporter, declarer, announcer : apparuit Christus rei maximae nuntiator, Arn. 1 fin. ; Tert. Carn. Christ. 7 .— An informer , Dig. 39, 1, 20 ; 48, 16, 6 .

nuntĭātrix.opening: ( ), , nuntiator , she that announces (late Lat.), Cassiod. Var. 2, 14 .

nuntĭo.opening: ( ), , v. a. nuntius , to announce, declare, report, relate, narrate, make known, inform, give intelligence of , etc. (cf.: narro, indico, trado, scribo, dico, certiorem facio, etc.). In gen., alike of verbal and of…

nuntĭus.opening: adj. perh. contr. from noventius, from obsol. novēre, to make new; v. novus . That announces, signifies, makes known; announcing, informing ( poet. ): nuntia fibra deos? Tib. 2, 1, 26 : fratre reversuro, nuntia venit…

nūper.opening: adv. for novum-per; cf. semper , newly, lately, recently, not long ago . Lit. : quamquam haec inter nos nuper notitia admodumst, Ter. Heaut. 1, 1, 1 Flect. Ussing. (al. nupera): nuper, et quid dico nuper? immo vero…

nūpĕrus.opening: adj. nuper , late, fresh, recent (ante- and post-class.): recens captum hominem nuperum et novicium Te perdocere, Plaut. Capt. 3, 5, 60 : elephanti nuperi a silvā (al. nuper), Flor. 4, 2 .— Sup. : nuperrimus etiam…

Nups.opening: (also written , ), the name of two cities in Egypt , Plin. 6, 29, 35 , §§ 178, 179.

nuptālīcĭus.opening: or , , adj. nupta , of or belonging to a marriage wedding-, nuptial (only in jurid. Lat.): donum, Dig. 50, 16, 194 .

nuptĭābĭlis.opening: adj. nuptiae , marriageable : nupta, nubilis, nuptiabilis, Not. Tir. p. 131 .

nuptĭae.opening: ( dat. nuptis, Inscr. Orell. 7421 ), plur. [nupta], a marriage, wedding, nuptials . Lit. : exornatis nuptiis, Plaut. Aul. 4, 10, 54 : dum ego cum Casinā faciam nuptias, id. Cas. 2, 8, 50 : nuptias adornare, id. Aul. 2,…

nuptĭālis.opening: adj. nuptiae , of or belonging to a marriage, wedding-, nuptial : ludi, Plaut. Cas. 5, 1, 2 : cena, id. Curc. 5, 2, 61 ; Suet. Calig. 25 : dona, Cic. Clu. 9, 28 : faces, id. ib. 6, 15 ; Hor. C. 3, 11, 33 : carmina, Cat.…

nuptĭātor.opening: id. , one who marries (late Lat.), Hier. ad Jov. 1 , n. 38: nuptiatores, γαμοστόλοι , Gloss. Philox.

nupto.opening: v. freq. n. [nubo], to marry wed (post-class.), Tert. Sod. 45 .

nuptŭla.opening: dim. nupta , a young wife , Varr. ap. Non. 357, 2 .

nuptŭrĭo.opening: v. desid. n. [nubo], to desire to marry (post-Aug.), Mart. 3, 93, 18 ; App. Mag. p. 319, 9 .

nuptus.opening: nubo , a covering, veiling , Varr. L. L. 5, § 72 Müll.— Transf. , marriage, wedlock (post-class.): nuptumque passa, Stat. S. 5, 1, 45 : solenni nuptu filias locabant, Aur. Vict. Vir. Ill. 59 .

nŭrīcŭla.opening: dim. nurus , a daughter-in-law , Inscr. De Vita Inscr. Benev. 53, 136.

Nursĭa.opening: or , , , a Sabine city , the mod. Norcia : frigida, Verg. A. 7, 715 .—Hence, , , adj., Nursian : rapa, Col. 10, 421 ; Plin. 18, 13, 34, § 130 : pilae, Mart. 13, 20, 2 .—In plur. subst. : , , , the Nursians , Plin. 3,…

nŭrus.opening: ( dat. nuru, Tac. A. 6, 29 .— Form , Rénier, Inscr. Afr. 1590), for snurus, kindr. with Sanscr. snusha and the Old Germ. snur, Schnur; Gr. νυός , a daughter-in-law . Lit. : uno animo omnes socrus oderunt nurus, Ter.…

nūs.opening: , = νοῦς . In gen., the understanding (post-class.), Mart. Cap. 2, § 126 . — In partic., one of the Æons of Valentinian , Tert. adv. Valent. 7 ; 9 .

nuscitiōsum.opening: ( ) , qui propter oculorum vitium parum videret. At Opilius Aurelius nusciciones ( fort. leg. nuscitiones) esse caecitudines nocturnas: Aelius Stilo, qui plus videret vesperi, quam meridie, nec cognosceret. nisi quod…

nusquam.opening: adv. ne-usquam , nowhere, in no place . Lit. : nusquam invenio Naucratem, Plaut. Am. 4, 1, 6 : fratrem nusquam invenio gentium, Ter. Ad. 4, 2, 1 ; Plaut. Am. 2, 1, 73 : sive est illa scripta uspiam, sive nusquam, Cic.…

nūtābĭlis.opening: adj. nuto , tottering (postclass.), App. de Deo Socrat. p. 44, 19 .

nūtābundus.opening: adj. id. , tottering, staggering (post-class.). Lit. : miles, App. M. 9, p. 237, 1 ; Salv. Gub. D. 6, 13 . — Trop. , vacillating, uncertain , Lact. 6, 3, 6 .

nūtāmen.opening: id. , a nodding, waving : tremulo pennae, Sil. 2, 399 .

nūtātĭo.opening: id. (post-Aug.). A nodding : capitis, Plin. 11, 37, 49, § 135 . — A swaying . Lit. : frequens et in utramque partem nutatio, Quint. 11, 3, 129 .— Trop. , a shaking, tottering : nutatio reipublicae, Plin. Pan. 5, 6 .

nūto.opening: v. freq. n. [nuo (of re-nuo, ab-nuo); Gr. νεύω ; cf. numen, nutus], to nod with the head. Lit. : neque illa ulli homini nutet, nictet, annuat, Plaut. As. 4, 1, 39 ; id. Merc. 2, 3, 72 : capite nutat, id. Mil. 2, 2, 52 :…

nūtrībĭlis.opening: adj. nutrio , nourishing, nutritious (post-class.): cibi, Cael. Aur. Tard. 5, 1, 9 : nutribiliores suci, id. ib. 5, 10, 126 : vina, id. Acut. 2, 37, 212 .— Subst. : , , , nourishing food , Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 4, 108…

nūtrīcātĭo.opening: nutrico , a suckling, nursing (ante- and post-class.): munus nutricationis grave ac difficile, Gell. 12, 1, 5 : puerorum nutricationes, App. Dogm. Plat. 2, p. 27, 18 : herbarum, a nourishing, rearing, Varr. R. R. 1, 44,…

nūtrīcātus.opening: id. , a suckling, nursing (ante-class.): plane eductus in nutricatu Venerio, Plaut. Mil. 3, 1, 55 : pecoris, Varr. R. R. 2, 1, 20 .— A nourishing, rearing : herba non evellenda in nutricatu, Varr. R. R. 1, 47 ; 1, 49 ;…

nūtrīcĭus.opening: and , , adj. nutrix , that suckles, nourishes, nurses . Adj. : quis Faustulum nescit pastorem fuisse nutricium, qui Romulum et Remum educavit? Varr. R. R. 2, 1, 9 : nutriciae curae, Arn. 2, 58 : humus radices tenero…

nūtrīco.opening: , and , , v. dep. id. , to suckle, nourish, bring up, rear . Lit. : pueros nutricare, Plaut. Merc. 3, 1, 11 : scrofae nutricare octonos porcos parvulos primo possunt, Varr. R. R. 2, 4, 13 ; 2, 2, 8 : nutricatur oliva,…

nūtrīcŭla.opening: dim. id. , a nurse . Lit. : quid voveat dulci nutricula majus alumno? Hor. Ep. 1, 4, 8 ; Suet. Aug. 94 : fabulae nutricularum, Quint. 1, 9, 2 .— Transf. , she who nourishes, maintains, preserves a thing: nutriculae…

nūtrīmen.opening: nutrio , nourishment : naturae, Ov. M. 15, 354 ; Juvenc. in Matt. 25 .

nūtrīmentālis.opening: adj. nutrimentum , nourishing (late Lat.), Dion. Exig. Greg. Creat. Hom. 15.

nūtrīmentum.opening: nutrio , nourishment, nutriment . Lit. : per hanc nutrimentorum consuetudinem. Suet. Calig. 9 .— Transf. , support, nourishment , etc.: pro nutrimento omni est raritas vulneris, Plin. 17, 23, 36, § 213 : suscepitque…

nūtrĭo.opening: (contr. form, nutrīmus for nutrivimus, Nemes. Ecl. 3, 26 : nutribat for nutriebat, Verg. A. 11, 572 ; Sil. 16, 29 ; so, nutribant, Verg. A. 7, 485 : nutribo for nutriam, Rhemn. Palaem. 1383; Cledon. 1914.—In the dep.…

nūtrītor.opening: nutrio , a bringer up, rearer, breeder (post-Aug.): volucrum equorum, Stat. Th. 10, 228 : Alexandri Severi, Lampr. Alex. Sev. 13 : a nutritore suo manumissus, Suet. Gram. 7 ; Inscr. Orell. 2816 .

nūtrītōrĭus.opening: adj. nutritor . Nourishing, nutritive : lac omne nutritorium est, Theod. Prisc. de Diaet. 3 .— Of or belonging to bringing up, rearing : cunae nutritoriae, Aug. Conf. 12, 27 .

nūtrītūra.opening: nutrio , = nutricatus, a nursing, suckling , Cassiod.

nūtrītus.opening: , a false read. for intrita, Plin. 22, 24, 53, § 114 ; v. Sillig ad h. l.

nūtrix.opening: (old orthogr. , acc. to Quint. 1, 4, 16 ), , nutrio , a wet-nurse, nurse . Lit. : omnia minima mansa, ut nutrices infantibus pueris, in os inserant, Cic. de Or. 2, 39, 162 : cum lacte nutricis errorem suxisse, id. Tusc.…

nūtus.opening: nuo, ĕre (of abnuo, etc.); cf. nuto , a nodding, a nod . Lit. : Scipio nutu finire disceptationem potuisset, Liv. 34, 62 : nutu tremefecit Olympum, Verg. A. 9, 106 : digitisque saepe est nutuque locutus, Ov. Tr. 2, 453…

nux.opening: ( gen. plur. nucerum for nucum, Cael. ap. Charis. p. 40 P.), etym. dub. , a nut . At weddings it was customary to strew nuts on the floor: sparge, marite, nuces, Verg. E. 8, 30 ; cf. Varr. ap. Serv. ad E. 8, 30 ; Paul.…

nyctălōpa.opening: nyctalops , the disease of one who cannot see in the twilight, nyctalopy , Marc. Emp. 8 .

nyctălōpĭa.opening: , = νυκταλωπία , the disease of one who cannot see in the twilight, nyctalopy , Isid. Orig. 4, 8, 8 (al. nyctalmos).

nyctălops.opening: adj. , = νυκτάλωψ . That cannot see in the twilight , Plin. 28, 11, 47, § 170 ; 8, 50, 76, § 203 ; Dig. 21, 1, 10 . — That sees only at night : nyctalopas, qui per noctem vident et per diem obscuritatem patiuntur,…

Nyctēgrĕsĭa.opening: , = Νυκτηγρεσία ( Νυκτεγερσια ), Night-watching , the title of a tragedy of Attius (v. Trag. Rel. Fragm. p. 168 Rib. sq.).

nyctēgrĕtos.opening: , or , , , = νυκτήγρετον , a plant that shines by night , Plin. 21, 11, 36, § 62 .

Nyctĕlĭus.opening: adj. , = Νυκτέλιος , an epithet of Bacchus , because his mysteries were celebrated at night: Nyctelius pater, Ov. A. A. 1, 567 : latex, wine, Sen. Oedip. 492 : Nyctelia sacra, the Bacchanalia, Serv. ad Verg. A. 4, 383

Nycteus.opening: , = Νυκτεύς , a son of Hyrieus and the nymph Clonia, and father of Antiopa : Nycteos Antiope, Prop. 3, 15 (4, 14), 12.—Hence, , , , the Nycteide , i. e. Antiopa : Nycteida, Ov. M. 6, 111 : Nycteidos, Stat. Th. 7, 190 ;…

nyctĭcŏrax.opening: , = νυκτικόραξ , the night-raven , Hier. Ep. 106 , n. 86; Isid. Orig. 12, 7, 41 ; Paul. Nol. Ep. 40, 6 .

Nyctĭmĕnē.opening: , = Νυκτιμένη , the daughter of Epopeus, king of Lesbos, who unknowingly had intercourse with her father: when she discovered it, she fled in despair to the woods, where she was changed by Minerva into a night-owl , Ov.…

nyctostrătēgus.opening: = νυκτοστράτηγος , the Greek name of the praefectus vigilum, Dig. 50, 4, 18, § 12 .

nyma.opening: a plant , otherwise unknown, Plin. 27, 12, 82, § 106 (al. nigina).

nympha.opening: , and , ( dat. plur. NYMPHABVS, Inscr. Orell. 1629 ; NYMFABVS, ib. 1630 ; NYMPHIS, ib. 1627 ; 1630 sq.), , = νύμφη . A bride, a mistress , Ov. H. 1, 27 ; Tib. 3, 1, 21 (al. merita).— A young woman : se quoque nympha…

nymphaea.opening: , = νυμφαία (Lat.: clava Herculis; cf. Marc. Emp. 33 ), the water-lily , Plin. 25, 7, 37, § 75 ; App. Herb. 67 .

Nymphaeum.opening: , = Νύμφαιον , a promontory and seaport in Illyria, on the borders of Macedonia , now Capo di Redeni , Caes. B. C. 3, 26, 4 ; Liv. 42, 36, 8 ; Plin. 3, 22, 26, § 144 ; Luc. 5, 720 .

Nymphaeus.opening: A river in Latium, between Circeii and Astura, now Ninfa , Plin. 3, 5, 9, § 57 .— A river in Mesopotamia , Amm. 18, 9, 2 .

nymphālis.opening: adj. nympha , of or belonging to a fountain : in aquā nymphali, Octav. Hor. 4 .

nympharēna.opening: , a false read. for Nipparene, Plin. 37, 10, 64, § 175 .

Nymphĕros.opening: , = νύμφη-ἔρως (Bridelove), a Roman surname , Inscr. Grut. 15, 3 .

nymphēum.opening: (NYMFEVM, Inscr. Orell. 57 ; 5049 ; NYMPHAEVM, ib. 3317 ), , , = νυμφεῖον , a fountain consecrated to the nymphs at Corinth , Plin. 35, 12, 43, § 151 ; Capitol. Gord. 32 ; Cod. Just. 11, 42, 5 ; 11, 42, 6 ; Amm. 15, 7,…

Nymphĭas.opening: nympha , i. e. descended from a nymph, a Roman surname , Inscr. Gud. 344, 5 .

Nymphĭcus.opening: , = Νυμφικός , a Roman surname , Inscr. Marin. Iscriz. Alb. p. 117.—In fem. : † NYMPHICE, Inscr. Murat. 1143, 9 .

Nymphĭdĭus.opening: nympha , a Roman surname , Suet. Galb. 11 ; Tac. H. 1, 5 ; 25 ; Inscr. Murat. 902, 7 .

nymphĭgĕna.opening: nympha- gigno , the Nymph-born , i. e. Achilles, the son of Thetis : sors nova nymphigenae votum post fata meretur: Quam pepigit thalamis, hanc habet in tumulis, i. e. Polyxena, who was immolated on his tomb , Poët. ap.…

Nymphŏdōrus.opening: , = νύμφη-δῶρον , a Roman surname : L. SAENIVS L. T. NYMPHODORVS, Inscr. Murat. 1599, 5 .

Nymphŏdŏtus.opening: , = νύμφη-δοτός , a Roman surname , Inscr. Maff. Mus. Ver. 109, 1 .

nymphon.opening: , = νυμφών , a bridal chamber , Tert. adv. Val. 32 .

Nȳsa.opening: ( ), , , = Νῦσα , the name of several cities . A city in Caria, on the slope of Mount Messogis , the modern Nasli or Sultan-hissar , Plin. 5, 29, 29, § 108 . — A city in Palestine , the modern El Baisan , Plin. 5, 18,…

Nyssos.opening: , i., , = Νύσσος , a city in Macedonia , Plin. 4, 10, 17, § 36 .

Nȳsus.opening: the tutor of Bacchus, to whom he intrusted Thebes during his expedition to India , Hyg. Fab. 131 and 167.

O.grammar: the fourteenth letter of the Latin alphabet
O.opening: , corresponding to the Gr. ο and ω . The Latin language possessed both the sound and the sign from the earliest times; whereas the Etruscan language never possessed the o , and the Umbrian seems not to have received it…

obba.opening: , a vessel large at the bottom, a beaker, noggin; a decanter : obba poculi genus, quod nunc ubba dicitur. Varro: obbas et Cumanos calices, Non. 146, 8 sq. ; cf.: obba poculi genus vel ligneum vel ex sparto. Varro (here…

Obba.opening: a city in Africa near Carthage , Liv. 30, 7, 10 .

obbātus.opening: , false read. for ovatae, App. M. 10, p. 254, 15 .

ob-blătĕrātus.opening: , false read. for adblaterantes, App. M. 9, p. 221, 25 .

ob-brūtesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become brutish, stupid (ante- and post-class.): obbrutuit, obstupuit, a bruto, quod antiqui pro gravi, interdum pro stupido dixerunt. Afranius: non possum verbum facere, obbrutui, Paul. ex Fest. p. 187…

ob-densātĭo.opening: a thickening (post-class.): cutis, Cael. Aur. Tard. 1, 1, 47 .

ob-do.opening: v. a. , to put, place , or set one thing before another; to put against; to shut, close, fasten , etc.: obdere, opponere vel operire, Paul. ex Fest. p. 191 Müll. (not in Cic. or Cæs.): pessulum ostio obdo, slip the…

ob-dormĭo.grammar: īvi or ii, ītum, 4 v. n. and a.
ob-dormĭo.opening: v. n. and a. , to fall asleep (class.): ebrium obdormivisse, Plaut. Am. 1, 1, 116 : Endymion nescio quando in Latmo obdormivit, Cic. Tusc. 1, 38, 92 : sub taxo, Plin. 16, 10, 20, § 51 : quem obdormire volumus, Cels. 3,…

obdormisco.opening: v. inch. n. [obdormio], to fall asleep (rare but class.): ibidem obdormiscemus, Plaut. Rud. 2, 7, 33 ; id. Am. 1, 1, 116 : quid melius, quam in mediis vitae laboribus obdormiscere, * Cic. Tusc. 1, 49, 117 : in jure…

obdormĭto.opening: v. freq. n. [id.], to fall asleep , Fortun. Carm. 3 .

ob-dūco.opening: ( inf. perf. sync. obduxe, Arg. ad Plaut. Merc. 7 ), 3, v. a. , to lead or draw before, lead or conduct against or towards, to draw or bring forward or around, draw over (class. and very freq.; syn.: obtendo, obtego).…

ob-ductĭo.opening: obduco , a covering, veiling, enveloping . * In gen.: nubila inimica obductione pendent, Arn. 1, 7 .— In partic., a veiling of criminals before their execution: obductio capitis, Cic. Rab. Perd. 5, 16 : capitum, Amm.…

obducto.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to lead or conduct in opposition or rivalry to another : nec pol ego patiar ... measque in aedes sic scorta obductarier, Plaut. Merc. 4, 4, 46 ; cf. obduco, I. B. 7.

ob-dulcesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become sweet : obdulcesco, περιγλυκύνομαι , Gloss. Philox.: in earum familiaritate obdulcuisses mihi, Aug. Conf. 7, 20, 2 .

ob-dulco.opening: v. a. , to sweeten, make sweet (post-class.): aliquid sale, Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 8, 146 ; 4, 1, 12 : fauces, Ambros. Hexaëm. 5, 12: obdulcatus panis, Cael. Aur. Tard. 3, 8 med. : fontes amari obdulcati, Vulg. Judith, 5,…

obdūrātĭo.opening: obduro , a hardening; of the mind, obduration, obduracy (eccl. Lat.), Aug. Ep. 105 ; id. in Psa. 77 et saep.

obdūrĕfăcĭo.opening: v. a. ob-durus-facio , to make hard, to harden , Non. 23, 7 .

ob-dūresco.opening: v. n. , to grow or become hard, to harden (class. only in the trop. signif.; syn. occalesco). Lit. , Cato, R. R. 50 : semen diuturnitate obdurescit, Varr. R. R. 3, 14, 5 : nervis divinis, Arn. 5, 18 .— Trop. , to become…

ob-dūro.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 v. a. and n.
ob-dūro.opening: v. a. and n. Act., to harden, render hard (only postclass.); in the trop. signif.: obdurare se contra manifestam veritatem, Lact. 1, 1, 23 : obdurata patientia, Nazar. Pan. ad Const. 13 : obdurata nequitia, Cod. Just.…

ob-ĭgĭto.opening: v. a. ob-agito , to disturb : obstant, obstringillant, obigitant, Enn. ap. Non. 147, 9 (Sat. v. 5 Vahl.); cf. Paul. ex Fest. p. 189 Müll.

ob-jăcĕo.opening: v. n. , to lie before or over against a thing (mostly post-Aug.; not in Cic. or Cæs.): Acherontem nunc obibo, ubi mortis thesauri objacent, Enn. ap. Paul. ex Fest. s. v. ob, p. 201 Müll. (Trag. v. 278 Vahl.); cf.:…

objectācŭlum.opening: objecto , a barrier, dam , Varr. R. R. 3, 17, 9 .

objectāmen.opening: id. , an objection, reproach : objectamen, ἔγκλημα , Vet. Gloss. Lat. Gr.

objectāmentum.opening: id. , a reproach (post-class.): objectamenta jurgio prolata, App. Mag. p. 274, 1 .

objectātĭo.opening: id. , a reproach : ex aliorum objectationibus, Caes. B. C. 3, 60 .

objectĭo.opening: obicio , a throwing or putting before (post-class.). Lit. : prorae, Ambros. Ep. 100, § 14 : saxorum objectione tutari, Arn. 6, 191 .— Trop. , an upbraiding, reproach : objectio nominis, Tert. ad Uxor. 2, 5 : objectionem…

objecto.opening: v. freq. a. id. , to throw before or against, to set against, oppose . Lit. ( poet. ): (pelagi volucres) Nunc caput objectare fretis, nunc currere in undas, i. e. to dive down, Verg. G. 1, 386 : huc illuc clipeum…

objector.opening: obicio , an accuser : falsi criminis objectores, Non. 130, 25 .

objectus.opening: obicio , a casting before, a putting against, in the way , or opposite, an opposing; or, neutr., a lying before or opposite (mostly poet. and in postAug. prose): dare objectum parmaï, the opposing of the shield , *…

objurgātĭo.opening: objurgo , a chiding, reproving, reproof, rebuke, reprehension (class.): objurgatio post turpe factum castigatio; monitio vero est ante commissum, Paul. ex Fest. p. 196 Müll.: ut objurgatio contumeliā careat, Cic. Lael.…

objurgātor.opening: id. , a chider, rebuker, blamer (class.): hic noster objurgator, Cic. Agr. 3, 3, 11 ; opp. accusator, Cic. Verr. 2, 3, 2, § 4 .—In plur. : benevoli, Cic. N. D. 1, 3, 5 ; id. Div. 1, 49, 111 ; Sen. Ep. 9, 20 .

objurgātōrĭus.opening: adj. objurgator , chiding, reproving, reproachful : epistula, Cic. Att. 13, 6, 3 : verba, Gell. 1, 26, 7 : sonitus vocis, id. 9, 2, 3 : clamor, Amm. 16, 12, 55 .

objurgĭto.opening: v. freq. a. objurgo , to chide, rebuke, reproach violently (Plautin.): aliquem verbis multis, Plaut. Trin. 1, 2, 30 ; 32 .

ob-jurgo.opening: (old form , Plaut. Trin. 1, 2, 30 ; 32 ), āvi, ātum, 1 ( part. pass. objurgatus, as a dep. in the act. signif.: Hirrius Curionem non mediocriter objurgatus, Cael. ap. Cic. Fam. 8, 9, 1 ), v. a. , to chide, scold, blame,…

ob-jūro.opening: v. a. , to bind by an oath : objurare jurejurando obstringere, Paul. ex Fest. pp. 188 and 189 Müll.

ob-languesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become feeble or languid, to languish : litterulae meae oblanguerunt, Cic. Fam. 16, 10, 2 .

oblăquĕātĭo.opening: oblaqueo, I. , a digging or clearing away around trees: ARBORVM, Kalend. in Inscr. Orell. II. p. 381 ; Isid. Orig. 17, 5, 30 .

ob-lăquĕo.opening: v. a. To dig about the roots of trees, etc. (cf. ablaqueo): arbores oblaqueatae sunt, Col. 2, 14, 3 ; Isid. Orig. 17, 5, 31 .— To surround, encircle, set (eccl. Lat.): argento gemmas oblaqueare, Tert. Res. Carn. 7 .

ob-lātīcĭus.opening: or , , adj. offero , freely offered or presented (postclass.): impendium, Sid. Ep. 7, 9 : aurum, a gratuitous offering of the Senate to the emperor , i. q. oblatio, Cod. Th. 6, 2, 5.

ob-lātĭo.opening: id. , an offering, presenting, a giving or bestowing gratuitously (post-class.; cf.: donum, munus, votum). In abstr.: honorum oblationibus, Eum. Pan. ad Const. 16 : si forte oblatio ei fiat ejus, quod, etc., Dig. 5, 2,…

oblātīvus.opening: adj. id. , freely given, voluntarily presented (post-class.): auguria, Serv. Verg. A. 6, 190 : functiones, Symm. Ep. 10, 43 .

ob-lātor.opening: id. , an offerer (eccl. Lat.): animae suae pro populi salute, Tert. adv. Marc. 2, 26 ; Ambros. Cain, 2, 6, 18 .

ob-lātrātĭo.opening: oblatro , a barking at; hence, transf., a railing, scolding , Hier. Ep. 133, 13 .

ob-lātrātor.opening: id. , he that barks at; a barker, railer (eccl. Lat.), Sid. Ep. 1, 3 .

ob-lātrātrix.opening: oblatrator , a female barker, railer : oblatratricem in aedes intromittere, Plaut. Mil. 3, 1, 87 .

ob-lātro.opening: v. n. , to bark at; only in the trop. signif., to rail or carp at (postAug.). With dat. : alicui, Sen. Ira, 3, 43, 1 : oblatrare veritati, Lact. 5, 4, 3 .— With acc. : aliquem, Sil. 8, 251 : nescio quid, Suet. Vesp. 13…

ob-lectābĭlis.opening: adj. oblecto , delightful, pleasant (post-class.): negotium, Aus. Ep. 19 .

ob-lectāmen.opening: id. , a delight ( poet. for oblectamentum, and perh. only in plur. ), Ov. M. 9, 342 : vitae, Stat. S. 3, 5, 95 : consulat ut sacras, hominum oblectamina, sortes, sources of consolation, Ov. M. 11, 412 .

ob-lectāmentum.opening: id. , a delight, pleasure, amusement (class.; cf.: voluptas, deliciae); with gen. obj. : requies oblectamentumque senectutis, Cic. Sen. 15, 52 : oblectamenta puerorum, id. Par. 5, 2, 38 : oblectamenta et solatia…

oblectānĕus.opening: adj. oblecto , delightful, pleasant , Inscr. Grut. 304, 1 .

ob-lectātĭo.opening: id. , a delighting, delight (a favorite word of Cic.): indagatio ipsa habet oblectationem, Cic. Ac. 2, 41, 127 : animi, id. de Or. 1, 26, 118 : curarum, id. Off. 2, 6 : vitae, id. Fin. 5, 19, 53 : requies plena…

ob-lectātor.opening: id. , a delighter, pleaser, charmer (post-class.): beluarum, App. Flor. p. 358, 17 : hominis, Tert. Cor. Mil. 8 fin.

ob-lectātōrĭus.opening: adj. id. , delighting, pleasing (post-class.): aenigmata, Gell. 18, 2 in lemm .

ob-lecto.opening: v. a. 2. lacto , to delight, please, divert, entertain, amuse (class.; most freq. with se and mid.; syn. delecto); constr. usually aliquem (aliquid, se), with abl. , with cum , with in and abl. With abl. : ut quam…

ob-lēnĭo.opening: v. a. , to soften, soothe (post-Aug.): lectio carminum illum obleniat, Sen. Ira, 3, 9, 1 .

ob-līdo.opening: v. a. laedo . To squeeze together (rare but class.): caelum digitulis duobus oblidere, Cic. Scaur. § 10, p. 261 Orell.: oblisis faucibus, strangled, Tac. A. 5, 9 ; so, obliso gutture, Prud. Psych. 589 ; App. M. 4, p.…

oblĭgāmentum.opening: obligo . Lit. , a band (post-class.): caput obligamento obnoxium, Tert. Cor. Mil. 14 .— Trop. , an obligation : legis obligamenta, Tert. adv. Marc. 3, 22 ; Hier. Ephes. 1, 14 ; Tert. Idol. 15 .

oblĭgātĭo.opening: id. . In gen. A binding (post-class. and very rare): propter linguae obligationem, because of his being tongue-tied, Just. 13, 7, 1 .— Trop. , an ensnaring, entangling : innocentium, Dig. 48, 10, 1 : declinantes in…

oblĭgātōrĭus.opening: adj. obligo , binding, obligatory (post-class.), Dig. 17, 1, 2, § 6 ; Just. 3, 27, 6 .

oblĭgātūra.opening: id. , a band, bandage : obligatura, κατάδεσμος , Gloss. Philox.

oblĭgātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from obligo.

ob-lĭgo.opening: v. a. Lit. To bind or tie around, to bind or fasten to any thing (very rare): obligatus corio, bound in a leathern sack, Auct. Her. 1, 13, 23 : articulis muscus obligatus, bound upon, Plin. 26, 11, 66, § 105 : cibum…

ob-lĭgūrĭo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to devour, consume, squander (very rare): mox dum alterius obligurias omnia, Enn. ap. Don. ad Ter. Phorm. 2, 2, 25 (dub.; Vahl. Sat. Rel. v. 29, reads abligurias): obligurisse, Jul. Val. Res Gest. Alex.…

oblĭgūrītor.opening: ( ), , obligurio , one who consumes his property in feasting, a squanderer, dissipated person (postclass.), Firm. Math. 5, 5, 2.

oblīmo.opening: v. a. ob-limus , to cover with mud or slime . Lit. (rare but class.): Aegyptum Nilus irrigat, mollitosque et oblimatos ad serendum agros relinquit, * Cic. N. D. 2, 52, 130 : fossae oblimatae, Suet. Aug. 18 : sulcos (i.…

ob-lĭnĭo.opening: v. a. (post-Aug. collat. form of oblino, q. v.), to bedaub, besmear : talearum capita misto fimo cum cinere oblinire, Col. 5, 9, 3 ; so fin. ; id. 12, 2, 42 ; 12, 15, 2 ; 12, 44, 6 : si quis aliquem caeno, luto…

ob-lĭno.opening: (Varr. ap. Prisc. p. 898 P.), lĭtum, 3 (form acc. to the 4th conj. oblinio, q. v.), v. a. , to daub or smear over, to bedaub, besmear (syn.: inficio, induco). Lit. In gen.: cerussā malas oblinere, Plaut. Most. 1, 3, 101…

oblīquātĭo.opening: obliquo , a bending, winding, oblique direction (post-class.), Macr. S. 7, 1 .

oblīquĭtas.opening: obliquus , a sidelong or slanting direction, obliqueness, obliquity (post-Aug.), Plin. 3, 5, 6, § 40 : sigui feri, id. 2, 19, 17, § 81 .— Transf. , ambiguity : oraculi, Prisc. 1137 P.

oblīquo.opening: v. a. obliquus , to turn, bend , or twist aside, awry , or in an oblique direction ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. : oculos, Ov. M. 7, 412 : visus, Stat. Ach. 1, 323 : equos, id. Th. 12, 749 : pedes, Sen. Ep. 121,…

Oblīquŏlŏquus.opening: obliquus-loquor , one who speaks indirectly , i. e. ambiguously , an epithet of Apollo, acc. to the Gr. Λοξίας , in allusion to his obscure oracles: Obliquoloquus, Λοξίας , Gloss. Philox.

oblīquus.opening: ( , v. Orthogr. Vergl. p. 449 Wagner), , adj. ob and liquus; root lek-; Gr. λέχριος, λέχρις, slantwise (cf.: λοξός, Λοξίας); Lat. licinus, limus, luxus, luxare , sidelong, slanting, awry, oblique (freq. and class.; cf.:…

obliscor.opening: , paragog. obliscier, archaic collat. form of obliviscor, Att. ap. Non. 500, 1 (Trag. Rel. v. 190 Rib.).— Fut. : obliscar, Att. ap. Non. 500, 1 (Trag. Rel. v. 488 Rib.); v. obliviscor.

ob-lĭtesco.opening: v. inch. n. [latesco], to hide or conceal one's self (rare but class.): a nostro aspectu oblitescant, Cic. Univ. 10, 33 : ne in rimis (areae) grana oblitescant, Varr. R. R. 1, 51, 1 : qui velut timidum atque iners…

oblītor.opening: obliviscor; but perh. from oblino, a defiler , a forgetter (late Lat.): judiciorum oblitores, Hier. in Psa. 88 .

ob-littĕrātĭo.opening: ( ), , oblittero , a blotting out, erasing, effacing, obliteration; and, in partic., a blotting out from the memory, a forgetting, forgetfulness (postAug.): aeris oblitteratio, Plin. 34, 7, 18, § 47 : vetustatis, Arn.…

ob-littĕrātor.opening: ( ), , id. , a blotter out, obliterator , sc. from the memory (eccl. Lat.): commemorator, non oblitterator vetustatum, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 26 fin. ; Paul. Nol. Ep. 16, 7 .

oblittĕro.opening: ( ), , v. a. oblino , to blot out, strike out, erase, obliterate . Lit. (post-Aug. and very rare; syn. deleo): oblitterata aerarii monumenta, Tac. A. 13, 23 fin. — Trop. , to blot out of remembrance, consign to…

oblittĕrus.opening: ( ), , adj. id. , for oblitteratus, consigned to forgetfulness, forgotten (ante-class.): Laevius oblitteram gentem pro oblitteratam dixit, Gell. 19, 7, 4 .

oblīvĭālis.opening: adj. oblivio , that causes forgetfulness, oblivious (post-class.): poculum, Prud. Cath. 6, 16 .

oblīvĭo.opening: obliviscor . Lit. , a being forgotten, forgetfulness, oblivion (class.): oblivio veteris belli, Cic. Imp. Pomp. 4 init. : laudem alicujus ab oblivione atque a silentio vindicare, to rescue from oblivion, id. de Or. 2,…

oblīvĭōsus.opening: adj. oblivio . Lit. , that easily forgets, forgetful, oblivious (rare but class.): hos (senes) significat credulos, obliviosos, Cic. Sen. 11, 36 .— Sup. : homo obliviosissimus, Tert. Anim. 24 .— Transf. , that produces…

oblīviscor.opening: (archaic inf. obliscier. Att. Tr. 190 ; 488 ), , v. dep. ob and livor, q. v.; livēre, to become dark; hence, to have the mind darkened, forget , to forget; constr. with gen. of pers. and with gen. or acc. of thing; less…

oblīvĭum.opening: obliviscor , forgetfulness, oblivion ( poet. and once in Tac. for oblivio; usually in the plur. ): oblivia rerum, Lucr. 3, 828 ; so id. 3, 1066 ; 6, 1213 : longa oblivia potant, Verg. A. 6, 715 : ducere sollicitae…

oblīvĭus.opening: adj. oblivio , sunk into oblivion, forgotten : verba, i. e. obsolete, Varr. L. L. 5, § 10 Müll.

ob-lŏco.opening: v. a. , to let out for hire (postAug. and post class.): operam ad puteos exhauriendos, Just. 11, 10, 9 ; v. l. for abloco, Suet. Caes. 26 .

oblŏcūtor.opening: ( ), , id. , a contradicter : neque ego oblocutor sum alteri in convivio, Plaut. Mil. 3, 1, 48 .

oblongŭlus.opening: adj. dim. [oblongus], rather long (post-class.): surculi, Gell. 17, 9, 7 .

ob-longus.opening: adj., rather long, longish; oblong (not in Cic. or Cæs.): missile telum hastili oblongo, Liv. 21, 8 : figura, Plin. 37, 12, 75, § 196 : folia, id. 25, 3, 6 . § 21: scutula, Tac. Agr. 10 .— Comp. : foramen oblongius,…

ob-lŏquor.opening: v. dep. In gen., to speak against a person or thing; to interrupt a speaker; to gainsay, contradict (class.; syn. interpello); constr. with dat. or absol. With dat. : alicui, Plaut. Men. 1, 2, 46 : vestra exspectatio,…

obluctātĭo.opening: obluctor , a striving or struggling against, vehement opposition (eccl. Lat.): obluctatio virtutis, Arn. 2, 77 : flammarum, Mart. Cap. 6, § 647 : adversus mala, Lact. 3, 11, 11 .— Plur. : quis obluctationes sensit?…

ob-luctor.opening: v. dep. , to strive or struggle against, to contend with, oppose a person or thing ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). Lit. With dat. of person : soli obluctandum Fabio, to contend with Fabius alone, Sil. 8, 10 .— With…

oblucuviasse.grammar: dicebant antiqui mente errasse, quasi in luco deorum alicui occurrisse
oblucuviasse.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 187 Müll. (al. oblucinasse).

ob-lūdo.opening: v. n. * To play off jokes : obludunt, qui custodem oblectent, Plaut. Truc. 1, 2, 10 .—* To make sport of, mock one; with dat. : alicui, Prud. Hamart. 6 .

ob-lūrĭdus.opening: adj., pale, sallow (post-class.): spadones obluridi, Amm. 14, 6, 17 .

obmănens.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 199 Müll.; and cf. ommento.

ob-marcesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to fall away, grow lean : obmarcescebat febris, Lucil. ap. Non. 2, 30 .

ob-mĕrĭtus.opening: Part. [ob-mereor], having deserved well of , Rénier, Inscr. Afr. 444 al.: parentes optime obmeritae, id. ib. 966 .

ob-mōlĭor.opening: v. dep. (perh. not ante-Aug.). Lit. , to push or throw up one thing before another (as a defence or obstruction): nec in promptu erat quod obmolirentur, Liv. 33, 5, 8 : arborum truncos et saxa, Curt. 6, 6, 24 .— Transf.…

ob-mordĕo.opening: v. a. , to bite around (late Lat.), Isid. Orig. 20, 16, 1 .

ob-mŏvĕo.opening: v. a. , to move or bring forward, produce, offer (ante-class.), Cato, R. R. 141, 4 : Juppiter te hoc ferto obmovendo bonas preces precor (a form of prayer), id. ib. 134, 2 .—Cf.: obmoveto pro admoveto dicebatur apud…

obmurmŭrātĭo.opening: obmurmuro , a murmuring against; a murmuring (post-class.): gravis, Amm. 26, 2, 3 .

ob-murmŭro.opening: v. n. , to murmur against, at , or to ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose); constr. with dat. or acc. : precibusque meis obmurmurat ipse, Ov. H. 18, 47 : itidem obmurmurasse: Τί γάρ μοι , etc., Suet. Oth. 7 : Pharisaei,…

obmussĭto.opening: v. freq. a. obmusso , to whisper or mutter against any one; to mutter (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Pall. 4 .

obmusso.opening: v. a. , to whisper against any one; to whisper, mutter (eccl. Lat.). Tert. Anim. 18 .

ob-mūtesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become dumb, to lose one's speech (syn.: taceo, sileo). Lit. : qui ebrius obmutuit, Cels. 2, 6 : cum obmutuerint, Plin. 27, 12, 104, § 127 : umbrae ejus (hyaenae) contactu canes obmutescere, lose their…

ob-nātus.opening: adj., growing on or about : obnata ripis salicta, Liv. 23, 19, 11 .

obnectĕre.grammar: obligare, maxime in nuptiis frequens est

obnexus.opening: obnecto , a connecting, connection (eccl. Lat.), Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 37 .

ob-nĭger.opening: adj., blackish : radices, Plin. 20, 23, 94, § 253 Sillig. (al. obliquis nigris).

obnīsē.opening: adv. , v. obnitor, P. a. fin .

obnīsus.opening: obnitor , exertion, trouble : Damascum capit obnisu levi, Auct. Itin. Alex. 41 Mai.

ob-nītor.opening: (rarely nīsus), 3 ( inf. obnitier for obniti, Lucr. 4, 437 ), v. dep. , to bear, press, push, struggle , or strive against any thing (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose; not in Cic. or Cæs.); constr. with the dat.,…

obnixē.opening: adv. , v. obnitor, P. a. fin .

obnixus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from obnitor.

obnoxĭo.opening: v. a. obnoxius , to render subject or obnoxious to any thing (postclass.): et alienis semet noxiis obnoxiantes, Claud. Mam. Stat. Anim. 2, 9 .

obnoxĭōsus.opening: adj. obnoxius (ante-class.). Subject, submissive, obedient : alicui, Plaut. Trin. 4, 3, 31 .—* Hurtful, injurious, dangerous : res, Enn. ap. Gell. 7, 17, 10 (Trag. v. 341 Vahl.).—Hence, adv. : , abjectly, timidly.—…

ob-noxĭus.opening: adj. Lit. Subject, liable to punishment, obnoxious to punishment, punishable : obnoxius poenae obligatus ob delictum, Paul. ex Fest. p. 191 Müll.: ego tibi me obnoxium esse fateor culpae compotem, Plaut. Truc. 4, 3, 61…

ob-nūbĭlo.opening: v. a. , to cover with clouds or fog; to overcloud, darken, obscure (post-class.): vultūs serenitatem, Gell. 1, 2, 5 : haec omnia vitium, to obscure, Amm. 28, 4, 2 : odore sulfuris obnubilatus, beclouded, stupefied,…

ob-nūbĭlus.opening: adj., overclouded, cloudy, dark, obscure : obnubila tenebris loca, Enn. ap. Cic. Tusc. 1, 21, 48 (Trag. v. 108 Vahl.).

ob-nūbo.opening: v. a. , to veil, cover (very rare; syn.: velo, induo, amicio). Lit. : LICTOR, CONLIGA MANVS, CAPVT OBNVBITO, ARBORI INFELICI SVSPENDITO, an old formula ap. Cic. Rab. Perd. 4, 13 : flammeo caput nubentis obvolvatur, quod…

obnuntĭātĭo.opening: ( ), , obnuntio , in the lang. of augurs, an announcement of an opposing, adverse, evil omen : dirarum, Cic. Div. 1, 16, 29 .—In plur. : obnuntiationibus per Scaevolam interpositis, Cic. Att. 4, 16, 7 : comitiorum…

ob-nuntio.opening: ( ), , v. a. To tell, report, announce any thing bad or unfortunate: primus rescisco omnia: Primus porro obnuntio, Ter. Ad. 4, 2, 7 .— In augury, t. t., to announce an opposing, adverse , or evil omen (used both of the…

ob-rădĭo.opening: v. n. , to shine forth (postclass.), Isid. Orig. 16, 18, 2 .

obraucātus.opening: Part. , from the obsol. obrauco, āre [ob - raucus], grown hoarse (post-class.): ea (grus) ubi obraucata est, succedit alia, Sol. 10, 13 .

obrendārĭus.opening: adj. for obruendarius, v. obruo , of or belonging to burial, burial- : VASA OBRENDARIA DVA, i. e. earthen sarcophagi, Inscr. Orell. 4544 . —Called also, subst. : , , Inscr. Grut. 607, 1 .

ob-rēpo.opening: v. n. , to creep up to any thing, approach stealthily (class.). Lit. : et possim mediā quamvis obrepere nocte, Tib. 1, 9 (8), 59; Flor. 4, 10, 2 : qui Gallos in obsidione Capitolii obrepentes per ardua depulerat, Gell.…

obreptīcĭus.opening: or , , adj. obrepo , surreptitious, obreptitious (postclass.): petitio, Cod. Just. 3, 6, 3 ; Cod. Th. 4, 22, 6 (al. obrepta).

obreptĭo.opening: id. , a creeping or stealing on, a coming on suddenly or by surprise, a surprise (post - Aug.): Ventidius, aggressus per obreptionem, Front. Strat. 2, 5, 36 ; Arn. 5, 162 : arrogari per obreptionem, Dig. 2, 4, 10 :…

obreptīvus.opening: adj. obrepo , secret, clandestine (post-class.): supplicatio, Symm. Ep. 5, 64 ; Cod. Th. 16, 10, 8.—Hence, adv. : , surreptitiously, clandestinely (post-class.): aut clanculo supplicare, Cod. Th. 16, 1, 4 fin.

obrepto.opening: v. freq. n. [id.], to steal on unawares, to come on imperceptibly (very rare): ne quis obreptaverit, Plaut. Pers. 1, 2, 27 : obreptantibus Satyris, Plin. 35, 10, 36, § 109 (but in Cic. Att. 6, 5, 3 , the correct read.…

obrētĭo.grammar: īvi or ĭi, ītum, 4 v. a.
obrētĭo.opening: v. a. ob-rete . to eatch in a net, to entangle ( poet. ), Lucr. 3, 384 .

ob-rĭgesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to stiffen, become stiff (class.). Lit. With abl. : pars obrigescit frigore, Lucil. ap. Non. 97, 12 : pars (terrae regionum) obriguerit nive, pruināque, Cic. N. D. 1, 10, 24 ; and: e quibus (cingulis) duos…

Obrĭmas.opening: a river in Phrygia Major, which flows into the Mæander , Plin. 5, 29, 29, § 106 : Obrimae fontes, conj. reading for Rhotrinos fontes (the latter name being unknown), Liv. 38, 15, 12 .

ob-rōdo.opening: v. a. , to gnaw (ante- and post-class. for mordeo). Lit. : vermis te semper obrodit, Ambros. Tob. 7, § 26 : ut quod obrodat sit, Plaut. Am. 2, 2, 92 .— Trop. , to gnaw over, chew upon; to backbite, depreciate : haec…

obrŏgātĭo.opening: obrogo , a motion partly to repeal or alter one law by another, an obrogation : cum duae leges inter se differunt, videndum est, num qua obrogatio aut derogatio sit, Auct. Her. 2, 10, 15 ; cf. obrogo.

ob-rŏgo.opening: v. a. Partly to repeal an existing law by proposing a new one, to evade, weaken, invalidate, abrogate it: obrogare est legis prioris infirmandae causā legem aliam ferre, Paul. ex Fest. p. 187 Müll.: obrogatur, id est…

obructans.opening: Part. from the obsol. obructo [ob-ructo], belching at one: tibi obructans, App. Mag. p. 312, 34 .

ob-rŭo.opening: ( inf. pres. pass. OBRI for obrui, Inscr. Marin. Fratr. Arv. p. 341; v. in the foll. I. B. 1.), v. a. ( Lucr. 3, 775 ; v. infra ), to overwhelm, overthrow, strike down; to cover, cover over with any thing; also to hide…

obrussa.opening: (pure Gr. collat. form = χρυσίον ὄβρυζον , , Vulg. 2 Par. 3, 5 ; Isid. 16, 18, 2 ), , = ὄβρυζον , the testing or assaying of gold by fire in a cupel (class.). Lit. : auri experimentum ignis est: id ipsum obrussam…

obrȳza.opening: (collat. form of obrȳzum aurum), , standard gold , Cod. 12, 6, 12; 12, 7, 3; v. obrussa init.

obrȳzātus.opening: adj. obryzum , made of standard gold (post-class.), Cod. Th. 11, 10, 3; 12, 49, 1.

obrȳzum.opening: ( , also written ), = ὄβρυζον (sc. χρυσίον ), pure gold , Vulg. 2 Par. 3, 5 ; Petr. 67 ; Vulg. Job, 28, 15 ; 31, 24 ; cf. obrussa init.

ob-saepĭo.opening: ( ), (old form obsipio, Caecil. ap. Diom. p. 378 P.), v. a. , to hedge or fence in, to enclose; hence, transf., to close up, to render impassable or inaccessible (class.; syn.: obstruo, oppilo). Lit. : NEQVE QVIS IN EO…

obsălūtāre.grammar: se offerre salutandi gratiā dicebant antiqui, ut consalutare, persalutare

ob-sătullo.opening: v. dim. a. [saturo], to sate : obstrudant, obsatullent, Poët. ap. Paul. ex Fest. p. 193 Müll. (Com. Rel. v. 73 Rib.).

ob-sătŭro.opening: v. a. , to sate, cloy, glut; trop.: ne tu propediem istius obsaturabere, you'll soon have enough of him, Ter. Heaut. 4, 8, 28 .

obscaevo.opening: v. n. ob-scaeva , to give or bring a bad omen : metuo, quod illic obscaevavit meae falsae fallaciae, Plaut. As. 2, 1, 18 .

obscēnĭtas.opening: ( , ), , obscenus . * Unfavorableness, inauspiciousness , of a bad omen: mali ominis obscenitas, Arn. 1, 10 .— Moral impurity, foulness, unchastity, lewdness, obscenity . In abstr. (the class. signif. of the word): si…

obscēnus.opening: ( , and less properly ), , adj. perh. ob and caenum, filth , of adverse, unfavorable, evil omen; ill-boding, inauspicious, ominous, portentous (cf.: sinister, funestus): apud antiquos omnes fere obscena dicta sunt, quae…

obscūrātĭo.opening: obscuro , a darkening, obscuring, obscuration (class.). Lit. : solis, Cic. Fragm. ap. Aug. Civ. Dei , 5, 15; Quint. 1, 10, 47 ; Plin. 36, 27, 69, § 202 : in illā obscuratione, darkness, obscurity , Auct. B. Hisp. 6.—…

obscūrĕfăcĭo.opening: (only in pres.), , v. a. obscurus-facio , for obscuro, to obscure, render invisible : oblitterare est obscurefacere, Non. 146, 28 .

obscūrĭtas.opening: obscurus , a being dark, darkness, obscurity . Lit. (perh. only post-Aug.): latebrarum, Tac. H. 3, 11 : atra, Plin. 2, 18, 16, § 79 : visūs, dimness, id. 23, 1, 20, § 35 : oculorum, id. 37, 3, 12, § 51 . — Trop.…

obscūro.opening: v. a. id. , to render dark, to darken, obscure (class.; syn.: obumbro, opaco). Lit. : obscuratur et offunditur luce solis lumen lucernae, Cic. Fin. 3, 14, 45 : nitor solis, Cat. 66, 3 : finitimas regiones eruptione…

obscūrus.opening: adj. Sanscr. sku, to cover, akin to Gr. σκευή, σκῦτος, κύτος; cf.: scutum, cutis , dark, darksome, dusky, shady, obscure (class.). Lit. : unde (Acherunte) animae excitantur obscurā umbrā, in dark, shadowy forms , Poët.…

obsĕcrātĭo.opening: obsecro . In gen., a beseeching, imploring, supplication, entreaty (class.): prece et obsecratione humili uti, Cic. Inv. 1, 16, 22 ; id. Font. 17, 39 : judicum, addressed to the judges, Quint. 6, 1, 33 : percipe…

obsĕcrātor.opening: id. , one who entreats, a suppliant , Ven. Fort. Vit. Ger. 6.

ob-sĕcro.opening: ( ), (separate, ob vos sacro, for vos obsecro, Paul. ex Fest. p. 190 , Müll.), v. a. sacro , qs. to ask on religious grounds (ob sacrum), i. e. to beseech, entreat, implore, supplicate, conjure : obsecrare est opem a…

obsĕcundātĭo.opening: obsecundo , compliance, obsequiousness (post-class.): servilis obsecundatio, Cod. Th. 12, 1, 92.

obsĕcundātor.opening: id. , a servant (post-class.): sacrorum scriniorum, Cod. Th. 6, 26, 3.

ob-sĕcundo.opening: v. n. , to be compliant, show obedience; to comply with, humor, fall in with, follow implicitly, obey a pers. or thing (rare but class.; syn.: morigeror, obsequor, oboedio): obsecundare in loco, Ter. Heaut. 4, 6, 23 ;…

obsĕcūtĭo.opening: ( ), , obsequor , compliance, obedience (postclass.): inviolabili obsecutione servare, Arn. 7, 215 : voluntariae obsecutionis assensus, id. 6, 203 .

obsĕcūtor.opening: ( ), , id. , an obeyer, keeper, observer (eccl. Lat.): obsecutores legis, Tert. adv. Marc. 4, 9 ; Jul. Val. Res Gest. Alex. 3, 2 .

ob-sĕquēla.opening: or , , obsequor , compliance, complaisance, obsequiousness : obsequela obsequium, Paul. ex Fest. p. 192 Müll. (ante-class. and in Sall.): neque erat tuae benignitatis atque obsequellae, Turp. ap. Non. 215, 32 ; 29 (Com.…

obsĕquens.opening: Part. and P. a. , from obsequor.

Obsĕquens.opening: a Roman proper name : C. IVLIVS OBSEQVENS, Inscr. Murat. 824, 7 .

obsĕquenter.opening: adv. , v. obsequor, P. a. fin .

obsĕquentĭa.opening: 1. obsequens , compliance, complaisance, obsequiousness (very rare; not in Cic.): omnes parentes liberis suis facient obsequentiam, Plaut. As. 1, 1, 50 : nimia obsequentia reliquorum, Caes. B. G. 7, 29, 4 ; v. obsequela.

obsĕquĭae.opening: obsequor , for exsequiae, funeral rites, obsequies , Inscr. Fabr. p. 702 , n. 235 (Burm. and Meyer read exsequias).

obsĕquĭālis.opening: adj. obsequium , complying, yielding, complaisant (late Lat.): amor, Ven. Carm. 6, 7, 274.

obsĕquĭbĭlis.opening: adj. obsequor , com plying, yielding, complaisant (post-class.), Gell. 2, 29, 12 .

obsĕquĭōsus.opening: adj. obsequium , complying, complaisant, obsequious (anteclass.): alicui, Plaut. Capt. 2, 3, 58 .

ob-sĕquĭum.opening: obsequor . In gen., compliance, yieldingness, complaisance, indulgence (class.; syn.: indulgentia, obsequentia): prosequium a prosequendo, obsequium ab obsequendo dicuntur, Paul. ex Fest. p. 226 Müll.: obsequium amicos,…

ob-sĕquor.opening: (quutus), , v. dep. Lit. , to accommodate one's self to the will of a person; to comply with, yield to, gratify, humor, submit to; with dat. of the pers. or thing (freq. and class.; syn.: morigeror, obtempero, pareo,…

obsĕro.opening: v. a. ob-sera , to bolt, bar, fasten , or shut up (not in Cic. or Cæs.; syn.: claudo, oppilo, obstruo). Lit. : ostium, Ter. Eun. 4, 6, 25 : aedificia, Liv. 5, 41 : fores (opp. aperire), Suet. Tit. 11 : tabellam liminis,…

ob-sĕro.opening: ( ), ( inf. perf. sync. obsesse for obsevisse, Att. ap. Non. 395, 27 ), v. a. Lit. To sow or plant (class.): frumentum, Plaut. Trin. 2, 4, 129 . —Comically: pugnos, to give a good drubbing, Plaut. Men. 5, 7, 23 .—…

observābĭlis.opening: adj. observo , remarkable, observable (post-Aug.): manus, Quint. 9, 1, 20 : patientia, remarkable, App. M. 11, p. 267, 8 : nox ista est observabilis Domini, Vulg. Exod. 12, 42 .

observans.opening: Part. and P. a. , from observo.

observanter.opening: adv. , v. observo, P. a. fin .

observantĭa.opening: observo , a remarking, noting, regard, observance . In gen.: temporum observantia, Vell. 2, 1063 . — In partic. Observance, attention, respect, regard, reverence shown to another: observantia est, per quam aetate, aut…

observātē.opening: adv. , v. observo, P. a. fin. 2.

observātĭo.opening: observo , a watching, observing, observance (class.). In gen.: observationi operam dare, Plaut. Mil. 2, 6, 5 : siderum, Cic. Div. 1, 1, 2 .—As a gift or faculty, the power of observation , Plin. 18, 29, 69, § 284 .— In…

observātor.opening: id. , a watcher, observer (perh. not ante-Aug.): nemo observator, nemo castigator assistet, Plin. Pan. 40 : observator et custos bonorum, Sen. Ep. 41, 2 : Catholicae legis, i. e. one who obeys it , Cod. Th. 16, 5, 1.

observātrix.opening: observator , she that observes, an observer (eccl. Lat.): fides observatrix, Tert. Cor. Mil. 4 .

observātus.opening: observo , observation (ante-class.): ex observatu dicere, Varr. R. R. 2, 7, 3 .

observĭto.opening: v. freq. a. observo , to watch carefully, to note, observe (class.): Assyrii.. trajectiones motusque stellarum observitaverunt, Cic. Div. 1, 1, 2 : deorum voces, id. ib. 1, 45, 102 : omnia, App. Deo Socr. p. 52, 31 ;…

ob-servo.opening: (archaic fut. perf. observasso, Plaut. Mil. 2, 3, 57 ), v. a. In gen., to watch, note, heed, observe a thing; to take notice of, pay attention to (class.; syn.: animadverto, attendo): ne me observare possis, quid rerum…

obses.opening: (old orthogr. , in the first Epit. of the Scipios; v. infra ; Inscr. Spec. Epigr. p. 5, 11 Jahn), ĭdis ( gen. plur. obsidium, Caes. B. G. 5, 27 ; 6, 9 ; Liv. 2, 13, 97 ), and ob-sedeo . Lit. , a hostage : OPSIDES…

obsessĭo.opening: obsideo , a blocking up, besieging, encompassing, a blockade of a place (class.): obsessio templorum, Cic. Dom. 3, 5 : militaris viae, id. Pis. 17, 40 : castrorum, Suet. Caes. 58 : obsessionem alicuius omittere, Caes.…

obsessor.opening: id. , one who sits, stays, abides in a place; a frequenter, haunter . In gen. (only ante-class. and poet. ): hoc ego fui hodie solus obsessor fori, sai in the forum alone, Plaut. Ps. 3, 2, 18 : vivarum aquarum (of a…

ob-sībĭlo.opening: v. a. , to whistle away, to rustle (post-class.): arbores dulces strepitus obsibilabant, App. M. 11, p. 260, 27 .

obsĭdātus.opening: obses , the condition of a hostage, hostageship (post-class.): pater ejus diu obsidatūs pignore tentus, Amm. 16, 12, 25 : obsidatūs sorte in Syriis detentus, id. 18, 6, 20 : in obsidatum datus, Schol. Juv. 2, 164 .

ob-sĭdĕo.grammar: ēdi, essum, 2 v. n. and a.
ob-sĭdĕo.opening: v. n. and a. [sedeo]. Neutr., to sit, stay, remain, abide anywhere (only poet. ): servi ne obsideant, liberis ut sit locus, Plaut. Poen. prol. 23 : domi obsidere, Ter. Ad. 4, 6, 6 : in limine, Val. Fl. 2, 237 .— Act.,…

obsĭdĭālis.opening: adj. obsidium , of or for besieging, siege- : admotis obsidialibus machinamentis (al. obsidionalibus), Auct. Itin. Alex. 47 Mai.

Obsĭdĭānus.opening: , a false read. for Obsianus, Plin. 36, 26, 67, § 196 ; v. Obsius.

obsĭdĭo.opening: obsideo . Lit. In gen., a siege, investment, blockade of a place (class.): obsidionem potias dicendum esse, quam obsidium, adjuvat nos testimonio suo Ennius in Telamone, Paul. ex Fest. p. 198 Müll.; v. Müll. ad loc.;…

obsĭdĭōnālis.opening: adj. obsidio , of or belonging to a siege : corona, a crown of grass, granted as a reward to a general who rescued others from siege , Paul. ex Fest. p. 190 Müll.; so Liv. 7, 37, 2 ; Plin. 22, 4, 4, § 7 ; Gell. 5, 6, 8…

obsĭdĭor.opening: v. dep. obsidium , to lie in wait for, to waylay one (perh. only postAug.): alicui, Col. 9, 14, 10 .—(In Cic. Scaur. p. 40 , instead of obsidietur, Mai. more correctly reads obsaepiatur; v. obsaepio.)

obsĭdĭum.opening: obses , the condition of a hostage, hostageship (Tacitean): Meherdates obsidio nobis datus, Tac. A. 11, 10 .

ob-sīdo.opening: v. a. , to beset, invest, besiege, blockade (mostly poet. ): ne auriculam obsidat caries, ne vermiculique, Lucil. ap. Non. 21, 25 : vias oculorum, Lucr. 4, 351 : certas partes, id. 4, 1092 : pontem, Sall. C. 45, 2 Kritz…

obsignātĭo.opening: obsigno , a sealing, sealing up (post-class.): testamenti, Paul. Sent. 4, 6, 1 sq. : tabularum, Gell. 14, 2, 7 ; Arn. 2, 81 .— Trop. (eccl. Lat.), Tert. Bapt. 13 .

obsignātor.opening: id. , a sealer, sealer up (class.): litterarum obsignator, Cic. Clu. 66, 186 .—Esp., the witnesses who set their seals to a will , Cic. Clu. 13, 37 : testamenti, id. Att. 12 18, b, 2: decisionis, id. Fl. 36, 89 .

ob-signo.opening: v. a. , to seal, seal up a will, a letter, etc. (class.). Lit. In gen.: cedo tu ceram ac linum actutum: age obliga, obsigna cito, Plaut. Bacch. 4, 4, 96 : cellas, id. Cas. 2, 1, 1 : lagenas, Q. Cic. Fam. 16, 26 :…

ob-sĭpo.opening: v. a. supo , to sprinkle at or upon (ante-class.): obsipat aquulam, prov., it refreshes, cheers me, Plaut. Cist. 2, 3, 37 .

ob-sisto.opening: v. n. , to set, place , or post one's self before any thing (class.; syn.: adversor, repugno). In gen.: hic obsistam, ne, etc., will station myself, Plaut. Mil. 2, 3, 62 : alicui obviam, to plant one's self in another's…

Obsĭus.opening: a Roman surname , Plin. 36, 26, 67, § 196 .—Hence, , , adj., belonging to Obsius : lapis, so named after the discoverer, Plin. 37, 10, 65, § 177 .— Also subst. : , , , Plin. 37, 13, 76, § 200 ; and , , plur. n., a kind…

obsŏlĕfăcĭo.opening: v. a. ; in pass. : , obsoleofacio , to wear out, spoil, injure, sully, degrade, lower, make common (mostly postAug.): rivi non opere, nec fistulā, nec ullo coacto itinere obsolefacti, sed sponte currentes, Sen. Ep. 90,…

obsŏlesco.opening: v. inch. n. [obs-olesco], to wear out, to grow old, decay, fall into disuse, lose value, become obsolete (class.; syn. exolesco): his (verbis) oportet, si possis, non uti: sic enim obsolescent, Varr. L. L. 9, § 16…

obsŏlēto.opening: v. a. obsoletus , to degrade, soil, sully, stain, defile (eccl. Lat.). Lit. : qui vestitum obsoletāssent nuptialem, Tert. adv. Gnost. 6 .— Trop. : majestatis vestigia obsoletant, Tert. Apol. 15 .

obsŏlĭdo.opening: v. a. ob-solido , to make firm or fast, to harden, consolidate , only in part. pass. : , made solid, firm : tectorio rigide obsolidato, Vitr. 2, 3, 2 .

obsōnātĭo.opening: ( ), , 1. obsono , a buying of victuals; a catering, marketing , Don. ad Ter. And. 2, 2, 32 .

obsōnātor.opening: ( ), , id.. , a buyer of victuals; a caterer, purveyor : obsonator optimus, Plaut. Mil. 3, 1, 73 ; Mart. 14, 217 in lemm.; Sen. Ep. 47, 8 .

obsōnātus.opening: ( ), , id. , a catering, marketing : dare minam in obsonatum, Plaut. Truc. 4, 2, 27 : obsonatu redeo, id. Men. 2, 2, 5 and 14.

obsōnĭto.opening: v. freq. n. [id.], to feast, entertain , Cato ap. Paul. ex Fest. p. 201 Müll.

obsōnĭum.opening: or , , , = ὀψώνιον , that which is eaten with bread; victuals, viands , esp. fish : tu facito obsonatum nobis sit opulentum obsonium, Plaut. Bacch. 1, 1, 64 : curare, id. Merc. 3, 3, 22 : obsonare, id. Stich. 3, 1, 36 :…

obsōno.grammar: āvi, ātum, 1 ātus, 1 v. a. v. dep.
obsōno.opening: or , , v. a. , and or , , v. dep. ὀψωνέω , to buy provisions, to cater, purvey (class.). Lit. : postquam opsonavit erus, Plaut. Aul. 2, 4, 1 ; id. Men. 1, 3, 26 : ibo atque opsonabo opsonium, id. Stich. 3, 1, 36 : vix…

ob-sŏno.opening: v. a. , to interrupt by a sound; trop.: alicui sermone, i. e. to interrupt by speaking, Plaut. Ps. 1, 2, 74 .

obsŏpesco.opening: v. n. , to fall asleep : obsopit, obsopitus, obsopesco, Not. Tir. p. 135 .

ob-sŏpĭo.opening: v. a. , to put or lull to sleep (post-class.): a somni tempore prohibere, ne obsopiantur, Scrib. Comp. 180 : somno obsopitus, fallen asleep, Sol. 12 : odoris novitate obsopitus, made faint, stupefied, id. ib.

ob-sorbĕo.opening: v. a. , to sup or drink up, to swallow or gulp down (poetical). Lit. , Plaut. Mil. 3, 2, 21 : aquam, id. Curc. 2, 3, 34 : placentas, to gulp down, bolt , Hor. S. 2, 8, 24: unionem liquefactum, Plin. 9, 35, 58, § 121 .—…

ob-sordesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become dirty, be soiled (ante- and post-class.). Lit. : ne coma fumo obsordescat, Prud. Apoth. 214 .— Trop. , to wear out, decrease : obsorduit jam haec in me aerumna, i. e. is moderated , Caecil. ap.…

ob-stācŭlum.opening: obsto , a hinderance, obstacle (post-class.; cf. impedimentum): teneris et rarioribus parcit (fulmen), quia transitu patente minus obstaculum invenit, Sen. Q. N. 2, 52, 1 : rumpere obstacula, Prud. Ham. 601 ; App. Flor.…

obstantĭa.opening: obsto , a standing before or against, a resistance, hinderance, obstruction (only in Vitr.): terrae, Vitr. 9, 5, 4 : aëris, id. 6, 1 : umbrarum, id. 8, 1 .

ob-sterno.opening: v. a. , to strew or cast before, to throw in one's way (postclass.): uxorem puero, App. Mag. p. 335, 31 .

obstē^trīcĭus.opening: ( ) or , , adj. obstetrix , of or belonging to a midwife, obstetric (post -Aug.). Lit. : manūs obstetriciae, Arn. 3, 166 .— Trop. , Front. Orat. p. 246 .— Subst. : (sc. officia), , , midwifery, obstetrics : Jove Liberum…

obstē^trīco.opening: ( ), , v. n. and a. [id.], to perform the office of a midwife (eccl. Lat.), Tert. ad Nat. 2, 12 : Hebraeas (sc. mulieres), to assist in childbirth, Vulg. Exod. 1, 16 : obstetricandi scientia, id. ib. 1, 19 .— Trop. :…

obstē^trix.opening: ( ) or ( ), , obsto , a midwife : peperit Sine obstetricis operā, Plaut. Cist. 1, 2, 22 ; id. Capt. 3, 4, 96 : mittere ad obstetricem, Ter. Ad. 3, 1, 5 ; Hor. Epod. 17, 51 ; Vulg. Exod. 1, 15 : obstetricum nobilitas,…

obstĭnātē.opening: adv. , v. obstino, P. a. fin .

obstĭnātĭo.opening: obstino , firmness , in a good and bad sense; resolution, steadfastness, determination, inflexibility, stubbornness, obstinacy (class.; syn.: pertinacia, contumacia): quae ego omnia obstinatione sententiae repudiavi,…

obstĭnātus.opening: Part. and P. a. , from obstino.

obstĭnet.opening: , Paul. ex Fest. p. 197 Müll.; so, iam se caelo cedens aurora obstinet suum patrem, Poët. ib. (Trag. Rel. p. 228 Rib.).

obstĭno.opening: v. a. a lengthened form of obsto , to set about a thing with firmness or resolution, to set one's mind firmly on, to persist in, be resolved on a thing (as a verb. fin. very rare; only the Part. as a P. a. is freq.).…

obstīpātĭo.opening: ob-stipo , the close pressure (eccl. Lat.): turbarum obstipatione, Laurent. Hom. 1.

ob-stĭpesco.opening: and , , v. inch. n. and a., to become senseless, lose feeling; to be stupefied, benumbed (syn.: obtorpesco; class.). Lit. : apes obstupescunt potantes, Varr. R. R. 3, 16 : corpus, Plin. 36, 7, 11, § 56 .— Trop. , to be…

obstīpus.opening: adj. ob-stipes , bent or inclined to one side; opp. to rectus ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose). In gen., oblique, shelving : omnia mendose fieri atque obstipa, necesse est, Lucr. 4 . 517: obstitum (leg. obstipum)…

ob-sto.opening: (obstaturus, Front. Aquaed. 123 ; Quint. 2, 11, 1 ; Stat. Th. 7, 247 ; gen. plur. obstantum, Sil. 5, 277 ), 1, v. n. , to stand before or against any thing. In gen. (very rare): soli luna obstitit, Enn. ap. Cic. Rep. 1,…

obstrāgŭlum.opening: obsterno , a strap, lace, latchet , that fastened the sandal to the foot: crepidarum obstragulis, Plin. 9, 35, 56, § 114 .

obstrangŭlātus.opening: Part. , from the obsol. obstrangulo [ob-strangulo], strangled; trop. (post - class.): obstrangulata mens, Prud. Cath. 7, 10 .

obstrĕpĕrus.opening: adj. obstrepo , clamorous, chirping (post-class.), App. Flor. p. 349, 22 .

obstrĕpĭtācŭlum.opening: obstrepito , a clamor against, an outcry (eccl. Lat.), Tert. adv. Marc. 3, 20 .

obstrĕpĭto.opening: v. freq. n. [obstrepo], to sound against, to interrupt by noise or clamor ( poet. ). obstrepitant lamenta choris, Claud. Rapt. Pros. 2, 355 .

ob-strĕpo.grammar: ŭi, ĭtum, 3 v. n. and a.
ob-strĕpo.opening: v. n. and a. Neutr. Prop., to make a noise against or at; to roar or resound at; to resound, sound .—With dat. : marisque Baiis obstrepentis urges Submovere litora, Hor. C. 2, 18, 20 : remotis Obstrepit Oceanus…

obstrictus.opening: obstringo , a binding, clasping : accendat flammam ipso obstrictu (al. affrictu), Sen. Q. N. 5, 14, 4 .

obstrĭgillātor.opening: obstrigillo , an opposer, blamer (ante-class.), Varr. ap. Non. 492, 18 .

obstrĭgillo.opening: or , , v. a. obstringo , to hinder, oppose, impede (ante-class.): restitant, occurrunt, obstant, obstringillant, obigitant, Enn. ap. Non. 147, 10 : innocenti, Varr. ib.: multa (al. obsigillant), Sen. Ep. 115, 6 .

obstrĭgillus.opening: id. , a shoe-sole, sandal , fastened to the foot by straps, Isid. Orig. 19, 34, 8 .

ob-stringo.opening: v. a. To bind to or about; to bind, tie , or fasten up (rare): follem obstringit ob gulam, Plaut. Aul. 2, 4, 23 : quom ego Amphitruonem collo hinc obstricto traham, id. Am. 3, 2, 72 : cervice obstrictā, Juv. 10, 88 :…

ob-structĭo.opening: obstruo , a building before or against, a closing up by building, a blocking up . Lit. (post-class.): corporum, Arn. 2, 63 .— Trop. , an obstruction, a barrier : haec obstructio non diuturna est, Cic. Sest. 9, 22 .

obstrūdulentus.opening: obtrudo , that can be swallowed down : obstrudulenti da aliquid, quo pectam sedens, Titin. ap. Paul. ex Fest. p. 193 Müll. (Com. Rel. p. 134 Rib.), v. obtrudo.

ob-strŭo.opening: ( ), , v. a. , to build before or against; to build, block , or wall up; to stop up, barricade, render impassable (class.; cf. obsaepio, claudo, oppilo). Lit. : validum pro diruto obstruentes murum, Liv. 38, 29 :…

obs-trūsus.opening: , false read. for abstrusus, Sen. Ep. 68, 4 .

ob-stŭpĕ-făcĭo.opening: v. a. ; in pass. , , to astonish, amaze, astound, stupefy; to render senseless, deprive of feeling, benumb (class.): eum timidum obstupefecit pudor, Ter. Phorm. 2, 1, 54 : ipso miraculo audaciae obstupefecit hostes,…

ob-stŭpĭdus.opening: adj., amazed, confounded, beside one's self, senseless, stupefied (ante- and post-class.): hiat sollicita, studio obstupida, suspenso animo civitas, Pac. ap. Non. 429, 7 (Trag. Rel. p. 68 Rib. fin. ): quid astitisti…

obstū^prātus.opening: Part. , from obsol. obstupro [ob-stupro], defiled, dishonored (post-class.), Lampr. Commod. 3 .

ob-sufflo.opening: v. a. , to blow against or at , Auct. Quint. Decl. 7

ob-sum.opening: (old form of fut. obescet, oberit vel aderit, Paul. ex Fest. p. 188 Müll.), v. n. , to be against, be prejudicial to; to hinder, hurt, injure; opp. to prodesse (cf.: officio, noceo, injuriam facio; class.): Ty. Nunc…

ob-sŭo.opening: v. a. To sew on (very rare): obsutum caput, Ov. F. 2, 578 . — To sew up, sew together; to stop or close up ( poet. and in post-Aug. prose): nares, et spiritus oris obsuitur, Verg. G. 4, 301 : sporta auri obsuta, Suet.…

obsurdātus.opening: adj. ob-surdus , rendered deaf (eccl. Lat.), Aug. in Psa. 57, 15 .

obsurdĕfăcĭo.opening: v. a. ob-surdusfacio , to render deaf (eccl. Lat.), Aug. c. Faust. 33, 6.

ob-surdesco.opening: v. inch. n. , to become deaf (class.). Lit. : hoc sonitu oppletae aures hominum obsurduerunt, Cic. Rep. 6, 18, 19 : si sapiens excaecatur, obsurdescat, etc., Aug. Civ. Dei , 19, 4, 4.— Trop. , to be deaf , not to give…

obt-.opening: in compounds. In some MSS. and editions .

ob-taedesco.opening: ( ), , v. inch. n. , to disgust : nolo optaedescat, Plaut. Stich. 5, 4, 52 Fleck.

offendĭcŭlum.opening: 1. offendo , a stumbling-block , obstacle , hinderance , cause of offence (post-Aug.): sunt enim in hac offendicula nonnulla. Plin. Ep. 9, 11, 1 ; Vulg. 1 Cor. 8, 9 ; id. Isa. 57, 14 ; Paul. Nol. Carm. 27, 96 .

offendo.opening: 1. offendo , an offence , Afran. ap. Non. 146, 32 (offendo, offensio, Non.).
